prompts.prompt: Name causes of fever of unknown origin (FUO).

answers.name: Familial Mediterranean fever
answers.pearl: FMF (MEFV mutations) causes recurrent 1-3 day fevers with serositis and responds to colchicine.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Look for fever, cytopenias, very high ferritin, hypertriglyceridemia and splenomegaly, and search for the trigger (infection, lymphoma).

answers.name: Whipple disease
answers.pearl: Tropheryma whipplei can cause prolonged fever with arthralgia, weight loss and diarrhea, diagnosed by PAS-positive macrophages or PCR.

answers.name: Babesiosis
answers.pearl: Tick-borne Babesia can cause prolonged fever with hemolysis, and is more severe after splenectomy or in immunosuppression.

answers.name: Central fever
answers.pearl: Central fever is a diagnosis of exclusion and characteristically does not respond to antipyretics.

answers.name: Sweet syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis; it can accompany hematologic malignancy, infection, or drugs such as G-CSF.

answers.name: Aortic graft infection
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever after vascular grafting may be graft infection, best identified with FDG-PET or CT.

answers.name: Adult Kawasaki disease
answers.pearl: Kawasaki disease is rare in adults and is easily missed; persistent fever with rash, conjunctivitis and adenopathy should prompt consideration.

answers.name: Tick-borne relapsing fever
answers.pearl: Borrelia spirochetes cause recurrent febrile episodes separated by afebrile intervals.

answers.name: Murine typhus
answers.pearl: Flea-borne Rickettsia typhi causes prolonged fever, headache and rash, and responds to doxycycline.

answers.name: Tularemia
answers.pearl: Francisella tularensis can present as prolonged fever after rabbit, tick or deer-fly exposure.

answers.name: Macrophage activation syndrome
answers.pearl: A secondary HLH-like state complicating rheumatic disease, especially Still's disease and systemic JIA.

answers.name: Melioidosis
answers.pearl: Burkholderia pseudomallei from endemic soil and water (Southeast Asia, northern Australia) can mimic TB with chronic fever and abscesses.

answers.name: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Presents with fever, generalized adenopathy, rash, hypergammaglobulinemia and often autoimmune phenomena.

answers.name: Pelvic septic thrombophlebitis
answers.pearl: Postpartum or postsurgical fever persisting despite antibiotics may reflect septic pelvic vein thrombosis, treated with anticoagulation.

answers.name: PFAPA syndrome
aliases: periodic fever aphthous stomatitis pharyngitis adenitis
answers.pearl: Periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis and adenitis is usually pediatric but adult-onset cases are described.

answers.name: BCG infection
answers.pearl: Disseminated BCG after intravesical therapy can produce months of fever with granulomatous hepatitis or pneumonitis.

answers.name: Schnitzler syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic urticarial rash plus monoclonal IgM gammopathy with fever and bone pain; responds to IL-1 blockade.

answers.name: Rat-bite fever
answers.pearl: Streptobacillus moniliformis or Spirillum minus causes relapsing fever, rash and migratory arthritis after rodent exposure.

answers.name: SAPHO syndrome
answers.pearl: Sterile osteitis with fever and bone pain, often with palmoplantar pustulosis or acne.

answers.name: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes
answers.pearl: NLRP3 gain-of-function causes fever with urticaria-like rash and responds to IL-1 inhibition.

answers.name: Multicentric Castleman disease
answers.pearl: IL-6 driven lymphoproliferative disorder (HHV-8 in some HIV patients) causing fever, adenopathy and cytopenias.

answers.name: TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant TNFRSF1A mutations cause prolonged febrile attacks with migratory myalgia and periorbital edema.

answers.name: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
answers.pearl: Self-limited fever with tender cervical lymphadenopathy, seen mostly in young women, diagnosed by lymph node biopsy.

answers.name: Cyclic neutropenia
answers.pearl: ELANE mutations cause roughly 21-day cycles of neutropenia with fever, mouth ulcers and infections.

answers.name: Chronic meningococcemia
answers.pearl: Neisseria meningitidis can cause weeks of intermittent fever, rash and arthralgia, with positive blood cultures.

answers.name: Mevalonate kinase deficiency
answers.pearl: MVK deficiency causes periodic fever with lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain and elevated IgD, and mevalonic aciduria during attacks.

answers.name: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Aggressive gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma with fever, hepatosplenomegaly and cytopenias, mostly in young men with long immunosuppression.

answers.name: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: A classic hidden cause of FUO with high LDH and few nodes; random skin biopsy can be diagnostic.

answers.name: VEXAS syndrome
answers.pearl: Somatic UBA1 mutation in older men causing fevers, macrocytic anemia, chondritis, neutrophilic dermatosis and vacuolated myeloid precursors.

answers.name: Erdheim-Chester disease
answers.pearl: A non-Langerhans histiocytosis, often BRAF V600E mutated, with long-bone sclerosis, retroperitoneal fibrosis and constitutional symptoms.

answers.name: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease
answers.pearl: Persistent EBV-driven T/NK lymphoproliferation with fever, hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: TAFRO syndrome
aliases: thrombocytopenia anasarca fever reticulin fibrosis organomegaly
answers.pearl: Castleman variant with thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis or renal dysfunction, and organomegaly.

answers.name: Deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2
answers.pearl: Biallelic ADA2 mutations cause fever, livedo, early-onset stroke and polyarteritis nodosa-like vasculitis.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect (raise the INR or bleeding risk).

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 and typically requires about a 30-50% warfarin dose reduction; the effect lingers for months after stopping.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: Cimetidine inhibits several CYP enzymes, including those clearing R-warfarin, and raises INR; famotidine does not meaningfully.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of S-warfarin and can raise INR sharply within days.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs impair platelet serotonin uptake, adding bleeding risk without necessarily changing INR.

answers.name: Levothyroxine
answers.pearl: Thyroid hormone increases catabolism of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, so starting or increasing it raises warfarin sensitivity.

answers.name: Cefotetan
answers.pearl: Cephalosporins with an N-methylthiotetrazole side chain (e.g., cefotetan, cefoperazone) can cause hypoprothrombinemia.

answers.name: Ticlopidine
answers.pearl: Adds antiplatelet bleeding risk; now rarely used because of neutropenia and TTP.

answers.name: Celecoxib
answers.pearl: Celecoxib is metabolized by CYP2C9 and can raise INR even though it spares platelet COX-1.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Tamoxifen has been reported to markedly raise INR with serious bleeding in patients on warfarin.

answers.name: Vitamin E
answers.pearl: High-dose vitamin E has antiplatelet effects and may antagonize vitamin K-dependent clotting.

answers.name: Fluvastatin
answers.pearl: Fluvastatin inhibits CYP2C9, the main metabolic route of S-warfarin.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine has been associated with reduced vitamin K-dependent factor levels and potentiated anticoagulation.

answers.name: Dong quai
answers.pearl: Contains coumarin derivatives; case reports describe INR elevation.

answers.name: Fluorouracil
answers.pearl: Fluorouracil has been reported to increase INR with warfarin, possibly by inhibiting warfarin metabolism.

answers.name: Testosterone
answers.pearl: Androgen labeling warns of increased sensitivity to oral anticoagulants, so INR should be monitored.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone labeling reports INR increases and bleeding in patients on warfarin.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid inhibits hepatic enzymes and has been reported to raise INR, an interaction that is easy to miss.

answers.name: Oxandrolone
answers.pearl: Anabolic steroids such as oxandrolone markedly increase warfarin sensitivity, often requiring large dose reductions.

answers.name: Turmeric
answers.pearl: Curcumin has antiplatelet activity that adds to bleeding risk.

answers.name: Danazol
answers.pearl: Danazol, a synthetic androgen, increases warfarin effect and can precipitate bleeding.

answers.name: Capecitabine
answers.pearl: Capecitabine labeling warns of altered coagulation parameters and bleeding, including death, in patients on warfarin.

answers.name: Disulfiram
answers.pearl: Disulfiram inhibits CYP2C9 and raises S-warfarin exposure.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Leflunomide labeling reports INR increases with concomitant warfarin.

answers.name: Miconazole
answers.pearl: Even oral-gel and vaginal miconazole can inhibit CYP2C9 and cause marked INR elevations.

answers.name: Zileuton
answers.pearl: Zileuton labeling recommends prothrombin time monitoring and warfarin dose adjustment.

answers.name: Tigecycline
answers.pearl: Tigecycline labeling reports prolonged PT and aPTT and advises monitoring with warfarin.

answers.name: Zafirlukast
answers.pearl: Zafirlukast inhibits CYP2C9 and labeling advises monitoring the prothrombin time with warfarin.

answers.name: Sulfinpyrazone
answers.pearl: Sulfinpyrazone inhibits metabolism of S-warfarin and also has antiplatelet effects.

answers.name: Orlistat
answers.pearl: Orlistat can reduce vitamin K absorption; INR changes have been reported in patients on warfarin.

answers.name: Chloral hydrate
answers.pearl: Its metabolite trichloroacetic acid displaces warfarin from albumin, transiently increasing anticoagulant effect.

answers.name: Danshen
answers.pearl: Salvia miltiorrhiza has been associated with case-reported INR elevations and bleeding with warfarin.

answers.name: Stanozolol
answers.pearl: Anabolic steroid long known to potentiate warfarin markedly.

answers.name: Argatroban
answers.pearl: Argatroban prolongs the INR directly, so transition to warfarin requires adjusted targets or a chromogenic factor X assay.

answers.name: Boldo-fenugreek
answers.pearl: A case report described markedly raised INR with a boldo-fenugreek herbal preparation.

prompts.prompt: Name unusual or atypical ways a myocardial infarction can present.

answers.name: Silent myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Silent MI is more common in diabetes and the elderly and is often found later as Q waves on ECG.

answers.name: Epigastric pain
answers.pearl: Inferior MI frequently presents with epigastric discomfort, nausea and vagal symptoms.

answers.name: Jaw pain
answers.pearl: Jaw or tooth pain, especially if exertional, can be an anginal equivalent.

answers.name: Anxiety or sense of impending doom
Stroke
answers.pearl: Left ventricular mural thrombus after anterior MI can embolize, so stroke or limb ischemia may be the first apparent event.

answers.name: Papillary muscle rupture
aliases: acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture
answers.pearl: A late-presenting MI can declare itself by flash pulmonary edema from papillary muscle rupture, most often the posteromedial muscle in inferior MI.

answers.name: Ventricular septal rupture
answers.pearl: Typically occurs days after an infarct and presents with new harsh holosystolic murmur and shock.

answers.name: Ventricular free wall rupture
answers.pearl: Free wall rupture classically occurs days to a week after transmural MI and presents with sudden pulseless electrical activity or tamponade.

answers.name: Seizure
answers.pearl: Arrhythmic cerebral hypoperfusion can cause convulsive activity that is mistaken for a primary seizure.

answers.name: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
answers.pearl: SCAD should be considered in young or peripartum women with MI and few traditional risk factors.

answers.name: Coronary embolism
answers.pearl: MI in a young patient without atherosclerosis may be embolic, from atrial fibrillation, endocarditis or a prosthetic valve.

answers.name: Kounis syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute coronary syndrome triggered by an allergic or anaphylactic reaction with mast cell mediator release.

answers.name: de Winter T-wave pattern
answers.pearl: Upsloping ST depression with tall symmetric T waves in the precordial leads is a STEMI equivalent indicating proximal LAD occlusion.

answers.name: Tongue pain
answers.pearl: Isolated tongue pain has been reported as an anginal equivalent in case reports.

answers.name: Wellens syndrome
answers.pearl: Biphasic or deeply inverted T waves in V2-V3 in a pain-free interval indicate critical proximal LAD stenosis.

answers.name: Posterior myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: ST depression in V1-V3 with tall R waves may be a posterior STEMI equivalent and is confirmed with posterior leads V7-V9.

answers.name: Right ventricular infarction
answers.pearl: Hypotension with clear lungs and elevated JVP in inferior MI suggests RV involvement; avoid preload reduction such as nitrates.

answers.name: New left bundle branch block
answers.pearl: Concordant ST changes by the Sgarbossa criteria can reveal MI in the presence of LBBB.

answers.name: Vasospastic angina
answers.pearl: Rest pain, often at night or early morning, with transient ST elevation due to coronary vasospasm.

answers.name: Early post-infarction pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pleuritic, positional pain with friction rub within days of a transmural MI.

answers.name: Perioperative myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Postoperative MI is frequently asymptomatic and found on troponin surveillance.

answers.name: Ventricular pseudoaneurysm
answers.pearl: A contained myocardial rupture sealed by pericardium, which can present late with heart failure, embolism or arrhythmia.

answers.name: Hiccups
answers.pearl: Persistent hiccups, particularly with inferior MI, have been reported as a presenting symptom.

answers.name: Wrist pain
answers.pearl: Isolated wrist or hand pain has been reported as an anginal equivalent.

answers.name: Vasovagal reaction
answers.pearl: Inferior MI can trigger the Bezold-Jarisch reflex, causing bradycardia and hypotension.

answers.name: Ear pain
answers.pearl: Referred ear pain has been reported as the only symptom of myocardial ischemia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Propylene glycol toxicity
answers.pearl: High-dose IV lorazepam (propylene glycol diluent) can cause a high osmolar gap and lactic acidosis, mostly from D- and L-lactate.

answers.name: Isoniazid toxicity
answers.pearl: Isoniazid overdose causes refractory seizures and lactic acidosis, treated with IV pyridoxine.

answers.name: Iron overdose
answers.pearl: Severe iron poisoning causes lactic acidosis through mitochondrial toxicity and hypoperfusion.

answers.name: Malignancy-associated lactic acidosis
aliases: type B lactic acidosis in lymphoma
answers.pearl: Aggressive hematologic malignancies can cause type B lactic acidosis from tumor glycolysis, sometimes responsive to chemotherapy.

answers.name: Valproate toxicity
answers.pearl: Valproate overdose can cause anion gap acidosis, hyperammonemia and CNS depression, and may be treated with hemodialysis.

answers.name: Ibuprofen overdose
answers.pearl: Massive ibuprofen ingestion can cause anion gap acidosis, renal failure and coma.

answers.name: Diethylene glycol poisoning
answers.pearl: Diethylene glycol-contaminated medicines have caused outbreaks of anion gap acidosis and acute kidney injury.

answers.name: D-lactic acidosis
answers.pearl: Short bowel with colonic bacterial overproduction of D-lactate causes encephalopathy and acidosis that the standard L-lactate assay misses.

answers.name: Methylmalonic acidemia
answers.pearl: An organic acidemia causing ketoacidosis and hyperammonemia during metabolic decompensation.

answers.name: Propionic acidemia
answers.pearl: An organic acidemia with episodic ketoacidosis and hyperammonemia, usually presenting in neonates.

answers.name: Maple syrup urine disease
answers.pearl: Defective branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase causes ketoacidosis with sweet-smelling urine and encephalopathy.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease type I
answers.pearl: Fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia and hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Mitochondrial disease
answers.pearl: Respiratory chain defects such as MELAS can cause chronic or stress-triggered lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Isovaleric acidemia
answers.pearl: A leucine catabolism defect with ketoacidosis and sweaty-feet odor.

answers.name: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency
answers.pearl: PDH deficiency causes lactic acidosis that worsens with carbohydrate loading; ketogenic diet is therapeutic.

answers.name: Hereditary fructose intolerance
answers.pearl: Fructose ingestion causes hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis and liver injury.

answers.name: 5-Oxoproline accumulation
answers.pearl: Chronic acetaminophen use in malnourished women, sepsis, renal failure, or flucloxacillin can produce unexplained high anion gap acidosis from 5-oxoproline.

answers.name: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes lactic acidosis with elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratio and hyperammonemia in infants.

answers.name: Methylene chloride exposure
answers.pearl: Methylene chloride is metabolized to carbon monoxide, so carboxyhemoglobin rises after exposure.

answers.name: Dinitrophenol toxicity
answers.pearl: A mitochondrial uncoupler causing hyperthermia, lactic acidosis, tachycardia and diaphoresis.

answers.name: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency
answers.pearl: A gluconeogenesis defect causing fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Biotinidase deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes organic aciduria, ketolactic acidosis, alopecia, rash and seizures, all treatable with biotin.

answers.name: Aluminum phosphide poisoning
answers.pearl: Releases phosphine gas, causing refractory shock, severe lactic acidosis and arrhythmias.

answers.name: Benzyl alcohol toxicity
answers.pearl: Benzyl alcohol preservative in neonates causes gasping syndrome with metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency
answers.pearl: Episodic severe ketoacidosis triggered by illness, with characteristic urinary 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyrate and tiglylglycine.

answers.name: HMG-CoA lyase deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia with metabolic acidosis and hyperammonemia during fasting.

answers.name: Metaldehyde poisoning
answers.pearl: Metaldehyde causes seizures, hyperthermia and high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Succinyl-CoA:3-oxoacid CoA transferase deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes persistent ketosis and recurrent severe ketoacidosis episodes.

prompts.prompt: Name paraneoplastic syndromes or the autoantibodies that define them.

answers.name: SIADH
aliases: syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

answers.name: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
answers.pearl: Proximal weakness with hyporeflexia that improves with repeated effort, most often with small cell lung cancer.

answers.name: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis
answers.pearl: Psychiatric symptoms, seizures and dyskinesias in young women, often with ovarian teratoma.

answers.name: Anti-Hu antibodies
answers.pearl: Classically associated with small cell lung cancer and sensory neuronopathy or encephalomyelitis.

answers.name: Anti-Yo antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration, most often with breast or gynecologic cancers.

answers.name: Anti-Ma2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Classically associated with limbic and brainstem encephalitis in young men with testicular germ cell tumors.

answers.name: Anti-CASPR2 antibodies
answers.pearl: CASPR2 antibodies cause neuromyotonia, Morvan syndrome and limbic encephalitis, with thymoma in a subset.

answers.name: Tripe palms
answers.pearl: Thickened velvety palms with exaggerated dermatoglyphics, strongly associated with underlying malignancy, especially lung and gastric cancer.

answers.name: Anti-AMPA receptor antibodies
answers.pearl: Limbic encephalitis often associated with thymoma, small cell lung, or breast cancer.

answers.name: Anti-SOX1 antibodies
answers.pearl: Strongly associated with small cell lung cancer, especially in Lambert-Eaton syndrome.

answers.name: Anti-Tr antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with cerebellar degeneration in Hodgkin lymphoma.

answers.name: Necrolytic migratory erythema
answers.pearl: Migratory erythematous eruption with erosions, characteristic of glucagonoma.

answers.name: Pure red cell aplasia with thymoma
answers.pearl: Pure red cell aplasia is a recognized thymoma-associated autoimmune disorder.

answers.name: POEMS syndrome
answers.pearl: Plasma cell dyscrasia with VEGF-driven polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, M-protein and skin changes.

answers.name: Paraneoplastic gastrointestinal dysmotility
answers.pearl: Anti-Hu related enteric neuropathy causes pseudo-obstruction, classically with small cell lung cancer.

answers.name: Pityriasis rotunda
answers.pearl: Round, scaly hyperpigmented patches reported with hepatocellular carcinoma and other malignancies.

answers.name: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis
answers.pearl: A variant of malignant acanthosis nigricans with wart-like papules, reported with gastric adenocarcinoma.

answers.name: Anti-TIF1-gamma antibodies
answers.pearl: Dermatomyositis with anti-TIF1-gamma antibodies carries a high association with cancer in adults.

answers.name: Anti-Zic4 antibodies
answers.pearl: Seen with small cell lung cancer and cerebellar degeneration.

answers.name: Good syndrome
answers.pearl: Thymoma with adult-onset hypogammaglobulinemia causing recurrent infections.

answers.name: Anti-striational muscle antibodies
answers.pearl: Titin and ryanodine receptor antibodies are associated with thymoma and more severe myasthenia.

answers.name: Acquired C1 inhibitor deficiency with lymphoproliferative disease
answers.pearl: Acquired angioedema without urticaria may herald B-cell lymphoproliferative disease.

answers.name: Anti-AQP4 antibodies with cancer
answers.pearl: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder can rarely be paraneoplastic, with lung or breast cancer.

answers.name: Paraneoplastic acral vascular syndrome
answers.pearl: Digital ischemia that often precedes cancer diagnosis.

answers.name: Bazex syndrome
answers.pearl: Psoriasiform acral eruption with nail dystrophy, associated with upper aerodigestive tract squamous carcinoma.

answers.name: Anti-NXP2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Dermatomyositis antibody associated with calcinosis and cancer in adults.

answers.name: Anti-enolase antibodies
answers.pearl: Seen in cancer-associated retinopathy.

answers.name: Anti-envoplakin and anti-periplakin antibodies
answers.pearl: Plakin autoantibodies are characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus.

answers.name: Anti-glycine receptor antibodies
answers.pearl: Cause progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus; a minority are paraneoplastic.

answers.name: Anti-GFAP antibodies
answers.pearl: GFAP meningoencephalomyelitis is paraneoplastic in a minority, with ovarian teratoma and other tumors reported.

answers.name: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Erosive polyarthritis with cutaneous nodules; a malignancy is found in a significant minority of patients.

answers.name: Hypertrichosis lanuginosa acquisita
answers.pearl: Sudden growth of lanugo hair, associated with lung and colorectal cancers.

answers.name: Anti-recoverin antibodies
answers.pearl: Photoreceptor autoantibodies causing photosensitivity and progressive vision loss in lung cancer.

answers.name: Anti-ganglionic acetylcholine receptor antibodies
answers.pearl: Cause pandysautonomia, which can be paraneoplastic in a subset.

answers.name: Anti-NELL1 antibodies
answers.pearl: NELL1-associated membranous nephropathy has been linked to malignancy.

answers.name: Palmar fasciitis and polyarthritis syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive palmar contractures with polyarthritis, often with ovarian cancer.

answers.name: Anti-mGluR5 antibodies
answers.pearl: Limbic encephalitis associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

answers.name: Melanoma-associated retinopathy
answers.pearl: Night blindness with electronegative ERG due to ON bipolar cell dysfunction in metastatic melanoma.

answers.name: Anti-KLHL11 antibodies
answers.pearl: Rhombencephalitis with ataxia and hearing loss in men with testicular seminoma.

answers.name: Anti-mGluR1 antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with subacute cerebellar ataxia in Hodgkin lymphoma and other cancers.

answers.name: Anti-DPPX antibodies
answers.pearl: Causes encephalitis with hyperexcitability and prominent GI symptoms such as diarrhea; only a minority are paraneoplastic, with B-cell neoplasms reported.

answers.name: Anti-PCA-2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with small cell lung cancer and multifocal neurologic syndromes.

answers.name: Anti-ANNA-3 antibodies
answers.pearl: Neuronal nuclear antibody associated with lung cancer and neurologic syndromes.

answers.name: Anti-ITPR1 antibodies
answers.pearl: Cerebellar ataxia sometimes with neoplasia, including carcinomas of the lung and breast.

answers.name: Anti-PKC-gamma antibodies
answers.pearl: Cerebellar ataxia antibody, associated with lung carcinoma in some patients.

answers.name: Anti-CARP VIII antibodies
aliases: carbonic anhydrase related protein VIII antibodies
answers.pearl: Cerebellar ataxia antibody reported in melanoma.

answers.name: Anti-glutamate receptor delta-2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Cerebellar ataxia antibody reported with tumors.

answers.name: Anti-AP3B2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Cerebellar ataxia antibody reported with neuroendocrine tumors.

answers.name: Anti-TRPM1 antibodies
answers.pearl: Antibodies to TRPM1 on ON bipolar cells cause melanoma-associated retinopathy.

answers.name: Bilateral diffuse uveal melanocytic proliferation
answers.pearl: Rapid vision loss with diffuse uveal melanocytic proliferation, usually with systemic carcinoma.

prompts.prompt: Name ways a pulmonary embolism can present (symptoms, signs, or test findings).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Shoulder pain (referred diaphragmatic pain; weak evidence), Hiccups and New-onset seizure (case reports only), Platypnea-orthodeoxia (PE-with-PFO shunt, rare), Westermark sign and Hampton hump scored as board traps, Incidental finding on CT (not a symptom), Elevated troponin (finding rather than presentation).

answers.name: Shortness of breath
answers.pearl: Dyspnea is the most common symptom of PE and is often sudden in onset.

answers.name: Chest pain
answers.pearl: Chest pain in PE may be pleuritic or non-pleuritic, and central emboli with RV strain can mimic angina.

answers.name: Pleuritic chest pain
answers.pearl: Pleuritic pain suggests a peripheral embolus with pulmonary infarction irritating the pleura.

answers.name: Tachycardia
answers.pearl: Sinus tachycardia is the most common ECG finding in PE, but a normal heart rate does not exclude it.

answers.name: Hypoxia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia is common, but a normal oxygen saturation does not rule out PE.

answers.name: Tachypnea
answers.pearl: A respiratory rate above 20 is one of the most frequent signs, often present even without dyspnea.

answers.name: Unilateral leg swelling
answers.pearl: Signs of DVT are found in only about a third of patients with confirmed PE, but they raise pretest probability.

answers.name: Cough
answers.pearl: Cough is usually dry and nonspecific.

answers.name: Hemoptysis
answers.pearl: Hemoptysis suggests pulmonary infarction from a distal embolus.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Syncope can be the sole presentation and signals a large clot burden or RV failure.

answers.name: Lightheadedness
answers.pearl: Dizziness can reflect reduced cardiac output from a significant embolus.

answers.name: Calf pain
answers.pearl: Calf tenderness or pain suggests an accompanying lower-extremity DVT.

answers.name: Palpitations
answers.pearl: Palpitations may reflect sinus tachycardia or new atrial arrhythmia.

answers.name: Hypotension
answers.pearl: Sustained hypotension defines high-risk (massive) PE and prompts consideration of thrombolysis.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Patients often report a sense of impending doom, and PE is often misattributed to a panic attack.

answers.name: Low-grade fever
answers.pearl: A temperature up to about 38.5 C may occur with infarction and can be mistaken for pneumonia.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue and exercise intolerance may be the only complaint in subacute cases.

answers.name: Wheezing
answers.pearl: New wheeze can occur from mediator release and may suggest asthma or COPD instead.

answers.name: Cardiac arrest
answers.pearl: PE is a recognized cause of pulseless electrical activity arrest and sudden death.

answers.name: Incidental finding on CT
answers.pearl: A substantial minority of PEs are found incidentally on imaging done for other reasons, especially in cancer patients.

answers.name: Right heart strain
answers.pearl: RV dilation or dysfunction on echo or CT identifies higher-risk PE (submassive PE).

answers.name: Elevated troponin
answers.pearl: A positive troponin in PE indicates RV myocardial injury and a worse prognosis, and can be mistaken for ACS.

answers.name: New atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Acute RA pressure overload can precipitate new atrial fibrillation or flutter.

answers.name: Elevated jugular venous pressure
answers.pearl: A raised JVP indicates acute RV pressure overload in significant PE.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Small, often exudative and sometimes bloody effusions accompany pulmonary infarction.

answers.name: Acute right heart failure
answers.pearl: Acute cor pulmonale results when the RV cannot overcome a sudden rise in pulmonary vascular resistance.

answers.name: New right bundle branch block
answers.pearl: New complete or incomplete RBBB reflects acute RV pressure overload.

answers.name: COPD or asthma exacerbation mimic
answers.pearl: PE can masquerade as, or be the unrecognized trigger of, an obstructive airway exacerbation that does not respond to treatment.

answers.name: Delirium in older adults
answers.pearl: Older patients may present with confusion or fall rather than dyspnea or chest pain.

answers.name: T wave inversions in V1-V4
answers.pearl: Anterior T wave inversions reflect RV strain and are frequently mistaken for anterior ischemia.

answers.name: Loud P2
answers.pearl: An accentuated pulmonic component of S2 reflects acute pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Pulmonary infarction
answers.pearl: Infarction occurs in a minority of PEs, usually with peripheral emboli, and causes pleuritic pain and hemoptysis.

answers.name: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: CTEPH develops in a small percentage of PE survivors with persistent dyspnea and is diagnosed by V/Q scan.

answers.name: Shoulder pain
answers.pearl: Embolic involvement of the diaphragmatic pleura can produce referred shoulder-tip pain.

answers.name: Paradoxical embolism
answers.pearl: With a patent foramen ovale and raised right-sided pressure, a venous clot can cross to cause stroke or limb ischemia.

answers.name: Hiccups
answers.pearl: Persistent hiccups from diaphragmatic irritation have been reported as the presenting feature in case reports.

answers.name: New-onset seizure
answers.pearl: Case reports describe seizure-like activity as the presenting feature, likely from cerebral hypoperfusion after syncope or paradoxical embolism.

answers.name: Clot in transit
answers.pearl: Thrombus visualized in the right heart on echo is a high-mortality form of PE that may prompt thrombolysis or embolectomy.

answers.name: Platypnea-orthodeoxia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia worse upright can occur when a PE raises right-sided pressure and drives right-to-left shunting across a PFO.

answers.name: S1Q3T3 pattern
answers.pearl: The S1Q3T3 ECG pattern is a classic but insensitive and nonspecific sign of acute RV strain.

answers.name: Hampton hump
answers.pearl: A pleural-based, wedge-shaped opacity on chest radiograph representing pulmonary infarction; seen in a minority of PEs.

answers.name: Westermark sign
answers.pearl: Focal peripheral oligemia distal to an occluded pulmonary artery on chest radiograph; specific but uncommon.

prompts.prompt: Name ways infection or sepsis can present in an elderly patient (for example, an 85-year-old).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypothermia and Hypoactive delirium as board traps (not truly obscure); Back pain (vertebral osteomyelitis/epidural abscess link); Hypoglycemia in sepsis; Demand ischemia; Colonic pseudo-obstruction and Recrudescence of old stroke deficits (case-report-level evidence); Acute psychosis; Normal white blood cell count (leukocytosis often absent, but not universal).

answers.name: Altered mental status
answers.pearl: Delirium is often the first or only sign of infection in older adults, especially with UTI or pneumonia.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever is present in only a subset of frail older adults with serious infection, so absence does not exclude it.

answers.name: Falls
answers.pearl: New or recurrent falls can be the presenting sign of infection in frail older adults.

answers.name: Generalized weakness
answers.pearl: Nonspecific weakness is a very common ED presentation of occult infection in older adults.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Malaise and fatigue are common nonspecific prodromal symptoms.

answers.name: Decreased appetite
answers.pearl: Poor oral intake or anorexia is a frequent early sign of infection in older adults.

answers.name: Functional decline
answers.pearl: A sudden drop in ADLs or mobility ('failure to thrive') should prompt a search for infection.

answers.name: Tachycardia
answers.pearl: Tachycardia is a key sepsis sign but may be blunted by age or beta blockers.

answers.name: Hypotension
answers.pearl: Hypotension signals severe sepsis, and baseline hypertension means a 'normal' pressure may be relatively low.

answers.name: Somnolence
answers.pearl: Sleepiness and lethargy often occur in hypoactive presentations of infection.

answers.name: Tachypnea
answers.pearl: Respiratory rate is an early and sensitive sepsis sign (qSOFA criterion).

answers.name: Behavioral change
answers.pearl: Family reports of 'not acting like themselves' are an important clue to infection in the elderly.

answers.name: Absent fever
answers.pearl: Blunted febrile response is common in older adults, so use lower fever thresholds and look for other signs.

answers.name: Agitation
answers.pearl: Restlessness or combativeness can reflect hyperactive delirium from infection.

answers.name: New urinary incontinence
answers.pearl: New incontinence can be a presenting sign of UTI, though symptoms alone should not prompt treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion from poor intake and fever commonly accompanies and complicates infection.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: GI symptoms can dominate in infections such as pneumonia, UTI, or intra-abdominal sepsis.

answers.name: Dizziness
answers.pearl: Lightheadedness is a nonspecific presentation of volume depletion and infection.

answers.name: Dyspnea
answers.pearl: Shortness of breath may be the main presenting feature of pneumonia in older adults when cough and fever are absent.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Diarrhea should prompt testing for C. difficile in older adults with recent antibiotics or hospitalization.

answers.name: Hypoxia
answers.pearl: Low oxygen saturation can be the only objective sign of pneumonia in an older adult.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Syncope or near-syncope can be the presenting symptom of sepsis or pneumonia.

answers.name: High blood sugar
answers.pearl: Infection can unmask diabetes or cause new loss of glycemic control.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Rising creatinine from volume depletion and sepsis can be the first clue.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Intra-abdominal infections (cholecystitis, diverticulitis, appendicitis) may produce minimal pain or peritoneal signs in older adults.

answers.name: Septic shock
answers.pearl: Septic shock is vasopressor-dependent hypotension with elevated lactate despite fluids.

answers.name: Exacerbation of chronic disease
answers.pearl: Infection frequently manifests as decompensation of existing heart failure, COPD, or diabetes.

answers.name: New atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: New AF with rapid ventricular response is a common sepsis complication in older adults.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia occurs with pneumonia, CNS infection, and Legionella due to SIADH.

answers.name: Lactic acidosis
answers.pearl: Elevated lactate indicates tissue hypoperfusion and predicts mortality in sepsis.

answers.name: Urinary retention
answers.pearl: UTI or prostatitis can cause acute urinary retention in older men.

answers.name: Blunted heart rate response
answers.pearl: Beta blockers, pacemakers, and aging can blunt the tachycardia expected with sepsis.

answers.name: Demand ischemia
answers.pearl: Sepsis, anemia, and tachycardia can cause type 2 MI or troponin elevation without plaque rupture.

answers.name: Low blood sugar
answers.pearl: Sepsis can cause hypoglycemia through impaired gluconeogenesis, especially with insulin or sulfonylureas and renal failure.

answers.name: Back pain
answers.pearl: New back pain with bacteremia should raise suspicion for vertebral osteomyelitis or spinal epidural abscess.

answers.name: Normal white blood cell count
answers.pearl: Leukocytosis is frequently absent in elderly patients with serious infection, though bandemia may still be present.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Falling platelets are a marker of sepsis-related organ dysfunction and may precede DIC.

answers.name: Acute psychosis
answers.pearl: Delirium from infection can include hallucinations and paranoia that is mistaken for primary psychiatric illness.

answers.name: New-onset seizure
answers.pearl: Infection and metabolic derangements can provoke seizures in older adults without epilepsy.

answers.name: Recrudescence of old stroke deficits
answers.pearl: Infection can transiently unmask prior stroke deficits (a stroke mimic), which resolve when the infection is treated.

answers.name: Colonic pseudo-obstruction
answers.pearl: Ogilvie syndrome and ileus complicate sepsis and critical illness in older adults.

answers.name: Hypothermia
answers.pearl: Older and frail patients may be hypothermic rather than febrile in sepsis, a poor prognostic sign.

answers.name: Hypoactive delirium
answers.pearl: Quiet, withdrawn delirium is more common than agitated delirium in older infected patients and is often missed.

answers.name: Meningitis without neck stiffness
answers.pearl: Older adults with bacterial meningitis often lack meningismus and fever, presenting with confusion or lethargy.

prompts.prompt: Name extraintestinal manifestations or complications of inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Fever and Weight loss (systemic, arguably intestinal rather than extraintestinal); Depression and Anxiety alias; Glomerulonephritis/IgA nephropathy; Myocarditis; Arterial thromboembolism and Stroke alias; Bronchiectasis (documented airway disease in IBD, aliases loose); Relapsing polychondritis (association reported); Metastatic Crohn disease; Sacroiliitis, Cholangiocarcinoma and Amyloidosis scored as board traps (judgment call).

answers.name: Peripheral arthritis
answers.pearl: Type 1 (oligoarticular) peripheral arthropathy tracks with bowel activity, whereas type 2 (polyarticular) runs an independent course.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum
answers.pearl: Painful red nodules on the shins that parallel bowel activity; more common in Crohn disease than ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
answers.pearl: Painful ulcer with violaceous undermined border; shows pathergy and often does not track bowel activity.

answers.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: PSC is more strongly associated with ulcerative colitis and raises the risk of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer.

answers.name: Uveitis
answers.pearl: Usually anterior and may be bilateral; it does not reliably follow bowel activity and needs urgent ophthalmology.

answers.name: Ankylosing spondylitis
answers.pearl: Axial disease runs independently of bowel activity and only a minority are HLA-B27 positive.

answers.name: Episcleritis
answers.pearl: Benign, mildly uncomfortable ocular redness that parallels bowel disease activity.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Anemia in IBD is usually from iron deficiency (blood loss) and chronic inflammation, and sometimes B12 or folate deficiency.

answers.name: Oral aphthous ulcers
answers.pearl: Aphthous stomatitis is common in IBD, especially Crohn disease, and often tracks activity.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Bone loss results from chronic inflammation, glucocorticoids, malabsorption, and vitamin D deficiency.

answers.name: Kidney stones
answers.pearl: Crohn ileal disease causes enteric hyperoxaluria (calcium oxalate stones); dehydration after colectomy promotes uric acid stones.

answers.name: Venous thromboembolism
answers.pearl: IBD flares are prothrombotic and VTE risk is increased even in remission.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss reflects active inflammation and reduced intake or malabsorption (systemic rather than strictly extraintestinal).

answers.name: Gallstones
answers.pearl: Ileal Crohn disease or resection interrupts the enterohepatic circulation of bile acids and raises gallstone risk.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue is among the most common and burdensome extraintestinal complaints, even in remission.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Mood disorders are more common in IBD and relate to disease activity.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: Terminal ileal disease or resection impairs B12 absorption.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever can accompany active IBD, but fever with abdominal pain should raise concern for abscess or perforation.

answers.name: Clubbing
answers.pearl: Digital clubbing is described in Crohn disease and, less often, ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Growth failure
answers.pearl: Pediatric Crohn disease often presents with growth retardation or delayed puberty, sometimes before GI symptoms.

answers.name: Scleritis
answers.pearl: Painful deep scleral inflammation that can threaten vision, seen mainly in Crohn disease, and requires urgent ophthalmology.

answers.name: Hepatic steatosis
answers.pearl: Fatty liver is common in IBD from nutritional factors, steroids, and metabolic syndrome.

answers.name: Psoriasis
answers.pearl: Psoriasis is more common in IBD, and anti-TNF therapy can paradoxically cause psoriasiform eruptions.

answers.name: Sweet syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis causes tender red plaques with fever and neutrophilia and is reported with IBD.

answers.name: Enthesitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation at tendon or ligament insertions (Achilles, plantar fascia) is part of IBD-associated spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune hepatitis and PSC-autoimmune hepatitis overlap occur in IBD, particularly in pediatric ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis is a rare but recognized IBD complication, and can be drug-induced (mesalamine).

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Pancreatitis in IBD can be due to gallstones, drugs (azathioprine, mesalamine), or the disease itself.

answers.name: Osteonecrosis
answers.pearl: Avascular necrosis (femoral head) is linked to glucocorticoid use and to IBD itself.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Neuropathy can arise from B12 deficiency, metronidazole, or anti-TNF therapy, and sometimes from the disease itself.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: IgA nephropathy and other glomerular disease have been reported with IBD.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Myocarditis is rare in IBD and can also be a mesalamine hypersensitivity reaction.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Pulmonary involvement in IBD includes ILD, organizing pneumonia, and drug reactions (e.g., mesalamine, methotrexate).

answers.name: Arterial thromboembolism
answers.pearl: IBD increases the risk of arterial events including stroke and MI, beyond the venous risk.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Large and small airway disease, including bronchiectasis, is a recognized pulmonary manifestation that can precede IBD diagnosis.

answers.name: Pyostomatitis vegetans
answers.pearl: Pustular, vegetating oral lesions ('snail-track' ulcers) are a specific marker of IBD, especially ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Metastatic Crohn disease
answers.pearl: Cutaneous Crohn lesions noncontiguous with the GI tract that show noncaseating granulomas on biopsy.

answers.name: Relapsing polychondritis
answers.pearl: An uncommon association with IBD causing ear or nasal cartilage inflammation.

answers.name: Sacroiliitis
answers.pearl: Radiographic sacroiliitis is common in IBD and may be asymptomatic, and it is HLA-B27-independent more often than not.

answers.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Patients with PSC-IBD have a markedly increased lifetime risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Secondary (AA) amyloidosis can complicate long-standing active Crohn disease and presents with proteinuria or nephrotic syndrome.

prompts.prompt: Name ways a patient with heart failure can present (symptoms, signs, or findings).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Thromboembolic event (alias 'stroke', 'DVT', 'pulmonary embolism' are loose); Sleep-disordered breathing; Sacral edema; Phantom tumor; Protein-losing enteropathy (mostly right HF / Fontan); Trepopnea and Bendopnea (documented but uncommon); Pulsus alternans scored 60 (could be argued a board trap); Cheyne-Stokes, Kerley B lines and hepatojugular reflux as board traps.

answers.name: Shortness of breath
answers.pearl: Dyspnea is the cardinal symptom of heart failure, from pulmonary venous congestion.

answers.name: Dyspnea on exertion
answers.pearl: Exertional dyspnea is typically the earliest symptom, and its threshold defines NYHA class.

answers.name: Leg edema
answers.pearl: Bilateral dependent pitting edema reflects elevated venous pressure and renal salt retention.

answers.name: Orthopnea
answers.pearl: Dyspnea when lying flat, often quantified by the number of pillows used.

answers.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
answers.pearl: Sudden awakening with breathlessness several hours after lying down, relieved by sitting up.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue results from low cardiac output and skeletal muscle changes.

answers.name: Weight gain
answers.pearl: Rapid weight gain over days signals fluid retention and is the basis for daily weight monitoring.

answers.name: Pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Flash pulmonary edema can be the first presentation, particularly with ischemia, hypertensive crisis, or valve disease.

answers.name: Exercise intolerance
answers.pearl: Reduced exercise capacity is a core feature and determines functional class.

answers.name: Cough
answers.pearl: A persistent, often nocturnal dry cough from pulmonary congestion can be mistaken for asthma or ACE inhibitor cough.

answers.name: Elevated jugular venous pressure
answers.pearl: Jugular venous distension is a specific sign of elevated right-sided filling pressures.

answers.name: Pulmonary crackles
answers.pearl: Rales reflect alveolar fluid but are absent in many chronic HF patients because of lymphatic compensation.

answers.name: Tachycardia
answers.pearl: Compensatory sympathetic activation raises the heart rate.

answers.name: Hypoxia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia results from pulmonary edema and ventilation-perfusion mismatch.

answers.name: Ascites
answers.pearl: Abdominal distension from ascites occurs in right-sided or biventricular failure.

answers.name: Palpitations
answers.pearl: Palpitations often reflect atrial fibrillation or ventricular ectopy.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Effusions are usually bilateral (right larger than left) and transudative.

answers.name: S3 gallop
answers.pearl: A third heart sound indicates rapid ventricular filling with volume overload and is specific for elevated filling pressures.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Cardiogenic shock is the extreme low-output presentation, with hypotension and hypoperfusion despite adequate filling.

answers.name: Wheezing
answers.pearl: 'Cardiac asthma' is wheezing from interstitial and bronchial wall edema, often mistaken for COPD or asthma.

answers.name: Nocturia
answers.pearl: Fluid redistributes and renal perfusion improves when supine, so nighttime urination is common.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Syncope in HF can signal arrhythmia (VT) or low-output states and is a high-risk feature.

answers.name: Hepatomegaly
answers.pearl: Tender, pulsatile liver enlargement indicates hepatic venous congestion.

answers.name: Confusion
answers.pearl: Older patients may present with confusion or poor concentration from reduced cerebral perfusion.

answers.name: New atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: AF is both a cause and consequence of heart failure and can be the precipitating presentation.

answers.name: Early satiety
answers.pearl: Gut edema and hepatic congestion cause anorexia, nausea, and early satiety.

answers.name: Sudden cardiac death
answers.pearl: Ventricular arrhythmia causes about half of deaths in HF with reduced ejection fraction.

answers.name: Anasarca
answers.pearl: Generalized edema including the trunk, scrotum, and face can occur in severe biventricular failure.

answers.name: Cardiac cachexia
answers.pearl: Unintentional weight loss with muscle wasting in advanced HF is a poor prognostic sign.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Neurohormonal activation (ADH, RAAS) causes dilutional hyponatremia, which predicts mortality.

answers.name: Pink frothy sputum
answers.pearl: Frothy, pink-tinged sputum is a classic sign of severe alveolar pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Sacral edema
answers.pearl: In bedbound patients, edema collects over the sacrum rather than the legs.

answers.name: Cardiorenal syndrome
answers.pearl: Worsening renal function from venous congestion and low output complicates HF and drives diuretic resistance.

answers.name: Sleep-disordered breathing
answers.pearl: Central sleep apnea with Cheyne-Stokes pattern and obstructive sleep apnea are both common in HF.

answers.name: Thromboembolic event
answers.pearl: Atrial fibrillation or LV thrombus in a dilated, hypokinetic ventricle can cause stroke or systemic embolism.

answers.name: Congestive hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Chronic hepatic congestion causes elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase and can progress to cardiac cirrhosis.

answers.name: Pulsus alternans
answers.pearl: Alternating strong and weak pulses signal severe LV systolic dysfunction.

answers.name: Bendopnea
answers.pearl: Dyspnea within 30 seconds of bending forward correlates with elevated filling pressures in advanced HF.

answers.name: Protein-losing enteropathy
answers.pearl: Gut venous hypertension can cause protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, and diarrhea, especially in right HF or after Fontan.

answers.name: Trepopnea
aliases: shortness of breath on one side
answers.pearl: Dyspnea in one lateral decubitus position, usually the right side, reflects asymmetric cardiac or pulmonary congestion.

answers.name: Phantom tumor
answers.pearl: Loculated fluid in a lung fissure appears as a mass on radiograph and vanishes with diuresis (vanishing tumor).

answers.name: Kerley B lines
answers.pearl: Septal lines at the lung periphery indicate interstitial edema on chest radiograph.

answers.name: Hepatojugular reflux
answers.pearl: Sustained JVP rise (over 4 cm for 15 seconds) with abdominal pressure suggests elevated right atrial pressure.

answers.name: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
answers.pearl: Crescendo-decrescendo periodic breathing in advanced HF reflects prolonged circulation time and chemoreceptor instability.

prompts.prompt: Name ways hypothyroidism can present (symptoms, signs, test findings, or complications).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Obstructive sleep apnea (association, mostly with obesity/macroglossia); Hyperprolactinemia; Psychosis (myxedema madness, rare); Paralytic ileus; Infertility aliases; Cardiomyopathy alias heart failure; Low voltage ECG; Hearing loss; Thyrotroph hyperplasia; Van Wyk-Grumbach and Kocher-Debre-Semelaigne (pediatric, well described but exceedingly rare); Acquired von Willebrand syndrome; Macroglossia scored as a board trap.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue and low energy are the most common complaints.

answers.name: Weight gain
answers.pearl: Gain is usually modest (a few kilograms) and partly from fluid retention, so it rarely explains severe obesity.

answers.name: Cold intolerance
answers.pearl: Reduced thermogenesis from lower basal metabolic rate.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Decreased gut motility is common and sometimes severe.

answers.name: Dry skin
answers.pearl: Skin becomes dry, coarse, and pale from decreased sweating and glycosaminoglycan deposition.

answers.name: Hair loss
answers.pearl: Diffuse thinning and coarse, brittle hair; the lateral eyebrows may also thin.

answers.name: Bradycardia
answers.pearl: Decreased chronotropy produces a slow resting heart rate.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Hypothyroidism can cause or worsen depression and should be checked in new depressive episodes.

answers.name: Somnolence
answers.pearl: Excessive sleepiness and slowed mentation are common.

answers.name: Goiter
answers.pearl: Goiter occurs in Hashimoto disease and iodine deficiency, though thyroid atrophy is common in later autoimmune disease.

answers.name: Memory impairment
answers.pearl: Cognitive slowing can mimic dementia and is often reversible with treatment.

answers.name: Menstrual irregularities
answers.pearl: Menorrhagia or oligomenorrhea are common because of altered estrogen metabolism and coagulation.

answers.name: Myalgias
answers.pearl: Muscle aches, cramps, and stiffness are common, and the CK may be elevated.

answers.name: Peripheral edema
answers.pearl: Myxedema is characteristically non-pitting from glycosaminoglycan deposition, though mild pitting edema also occurs.

answers.name: Hyperlipidemia
answers.pearl: Elevated LDL cholesterol results from reduced LDL receptor activity, and secondary causes should be excluded before starting statins.

answers.name: Periorbital puffiness
answers.pearl: Periorbital and facial puffiness from myxedematous infiltration.

answers.name: Hoarseness
answers.pearl: Vocal cord myxedema causes a deep, hoarse voice.

answers.name: Muscle weakness
answers.pearl: Proximal myopathy with elevated CK is seen in hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Joint pain, stiffness, and effusions can occur.

answers.name: Brittle nails
answers.pearl: Nails become brittle, ridged, and slow growing.

answers.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
answers.pearl: Mucopolysaccharide deposition in the carpal tunnel causes median neuropathy.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Anemia can be normocytic, macrocytic, or iron deficient (from menorrhagia), and B12 deficiency is associated with autoimmune thyroiditis.

answers.name: Infertility
answers.pearl: Anovulation, luteal-phase defects, and miscarriage are linked to hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Diastolic hypertension occurs from increased systemic vascular resistance.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Reduced free water clearance and elevated ADH cause hyponatremia, usually in severe disease.

answers.name: Pericardial effusion
answers.pearl: Slowly accumulating effusion is common and rarely causes tamponade.

answers.name: Hypothermia
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism and myxedema coma may present with low body temperature.

answers.name: Hearing loss
answers.pearl: Hearing loss is reported in congenital and acquired hypothyroidism, often sensorineural.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: Hypothyroidism is linked with sleep apnea, and TSH screening is reasonable in unexplained cases.

answers.name: Elevated creatine kinase
answers.pearl: CK elevation, sometimes marked, is common even without symptoms and can mimic statin myopathy.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Reduced contractility and cardiac output can lead to heart failure that improves with levothyroxine.

answers.name: Low voltage ECG
answers.pearl: Low QRS voltage results from pericardial effusion and myocardial changes.

answers.name: Hyperprolactinemia
answers.pearl: Elevated TRH stimulates prolactin, causing galactorrhea and menstrual irregularity.

answers.name: Psychosis
answers.pearl: 'Myxedema madness' includes paranoia and hallucinations in severe hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Paralytic ileus
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism can cause ileus, pseudo-obstruction, or megacolon.

answers.name: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome
answers.pearl: Hypothyroidism can lower vWF and factor VIII and cause mucocutaneous bleeding, which corrects with levothyroxine.

answers.name: Thyrotroph hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Long-standing primary hypothyroidism can enlarge the pituitary and mimic an adenoma that regresses with levothyroxine.

answers.name: Kocher-Debre-Semelaigne syndrome
answers.pearl: Pediatric hypothyroid myopathy with muscular pseudohypertrophy ('infant Hercules').

answers.name: Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome
answers.pearl: Severe juvenile hypothyroidism causing precocious puberty features, including breast development, ovarian cysts, and delayed bone age.

answers.name: Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes
answers.pearl: Slowed relaxation phase of the Achilles reflex is a classic sign of hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Myxedema coma
answers.pearl: Decompensated severe hypothyroidism with altered mentation, hypothermia, and often a precipitant such as infection, carrying high mortality.

answers.name: Macroglossia
answers.pearl: Tongue enlargement from myxedematous infiltration, classically in congenital hypothyroidism.

prompts.prompt: Name extra-articular manifestations or complications of rheumatoid arthritis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Increased infection risk (largely treatment-related); Depression; Leg ulcers; Cardiac valvular disease and Conduction abnormalities (documented, uncommon); Glomerulonephritis (often drug-induced); Bronchiectasis; Rheumatoid meningitis, Cricoarytenoid arthritis, Scleromalacia perforans, LGL leukemia (rare but described); Felty, Caplan and Atlantoaxial subluxation scored as board traps (judgment call).

answers.name: Rheumatoid nodules
answers.pearl: Subcutaneous nodules occur in seropositive disease on extensor surfaces and pressure points.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: ILD (UIP or NSIP pattern) is a leading cause of RA-related mortality.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Anemia of chronic inflammation is the most common hematologic manifestation.

answers.name: Cardiovascular disease
answers.pearl: RA carries cardiovascular risk similar to diabetes, with accelerated atherosclerosis driven by inflammation.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue is among the most disabling symptoms.

answers.name: Dry eyes
answers.pearl: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca is the most common ocular manifestation.

answers.name: Dry mouth
answers.pearl: Xerostomia from salivary gland involvement is common.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Bone loss from inflammation, immobility, and glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid effusions are exudative with very low glucose and low pH.

answers.name: Scleritis
answers.pearl: Painful scleral inflammation that can progress to scleral thinning and perforation.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis and effusion occur in a substantial minority and are often subclinical.

answers.name: Rheumatoid vasculitis
answers.pearl: Vasculitis presents with digital infarcts, skin ulcers, or mononeuritis in long-standing seropositive disease.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever and constitutional symptoms can accompany flares.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid cachexia reflects cytokine-driven muscle loss.

answers.name: Secondary Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Sicca symptoms from lymphocytic infiltration of lacrimal and salivary glands occur in many RA patients.

answers.name: Increased infection risk
answers.pearl: Both the disease and immunosuppressive therapy raise the risk of serious infection.

answers.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
answers.pearl: Synovitis of the flexor tendon sheaths compresses the median nerve.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Sensory or sensorimotor neuropathy can result from entrapment, vasculitis, or medication.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression is common and is associated with worse pain and disease activity.

answers.name: Leg ulcers
answers.pearl: Chronic leg ulcers in RA may be vasculitic, venous, or pyoderma-related.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: RA is associated with an increased risk of lymphoma, particularly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, related to disease activity.

answers.name: Neutropenia
answers.pearl: Neutropenia can be disease-related (Felty and LGL) or drug-related (methotrexate, DMARDs).

answers.name: Thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Reactive thrombocytosis is common with active inflammation.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Splenomegaly may be an isolated finding or part of Felty syndrome.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Bronchiectasis is more common in RA and may precede joint disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary nodules
answers.pearl: Necrobiotic rheumatoid nodules appear in the lungs, sometimes cavitating, and can mimic malignancy or infection.

answers.name: Mononeuritis multiplex
answers.pearl: Vasculitic involvement of the vasa nervorum can cause foot drop or wrist drop.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Secondary AA amyloidosis from chronic inflammation causes proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: Bronchiolitis obliterans
answers.pearl: Constrictive bronchiolitis causes progressive airflow obstruction in RA and can be drug-associated.

answers.name: Cervical myelopathy
answers.pearl: Cervical spine involvement can compress the cord, causing weakness, sensory change, or gait disturbance.

answers.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
answers.pearl: Pyoderma gangrenosum is associated with RA and inflammatory arthritis.

answers.name: Conduction abnormalities
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid nodules or inflammation of the conduction system can cause heart block.

answers.name: Peripheral ulcerative keratitis
answers.pearl: Marginal corneal melt that is sight-threatening and often accompanies active systemic vasculitis.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Glomerular disease in RA is often drug-induced (gold, penicillamine, NSAIDs) but mesangial GN also occurs.

answers.name: Valvular disease
answers.pearl: Valve nodules and valvulitis causing regurgitation are described in RA.

answers.name: Cricoarytenoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Involvement of the cricoarytenoid joint causes hoarseness, stridor, or dysphagia and may cause airway obstruction.

answers.name: Large granular lymphocyte leukemia
answers.pearl: T-LGL leukemia is associated with RA and can mimic Felty syndrome with neutropenia and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Scleromalacia perforans
answers.pearl: Painless scleral thinning in long-standing RA that can lead to uveal prolapse.

answers.name: Rheumatoid meningitis
answers.pearl: Rare CNS involvement with pachymeningitis or leptomeningeal inflammation, often with headache or seizures.

answers.name: Felty syndrome
aliases: triad of RA splenomegaly and neutropenia
answers.pearl: The triad of RA, splenomegaly, and neutropenia, typically in long-standing seropositive disease.

answers.name: Caplan syndrome
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid pneumoconiosis with multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules in RA patients exposed to coal dust or silica.

answers.name: Atlantoaxial subluxation
answers.pearl: C1-C2 instability from erosion of the transverse ligament and odontoid, which must be assessed before intubation.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyponatremia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: TMP-SMX (ENaC blockade, mainly high dose), cisplatin (salt wasting vs SIADH), Rocky Mountain spotted fever (lab finding more than classic cause), IVIG (translocational/pseudo), NSIAD (rare genetic), MDMA, tea and toast diet, exercise-associated hyponatremia scored as plankton; reset osmostat scored as trap though clinically real.

answers.name: SIADH
answers.pearl: SIADH is euvolemic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine (urine osm above 100) and urine sodium usually above 30 mEq/L.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Reduced effective arterial volume drives ADH release and water retention despite total-body sodium excess.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume and triggers non-osmotic ADH release; hyponatremia predicts worse survival.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides are a more common cause than loop diuretics because they impair urinary dilution without disrupting the medullary gradient.

answers.name: Hypovolemia
answers.pearl: Volume depletion from GI, renal, or skin losses stimulates ADH release; urine sodium below 20 suggests extrarenal loss.

answers.name: Vomiting
answers.pearl: Volume loss and nausea both drive ADH secretion.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: GI fluid loss replaced by hypotonic fluid intake produces hyponatremia with low urine sodium.

answers.name: Psychogenic polydipsia
answers.pearl: Intake must exceed roughly 10-15 L/day to overwhelm normal renal water excretion; urine is maximally dilute.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs cause SIADH, typically within the first weeks of therapy and most often in older women.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency removes inhibition of ADH release; mineralocorticoid deficiency adds renal sodium loss.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism or myxedema lowers GFR and free-water clearance.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Impaired free-water excretion in advanced kidney disease limits the ability to dilute urine.

answers.name: Small cell lung cancer
aliases: small cell carcinoma of the lung
answers.pearl: Ectopic ADH secretion from small cell carcinoma is the classic malignant cause of SIADH.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Pulmonary infection can cause SIADH through non-osmotic ADH release.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Edematous state with reduced effective arterial volume and non-osmotic ADH release.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics cause hyponatremia less often than thiazides because they impair the medullary concentrating gradient.

answers.name: Hyperglycemia
answers.pearl: Each 100 mg/dL of glucose above normal lowers measured sodium by roughly 1.6-2.4 mEq/L through osmotic water shift.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Acute CNS injury can cause SIADH or cerebral salt wasting.

answers.name: Nausea
answers.pearl: Nausea and pain are potent non-osmotic stimuli of ADH release.

answers.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia after SAH may come from SIADH or cerebral salt wasting and affects management of vasospasm.

answers.name: Postoperative state
answers.pearl: Postoperative pain, nausea, and hypotonic IV fluids combine to produce ADH-mediated hyponatremia.

answers.name: Exercise-associated hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Overdrinking of hypotonic fluids plus non-osmotic ADH release occurs in marathon and ultramarathon runners.

answers.name: Beer potomania
answers.pearl: Very low solute intake limits urinary water excretion even with modest fluid intake.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine cause SIADH, with oxcarbazepine more often producing hyponatremia.

answers.name: Desmopressin
answers.pearl: Desmopressin (DDAVP) causes free-water retention, so sodium should be monitored with its use.

answers.name: Tea and toast diet
answers.pearl: Low solute intake limits free-water excretion because the kidney needs osmoles to excrete water.

answers.name: MDMA (ecstasy)
answers.pearl: MDMA causes SIADH and also promotes heavy water drinking.

answers.name: Meningitis
answers.pearl: CNS infection can cause SIADH.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Tricyclics can cause SIADH like other antidepressants.

answers.name: Oxytocin
answers.pearl: High-dose oxytocin infusion for labor induction has ADH-like antidiuretic effects, causing water intoxication.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia is common in HIV, driven by pulmonary or CNS infection, adrenal insufficiency, or volume depletion.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Pulmonary or CNS tuberculosis can cause SIADH and adrenal involvement.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloids cause SIADH, usually with high-dose therapy.

answers.name: Hypopituitarism
answers.pearl: ACTH and TSH deficiency impair free-water excretion.

answers.name: Legionella pneumonia
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia is a classic laboratory feature of Legionnaires disease.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids can cause SIADH, especially in perioperative and cancer pain settings.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: High-dose IV cyclophosphamide impairs free-water excretion, so aggressive hydration can cause hyponatremia.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents can cause hyponatremia through renal salt wasting or SIADH.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: High-dose TMP-SMX can cause hyponatremia through trimethoprim's amiloride-like ENaC blockade.

answers.name: TURP syndrome
answers.pearl: Absorption of hypotonic glycine or sorbitol irrigant during transurethral prostatectomy or hysteroscopy causes acute hyponatremia.

answers.name: Rocky Mountain spotted fever
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia is a common laboratory finding in RMSF along with thrombocytopenia and elevated transaminases.

answers.name: Acute intermittent porphyria
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia from SIADH or hypothalamic involvement accompanies acute porphyric attacks.

answers.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin
answers.pearl: High-dose IVIG can lower measured sodium via protein-induced translocational or pseudohyponatremia.

answers.name: Nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis
answers.pearl: An activating AVPR2 mutation causes SIADH physiology with undetectable vasopressin.

answers.name: Cerebral salt wasting
answers.pearl: Distinguished from SIADH by hypovolemia; treatment is volume repletion rather than fluid restriction.

answers.name: Reset osmostat
answers.pearl: The osmotic threshold for ADH release is lowered, so sodium is stable at a lower setpoint; seen in pregnancy, TB, and malnutrition.

answers.name: Pseudohyponatremia
answers.pearl: Extreme hypertriglyceridemia or hyperproteinemia can lower measured sodium with normal serum osmolality when using indirect ion-selective electrodes.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of acute pancreatitis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: hypothermia, methanol, Cryptosporidium (case-report level), SPINK1 (modifier more than sole cause), ACE inhibitors and DPP-4 inhibitors (weak association), thiazides, autoimmune pancreatitis (more often chronic or mass-like), ischemia, pregnancy (usually via gallstones or hypertriglyceridemia), asparaginase and propofol, COVID-19.

answers.name: Gallstones
answers.pearl: Gallstones are the most common cause worldwide; an ALT above 150 suggests a biliary etiology.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Alcohol is typically the second most common cause and usually requires years of heavy use.

answers.name: Hypertriglyceridemia
answers.pearl: Triglycerides above about 1000 mg/dL can precipitate pancreatitis.

answers.name: Medications
answers.pearl: Drug-induced pancreatitis accounts for a small percentage of cases; diagnosis is made after excluding other causes.

answers.name: Post-ERCP pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Rectal indomethacin and pancreatic duct stenting reduce risk in high-risk patients.

answers.name: Trauma
answers.pearl: Blunt abdominal injury, such as handlebar injuries in children, can injure the pancreas.

answers.name: Idiopathic
answers.pearl: About 10-20% of cases remain without a cause after standard evaluation, including endoscopic ultrasound.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia, often from hyperparathyroidism, can trigger intrapancreatic trypsinogen activation.

answers.name: Viral infection
answers.pearl: Several viruses can cause pancreatitis, including mumps, coxsackievirus, CMV, and HIV.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer
answers.pearl: Tumor obstruction of the pancreatic duct can present as acute pancreatitis, especially in older adults without another cause.

answers.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
answers.pearl: Incretin-based drugs carry a labeled warning for pancreatitis, though causality remains debated.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate pancreatitis can be severe and recur on rechallenge.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Pancreatitis typically occurs within the first weeks of therapy and recurs with rechallenge.

answers.name: Mumps
answers.pearl: Mumps virus is a classic infectious cause of pancreatitis and parotitis.

answers.name: Postoperative pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Cardiopulmonary bypass and abdominal surgery can cause pancreatic hypoperfusion or manipulation injury.

answers.name: Biliary sludge
answers.pearl: Microlithiasis and sludge can cause pancreatitis when no stones are seen on imaging.

answers.name: Ischemia
answers.pearl: Hypoperfusion from shock or vascular disease can cause pancreatic injury.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV infection, opportunistic pathogens, and antiretroviral drugs can all contribute.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Pregnancy-associated pancreatitis is usually due to gallstones or hypertriglyceridemia in the third trimester.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Pancreatitis occurs mainly in pancreatic-sufficient patients with CFTR mutations.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides are a documented but infrequent cause of drug-induced pancreatitis.

answers.name: Hereditary pancreatitis
answers.pearl: PRSS1 gain-of-function mutations cause recurrent attacks beginning in childhood and carry high pancreatic cancer risk.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with acute pancreatitis, though most cases involve other contributors.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors rarely cause pancreatitis, possibly via angioedema of the pancreas.

answers.name: DPP-4 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Gliptins such as sitagliptin have been linked to pancreatitis in case reports and pharmacovigilance data.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: DKA can cause pancreatitis through hypertriglyceridemia, and enzymes may rise without true pancreatitis.

answers.name: Estrogen therapy
answers.pearl: Oral estrogens can raise triglycerides sharply in patients with underlying lipid disorders.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus
answers.pearl: CMV is an opportunistic cause of pancreatitis in immunocompromised patients.

answers.name: Ampullary tumor
answers.pearl: Obstruction at the ampulla can cause recurrent pancreatitis, including in older adults without stones.

answers.name: Autoimmune pancreatitis
answers.pearl: IgG4-related disease can present with an acute episode, though it more often presents as painless jaundice with a mass.

answers.name: Penetrating peptic ulcer
answers.pearl: A posterior duodenal ulcer can penetrate into the pancreas.

answers.name: Propofol
answers.pearl: Propofol can cause hypertriglyceridemia, especially with prolonged infusions.

answers.name: Asparaginase
answers.pearl: Asparaginase and pegaspargase cause pancreatitis in a notable fraction of pediatric ALL patients.

answers.name: Ascariasis
answers.pearl: Ascaris worms can migrate into the biliary or pancreatic duct, especially in endemic regions.

answers.name: Hypothermia
answers.pearl: Pancreatitis has been reported with accidental hypothermia and exposure.

answers.name: Scorpion sting
answers.pearl: Tityus trinitatis envenomation in Trinidad is a well-known cause of pancreatitis.

answers.name: Methanol poisoning
answers.pearl: Methanol intoxication has been associated with acute pancreatitis.

answers.name: SPINK1 mutation
answers.pearl: SPINK1 variants lower the threshold for premature trypsin activation and act as disease modifiers.

answers.name: Cryptosporidiosis
answers.pearl: Opportunistic infections in advanced AIDS, including Cryptosporidium, can cause pancreatitis or papillary stenosis.

answers.name: Pancreas divisum
answers.pearl: Common anatomical variant (about 7%) that is rarely the sole cause and is debated as an independent risk factor.

answers.name: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction
answers.pearl: Considered mainly in unexplained recurrent pancreatitis, and a diagnosis of exclusion.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of eosinophilia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: interstitial nephritis (blood eosinophilia inconsistent; eosinophiluria more classic), nitrofurantoin (more eosinophilic lung disease), cholesterol emboli, checkpoint inhibitors, CML, T-cell lymphoma, Omenn syndrome and Hyper-IgE (eosinophilia variable), eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome (historic L-tryptophan outbreak), Angiostrongylus (CSF eosinophilia more than blood), adrenal insufficiency (mild).

answers.name: Parasitic infection
answers.pearl: Tissue-invasive helminths drive the highest eosinophil counts; protozoa generally do not.

answers.name: Asthma
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic asthma responds to inhaled steroids and biologics such as anti-IL-5 therapy.

answers.name: Allergic rhinitis
answers.pearl: Atopic conditions typically cause mild to moderate eosinophilia.

answers.name: Drug hypersensitivity
answers.pearl: Many drugs can cause eosinophilia, often with rash and fever.

answers.name: Atopic dermatitis
answers.pearl: Eczema is commonly associated with elevated IgE and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Food allergy
answers.pearl: IgE-mediated food allergy is associated with eosinophilia and eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease.
