answers.name: Strongyloidiasis
answers.pearl: Chronic Strongyloides infection can persist for decades and cause fatal hyperinfection with steroids.

answers.name: Penicillins
answers.pearl: Beta-lactam antibiotics are among the most common drug causes of eosinophilia.

answers.name: Eosinophilic esophagitis
answers.pearl: EoE is defined by 15 or more eosinophils per high-power field in esophageal biopsies and often has little peripheral eosinophilia.

answers.name: Ascariasis
answers.pearl: Ascaris larvae passing through the lungs can cause transient pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophilia.

answers.name: DRESS syndrome
aliases: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
answers.pearl: DRESS develops 2-8 weeks after drug exposure, with rash, fever, organ involvement, and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Hookworm infection
answers.pearl: Hookworm causes iron deficiency anemia and eosinophilia in endemic areas.

answers.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
answers.pearl: ABPA complicates asthma and cystic fibrosis with high IgE and central bronchiectasis.

answers.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
answers.pearl: Defined by an eosinophil count above 1500/uL for over 6 months with end-organ damage and no secondary cause.

answers.name: Eosinophilic pneumonia
answers.pearl: Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia shows peripheral lung infiltrates and responds dramatically to steroids.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever) produces marked eosinophilia.

answers.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia is seen in a minority of Hodgkin lymphoma patients, mediated by IL-5 from Reed-Sternberg cells.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Allopurinol is a common trigger of DRESS, especially in patients with HLA-B*58:01.

answers.name: Acute interstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Drug-induced AIN may show eosinophilia and pyuria, though urine eosinophils are neither sensitive nor specific.

answers.name: Filariasis
answers.pearl: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia is a hypersensitivity response to filarial antigens and responds to diethylcarbamazine.

answers.name: Anticonvulsants
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine, phenytoin, and phenobarbital are common causes of DRESS.

answers.name: Trichinellosis
answers.pearl: Muscle pain, periorbital edema, and marked eosinophilia follow ingestion of undercooked pork or game.

answers.name: Toxocariasis
answers.pearl: Visceral larva migrans from dog or cat roundworm can cause eosinophilia and hepatic lesions in children.

answers.name: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic infiltration of the GI wall can cause abdominal pain, ascites, or obstruction.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Nitrofurantoin can cause eosinophilic lung disease in acute or chronic forms.

answers.name: Chronic myeloid leukemia
answers.pearl: Basophilia is typical of CML, and eosinophilia is a recognized feature.

answers.name: Echinococcosis
answers.pearl: Hydatid cysts may cause eosinophilia, especially after leak or rupture.

answers.name: T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia from IL-5 secretion is recognized in T-cell lymphomas, including cutaneous forms.

answers.name: Bullous pemphigoid
answers.pearl: Peripheral eosinophilia is common in bullous pemphigoid and tissue eosinophils fill the blister fluid.

answers.name: Cholesterol emboli
answers.pearl: Atheroembolic renal disease can cause eosinophilia and eosinophiluria weeks after vascular procedures.

answers.name: Onchocerciasis
answers.pearl: River blindness causes eosinophilia, skin disease, and ocular involvement; ivermectin is treatment.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia occurs in a subset of mastocytosis patients, especially with associated clonal neoplasms.

answers.name: Coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia is seen in a notable fraction of acute pulmonary or disseminated coccidioidomycosis cases.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia can accompany immune-related adverse events and may signal response in some cancers.

answers.name: Eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome
answers.pearl: An epidemic in 1989 was linked to contaminated L-tryptophan supplements.

answers.name: Hyper-IgE syndrome
answers.pearl: Job syndrome features recurrent staph skin and lung infections, eczema, and eosinophilia from STAT3 mutations.

answers.name: Angiostrongylus
answers.pearl: Rat lungworm causes eosinophilic meningitis after ingestion of raw snails or slugs.

answers.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia
answers.pearl: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion defines a subset that responds to imatinib.

answers.name: Omenn syndrome
answers.pearl: A leaky form of severe combined immunodeficiency with erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Asthma, eosinophilia, neuropathy, and vasculitis; ANCA is positive in about 40%.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Loss of cortisol can cause mild eosinophilia, and steroid replacement reverses it.

answers.name: Loeffler syndrome
answers.pearl: Transient pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophilia during larval migration of Ascaris, hookworm, or Strongyloides.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of an elevated troponin other than plaque-rupture myocardial infarction.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: carbon monoxide, neurogenic stunned myocardium, inflammatory myopathy (more cTnT than cTnI), pulmonary hypertension, endocarditis (emboli or abscess), Chagas (acute phase), Kounis syndrome, scorpion sting, heterophile interference, macrotroponin, radiofrequency ablation, coronary embolism; peripartum cardiomyopathy scored as trap.

answers.name: Demand ischemia
answers.pearl: Type 2 MI results from supply-demand mismatch without plaque rupture, e.g. tachycardia, hypotension, anemia, or hypoxemia.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Chronically elevated baseline troponin is common in advanced kidney disease, so delta changes matter.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Wall stress and myocyte injury cause chronic low-level troponin elevation that predicts outcomes.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Troponin elevation is common in sepsis and carries worse prognosis.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Troponin rises with right ventricular strain and signals higher risk.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Troponin is typically markedly elevated with preserved coronary arteries.

answers.name: Tachyarrhythmias
aliases: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
answers.pearl: Rapid rates increase demand and may cause myocyte injury.

answers.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Apical ballooning triggered by emotional or physical stress, with a modest troponin rise relative to wall motion abnormality.

answers.name: Hypertensive emergency
answers.pearl: Severe hypertension raises afterload and wall stress, causing myocardial injury.

answers.name: Cardiac arrest
answers.pearl: CPR and ischemia-reperfusion injury raise troponin after arrest.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Coronary ostial involvement or hypertension can raise troponin, which can mislead toward ACS.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Low output states cause myocardial ischemia and injury.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Epicardial inflammation can raise troponin, often termed myopericarditis.

answers.name: Cardiac contusion
answers.pearl: Blunt chest trauma can injure myocardium, and a normal troponin plus ECG helps exclude clinically important injury.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Severe AS increases wall stress and subendocardial ischemia.

answers.name: Respiratory failure
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia during COPD exacerbation or other acute respiratory failure causes injury.

answers.name: Electrical cardioversion
answers.pearl: Direct current shocks release small amounts of troponin.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Acute stroke, particularly intracerebral and subarachnoid hemorrhage, can raise troponin through catecholamine surges.

answers.name: Severe anemia
answers.pearl: Reduced oxygen delivery with compensatory tachycardia can cause demand injury.

answers.name: Cardiac surgery
answers.pearl: Troponin rises after CABG or valve surgery from surgical injury and cardioplegia.

answers.name: Chemotherapy cardiotoxicity
answers.pearl: Anthracyclines and trastuzumab can cause myocyte injury detectable by troponin.

answers.name: Stimulant use
answers.pearl: Cocaine and amphetamines raise demand, vasospasm, and thrombosis risk and can cause direct myocardial toxicity.

answers.name: Extreme exercise
answers.pearl: Marathon and ultra-endurance events cause transient troponin elevations in many healthy athletes.

answers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Outflow obstruction, microvascular ischemia, and myocardial disarray can raise troponin chronically.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: Myocardial injury in COVID-19 predicts worse outcomes and has multiple mechanisms.

answers.name: Myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery
answers.pearl: Perioperative troponin elevation is usually asymptomatic and associated with higher 30-day mortality.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: RV pressure overload and wall stress can elevate troponin and predict outcomes.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Septic coronary emboli, valve ring abscess, or sepsis can raise troponin.

answers.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposition causes persistently elevated troponin that carries prognostic weight.

answers.name: Cardiac sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration may raise troponin and cause arrhythmia or heart block.

answers.name: Radiofrequency ablation
answers.pearl: Ablation intentionally injures myocardium and releases troponin.

answers.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
answers.pearl: CO binds hemoglobin and myoglobin and causes myocardial injury, which predicts outcomes.

answers.name: Coronary embolism
answers.pearl: Cardiogenic emboli from atrial fibrillation, endocarditis, or valve thrombus can occlude normal coronaries.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis
answers.pearl: Fulminant myocarditis is rare but carries high mortality, often with myositis overlap.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surges can cause stress cardiomyopathy or direct myocyte toxicity.

answers.name: Inflammatory myopathy
answers.pearl: Troponin T can be elevated by regenerating skeletal muscle, whereas troponin I is more specific.

answers.name: Neurogenic stunned myocardium
answers.pearl: Intracranial injury can cause catecholamine-mediated myocardial stunning.

answers.name: Heterophile antibody interference
answers.pearl: Heterophile antibodies or rheumatoid factor can produce false-positive immunoassay troponin results with an unchanging value.

answers.name: Kounis syndrome
answers.pearl: Allergic acute coronary syndrome occurs from mast-cell mediator release during allergic reaction.

answers.name: Scorpion sting
answers.pearl: Scorpion envenomation can cause catecholamine-mediated myocardial injury and acute pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Chagas disease
answers.pearl: Acute and chronic Chagas myocarditis can cause cardiac injury in patients from Latin America.

answers.name: Macrotroponin
answers.pearl: Troponin bound to autoantibodies forms complexes that are cleared slowly, causing persistent isolated elevation.

answers.name: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
answers.pearl: Typically occurs in younger women without atherosclerosis, and is associated with fibromuscular dysplasia.

answers.name: Coronary vasospasm
answers.pearl: Variant angina with transient ST elevation from coronary spasm that can raise troponin.

answers.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Systolic dysfunction presents late in pregnancy to 5 months postpartum, with bromocriptine investigated as adjunct therapy.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of syncope.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: postprandial hypotension, pulmonary hypertension, WPW (arrhythmic via pre-excited AF), subarachnoid hemorrhage (usually presents with headache), vertebrobasilar insufficiency (rarely isolated syncope), mastocytosis (case-level), baroreflex failure, pure autonomic failure, alcohol intoxication, hypoglycemia (usually a mimic rather than true syncope), nitrates.

answers.name: Vasovagal syncope
answers.pearl: The most common cause of syncope in young patients, typically triggered by pain, emotion, or prolonged standing with a prodrome.

answers.name: Orthostatic hypotension
answers.pearl: Defined as a drop in systolic BP of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion lowers preload and is a common contributor, especially in elderly patients.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Cardiac syncope has higher mortality than other causes and is often abrupt without prodrome.

answers.name: Antihypertensive medications
answers.pearl: Drugs lowering blood pressure are a leading cause of syncope in older adults, with polypharmacy as a major risk.

answers.name: Bradycardia
answers.pearl: Beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, and digoxin can cause significant bradycardia.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Exertional syncope is one of the classic symptoms and signals severe disease.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Hypoglycemia mimics syncope but rarely causes true transient global cerebral hypoperfusion.

answers.name: Ventricular tachycardia
answers.pearl: Sustained VT in structural heart disease or scar is an important cause of cardiac syncope.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Syncope may be the only presenting symptom in PE and reflects large clot burden.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Reduced oxygen delivery lowers cerebral perfusion during hemodynamic stress.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
answers.pearl: Occult GI hemorrhage can present as syncope without obvious melena.

answers.name: Myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Acute MI can cause syncope via arrhythmia, low output, or vagal reflex.

answers.name: Situational syncope
answers.pearl: Triggers include cough, micturition, defecation, swallowing, and laughing, mediated by reflex mechanisms.

answers.name: Diuretics
answers.pearl: Volume depletion and electrolyte shifts from diuretics predispose to syncope.

answers.name: Atrioventricular block
answers.pearl: High-grade or complete AV block causes abrupt syncope, sometimes called Stokes-Adams attacks.

answers.name: Sick sinus syndrome
answers.pearl: Sinus pauses and tachy-brady syndrome are classic causes in older adults.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Vasodilation and volume depletion in sepsis can cause syncope, especially in elderly patients.

answers.name: Alcohol intoxication
answers.pearl: Alcohol causes vasodilation and volume depletion and can impair autonomic reflexes.

answers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Exertional syncope in a young athlete should prompt echocardiography to exclude HCM.

answers.name: Long QT syndrome
answers.pearl: QT prolongation predisposes to torsades de pointes causing syncope or sudden death.

answers.name: Alpha blockers
answers.pearl: Alpha blockers such as tamsulosin and doxazosin cause orthostatic hypotension, especially after the first dose.

answers.name: Nitrates
answers.pearl: Nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors cause venodilation with hypotension, particularly in combination.

answers.name: Anaphylaxis
answers.pearl: Vasodilation and distributive shock from anaphylaxis can cause syncope, usually with urticaria or wheeze.

answers.name: QT-prolonging drugs
answers.pearl: Macrolides, fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics, and antiemetics can precipitate torsades.

answers.name: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome
answers.pearl: POTS is a sustained heart rate increase of at least 30 bpm on standing without orthostatic hypotension, typically in young women.

answers.name: Cardiac tamponade
answers.pearl: Hypotension from impaired filling can cause syncope; look for Beck triad and pulsus paradoxus.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Syncope can occur from tamponade, rupture, or carotid involvement and is associated with worse outcomes.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Fixed low cardiac output with exertion can cause syncope in PAH.

answers.name: Autonomic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Diabetic and other autonomic neuropathies impair vasoconstriction and cause orthostatic syncope.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol and mineralocorticoid deficiency cause hypotension and volume depletion.

answers.name: Postprandial hypotension
answers.pearl: Splanchnic pooling after meals lowers blood pressure in older patients.

answers.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
answers.pearl: Pre-excited atrial fibrillation with rapid conduction over an accessory pathway can cause syncope or sudden death.

answers.name: Vertebrobasilar insufficiency
answers.pearl: Brainstem hypoperfusion typically comes with vertigo, diplopia, or ataxia rather than isolated syncope.

answers.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Transient loss of consciousness at onset occurs in a notable fraction of patients with SAH.

answers.name: Multiple system atrophy
answers.pearl: Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension appears early in MSA, with parkinsonism or cerebellar features.

answers.name: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Fibrofatty replacement of RV myocardium causes ventricular arrhythmias with syncope or sudden death.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surges followed by profound hypotension can cause syncope, with paroxysmal headache and sweating.

answers.name: Left atrial myxoma
answers.pearl: A mobile tumor can obstruct mitral inflow, causing positional syncope.

answers.name: Pure autonomic failure
answers.pearl: Autonomic failure without CNS involvement, with supine hypertension and orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
answers.pearl: Exertion or emotion triggers bidirectional VT from RYR2 mutations in structurally normal hearts.

answers.name: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
answers.pearl: Throat pain triggered by swallowing may be accompanied by bradycardia and syncope via vagal outflow.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Mast cell mediator release can cause flushing, hypotension, and syncope.

answers.name: Baroreflex failure
answers.pearl: Neck radiation or surgery can damage baroreceptors, causing labile BP and recurrent syncope.

answers.name: Brugada syndrome
answers.pearl: SCN5A channelopathy with coved ST elevation in V1-V2 and risk of ventricular fibrillation.

answers.name: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity
answers.pearl: A pause of 3 seconds or more or a 50 mmHg systolic drop during carotid sinus massage suggests the diagnosis.

answers.name: Subclavian steal syndrome
answers.pearl: Subclavian stenosis proximal to the vertebral origin causes retrograde vertebral flow and arm-exercise symptoms.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of ascites.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: portal vein thrombosis (ascites mainly with cirrhosis), IVC obstruction, SLE serositis, dialysis-associated (nephrogenic) ascites, ovarian hyperstimulation, biliary ascites, protein-losing enteropathy (indirect via low albumin), nodular regenerative hyperplasia, eosinophilic gastroenteritis, struma ovarii, schistosomiasis (via portal hypertension), lymphoma (portal hypertension or chylous ascites), acute liver failure.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis is responsible for about 75% of ascites, and a SAAG of 1.1 or more reflects portal hypertension.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Right-sided congestion produces high-SAAG ascites with high ascitic protein.

answers.name: Alcoholic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Severe alcoholic hepatitis can cause ascites through sinusoidal hypertension even without established cirrhosis.

answers.name: Peritoneal carcinomatosis
answers.pearl: Peritoneal metastases cause low-SAAG ascites; cytology is positive in most cases.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Low oncotic pressure and sodium retention cause low-SAAG ascites.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: HCC in a cirrhotic liver can cause ascites via portal vein invasion or decompensation.

answers.name: Ovarian cancer
answers.pearl: Ovarian carcinoma can cause ascites via peritoneal seeding and is a common cause of malignant ascites in women.

answers.name: Chronic viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Hepatitis B and C are leading global causes of cirrhosis and thus ascites.

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Malnutrition or protein loss lowers oncotic pressure and contributes to transudative ascites.

answers.name: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
answers.pearl: NASH-related cirrhosis is a rapidly growing cause of ascites in Western countries.

answers.name: Tuberculous peritonitis
answers.pearl: Ascites in TB peritonitis is lymphocyte-predominant with elevated ADA.

answers.name: Liver metastases
answers.pearl: Extensive hepatic metastases can cause portal hypertension and ascites.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer
answers.pearl: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma can cause ascites through peritoneal spread or portal vein compression.

answers.name: Cor pulmonale
answers.pearl: Right heart strain from lung disease or pulmonary hypertension causes systemic venous congestion.

answers.name: Pancreatic ascites
answers.pearl: Pancreatic duct disruption causes amylase-rich ascites with protein above 3 g/dL.

answers.name: Gastric cancer
answers.pearl: Diffuse gastric cancer commonly spreads to the peritoneum and ovaries (Krukenberg tumors).

answers.name: Acute liver failure
answers.pearl: Fulminant hepatitis can cause acute ascites, particularly with Budd-Chiari or veno-occlusive injury.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Lymphomatous involvement of the peritoneum or lymphatics causes ascites, sometimes chylous.

answers.name: Portal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Acute thrombosis can cause ascites, and chronic thrombosis commonly accompanies cirrhosis.

answers.name: Tricuspid regurgitation
answers.pearl: Severe TR causes systemic venous congestion and hepatic congestion with ascites.

answers.name: Dialysis-associated ascites
answers.pearl: Nephrogenic ascites occurs in patients on long-term dialysis, with protein-rich ascites and no other cause.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Myxedema ascites is rare and protein-rich, resolving with thyroid replacement.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus serositis can produce exudative ascites and peritoneal inflammation.

answers.name: Protein-losing enteropathy
answers.pearl: GI protein loss lowers albumin and can cause transudative ascites.

answers.name: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
answers.pearl: Fertility treatment with hCG causes capillary leak, ascites, and hemoconcentration.

answers.name: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic veno-occlusive disease follows stem cell transplant or pyrrolizidine alkaloid exposure with painful hepatomegaly and ascites.

answers.name: Inferior vena cava obstruction
answers.pearl: Membranous or thrombotic IVC obstruction at the hepatic level can mimic Budd-Chiari.

answers.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Restrictive physiology causes right-sided congestion and ascites.

answers.name: Peritoneal mesothelioma
answers.pearl: A rare cancer that causes ascites and is linked with asbestos exposure.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis causes presinusoidal portal hypertension in endemic regions.

answers.name: Biliary ascites
answers.pearl: Bile leak after surgery or trauma causes bilirubin-rich ascites, with fluid bilirubin exceeding serum.

answers.name: Pseudomyxoma peritonei
answers.pearl: Mucinous tumors, usually from the appendix, fill the peritoneum with gelatinous ascites.

answers.name: Nodular regenerative hyperplasia
answers.pearl: A cause of noncirrhotic portal hypertension associated with autoimmune disease and some drugs.

answers.name: Urinary ascites
answers.pearl: Bladder or ureteral rupture leaks urine into the peritoneum, raising creatinine in ascitic fluid above serum.

answers.name: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
answers.pearl: Serosal-predominant disease causes eosinophil-rich ascites with peripheral eosinophilia.

answers.name: Fontan-associated liver disease
answers.pearl: Chronic venous congestion after the Fontan operation leads to fibrosis, portal hypertension, and ascites.

answers.name: Struma ovarii
answers.pearl: A thyroid-containing ovarian teratoma can cause ascites and pleural effusion, sometimes as pseudo-Meigs syndrome.

answers.name: Meigs syndrome
answers.pearl: Benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion that resolves after tumor resection.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic vein outflow obstruction causes painful hepatomegaly and ascites, often from a hypercoagulable state.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis
answers.pearl: Elevated JVP with Kussmaul sign and a pericardial knock; ascites can precede peripheral edema.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can prolong the QT interval.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: trazodone, tacrolimus, proton pump inhibitors, loop/thiazide diuretics (indirect, via K/Mg), dronedarone, donepezil (listed risk categories vary by source), domperidone (not US-marketed), probucol/halofantrine (withdrawn), olanzapine deliberately omitted from atypicals.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone markedly prolongs QT yet rarely causes torsades because it also blocks other channels.

answers.name: Haloperidol
answers.pearl: IV haloperidol carries a higher torsades risk than oral dosing.

answers.name: Ondansetron
answers.pearl: Ondansetron prolongs QT in a dose-dependent way, so use small IV doses when other risk factors are present.

answers.name: Sotalol
answers.pearl: Sotalol's class III effect is dose dependent and torsades risk rises with renal impairment and bradycardia.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Moxifloxacin has the largest QT effect among commonly used fluoroquinolones and ciprofloxacin the least.

answers.name: Macrolide antibiotics
answers.pearl: Erythromycin and clarithromycin also inhibit CYP3A4, raising levels of other QT-prolonging drugs.

answers.name: Methadone
answers.pearl: Methadone prolongs QT in a dose-dependent manner and an ECG is advised before and after dose escalation.

answers.name: Citalopram
answers.pearl: FDA caps citalopram at 40 mg/day (20 mg/day over age 60 or with hepatic impairment) because of dose-dependent QT prolongation.

answers.name: Atypical antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Ziprasidone has among the largest QT effects of the atypicals and is avoided with other QT-prolonging drugs.

answers.name: Azole antifungals
answers.pearl: Azoles prolong QT directly and by inhibiting CYP3A4, which raises levels of other QT-prolonging drugs.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: QT risk with hydroxychloroquine drew attention in COVID-19, especially combined with azithromycin.

answers.name: Dofetilide
answers.pearl: Dofetilide must be started in hospital with telemetry and renally adjusted dosing.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs prolong QRS and QT, especially in overdose.

answers.name: Loop and thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Diuretics predispose to torsades indirectly by causing hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Chlorpromazine
answers.pearl: Phenothiazines such as chlorpromazine prolong QT by blocking IKr.

answers.name: Procainamide
answers.pearl: Class IA agents like procainamide prolong QT and can cause torsades, particularly with high levels from renal failure (NAPA metabolite).

answers.name: Ibutilide
answers.pearl: Ibutilide for chemical cardioversion carries a notable torsades risk and requires several hours of monitoring.

answers.name: Droperidol
answers.pearl: Droperidol carries an FDA boxed warning for QT prolongation, which curtailed its use for nausea and sedation.

answers.name: Thioridazine
answers.pearl: Thioridazine has a boxed warning for dose-related QTc prolongation and is reserved for refractory schizophrenia.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone is contraindicated in permanent atrial fibrillation and decompensated heart failure and can prolong QT.

answers.name: Trazodone
answers.pearl: Trazodone's QT effect is mainly seen at higher doses or with other risk factors.

answers.name: Disopyramide
answers.pearl: Disopyramide is a class IA antiarrhythmic that also has strong anticholinergic effects.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Long-term PPI use can cause hypomagnesemia, which indirectly raises the risk of QT prolongation and torsades.

answers.name: Loperamide
answers.pearl: High-dose loperamide misuse for opioid withdrawal or euphoria causes QT prolongation, torsades and death.

answers.name: Pimozide
answers.pearl: Pimozide is contraindicated with macrolides and azoles because CYP3A4 inhibition raises levels and QT risk.

answers.name: Donepezil
answers.pearl: Donepezil is a recognized torsades-risk drug, with bradycardia contributing.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: IV pentamidine can cause QT prolongation and torsades; aerosolized dosing has little systemic effect.

answers.name: Arsenic trioxide
answers.pearl: Arsenic trioxide for acute promyelocytic leukemia carries a boxed warning, with potassium and magnesium repleted before each dose.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus can prolong QT, especially with electrolyte disturbances or CYP3A4 inhibitors.

answers.name: Domperidone
answers.pearl: Domperidone is not FDA-approved in the US and is linked to QT prolongation and sudden cardiac death.

answers.name: Nilotinib
answers.pearl: Nilotinib carries a boxed warning for QT prolongation and sudden death; it is taken fasting and avoided with CYP3A4 inhibitors.

answers.name: Bedaquiline
answers.pearl: Bedaquiline for multidrug-resistant TB prolongs QT, and the effect is additive with clofazimine and fluoroquinolones.

answers.name: Vandetanib
answers.pearl: Vandetanib for medullary thyroid cancer has a boxed warning for QT prolongation, torsades and sudden death.

answers.name: Ribociclib
answers.pearl: Ribociclib requires an ECG and electrolytes at baseline and during treatment.

answers.name: Anagrelide
answers.pearl: Anagrelide for essential thrombocythemia can prolong QT and cause tachyarrhythmias; get a baseline ECG.

answers.name: Toremifene
answers.pearl: Toremifene has a boxed warning for dose-related QT prolongation.

answers.name: Halofantrine
answers.pearl: Halofantrine, an antimalarial no longer marketed in the US, causes marked QT prolongation and sudden death.

answers.name: Probucol
answers.pearl: Probucol, a withdrawn lipid-lowering drug, was notable for marked QT prolongation and torsades.

answers.name: Cisapride
answers.pearl: Cisapride was withdrawn in the US for QT prolongation and torsades, especially with CYP3A4 inhibitors.

answers.name: Terfenadine
answers.pearl: Terfenadine was withdrawn after torsades occurred when metabolism was blocked by macrolides or azoles.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine syncope from torsades is a classic example of drug-induced long QT.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hyponatremia or SIADH.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: sulfonylureas as a class, lamotrigine, interferons, intravenous immunoglobulin (pseudo/translocational mechanism), glycine irrigation (not a drug per se), clofibrate (withdrawn), mannitol (translocational), terlipressin, trazodone; ACE inhibitors, valproate and tramadol kept at plankton tier but rely on labeling/case-report data.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause hyponatremia far more often than loop diuretics, typically within weeks of starting, especially in older women.

answers.name: SSRIs and SNRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs and SNRIs cause SIADH, usually within the first weeks, with highest risk in older adults, women and those on diuretics.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Oxcarbazepine causes hyponatremia more often than carbamazepine, and the effect is dose-related.

answers.name: Desmopressin
answers.pearl: Desmopressin for nocturia or enuresis can cause severe hyponatremia, so serum sodium is checked after starting.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Antipsychotics cause SIADH and are also associated with primary polydipsia.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs cause SIADH, with risk highest in older adults.

answers.name: Oxytocin
answers.pearl: Oxytocin has antidiuretic activity, and large volumes of hypotonic fluid during induction can cause water intoxication.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents cause hyponatremia through SIADH and renal salt wasting.

answers.name: MDMA
answers.pearl: MDMA causes vasopressin release plus compulsive water drinking, producing severe hyponatremia.

answers.name: Hypotonic intravenous fluids
answers.pearl: Hypotonic maintenance fluids in postoperative or hospitalized patients with non-osmotic ADH release cause hospital-acquired hyponatremia.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids stimulate ADH release and can cause SIADH.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs potentiate ADH action in the collecting duct and reduce free-water excretion.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics cause hyponatremia less often than thiazides because they impair medullary concentrating ability.

answers.name: Vasopressin
answers.pearl: Exogenous vasopressin directly causes water retention and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Mirtazapine has been associated with hyponatremia, particularly in older adults.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Tramadol labeling warns of hyponatremia and SIADH.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors have been associated with hyponatremia, particularly in older patients and those on diuretics.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Valproate has been reported to cause SIADH.

answers.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
answers.pearl: Potassium-sparing diuretics cause renal sodium loss and can produce hyponatremia, particularly in combination with thiazides.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: High-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole used for Pneumocystis pneumonia is a recognized cause of hyponatremia.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide can cause SIADH and renal tubular injury with sodium wasting.

answers.name: Trazodone
answers.pearl: Trazodone, like other serotonergic antidepressants, can cause SIADH.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone has been reported to cause SIADH, including with intravenous loading.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Lamotrigine has been reported to cause hyponatremia, though much less commonly than carbamazepine.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: PPIs have been associated with hyponatremia in case reports and large observational studies.

answers.name: Sulfonylureas
answers.pearl: Sulfonylureas other than chlorpropamide have also been reported to cause SIADH, though less commonly.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Mannitol and other osmotically active solutes pull water out of cells and lower measured serum sodium (translocational hyponatremia).

answers.name: Terlipressin
answers.pearl: Terlipressin, a vasopressin analog used in hepatorenal syndrome, can cause hyponatremia.

answers.name: Interferons
answers.pearl: Interferons have been reported to cause SIADH.

answers.name: Melphalan
answers.pearl: Alkylating agents beyond cyclophosphamide, including melphalan, can cause SIADH.

answers.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin
answers.pearl: IVIG can cause pseudohyponatremia from hyperproteinemia or translocational hyponatremia from sucrose-containing products.

answers.name: Clofibrate
answers.pearl: Clofibrate stimulates ADH release or action and was a classic cause of drug-induced SIADH.

answers.name: Glycine irrigation
answers.pearl: Absorption of glycine or sorbitol irrigant during TURP produces TURP syndrome with hyponatremia and encephalopathy.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloids cause SIADH, likely by neurotoxic effects on the hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal system.

answers.name: Chlorpropamide
answers.pearl: Chlorpropamide potentiates ADH action at the collecting duct and is the classic sulfonylurea cause of SIADH.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: High-dose IV cyclophosphamide potentiates ADH action, so avoid vigorous hypotonic hydration.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause acute kidney injury.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: statins (via rhabdomyolysis), SGLT2 inhibitors (volume depletion), PPIs (AIN), hydroxyethyl starch (restricted/withdrawn in many regions), sulfadiazine, deferasirox, gallium nitrate, streptozocin, parenteral bacitracin (withdrawn), methoxyflurane (withdrawn), aristolochic acid (herbal).

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs reduce afferent arteriolar prostaglandin-mediated flow and can also cause acute interstitial nephritis.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors cause AKI by dilating the efferent arteriole, especially with bilateral renal artery stenosis or volume depletion.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides cause nonoliguric acute tubular necrosis, with risk rising with duration and trough levels.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Vancomycin nephrotoxicity is more likely with high trough exposure and concurrent piperacillin-tazobactam.

answers.name: Iodinated contrast
answers.pearl: Contrast-associated AKI typically peaks 3 to 5 days after exposure.

answers.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers
answers.pearl: ARBs reduce efferent arteriolar tone like ACE inhibitors and can precipitate AKI in volume depletion.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Over-diuresis causes prerenal AKI.

answers.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
answers.pearl: Piperacillin-tazobactam combined with vancomycin has a higher AKI rate than vancomycin with cefepime.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors cause dose-dependent afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction as well as chronic structural injury.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: High-dose methotrexate crystallizes in acidic urine and delays its own clearance; urinary alkalinization, hydration and leucovorin or glucarpidase mitigate.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim raises creatinine by blocking tubular secretion and can also cause true AKI, interstitial nephritis and hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: PPIs are a leading drug cause of acute interstitial nephritis, which can present with little or no rash or eosinophilia.

answers.name: Beta-lactam antibiotics
answers.pearl: Beta-lactams are a classic cause of acute interstitial nephritis, with methicillin the historical prototype.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause prerenal AKI via volume depletion and can rarely cause interstitial nephritis.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and chronic tubulointerstitial disease, and levels rise with dehydration and NSAIDs.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate causes proximal tubulopathy and Fanconi syndrome; tenofovir alafenamide is less nephrotoxic.

answers.name: Intravenous bisphosphonates
answers.pearl: IV zoledronate and pamidronate can cause tubular injury, and pamidronate is linked to collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

answers.name: Colistin
answers.pearl: Polymyxins cause dose-related tubular injury through increased membrane permeability.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitors cause acute interstitial nephritis, and PPIs may be a risk factor.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones are recognized causes of acute interstitial nephritis.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Allopurinol can cause interstitial nephritis, particularly as part of hypersensitivity syndrome, and oxypurinol accumulates in renal failure.

answers.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
answers.pearl: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause volume-depletion AKI, and an initial eGFR dip is expected.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: 5-ASA products can cause interstitial nephritis, so creatinine should be monitored.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide causes proximal tubulopathy with Fanconi syndrome and AKI.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Foscarnet causes crystal-associated and direct tubular injury, so saline loading is used.

answers.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin
answers.pearl: Sucrose-stabilized IVIG products cause osmotic nephrosis.

answers.name: Sodium phosphate bowel preparation
answers.pearl: Oral sodium phosphate bowel preps cause acute phosphate nephropathy with calcium-phosphate deposition.

answers.name: Hydroxyethyl starch
answers.pearl: Hydroxyethyl starch resuscitation fluids increase AKI and renal replacement therapy in critical illness.

answers.name: Cidofovir
answers.pearl: Cidofovir causes proximal tubular toxicity, so probenecid and saline hydration are given.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Statins can cause AKI through rhabdomyolysis, mainly at high doses or with interacting drugs.

answers.name: Indinavir
answers.pearl: Indinavir forms urinary crystals causing nephrolithiasis and obstructive AKI, so hydration is advised.

answers.name: Pemetrexed
answers.pearl: Pemetrexed is renally cleared and can cause tubular injury; it is avoided at low creatinine clearance.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Gemcitabine can cause thrombotic microangiopathy with AKI.

answers.name: Sulfadiazine
answers.pearl: Sulfadiazine forms crystals in acidic urine, an issue when treating toxoplasmosis.

answers.name: Deferasirox
answers.pearl: Deferasirox has a boxed warning for acute kidney injury, renal tubular injury and Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Bacitracin
answers.pearl: Parenteral bacitracin was withdrawn in the US because it caused dose-related renal tubular necrosis.

answers.name: Methoxyflurane
answers.pearl: Methoxyflurane's fluoride metabolite caused high-output renal failure and ended its clinical use.

answers.name: Streptozocin
answers.pearl: Streptozocin's main dose-limiting toxicity is renal tubular injury.

answers.name: Aristolochic acid
answers.pearl: Aristolochic acid in some herbal remedies causes progressive interstitial nephropathy and urothelial cancer.

answers.name: Gallium nitrate
answers.pearl: Gallium nitrate for cancer-related hypercalcemia had a boxed warning for nephrotoxicity.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin injures proximal tubules, mitigated by saline hydration and magnesium repletion.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin B constricts afferent arterioles and injures tubules, less so with liposomal forms and sodium loading.

answers.name: Acyclovir
answers.pearl: IV acyclovir forms needle-shaped crystals in the tubules, so hydration and slow infusion are advised.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause constipation.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: mecamylamine (obscure; constipation prominent in labeling), lanthanum, patiromer, alosetron, anticonvulsants as a class (carbamazepine/phenytoin), mirtazapine, SNRIs, amantadine, lenalidomide, disopyramide, diuretics (indirect), levodopa/dopamine agonists (partly disease effect).

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioid-induced constipation does not develop tolerance, so a laxative regimen should start with the opioid.

answers.name: Anticholinergics
answers.pearl: Anticholinergics slow gut motility by blocking muscarinic receptors.

answers.name: Iron supplements
answers.pearl: Oral iron commonly causes constipation and dark stools.

answers.name: Calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Calcium channel blockers reduce gut smooth-muscle contraction.

answers.name: Calcium carbonate
answers.pearl: Calcium carbonate antacids and calcium supplements are common contributors to constipation.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs have strong anticholinergic activity that slows gut transit.

answers.name: First-generation antihistamines
answers.pearl: Sedating antihistamines are anticholinergic and a frequent hidden contributor in older adults.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Antipsychotics with anticholinergic activity reduce gut motility.

answers.name: Ondansetron
answers.pearl: 5-HT3 antagonists slow colonic transit, and constipation is one of ondansetron's most common effects.

answers.name: Bile acid sequestrants
answers.pearl: Bile acid sequestrants bind water and cause constipation, and also bind other drugs in the gut.

answers.name: Clonidine
answers.pearl: Clonidine, an alpha-2 agonist, reduces gut motility and secretion.

answers.name: Sucralfate
answers.pearl: Sucralfate contains aluminum, and constipation is its most common adverse effect.

answers.name: Loperamide
answers.pearl: Loperamide is an opioid-receptor agonist in the gut and can cause severe constipation or ileus when overused.

answers.name: Diphenoxylate-atropine
answers.pearl: Diphenoxylate-atropine combines an opioid and an anticholinergic and can cause ileus in overdose.

answers.name: Loop and thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Diuretics contribute to constipation mainly through dehydration and electrolyte changes.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Clozapine can cause severe gastrointestinal hypomotility, including ileus and bowel obstruction, and carries a labeled warning.

answers.name: Cyclobenzaprine
answers.pearl: Cyclobenzaprine is a tricyclic-like muscle relaxant with anticholinergic effects.

answers.name: Levodopa and dopamine agonists
answers.pearl: Dopaminergic Parkinson's disease drugs can add to constipation already caused by the disease itself.

answers.name: Anticonvulsants
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine and phenytoin are associated with constipation among their gastrointestinal effects.

answers.name: Sevelamer
answers.pearl: Sevelamer, a phosphate binder, commonly causes constipation and has been linked to bowel obstruction.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Constipation is a common labeled adverse effect of mirtazapine.

answers.name: SNRIs
answers.pearl: Constipation is a common adverse effect of SNRIs.

answers.name: Amantadine
answers.pearl: Amantadine has anticholinergic properties and constipation is common.

answers.name: Disopyramide
answers.pearl: Disopyramide is strongly anticholinergic, causing constipation, urinary retention and dry mouth.

answers.name: Octreotide
answers.pearl: Somatostatin analogs reduce GI motility and secretion.

answers.name: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate
answers.pearl: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate can cause constipation and, rarely, colonic necrosis, particularly with sorbitol or postoperatively.

answers.name: Thalidomide
answers.pearl: Constipation is a common adverse effect of thalidomide.

answers.name: Lenalidomide
answers.pearl: Constipation is a common labeled adverse effect of lenalidomide.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Bortezomib causes constipation, sometimes severe, through autonomic neuropathy.

answers.name: Alosetron
answers.pearl: Alosetron for severe diarrhea-predominant IBS in women carries a boxed warning for ischemic colitis and serious complications of constipation.

answers.name: Patiromer
answers.pearl: Constipation is the most common adverse effect of the potassium binder patiromer.

answers.name: Lanthanum carbonate
answers.pearl: Lanthanum carbonate, a phosphate binder, commonly causes GI effects including constipation.

answers.name: Mecamylamine
answers.pearl: Ganglionic blockade with mecamylamine causes significant constipation that can progress to ileus.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Verapamil causes constipation more often than other calcium channel blockers.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vincristine causes autonomic neuropathy that can lead to severe constipation or ileus.

answers.name: Aluminum-containing antacids
answers.pearl: Aluminum antacids cause constipation, while magnesium antacids cause diarrhea.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause liver injury.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: oral contraceptives, vitamin A, niacin, chlorpromazine, macrolides, carbamazepine, labetalol, duloxetine, ximelagatran (never US-marketed), bromfenac, troglitazone, pemoline, trovafloxacin (all withdrawn). Pyrazinamide listed separately from isoniazid and rifampin.

answers.name: Acetaminophen
answers.pearl: Acetaminophen is the leading cause of acute liver failure in the US, and N-acetylcysteine is the antidote.

answers.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
answers.pearl: Amoxicillin-clavulanate is the most common single prescription cause of idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury, often cholestatic.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid hepatotoxicity risk rises with age, alcohol use and slow acetylators, so monitor transaminases when risk factors are present.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Statins commonly cause mild transaminase elevations; clinically significant liver injury is rare.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Methotrexate causes dose- and duration-related fibrosis and cirrhosis, with added risk from alcohol, obesity and diabetes.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Valproate can cause hepatotoxicity, particularly in young children with mitochondrial disease such as POLG mutations.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone can cause steatohepatitis resembling alcoholic liver disease, and its long half-life prolongs injury.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Rifampin can cause cholestatic or mixed liver injury, additive with isoniazid and pyrazinamide.

answers.name: Azole antifungals
answers.pearl: Ketoconazole has the greatest hepatotoxicity among the azoles and has a boxed warning against use.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Chronic nitrofurantoin use can cause autoimmune-like hepatitis, and acute reactions include cholestasis.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Phenytoin can cause hypersensitivity hepatitis, sometimes as part of DRESS.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Diclofenac is the NSAID most often linked to clinically significant liver injury.

answers.name: Pyrazinamide
answers.pearl: Pyrazinamide is the most hepatotoxic of the first-line antituberculous drugs.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides can cause cholestatic or mixed hepatitis as part of a hypersensitivity reaction.

answers.name: Anabolic steroids
answers.pearl: 17-alpha-alkylated androgens cause cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and hepatic tumors.

answers.name: Herbal and dietary supplements
answers.pearl: Herbal and dietary supplements are an increasing cause of drug-induced liver injury, including green tea extract and kava.

answers.name: Nevirapine
answers.pearl: Nevirapine hepatotoxicity occurs mostly in the first 18 weeks, with higher risk at higher CD4 counts and in women.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones can cause cholestatic or hepatocellular injury, rarely severe.

answers.name: Macrolide antibiotics
answers.pearl: Erythromycin estolate in particular causes cholestatic hepatitis, and other macrolides can also cause liver injury.

answers.name: Tetracyclines
answers.pearl: Minocycline can cause autoimmune-like hepatitis, and IV tetracyclines cause microvesicular steatosis.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine can cause hypersensitivity hepatitis and cholestatic injury.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Allopurinol hepatotoxicity usually occurs as part of a hypersensitivity syndrome.

answers.name: Chlorpromazine
answers.pearl: Chlorpromazine causes cholestatic hepatitis, typically within the first weeks.

answers.name: Niacin
answers.pearl: High-dose sustained-release niacin carries the highest hepatotoxicity risk among niacin formulations.

answers.name: Pazopanib
answers.pearl: Pazopanib has a boxed warning for severe and fatal hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfasalazine can cause hypersensitivity-type liver injury.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Thiopurines can cause cholestatic injury and sinusoidal obstruction or nodular regenerative hyperplasia.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated hepatitis from checkpoint inhibitors is treated with corticosteroids after ruling out other causes.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil
answers.pearl: Propylthiouracil has a boxed warning for liver failure, so methimazole is preferred except in first-trimester pregnancy.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen-containing contraceptives can cause cholestasis, hepatic adenomas and rarely hepatic vein thrombosis.

answers.name: Labetalol
answers.pearl: Labetalol can cause hepatocellular injury, rarely severe.

answers.name: Disulfiram
answers.pearl: Disulfiram can cause severe idiosyncratic hepatitis, so baseline and periodic liver tests are recommended.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Leflunomide has a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, and cholestyramine washout speeds elimination.

answers.name: Duloxetine
answers.pearl: Duloxetine can cause hepatocellular injury and is avoided in heavy alcohol use or chronic liver disease.

answers.name: Flutamide
answers.pearl: Flutamide has a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, so liver tests are required during use.

answers.name: Bosentan
answers.pearl: Bosentan causes dose-related transaminase elevations, requiring monthly monitoring.

answers.name: Vitamin A
answers.pearl: Chronic vitamin A excess injures hepatic stellate cells, causing fibrosis and cirrhosis.

answers.name: Felbamate
answers.pearl: Felbamate carries boxed warnings for aplastic anemia and hepatic failure.

answers.name: Tolcapone
answers.pearl: Tolcapone has a boxed warning for liver failure, with monitoring of liver tests.

answers.name: Nefazodone
answers.pearl: Nefazodone has a boxed warning for liver failure and was withdrawn in many countries.

answers.name: Troglitazone
answers.pearl: Troglitazone was withdrawn in 2000 after cases of liver failure.

answers.name: Pemoline
answers.pearl: Pemoline was withdrawn because of acute liver failure.

answers.name: Trovafloxacin
answers.pearl: Trovafloxacin was restricted and then withdrawn for severe hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Bromfenac
answers.pearl: Bromfenac was withdrawn within a year of release because of liver failure.

answers.name: Ximelagatran
answers.pearl: Ximelagatran, an oral direct thrombin inhibitor, was never approved in the US because of hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Halothane
answers.pearl: Halothane hepatitis is an immune-mediated reaction, more likely with repeated exposure.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: Methyldopa can cause autoimmune-type hepatitis and a positive Coombs test.

answers.name: Dantrolene
answers.pearl: Chronic oral dantrolene carries a boxed warning for dose-related hepatotoxicity.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause orthostatic hypotension.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: tizanidine, SGLT2 inhibitors (volume effect), sacubitril-valsartan, mirtazapine, duloxetine, spironolactone, dexmedetomidine, thalidomide, bortezomib, vincristine (autonomic neuropathy), quinidine, reserpine, amifostine, mecamylamine. MAOIs include selegiline as an alias (orthostasis is more marked with nonselective agents).

answers.name: Alpha-1 blockers
answers.pearl: Alpha-1 blockers cause first-dose and orthostatic hypotension, so bedtime dosing is advised.

answers.name: Nitrates
answers.pearl: Nitrates cause venodilation and orthostatic hypotension, especially when combined with PDE-5 inhibitors.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Volume depletion from loop diuretics unmasks orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers impair compensatory tachycardia, and carvedilol adds alpha-blockade.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs block alpha-1 receptors and are a leading cause of orthostatic hypotension in older adults.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Alpha-1 blockade makes quetiapine, risperidone, clozapine and chlorpromazine frequent culprits.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause volume depletion and orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers vasodilate and can cause orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors blunt angiotensin-mediated vasoconstriction, especially when volume depleted.

answers.name: Trazodone
answers.pearl: Trazodone causes orthostatic hypotension through alpha-1 blockade, an issue at the doses used for sleep.

answers.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers
answers.pearl: ARBs can cause orthostatic hypotension, particularly in volume-depleted patients.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids cause histamine-mediated vasodilation and blunted sympathetic reflexes.

answers.name: Levodopa
answers.pearl: Levodopa causes orthostatic hypotension in Parkinson's disease, compounding autonomic failure from the disease.

answers.name: Hydralazine
answers.pearl: Hydralazine is a direct arterial vasodilator that can cause hypotension and reflex tachycardia.

answers.name: Benzodiazepines
answers.pearl: Benzodiazepines cause sedation and impair postural reflexes, which increases falls in older adults.

answers.name: Clonidine
answers.pearl: Central alpha-2 agonists lower sympathetic outflow and cause orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Dopamine agonists
answers.pearl: Dopamine agonists cause orthostatic hypotension and sudden sleep attacks.

answers.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
answers.pearl: SGLT2 inhibitors cause osmotic diuresis and volume depletion, which can lead to orthostasis.

answers.name: Sacubitril-valsartan
answers.pearl: Sacubitril-valsartan causes symptomatic hypotension more often than enalapril in heart failure trials.

answers.name: Tizanidine
answers.pearl: Tizanidine, an alpha-2 agonist muscle relaxant, can cause hypotension and sedation.

answers.name: Minoxidil
answers.pearl: Minoxidil is a potent vasodilator that also causes fluid retention and reflex tachycardia.

answers.name: Spironolactone
answers.pearl: Spironolactone's diuretic effect can contribute to volume depletion and hypotension.

answers.name: Labetalol
answers.pearl: Labetalol's combined alpha and beta blockade makes orthostatic hypotension a frequent adverse effect.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Mirtazapine can cause orthostatic hypotension through alpha-blockade.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: Methyldopa lowers sympathetic tone and can cause orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Duloxetine
answers.pearl: Duloxetine has a labeled warning for orthostatic hypotension and syncope.

answers.name: Dexmedetomidine
answers.pearl: Dexmedetomidine's alpha-2 agonism causes hypotension and bradycardia.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine has alpha-blocking effects that can cause orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Thalidomide
answers.pearl: Orthostatic hypotension is a labeled adverse effect of thalidomide.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloids can cause autonomic neuropathy with orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Bortezomib is associated with orthostatic hypotension, possibly via autonomic neuropathy.

answers.name: Amifostine
answers.pearl: Amifostine, a cytoprotectant given with chemotherapy or radiation, commonly causes hypotension.

answers.name: Reserpine
answers.pearl: Reserpine depletes catecholamine stores and can cause orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Guanethidine
answers.pearl: Guanethidine blocks sympathetic neurotransmitter release and prominently causes orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Mecamylamine
answers.pearl: Ganglionic blockade with mecamylamine causes orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors
answers.pearl: MAOIs commonly cause orthostatic hypotension, sometimes limiting dose.

answers.name: Phenoxybenzamine
answers.pearl: Phenoxybenzamine, an irreversible alpha blocker used before pheochromocytoma surgery, causes orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors
answers.pearl: PDE-5 inhibitors can cause profound hypotension with nitrates, which are contraindicated within 24 to 48 hours.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypercalcemia
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dehydration (contributory, mild effect on total calcium); Rhabdomyolysis recovery phase (rebound hypercalcemia, usually modest); Pneumocystis pneumonia and Silicone/paraffin granulomas (case-report level, calcitriol-mediated); Tamoxifen flare and Teriparatide (transient/mild); Coccidioidomycosis and Histoplasmosis (documented but uncommon). Kidney transplantation (post-transplant hyperparathyroidism; tertiary hyperparathyroidism was dropped because it fuzzy-matches primary). Remaining fuzzy pair: parathyroid adenoma vs parathyroid carcinoma. Williams syndrome scored as a Board Prep Trap (pediatric board classic).

answers.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: The most common cause of hypercalcemia in outpatients, with an inappropriately normal or elevated PTH, usually from a single parathyroid adenoma.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Malignancy is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in hospitalized patients, acting through PTHrP, osteolytic metastases, or calcitriol production.

answers.name: Bone metastases
answers.pearl: Osteolytic metastases (classically breast and lung) cause local cytokine-driven osteoclast activation and calcium release.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Myeloma cells secrete osteoclast-activating factors, producing lytic lesions and hypercalcemia that is worsened by light-chain kidney injury.

answers.name: Vitamin D toxicity
answers.pearl: Excess 25-hydroxyvitamin D increases intestinal calcium absorption, and hypercalcemia can persist for weeks because of its long half-life.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion and can unmask underlying primary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granuloma macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase and make calcitriol independent of PTH, so PTH is suppressed.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium raises the parathyroid set point for calcium, causing hypercalcemia with mildly elevated PTH, and can unmask hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Immobilization
answers.pearl: Prolonged immobility increases bone resorption; the effect is greatest in high-turnover states such as Paget disease and in the young.

answers.name: Excess calcium intake
answers.pearl: Large doses of calcium supplements or carbonate antacids can raise serum calcium, especially with renal impairment or vitamin D co-ingestion.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Thyroid hormone increases bone turnover and can mildly raise serum calcium.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Some lymphomas overproduce calcitriol through extrarenal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity, giving hypercalcemia with suppressed PTH.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume contraction lowers renal calcium clearance and hemoconcentrates the serum, worsening hypercalcemia from other causes.

answers.name: PTHrP secretion
answers.pearl: Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy is driven by PTH-related peptide, classically from squamous cell, breast, renal, and bladder tumors, with suppressed PTH.

answers.name: Breast cancer
answers.pearl: Breast cancer causes hypercalcemia through osteolytic bone metastases and PTHrP production.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Squamous cell lung cancer is a classic PTHrP-secreting tumor.

answers.name: Renal cell carcinoma
answers.pearl: Renal cell carcinoma causes hypercalcemia via PTHrP and bone metastases.

answers.name: Kidney transplantation
answers.pearl: Persistent post-transplant hyperparathyroidism plus restored calcitriol synthesis causes hypercalcemia in many recipients during the first year.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infections such as TB produce calcitriol in activated macrophages.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: During recovery from rhabdomyolysis-related AKI, calcium deposited in injured muscle is remobilized and can cause rebound hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Inactivating CaSR mutation with a calcium/creatinine clearance ratio below about 0.01 and a typically benign course.

answers.name: Milk-alkali syndrome
answers.pearl: Excess calcium plus absorbable alkali causes hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and AKI; now usually from calcium carbonate antacids or supplements.

answers.name: Williams syndrome
answers.pearl: Elastin gene deletion (7q11.23) with supravalvular aortic stenosis and infantile hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia
answers.pearl: MEN1 (menin; parathyroid hyperplasia in nearly all carriers) and MEN2A (RET; hypercalcemia in a minority) cause multigland parathyroid disease.

answers.name: Parathyroid carcinoma
answers.pearl: Rare cause that presents with severe hypercalcemia (often above 14 mg/dL), a palpable neck mass, and markedly high PTH.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency (as in Addisonian crisis) can raise calcium via volume depletion and increased tubular reabsorption, and it resolves with glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous fungal infection with extrarenal calcitriol production; hypercalcemia is reported in disseminated and chronic disease.

answers.name: Coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous endemic mycosis (southwestern US) that can cause calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Berylliosis
answers.pearl: Chronic beryllium disease is a sarcoid-like granulomatous disease that can cause hypercalcemia via calcitriol.

answers.name: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
answers.pearl: HTLV-1-associated ATLL causes hypercalcemia in a majority of patients through osteoclast-activating cytokines and PTHrP.

answers.name: Teriparatide
answers.pearl: PTH analog that can cause transient mild hypercalcemia several hours after dosing.

answers.name: Tamoxifen flare
answers.pearl: Starting tamoxifen or other hormonal therapy in breast cancer with bone metastases can precipitate a hypercalcemic flare within weeks.

answers.name: Ectopic PTH secretion
answers.pearl: Very rare tumors (ovarian, lung, neuroendocrine) secreting true PTH mimic primary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Calcipotriene
answers.pearl: Topical vitamin D analog used for psoriasis; excessive use over large body surface area can cause hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Retinoid toxicity
answers.pearl: Excess vitamin A or retinoids stimulate osteoclastic bone resorption.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
answers.pearl: CDC73 (HRPT2) mutation causes parathyroid adenomas or carcinoma with ossifying jaw fibromas.

answers.name: CYP24A1 deficiency
answers.pearl: Loss of CYP24A1 reduces calcitriol catabolism, causing infantile hypercalcemia and later hypercalcemia with vitamin D supplementation.

answers.name: Silicone granulomas
answers.pearl: Silicone or paraffin injections can form granulomas that produce calcitriol, reported after cosmetic augmentation.

answers.name: Pneumocystis pneumonia
answers.pearl: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in HIV has been linked to calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia from granulomatous inflammation.

answers.name: Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
answers.pearl: Activating PTH1R mutation produces PTH-independent hypercalcemia with short-limbed dwarfism.

answers.name: Neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Homozygous or severe heterozygous inactivating CaSR mutations cause life-threatening neonatal hypercalcemia with high PTH.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of normal anion gap (hyperchloremic) metabolic acidosis
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Lithium (incomplete distal RTA, mostly case/series level); Zonisamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, less commonly cited than topiramate); Sjogren syndrome and Medullary sponge kidney (distal RTA); Heparin (type 4 RTA via aldosterone suppression, rarely clinically important); Tenofovir (proximal tubulopathy). Distal RTA vs Proximal RTA share a long common suffix, so they are named in short form with long-form aliases; matcher may confuse them, so watch that in playtesting. Toluene, ureterosigmoidostomy, cholestyramine chosen as Board Prep Traps. General 'renal tubular acidosis' is intentionally not an answer; players must name the type. Known fuzzy residue: the aliases 'type 1 RTA', 'type 2 RTA', 'type 4 RTA' differ by one character, so rely on exact matches.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Stool bicarbonate loss produces a normal-gap acidosis with a negative urine anion gap (high urinary ammonium).

answers.name: Normal saline infusion
answers.pearl: Large-volume 0.9% saline causes hyperchloremic dilutional acidosis by diluting bicarbonate and adding chloride.

answers.name: Distal RTA
answers.pearl: Type 1 RTA: failure of distal H+ secretion gives urine pH above 5.5, hypokalemia, and risk of nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.

answers.name: Proximal RTA
answers.pearl: Type 2 RTA: impaired proximal bicarbonate reabsorption; urine can still acidify (pH below 5.5) once serum bicarbonate has fallen.

answers.name: Type 4 RTA
answers.pearl: Aldosterone deficiency or resistance causes hyperkalemia and impaired ammoniagenesis; often hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism in diabetes.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition blocks proximal bicarbonate reabsorption, causing bicarbonate wasting.

answers.name: Ileal conduit urinary diversion
answers.pearl: In an ileal conduit or neobladder, chloride-for-bicarbonate exchange and ammonium reabsorption across the bowel mucosa cause hyperchloremic acidosis.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced ammoniagenesis in stage 3-4 CKD produces a normal-gap acidosis before the gap rises in advanced CKD.

answers.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
answers.pearl: Spironolactone, amiloride, and triamterene cause hyperkalemic acidosis by impairing distal H+ and K+ secretion.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors or ARBs
answers.pearl: RAAS blockade lowers aldosterone, causing hyperkalemic type 4 RTA, particularly in diabetes or CKD.

answers.name: Trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC like amiloride, causing hyperkalemia and a hyperchloremic acidosis, especially at high doses.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs suppress renin and cause hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism with hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Primary adrenal insufficiency causes aldosterone deficiency leading to hyperkalemia and a normal-gap acidosis.

answers.name: Diabetic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Diabetic kidney disease is the classic cause of hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Pancreatic fistula
answers.pearl: Pancreatic secretions are rich in bicarbonate, so external drainage or a fistula wastes it.

answers.name: High-output ileostomy
answers.pearl: Small bowel or ileostomy effluent is bicarbonate-rich, so high output produces non-gap acidosis and volume depletion.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use causes diarrhea with bicarbonate and potassium loss.

answers.name: Post-DKA hyperchloremic acidosis
answers.pearl: During DKA treatment, ketoanions lost in urine represent lost potential bicarbonate, and chloride-rich fluids replace them, leaving a non-gap acidosis.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy
answers.pearl: Urinary obstruction damages the collecting duct, causing distal or type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus cause hyperkalemic type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Toluene inhalation
answers.pearl: Glue sniffing: hippurate is rapidly excreted, so toluene often produces non-gap acidosis with hypokalemia even though it begins with a high gap.

answers.name: Ureterosigmoidostomy
answers.pearl: Colonic mucosa exchanges chloride for bicarbonate and reabsorbs ammonium; the classic surgical cause of hyperchloremic acidosis.

answers.name: Cholestyramine
answers.pearl: Bile acid resins exchange chloride for bicarbonate in the gut; acidosis is usually seen with high doses or renal impairment.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction: glucosuria, phosphaturia, aminoaciduria, and uricosuria with proximal RTA.

answers.name: Topiramate
answers.pearl: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition by topiramate causes a bicarbonate-wasting, non-gap acidosis and kidney stones.

answers.name: Zonisamide
answers.pearl: Weak carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that can cause non-gap metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Light chains injure proximal tubules, producing Fanconi syndrome and proximal RTA.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin creates membrane pores that leak H+, causing distal RTA with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium can impair distal acidification (incomplete distal RTA) in addition to nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide metabolites cause proximal tubular injury (Fanconi syndrome with proximal RTA).

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir disoproxil causes proximal tubulopathy with proximal RTA and phosphate wasting.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Interstitial nephritis from Sjogren syndrome commonly causes distal RTA.

answers.name: Medullary sponge kidney
answers.pearl: Cystic dilation of collecting ducts causes distal RTA, nephrocalcinosis, and stones.

answers.name: Interstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Tubulointerstitial disease damages distal tubules and the cortical collecting duct, causing type 1 or type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Ammonium chloride ingestion
answers.pearl: Acid loads such as ammonium chloride or arginine hydrochloride add H+ and chloride directly, generating non-gap acidosis.

answers.name: Pseudohypoaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid resistance (ENaC or receptor defects in type 1, WNK/CUL3/KLHL3 in type 2) gives hyperkalemia with non-gap acidosis.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin suppresses adrenal aldosterone synthesis and can cause hyperkalemic type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Cystinosis
answers.pearl: Lysosomal cystine accumulation (CTNS mutation) causes Fanconi syndrome and proximal RTA in infancy.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper deposition in tubules can cause distal and proximal RTA.

answers.name: Carbonic anhydrase II deficiency
answers.pearl: Osteopetrosis with renal tubular acidosis and cerebral calcification (marble brain disease).

answers.name: Dent disease
answers.pearl: X-linked CLCN5 mutation causes low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, and proximal tubular dysfunction.

answers.name: Lowe syndrome
answers.pearl: X-linked OCRL mutation: congenital cataracts, intellectual disability, and Fanconi syndrome with proximal RTA.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyperkalemia
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Epsilon-aminocaproic acid (case reports, often with rhabdomyolysis); Pentamidine (ENaC blockade, reported mainly at high-dose IV); Drospirenone (anti-mineralocorticoid; mostly a concern with CKD/ACEi/MRA); Sickle cell nephropathy; Penicillin G potassium (dose-dependent); GI bleed (modest effect). Gordon syndrome and Pseudohypoaldosteronism are listed without PHA1/PHA2 aliases to prevent fuzzy confusion. Pseudohyperkalemia deliberately includes in-vitro hemolysis/fist clenching in its pearl. Traps: succinylcholine, digoxin toxicity, hyperkalemic periodic paralysis.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced nephron mass lowers K+ excretion; hyperkalemia usually emerges at low GFR (below roughly 15-20 mL/min) or when drugs and acidosis contribute.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Oliguric AKI is a leading cause of severe hyperkalemia in hospitalized patients.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors lower aldosterone, impairing distal K+ secretion; risk is highest with CKD, diabetes, or other K+-raising drugs.

answers.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers
answers.pearl: ARBs reduce aldosterone effect, impairing K+ excretion, particularly in CKD or when combined with ACE inhibitors or MRAs.

answers.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
answers.pearl: Spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride, and triamterene block aldosterone action or ENaC and are a classic drug cause.

answers.name: Potassium supplements
answers.pearl: Oral or IV potassium replacement can cause hyperkalemia, particularly with reduced GFR.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Muscle necrosis releases intracellular K+ and phosphate, often with AKI; crush injury acts the same way.

answers.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid cell turnover after chemotherapy releases K+, phosphate, and uric acid, causing hyperkalemia and AKI.

answers.name: Hemolysis
answers.pearl: Intravascular hemolysis releases red cell potassium; large hemolytic crises can raise serum K+ in vivo.

answers.name: Metabolic acidosis
answers.pearl: Cellular buffering of extracellular H+ drives potassium out of cells, more with non-anion-gap than organic acidoses.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Insulin deficiency and hyperosmolality shift K+ out of cells, so serum K+ is high despite total body potassium depletion.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid deficiency impairs distal K+ secretion, causing hyperkalemia with hyponatremia.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs reduce renin and aldosterone and renal blood flow, raising K+ in at-risk patients.

answers.name: Trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC like amiloride, causing hyperkalemia within days, especially with CKD or RAAS blockade.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin inhibits adrenal aldosterone synthesis; hyperkalemia can occur within days even with low-dose or low molecular weight heparin.

answers.name: Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Type 4 RTA, common in diabetic nephropathy and interstitial renal disease, presents with hyperkalemia and a mild non-gap acidosis.

answers.name: Pseudohyperkalemia
answers.pearl: In vitro hemolysis, fist clenching, or delayed processing falsely elevates measured K+; confirm with a repeat or whole-blood or plasma sample.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Extensive burns release K+ from damaged tissue and make later succinylcholine use dangerous.

answers.name: Blood transfusion
