answers.pearl: Stored red cells leak K+ in the bag; massive or large-volume transfusion is the high-risk setting.

answers.name: Salt substitutes
answers.pearl: Potassium chloride salt substitutes are an underrecognized source in CKD or with ACE inhibitor or MRA therapy.

answers.name: Succinylcholine
answers.pearl: Depolarization increases K+ efflux (about 0.5 mEq/L), with exaggerated release in burns, denervation, prolonged immobility, or crush injury.

answers.name: Digoxin toxicity
answers.pearl: Digoxin inhibits Na-K ATPase; in acute overdose hyperkalemia predicts mortality and is a Digifab indication.

answers.name: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: SCN4A mutation causes attacks of weakness provoked by rest after exercise or potassium intake.

answers.name: Beta-blockers
answers.pearl: Nonselective beta-blockers impair beta-2-mediated cellular K+ uptake and renin release.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy
answers.pearl: Urinary obstruction impairs distal K+ secretion and causes type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine cause hyperkalemia by reducing aldosterone and blocking distal K+ secretion channels.

answers.name: Volume depletion
answers.pearl: Reduced distal sodium and water delivery limits K+ secretion in the collecting duct.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Muscle K+ release raises serum K+ transiently, more so with beta-blockade or in sedentary patients.

answers.name: Hyperosmolality
answers.pearl: Solvent drag from hyperosmolality (hyperglycemia, mannitol) shifts K+ out of cells.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
answers.pearl: Absorbed blood protein and red cell breakdown can produce hyperkalemia in patients with reduced kidney function.

answers.name: Penicillin G potassium
answers.pearl: Each million units of IV penicillin G potassium contains roughly 1.7 mEq of potassium.

answers.name: Extreme leukocytosis or thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Cell lysis in the tube during clotting releases K+ in serum samples when WBC or platelet counts are extremely high.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes aldosterone deficiency with hyperkalemia and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Interstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Tubulointerstitial disease damages distal tubules and causes type 4 RTA with hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine blocks ENaC, similar to amiloride and trimethoprim, causing hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Drospirenone
answers.pearl: Spironolactone-derived progestin with anti-mineralocorticoid activity, a hyperkalemia risk with CKD or other K+-raising drugs.

answers.name: Sickle cell nephropathy
answers.pearl: Medullary injury causes hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism and impaired distal K+ secretion.

answers.name: Gordon syndrome
answers.pearl: Familial hyperkalemic hypertension from WNK1/WNK4/KLHL3/CUL3 mutations increases NCC activity; thiazides are the treatment.

answers.name: Pseudohypoaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Type 1 mineralocorticoid resistance (ENaC or receptor mutations) causes neonatal salt wasting, hyperkalemia, and acidosis.

answers.name: Arginine infusion
answers.pearl: Cationic amino acids such as arginine hydrochloride exchange into cells for K+, causing hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Epsilon-aminocaproic acid
answers.pearl: Antifibrinolytic reported to cause hyperkalemia, in some cases alongside rhabdomyolysis.

answers.name: Aldosterone synthase deficiency
answers.pearl: CYP11B2 mutation causes isolated hypoaldosteronism with hyperkalemia and salt wasting.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of metabolic alkalosis
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hyperemesis gravidarum scored as separate answer from Vomiting (valid but near-duplicate mechanism); Post-hypercapnic alkalosis (accepted as metabolic compensation overshoot); Aminoglycoside Bartter-like syndrome; Dialysis with high-bicarbonate dialysate; Acetate in TPN; Citrate anticoagulation; Sodium polystyrene with non-absorbable antacids (documented in renal failure reports); Carbenoxolone (UK, rarely used). Primary and secondary hyperaldosteronism were deliberately kept to one answer to avoid fuzzy collisions. Traps: Bartter, Gitelman, Milk-alkali syndrome.

answers.name: Vomiting
answers.pearl: Loss of gastric HCl leaves excess bicarbonate; volume contraction and hypokalemia then maintain the alkalosis, and urine chloride is low.

answers.name: Nasogastric suction
answers.pearl: Continuous NG suction removes HCl, producing chloride-responsive alkalosis identical to vomiting.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics cause chloride, volume, and potassium loss, producing contraction alkalosis with high urine chloride while the drug is active.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause chloride and potassium wasting and volume contraction, leading to alkalosis.

answers.name: Volume depletion
answers.pearl: Contraction of extracellular volume with bicarbonate retained in a smaller volume, driven by aldosterone and angiotensin II effects on the kidney.

answers.name: Hypokalemia
answers.pearl: Potassium depletion increases H+ secretion and ammonia production in the collecting duct and shifts H+ into cells.

answers.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Aldosterone excess causes sodium retention with H+ and K+ wasting, giving hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis with high urine chloride.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoid excess at high levels saturates 11-beta-HSD2 and acts on the mineralocorticoid receptor, causing hypokalemic alkalosis, especially with ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Exogenous glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: High-dose steroids with mineralocorticoid effect cause sodium retention and renal H+ and K+ loss.

answers.name: Bicarbonate administration
answers.pearl: Excess sodium bicarbonate or other alkali loads raise serum bicarbonate, especially with reduced GFR or volume depletion.

answers.name: Massive transfusion
answers.pearl: Citrate in banked blood is metabolized to bicarbonate in the liver.

answers.name: Licorice ingestion
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhizic acid inhibits 11-beta-HSD2, causing apparent mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension, hypokalemia, and alkalosis.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Renovascular hypertension raises renin and aldosterone, causing hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Bulimia nervosa
answers.pearl: Self-induced vomiting or diuretic or laxative misuse causes metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Gastric outlet obstruction
answers.pearl: Persistent vomiting from pyloric obstruction produces hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Post-hypercapnic alkalosis
answers.pearl: Renal bicarbonate retained in chronic respiratory acidosis persists after rapid correction of PaCO2 by ventilation.

answers.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
answers.pearl: Severe vomiting of pregnancy can cause hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use causes volume depletion and potassium loss that can produce metabolic alkalosis in some patients.

answers.name: Chloride depletion
answers.pearl: Chloride-responsive alkalosis has a urine chloride below about 20 mEq/L and corrects with saline.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome
answers.pearl: Loss of function of NKCC2, ROMK, or ClC-Kb causes salt wasting, hypokalemic alkalosis, hypercalciuria, and normal or low BP, mimicking chronic loop diuretic use.

answers.name: Gitelman syndrome
answers.pearl: NCC mutation gives hypokalemic alkalosis with hypomagnesemia and hypocalciuria, mimicking chronic thiazide use.

answers.name: Milk-alkali syndrome
answers.pearl: Calcium plus absorbable alkali causes hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and AKI; now usually from calcium carbonate supplements or antacids.

answers.name: Liddle syndrome
answers.pearl: Activating ENaC mutation gives hypertension, hypokalemia, and alkalosis with low renin and low aldosterone, treated with amiloride.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Sweat chloride and sodium loss cause volume contraction, hypochloremic alkalosis, and a pseudo-Bartter picture, especially in hot weather.

answers.name: Ectopic ACTH syndrome
answers.pearl: Very high cortisol from ectopic ACTH (e.g., small cell lung cancer) overwhelms 11-beta-HSD2, causing severe hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Fludrocortisone
answers.pearl: Synthetic mineralocorticoid causes sodium retention and renal K+ and H+ wasting.

answers.name: Congenital chloride diarrhea
answers.pearl: Defective ileal Cl-/HCO3- exchange (SLC26A3) causes chloride-rich diarrhea with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: High-dose penicillins
answers.pearl: Poorly reabsorbable anions such as carbenicillin or high-dose penicillin increase distal H+ and K+ secretion.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
answers.pearl: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I from a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene, suppressed by glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: 11-beta-hydroxylase and 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency cause excess deoxycorticosterone, with hypertension and hypokalemic alkalosis (virilization in the former, sexual infantilism in the latter).

answers.name: Regional citrate anticoagulation
answers.pearl: Citrate used for CRRT circuits is metabolized to bicarbonate, causing alkalosis when delivery exceeds clearance.

answers.name: High-bicarbonate dialysis
answers.pearl: Excess bicarbonate or acetate buffer in dialysate can cause post-dialysis metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Rebound alkalosis after organic acidosis
answers.pearl: Metabolism of lactate or ketoanions regenerates bicarbonate, and added alkali therapy can overshoot into alkalosis.

answers.name: Aminoglycoside-induced Bartter-like syndrome
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides can activate the calcium-sensing receptor, causing a Bartter-like syndrome with hypokalemic alkalosis and hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Acetate in parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Acetate added to TPN is metabolized to bicarbonate.

answers.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
answers.pearl: 11-beta-HSD2 deficiency allows cortisol to occupy the mineralocorticoid receptor, causing severe hypertension, hypokalemia, and alkalosis with low renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Reninoma
answers.pearl: Renin-secreting juxtaglomerular cell tumor causes severe secondary hyperaldosteronism with hypertension and hypokalemic alkalosis.

answers.name: Deoxycorticosterone-producing tumor
answers.pearl: Adrenal tumor secreting deoxycorticosterone causes mineralocorticoid excess with suppressed renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Carbenoxolone
answers.pearl: Licorice derivative used for peptic ulcers that inhibits 11-beta-HSD2, with the same effects as licorice ingestion.

answers.name: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate with antacids
answers.pearl: Kayexalate given with non-absorbable antacids or laxatives can cause metabolic alkalosis, mainly in renal failure.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of thrombocytopenia in a hospitalized patient
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mechanical circulatory support grouping (ECMO/LVAD/IABP/Impella/bypass share consumptive and hemolytic mechanisms); Malaria and Dengue (documented, moderate relevance in a US inpatient setting); Snake envenomation (hemotoxic species only); Cyclic thrombocytopenia and Gray platelet syndrome (rare); Medication reaction answer is named generically to avoid fuzzy confusion with 'heparin-induced thrombocytopenia'; MYH9-related disorders aliases list the historical eponyms (May-Hegglin, Fechtner, Sebastian, Epstein). Traps: post-transfusion purpura, Wiskott-Aldrich, Bernard-Soulier.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Infection drives platelet consumption, marrow suppression, and DIC; platelet count is a component of SOFA scoring.

answers.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
answers.pearl: Widespread thrombin generation consumes platelets and clotting factors; look for prolonged PT/aPTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, and schistocytes.

answers.name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Anti-PF4/heparin IgG activates platelets, typically 5-10 days after exposure, causing thrombosis; use the 4Ts score and stop all heparin.

answers.name: Medication reaction
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent antibodies or marrow suppression are common causes of inpatient thrombocytopenia; counts usually recover within about a week of stopping the drug.

answers.name: Immune thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction and impaired production; a diagnosis of exclusion with an otherwise normal smear.

answers.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
answers.pearl: ADAMTS13 deficiency causes microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, and it is a medical emergency needing plasma exchange.

answers.name: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
answers.pearl: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia and AKI, from Shiga toxin or complement dysregulation.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension with splenic sequestration and reduced hepatic thrombopoietin production lowers platelet count.

answers.name: Hypersplenism
answers.pearl: An enlarged spleen can sequester up to about 90% of the platelet mass.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Alcohol directly suppresses megakaryopoiesis and causes folate deficiency; platelets typically recover within about a week of abstinence.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Cytotoxic drugs suppress marrow megakaryocytes with a nadir typically 7-14 days after treatment.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Marrow replacement by leukemic blasts suppresses thrombopoiesis; DIC adds consumption in APL.

answers.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome
answers.pearl: Ineffective hematopoiesis causes cytopenias, including thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV causes immune thrombocytopenia and marrow suppression, often an early manifestation.

answers.name: Hepatitis C
answers.pearl: HCV causes thrombocytopenia through splenic sequestration, immune destruction, and reduced thrombopoietin.

answers.name: Viral infections
answers.pearl: Many viruses (EBV, CMV, parvovirus, others) cause transient thrombocytopenia through marrow suppression or immune destruction.

answers.name: Massive transfusion
answers.pearl: Dilution of platelets by red cell transfusion without platelets reduces the count.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency
answers.pearl: Megaloblastic ineffective hematopoiesis lowers all cell lines, including platelets.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Autoantibodies and antiphospholipid antibodies can cause immune thrombocytopenia, sometimes the first manifestation.

answers.name: Pseudothrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: EDTA-dependent platelet clumping gives a falsely low count; check a smear or a citrate or heparin tube.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Vancomycin can cause drug-dependent antibody thrombocytopenia, which may be severe.

answers.name: Post-transfusion purpura
answers.pearl: Anti-HPA-1a alloantibodies in a previously sensitized patient, usually a multiparous woman, destroy the patient's own platelets 5-10 days after transfusion.

answers.name: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome
answers.pearl: X-linked WAS mutation: eczema, immunodeficiency, and microthrombocytopenia with small platelets.

answers.name: Bernard-Soulier syndrome
answers.pearl: GPIb-IX-V defect causes giant platelets, mild thrombocytopenia, and failed ristocetin aggregation not corrected by plasma.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Linezolid causes dose- and duration-dependent myelosuppression, typically after more than 10-14 days of therapy, with renal impairment as a risk factor.

answers.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
answers.pearl: Beta-lactams, especially piperacillin-tazobactam, are a recognized cause of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate causes dose-dependent thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides can cause drug-dependent antibody thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Aplastic anemia
answers.pearl: Marrow failure causes pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets in a pregnant or postpartum patient, usually with preeclampsia.

answers.name: Mechanical circulatory support
answers.pearl: ECMO, LVADs, intra-aortic balloon pumps, Impella, and bypass circuits consume and destroy platelets.

answers.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome
answers.pearl: Antiphospholipid antibodies can cause mild to moderate thrombocytopenia alongside thrombosis.

answers.name: Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors
answers.pearl: Abciximab, eptifibatide, and tirofiban can cause acute severe thrombocytopenia within hours of exposure, sometimes from pre-existing antibodies.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Cytokine storm with cytopenias, fever, hyperferritinemia, and organomegaly; HScore or HLH-2004 criteria guide diagnosis.

answers.name: Bone marrow infiltration
answers.pearl: Metastatic cancer, myelofibrosis, or granulomas replace normal marrow, causing leukoerythroblastic cytopenias.

answers.name: Dengue fever
answers.pearl: Dengue causes marrow suppression and immune destruction; thrombocytopenia plus hemoconcentration signals plasma leakage.

answers.name: Vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Adenoviral vector COVID-19 vaccines (e.g., Ad26.COV2.S) caused anti-PF4 antibody thrombosis with thrombocytopenia, mimicking autoimmune HIT.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine, including tonic water exposure, is a classic cause of drug-dependent antibody thrombocytopenia that can also cause TTP-like HUS.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Malaria causes thrombocytopenia through immune destruction and splenic sequestration, especially falciparum.

answers.name: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon
answers.pearl: Consumptive coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia from kaposiform hemangioendothelioma or tufted angioma, usually in infancy.

answers.name: MYH9-related disorders
answers.pearl: MYH9 mutations (May-Hegglin, Fechtner, Sebastian, and Epstein syndromes) cause macrothrombocytopenia with Dohle-like inclusions and sometimes nephritis or deafness.

answers.name: Cyclic thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Rare disorder with periodic oscillations of platelet count every 20-40 days, sometimes autoimmune.

answers.name: Gray platelet syndrome
answers.pearl: NBEAL2 mutation causes macrothrombocytopenia with absent alpha granules, giving a gray smear appearance and myelofibrosis.

answers.name: Snake envenomation
answers.pearl: Hemotoxic venoms (pit vipers) can cause consumptive coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypoglycemia in a patient without diabetes
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Heart failure and Hypothyroidism (association/mechanism documented but not a leading cause); Hepatocellular carcinoma (overlaps with non-islet tumor trap); Growth hormone deficiency (mainly children); Hemodialysis (glucose-free dialysate; older practice); Disopyramide; Prolonged exercise (rare in non-diabetics); Reye syndrome and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (pediatric); insulin therapy for hyperkalemia in non-diabetics (strictly iatrogenic). Traps: non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia, insulin autoimmune syndrome, nesidioblastosis/NIPHS.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Ethanol metabolism raises the NADH/NAD ratio and blocks gluconeogenesis, typically after binge drinking with poor intake and depleted glycogen.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Increased glucose utilization, impaired gluconeogenesis, and hepatic dysfunction produce hypoglycemia, which predicts poor prognosis.

answers.name: Starvation
answers.pearl: Glycogen stores are depleted after about 24 hours, so prolonged fasting leads to hypoglycemia, especially in the malnourished.

answers.name: Liver failure
answers.pearl: The liver supplies glucose via glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; severe hepatic dysfunction or acute liver failure causes fasting hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol is a counter-regulatory hormone, so deficiency causes fasting hypoglycemia, especially in children and with critical illness.

answers.name: Insulinoma
answers.pearl: Insulin-secreting pancreatic tumor causing fasting hypoglycemia with high insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin and a negative sulfonylurea screen.

answers.name: Renal failure
answers.pearl: Reduced insulin clearance and loss of renal gluconeogenesis increase hypoglycemia risk in kidney failure.

answers.name: Post-gastric bypass hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Rapid nutrient delivery after Roux-en-Y bypass causes an exaggerated GLP-1 and insulin response and late postprandial hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Reactive hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Postprandial hypoglycemia 2-4 hours after meals; most patients with symptoms do not have documented low glucose when tested properly.

answers.name: Factitious insulin use
answers.pearl: Low C-peptide with high insulin points to exogenous insulin, while high C-peptide with high insulin suggests secretagogue use or insulinoma.

answers.name: Sulfonylurea ingestion
answers.pearl: Elevated insulin and C-peptide with a positive drug screen; can cause prolonged hypoglycemia treated with octreotide.

answers.name: Dumping syndrome
answers.pearl: Late dumping, 1-3 hours after meals, results from rapid gastric emptying and an exaggerated insulin response.

answers.name: Hypopituitarism
answers.pearl: Deficiency of cortisol and growth hormone, counter-regulatory hormones, can cause fasting hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Beta-blockers
answers.pearl: Nonselective beta-blockade impairs glycogenolysis and masks adrenergic warning symptoms, and fasting and renal impairment add risk.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Severe falciparum malaria causes hypoglycemia through parasite glucose consumption and impaired gluconeogenesis, worsened by quinine.

answers.name: Insulin therapy for hyperkalemia
answers.pearl: IV regular insulin for hyperkalemia frequently causes hypoglycemia, especially in renal failure or low baseline glucose; co-administer dextrose and monitor.

answers.name: Anorexia nervosa
answers.pearl: Depleted glycogen and fat-derived substrate limit counter-regulation, and severe hypoglycemia can be a presenting sign.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Large HCC may cause hypoglycemia through hepatic replacement, increased glucose uptake, or tumor IGF-2 production.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine stimulates pancreatic beta cells directly, causing hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, particularly in malaria and pregnancy.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Hepatic congestion, poor intake, and low-output states predispose to hypoglycemia, and it is associated with worse outcomes in acute heart failure.

answers.name: Non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Tumors secreting incompletely processed IGF-2 (big IGF-2) cause low insulin and C-peptide hypoglycemia with an IGF-2 to IGF-1 ratio above 10.

answers.name: Insulin autoimmune syndrome
answers.pearl: Autoantibodies to insulin cause postprandial hypoglycemia with very high total insulin; often triggered by methimazole or alpha-lipoic acid, mainly in Japanese patients.

answers.name: Nesidioblastosis
answers.pearl: Beta-cell hypertrophy or islet hyperplasia (noninsulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglycemia) causes hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, classically after gastric bypass.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones, notably gatifloxacin (withdrawn) and levofloxacin, block beta-cell K-ATP channels, with risk higher in elderly, renal impairment, and with sulfonylureas.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine is toxic to beta cells, causing initial insulin release with hypoglycemia and later diabetes.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Aspirin overdose can cause neuroglycopenia despite normal or low serum glucose and hypoglycemia, especially in children and the elderly.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfamethoxazole can stimulate insulin release, with hypoglycemia seen most often in renal failure.

answers.name: Disopyramide
answers.pearl: Class IA antiarrhythmic that blocks beta-cell K-ATP channels and can cause hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, particularly in the elderly with renal impairment.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism or myxedema can cause hypoglycemia through reduced gluconeogenesis, often with adrenal insufficiency.

answers.name: Growth hormone deficiency
answers.pearl: Growth hormone is a counter-regulatory hormone, so deficiency causes fasting hypoglycemia, mainly in children.

answers.name: Prolonged strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Endurance exercise can deplete glycogen and increase glucose utilization, rarely causing hypoglycemia in non-diabetics.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease
answers.pearl: Enzyme defects such as glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (von Gierke disease) cause fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly.

answers.name: Fatty acid oxidation disorders
answers.pearl: Defects such as MCAD deficiency cause hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting or illness.

answers.name: Hereditary fructose intolerance
answers.pearl: Aldolase B deficiency causes hypoglycemia, vomiting, and liver injury after fructose, sucrose, or sorbitol ingestion.

answers.name: Congenital hyperinsulinism
answers.pearl: Mutations in K-ATP channel genes (ABCC8, KCNJ11) and others cause persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia presenting in infancy.

answers.name: Hemodialysis
answers.pearl: Glucose-free dialysate or poor intake during dialysis sessions can cause hypoglycemia, especially in patients with diabetes or poor nutrition.

answers.name: Abrupt cessation of parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Sudden discontinuation of TPN leaves endogenous insulin secretion elevated, causing rebound hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Doege-Potter syndrome
answers.pearl: Solitary fibrous tumors (pleural, retroperitoneal) secrete big IGF-2, and resection is curative.

answers.name: Type B insulin resistance
answers.pearl: Autoantibodies against the insulin receptor can cause severe fasting hypoglycemia, often with acanthosis nigricans and lupus-like features.

answers.name: Ackee fruit poisoning
answers.pearl: Unripe ackee contains hypoglycin A, which inhibits fatty acid oxidation and causes Jamaican vomiting sickness with severe hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Reye syndrome
answers.pearl: Aspirin-associated mitochondrial hepatic injury with encephalopathy and hypoglycemia, mainly in children after viral illness.

answers.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
answers.pearl: Imprinting disorder with macroglossia, omphalocele, and neonatal hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hematuria.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hemorrhagic renal cyst and Medullary sponge kidney (uncommon); Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and Renal hemangioma (literature-supported, uncommon); Iliac artery-ureteral fistula (case-series level); Viral hemorrhagic cystitis (mostly transplant/HSCT settings); Strenuous exercise (diagnosis of exclusion); Anti-GBM disease, Schistosomiasis and Alport syndrome scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Urinary tract infection
answers.pearl: Cystitis is the most frequent cause of gross and microscopic hematuria in women, usually with dysuria and pyuria.

answers.name: Kidney stones
answers.pearl: Stones cause colicky flank pain with hematuria, and a noncontrast CT is the usual test.

answers.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Enlarged, friable prostatic vessels at the bladder neck can bleed, producing painless hematuria in older men.

answers.name: Bladder cancer
answers.pearl: Painless gross hematuria in a smoker is bladder cancer until proven otherwise and needs cystoscopy.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Glomerular bleeding gives dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts, often with proteinuria and hypertension.

answers.name: Anticoagulant therapy
answers.pearl: Anticoagulants rarely cause hematuria on their own, so bleeding on therapy still warrants evaluation for an underlying lesion.

answers.name: Renal cell carcinoma
answers.pearl: The classic triad of hematuria, flank pain and mass is seen in a minority and is a late presentation.

answers.name: Prostatitis
answers.pearl: Acute bacterial prostatitis causes fever, perineal pain and urinary symptoms, with occasional hematuria.

answers.name: Trauma
answers.pearl: Blunt or penetrating injury to the kidney, ureter or bladder causes hematuria, and the degree of bleeding does not predict severity.

answers.name: Pyelonephritis
answers.pearl: Upper tract infection causes flank pain and fever, and hematuria is common with it.

answers.name: IgA nephropathy
answers.pearl: The most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, classically with gross hematuria 1-3 days after an upper respiratory infection.

answers.name: Polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Cyst rupture or hemorrhage and stones produce episodic gross hematuria in ADPKD.

answers.name: Prostate cancer
answers.pearl: Advanced local disease can invade the urethra or bladder neck and cause hematuria.

answers.name: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Cola-colored urine, edema and hypertension 1-3 weeks after pharyngitis or 3-6 weeks after skin infection, with low C3.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Marathon running and other exertion cause transient hematuria, a diagnosis made only after other causes are excluded.

answers.name: Urinary catheterization
answers.pearl: Traumatic Foley placement, cystoscopy and other instrumentation cause iatrogenic hematuria.

answers.name: Hemorrhagic cystitis
answers.pearl: Cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide metabolite (acrolein) injury to the bladder wall; mesna prophylaxis helps.

answers.name: Lupus nephritis
answers.pearl: Proliferative classes produce hematuria and proteinuria with low complements and anti-dsDNA.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease or trait
answers.pearl: Medullary hypoxia and sickling cause papillary necrosis, and hematuria is a well-known renal complication even in trait.

answers.name: Coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Thrombocytopenia, hemophilia, DIC and other bleeding disorders can cause hematuria, but they should not be assumed to be the sole cause.

answers.name: Bladder stones
answers.pearl: Vesical calculi form with outlet obstruction, bladder diverticula or catheters and cause terminal hematuria with suprapubic pain.

answers.name: Radiation cystitis
answers.pearl: Pelvic radiation causes telangiectatic, friable bladder mucosa with hematuria months to years later.

answers.name: ANCA-associated vasculitis
answers.pearl: Pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis with hematuria and rapidly progressive renal failure, sometimes with pulmonary hemorrhage.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Immune complex glomerulonephritis or septic renal emboli and infarcts cause hematuria.

answers.name: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma
aliases: transitional cell carcinoma of the renal pelvis
answers.pearl: Renal pelvis or ureteral cancers cause hematuria with a normal cystoscopy and require upper tract imaging.

answers.name: IgA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura, arthralgia, abdominal pain and nephritis with IgA deposits; hematuria reflects renal involvement.

answers.name: Thin basement membrane disease
answers.pearl: Benign familial hematuria from COL4A3/COL4A4 mutations with preserved kidney function in most cases.

answers.name: Papillary necrosis
answers.pearl: Sloughed renal papillae occur with diabetes, sickle cell, analgesic or NSAID use, and obstruction, with hematuria and flank pain.

answers.name: Hemorrhagic renal cyst
answers.pearl: Bleeding into a simple or complex renal cyst can present with flank pain and gross hematuria.

answers.name: Renal infarction
answers.pearl: Embolic or thrombotic occlusion presents with flank pain, hematuria and a markedly raised LDH, and a normal urinalysis is often misleading.

answers.name: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
answers.pearl: Microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and AKI with hematuria and proteinuria, often after Shiga toxin E. coli.

answers.name: Renal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Seen in nephrotic syndrome and hypercoagulable states, causing flank pain and hematuria.

answers.name: Medullary sponge kidney
answers.pearl: Cystic dilation of collecting ducts predisposes to stones, infection and hematuria and is seen on IVU as papillary blush.

answers.name: Angiomyolipoma
answers.pearl: Fat-containing renal tumors in tuberous sclerosis can bleed spontaneously, causing hematuria or retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
answers.pearl: Hepatitis C-associated immune complex membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis with hematuria and low C4.

answers.name: Nutcracker syndrome
answers.pearl: Left renal vein compression between the aorta and SMA raises renal venous pressure and causes left-sided hematuria and flank pain.

answers.name: Renal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Genitourinary TB causes sterile pyuria and hematuria, with cavitation and ureteral strictures on imaging.

answers.name: Viral hemorrhagic cystitis
answers.pearl: BK virus or adenovirus reactivation after stem cell or kidney transplant causes late hemorrhagic cystitis.

answers.name: Renal arteriovenous malformation
answers.pearl: Congenital or post-biopsy AV fistulae cause recurrent, sometimes massive, hematuria.

answers.name: Bladder endometriosis
answers.pearl: Cyclic hematuria that coincides with menses suggests endometrial implants in the bladder wall.

answers.name: Loin pain hematuria syndrome
answers.pearl: Severe unilateral or bilateral loin pain with hematuria after exclusion of stones, glomerular disease and other causes.

answers.name: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome
answers.pearl: Old World hantavirus infection causes fever, thrombocytopenia, AKI and hematuria.

answers.name: Renal hemangioma
answers.pearl: A rare vascular tumor that causes essential unilateral hematuria in young adults, found at ureteroscopy.

answers.name: Iliac artery-ureteral fistula
answers.pearl: Prior pelvic surgery, radiation or a ureteral stent can create a fistula presenting with massive, intermittent hematuria.

answers.name: Anti-GBM disease
answers.pearl: Anti-GBM antibody disease causes rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with hematuria, with or without pulmonary hemorrhage (Goodpasture).

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Schistosoma haematobium causes terminal hematuria and chronic bladder inflammation, with squamous cell carcinoma risk.

answers.name: Alport syndrome
answers.pearl: X-linked COL4A5 disease with hematuria, progressive kidney failure, sensorineural hearing loss and lens abnormalities.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of chronic cough (lasting more than 8 weeks).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Tracheobronchial amyloidosis and Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (uncommon, literature level); Relapsing polychondritis (airway chondritis, rare); Arnold nerve reflex (guideline-listed but low-quality evidence); Beta blockers (via bronchospasm); Inhaled medication cough; E-cigarette use (limited chronic data); Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, primary ciliary dyskinesia and EGPA scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Upper airway cough syndrome
answers.pearl: Postnasal drip from rhinitis or sinus disease is the leading cause of chronic cough in nonsmokers and is treated empirically.

answers.name: Asthma
answers.pearl: Cough-variant asthma presents with cough alone and is confirmed by methacholine challenge or response to bronchodilators.

answers.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
answers.pearl: Reflux can cause cough via an esophageal-bronchial vagal reflex even without heartburn.

answers.name: ACE inhibitor cough
answers.pearl: Bradykinin accumulation causes a dry cough in up to 10-15% of patients, resolving within weeks of stopping the drug.

answers.name: Smoking
answers.pearl: Cigarette smoke is the commonest cause of chronic cough, and quitting often resolves it within weeks.

answers.name: COPD
answers.pearl: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease causes chronic cough with or without sputum and airflow obstruction on spirometry.

answers.name: Post-infectious cough
answers.pearl: A cough persisting 3-8 weeks after a viral respiratory infection from airway hyperresponsiveness and inflammation.

answers.name: Chronic bronchitis
answers.pearl: Defined as a productive cough on most days for at least three months in two consecutive years.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Persistent new or changed cough in a smoker is a classic presenting symptom of bronchogenic carcinoma.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Pulmonary TB should be considered with cough of more than 2-3 weeks, especially with weight loss and night sweats.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Permanent airway dilation causes daily productive cough and recurrent infections, seen as signet rings on CT.

answers.name: Allergic rhinitis
answers.pearl: Allergic nasal inflammation produces postnasal drainage and throat clearing that drives chronic cough.

answers.name: Chronic sinusitis
answers.pearl: Persistent sinus inflammation drains posteriorly and triggers cough receptors.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Pulmonary venous congestion can cause a nocturnal dry cough, sometimes mistaken for asthma.

answers.name: Pertussis
answers.pearl: Bordetella pertussis causes a paroxysmal cough lasting weeks to months in adolescents and adults, often without a whoop.

answers.name: Environmental or occupational irritants
answers.pearl: Dust, fumes, air pollution and secondhand smoke are reversible triggers of persistent cough.

answers.name: E-cigarette use
answers.pearl: Vaping aerosol irritates the airways and can cause persistent cough, and EVALI is on the differential.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Dry cough with dyspnea and basilar crackles; IPF and CTD-ILD are the main considerations.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: CFTR dysfunction leads to thick secretions, bronchiectasis and chronic productive cough; adult-onset presentations occur.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous airway and parenchymal disease produces cough with hilar adenopathy.

answers.name: Chronic aspiration
answers.pearl: Silent aspiration from dysphagia or neurologic disease causes recurrent cough and pneumonia.

answers.name: Laryngopharyngeal reflux
answers.pearl: Extraesophageal reflux reaching the larynx causes throat clearing, hoarseness and cough, often without heartburn.

answers.name: Airway foreign body
answers.pearl: A retained aspirated object can cause cough for months, even without a clear choking history.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers, even eye drops, can provoke bronchospasm and cough in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Immune reaction to inhaled antigens such as birds, mold or farm dust, with cough, dyspnea and ground-glass opacities.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: OSA is linked to chronic cough through reflux, airway inflammation and upper airway hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Psychogenic cough
answers.pearl: A diagnosis of exclusion with absent nocturnal cough and a honking or tic-like quality.

answers.name: Refractory chronic cough
answers.pearl: Persistent cough despite a thorough workup and treatment, attributed to a hypersensitive cough reflex.

answers.name: Amiodarone lung toxicity
answers.pearl: Amiodarone can cause interstitial pneumonitis with cough, dyspnea and low DLCO.

answers.name: Nonasthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis
answers.pearl: Chronic cough with sputum eosinophilia, normal spirometry and no airway hyperresponsiveness, steroid-responsive.

answers.name: Vocal cord dysfunction
answers.pearl: Paradoxical adduction of the vocal folds causes cough and stridor and is confirmed by laryngoscopy.

answers.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity to Aspergillus in asthma or CF with high IgE, eosinophilia and central bronchiectasis.

answers.name: Mitral stenosis
answers.pearl: Left atrial hypertension produces cough and hemoptysis, and pulmonary congestion may mimic asthma.

answers.name: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
answers.pearl: MAC and other NTM cause chronic cough, particularly nodular bronchiectasis in older women.

answers.name: Tracheal stenosis
answers.pearl: Post-intubation or tracheostomy scarring causes cough, stridor and wheeze that mimic asthma.

answers.name: Achalasia
answers.pearl: Retained esophageal contents cause regurgitation and nocturnal cough or aspiration.

answers.name: Tracheobronchomalacia
answers.pearl: Expiratory airway collapse causes a barking cough and recurrent infection, shown on dynamic CT or bronchoscopy.

answers.name: Inhaled medication cough
answers.pearl: Dry powder inhalers and inhaled corticosteroids can irritate the airway and cause cough.

answers.name: Arnold nerve ear-cough reflex
answers.pearl: Stimulation of the auricular branch of the vagus by wax or a foreign body in the ear canal can trigger cough.

answers.name: Tracheoesophageal fistula
answers.pearl: Acquired fistula in adults (cancer, ventilator, trauma) causes cough with every swallow.

answers.name: Relapsing polychondritis
answers.pearl: Cartilage inflammation in the airway causes cough, stridor and collapse, often with ear and nose chondritis.

answers.name: Tracheobronchial amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Submucosal amyloid deposits narrow the airways and can present with chronic cough and hemoptysis.

answers.name: Mounier-Kuhn syndrome
answers.pearl: Tracheobronchomegaly with dilated central airways leads to ineffective clearance, chronic cough and recurrent infection.

answers.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
answers.pearl: Early-onset emphysema and chronic cough in a nonsmoker or young patient with basilar-predominant disease.

answers.name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia
answers.pearl: Defective mucociliary clearance leads to year-round wet cough, sinusitis and bronchiectasis (Kartagener syndrome with situs inversus).

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Asthma, eosinophilia and vasculitis (Churg-Strauss) present with cough from airway disease or pulmonary infiltrates.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypokalemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pseudohypokalemia (in-vitro cellular uptake with marked leukocytosis, not true hypokalemia); Acute monocytic leukemia (lysozyme-mediated renal wasting, uncommon); Reninoma (rare tumor); Toluene inhalation via distal RTA; Barium poisoning (toxicology literature); Treatment of megaloblastic anemia; Potassium binders (iatrogenic overcorrection); Theophylline toxicity. Bartter, Gitelman and Liddle syndromes scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Furosemide and related drugs increase distal sodium delivery and aldosterone effects, wasting potassium in urine.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause renal potassium wasting along with metabolic alkalosis, and the effect is dose dependent.

answers.name: Vomiting
answers.pearl: Gastric potassium loss is small; hypokalemia comes from bicarbonaturia and aldosterone-driven renal wasting after volume depletion and alkalosis.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Colonic fluid is potassium-rich, so secretory or infectious diarrhea causes large stool losses.

answers.name: Poor oral intake
answers.pearl: Inadequate intake rarely causes hypokalemia alone because the kidney conserves potassium, but it contributes with other losses.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: Low magnesium disinhibits renal outer medullary potassium channels, causing wasting and refractory hypokalemia until Mg is replaced.

answers.name: Insulin therapy
answers.pearl: Insulin drives potassium into cells via Na-K ATPase, a key reason for monitoring in DKA treatment.

answers.name: Beta-agonists
answers.pearl: Beta-2 stimulation shifts potassium intracellularly, a recognized effect of nebulized albuterol.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use causes colonic potassium loss and volume depletion, and the history is often concealed in eating disorders.

answers.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Autonomous aldosterone causes hypertension, hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis, though normokalemia is common.

answers.name: Metabolic alkalosis
answers.pearl: Alkalemia shifts potassium into cells and increases renal losses, and the two problems often coexist.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids, particularly those with mineralocorticoid activity, cause renal potassium wasting.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Cortisol excess overwhelms 11-beta-HSD2 and acts on the mineralocorticoid receptor, causing hypokalemia, especially with ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Nasogastric suction
answers.pearl: Continuous gastric drainage causes volume and chloride loss with alkalosis and renal potassium wasting.

answers.name: Renal tubular acidosis
answers.pearl: Proximal (type 2) and distal (type 1) RTA both cause hypokalemic non-anion gap acidosis.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin increases distal tubular permeability, causing potassium and magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Eating disorders
answers.pearl: Bulimia and anorexia combine vomiting, laxative and diuretic use, and starvation; severe hypokalemia is common and arrhythmogenic.

answers.name: Renal replacement therapy
answers.pearl: Low-potassium dialysate or high-volume CRRT can overshoot into hypokalemia, especially in intensive care.

answers.name: Refeeding syndrome
answers.pearl: Insulin surge and anabolic cell uptake drive potassium, phosphate and magnesium into cells on refeeding.

answers.name: High-output ostomy or fistula
answers.pearl: Ileostomy and enterocutaneous fistula losses are potassium-rich and cause hypokalemia, volume depletion and acidosis.

answers.name: Osmotic diuresis
answers.pearl: Glucosuria or mannitol increases tubular flow and potassium excretion, with hypokalemia often masked at presentation in DKA.

answers.name: Sodium bicarbonate administration
answers.pearl: Alkali therapy shifts potassium into cells and increases urinary potassium loss.

answers.name: Licorice ingestion
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhetinic acid inhibits 11-beta-HSD2, causing apparent mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Ectopic ACTH syndrome
answers.pearl: Tumors such as small cell lung cancer or bronchial carcinoid produce severe hypercortisolism with profound hypokalemia.

answers.name: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: Hyperthyroidism with a Na-K ATPase surge causes episodic paralysis with hypokalemia, mainly in Asian men.

answers.name: Villous adenoma
answers.pearl: Large secretory colorectal adenomas can produce profuse mucous diarrhea with hypokalemia and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Renovascular hypertension causes secondary hyperaldosteronism with potassium wasting.

answers.name: Post-obstructive diuresis
answers.pearl: Relief of urinary obstruction produces a brisk solute and water diuresis with urinary potassium loss.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycoside tubular toxicity causes renal wasting of potassium and magnesium.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents cause tubular injury with magnesium and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction causes glucosuria, phosphaturia, bicarbonate and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Familial hypokalemic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: Calcium or sodium channel mutations cause attacks of flaccid paralysis with hypokalemia, triggered by carbohydrate meals or rest after exercise.

answers.name: VIPoma
answers.pearl: Pancreatic VIP tumors cause profuse watery diarrhea, hypokalemia and achlorhydria (Verner-Morrison).

answers.name: Penicillin antibiotics
answers.pearl: High-dose penicillins act as non-reabsorbable anions in the distal tubule, increasing potassium secretion.

answers.name: Treatment of megaloblastic anemia
answers.pearl: Brisk hematopoiesis after B12 or folate repletion consumes potassium and can cause severe hypokalemia.

answers.name: Potassium binders
answers.pearl: Overuse of sodium polystyrene or other binders can cause potassium depletion, particularly with diarrhea.

answers.name: Acute monocytic leukemia
answers.pearl: Lysozymuria from monocytic blasts causes proximal tubular injury and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
answers.pearl: 11-beta-HSD2 deficiency allows cortisol to activate the mineralocorticoid receptor, causing hypertension with low renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
answers.pearl: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I from an ACTH-responsive chimeric gene, treated with glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Theophylline toxicity
answers.pearl: Methylxanthines produce beta-adrenergic hypokalemia, often with tachyarrhythmias and seizures.

answers.name: Pseudohypokalemia
answers.pearl: In vitro potassium uptake by white cells in very high WBC counts lowers the measured value in a standing sample.

answers.name: Barium poisoning
answers.pearl: Barium blocks potassium efflux channels, causing intracellular shift and profound hypokalemia with paralysis.

answers.name: Reninoma
answers.pearl: A juxtaglomerular tumor secretes renin, causing secondary hyperaldosteronism, hypertension and hypokalemia in young patients.

answers.name: Toluene inhalation
answers.pearl: Glue sniffing causes distal RTA with hypokalemic non-anion gap acidosis and rhabdomyolysis.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome
answers.pearl: Loop of Henle transport defects cause hypokalemic alkalosis with hypercalciuria and normal blood pressure.

answers.name: Gitelman syndrome
answers.pearl: NCC defect (thiazide-like) with hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and hypocalciuria, usually presenting in adolescence or adulthood.

answers.name: Liddle syndrome
answers.pearl: ENaC gain of function causes hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis with low renin and aldosterone, responding to amiloride.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of an elevated alkaline phosphatase.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hyperthyroidism (mild bone-derived rise); Transient hyperphosphatasemia of infancy; Macro-ALP (immunoglobulin-bound enzyme, rare); Tumor-induced osteomalacia (rare, FGF23 mediated); Hungry bone syndrome; Vanishing bile duct syndrome; Lymphoma and Sarcoidosis (infiltrative pattern); Sepsis cholestasis; Osteosarcoma, Alagille syndrome and X-linked hypophosphatemia scored as Board Prep Traps. Hypophosphatasia deliberately excluded (low ALP).

answers.name: Biliary obstruction
answers.pearl: Obstruction increases hepatic ALP synthesis, and the elevation often precedes the bilirubin rise.

answers.name: Choledocholithiasis
answers.pearl: Stones in the common bile duct cause obstructive cholestasis with pain and cholangitis risk.

answers.name: Bone metastases
answers.pearl: Osteoblastic and mixed metastases raise ALP through increased bone formation, particularly with prostate and breast cancer.

answers.name: Hepatic metastases
answers.pearl: Infiltrative liver disease gives an isolated ALP rise with normal bilirubin.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Chronic liver disease often shows a modest ALP elevation with predominant transaminase and bilirubin abnormalities.

answers.name: Paget disease of bone
answers.pearl: Disordered, high-turnover remodeling causes a markedly raised ALP with normal calcium and normal GGT.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Placental alkaline phosphatase rises in the third trimester and is a normal finding.

answers.name: Fracture healing
answers.pearl: Osteoblastic activity during callus formation raises bone ALP for weeks to months.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Osteomalacia and rickets raise ALP with low or normal calcium and phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune destruction of small bile ducts in middle-aged women with antimitochondrial antibodies.

answers.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: Beaded strictures on MRCP, strong association with ulcerative colitis, and risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

answers.name: Cholangitis
answers.pearl: Acute ascending infection of an obstructed biliary tree causes fever, jaundice and RUQ pain (Charcot triad).

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer
aliases: carcinoma of the head of the pancreas
answers.pearl: A pancreatic head tumor obstructs the distal bile duct, causing painless jaundice with a rising ALP.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: HCC in cirrhotic patients may raise ALP and should be checked with imaging and AFP.

answers.name: Drug-induced cholestasis
answers.pearl: Cholestatic or mixed liver injury from drugs such as amoxicillin-clavulanate, anabolic steroids or chlorpromazine.

answers.name: Adolescent growth spurt
answers.pearl: Bone ALP is physiologically high in growing children and peaks during puberty.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Increased osteoclast and osteoblast activity in PTH excess, notably in osteitis fibrosa cystica.

answers.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Hilar (Klatskin) and intrahepatic bile duct tumors cause obstruction with ALP-predominant cholestasis.

answers.name: Fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: NAFLD/MASLD and steatohepatitis can raise ALP and GGT modestly alongside transaminases.

answers.name: Viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Cholestatic hepatitis A or hepatitis B/C can produce a moderate ALP rise.

answers.name: Congestive hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Passive hepatic congestion from right heart failure causes a cholestatic pattern with raised ALP.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Increased bone turnover in thyrotoxicosis elevates bone-derived ALP.

answers.name: CKD-mineral bone disorder
answers.pearl: Secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal osteodystrophy raise ALP in advanced CKD.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Hepatic granulomas cause an isolated ALP elevation with or without cholestasis.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Cytokine-mediated impairment of bile transport causes cholestasis in critical illness.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Prolonged TPN causes steatosis and cholestasis, with gallbladder stasis contributing.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Hepatic infiltration or biliary compression by nodes, especially Hodgkin lymphoma, can raise ALP.

answers.name: Liver abscess
answers.pearl: Pyogenic and amebic abscesses raise ALP with fever and RUQ pain.

answers.name: Gallbladder cancer
answers.pearl: Often diagnosed late with biliary obstruction by direct invasion.

answers.name: Postoperative bile duct stricture
answers.pearl: Iatrogenic bile duct injury after cholecystectomy or transplant causes progressive cholestasis.

answers.name: Chronic pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Fibrosis of the pancreatic head can compress the intrapancreatic bile duct.

answers.name: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Pruritus in the third trimester with raised bile acids; ALP also reflects the placental component.

answers.name: Granulomatous liver disease
answers.pearl: Hepatic granulomas from TB, sarcoid, drugs or fungi produce an infiltrative ALP elevation.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Hepatic amyloid deposition gives ALP elevation and hepatomegaly with modest bilirubin changes.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction causes ascites, hepatomegaly and abdominal pain.

answers.name: Graft-versus-host disease
answers.pearl: Hepatic GVHD after allogeneic transplant causes cholestasis with elevated ALP and bilirubin.

answers.name: Mirizzi syndrome
answers.pearl: A stone impacted in the cystic duct or gallbladder neck compresses the common hepatic duct.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: IgG4 sclerosing cholangitis and autoimmune pancreatitis mimic PSC or pancreatic cancer and respond to steroids.

answers.name: Vanishing bile duct syndrome
answers.pearl: Progressive ductopenia from drugs, chronic rejection, GVHD or lymphoma leads to cholestasis.

answers.name: Hungry bone syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid skeletal remineralization after parathyroidectomy lowers calcium and raises ALP.

answers.name: AIDS cholangiopathy
answers.pearl: Opportunistic infection (Cryptosporidium, CMV, microsporidia) of the biliary tract at low CD4 counts.

answers.name: Stauffer syndrome
aliases: renal cell carcinoma paraneoplastic liver dysfunction
answers.pearl: Nonmetastatic hepatic dysfunction from renal cell carcinoma with raised ALP that resolves after nephrectomy.

answers.name: Transient hyperphosphatasemia of infancy
answers.pearl: A benign, self-limited marked ALP rise in young children, usually with a viral illness and normal liver tests.

answers.name: Macro-ALP
answers.pearl: Alkaline phosphatase complexed with immunoglobulin gives a persistently raised level, with ulcerative colitis and autoimmune disorders as associations.

answers.name: Tumor-induced osteomalacia
answers.pearl: FGF23-secreting mesenchymal tumors cause renal phosphate wasting, osteomalacia and raised ALP.

answers.name: Osteosarcoma
answers.pearl: A high-grade bone tumor of adolescents whose ALP level has prognostic value.

answers.name: Alagille syndrome
answers.pearl: JAG1 mutation causes bile duct paucity with cholestasis, butterfly vertebrae, posterior embryotoxon and peripheral pulmonic stenosis.

answers.name: X-linked hypophosphatemia
answers.pearl: PHEX mutation causes FGF23 excess, rickets/osteomalacia and raised bone ALP.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of a pleural effusion.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Esophageal variceal sclerotherapy (documented, rare); Thoracic endometriosis; Pseudochylothorax; Urinothorax; Misplaced central venous catheter; Paragonimiasis; Subphrenic abscess (sympathetic effusion); Radiation therapy; Benign asbestos effusion; Meigs syndrome, Dressler syndrome, Esophageal rupture (Boerhaave) and Yellow nail syndrome scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Congestive heart failure
answers.pearl: The leading cause of transudative effusions, usually bilateral or right-sided, resolving with diuresis.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Parapneumonic effusions are exudates; a pH under 7.2 or loculation indicates complicated effusion needing drainage.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Malignant effusions are exudative and often hemorrhagic; cytology is positive in about 60%.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Occurs in a minority of PE patients, usually small and exudative with pulmonary infarction.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Ascitic fluid passes through diaphragmatic defects, most often into the right pleural space (hepatic hydrothorax).

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Low oncotic pressure and sodium retention cause bilateral transudates.

answers.name: Empyema
answers.pearl: Pus in the pleural space, with positive culture or Gram stain, or pH under 7.2, needs drainage.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Lymphocyte-predominant exudate with elevated ADA, which often presents as primary TB in younger patients.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Direct or hematogenous pleural spread by adenocarcinoma is the most common cause of malignant effusion.

answers.name: Fluid overload
answers.pearl: Positive fluid balance and renal failure cause transudates, often bilateral.

answers.name: Breast cancer
answers.pearl: The second most common cause of malignant effusion, which may appear years after initial treatment.

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Low oncotic pressure from malnutrition or protein loss allows transudation of fluid.

answers.name: Hemothorax
answers.pearl: Pleural fluid hematocrit over 50% of blood from trauma, vascular injury or iatrogenic causes.

answers.name: Post-cardiac surgery
answers.pearl: Common after CABG, especially left-sided, due to pleural injury and inflammation, and usually resolves.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Left-sided effusion with very high amylase from a pancreatico-pleural fistula or inflammation.

answers.name: Atelectasis
answers.pearl: Collapsed lung increases negative interstitial pressure and produces small transudates.

answers.name: Mesothelioma
answers.pearl: Asbestos-related pleural cancer causing a progressive, often bloody exudate that frequently needs pleural biopsy.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid pleurisy gives exudates with very low glucose, low pH, high LDH and a high rheumatoid factor.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus serositis causes small bilateral exudates, with pleural fluid ANA titers elevated.

answers.name: Subphrenic abscess
answers.pearl: Sympathetic sterile effusion from abdominal infection adjacent to the diaphragm.

answers.name: Radiation therapy
answers.pearl: Radiation pleuritis causes effusion weeks to months after thoracic radiotherapy.

answers.name: Chylothorax
answers.pearl: Milky effusion with triglycerides over 110 mg/dL from thoracic duct injury or obstruction, commonly lymphoma or surgery.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Myxedema can cause serous effusions in pleural and pericardial spaces, which clear with thyroid replacement.

answers.name: Uremic pleuritis
answers.pearl: Fibrinous inflammation in advanced renal failure causes a bloody or serous exudate.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Leakage or rupture of blood into the pleural space, usually left-sided hemothorax in thoracic aortic emergencies.

answers.name: Drug-induced pleural disease
answers.pearl: Amiodarone, nitrofurantoin, methotrexate, dasatinib and others can cause pleural effusion, often eosinophilic.

answers.name: Benign asbestos pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Exudate occurring within years of asbestos exposure and diagnosed after excluding mesothelioma.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial constriction raises venous pressures and causes pleural effusion with ascites and edema.

answers.name: Trapped lung
answers.pearl: Visceral pleural fibrosis prevents re-expansion, producing a persistent transudative or lymphocytic effusion with high negative pressures on thoracentesis.

answers.name: Peritoneal dialysis
answers.pearl: Pleuroperitoneal communication causes a massive glucose-rich effusion (hydrothorax) soon after dialysate infusion.

answers.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Restrictive cardiomyopathy raises filling pressures, causing recurrent bilateral effusions refractory to diuresis.

answers.name: Misplaced central venous catheter
answers.pearl: Catheter tip erosion into the pleura leads to infusion of fluids or parenteral nutrition into the pleural space.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Pleural involvement is uncommon but causes lymphocytic exudative effusion in stage II-III disease.

answers.name: Amebic liver abscess
answers.pearl: A right-sided sympathetic or rupture-related effusion; rupture into the pleura can produce anchovy-paste empyema.

answers.name: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
answers.pearl: Capillary leak after gonadotropins produces ascites and pleural effusion in fertility treatment.

answers.name: Urinothorax
answers.pearl: Obstructive uropathy or retroperitoneal urine leak can enter the pleural space with a transudate that smells of urine and has a pleural-to-serum creatinine ratio above 1.

answers.name: Paragonimiasis
answers.pearl: Lung fluke infection acquired from raw crustaceans causes an eosinophilic effusion and pulmonary cysts.

answers.name: Thoracic endometriosis
answers.pearl: Catamenial hemothorax and pneumothorax occur within 72 hours of menses, usually right-sided.

answers.name: Pseudochylothorax
answers.pearl: Chronic effusions (rheumatoid, TB) accumulate cholesterol crystals and look milky, with cholesterol over 200 mg/dL.

answers.name: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
answers.pearl: Cystic lung disease in women of childbearing age with chylous effusions, tuberous sclerosis link and response to sirolimus.

answers.name: Esophageal variceal sclerotherapy
answers.pearl: Injection sclerotherapy causes sclerosant-induced mediastinal and pleural inflammation with effusion.

answers.name: Meigs syndrome
aliases: ovarian fibroma with ascites and effusion
answers.pearl: Benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion, resolving after tumor removal.

answers.name: Dressler syndrome
answers.pearl: Post-MI or postcardiac injury pericarditis and pleuritis weeks after infarction, with fever and pleuropericardial effusion.

answers.name: Esophageal rupture
answers.pearl: Boerhaave syndrome causes a left-sided effusion with very high salivary-type amylase and low pH after vomiting.

answers.name: Yellow nail syndrome
answers.pearl: Triad of yellow dystrophic nails, lymphedema and respiratory disease, including recurrent pleural effusions.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of macrocytic anemia (elevated MCV).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cigarette smoking (mild macrocytosis, not true anemia on its own); Cold agglutinin disease and Severe hyperglycemia (spurious MCV elevation, not true macrocytosis); Triamterene and Sulfasalazine (folate antagonism, uncommon); Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia (rare genetic); Imerslund-Grasbeck, Transcobalamin II and congenital intrinsic factor deficiency (rare); Neonatal macrocytosis; Nitrous oxide. Fish tapeworm infection, Hereditary orotic aciduria and Diamond-Blackfan anemia scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired DNA synthesis causes megaloblastic anemia with hypersegmented neutrophils, and neurologic findings may occur without anemia.

answers.name: Folate deficiency
answers.pearl: Poor diet, alcohol, pregnancy or antifolates cause megaloblastic anemia without neurologic disease.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol directly causes macrocytosis, independent of folate deficiency or liver disease, and may resolve within months of abstinence.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Low thyroid hormone causes a mild macrocytic anemia, with possible coexistent pernicious anemia.

answers.name: Liver disease
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis produces macrocytosis through altered red cell membrane lipids, often with target cells.

answers.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome
answers.pearl: Clonal ineffective hematopoiesis in older adults causes macrocytic anemia with dysplasia and sometimes cytopenias.

answers.name: Pernicious anemia
answers.pearl: Autoimmune loss of intrinsic factor with anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies causes B12 malabsorption.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Folate antagonist that inhibits DHFR, leading to macrocytosis and megaloblastic changes.

answers.name: Hydroxyurea
answers.pearl: Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor causing macrocytosis, which is used as a marker of adherence.

answers.name: Reticulocytosis
answers.pearl: Young red cells are larger, so a high reticulocyte response after bleeding or hemolysis raises MCV.

answers.name: Dietary B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: Strict vegetarian or vegan diets without supplements deplete B12 stores over years.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Brisk hemolysis with reticulocytosis can macrocytose red cells, and coexisting folate deficiency adds to this.

answers.name: Gastric bypass or gastrectomy
answers.pearl: Loss of intrinsic factor and acid reduces B12 absorption, and deficiency may take years to develop.

answers.name: Zidovudine
answers.pearl: AZT and other NRTIs commonly cause macrocytosis, even without anemia, as a drug effect.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Long-term use can reduce ileal B12 absorption and cause B12 deficiency.

answers.name: Terminal ileal disease
answers.pearl: The ileum absorbs the B12-intrinsic factor complex, so Crohn disease or resection causes deficiency.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Proximal small bowel injury causes malabsorption of folate, and less often B12.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Purine analogs 6-mercaptopurine and azathioprine commonly raise MCV, an indicator of thiopurine exposure.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Reduced gastric acid impairs release of food-bound B12 with long-term use.

answers.name: Atrophic gastritis
answers.pearl: Chronic atrophic gastritis, including H. pylori, impairs acid and intrinsic factor secretion.

answers.name: Trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim inhibits bacterial and, at high doses, human DHFR, causing megaloblastic changes.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Anticonvulsants impair folate absorption and metabolism, leading to macrocytosis.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Antimetabolites such as 5-FU, cytarabine and capecitabine interfere with DNA synthesis.

answers.name: Cigarette smoking
answers.pearl: Smokers show a modest rise in MCV compared with nonsmokers, usually without anemia.

answers.name: Aplastic anemia
answers.pearl: Marrow failure with pancytopenia and a mildly raised MCV in many cases.

answers.name: Neonatal macrocytosis
answers.pearl: Newborns have physiologically high MCV values that decline over the first months of life.

answers.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
answers.pearl: Bacteria consume B12 and produce folate, so blind-loop syndrome causes B12 deficiency.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate commonly causes macrocytosis, with or without anemia, and it is often dose-related.

answers.name: Nitrous oxide
answers.pearl: Nitrous oxide oxidizes cobalamin and inactivates methionine synthase, producing megaloblastic changes and myeloneuropathy after chronic recreational use.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Impairs folate absorption and causes macrocytosis and sometimes hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.

answers.name: Sideroblastic anemia
answers.pearl: Alcohol, drugs, copper deficiency and clonal disease (MDS with ring sideroblasts) cause acquired forms that may be macrocytic.

answers.name: Acute myeloid leukemia
answers.pearl: Dysplastic erythropoiesis in AML, especially erythroid leukemia, raises MCV.

answers.name: Copper deficiency
answers.pearl: Gastric bypass, zinc excess and malabsorption cause anemia mimicking MDS with a B12-like myeloneuropathy.

answers.name: Tropical sprue
answers.pearl: Chronic diarrhea and malabsorption in endemic areas cause folate and B12 deficiency, and antibiotic therapy plus folate is curative.

answers.name: Fanconi anemia
aliases: inherited bone marrow failure with radial anomalies
answers.pearl: Inherited DNA repair defect with macrocytosis, pancytopenia, short stature and radial ray anomalies.

answers.name: Triamterene
answers.pearl: Weak folate antagonist that can contribute to megaloblastic anemia in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Cold agglutinin disease
answers.pearl: Red cell agglutination in an automated counter spuriously raises MCV and lowers the red cell count.

answers.name: Imerslund-Grasbeck syndrome
answers.pearl: Selective ileal B12 malabsorption with proteinuria from cubilin or amnionless mutations, presenting in childhood.

answers.name: Severe hyperglycemia
answers.pearl: Osmotic swelling of red cells in vitro falsely raises MCV, which normalizes when glucose is corrected.

answers.name: Transcobalamin II deficiency
answers.pearl: Defective B12 transport causes severe megaloblastic anemia in infancy despite a normal serum B12.

answers.name: Congenital intrinsic factor deficiency
answers.pearl: Inherited absence of intrinsic factor causes B12 deficiency from childhood without gastric atrophy.

answers.name: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
answers.pearl: SLC19A2 mutation causes megaloblastic anemia, diabetes mellitus and sensorineural deafness, improving with thiamine.

answers.name: Fish tapeworm infection
answers.pearl: Diphyllobothrium latum competes for dietary B12 and causes megaloblastic anemia, after eating raw freshwater fish.

answers.name: Hereditary orotic aciduria
answers.pearl: Pyrimidine synthesis defect (UMPS) with megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12 or folate, treated with uridine.

answers.name: Diamond-Blackfan anemia
answers.pearl: Congenital pure red cell aplasia in infancy with macrocytosis, ribosomal protein defects and elevated adenosine deaminase.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of chronic diarrhea (lasting more than 4 weeks).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Congenital chloride diarrhea (lifelong, rarely first diagnosed in adults), Somatostatinoma (diarrhea inconsistent, mostly case series), Medullary thyroid carcinoma (only in advanced disease), Autoimmune enteropathy, Olmesartan enteropathy. Whipple disease, carcinoid syndrome and VIPoma scored as board traps.

answers.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
answers.pearl: Diarrhea-predominant IBS is the most common cause of chronic diarrhea, but it is a diagnosis of exclusion that needs alarm features absent.

answers.name: Lactose intolerance
answers.pearl: Lactase deficiency causes osmotic diarrhea, bloating, and gas after dairy that resolves with avoidance.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Gluten-triggered villous atrophy causes malabsorptive diarrhea; screen with tissue transglutaminase IgA plus total IgA.

answers.name: Ulcerative colitis
answers.pearl: Bloody diarrhea with urgency and tenesmus from continuous colonic inflammation starting in the rectum.

answers.name: Crohn disease
answers.pearl: Skip-lesion transmural inflammation, most often of the terminal ileum, can cause diarrhea, weight loss, and fistulas.

answers.name: Medication-induced diarrhea
answers.pearl: Metformin, magnesium-containing antacids, antibiotics, colchicine, and many others commonly cause chronic diarrhea, so always review the medication list.

answers.name: Giardiasis
answers.pearl: Giardia lamblia causes chronic watery, greasy diarrhea with bloating, diagnosed by stool antigen or PCR.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Thyroid hormone excess increases gut motility and causes frequent loose stools alongside weight loss and tachycardia.

answers.name: Colorectal cancer
answers.pearl: A change in bowel habit with bleeding or iron deficiency in an older adult warrants colonoscopy.

answers.name: Chronic pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Loss of exocrine function leads to fat malabsorption and greasy, foul stools once lipase output falls below about 10 percent.

answers.name: Clostridioides difficile infection
answers.pearl: Recurrent or persistent C. difficile can cause diarrhea lasting weeks after antibiotic exposure.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Surreptitious stimulant or osmotic laxative use produces chronic watery diarrhea; stool laxative screen and low stool osmotic gap or high magnesium clues help.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Chronic alcohol use causes diarrhea through rapid transit, pancreatic insufficiency, and mucosal injury.

answers.name: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Long-standing diabetes can cause intermittent, often nocturnal, watery diarrhea from enteric neuropathy and bacterial overgrowth.

answers.name: Fructose or sugar alcohol malabsorption
answers.pearl: Sorbitol in sugar-free gum and fructose in juice are poorly absorbed and cause osmotic diarrhea.

answers.name: Microscopic colitis
answers.pearl: Collagenous or lymphocytic colitis causes chronic watery diarrhea with a normal-looking colon, diagnosed only on biopsy and often linked to NSAIDs, PPIs, or SSRIs.

answers.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
answers.pearl: Bacterial overgrowth deconjugates bile acids and ferments carbohydrates, causing diarrhea, bloating, and B12 deficiency.

answers.name: Fecal impaction with overflow
answers.pearl: Liquid stool leaking around a rectal impaction mimics diarrhea in elderly or bedbound patients.

answers.name: Chemotherapy or radiation-related diarrhea
answers.pearl: Fluoropyrimidines, irinotecan, and other cytotoxics injure the gut mucosa and cause diarrhea that can persist.

answers.name: Short bowel syndrome
answers.pearl: After extensive resection, absorptive surface is inadequate and diarrhea and malabsorption result.

answers.name: Bile acid malabsorption
answers.pearl: Ileal disease or resection spills bile acids into the colon, causing secretory diarrhea that responds to cholestyramine.

answers.name: Post-cholecystectomy diarrhea
answers.pearl: Loss of the gallbladder reservoir increases bile acid delivery to the colon in a subset of patients.

answers.name: HIV enteropathy
answers.pearl: Advanced HIV causes chronic diarrhea through direct enteropathy, opportunistic pathogens, and antiretroviral side effects.

answers.name: Post-infectious IBS
answers.pearl: A subset of patients develop persistent IBS-type symptoms after bacterial gastroenteritis.

answers.name: Radiation enteritis
answers.pearl: Pelvic or abdominal radiation causes mucosal injury, bile acid malabsorption, and sometimes strictures or bacterial overgrowth.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor colitis
answers.pearl: PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 inhibitors can cause immune-mediated colitis that responds to steroids and sometimes infliximab or vedolizumab.

answers.name: Cryptosporidiosis
answers.pearl: Cryptosporidium causes prolonged watery diarrhea in immunocompromised patients, detected by modified acid-fast stain or antigen testing.

answers.name: Dumping syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid gastric emptying after gastrectomy or bariatric surgery causes early postprandial diarrhea, flushing, and tachycardia.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency commonly causes diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, and hyperpigmentation.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Pancreatic insufficiency causes steatorrhea, and milder genotypes can present in adulthood with pancreatitis or diarrhea.

answers.name: Graft-versus-host disease
aliases: graft versus host disease of the gut
answers.pearl: Intestinal GVHD after allogeneic transplant causes voluminous secretory diarrhea and is diagnosed by biopsy.

answers.name: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic infiltration of the gut wall causes diarrhea, pain, and sometimes ascites, with peripheral eosinophilia in many cases.

answers.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
answers.pearl: Gastrin-secreting tumors cause refractory peptic ulcers and secretory diarrhea from acid inactivating pancreatic enzymes.

answers.name: Tropical sprue
answers.pearl: Postinfectious malabsorption in people living in or returning from endemic tropical areas, responsive to tetracycline plus folate.
