answers.name: Olmesartan-associated enteropathy
answers.pearl: Olmesartan can cause severe sprue-like enteropathy with villous atrophy that resolves after stopping the drug.

answers.name: Intestinal amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposition in the gut or autonomic nerves causes diarrhea, malabsorption, and protein loss.

answers.name: Villous adenoma
answers.pearl: Large rectosigmoid villous adenomas can secrete mucus and potassium, causing chronic secretory diarrhea with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Intestinal lymphangiectasia
answers.pearl: Dilated lymphatics leak lymph into the gut, causing protein-losing enteropathy, steatorrhea, and lymphopenia.

answers.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
answers.pearl: Calcitonin and prostaglandin secretion cause watery diarrhea in advanced disease and may be accompanied by a thyroid nodule.

answers.name: Refractory celiac disease or enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Persistent diarrhea and weight loss despite a strict gluten-free diet should prompt evaluation for refractory sprue or EATL.

answers.name: Autoimmune enteropathy
answers.pearl: Anti-enterocyte antibodies and severe villous atrophy cause refractory diarrhea, typically unresponsive to a gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Somatostatinoma
answers.pearl: Somatostatin excess inhibits pancreatic enzymes and bile secretion, causing steatorrhea, gallstones, and diabetes.

answers.name: Congenital chloride diarrhea
answers.pearl: A SLC26A3 defect impairs chloride-bicarbonate exchange, causing lifelong watery diarrhea with metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Carcinoid syndrome
answers.pearl: Serotonin-secreting midgut neuroendocrine tumors with liver metastases cause watery diarrhea, flushing, and right-sided valvular disease.

answers.name: VIPoma
answers.pearl: A vasoactive intestinal peptide tumor causes profuse watery diarrhea with hypokalemia and achlorhydria (WDHA syndrome).

answers.name: Whipple disease
answers.pearl: Tropheryma whipplei infection causes chronic diarrhea, weight loss, arthralgia, and foamy PAS-positive macrophages on small bowel biopsy.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of an elevated ferritin.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hyperthyroidism (association is modest), Tuberculosis and Dengue (acute phase/macrophage activation; ferritin elevation well described but not a diagnostic tool), Bantu siderosis (regional dietary iron overload), Neuroblastoma (pediatric tumor marker), Sarcoidosis, Porphyria cutanea tarda. HLH, adult-onset Still disease, and hyperferritinemia-cataract syndrome scored as board traps.

answers.name: Inflammation
answers.pearl: Ferritin is an acute phase reactant, so any systemic inflammatory state raises it independent of iron stores.

answers.name: Hereditary hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: HFE (C282Y homozygosity) disease causes progressive iron overload, with high transferrin saturation as the discriminating test.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol increases ferritin through hepatocellular injury and enhanced iron absorption, even without overt liver disease.

answers.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: MASLD is among the most common causes of mildly to moderately high ferritin with normal transferrin saturation.

answers.name: Chronic liver disease
answers.pearl: Hepatocyte injury and Kupffer cell iron release raise ferritin in cirrhosis and chronic hepatitis.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Many cancers raise ferritin through inflammation, marrow involvement, and tumor production.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Inflammation and IV iron in CKD and dialysis patients raise ferritin, making iron deficiency harder to diagnose.

answers.name: Metabolic syndrome
answers.pearl: Insulin resistance is associated with hyperferritinemia and mild hepatic iron accumulation (dysmetabolic iron overload).

answers.name: Infection
answers.pearl: Many infections drive hepcidin up and ferritin synthesis up, producing elevated ferritin alongside low serum iron.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Septic shock can produce very high ferritin through macrophage activation and tissue injury.

answers.name: Transfusional iron overload
answers.pearl: Each unit of red cells delivers about 200 to 250 mg of iron, and the body has no excretory pathway.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Active RA raises ferritin as an acute phase reactant and with anemia of chronic disease.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus flares and macrophage activation can raise ferritin, and markedly high levels should raise concern for macrophage activation.

answers.name: Hepatitis C
answers.pearl: Chronic HCV raises ferritin through hepatic inflammation and iron deposition, and high levels predict worse treatment response and fibrosis.

answers.name: Acute hepatocellular injury
answers.pearl: Necrosis of hepatocytes releases stored ferritin, so acute hepatitis of any cause can raise it sharply.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Chronic hemolysis and ineffective erythropoiesis increase iron absorption and macrophage iron turnover.

answers.name: Anemia of chronic disease
answers.pearl: Hepcidin traps iron in macrophages, giving low serum iron, low TIBC, and normal to high ferritin.

answers.name: Intravenous iron or oral iron supplementation
answers.pearl: Recent iron administration transiently raises ferritin, and checking levels too soon after an infusion is misleading.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV is associated with elevated ferritin that tracks with disease activity and opportunistic infection.

answers.name: Thalassemia
answers.pearl: Ineffective erythropoiesis suppresses hepcidin and increases gut iron absorption, so even non-transfused patients accumulate iron.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma can raise ferritin through macrophage activation and disease burden.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Acute leukemia raises ferritin through inflammation, transfusions, and tumor lysis of iron-rich cells.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: HCC can raise ferritin through tumor secretion and underlying liver disease and iron overload.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Repeated transfusions and chronic hemolysis cause hepatic and cardiac iron loading.

answers.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome
answers.pearl: Transfusion dependence and ineffective erythropoiesis drive iron overload, and high ferritin is a poor prognostic marker.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous macrophage activation raises ferritin in active TB, sometimes dramatically in disseminated disease.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: Severe COVID-19 produces a hyperinflammatory state with markedly raised ferritin that tracks with outcomes.

answers.name: Tissue injury or rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Large-volume muscle or tissue necrosis releases intracellular ferritin into the circulation.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Active granulomatous disease can cause mild to moderate hyperferritinemia through macrophage activation.

answers.name: Sideroblastic anemia
answers.pearl: Impaired heme synthesis causes mitochondrial iron accumulation, ringed sideroblasts, and systemic iron overload.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Thyroid hormone excess is associated with higher ferritin, which falls after the euthyroid state is restored.

answers.name: Porphyria cutanea tarda
answers.pearl: Hepatic iron overload (often with HFE variants or hepatitis C) inhibits uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase and causes blistering skin lesions.

answers.name: Juvenile hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Mutations in HJV or HAMP cause severe early-onset iron overload with cardiomyopathy and hypogonadism.

answers.name: Dysmetabolic iron overload syndrome
aliases: insulin resistance hepatic iron overload syndrome
answers.pearl: Hyperferritinemia with mild hepatic iron deposition, normal transferrin saturation, and the metabolic syndrome.

answers.name: Dengue
answers.pearl: Dengue can cause marked hyperferritinemia and in severe cases a secondary HLH-like picture.

answers.name: Gaucher disease
answers.pearl: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency with macrophage activation raises ferritin even without iron overload, alongside splenomegaly and cytopenias.

answers.name: Ferroportin disease
answers.pearl: Hemochromatosis type 4 from SLC40A1 variants causes high ferritin with low to normal transferrin saturation and poor tolerance of phlebotomy in the loss-of-function form.

answers.name: Bantu siderosis
answers.pearl: Chronic dietary iron overload from traditional iron-brewed beer in sub-Saharan Africa, modulated by a ferroportin variant.

answers.name: Neuroblastoma
answers.pearl: Tumor-secreted ferritin and macrophage activation produce very high ferritin that serves as a prognostic marker.

answers.name: Atransferrinemia
answers.pearl: Absent transferrin causes hypochromic anemia with parenchymal iron overload because iron cannot reach erythroid cells.

answers.name: Aceruloplasminemia
answers.pearl: Absent ceruloplasmin traps iron in tissues, causing diabetes, retinal degeneration, neurologic disease, and high ferritin with low serum iron.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Ferritin above 10,000 is highly suggestive of HLH in adults, with fever, cytopenias, and hepatosplenomegaly.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Very high ferritin with a low glycosylated fraction accompanies quotidian fever, salmon rash, and arthritis.

answers.name: Hyperferritinemia-cataract syndrome
answers.pearl: Mutations in the L-ferritin IRE cause constitutively high serum ferritin with normal iron stores and early cataracts.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of delirium in a hospitalized older adult.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation and Intravascular lymphoma (case-series level), Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (usually subacute rather than delirium), Valproate hyperammonemic encephalopathy, Dopaminergic medication withdrawal, Brain metastases. Wernicke encephalopathy, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and acute intermittent porphyria scored as board traps.

answers.name: Urinary tract infection
answers.pearl: UTI is the classic trigger in older adults, though asymptomatic bacteriuria should not be treated reflexively when delirium has another cause.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Older adults with pneumonia often present with confusion rather than cough or fever.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Systemic infection with hypoperfusion is a leading cause of acute brain dysfunction (septic encephalopathy).

answers.name: Anticholinergic medications
answers.pearl: Diphenhydramine, oxybutynin, and tricyclics are Beers-list drugs that are major deliriogenic offenders.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids, particularly meperidine, can precipitate delirium, though untreated pain is also a trigger.

answers.name: Benzodiazepines
answers.pearl: Sedative-hypnotics are among the strongest modifiable risk factors for delirium in older adults.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion and prerenal azotemia cause reduced cerebral perfusion and altered drug clearance.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Low serum sodium causes brain swelling and confusion, especially with acute decline.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Low blood glucose is quickly reversible and must be excluded with a point-of-care glucose in every confused patient.

answers.name: Urinary retention
answers.pearl: Bladder distension causes agitation and confusion that resolves after catheterization.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Fecal impaction is a frequently overlooked precipitant in older adults.

answers.name: Uncontrolled pain
answers.pearl: Untreated pain is an independent risk factor, and both under- and over-treatment can cause delirium.

answers.name: Sleep deprivation
answers.pearl: Noise, lights, and overnight vitals disrupt circadian rhythm, and sleep promotion is a core non-drug prevention strategy.

answers.name: Hyperglycemia
answers.pearl: Severe hyperglycemia with hyperosmolality or DKA reduces consciousness and is a common precipitant in diabetics.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Delirium tremens develops about 48 to 96 hours after the last drink, with autonomic hyperactivity and hallucinations.

answers.name: Hypoxia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia from any cause impairs cerebral function and can be subtle in older patients.

answers.name: Acute ischemic stroke
answers.pearl: Right hemisphere, thalamic, and posterior cerebral artery strokes can present as acute confusion without clear motor deficits.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Uremia and accumulation of renally cleared drugs both cause encephalopathy.

answers.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Elevated ammonia and other gut-derived toxins cause delirium in cirrhosis, often triggered by infection, GI bleeding, or constipation.

answers.name: Postoperative delirium
answers.pearl: Anesthesia, surgical stress, pain, and medications combine to cause delirium, particularly after hip fracture and cardiac surgery.

answers.name: Subdural hematoma
answers.pearl: Falls with minor trauma in anticoagulated or atrophic brains can cause a subacute SDH presenting with confusion.

answers.name: Sensory impairment
answers.pearl: Lack of glasses or hearing aids reduces orientation and increases delirium risk.

answers.name: Hypercapnia
answers.pearl: CO2 retention in COPD or sedative use produces narcosis with somnolence and confusion.

answers.name: Physical restraints and tethers
answers.pearl: Restraints, urinary catheters, and IV lines are modifiable risk factors that increase delirium and agitation.

answers.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Thiamine deficiency causes confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia, often incomplete, and should be treated empirically in at-risk patients.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Calcium above about 12 causes lethargy, confusion, and constipation, often from malignancy or hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Older adults with ACS may present with confusion alone because of low cardiac output or atypical symptoms.

answers.name: Meningitis or encephalitis
answers.pearl: CNS infection should be considered in febrile, confused patients, particularly with headache, neck stiffness, or seizures.

answers.name: Congestive heart failure
answers.pearl: Low cardiac output, hypoxia, and renal dysfunction from decompensated HF all contribute to delirium.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: High-dose steroids can cause steroid psychosis with mood changes, agitation, and delirium within days.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism and myxedema coma cause cognitive slowing, hypothermia, and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Nonconvulsive status epilepticus
answers.pearl: Ongoing electrographic seizures without convulsions cause fluctuating confusion and need EEG to diagnose.

answers.name: Benzodiazepine withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt discontinuation of chronic benzodiazepines or barbiturates on admission causes agitation, tremor, and delirium.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: B12 deficiency causes neuropsychiatric changes including confusion and cognitive decline, sometimes without anemia.

answers.name: Thyrotoxicosis
answers.pearl: Apathetic hyperthyroidism and thyroid storm in older adults can present with confusion, atrial fibrillation, and weight loss.

answers.name: Brain metastases
answers.pearl: Intracranial tumors can present as subacute confusion or personality change from edema, mass effect, or seizures.

answers.name: Temperature dysregulation
answers.pearl: Hypothermia and hyperthermia, including heat stroke, impair mentation, and older adults regulate temperature poorly.

answers.name: Adrenal crisis
answers.pearl: Acute cortisol deficiency, especially after abrupt steroid withdrawal or sepsis, causes hypotension, hyponatremia, and confusion.

answers.name: Dopaminergic medication withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation of levodopa or dopamine agonists can cause a parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia state with delirium.

answers.name: Autoimmune encephalitis
answers.pearl: Anti-NMDA receptor, LGI1, and other antibodies cause subacute confusion, seizures, and psychiatric symptoms.

answers.name: Valproate-induced hyperammonemic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Valproate can raise ammonia even with normal liver tests, causing confusion that responds to stopping the drug and sometimes carnitine.

answers.name: Neurosyphilis
answers.pearl: Tertiary syphilis can cause cognitive decline and confusion, diagnosed by CSF VDRL and treated with IV penicillin.

answers.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus, restricted diffusion on MRI, and periodic EEG complexes can mimic delirium early on.

answers.name: Hyperviscosity syndrome
answers.pearl: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia or myeloma with high paraprotein levels causes mucosal bleeding, visual change, and confusion.

answers.name: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation
answers.pearl: Subacute confusion with asymmetric vasogenic edema and microbleeds on MRI that responds to steroids.

answers.name: Intravascular lymphoma
answers.pearl: Lymphoma cells within small vessels cause fever, stroke-like episodes, and subacute encephalopathy, diagnosed by random skin or brain biopsy.

answers.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
answers.pearl: Dopamine antagonists cause fever, lead-pipe rigidity, autonomic instability, elevated CK, and delirium.

answers.name: Acute intermittent porphyria
answers.pearl: Acute attacks cause severe abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and hyponatremia, triggered by drugs, fasting, or infection.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of acute liver failure.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Bacillus cereus emetic toxin and Pennyroyal oil (case reports), Mitochondrial hepatopathy (POLG, mostly pediatric), Neonatal hemochromatosis/GALD (neonatal), Hepatitis C (very rare), VZV hepatitis (immunocompromised), Viral hemorrhagic fevers and Dengue (geographic). Wilson disease, Amanita phalloides, and Reye syndrome scored as board traps.

answers.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
answers.pearl: Dose-dependent hepatotoxicity from NAPQI is the leading cause of ALF in the US and UK, and N-acetylcysteine is the antidote.

answers.name: Hepatitis B
answers.pearl: Acute HBV, or reactivation in an immunosuppressed carrier, can cause fulminant hepatitis with a rapid course.

answers.name: Hepatitis A
answers.pearl: Hepatitis A rarely causes ALF but the risk rises with age and underlying chronic liver disease.

answers.name: Idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury
answers.pearl: Unpredictable reactions to drugs such as isoniazid, antibiotics, and anticonvulsants are the next most common cause after acetaminophen.

answers.name: Ischemic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Hypoperfusion from shock or cardiac failure causes massive transaminase elevation with rapid improvement after hemodynamic recovery.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Rarely, AIH presents as ALF, and steroid response is variable, so early transplant evaluation is important.

answers.name: Isoniazid hepatotoxicity
answers.pearl: Isoniazid is a leading drug cause of ALF, with risk rising with age, alcohol use, and slow acetylators.

answers.name: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Third-trimester microvesicular steatosis with coagulopathy, hypoglycemia, and encephalopathy requires prompt delivery.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets complicating preeclampsia can progress to hepatic rupture or infarction.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute hepatic vein thrombosis causes tender hepatomegaly, ascites, and liver failure, often with an underlying prothrombotic state.

answers.name: Hepatitis E
answers.pearl: HEV is particularly severe in pregnancy and in patients with chronic liver disease.

answers.name: Herpes simplex virus hepatitis
answers.pearl: HSV causes fulminant hepatitis with fever, marked transaminases, and little jaundice, especially in pregnancy or immunosuppression.

answers.name: Valproic acid toxicity
answers.pearl: Valproate causes hepatotoxicity through mitochondrial injury, and hyperammonemia may occur with normal liver tests.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Systemic infection with hypoperfusion and cytokine injury can cause hepatic dysfunction that progresses to ALF.

answers.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
answers.pearl: A leading cause of idiosyncratic cholestatic or mixed DILI, though ALF is uncommon.

answers.name: Herbal and dietary supplement hepatotoxicity
answers.pearl: Green tea extract, kava, bodybuilding supplements, and other products are an increasing cause of ALF.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus
answers.pearl: CMV can cause hepatitis in transplant and immunocompromised patients, and rarely ALF.

answers.name: Epstein-Barr virus
answers.pearl: EBV, especially with HLH or in immunocompromised hosts, can cause fulminant hepatitis.

answers.name: Ecstasy (MDMA)
answers.pearl: MDMA can cause fulminant hepatic failure through hyperthermia, serotonin excess, and direct toxicity.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Core temperature above 40 C causes direct hepatocellular injury and ALF.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil
answers.pearl: PTU can cause severe idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity and liver failure, so methimazole is preferred in most patients.

answers.name: Hepatitis C
answers.pearl: Acute HCV rarely causes ALF in the Western world.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Nitrofurantoin can cause acute hepatitis or chronic autoimmune-like liver injury that rarely leads to liver failure.

answers.name: Malignant infiltration of the liver
answers.pearl: Massive infiltration by lymphoma, breast cancer, or other metastases can cause ALF with hepatomegaly and elevated alkaline phosphatase.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Phenytoin hypersensitivity can cause a DRESS-like syndrome with hepatitis and liver failure.

answers.name: Ketoconazole
answers.pearl: Oral ketoconazole carries a boxed warning for severe hepatotoxicity and ALF.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine can cause acute hepatic necrosis through hypoperfusion, hyperthermia, and oxidative metabolites.

answers.name: Nevirapine
answers.pearl: Nevirapine causes hepatitis and hypersensitivity in the first weeks, with higher risk in women with high CD4 counts.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor hepatitis
answers.pearl: PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade causes immune-mediated hepatitis that is usually steroid responsive but can progress to ALF.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides can cause hypersensitivity hepatitis and rarely fulminant liver failure.

answers.name: Congestive hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Severe acute right-sided heart failure, tamponade, or tricuspid disease causes hepatic congestion and cardiogenic liver injury.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: HLH can cause fulminant hepatitis with fever, cytopenias, and extreme ferritin.

answers.name: Halothane hepatitis
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated injury from trifluoroacetylated hepatocyte proteins after repeated halothane exposure.

answers.name: Flutamide
answers.pearl: Flutamide has a boxed warning for severe liver injury, including fatal ALF.

answers.name: Tetracycline toxicity
answers.pearl: High-dose IV tetracycline in pregnancy was a classic cause of microvesicular steatosis and ALF.

answers.name: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic veno-occlusive disease after myeloablative conditioning or pyrrolizidine alkaloid ingestion causes painful hepatomegaly, weight gain, and jaundice.

answers.name: Varicella zoster virus hepatitis
answers.pearl: Disseminated VZV in immunocompromised or pregnant patients can cause fulminant hepatitis, sometimes before the rash appears.

answers.name: Dengue hepatitis
answers.pearl: Severe dengue can cause marked transaminase elevation and ALF through direct viral and immune-mediated injury.

answers.name: Industrial solvent or phosphorus poisoning
answers.pearl: Carbon tetrachloride, chloroform, and white phosphorus cause centrilobular necrosis and liver failure.

answers.name: Yellow fever
answers.pearl: Severe yellow fever causes massive hepatic necrosis with hemorrhage and is endemic in parts of Africa and South America.

answers.name: Viral hemorrhagic fevers
answers.pearl: Lassa, Ebola, and Rift Valley fever cause hepatic necrosis as part of multisystem disease.

answers.name: Pennyroyal oil toxicity
answers.pearl: Pulegone in pennyroyal oil, taken as an abortifacient or tea, causes hepatic necrosis via glutathione depletion.

answers.name: Mitochondrial hepatopathy
answers.pearl: POLG-related Alpers disease and other mitochondrial disorders can cause acute liver failure, particularly after valproate exposure.

answers.name: Neonatal hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Gestational alloimmune liver disease causes neonatal ALF with extrahepatic siderosis.

answers.name: Bacillus cereus emetic toxin
answers.pearl: Cereulide in contaminated rice dishes has caused fulminant hepatic failure with microvesicular steatosis in rare reports.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Acute presentation with Coombs-negative hemolysis, a low alkaline phosphatase to bilirubin ratio, and low uric acid in a young patient.

answers.name: Amanita phalloides poisoning
answers.pearl: Death cap ingestion causes a delayed hepatotoxic phase after initial GI symptoms, treated with supportive care, penicillin G, silibinin, or NAC.

answers.name: Reye syndrome
aliases: salicylate and viral infection in children
answers.pearl: Aspirin use during viral illness in children causes microvesicular steatosis, cerebral edema, and hyperammonemia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of generalized lymphadenopathy.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dermatopathic lymphadenopathy (usually regional), Hyperthyroidism (lymphoid hyperplasia, weak evidence), Trypanosomiasis, Filariasis, Paracoccidioidomycosis (geographic), Lymphomatoid granulomatosis (adenopathy not a prominent feature), Amyloidosis, Kimura disease, Cat scratch disease (usually regional). Kikuchi-Fujimoto, Castleman disease, and Rosai-Dorfman disease scored as board traps.

answers.name: Infectious mononucleosis
answers.pearl: EBV causes generalized, often posterior cervical adenopathy with pharyngitis, fever, and atypical lymphocytes.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: Persistent generalized lymphadenopathy is common in early and acute HIV, and recent exposure should prompt RNA testing.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma cause painless, rubbery adenopathy, often with B symptoms.

answers.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
answers.pearl: CLL causes generalized lymphadenopathy with lymphocytosis and smudge cells in older adults.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated or miliary TB, and scrofula in the neck, cause adenopathy that may caseate and drain.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Noncaseating granulomas cause hilar and extrathoracic adenopathy, with raised ACE and hypercalcemia in some cases.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lymphadenopathy occurs in about half of lupus patients, particularly during flares.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Active RA can cause reactive lymphadenopathy, with Castleman-like histology reported in some cases.

answers.name: Secondary syphilis
answers.pearl: Generalized painless adenopathy with a palmar and plantar rash and condyloma lata.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus
answers.pearl: CMV mononucleosis is heterophile-negative and produces fever, adenopathy, and hepatitis.

answers.name: Toxoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Toxoplasma gondii causes posterior cervical lymphadenopathy in immunocompetent hosts, often with a mononucleosis-like picture.

answers.name: Metastatic cancer
answers.pearl: Carcinomas from breast, lung, and others typically cause regional nodes, but widespread metastasis can cause generalized disease.

answers.name: Drug reaction
answers.pearl: Phenytoin, allopurinol, carbamazepine, and other drugs cause hypersensitivity with lymphadenopathy, rash, and fever.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Acute lymphoblastic and other leukemias can cause generalized nodal enlargement along with cytopenias.

answers.name: Viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Acute hepatitis B or A can cause mild generalized adenopathy and serum-sickness-like illness.

answers.name: Serum sickness
answers.pearl: Immune complex reactions to drugs or antitoxin cause fever, rash, arthralgia, and lymphadenopathy 1 to 2 weeks after exposure.

answers.name: Acute HIV seroconversion
answers.pearl: Acute retroviral syndrome causes fever, pharyngitis, rash, and generalized adenopathy before antibodies develop.

answers.name: Rubella
answers.pearl: Rubella causes posterior auricular, suboccipital, and cervical adenopathy that precedes the rash.

answers.name: Cat scratch disease
answers.pearl: Bartonella henselae usually causes regional adenopathy, but disseminated disease can cause generalized involvement.

answers.name: Adenovirus infection
answers.pearl: Adenovirus can cause pharyngoconjunctival fever with cervical adenopathy and, occasionally, generalized lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Measles
answers.pearl: Measles causes generalized lymphadenopathy, along with cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and Koplik spots.

answers.name: Brucellosis
answers.pearl: Zoonotic infection from unpasteurized dairy or livestock causing undulant fever, sweats, and lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic B-cell activation can cause lymphadenopathy and carries an increased risk of lymphoma.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Quotidian fevers, salmon-colored rash, arthritis, and lymphadenopathy with very high ferritin.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated histoplasmosis in endemic areas causes generalized adenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and cytopenias.

answers.name: Coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated Coccidioides infection in endemic Southwest US patients can involve lymph nodes.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Graves disease can produce generalized lymphoid hyperplasia with modest nodal enlargement.

answers.name: Dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammatory myopathies occasionally present with generalized adenopathy as part of the autoimmune picture.

answers.name: DRESS syndrome
aliases: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
answers.pearl: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms causes fever, rash, eosinophilia, hepatitis, and lymphadenopathy 2 to 8 weeks after drug exposure.

answers.name: Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex
answers.pearl: Advanced HIV with CD4 below 50 can cause fever, weight loss, and mesenteric or generalized lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with IgM paraprotein can cause adenopathy, splenomegaly, and hyperviscosity.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: Lymphadenopathy is common in IgG4-RD, which also causes autoimmune pancreatitis, sialadenitis, and retroperitoneal fibrosis.

answers.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
answers.pearl: CVID can cause lymphoid hyperplasia and granulomatous disease alongside recurrent infections.

answers.name: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Generalized lymphadenopathy with fever, rash, hypergammaglobulinemia, and autoimmune phenomena in an older adult.

answers.name: Sezary syndrome
answers.pearl: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with erythroderma, circulating atypical T cells, and generalized lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
answers.pearl: Sustained eosinophilia with organ damage may include lymphadenopathy in lymphocytic and myeloproliferative variants.

answers.name: Lymphatic filariasis
answers.pearl: Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia infection cause adenolymphangitis, lymphedema, and nodal enlargement in endemic areas.

answers.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
answers.pearl: Kala-azar causes fever, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and generalized lymphadenopathy in some regions.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Systemic AL amyloid can occasionally cause generalized nodal enlargement.

answers.name: African trypanosomiasis
answers.pearl: Early-stage Trypanosoma brucei infection causes posterior cervical nodes (Winterbottom sign).

answers.name: Kimura disease
answers.pearl: Subcutaneous masses and lymphadenopathy with marked eosinophilia and elevated IgE, mostly in Asian men.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Mast cell infiltration can cause lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and flushing.

answers.name: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
answers.pearl: FAS pathway defects cause chronic non-malignant lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and autoimmune cytopenias with elevated double-negative T cells.

answers.name: Paracoccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: South American fungal infection of the lungs, mucosa, and lymph nodes, with a juvenile form causing prominent lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
answers.pearl: Necrotizing histiocytic lymphadenitis causing tender cervical nodes and fever, mostly in young Asian women.

answers.name: Castleman disease
answers.pearl: Angiofollicular lymph node hyperplasia, with multicentric disease linked to HHV-8, IL-6, and systemic inflammatory symptoms.

answers.name: Rosai-Dorfman disease
answers.pearl: Sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy, with large painless cervical nodes and S100-positive emperipolesis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of splenomegaly.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mixed cryoglobulinemia, Babesiosis, POEMS syndrome (organomegaly is a minor criterion), Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, Tropical splenomegaly syndrome, Systemic mastocytosis. Gaucher disease, hairy cell leukemia, and Felty syndrome scored as board traps.

answers.name: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension
answers.pearl: Congestive splenomegaly from portal hypertension is the most common cause, often with thrombocytopenia from hypersplenism.

answers.name: Infectious mononucleosis
answers.pearl: EBV causes splenic enlargement in up to half of patients, with risk of rupture, so avoid contact sports for about 4 weeks.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Splenic involvement occurs in Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, sometimes with massive enlargement.

answers.name: Myelofibrosis
answers.pearl: Extramedullary hematopoiesis causes massive splenomegaly with teardrop cells and leukoerythroblastosis; JAK inhibitors can shrink the spleen.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Repeated Plasmodium infection causes splenic hyperplasia and sometimes tropical splenomegaly; rupture is a recognized complication.

answers.name: Chronic myeloid leukemia
answers.pearl: Massive splenomegaly with marked leukocytosis, left shift, and BCR-ABL translocation.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Extravascular hemolysis causes splenic hyperplasia due to increased red cell clearance.

answers.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
answers.pearl: CLL causes splenomegaly with lymphocytosis and smudge cells, and splenic enlargement indicates intermediate-stage disease.

answers.name: Polycythemia vera
answers.pearl: Splenomegaly occurs in about 40 percent of patients and reflects expanded erythropoiesis; JAK2 V617F is present in most.

answers.name: Hereditary spherocytosis
answers.pearl: Spherocytes are trapped in the spleen, causing hemolysis and splenomegaly with a positive osmotic fragility test or EMA binding test.

answers.name: Congestive heart failure
answers.pearl: Right-sided heart failure causes venous congestion that enlarges both the liver and the spleen.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Subacute endocarditis causes splenomegaly through immune hyperplasia and sometimes splenic infarct or abscess.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration of the spleen produces splenomegaly in a minority of patients.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Children with sickle cell anemia develop splenomegaly before autoinfarction, while adults with SC or S-beta thalassemia may retain big spleens.

answers.name: Thalassemia
answers.pearl: Ineffective erythropoiesis and hemolysis cause splenomegaly, especially in thalassemia intermedia and untransfused major disease.

answers.name: Portal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Thrombosis of the portal vein causes presinusoidal portal hypertension with splenomegaly and varices.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction causes ascites, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV causes splenomegaly through reactive hyperplasia, opportunistic infections, or lymphoma.

answers.name: Acute leukemia
answers.pearl: Leukemic infiltration produces moderate splenomegaly, especially in ALL and monocytic AML.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Splenomegaly can occur in active lupus, with functional hyposplenism also described.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Miliary or splenic tuberculosis can cause splenomegaly with caseating granulomas or abscesses.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus
answers.pearl: CMV mononucleosis often causes mild splenomegaly with fever and hepatitis.

answers.name: Typhoid fever
answers.pearl: Salmonella Typhi causes fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots, and splenomegaly in the second week.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis causes periportal fibrosis, portal hypertension, and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Splenic abscess
answers.pearl: Hematogenous seeding from endocarditis or sepsis in IV drug users causes a focal collection and enlargement.

answers.name: Brucellosis
answers.pearl: Zoonotic infection from unpasteurized dairy with undulant fever, sweats, and hepatosplenomegaly.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Longstanding seropositive RA can cause splenomegaly, even without the full triad of Felty syndrome.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: HLH causes fever, cytopenias, hepatosplenomegaly, high ferritin, and hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Splenic vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Often following pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer, it causes isolated gastric varices and splenomegaly (left-sided portal hypertension).

answers.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
answers.pearl: Kala-azar causes fever, massive splenomegaly, and pancytopenia in endemic areas and in immunocompromised travelers.

answers.name: Myelodysplastic or myeloproliferative overlap
answers.pearl: CMML and related overlap neoplasms often cause splenomegaly with monocytosis.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration of the spleen causes firm splenomegaly, with hyposplenic function sometimes found.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated histoplasmosis can cause hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and adrenal involvement.

answers.name: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis or adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammatory flares cause splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and macrophage activation.

answers.name: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma
answers.pearl: Indolent B-cell lymphoma with massive splenomegaly, villous lymphocytes, and association with hepatitis C.

answers.name: Babesiosis
answers.pearl: Babesia microti, tick-borne in the Northeast US, causes fever, hemolysis, and splenomegaly, especially in asplenic hosts.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Mast cell infiltration of the spleen, liver, and marrow causes organomegaly and cytopenias.

answers.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
answers.pearl: Granulomatous-lymphocytic disease and lymphoid hyperplasia in CVID can enlarge the spleen.

answers.name: Tropical splenomegaly syndrome
answers.pearl: Hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly from exaggerated immune response with high IgM and responsive to antimalarials.

answers.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia or HES variants can produce splenomegaly and organ infiltration.

answers.name: Niemann-Pick disease
answers.pearl: Sphingomyelinase deficiency (types A and B) produces hepatosplenomegaly with foam cells and interstitial lung disease.

answers.name: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Lymphoproliferation associated with hepatitis C can cause splenomegaly along with purpura and glomerulonephritis.

answers.name: POEMS syndrome
aliases: polyneuropathy organomegaly endocrinopathy M-protein skin changes
answers.pearl: Plasma cell dyscrasia with polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, M-protein, and skin changes, and elevated VEGF.

answers.name: Cystic echinococcosis
answers.pearl: Hydatid cysts of Echinococcus granulosus occasionally involve the spleen.

answers.name: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
answers.pearl: FAS pathway defects cause chronic splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and autoimmune cytopenias, with elevated double-negative T cells.

answers.name: Gaucher disease
answers.pearl: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes massive splenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone disease, treatable with enzyme replacement.

answers.name: Hairy cell leukemia
answers.pearl: Massive splenomegaly with pancytopenia, a dry marrow tap, BRAF V600E, and excellent response to cladribine.

answers.name: Felty syndrome
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid arthritis, splenomegaly, and neutropenia, usually in long-standing seropositive HLA-DR4 disease.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hyperkalemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: mannitol (solvent-drag shift, mainly in renal failure), drugs causing rhabdomyolysis (indirect), immune checkpoint inhibitors (via primary adrenal insufficiency, rare), propofol infusion syndrome, aminocaproic acid and arginine (case-report to labeling level), potassium iodide, esaxerenone (Japan only), nafamostat (mostly Japanese literature), stored red cell transfusion (a therapy rather than a drug), cardiac glycoside plants.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors lower aldosterone and efferent arteriolar tone, so hyperkalemia is greatest in CKD, diabetes and with potassium-sparing drugs.

answers.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers
answers.pearl: ARBs raise potassium through reduced aldosterone and are no safer than ACE inhibitors in this respect.

answers.name: Spironolactone
answers.pearl: Spironolactone blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor, and hyperkalemia is the main limit to its use in heart failure and resistant hypertension.

answers.name: Potassium supplements
answers.pearl: Oral or IV potassium chloride, phosphate or citrate causes hyperkalemia particularly when renal function is reduced.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC in the collecting duct like amiloride, and high-dose treatment in older or renally impaired patients often raises potassium.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs suppress renin and aldosterone and reduce renal perfusion, producing hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism.

answers.name: Amiloride
answers.pearl: Amiloride blocks epithelial sodium channels and impairs potassium secretion in the distal nephron.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers impair cellular potassium uptake and renin release, with nonselective agents most affected.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus causes a type 4 renal tubular acidosis picture with hyperkalemia and hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: Toxic digoxin levels inhibit the Na-K ATPase and cause hyperkalemia, which predicts mortality in acute overdose.

answers.name: Triamterene
answers.pearl: Triamterene is an ENaC blocker that often comes in fixed-dose combination with hydrochlorothiazide, which can hide the risk.

answers.name: Eplerenone
answers.pearl: Eplerenone is a selective mineralocorticoid antagonist, contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and in significant renal impairment.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine reduces tubular potassium secretion and aldosterone responsiveness, contributing to hyperkalemic renal tubular acidosis.

answers.name: Potassium-containing salt substitutes
answers.pearl: Salt substitutes such as Lo-Salt or NoSalt are mostly potassium chloride and are a hidden source in patients on ACE inhibitors.

answers.name: Ketorolac
answers.pearl: Ketorolac is a potent NSAID commonly given IV and can precipitate hyperkalemia as well as AKI in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Sacubitril-valsartan
answers.pearl: Sacubitril-valsartan carries a hyperkalemia risk similar to ARBs, particularly with mineralocorticoid antagonists.

answers.name: Aliskiren
answers.pearl: Aliskiren, a direct renin inhibitor, raises potassium especially combined with ACE inhibitors or ARBs and is avoided in that combination in diabetes.

answers.name: Finerenone
answers.pearl: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal MRA for diabetic kidney disease, and potassium must be checked at start and during dose changes.

answers.name: Penicillin G potassium
answers.pearl: Each million units of potassium penicillin G carries about 1.7 mEq potassium, enough to cause hyperkalemia in high-dose therapy with renal impairment.

answers.name: Enoxaparin
answers.pearl: Heparins suppress aldosterone synthesis, and low-molecular-weight heparin also has a reported hyperkalemia effect, mainly in CKD and diabetes.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine blocks ENaC like trimethoprim, and hyperkalemia is more common with IV therapy.

answers.name: Indomethacin
answers.pearl: Indomethacin causes marked hyperkalemia through effects on renin and aldosterone, particularly in neonates and the elderly.

answers.name: Sirolimus
answers.pearl: Sirolimus and other mTOR inhibitors can cause hyperkalemia via reduced ENaC and Na-K ATPase activity.

answers.name: Drugs causing rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Massive muscle breakdown releases intracellular potassium, so statins, daptomycin and other myotoxic drugs can cause hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Chemotherapy causing tumor lysis syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid cell kill from chemotherapy, rituximab or venetoclax releases potassium, phosphate and uric acid.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Hyperosmolar mannitol draws water and potassium out of cells, an effect most important in patients with renal failure.

answers.name: Potassium iodide
answers.pearl: Saturated solution of potassium iodide contains substantial potassium and has caused hyperkalemia in renal impairment.

answers.name: Voclosporin
answers.pearl: Voclosporin, a calcineurin inhibitor for lupus nephritis, lists hyperkalemia among its common adverse effects.

answers.name: Arginine hydrochloride
answers.pearl: Intravenous arginine drives potassium out of cells in exchange for arginine uptake and can cause life-threatening hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Propofol infusion syndrome
answers.pearl: Prolonged high-dose propofol can cause rhabdomyolysis, lactic acidosis and hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Primary adrenalitis from checkpoint inhibitors can cause mineralocorticoid deficiency and hyperkalemia, though rare.

answers.name: Esaxerenone
answers.pearl: Esaxerenone is a nonsteroidal MRA marketed in Japan for hypertension, with hyperkalemia as its main adverse effect.

answers.name: Aminocaproic acid
answers.pearl: Epsilon-aminocaproic acid has been reported to cause hyperkalemia through cellular potassium release, especially in renal dysfunction.

answers.name: Noni juice
answers.pearl: Noni juice and some herbal remedies are very potassium rich and have caused hyperkalemia in patients with CKD.

answers.name: Cardiac glycoside plants
answers.pearl: Oleander and foxglove poisoning blocks the Na-K ATPase like digoxin and raises serum potassium.

answers.name: Nafamostat
answers.pearl: Nafamostat mesylate, used as an anticoagulant for dialysis in Japan, blocks ENaC and causes hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Succinylcholine
answers.pearl: Succinylcholine raises potassium by about 0.5 mEq/L normally, and much more after burns, crush injury, denervation or prolonged immobility.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin suppresses adrenal aldosterone synthesis, producing hyperkalemia within days, mainly in CKD and diabetes.

answers.name: Drospirenone
answers.pearl: Drospirenone in oral contraceptives is a spironolactone analog, so potassium should be monitored with ACE inhibitors or renal impairment.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hypoglycemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: metformin (rare alone), GLP-1 RAs/DPP-4/SGLT2/pioglitazone/acarbose (hypoglycemia mainly with insulin or sulfonylurea), ARBs, MAOIs, SSRIs, anabolic steroids, chloramphenicol, gemfibrozil and cimetidine/fluconazole/clarithromycin (interaction-mediated), tyrosine kinase inhibitors, quinidine, pegvisomant, propoxyphene (withdrawn), ackee fruit (toxin not a drug), perhexiline and cibenzoline (limited availability).

answers.name: Insulin
answers.pearl: Insulin is the leading cause of drug-induced hypoglycemia, and renal failure prolongs its action.

answers.name: Sulfonylureas
answers.pearl: Sulfonylureas cause prolonged hypoglycemia, especially glyburide and chlorpropamide in older adults or those with renal failure.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones, especially gatifloxacin and levofloxacin, cause severe dysglycemia in diabetics on sulfonylureas.

answers.name: Meglitinides
answers.pearl: Repaglinide and nateglinide stimulate insulin release in a short-acting way, with a smaller hypoglycemia risk than sulfonylureas.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Ethanol blocks hepatic gluconeogenesis, so hypoglycemia occurs after fasting with heavy drinking.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers blunt adrenergic warning symptoms and impair glycogenolysis, prolonging recovery from hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: TMP-SMX can cause severe hypoglycemia especially with renal failure or when given with a sulfonylurea.

answers.name: Salicylates
answers.pearl: High-dose aspirin enhances insulin secretion and sensitivity and can cause hypoglycemia, especially in children and the malnourished.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Metformin alone rarely causes hypoglycemia but can contribute with fasting, alcohol or other glucose-lowering drugs.

answers.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
answers.pearl: GLP-1 agonists seldom cause hypoglycemia alone, but the risk rises when combined with sulfonylureas or insulin.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors may enhance insulin sensitivity and are linked to hypoglycemia in diabetic patients on insulin or sulfonylureas.

answers.name: DPP-4 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Gliptins have low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk, but it increases when they are added to a sulfonylurea or insulin.

answers.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
answers.pearl: SGLT2 inhibitors seldom cause hypoglycemia alone but add to risk when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas.

answers.name: Thiazolidinediones
answers.pearl: Pioglitazone does not cause hypoglycemia alone but can contribute when combined with insulin or secretagogues.

answers.name: Pramlintide
answers.pearl: Pramlintide carries a boxed warning for severe hypoglycemia when used with mealtime insulin, so insulin doses are reduced.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine can lower glucose by enhancing insulin secretion and reducing its clearance.

answers.name: Acarbose
answers.pearl: Acarbose does not cause hypoglycemia on its own, but when it occurs with a sulfonylurea it must be treated with glucose rather than sucrose.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Tramadol labeling warns of hypoglycemia, with increased risk in diabetics and in those with renal or hepatic impairment.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Linezolid is labeled for symptomatic hypoglycemia in diabetics on insulin or oral agents, possibly via MAO inhibition.

answers.name: ARBs
answers.pearl: Angiotensin receptor blockers may improve insulin sensitivity and have been linked to hypoglycemia in patients treated with insulin.

answers.name: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors
answers.pearl: MAO inhibitors can potentiate insulin and oral agents and cause hypoglycemia, and are labeled for it.

answers.name: Octreotide
answers.pearl: Octreotide suppresses insulin and counterregulatory hormones, so both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia can occur.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: Cimetidine inhibits sulfonylurea clearance, raising the risk of hypoglycemia.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs, notably fluoxetine, are associated with lower glucose and hypoglycemia, especially in diabetics.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine stimulates insulin secretion like quinine and has been associated with hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Anabolic steroids
answers.pearl: Androgens such as oxandrolone enhance insulin sensitivity and are labeled for hypoglycemia in diabetics.

answers.name: Fluconazole
answers.pearl: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 and so raises sulfonylurea levels and hypoglycemia risk.

answers.name: Mecasermin
answers.pearl: Mecasermin, recombinant IGF-1 for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, commonly causes hypoglycemia and requires meals around dosing.

answers.name: Clarithromycin
answers.pearl: Clarithromycin has been linked to hypoglycemia in patients on sulfonylureas or repaglinide, particularly older adults.

answers.name: Chloramphenicol
answers.pearl: Chloramphenicol inhibits hepatic metabolism of tolbutamide and chlorpropamide and can precipitate hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Gemfibrozil
answers.pearl: Gemfibrozil strongly increases repaglinide exposure via CYP2C8 and glucuronidation inhibition, causing hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Pegvisomant
answers.pearl: Pegvisomant, a growth hormone receptor antagonist for acromegaly, improves insulin sensitivity and can cause hypoglycemia in diabetics.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Imatinib, sunitinib and related agents have been reported to lower glucose and cause hypoglycemia in diabetics.

answers.name: Streptozocin
answers.pearl: Streptozocin destroys pancreatic beta cells and can cause acute hypoglycemia from insulin release, as well as diabetes later.

answers.name: Propoxyphene
answers.pearl: Propoxyphene, withdrawn in 2010, was associated with hypoglycemia, particularly in renal impairment and overdose.

answers.name: Ackee fruit
answers.pearl: Unripe ackee contains hypoglycin A, which blocks fatty acid oxidation and gluconeogenesis, causing Jamaican vomiting sickness.

answers.name: Sulfhydryl-containing drugs
answers.pearl: Methimazole and other thiol drugs can induce insulin autoimmune syndrome, with autoantibodies releasing insulin and causing fasting hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Perhexiline
answers.pearl: Perhexiline, an antianginal available in a few countries, causes hypoglycemia and hepatic and neurologic toxicity.

answers.name: Cibenzoline
answers.pearl: Cibenzoline, a class I antiarrhythmic used in Japan, binds the KATP channel and causes hypoglycemia, especially in renal failure.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine stimulates pancreatic insulin release, and malaria and pregnancy increase hypoglycemia risk.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine destroys beta cells, causing insulin release and hypoglycemia followed by diabetes.

answers.name: Disopyramide
answers.pearl: Disopyramide causes hypoglycemia, particularly in older adults with renal impairment, by blocking KATP channels.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hyperglycemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: calcium channel blockers, thyroid hormone, TCAs omitted, glucagon (intended effect), ACTH, tesamorelin, pasireotide, dolutegravir (case-level), ADT, teprotumumab, nilotinib, capivasertib/inavolisib, Vacor (withdrawn rodenticide), streptozocin (hypoglycemia first), phenothiazines, loop diuretics, interferon alfa (autoimmune diabetes).

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids cause postprandial hyperglycemia by increasing hepatic gluconeogenesis and insulin resistance.

answers.name: Atypical antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Olanzapine and clozapine carry the highest risk of hyperglycemia, and diabetic ketoacidosis has occurred.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides impair insulin secretion partly through hypokalemia, and correcting potassium can improve glucose.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus is a major cause of post-transplant diabetes mellitus by toxic effects on beta cells.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Statins modestly raise glucose and slightly increase diabetes incidence, particularly high-intensity regimens.

answers.name: Niacin
answers.pearl: Niacin worsens insulin resistance and glycemic control in diabetics.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers can worsen glycemic control and raise diabetes risk, with the largest effect seen with atenolol and metoprolol.

answers.name: Beta-adrenergic agonists
answers.pearl: Albuterol and terbutaline raise glucose via glycogenolysis and are linked to hyperglycemia and ketosis with tocolysis.

answers.name: Dextrose and parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Dextrose-containing fluids and TPN are common iatrogenic causes of inpatient hyperglycemia.

answers.name: Catecholamines
answers.pearl: Epinephrine and other vasopressors raise glucose through glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis and suppressed insulin.

answers.name: HIV protease inhibitors
answers.pearl: Protease inhibitors induce insulin resistance and sometimes lipodystrophy, with indinavir and lopinavir implicated.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen-progestin pills can modestly impair glucose tolerance, particularly older high-dose formulations.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitors, especially PD-1/PD-L1 agents, can cause autoimmune diabetes presenting abruptly with DKA.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine impairs insulin secretion and contributes to post-transplant diabetes, though less than tacrolimus.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics can raise glucose through hypokalemia and volume depletion, though less than thiazides.

answers.name: mTOR inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sirolimus and everolimus cause insulin resistance and beta cell dysfunction, and hyperglycemia is common.

answers.name: Growth hormone
answers.pearl: Growth hormone antagonizes insulin action and raises glucose.

answers.name: Glucagon
answers.pearl: Glucagon raises glucose by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Phenytoin inhibits insulin release, and hyperglycemia is described mainly with toxic levels or IV overdose.

answers.name: Phenothiazines
answers.pearl: Chlorpromazine and other low-potency phenothiazines can impair glucose tolerance.

answers.name: Octreotide
answers.pearl: Octreotide suppresses insulin secretion, and hyperglycemia is common in some patients.

answers.name: Asparaginase
answers.pearl: Asparaginase and pegaspargase cause hyperglycemia in many patients by reducing insulin synthesis and by pancreatitis.

answers.name: Corticotropin
answers.pearl: ACTH raises cortisol and causes steroid-like hyperglycemia.

answers.name: Megestrol
answers.pearl: Megestrol acetate has glucocorticoid activity, can worsen diabetes and cause adrenal suppression.

answers.name: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Older NRTIs such as stavudine and zidovudine cause mitochondrial toxicity, insulin resistance and hyperglycemia.

answers.name: Androgen deprivation therapy
answers.pearl: GnRH agonists and other ADT promote insulin resistance and raise diabetes risk in prostate cancer.

answers.name: Thyroid hormone
answers.pearl: Excess levothyroxine increases hepatic glucose output and can unmask or worsen diabetes.

answers.name: Calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Nifedipine and related dihydropyridines can modestly impair insulin release by blocking calcium entry in beta cells.

answers.name: PI3K and AKT inhibitors
answers.pearl: Alpelisib and related inhibitors cause hyperglycemia as an on-target effect since PI3K is in the insulin signaling pathway.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon alfa can trigger autoimmune diabetes, including in hepatitis C therapy.

answers.name: Tesamorelin
answers.pearl: Tesamorelin, a GHRH analog for HIV lipodystrophy, is labeled for glucose intolerance and diabetes.

answers.name: Pasireotide
answers.pearl: Pasireotide for Cushing disease causes hyperglycemia in most patients through suppression of insulin and incretins.

answers.name: Teprotumumab
answers.pearl: Teprotumumab for thyroid eye disease carries a warning for hyperglycemia, and glucose should be monitored.

answers.name: Nilotinib
answers.pearl: Nilotinib frequently causes hyperglycemia in addition to QT prolongation.

answers.name: Dolutegravir
answers.pearl: Integrase inhibitors, notably dolutegravir, have been associated with hyperglycemia and new-onset diabetes.

answers.name: Streptozocin
answers.pearl: Streptozocin destroys beta cells and can cause diabetes, which is why it is used experimentally in animals.

answers.name: Vacor
answers.pearl: Vacor, a rodenticide withdrawn in the 1970s, selectively destroyed beta cells and caused insulin-dependent diabetes.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine's islet toxicity causes initial hypoglycemia, and later permanent insulin deficiency and diabetes.

answers.name: Diazoxide
answers.pearl: Diazoxide opens KATP channels in beta cells and suppresses insulin secretion, used to treat hyperinsulinism.

answers.name: Gatifloxacin
answers.pearl: Gatifloxacin was withdrawn in the US after causing severe dysglycemia, including hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause pulmonary toxicity (interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: brentuximab (the labeled problem is the bleomycin combination), trastuzumab, bortezomib, irinotecan, pemetrexed, cetuximab, daptomycin and mesalamine (eosinophilic pneumonia rather than fibrosis), azathioprine, fludarabine, procarbazine, gold salts, tocainide (withdrawn), nilutamide, intravenous talc from crushed tablets (misuse not a prescribed drug).

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone can cause interstitial pneumonitis or fibrosis, with higher risk at doses above 400 mg per day and with long duration.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Methotrexate pneumonitis is a hypersensitivity reaction that can occur at any dose and at any time during therapy.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Acute nitrofurantoin lung reactions mimic hypersensitivity pneumonitis, while chronic use can lead to fibrosis.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: Bleomycin lung toxicity is dose-related and increased by oxygen exposure, radiation and renal dysfunction.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis can occur at any time, often within months of starting, and is treated with steroids.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: Cyclophosphamide can cause early hypersensitivity pneumonitis or late fibrosis.

answers.name: EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Gefitinib, erlotinib and osimertinib cause drug-induced ILD, which was recognized first in Japanese patients.

answers.name: Mitomycin C
answers.pearl: Mitomycin causes interstitial pneumonitis and also hemolytic uremic syndrome.

answers.name: mTOR inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sirolimus, everolimus and temsirolimus cause non-infectious pneumonitis, which can resolve with dose reduction.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Leflunomide can cause or exacerbate ILD, particularly in patients with pre-existing lung disease.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Gemcitabine can cause pulmonary toxicity ranging from pneumonitis to noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and capillary leak.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfasalazine can cause eosinophilic pneumonia or interstitial lung disease.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Rituximab can cause interstitial pneumonitis weeks after infusion in addition to infusion reactions.

answers.name: Melphalan
answers.pearl: Melphalan, particularly at high dose, can cause pulmonary fibrosis.

answers.name: Taxanes
answers.pearl: Docetaxel and paclitaxel can cause interstitial pneumonitis and hypersensitivity lung reactions.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone is labeled for new or worsening pulmonary toxicity, though less than amiodarone.

answers.name: TNF inhibitors
answers.pearl: Infliximab, etanercept and adalimumab have been linked to new or worsened ILD.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: Penicillamine can cause bronchiolitis obliterans and, rarely, a pulmonary-renal syndrome.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Gold therapy for rheumatoid arthritis can cause pneumonitis with fibrosis.

answers.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan
answers.pearl: Trastuzumab deruxtecan has a boxed warning for ILD and pneumonitis, which requires early recognition and steroids.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Mesalamine and other 5-ASA drugs can cause eosinophilic or interstitial pneumonitis.

answers.name: Minocycline
answers.pearl: Minocycline can cause acute eosinophilic pneumonia and sometimes drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Ergot-derived dopamine agonists
answers.pearl: Bromocriptine, cabergoline and pergolide have been linked to pleuropulmonary fibrosis.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferons are labeled for interstitial pneumonitis, occasionally fatal.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Azathioprine rarely causes an interstitial pneumonitis or hypersensitivity lung reaction.

answers.name: Fludarabine
answers.pearl: Fludarabine can cause interstitial pneumonitis, and the risk with pentostatin is high enough that the combination is contraindicated.

answers.name: Pemetrexed
answers.pearl: Pemetrexed has been reported to cause interstitial pneumonitis, including after radiation.

answers.name: Trastuzumab
answers.pearl: Trastuzumab has been associated with interstitial pneumonitis, in addition to its cardiotoxicity.

answers.name: Irinotecan
answers.pearl: Irinotecan has been linked to interstitial pneumonia, most prominently in Japanese patients.

answers.name: Cetuximab
answers.pearl: Cetuximab labeling includes interstitial lung disease, with onset usually in the first months.

answers.name: Abemaciclib
answers.pearl: Abemaciclib carries a warning for ILD or pneumonitis, which is seen less with other CDK4/6 inhibitors.

answers.name: Chlorambucil
answers.pearl: Chlorambucil is a rare cause of interstitial pneumonitis and fibrosis.

answers.name: Daptomycin
answers.pearl: Daptomycin can cause eosinophilic pneumonia, usually 2 to 4 weeks after starting.

answers.name: Procarbazine
answers.pearl: Procarbazine, used in MOPP or BEACOPP regimens, can cause pneumonitis, often hypersensitivity type.

answers.name: Idelalisib
answers.pearl: Idelalisib has a boxed warning for fatal and serious pneumonitis.

answers.name: Brentuximab vedotin
answers.pearl: Brentuximab combined with bleomycin is contraindicated because of excess pulmonary toxicity.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Bortezomib has been associated with ILD, including acute respiratory failure.

answers.name: Nilutamide
answers.pearl: Nilutamide, an antiandrogen, causes interstitial pneumonitis that may be more common in Japanese patients.

answers.name: Tocainide
answers.pearl: Tocainide, a withdrawn class IB antiarrhythmic, caused pulmonary fibrosis that was often fatal.

answers.name: Intravenous crushed tablets
answers.pearl: Intravenous injection of crushed oral tablets causes talc granulomatosis from insoluble fillers, producing ILD and pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Busulfan
answers.pearl: Busulfan lung is a delayed pulmonary fibrosis that can occur months to years after therapy.

answers.name: Nitrosoureas
answers.pearl: Carmustine causes dose-dependent delayed pulmonary fibrosis, with a cumulative-dose threshold of about 1400 mg/m2.

answers.name: Methysergide
answers.pearl: Methysergide, withdrawn migraine prophylaxis, caused retroperitoneal and pleuropulmonary fibrosis.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause bradycardia or AV block.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: lacosamide, carbamazepine, phenytoin (rapid IV), reserpine, pilocarpine/bethanechol, baclofen, bupivacaine, paclitaxel, thalidomide, crizotinib, octreotide, ticagrelor, hydroxychloroquine (conduction disorders), sugammadex, aconite, veratrum alkaloids and mad honey (toxins, case-level), cardiac glycoside plants.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockers slow sinus and AV node conduction and are the usual cause of drug-induced bradycardia, including in elderly patients using ophthalmic agents.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: Digoxin enhances vagal tone and slows AV nodal conduction; toxicity can cause nearly any bradyarrhythmia, notably AV block with atrial tachycardia.

answers.name: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Verapamil and diltiazem slow AV nodal conduction, and combining them with beta blockers raises the risk of high-grade block.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone slows sinus and AV nodal conduction, and bradycardia is its commonest cardiac adverse effect.

answers.name: Adenosine
answers.pearl: Adenosine transiently blocks AV nodal conduction, producing pauses or asystole lasting seconds, and is potentiated by dipyridamole.

answers.name: Alpha-2 agonists
answers.pearl: Clonidine and similar central agents reduce sympathetic outflow and can cause sinus bradycardia, and clonidine plus beta blocker can cause severe bradycardia.

answers.name: Dexmedetomidine
answers.pearl: Dexmedetomidine commonly causes bradycardia and sometimes sinus arrest, especially with loading doses.

answers.name: Sotalol
answers.pearl: Sotalol combines beta blockade with class III effects, and bradycardia increases torsades risk.

answers.name: Cholinesterase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Donepezil, rivastigmine and galantamine increase vagal tone and can cause syncope, bradycardia and heart block.

answers.name: Ivabradine
answers.pearl: Ivabradine blocks the funny current and slows the sinus rate, with bradycardia and visual phosphenes as common effects.

answers.name: Timolol eye drops
answers.pearl: Topical timolol is systemically absorbed and can cause bradycardia, heart block and bronchospasm.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Fentanyl and remifentanil increase vagal tone and commonly cause bradycardia during anesthesia.

answers.name: Neostigmine
answers.pearl: Neostigmine can cause profound bradycardia and is combined with glycopyrrolate when reversing neuromuscular blockade.

answers.name: Propofol
answers.pearl: Propofol reduces sympathetic tone and baroreflex responses and can cause bradycardia and asystole.

answers.name: Phenylephrine
answers.pearl: Pure alpha agonists cause reflex bradycardia from baroreceptor activation.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone slows sinus and AV nodal conduction and is contraindicated with significant bradycardia or second- or third-degree block.

answers.name: Succinylcholine
answers.pearl: Succinylcholine can cause bradycardia and asystole by stimulating cardiac muscarinic receptors, particularly after a second dose and in children.

answers.name: Class IC antiarrhythmics
answers.pearl: Flecainide and propafenone slow conduction and can cause sinus node dysfunction or AV block, especially in structural heart disease.

answers.name: Pyridostigmine
answers.pearl: Pyridostigmine increases cholinergic tone and may cause bradycardia, particularly in myasthenia gravis patients on higher doses.

answers.name: Organophosphate poisoning
answers.pearl: Organophosphates and carbamates inhibit acetylcholinesterase, producing bradycardia and heart block among other muscarinic effects.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs slow His-Purkinje conduction, and overdose can produce wide QRS, AV block and bradycardia.

answers.name: Class IA antiarrhythmics
answers.pearl: Procainamide, quinidine and disopyramide may cause sinus node dysfunction or AV block.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Rapid IV phenytoin or fosphenytoin loading can cause bradycardia, heart block and hypotension, so infusion rate is limited.

answers.name: Octreotide
answers.pearl: Octreotide commonly causes sinus bradycardia and conduction disturbances.

answers.name: Ticagrelor
answers.pearl: Ticagrelor causes ventricular pauses and, less often, bradyarrhythmias, probably via adenosine effects.

answers.name: Paclitaxel
answers.pearl: Paclitaxel can cause asymptomatic bradycardia and occasionally AV block.

answers.name: Bupivacaine
answers.pearl: Systemic bupivacaine toxicity causes conduction block, bradycardia and asystole, treated with lipid emulsion.

answers.name: Thalidomide
answers.pearl: Thalidomide is labeled for bradycardia, and the risk may rise with other bradycardic drugs.

answers.name: Baclofen
answers.pearl: Baclofen toxicity or abrupt intrathecal dose changes can cause bradycardia and hypotension.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: Chronic chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine use can cause conduction disorders including bundle branch block and complete AV block.

answers.name: Reserpine
answers.pearl: Reserpine depletes catecholamines and commonly causes bradycardia.

answers.name: Lacosamide
answers.pearl: Lacosamide prolongs PR interval and is labeled for AV block, bradycardia and arrhythmia.

answers.name: Cholinergic agonists
answers.pearl: Bethanechol and pilocarpine stimulate muscarinic receptors and can cause bradycardia and heart block.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine can cause AV conduction block and bradycardia, notably in older adults and women.

answers.name: Crizotinib
answers.pearl: Crizotinib is labeled for symptomatic bradycardia, with heart rate decreases seen in many patients.

answers.name: Sugammadex
answers.pearl: Sugammadex has been associated with marked bradycardia and cardiac arrest within minutes of administration.

answers.name: Cardiac glycoside plants
answers.pearl: Oleander and foxglove contain cardenolides that cause bradycardia and AV block like digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Aconite
answers.pearl: Aconite alkaloids in some herbal medicines keep sodium channels open and cause bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmias and paresthesias.

answers.name: Veratrum alkaloids
answers.pearl: Veratrum (false hellebore) alkaloids trigger the Bezold-Jarisch reflex, causing bradycardia and hypotension.

answers.name: Grayanotoxin honey
answers.pearl: Honey from certain Rhododendron species (mad honey) causes bradycardia, AV block and hypotension that respond to atropine.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium can cause sinus node dysfunction and sinus bradycardia, especially in toxicity.

answers.name: Fingolimod
answers.pearl: Fingolimod and other S1P receptor modulators cause transient bradycardia and AV block with the first dose, so first-dose observation is required.

answers.name: Sofosbuvir with amiodarone
answers.pearl: Sofosbuvir-containing hepatitis C regimens with amiodarone have caused severe symptomatic bradycardia and need for a pacemaker.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause delirium or confusion in older adults.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: indomethacin, beta blockers (lipophilic), SSRIs/thiazides (via hyponatremia), topiramate, efavirenz, bupropion, mefloquine, macrolides, isoniazid, cycloserine, ifosfamide, calcineurin inhibitors, ketamine (emergence), jimsonweed/bismuth (toxin-level). Cefepime, imipenem, metronidazole and acyclovir are mainly in renal impairment.

answers.name: Anticholinergics
answers.pearl: Strongly anticholinergic drugs, including bladder antimuscarinics and benztropine, are the classic drug cause of delirium in older adults and appear on the Beers list.

answers.name: Benzodiazepines
answers.pearl: Benzodiazepines cause or worsen delirium in older adults and are on the Beers list, though abrupt withdrawal also causes delirium.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids cause delirium in older adults, particularly with renal impairment, polypharmacy and new dose escalations.

answers.name: First-generation antihistamines
answers.pearl: Diphenhydramine and hydroxyzine are highly anticholinergic, can cause delirium and are on the Beers list.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: High-dose steroids can cause steroid psychosis or delirium, usually within the first days or weeks of therapy.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Tertiary amine TCAs such as amitriptyline have strong anticholinergic effects and should be avoided in older adults.

answers.name: Z-drugs
answers.pearl: Zolpidem and other Z-drugs increase delirium, falls and fractures and are on the Beers list.

answers.name: Gabapentinoids
answers.pearl: Gabapentin and pregabalin accumulate in renal impairment and can cause confusion, sedation and falls.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Antipsychotics, especially low-potency ones with anticholinergic effects, can cause or worsen delirium in dementia.

answers.name: Muscle relaxants
answers.pearl: Skeletal muscle relaxants such as cyclobenzaprine and carisoprodol are poorly tolerated and Beers-listed for sedation and confusion.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones can cause delirium, hallucinations and seizures, particularly in older adults with renal impairment.

answers.name: Insulin and sulfonylureas
answers.pearl: Hypoglycemia from insulin or sulfonylureas presents as confusion in older adults and must be excluded in any new delirium.

answers.name: Anticonvulsants
answers.pearl: Phenobarbital, phenytoin and other antiseizure drugs can cause confusion and slowed cognition, particularly with high levels.

answers.name: Dopaminergic Parkinson drugs
answers.pearl: Levodopa and dopamine agonists can cause hallucinations and delirium in older adults with Parkinson disease.

answers.name: Baclofen
answers.pearl: Baclofen is renally cleared, and toxicity or abrupt withdrawal both cause confusion and delirium.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium toxicity causes confusion and tremor, and levels rise with dehydration, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and thiazides.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Tramadol can cause confusion, serotonin syndrome and hyponatremia in older adults.

answers.name: Promethazine
answers.pearl: Promethazine is strongly anticholinergic and sedating and should be avoided in older adults.

answers.name: Metoclopramide
