answers.pearl: Metoclopramide crosses the blood-brain barrier and can cause confusion, extrapyramidal effects and tardive dyskinesia.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: Digoxin toxicity in older adults often presents with confusion, visual changes and nausea, and levels rise with renal impairment.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazide-induced hyponatremia can present as confusion in older adults.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Lipophilic beta blockers such as propranolol cross into the brain and can cause confusion, vivid dreams and depression.

answers.name: Amantadine
answers.pearl: Amantadine has dopaminergic and anticholinergic effects and, being renally cleared, causes confusion, hallucinations and delirium in older adults.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs can cause SIADH with hyponatremia and confusion in older adults, as well as serotonin toxicity.

answers.name: Topiramate
answers.pearl: Topiramate causes cognitive slowing, word-finding difficulty and confusion, even at moderate doses.

answers.name: Scopolamine
answers.pearl: Transdermal scopolamine is a classic anticholinergic cause of postoperative delirium in older adults.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Chronic salicylism in older adults presents as confusion or delirium with tachypnea and tinnitus and is often missed.

answers.name: Indomethacin
answers.pearl: Indomethacin is Beers-listed for CNS adverse effects including confusion and headache.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Valproate can cause hyperammonemic encephalopathy even with normal liver tests and normal levels.

answers.name: Theophylline
answers.pearl: Theophylline toxicity causes agitation, confusion and seizures, and levels are raised by ciprofloxacin and other CYP1A2 inhibitors.

answers.name: Imipenem
answers.pearl: Imipenem lowers seizure threshold and can cause confusion, particularly when not renally dosed.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Metronidazole can cause an encephalopathy with cerebellar signs and characteristic MRI lesions.

answers.name: Bupropion
answers.pearl: Bupropion can cause agitation, confusion and seizures, especially at high doses or with renal impairment.

answers.name: Acyclovir
answers.pearl: IV acyclovir or valacyclovir causes encephalopathy with hallucinations in renal failure.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: Efavirenz causes neuropsychiatric effects such as vivid dreams, confusion and hallucinations.

answers.name: Ketamine
answers.pearl: Ketamine can cause emergence delirium and dissociative confusion, particularly in older adults.

answers.name: Macrolides
answers.pearl: Clarithromycin has been linked to delirium, mania and psychosis in older adults.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide causes encephalopathy ranging from confusion to coma, treated with methylene blue.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine can cause encephalopathy and PRES with confusion, headache and seizures.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid can cause psychosis, confusion and encephalopathy, partly through pyridoxine depletion.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon alfa causes neuropsychiatric effects including confusion, depression and delirium.

answers.name: Mefloquine
answers.pearl: Mefloquine causes neuropsychiatric effects such as confusion, hallucinations and vestibular symptoms that can persist.

answers.name: Jimsonweed
answers.pearl: Datura ingestion produces an anticholinergic toxidrome with delirium, mydriasis and dry skin.

answers.name: Cycloserine
answers.pearl: Cycloserine, a second-line TB drug, causes psychosis, confusion and seizures, partly reversed by pyridoxine.

answers.name: Bismuth
answers.pearl: Bismuth encephalopathy is a subacute confusional state reported with chronic bismuth subsalicylate or subnitrate use.

answers.name: Meperidine
answers.pearl: Meperidine's normeperidine metabolite accumulates in renal failure and lowers seizure threshold and causes delirium, so Beers criteria advise avoiding it.

answers.name: H2 receptor blockers
answers.pearl: Cimetidine and other H2 blockers cause confusion in older adults, particularly with renal impairment.

answers.name: Cefepime
answers.pearl: Cefepime causes encephalopathy, myoclonus and nonconvulsive status when not dose-adjusted for renal function.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs or substances that inhibit CYP3A4.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: goldenseal (modest clinical data), schisandra (mainly herb-drug case/PK data), isoniazid (weak), cyclosporine (weak-to-moderate), ranolazine and cimetidine (weak), ribociclib/letermovir/tucatinib (strength categories vary by source), mibefradil (withdrawn), bergamottin (grapefruit constituent rather than a drug).

answers.name: Clarithromycin
answers.pearl: Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and a classic cause of statin myopathy and calcium-channel-blocker toxicity.

answers.name: Ketoconazole
answers.pearl: Ketoconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, and the FDA restricted its oral use because of hepatotoxicity and interactions.

answers.name: Ritonavir
answers.pearl: Ritonavir is a very potent CYP3A4 inhibitor used at low dose as a pharmacokinetic booster for other antiretrovirals.

answers.name: Grapefruit juice
answers.pearl: Grapefruit juice irreversibly inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, raising oral bioavailability of drugs such as simvastatin and felodipine.

answers.name: Itraconazole
answers.pearl: Itraconazole is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, and its active metabolite hydroxyitraconazole adds to the effect.

answers.name: Erythromycin
answers.pearl: Erythromycin is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, and the mechanism-based inhibition builds with repeated dosing.

answers.name: Diltiazem
answers.pearl: Diltiazem is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises levels of tacrolimus, cyclosporine and simvastatin.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Verapamil is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and also inhibits P-glycoprotein, increasing digoxin levels.

answers.name: Voriconazole
answers.pearl: Voriconazole inhibits CYP3A4 as well as CYP2C19 and CYP2C9.

answers.name: Fluconazole
answers.pearl: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor at doses of 200 mg or more and also a strong CYP2C9 inhibitor.

answers.name: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir
answers.pearl: The ritonavir component of this COVID-19 antiviral makes it a major source of CYP3A4 interactions with statins, DOACs and immunosuppressants.

answers.name: Cobicistat
answers.pearl: Cobicistat boosts HIV regimens purely through CYP3A inhibition and has no antiviral activity of its own.

answers.name: Posaconazole
answers.pearl: Posaconazole is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, and simvastatin and ergot alkaloids are contraindicated with it.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone weakly to moderately inhibits CYP3A4 and several other enzymes, and its long half-life means interactions persist for months.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: Cimetidine is a nonselective, weak CYP inhibitor; famotidine lacks this effect.

answers.name: Nelfinavir
answers.pearl: Nelfinavir is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor among the HIV protease inhibitors.

answers.name: Indinavir
answers.pearl: Indinavir inhibits CYP3A4, and its dose is lowered when it is given with other inhibitors.

answers.name: Lopinavir
answers.pearl: Lopinavir is co-formulated with ritonavir, and the combination inhibits CYP3A4 strongly.

answers.name: Ciprofloxacin
answers.pearl: Ciprofloxacin is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and a strong CYP1A2 inhibitor.

answers.name: Aprepitant
answers.pearl: Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, and it can lower warfarin and oral contraceptive effect through induction.

answers.name: Fluvoxamine
answers.pearl: Fluvoxamine is best known for CYP1A2 and 2C19 inhibition but also weakly to moderately inhibits CYP3A4.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Imatinib is both a CYP3A4 substrate and a moderate inhibitor of it.

answers.name: Isavuconazole
answers.pearl: Isavuconazole is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and, unlike other azoles, shortens the QT interval.

answers.name: Saquinavir
answers.pearl: Saquinavir is boosted with ritonavir and inhibits CYP3A4, and the combination prolongs QT.

answers.name: Atazanavir
answers.pearl: Atazanavir inhibits CYP3A4 and UGT1A1, the latter producing indirect hyperbilirubinemia.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor that also inhibits CYP2D6 and P-glycoprotein.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine is a CYP3A4 substrate and a weak-to-moderate inhibitor, raising levels of statins and sirolimus.

answers.name: Crizotinib
answers.pearl: Crizotinib is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor as well as a substrate.

answers.name: Nilotinib
answers.pearl: Nilotinib inhibits CYP3A4 and prolongs QT, so strong inhibitors are avoided with it.

answers.name: Conivaptan
answers.pearl: Conivaptan, an IV vasopressin antagonist, is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor.

answers.name: Mifepristone
answers.pearl: Mifepristone is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, and the Cushing's formulation is contraindicated with simvastatin.

answers.name: Ranolazine
answers.pearl: Ranolazine is a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises simvastatin and tacrolimus exposure.

answers.name: Danazol
answers.pearl: Danazol inhibits CYP3A4 and can increase carbamazepine and cyclosporine levels.

answers.name: Idelalisib
answers.pearl: Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor with a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity and serious infections.

answers.name: Boceprevir
answers.pearl: The first-generation HCV protease inhibitors boceprevir and telaprevir strongly inhibit CYP3A4 and are no longer used.

answers.name: Chloramphenicol
answers.pearl: Chloramphenicol inhibits several CYP enzymes, including CYP3A4 and CYP2C19, and raises phenytoin levels.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid inhibits CYP2C19 and, more weakly, CYP3A4 and CYP2E1.

answers.name: Letermovir
answers.pearl: Letermovir for CMV prophylaxis is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor, which raises tacrolimus and sirolimus levels.

answers.name: Tucatinib
answers.pearl: Tucatinib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor, an unexpected property for a HER2 kinase inhibitor.

answers.name: Ribociclib
answers.pearl: Ribociclib is a moderate-to-strong CYP3A4 inhibitor as well as a QT-prolonging drug.

answers.name: Goldenseal
answers.pearl: Goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis) inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 through its alkaloids berberine and hydrastine.

answers.name: Bergamottin
answers.pearl: Bergamottin and related furanocoumarins are the main components of grapefruit juice that inhibit CYP3A4.

answers.name: Mibefradil
answers.pearl: Mibefradil, a calcium-channel blocker withdrawn in 1998, strongly inhibited CYP3A4 and caused dangerous statin and other interactions.

answers.name: Schisandra
answers.pearl: Schisandra lignans inhibit CYP3A4 and raise tacrolimus levels.

answers.name: Lonafarnib
answers.pearl: Lonafarnib for progeria is a strong CYP3A inhibitor and is itself a CYP3A substrate.

answers.name: Nefazodone
answers.pearl: Nefazodone strongly inhibits CYP3A4, and its pairing with simvastatin or triazolam is a classic interaction.

answers.name: Telithromycin
answers.pearl: Telithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; the ketolide was largely abandoned for hepatotoxicity and myasthenia exacerbation.

answers.name: Seville orange
answers.pearl: Seville (bitter) orange contains furanocoumarins and inhibits CYP3A4 as grapefruit does.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause or contribute to serotonin syndrome.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: ritonavir and carbamazepine (case reports/pharmacokinetic), methylphenidate (case reports), oxycodone (labeling class warning), sibutramine and fenfluramine (withdrawn/specific indication), safinamide, Syrian rue, ayahuasca, procarbazine, isoniazid (weak MAO inhibition; case reports), synthetic cathinones, 5-HTP.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: SSRIs are the most common drug class implicated, usually in combination with another serotonergic agent.

answers.name: SNRIs
answers.pearl: SNRIs like venlafaxine carry serotonin syndrome risk, especially at high dose or with other serotonergic drugs.

answers.name: MAOIs
answers.pearl: MAOIs combined with serotonergic drugs cause the most severe serotonin syndrome, and a washout of two weeks (five weeks for fluoxetine) is needed.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Tramadol inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake and is a common culprit when added to an SSRI.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Linezolid is a weak reversible MAO inhibitor, and serotonin syndrome risk is highest with concurrent SSRIs.

answers.name: Triptans
answers.pearl: Triptans are 5-HT1B/1D agonists, and the added risk with SSRIs is real but uncommon.

answers.name: Ondansetron
answers.pearl: The FDA has warned that 5-HT3 antagonists can contribute to serotonin syndrome, mostly with other serotonergic drugs.

answers.name: Fentanyl
answers.pearl: Fentanyl has weak serotonergic activity and is a recognized trigger in perioperative serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: MDMA
answers.pearl: MDMA causes massive serotonin release and is a classic recreational cause of serotonin toxicity and hyperthermia.

answers.name: St John's wort
answers.pearl: St John's wort inhibits serotonin reuptake and should not be combined with other serotonergic antidepressants.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium enhances serotonergic transmission and can precipitate serotonin syndrome when combined with antidepressants.

answers.name: Dextromethorphan
answers.pearl: Dextromethorphan inhibits serotonin reuptake and is metabolized by CYP2D6, so SSRIs that inhibit CYP2D6 raise its level.

answers.name: Trazodone
answers.pearl: Trazodone and its metabolite mCPP act on serotonin pathways and contribute to toxicity at high dose or in combinations.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs, especially clomipramine, inhibit serotonin reuptake and can contribute to serotonin toxicity.

answers.name: Buspirone
answers.pearl: Buspirone, a 5-HT1A partial agonist, can add to serotonergic toxicity.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Mirtazapine antagonizes 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors and carries lower risk, but it has been reported in serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: Metoclopramide
answers.pearl: Metoclopramide has 5-HT4 agonist and 5-HT3 antagonist activity and has been implicated in serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: Cyclobenzaprine
answers.pearl: Cyclobenzaprine is structurally a tricyclic and inhibits serotonin reuptake.

answers.name: Methadone
answers.pearl: Methadone inhibits serotonin reuptake, and cases are reported with SSRIs.

answers.name: Amphetamines
answers.pearl: Amphetamines increase serotonin release in addition to dopamine and norepinephrine.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine blocks serotonin reuptake and can contribute to serotonin toxicity.

answers.name: Vilazodone
answers.pearl: Vilazodone combines SSRI action with 5-HT1A partial agonism.

answers.name: Vortioxetine
answers.pearl: Vortioxetine is a multimodal serotonergic antidepressant with a labeled serotonin syndrome warning.

answers.name: Selegiline
answers.pearl: Selegiline loses MAO-B selectivity at higher doses (and in the Emsam patch), so serotonergic drugs are restricted.

answers.name: Granisetron
answers.pearl: Other 5-HT3 antagonists such as granisetron and palonosetron carry the same FDA serotonin syndrome warning as ondansetron.

answers.name: Tapentadol
answers.pearl: Tapentadol inhibits norepinephrine reuptake and carries a warning for serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: Oxycodone
answers.pearl: Opioid labeling warns of serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs even though oxycodone's own serotonergic activity is weak.

answers.name: 5-HTP
answers.pearl: 5-Hydroxytryptophan is a serotonin precursor sold as a supplement and can cause toxicity when combined with other serotonergic agents.

answers.name: Methylphenidate
answers.pearl: Methylphenidate has rarely been reported in serotonin syndrome, mainly with other serotonergic drugs.

answers.name: LSD
answers.pearl: LSD is a 5-HT2A agonist and has been linked to serotonin toxicity, especially with SSRIs or MAOIs.

answers.name: Ritonavir
answers.pearl: Ritonavir inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 and has been reported to precipitate serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs.

answers.name: Psilocybin
answers.pearl: Psilocybin is a serotonergic psychedelic, and combining it with MAOIs or lithium can be dangerous.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine is structurally related to tricyclics and has case-report links to serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: Procarbazine
answers.pearl: Procarbazine has MAO-inhibitor properties, so serotonergic drugs and tyramine foods are cautioned against.

answers.name: Ayahuasca
answers.pearl: Ayahuasca combines DMT with beta-carboline MAO inhibitors and can cause serotonin toxicity, especially with SSRIs.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid is a weak MAO inhibitor and has been reported to contribute to serotonin syndrome.

answers.name: Synthetic cathinones
answers.pearl: Bath-salt cathinones such as mephedrone and methylone release serotonin and can cause serotonin toxicity.

answers.name: Sibutramine
answers.pearl: Sibutramine, an SNRI weight-loss drug withdrawn from the US market, carried a serotonin syndrome warning.

answers.name: Fenfluramine
answers.pearl: Fenfluramine releases serotonin, and the current Dravet syndrome formulation carries a serotonin syndrome warning.

answers.name: Dapoxetine
answers.pearl: Dapoxetine is a short-acting SSRI for premature ejaculation, available outside the US, and its combination with MAOIs is contraindicated.

answers.name: Safinamide
answers.pearl: Safinamide is an MAO-B inhibitor for Parkinson's disease and is contraindicated with SSRIs, SNRIs and opioids such as tramadol.

answers.name: Syrian rue
answers.pearl: Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) contains harmala alkaloids that inhibit MAO-A, mimicking the ayahuasca interaction.

answers.name: Methylene blue
answers.pearl: Methylene blue is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor, and the FDA warns of serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs.

answers.name: Meperidine
answers.pearl: Meperidine's normeperidine metabolite and weak serotonin reuptake inhibition make the MAOI interaction a classic fatal one.

answers.name: L-tryptophan
answers.pearl: L-tryptophan is a serotonin precursor, and its combination with MAOIs or SSRIs historically produced serotonin toxicity.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause drug-induced lupus.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: levetiracetam, clopidogrel, nitrofurantoin, griseofulvin, hydroxyurea, praziquantel, bupropion, anastrozole (case reports, often subacute cutaneous rather than systemic lupus), docetaxel and fluorouracil/capecitabine (SCLE), interferon-beta, trimethadione, mephenytoin and practolol (older/withdrawn), checkpoint inhibitors. SCLE-inducing drugs (HCTZ, PPIs, CCBs, terbinafine) are included because they are commonly taught under drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Hydralazine
answers.pearl: Hydralazine causes drug-induced lupus mainly in slow acetylators and at higher cumulative doses; antihistone antibodies are typical and ANCA may occur.

answers.name: Procainamide
answers.pearl: Procainamide has the highest rate of drug-induced lupus, with antihistone antibodies appearing in most long-term users.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid-induced lupus is more common in slow acetylators and usually resolves after stopping the drug.

answers.name: TNF inhibitors
answers.pearl: Anti-TNF drugs more often produce anti-dsDNA antibodies than antihistone antibodies, and low complements and rash can appear.

answers.name: Minocycline
answers.pearl: Minocycline can cause lupus-like illness and autoimmune hepatitis, often with p-ANCA.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine, a class IA antiarrhythmic like procainamide, is a recognized cause of drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine is a probable cause of drug-induced lupus, with typically mild symptoms.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Phenytoin can cause a lupus-like syndrome, sometimes with lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfasalazine is reported to cause drug-induced lupus, particularly in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil
answers.pearl: PTU can cause lupus-like illness and ANCA-associated vasculitis.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Statins have been reported to cause lupus-like syndromes and a dermatomyositis-like picture.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium has been reported to cause lupus-like syndromes.

answers.name: Terbinafine
answers.pearl: Terbinafine is a well-known cause of subacute cutaneous lupus, often anti-Ro positive.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon alfa can cause or unmask lupus and other autoimmune disease, and type I interferon is central to lupus pathogenesis.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Hydrochlorothiazide is one of the most common causes of drug-induced subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: PPIs are a recognized cause of drug-induced subacute cutaneous lupus, usually with anti-Ro antibodies.

answers.name: Calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Diltiazem is the calcium channel blocker most associated with subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitors, particularly captopril and enalapril, are reported to cause subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Beta-blockers
answers.pearl: Acebutolol is the beta-blocker best documented to induce antinuclear antibodies and lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Methimazole
answers.pearl: Methimazole and carbimazole are reported causes of drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Ethosuximide
answers.pearl: Ethosuximide is a documented cause of drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Primidone
answers.pearl: Primidone is among the anticonvulsants associated with drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Griseofulvin
answers.pearl: Griseofulvin can induce or exacerbate lupus, including subacute cutaneous forms.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Lamotrigine has been reported to cause a lupus-like syndrome, though much less often than older anticonvulsants.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Valproate has been reported to induce lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Nitrofurantoin is reported to cause drug-induced lupus, sometimes with pleuropulmonary involvement.

answers.name: Ticlopidine
answers.pearl: Ticlopidine is listed as a cause of drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitors can trigger lupus-like syndromes, including cutaneous and nephritic presentations.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Leflunomide has been associated with subacute cutaneous lupus and other autoimmune phenomena.

answers.name: Clopidogrel
answers.pearl: Clopidogrel has been reported to cause lupus-like syndromes in a few cases.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Parenteral gold therapy for rheumatoid arthritis has been reported to induce lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Levetiracetam
answers.pearl: Levetiracetam has been reported to cause lupus-like illness in rare cases.

answers.name: Interferon beta
answers.pearl: Interferon beta for multiple sclerosis has been associated with lupus-like syndromes.

answers.name: Docetaxel
answers.pearl: Docetaxel and other taxanes have been reported to induce subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Fluorouracil
answers.pearl: Fluoropyrimidines, especially capecitabine and tegafur, have been linked to subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Hydroxyurea
answers.pearl: Hydroxyurea is reported to induce lupus-like skin disease and dermatomyositis-like eruptions.

answers.name: Anastrozole
answers.pearl: Aromatase inhibitors such as anastrozole have been reported to induce subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Bupropion
answers.pearl: Bupropion has been reported to cause drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Aminoglutethimide
answers.pearl: Aminoglutethimide, an older adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitor, was associated with lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Praziquantel
answers.pearl: Praziquantel has a few case reports of drug-induced lupus.

answers.name: Mephenytoin
answers.pearl: Mephenytoin, an old hydantoin anticonvulsant, was among the earliest antiepileptics linked to lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Trimethadione
answers.pearl: Trimethadione was an early oxazolidinedione anticonvulsant reported to cause lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Practolol
answers.pearl: Practolol, a beta-blocker withdrawn for oculomucocutaneous syndrome, was also associated with antinuclear antibodies and lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: D-penicillamine can induce lupus along with myasthenia and other autoimmune syndromes.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: Methyldopa classically causes antibody-mediated phenomena, including positive ANA and, less commonly, lupus-like illness.

answers.name: Chlorpromazine
answers.pearl: Chlorpromazine is a classic cause of positive ANA and drug-induced lupus.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hypokalemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: polymyxin B/colistin (renal wasting reports), deferasirox (Fanconi), gossypol (historical), carbenoxolone (UK/Europe), ritodrine (withdrawn), toluene (a substance, not a drug), patiromer (overcorrection), itraconazole/posaconazole (mineralocorticoid excess), chloroquine overdose, dextrose/TPN (refeeding shift), caffeine toxicity, dobutamine (modest beta effect), azacitidine, lenalidomide, streptozocin, clenbuterol.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics increase distal sodium delivery, which drives potassium secretion, and also waste magnesium.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause hypokalemia dose-dependently and often with hyponatremia and metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Insulin
answers.pearl: Insulin drives potassium into cells and is a standard treatment for hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Beta-2 agonists
answers.pearl: Albuterol and other beta-2 agonists shift potassium into cells via Na-K-ATPase, which is why they are used to treat hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids with mineralocorticoid activity cause renal potassium wasting.

answers.name: Laxatives
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative abuse causes GI potassium loss and is a classic hidden cause of hypokalemia.

answers.name: Antipseudomonal penicillins
answers.pearl: High-dose nafcillin and antipseudomonal penicillins act as nonreabsorbable anions and increase renal potassium excretion.

answers.name: Theophylline
answers.pearl: Theophylline toxicity causes beta-adrenergic hypokalemia, and acute overdose can cause severe low potassium.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin causes renal magnesium and potassium wasting, so electrolytes are replaced with each cycle.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides cause tubular injury with magnesium and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Fludrocortisone
answers.pearl: Fludrocortisone is a potent mineralocorticoid that promotes renal potassium excretion.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Acetazolamide causes bicarbonaturia with potassium loss and a non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Foscarnet causes hypokalemia as well as hypomagnesemia and hypocalcemia, so electrolytes are checked.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide causes a proximal tubulopathy (Fanconi syndrome) with potassium wasting.

answers.name: Sodium bicarbonate
answers.pearl: Bicarbonate shifts potassium into cells and increases distal potassium secretion.

answers.name: Terbutaline
answers.pearl: Terbutaline, used for asthma and tocolysis, causes beta-mediated intracellular potassium shift.

answers.name: Epinephrine
answers.pearl: Beta-2 stimulation by epinephrine shifts potassium into cells, as in the transient hypokalemia of acute stress.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir disoproxil can cause Fanconi syndrome with renal potassium and phosphate wasting.

answers.name: Dextrose and parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Dextrose loads stimulate insulin release, and parenteral nutrition can trigger refeeding-related hypokalemia.

answers.name: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate
answers.pearl: Over-treatment with potassium binders can cause hypokalemia, and sodium polystyrene sulfonate also causes colonic injury.

answers.name: Caffeine
answers.pearl: Caffeine toxicity produces beta-adrenergic hypokalemia similar to theophylline.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis from mannitol increases urinary potassium loss.

answers.name: Dobutamine
answers.pearl: Dobutamine's beta-2 effect can cause a modest intracellular potassium shift during infusion.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Long-term PPIs can cause hypomagnesemia, which causes refractory renal potassium wasting.

answers.name: Cetuximab
answers.pearl: EGFR antibodies cause hypomagnesemia by blocking magnesium reabsorption, with secondary hypokalemia.

answers.name: Patiromer
answers.pearl: Potassium binders such as patiromer and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate can overshoot and cause hypokalemia.

answers.name: Itraconazole
answers.pearl: Itraconazole and posaconazole can cause a pseudohyperaldosteronism state with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Toluene
answers.pearl: Toluene inhalant abuse (glue sniffing) causes distal renal tubular acidosis with hypokalemia and weakness.

answers.name: Abiraterone
answers.pearl: Abiraterone blocks CYP17 and raises mineralocorticoids, causing hypokalemia and hypertension, so prednisone is given with it.

answers.name: Deferasirox
answers.pearl: Deferasirox can cause renal tubular injury and Fanconi syndrome with potassium wasting.

answers.name: Ritodrine
answers.pearl: Ritodrine, a beta-agonist tocolytic, causes intracellular potassium shift.

answers.name: Vitamin B12
answers.pearl: Starting B12 for severe megaloblastic anemia drives potassium into rapidly proliferating cells.

answers.name: Polymyxin B
answers.pearl: Polymyxins can cause renal tubular injury with potassium and magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Lenalidomide
answers.pearl: Hypokalemia is a commonly reported laboratory adverse effect of lenalidomide in myeloma.

answers.name: Azacitidine
answers.pearl: Azacitidine can cause renal tubular acidosis with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Clenbuterol
answers.pearl: Clenbuterol, a beta-agonist misused for weight loss and in bodybuilding, causes hypokalemia and tachyarrhythmia.

answers.name: Chloroquine overdose
answers.pearl: Acute chloroquine toxicity causes severe hypokalemia as a hallmark and worsens arrhythmia risk.

answers.name: Streptozocin
answers.pearl: Streptozocin causes proximal tubular injury and Fanconi syndrome with potassium wasting.

answers.name: Carbenoxolone
answers.pearl: Carbenoxolone, a licorice derivative, inhibits 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase and causes mineralocorticoid excess.

answers.name: Gossypol
answers.pearl: Gossypol, from cottonseed oil, was linked to hypokalemic paralysis when tested as a male contraceptive.

answers.name: Licorice
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhizin in licorice inhibits 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, causing pseudohyperaldosteronism with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin B forms membrane pores in the collecting duct, causing distal renal tubular acidosis and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Barium
answers.pearl: Barium poisoning blocks potassium channels, causing profound hypokalemia and paralysis.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that lower the seizure threshold or can cause seizures.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: alcohol withdrawal (a withdrawal state, not a drug), insulin/sulfonylureas (via hypoglycemia), salicylates, metoclopramide, cyclosporine/tacrolimus (PRES-related), busulfan, nelarabine, CAR-T/blinatumomab (ICANS), enflurane, propoxyphene (withdrawn), carbamazepine (overdose/paradoxical), tiagabine, intrathecal ionic contrast, synthetic cannabinoids.

answers.name: Bupropion
answers.pearl: Bupropion has dose-related seizure risk and is contraindicated in seizure disorders, bulimia and abrupt alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Tramadol lowers the seizure threshold, especially at high doses or with SSRIs, TCAs or MAOIs.

answers.name: Imipenem
answers.pearl: Imipenem has the highest seizure risk among the carbapenems, particularly in renal impairment or CNS disease.

answers.name: Theophylline
answers.pearl: Theophylline toxicity can cause refractory seizures, and levels do not always correlate with symptoms in chronic toxicity.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones antagonize GABA-A receptors, with risk increased by NSAIDs and renal impairment.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCA overdose causes seizures along with QRS widening, and sodium bicarbonate treats the cardiac toxicity.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Clozapine causes dose-dependent seizures, and risk is highest above 600 mg per day.

answers.name: Cefepime
answers.pearl: Cefepime can cause encephalopathy, myoclonus and nonconvulsive status epilepticus in patients with renal impairment.

answers.name: Meperidine
answers.pearl: The normeperidine metabolite of meperidine is neurotoxic and accumulates in renal failure, causing seizures.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine toxicity can cause seizures through sodium-channel blockade and catecholamine excess.

answers.name: Amphetamines
answers.pearl: Amphetamines and related stimulants can cause seizures in overdose or intoxication.

answers.name: Lidocaine
answers.pearl: Lidocaine toxicity begins with perioral numbness and tinnitus before seizures.

answers.name: Benzodiazepine withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation of benzodiazepines or barbiturates can cause withdrawal seizures.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Alcohol withdrawal seizures occur 6 to 48 hours after the last drink and are typically generalized.

answers.name: Insulin and sulfonylureas
answers.pearl: Hypoglycemia from insulin or sulfonylureas is a treatable cause of seizures.

answers.name: Penicillins
answers.pearl: High-dose penicillins and other beta-lactams antagonize GABA and can cause seizures, especially in renal failure.

answers.name: SSRIs and SNRIs
answers.pearl: Seizures occur with SSRI or SNRI overdose and with serotonin syndrome, and venlafaxine carries higher risk.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Metronidazole can cause encephalopathy and seizures with prolonged courses.

answers.name: Diphenhydramine
answers.pearl: Diphenhydramine overdose causes anticholinergic toxicity with seizures and QRS widening.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium toxicity can cause seizures, particularly in chronic toxicity with renal failure.

answers.name: Baclofen
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation of intrathecal or oral baclofen causes withdrawal with seizures, hyperthermia and rebound spasticity.

answers.name: Other antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Low-potency phenothiazines, loxapine and olanzapine lower seizure threshold, with chlorpromazine among the highest risks.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors cause seizures through neurotoxicity and PRES, particularly with hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus neurotoxicity includes tremor, PRES and seizures.

answers.name: Metoclopramide
answers.pearl: Metoclopramide is contraindicated in seizure disorders and can lower the seizure threshold.

answers.name: Bupivacaine
answers.pearl: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity causes seizures and cardiovascular collapse, treated with lipid emulsion.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide neurotoxicity can present as encephalopathy and seizures, and methylene blue is used for treatment.

answers.name: Mefloquine
answers.pearl: Mefloquine is contraindicated in patients with seizure disorders and can cause neuropsychiatric effects.

answers.name: Salicylates
answers.pearl: Severe salicylate toxicity causes seizures, often from CNS hypoglycemia and acidosis.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine overdose can produce seizures, and it can worsen generalized epilepsies such as absence.

answers.name: Chloroquine
answers.pearl: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can lower the seizure threshold in overdose and in epilepsy.

answers.name: Cycloserine
answers.pearl: Cycloserine causes CNS toxicity including seizures, and pyridoxine is given with it.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Intrathecal or high-dose methotrexate can cause seizures and leukoencephalopathy.

answers.name: Busulfan
answers.pearl: High-dose busulfan used in transplant conditioning causes seizures, so anticonvulsant prophylaxis is standard.

answers.name: Phencyclidine
answers.pearl: PCP intoxication can cause seizures, hypertension and agitation.

answers.name: Cytarabine
answers.pearl: High-dose cytarabine causes cerebellar toxicity and seizures.

answers.name: Synthetic cannabinoids
answers.pearl: Synthetic cannabinoids (K2, spice) are more likely than cannabis to cause seizures.

answers.name: Physostigmine
answers.pearl: Physostigmine can cause seizures, especially in tricyclic overdose, so it is generally avoided there.

answers.name: Enflurane
answers.pearl: Enflurane produces epileptiform EEG activity and is avoided in patients with seizure disorders.

answers.name: Intrathecal ionic contrast
answers.pearl: Intrathecal ionic contrast agents such as metrizamide cause seizures, and only nonionic agents are used now.

answers.name: CAR-T therapy and blinatumomab
answers.pearl: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity can present with seizures and cerebral edema.

answers.name: Propoxyphene
answers.pearl: Propoxyphene overdose causes seizures, and the drug was withdrawn for cardiotoxicity.

answers.name: Nelarabine
answers.pearl: Nelarabine has a boxed warning for severe neurotoxicity including seizures and demyelination.

answers.name: Tiagabine
answers.pearl: Tiagabine can cause seizures or nonconvulsive status epilepticus in people without epilepsy.

answers.name: Strychnine
answers.pearl: Strychnine antagonizes glycine receptors, producing painful convulsions with preserved consciousness.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid overdose causes refractory seizures that respond to pyridoxine, because it depletes GABA synthesis.

answers.name: Flumazenil
answers.pearl: Flumazenil can precipitate seizures in patients with chronic benzodiazepine dependence or co-ingested TCAs.

answers.name: Lindane
answers.pearl: Lindane, a topical scabicide, is neurotoxic and can cause seizures, especially in infants and with overuse.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hemolytic anemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: glyburide/sulfonylureas (G6PD labeling), isoniazid, flutamide, metamizole, furazolidone, nitrites, henna (a substance), IV vitamin C, menadione, complement inhibitors (extravascular hemolysis), oxaliplatin/carboplatin (immune hemolysis), NSAIDs covered as a class (mainly diclofenac/mefenamic acid).

answers.name: Primaquine
answers.pearl: Primaquine causes oxidant hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, so screen before starting.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Dapsone causes dose-dependent hemolysis and methemoglobinemia, more severe in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Nitrofurantoin triggers hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and can rarely cause immune hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Sulfonamides
answers.pearl: Sulfa drugs can cause oxidant hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and immune hemolysis.

answers.name: Ceftriaxone
answers.pearl: Ceftriaxone is a leading cause of severe immune hemolytic anemia, often in children and with sudden intravascular hemolysis.

answers.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
answers.pearl: Piperacillin-tazobactam can cause drug-dependent antibody immune hemolysis, sometimes severe.

answers.name: Penicillin
answers.pearl: High-dose penicillin can cause hapten-mediated immune hemolysis with a positive direct antiglobulin test.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine can cause immune hemolysis and also drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Ribavirin
answers.pearl: Ribavirin causes dose-dependent hemolysis and anemia, especially with interferon.

answers.name: Fludarabine
answers.pearl: Fludarabine causes autoimmune hemolytic anemia in CLL, and it is typically avoided after an AIHA episode.

answers.name: Phenazopyridine
answers.pearl: Phenazopyridine can cause oxidant hemolysis and methemoglobinemia, especially in G6PD deficiency or overdose.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Diclofenac and mefenamic acid are the NSAIDs most often linked to immune hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Rifampin can cause immune hemolysis, particularly with intermittent dosing.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine can cause immune hemolysis through a drug-dependent antibody mechanism.

answers.name: Chloroquine
answers.pearl: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, though the risk is low with standard dosing.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfasalazine can cause Heinz body hemolysis, especially in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Methylene blue
answers.pearl: Methylene blue is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency because it causes hemolysis and fails to reduce methemoglobin.

answers.name: Naphthalene
answers.pearl: Mothball naphthalene exposure causes hemolysis, particularly in G6PD-deficient infants.

answers.name: Clopidogrel
answers.pearl: Clopidogrel and ticlopidine can cause thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura with microangiopathic hemolysis.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Gemcitabine can cause drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis and renal failure.

answers.name: Mitomycin C
answers.pearl: Mitomycin causes cumulative-dose microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with renal failure.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors can cause thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus is an established cause of transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferons can cause autoimmune hemolytic anemia and thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
answers.pearl: Hydrochlorothiazide is a rare cause of immune hemolytic anemia, sometimes with severe intravascular hemolysis.

answers.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin
answers.pearl: IVIG can cause hemolysis from anti-A or anti-B isoagglutinins in non-O blood group recipients.

answers.name: Levodopa
answers.pearl: Levodopa can cause direct antiglobulin test positivity and, rarely, hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Procainamide
answers.pearl: Procainamide has been reported to cause autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones carry labeled hemolytic anemia warnings, including in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Bevacizumab
answers.pearl: VEGF inhibitors like bevacizumab can cause thrombotic microangiopathy, usually with proteinuria and hypertension.

answers.name: Pegloticase
answers.pearl: Pegloticase carries a boxed warning for hemolysis and methemoglobinemia in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid has been reported to cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and rarely immune hemolysis.

answers.name: Anti-D immunoglobulin
answers.pearl: WinRho and similar Rh immune globulin products can cause intravascular hemolysis when given to Rh-positive ITP patients.

answers.name: Tafenoquine
answers.pearl: Tafenoquine requires quantitative G6PD testing before use because of oxidant hemolysis.

answers.name: Glyburide
answers.pearl: Sulfonylureas, including glyburide, are labeled for hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Oxaliplatin
answers.pearl: Oxaliplatin can cause immune-mediated hemolysis, sometimes severe and life threatening.

answers.name: Carboplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents like carboplatin can cause drug-dependent antibody hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Menadione
answers.pearl: Menadione (synthetic vitamin K3) causes hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and neonates.

answers.name: Nitrites
answers.pearl: Nitrite exposure causes oxidant hemolysis and methemoglobinemia, and sodium nitrite carries a G6PD warning.

answers.name: High-dose intravenous vitamin C
answers.pearl: High-dose IV ascorbic acid can precipitate severe hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Flutamide
answers.pearl: Flutamide has been reported to cause hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia.

answers.name: Metamizole
answers.pearl: Metamizole (dipyrone), used outside the US, can cause immune hemolysis and agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Furazolidone
answers.pearl: Furazolidone is a nitrofuran that causes hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

answers.name: Complement inhibitors
answers.pearl: Eculizumab and similar agents can unmask extravascular hemolysis in PNH, and pegcetacoplan can cause hemolysis after discontinuation.

answers.name: Henna
answers.pearl: Henna (lawsone) causes severe hemolysis in G6PD-deficient infants.

answers.name: Rasburicase
answers.pearl: Rasburicase causes hemolysis and methemoglobinemia in G6PD deficiency, so test before use.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: Methyldopa induces autoimmune hemolytic anemia with a positive direct antiglobulin test.

answers.name: Cefotetan
answers.pearl: Cefotetan is a classic cause of severe immune hemolytic anemia, along with cefoxitin.

prompts.prompt: Name ways an aortic dissection can present (symptoms, signs, complications, or test findings).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dysphagia and Seizure (case-report level), Hemoptysis and Aortoesophageal fistula (rupture complications, rare), Superior vena cava syndrome (case reports), Fever (inflammatory, weak evidence), Calcium sign / Pleural apical cap / Tracheal deviation scored as board traps (judgment call).

answers.name: Chest pain
answers.pearl: Anterior chest pain is the most common presenting symptom of ascending (Stanford A) dissection.

answers.name: Back pain
answers.pearl: Interscapular or posterior pain is typical of descending (Stanford B) dissection.

answers.name: Sudden severe tearing pain
answers.pearl: Abrupt-onset, maximal-at-onset pain described as ripping or tearing is the classic quality.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Most patients are hypertensive at presentation, and chronic hypertension is the major risk factor.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Syncope occurs in a minority and suggests tamponade, rupture, or cerebral involvement.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Abdominal or flank pain suggests extension into the abdominal aorta with visceral or renal malperfusion.

answers.name: Pulse deficit
answers.pearl: Unequal or absent pulses reflect a dissection flap compromising a branch vessel.

answers.name: Arm blood pressure differential
answers.pearl: A systolic difference of more than 20 mmHg between arms raises suspicion but is absent in many cases.

answers.name: Shortness of breath
answers.pearl: Dyspnea may reflect acute aortic regurgitation with pulmonary edema, tamponade, or hemothorax.

answers.name: Hypotension
answers.pearl: Hypotension or shock indicates rupture, tamponade, or severe acute aortic regurgitation.

answers.name: Aortic regurgitation murmur
answers.pearl: A new diastolic decrescendo murmur results from root dilation or leaflet disruption in type A dissection.

answers.name: Diaphoresis
answers.pearl: Autonomic activation from severe pain produces sweating and pallor.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Involvement of the innominate or carotid arteries causes ischemic stroke or focal deficits and may delay recognition.

answers.name: Cardiac tamponade
answers.pearl: Hemopericardium from retrograde rupture into the pericardium is the leading cause of death in type A dissection.

answers.name: Widened mediastinum
answers.pearl: Mediastinal widening on chest radiograph is the most common radiographic abnormality but is absent in many.

answers.name: Myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Dissection into the coronary ostium, usually the right, can cause an inferior STEMI and misdirect treatment toward anticoagulation.

answers.name: Sudden death
answers.pearl: Rupture or tamponade can cause sudden cardiac death before medical contact.

answers.name: Acute limb ischemia
answers.pearl: Iliofemoral extension can cause a cold, pulseless, painful extremity.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Visceral pain and vagal activation cause nausea and emesis.

answers.name: Intimal flap on imaging
answers.pearl: A flap separating true and false lumens on CT angiography or TEE is the diagnostic finding.

answers.name: Acute heart failure
answers.pearl: Severe acute aortic regurgitation can cause flash pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Renal artery involvement causes malperfusion, flank pain, hematuria, and rising creatinine.

answers.name: Hemothorax
answers.pearl: Left hemothorax or hemorrhagic pleural effusion follows leak or rupture of a descending dissection.

answers.name: Elevated D-dimer
answers.pearl: D-dimer is highly sensitive and can help exclude dissection in low-risk patients, but it is nonspecific.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: A sense of impending doom may be prominent and is easily misattributed to panic.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Involvement of the celiac or mesenteric arteries causes bowel ischemia with lactate elevation and a poor prognosis.

answers.name: Paraplegia
answers.pearl: Compromise of the intercostal and lumbar arteries causes spinal cord ischemia with leg weakness.

answers.name: Elevated troponin
answers.pearl: Troponin may rise from coronary involvement or demand, and it can wrongly point to ACS.

answers.name: Hoarseness
answers.pearl: Compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve by an expanding arch or false lumen causes vocal cord paralysis.

answers.name: Normal ECG
answers.pearl: The ECG is normal or nonspecific in a large fraction of cases, which can falsely reassure.

answers.name: Painless dissection
answers.pearl: A minority, particularly the elderly and those with diabetes or neuropathy, present with no pain at all.

answers.name: Horner syndrome
answers.pearl: Compression of the sympathetic chain or carotid involvement can cause ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis.

answers.name: Neck or jaw pain
answers.pearl: Extension into the arch and carotids may produce neck, jaw, or head pain.

answers.name: Intramural hematoma
answers.pearl: Crescentic aortic wall thickening without an intimal flap is a variant of acute aortic syndrome with similar presentation.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever and leukocytosis from an inflammatory response may lead to a mistaken diagnosis of infection.

answers.name: Aortic root dilation
answers.pearl: Annuloaortic ectasia from Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos, or bicuspid aortopathy predisposes to type A dissection.

answers.name: Hemoptysis
answers.pearl: Rupture into the lung or tracheobronchial tree can cause hemoptysis, usually as a premorbid event.

answers.name: Pulsatile mass
answers.pearl: A pulsatile neck, chest wall, or sternoclavicular swelling can reflect false aneurysm formation after rupture.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Compression of the esophagus by a false lumen or hematoma has been reported to cause difficulty swallowing.

answers.name: Seizure
answers.pearl: Cerebral malperfusion has been reported to present with seizure, with dissection found only on later imaging.

answers.name: Superior vena cava syndrome
answers.pearl: A large aortic hematoma or pseudoaneurysm can compress the SVC in case reports.

answers.name: Aortoesophageal fistula
answers.pearl: Rupture into the esophagus causes hematemesis and is essentially a terminal event.

answers.name: Calcium sign
answers.pearl: Displacement of intimal calcification more than 1 cm from the aortic wall edge on radiograph is a memorized but insensitive sign.

answers.name: Pleural apical cap
answers.pearl: A left apical pleural cap on chest radiograph can reflect extrapleural blood from rupture of the aortic arch.

answers.name: Tracheal deviation
aliases: NG tube deviation to the right
answers.pearl: Rightward deviation of the trachea or nasogastric tube from mediastinal hematoma is a classic but unreliable radiographic clue.

prompts.prompt: Name ways hyperthyroidism can present (symptoms, signs, test findings, or complications), including in older adults.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Chorea (case reports), Pulmonary hypertension, Splenomegaly/lymphoid hyperplasia, Hyperemesis gravidarum (gestational transient thyrotoxicosis, not primary hyperthyroidism), Gynecomastia, Cholestasis, Hypercalcemia (mild), Onycholysis; Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis / Pretibial myxedema / Thyroid acropachy scored as board traps.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Unintentional weight loss despite normal or increased appetite reflects a hypermetabolic state.

answers.name: Palpitations
answers.pearl: Patients feel a racing or pounding heart from sinus tachycardia or atrial arrhythmias.

answers.name: Heat intolerance
answers.pearl: Increased heat production leads to discomfort in warm environments and preference for cool temperatures.

answers.name: Tremor
answers.pearl: A fine, rapid postural tremor of the outstretched hands is typical.

answers.name: Tachycardia
answers.pearl: Resting sinus tachycardia is the most common cardiovascular sign and persists during sleep.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Nervousness and restlessness are common and may be mistaken for a primary anxiety disorder.

answers.name: Excessive sweating
answers.pearl: Warm, moist, sweaty skin results from increased heat production and vasodilation.

answers.name: Suppressed TSH
answers.pearl: A low or undetectable TSH is the most sensitive test finding in primary hyperthyroidism.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue coexists with restlessness because of muscle weakness and poor sleep.

answers.name: Goiter
answers.pearl: Diffuse enlargement suggests Graves disease, whereas nodular enlargement suggests a toxic multinodular goiter.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Increased gut motility causes frequent loose stools or hyperdefecation.

answers.name: Insomnia
answers.pearl: Sleep disruption results from adrenergic excess and anxiety.

answers.name: Increased appetite
answers.pearl: Hyperphagia with weight loss is a clue to hypermetabolism rather than malignancy.

answers.name: Elevated free T4
answers.pearl: Elevated free T4 and/or T3 with suppressed TSH confirms overt hyperthyroidism.

answers.name: Irritability
answers.pearl: Emotional lability and irritability are frequent and affect relationships.

answers.name: Exophthalmos
answers.pearl: Proptosis from retro-orbital inflammation is specific to Graves disease and does not occur with other causes.

answers.name: Proximal muscle weakness
answers.pearl: Thyrotoxic myopathy causes difficulty climbing stairs or rising from a chair.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: AF occurs in 10 to 15 percent of patients and may be the only presenting feature in older adults.

answers.name: Hyperreflexia
answers.pearl: Brisk deep tendon reflexes with a shortened relaxation phase are common signs.

answers.name: Thyroid storm
answers.pearl: Thyroid storm is life-threatening decompensation with fever, tachycardia, and altered mentation, often precipitated by infection or surgery.

answers.name: Dyspnea on exertion
answers.pearl: Reduced exercise tolerance results from muscle weakness, increased oxygen demand, and cardiac effects.

answers.name: Lid lag
answers.pearl: Upper lid retraction and lid lag give a stare and result from sympathetic overactivity.

answers.name: Oligomenorrhea
answers.pearl: Menstrual irregularity and light or absent periods are common and can impair fertility.

answers.name: Hair loss
answers.pearl: Fine, thinning hair and diffuse alopecia occur with thyroid hormone excess.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: High-output states and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy can cause heart failure, especially in older adults.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Accelerated bone turnover causes bone loss and fracture, particularly in postmenopausal women.

answers.name: Wide pulse pressure
answers.pearl: Elevated stroke volume and reduced peripheral resistance widen the pulse pressure and cause isolated systolic hypertension.

answers.name: Apathetic hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Older adults may present with apathy, lethargy, and weakness instead of adrenergic symptoms.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Older adults may present with depressive symptoms and withdrawal rather than anxiety.

answers.name: Angina
answers.pearl: Increased myocardial oxygen demand can provoke angina in patients with underlying coronary disease.

answers.name: Confusion
answers.pearl: Elderly patients may present with delirium or cognitive decline that is reversible with treatment.

answers.name: Anorexia
answers.pearl: Older adults often lose appetite rather than gain it, mimicking malignancy or depression.

answers.name: Painful thyroid
answers.pearl: A tender goiter with elevated ESR points to subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis causing transient thyrotoxicosis.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Increased bone resorption causes mild hypercalcemia with suppressed PTH in a minority of patients.

answers.name: Onycholysis
answers.pearl: Separation of the nail from the nail bed (Plummer nails) is a sign of thyrotoxicosis.

answers.name: Mania or psychosis
answers.pearl: Severe thyrotoxicosis can produce mania, paranoia, or frank psychosis.

answers.name: Diplopia
answers.pearl: Extraocular muscle swelling in Graves orbitopathy restricts movement and causes double vision.

answers.name: Gynecomastia
answers.pearl: Increased conversion of androgens to estrogens and raised SHBG cause breast enlargement in men.

answers.name: Cholestasis
answers.pearl: Severe thyrotoxicosis and storm can cause hyperbilirubinemia and abnormal liver tests.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Graves disease can cause generalized lymphoid hyperplasia with mild splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and thymic enlargement.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Pulmonary hypertension is reported in Graves disease and often improves after restoration of euthyroidism.

answers.name: Chorea
answers.pearl: Thyrotoxic chorea is a rare movement disorder that resolves with treatment.

answers.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
answers.pearl: Very high hCG can stimulate the TSH receptor, producing transient biochemical thyrotoxicosis in pregnancy.

answers.name: Pretibial myxedema
answers.pearl: Nonpitting, violaceous plaques over the shins (thyroid dermopathy) are specific to Graves disease and rare.

answers.name: Thyroid acropachy
answers.pearl: Digital clubbing with periosteal bone formation is the rarest Graves extrathyroidal manifestation.

answers.name: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: Episodic hypokalemic flaccid weakness, usually in Asian or Hispanic men, is triggered by carbohydrate load or rest after exertion.

prompts.prompt: Name ways adrenal insufficiency can present (symptoms, signs, test findings, or complications).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Elevated TSH (reversible, case series), Ear cartilage calcification (older reports), Microcardia, Adrenal hemorrhage in antiphospholipid syndrome, Hypercalcemia, Muscle cramps/contractures, Checkpoint inhibitor hypophysitis (cause rather than presentation); Waterhouse-Friderichsen / Adrenoleukodystrophy / Sheehan syndrome scored as board traps (causes/syndromes rather than presentations).

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Profound fatigue and lack of energy are the most common and earliest symptoms.

answers.name: Weakness
answers.pearl: Generalized muscle weakness results from cortisol deficiency and electrolyte disturbances.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss is nearly universal in chronic primary adrenal insufficiency.

answers.name: Anorexia
answers.pearl: Loss of appetite accompanies weight loss and gastrointestinal symptoms.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Gastrointestinal symptoms can be prominent and are often mistaken for gastroenteritis.

answers.name: Hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: Excess ACTH and related peptides stimulate melanocytes, darkening skin, scars, and creases in primary disease.

answers.name: Hypotension
answers.pearl: Loss of mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid effects reduces vascular tone and volume.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Hyponatremia occurs in both primary and secondary disease from cortisol-dependent free water excretion and ADH excess.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Abdominal pain can be severe in adrenal crisis and mimic an acute surgical abdomen.

answers.name: Hyperkalemia
answers.pearl: Hyperkalemia results from mineralocorticoid deficiency and is present in primary but not secondary disease.

answers.name: Orthostatic hypotension
answers.pearl: Volume depletion causes postural dizziness and light-headedness.

answers.name: Dizziness
answers.pearl: Lightheadedness occurs from hypotension and volume depletion.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Lack of cortisol impairs gluconeogenesis, particularly in children and after fasting.

answers.name: Adrenal crisis
answers.pearl: Acute decompensation with shock, vomiting, and abdominal pain is precipitated by infection, surgery, or missed steroid doses.

answers.name: Salt craving
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid deficiency drives sodium wasting, so patients seek out salty foods.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Fainting follows orthostasis or a crisis with hypovolemia.

answers.name: Myalgia
answers.pearl: Muscle aches and joint pains are common nonspecific symptoms.

answers.name: Eosinophilia
answers.pearl: Loss of cortisol's suppressive effect on eosinophils produces mild eosinophilia.

answers.name: Low morning cortisol
answers.pearl: A morning cortisol below about 3 mcg/dL strongly suggests adrenal insufficiency, whereas above 15 largely excludes it.

answers.name: Abnormal cosyntropin stimulation test
answers.pearl: Failure of cortisol to rise after cosyntropin establishes the diagnosis.

answers.name: Elevated ACTH
answers.pearl: A high ACTH with low cortisol localizes disease to the adrenal gland (primary).

answers.name: Confusion
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency can cause delirium, lethargy, or obtundation.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Mood changes, irritability, and depression are common and may delay diagnosis.

answers.name: Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid deficiency impairs distal acidification and potassium and hydrogen secretion.

answers.name: Prerenal azotemia
answers.pearl: Volume depletion raises BUN and creatinine and can mimic acute kidney injury.

answers.name: Normocytic anemia
answers.pearl: A mild normocytic anemia and relative lymphocytosis are common hematologic findings.

answers.name: Vitiligo
answers.pearl: Coexisting vitiligo points to autoimmune Addison disease and may precede it.

answers.name: Hypotension refractory to vasopressors
answers.pearl: Shock in adrenal crisis often fails to respond to fluids and pressors until hydrocortisone is given.

answers.name: Loss of axillary and pubic hair
answers.pearl: Loss of adrenal androgens in women reduces body hair and libido.

answers.name: Mucosal hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: Dark patches on the buccal mucosa, gums, or palmar creases are characteristic of primary disease.

answers.name: Lymphocytosis
answers.pearl: Relative lymphocytosis accompanies eosinophilia from loss of cortisol's effect on lymphoid cells.

answers.name: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome
answers.pearl: Autoimmune Addison disease may be accompanied by thyroid disease and type 1 diabetes (APS type 2).

answers.name: Bilateral adrenal enlargement
answers.pearl: Enlarged adrenals on CT suggest infection (tuberculosis, histoplasmosis), hemorrhage, or infiltration.

answers.name: Adrenal calcifications
answers.pearl: Calcified adrenals on imaging suggest chronic tuberculosis or prior hemorrhage.

answers.name: Muscle cramps
answers.pearl: Cramps and rarely muscle contractures are reported, partly from electrolyte disturbance.

answers.name: Checkpoint inhibitor hypophysitis
answers.pearl: Anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1 therapy can cause ACTH deficiency, often presenting with headache, fatigue, and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Microcardia
answers.pearl: A small, narrow heart shadow on chest radiograph results from chronic hypovolemia.

answers.name: Elevated TSH
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency can raise TSH mildly and reversibly, which should not be mistaken for primary hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage in antiphospholipid syndrome
answers.pearl: Adrenal vein thrombosis and hemorrhage in APS can present as acute adrenal failure.

answers.name: Ear cartilage calcification
answers.pearl: Calcification of auricular cartilage is described in Addison disease.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Mild hypercalcemia occurs in some patients and corrects with glucocorticoid replacement.

answers.name: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome
answers.pearl: Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage with purpura and shock complicates fulminant meningococcemia.

answers.name: Adrenoleukodystrophy
answers.pearl: X-linked ALD presents with adrenal insufficiency in boys or young men, with elevated very long chain fatty acids.

answers.name: Sheehan syndrome
answers.pearl: Postpartum pituitary necrosis after hemorrhage causes secondary adrenal insufficiency and failure to lactate.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of sarcoidosis (pulmonary and extrapulmonary).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Gastric sarcoidosis, Epididymal involvement, Laryngeal sarcoidosis, Egg-shell calcification, Elevated soluble IL-2 receptor, Small-fiber neuropathy, Aspergilloma; Lofgren / Heerfordt / Panda sign scored as board traps.

answers.name: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Symmetric hilar and paratracheal nodes are the radiographic hallmark and the typical stage I finding.

answers.name: Cough
answers.pearl: A dry cough is among the most frequent respiratory symptoms.

answers.name: Shortness of breath
answers.pearl: Dyspnea on exertion reflects parenchymal involvement and fibrosis.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum
answers.pearl: Tender shin nodules are a sign of acute sarcoidosis and indicate a good prognosis.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue is common and disabling and may persist despite disease control.

answers.name: Uveitis
answers.pearl: Anterior uveitis is the most common ocular manifestation and can cause vision loss if missed.

answers.name: Joint pain
answers.pearl: Arthralgia and ankle periarthritis are frequent, especially with acute disease.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Granulomas produce 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, which raises calcium and urinary calcium.

answers.name: Skin lesions
answers.pearl: Cutaneous involvement includes papules, plaques, and nodules, and biopsy yields noncaseating granulomas.

answers.name: Noncaseating granulomas
answers.pearl: Noncaseating epithelioid granulomas on biopsy are the defining histologic finding but are not specific.

answers.name: Elevated ACE level
answers.pearl: Serum ACE is raised in many patients but has poor sensitivity and specificity.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever and constitutional symptoms accompany active disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary fibrosis
answers.pearl: Stage IV disease shows fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis and upper lobe volume loss.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss and anorexia can occur with active multisystem disease.

answers.name: Chest pain
answers.pearl: Substernal pain or tightness is common and usually noncardiac.

answers.name: Lupus pernio
answers.pearl: Violaceous indurated plaques on the nose, cheeks, and ears indicate chronic disease with upper respiratory and lung involvement.

answers.name: Peripheral lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Cervical, axillary, and inguinal nodes may be enlarged and firm without being tender.

answers.name: Perilymphatic nodules on CT
answers.pearl: Micronodules along bronchovascular bundles, septa, and fissures are the typical CT pattern.

answers.name: Cardiac sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Cardiac involvement is clinically evident in a minority but is a major cause of death.

answers.name: Heart block
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration of the septum causes atrioventricular block in young patients.

answers.name: Ventricular tachycardia
answers.pearl: Scar and granulomas provide a substrate for ventricular arrhythmias and sudden death.

answers.name: Facial nerve palsy
answers.pearl: Unilateral or bilateral Bell palsy-type weakness is the most common cranial neuropathy in neurosarcoidosis.

answers.name: Parotid enlargement
answers.pearl: Painless parotid swelling reflects glandular infiltration.

answers.name: Hepatic granulomas
answers.pearl: Liver involvement is often asymptomatic with a cholestatic enzyme pattern.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy leads to heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

answers.name: Nephrolithiasis
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria predisposes to kidney stones.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Splenic involvement can cause enlargement with cytopenias and hypersplenism.

answers.name: Aseptic meningitis
answers.pearl: Leptomeningeal granulomas cause a lymphocytic meningitis with low glucose in some patients.

answers.name: Dry eye
answers.pearl: Lacrimal gland infiltration reduces tear production and mimics Sjogren syndrome.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Fibrosis, vasculopathy, and extrinsic compression of pulmonary vessels can cause pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic-pituitary involvement causes diabetes insipidus and hypopituitarism.

answers.name: Sinonasal disease
answers.pearl: Nasal crusting, obstruction, and sinusitis, sometimes with septal destruction, reflect upper airway sarcoid.

answers.name: Interstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous interstitial nephritis can cause renal impairment that responds to steroids.

answers.name: Optic neuritis
answers.pearl: Optic nerve involvement causes visual loss and is one of the more serious ocular complications.

answers.name: Subcutaneous nodules
answers.pearl: Painless firm nodules in the subcutis (Darier-Roussy sarcoid) occur with systemic disease.

answers.name: Scar sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Old scars, tattoos, or traumatic sites become infiltrated and inflamed during active disease.

answers.name: Bone cysts in phalanges
answers.pearl: Lytic lesions with a lacy pattern in the hands and feet occur in chronic cutaneous disease.

answers.name: Elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
answers.pearl: Macrophage 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity drives extrarenal calcitriol production and hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Aspergilloma
answers.pearl: Cavitary fibrotic disease can become colonized by Aspergillus, producing a mycetoma and hemoptysis.

answers.name: Small fiber neuropathy
answers.pearl: Burning pain, dysautonomia, and fatigue in sarcoidosis may reflect small fiber neuropathy with normal EMG.

answers.name: Egg-shell calcification
answers.pearl: Peripheral rim calcification of hilar nodes is seen in chronic sarcoidosis (and silicosis).

answers.name: Elevated soluble IL-2 receptor
answers.pearl: Soluble interleukin-2 receptor levels reflect T-cell activation and track disease burden.

answers.name: Laryngeal sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Supraglottic infiltration causes hoarseness, stridor, and dysphagia.

answers.name: Epididymal involvement
answers.pearl: Epididymal or testicular nodules can mimic neoplasm and are found incidentally or on biopsy.

answers.name: Gastric sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Gastric involvement can mimic peptic ulcer disease, linitis plastica, or lymphoma.

answers.name: Lofgren syndrome
answers.pearl: Erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar adenopathy, fever, and ankle arthritis form an acute triad with a favorable course.

answers.name: Heerfordt syndrome
answers.pearl: Uveoparotid fever involves uveitis, parotid enlargement, fever, and facial nerve palsy.

answers.name: Panda sign
answers.pearl: Symmetric gallium uptake in the lacrimal and parotid glands creates a panda face on gallium scan (with the lambda sign in nodes).

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus (clinical or laboratory).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Lupus enteritis, Lupus cystitis, Bullous SLE, Anti-C1q, Lupus panniculitis, Shrinking lung syndrome, Macrophage activation syndrome, TTP; Libman-Sacks / Jaccoud arthropathy / False-positive syphilis serology scored as board traps.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue is the most common and often most disabling symptom.

answers.name: Joint pain
answers.pearl: Symmetric small-joint arthralgia or nonerosive arthritis of the hands and wrists is the most common presenting feature.

answers.name: Malar rash
answers.pearl: A fixed erythema over the cheeks and nasal bridge that spares the nasolabial folds.

answers.name: Positive ANA
answers.pearl: ANA is highly sensitive and a required entry criterion in classification, but is nonspecific.

answers.name: Photosensitivity
answers.pearl: Sun exposure triggers rash or flares of systemic disease.

answers.name: Lupus nephritis
answers.pearl: Glomerulonephritis affects up to half of patients and is a leading cause of morbidity; biopsy classes guide therapy.

answers.name: Proteinuria
answers.pearl: Persistent proteinuria above 0.5 g/day is a classification criterion and often the earliest sign of nephritis.

answers.name: Oral ulcers
answers.pearl: Painless oral or nasal ulcers on the hard palate are typical.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever and constitutional symptoms accompany flares, though infection must be excluded.

answers.name: Anti-dsDNA antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-double-stranded DNA is highly specific and its titer correlates with disease activity and nephritis.

answers.name: Pleuritis
answers.pearl: Pleuritic chest pain with or without effusion is a serositis criterion.

answers.name: Low complement
answers.pearl: Low C3 and C4 reflect consumption by immune complexes and track activity, particularly nephritis.

answers.name: Alopecia
answers.pearl: Diffuse thinning or non-scarring hair loss occurs with flares; scarring alopecia suggests discoid lesions.

answers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
answers.pearl: Digital vasospasm with color changes occurs in a substantial minority.

answers.name: Leukopenia
answers.pearl: Leukopenia and lymphopenia are common hematologic findings in active disease.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Immune thrombocytopenia can be the first manifestation and must be separated from TTP and antiphospholipid syndrome.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Anemia is usually of chronic disease but may be autoimmune hemolytic or iron deficiency.

answers.name: Anti-Smith antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-Sm is highly specific for SLE but present in only 20 to 30 percent of patients.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis with or without effusion is the most common cardiac manifestation.

answers.name: Lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Generalized soft, nontender lymph node enlargement is common during flares.

answers.name: Discoid lesions
answers.pearl: Chronic scarring plaques with follicular plugging, atrophy, and dyspigmentation on the face and scalp.

answers.name: Seizures
answers.pearl: Seizures are a neuropsychiatric criterion and may signal active CNS disease.

answers.name: Psychosis
answers.pearl: Lupus psychosis occurs in a small percentage and may be provoked by high-dose glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Antiphospholipid antibodies
answers.pearl: Lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies predict thrombosis and pregnancy loss.

answers.name: Venous thrombosis
answers.pearl: Thromboembolism is common, particularly in the setting of antiphospholipid antibodies and nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia with a positive direct Coombs test and low haptoglobin is a classification criterion.

answers.name: Recurrent miscarriage
answers.pearl: Fetal loss relates to antiphospholipid antibodies, active nephritis, and placental insufficiency.

answers.name: Subacute cutaneous lupus
answers.pearl: Annular or papulosquamous photosensitive lesions that heal without scarring, associated with anti-Ro/SSA.

answers.name: Elevated ESR
answers.pearl: ESR is typically markedly raised while CRP remains modest unless there is infection or serositis.

answers.name: Anti-Ro antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB are associated with sicca symptoms, SCLE, and neonatal lupus.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Stroke results from antiphospholipid-related thrombosis, vasculopathy, or Libman-Sacks emboli.

answers.name: Cognitive dysfunction
answers.pearl: Subtle impairment of memory, attention, and executive function is common and can occur without MRI changes.

answers.name: Accelerated atherosclerosis
answers.pearl: Premature coronary disease results from inflammation, steroids, and traditional risk factors and is a leading late cause of death.

answers.name: Congenital heart block
answers.pearl: Maternal anti-Ro/La transplacentally injures the fetal conduction system, causing neonatal lupus.

answers.name: Retinal vasculopathy
answers.pearl: Cotton wool spots, retinal hemorrhage, or vascular occlusion indicate active disease and warrant urgent evaluation.

answers.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
answers.pearl: TTP can occur in SLE and requires plasma exchange, not just immunosuppression.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: A rare but life-threatening complication with hemoptysis, anemia, and diffuse infiltrates, often with active nephritis.

answers.name: Lupus panniculitis
answers.pearl: Deep painful subcutaneous nodules heal with lipoatrophy and may precede systemic disease.

answers.name: Lupus enteritis
answers.pearl: Mesenteric vasculitis or enteritis causes abdominal pain with bowel wall edema on CT, sometimes mimicking an acute abdomen.

answers.name: Shrinking lung syndrome
aliases: restrictive lung disease with elevated diaphragms
answers.pearl: Dyspnea with elevated hemidiaphragms and restriction without parenchymal disease, likely from diaphragmatic dysfunction.

answers.name: Bullous lupus
answers.pearl: A subepidermal vesiculobullous eruption with anti-collagen VII antibodies that responds dramatically to dapsone.
