answers.name: Macrophage activation syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemophagocytic activation can complicate SLE and presents with fever, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, and hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Anti-C1q antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-C1q correlates with active lupus nephritis, particularly with low complement.

answers.name: Lupus cystitis
answers.pearl: Interstitial cystitis with bladder wall thickening, hydronephrosis, or ureteral involvement is a rare urinary tract manifestation.

answers.name: Libman-Sacks endocarditis
answers.pearl: Sterile verrucous vegetations on both sides of the mitral valve are associated with antiphospholipid antibodies.

answers.name: Jaccoud arthropathy
answers.pearl: Reducible, nonerosive deformities (ulnar deviation, swan neck) result from ligamentous laxity rather than synovitis.

answers.name: False-positive syphilis serology
answers.pearl: Biologic false-positive RPR or VDRL with negative treponemal tests occurs with antiphospholipid antibodies.

prompts.prompt: Name ways infective endocarditis can present (symptoms, signs, complications, or test findings).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: ANCA positivity (reported cases), Austin Flint murmur, Colon cancer association (S. gallolyticus), Endophthalmitis, Cutaneous vasculitis, Myocardial abscess, Coronary embolism, Mesenteric emboli; Osler nodes / Janeway lesions / Roth spots scored as board traps.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever is present in the large majority of patients, often low grade in subacute disease and absent in the elderly or immunocompromised.

answers.name: Positive blood cultures
answers.pearl: Multiple sets with typical organisms (viridans streptococci, S. aureus, enterococci, HACEK) are the major diagnostic criterion.

answers.name: New heart murmur
answers.pearl: A new or changing regurgitant murmur suggests valve destruction.

answers.name: Vegetation on echocardiogram
answers.pearl: An oscillating intracardiac mass on a valve or device is a major criterion, best seen on TEE.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue and malaise are frequent in subacute endocarditis.

answers.name: Chills
answers.pearl: Chills and rigors accompany bacteremia.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss and anorexia are typical of subacute disease.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Valve destruction with acute regurgitation is the most common cause of death and an indication for surgery.

answers.name: Petechiae
answers.pearl: Petechiae on the conjunctivae, palate, and extremities are the most common cutaneous finding.

answers.name: Splinter hemorrhages
answers.pearl: Linear subungual hemorrhages reflect microemboli or vasculitis but are nonspecific.

answers.name: Embolic stroke
answers.pearl: Septic emboli to the brain cause stroke in up to a fifth of patients and can be the presenting event.

answers.name: Joint pain
answers.pearl: Arthralgia, myalgia, and back pain are common and can mislead toward rheumatologic disease.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Splenic enlargement is more typical of subacute disease and reflects immune stimulation.

answers.name: Septic pulmonary emboli
answers.pearl: Right-sided endocarditis, classically in injection drug users, produces multiple cavitating nodules.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Normocytic anemia of chronic disease is present in most subacute cases.

answers.name: Elevated ESR and CRP
answers.pearl: Inflammatory markers are raised in nearly all patients but are nonspecific.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Staphylococcus aureus endocarditis may present as fulminant sepsis with shock.

answers.name: Valvular perforation
answers.pearl: Leaflet perforation or chordal rupture causes sudden severe regurgitation and hemodynamic collapse.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Renal injury arises from glomerulonephritis, emboli, septic shock, or antibiotic toxicity.

answers.name: Hematuria
answers.pearl: Microscopic hematuria suggests immune complex glomerulonephritis or renal emboli.

answers.name: Peripheral embolization
answers.pearl: Emboli to limbs cause acute arterial occlusion and ischemia.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Immune complex glomerulonephritis causes hematuria, proteinuria, and hypocomplementemia.

answers.name: Altered mental status
answers.pearl: Confusion may reflect emboli, meningitis, abscess, or sepsis and is common in elderly patients.

answers.name: Clubbing
answers.pearl: Digital clubbing occurs in long-standing subacute disease.

answers.name: Splenic infarct
answers.pearl: Left upper quadrant or left shoulder pain from splenic embolization.

answers.name: Back pain
answers.pearl: Back pain can reflect vertebral osteomyelitis, discitis, or epidural abscess complicating bacteremia.

answers.name: Paravalvular abscess
answers.pearl: Abscess of the valve ring is more common in aortic valve and prosthetic valve disease and portends surgery.

answers.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Hemorrhagic stroke arises from septic arteritis, mycotic aneurysm rupture, or hemorrhagic transformation of an embolic infarct.

answers.name: Mycotic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Infected arterial aneurysms, usually intracranial, form at emboli sites and can rupture.

answers.name: Prolonged PR interval
answers.pearl: New conduction delay or AV block suggests aortic root abscess extending into the septum.

answers.name: Rheumatoid factor positivity
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid factor is positive in about a quarter to half of subacute cases and falls with treatment.

answers.name: Septic arthritis
answers.pearl: Metastatic joint infection can be the presenting feature, especially with S. aureus.

answers.name: Low complement
answers.pearl: Hypocomplementemia from immune complex deposition accompanies glomerulonephritis.

answers.name: Splenic abscess
answers.pearl: A splenic abscess complicates splenic infarction and causes persistent bacteremia and left upper quadrant pain.

answers.name: Culture-negative endocarditis
answers.pearl: Prior antibiotics or fastidious organisms (Coxiella, Bartonella, HACEK, Brucella) cause negative cultures, requiring serology or PCR.

answers.name: Meningitis
answers.pearl: Purulent or aseptic meningitis can result from embolic or hematogenous seeding.

answers.name: Cerebral abscess
answers.pearl: Septic emboli can seed the brain, producing a ring-enhancing abscess.

answers.name: Acute myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Coronary artery embolization from vegetations, or compression by an aortic root abscess, can cause infarction.

answers.name: Cutaneous vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura from leukocytoclastic vasculitis can mimic primary vasculitis.

answers.name: Myocardial abscess
answers.pearl: Extension beyond the valve annulus into the myocardium causes abscess formation with conduction disturbance.

answers.name: Endophthalmitis
answers.pearl: Hematogenous seeding of the eye causes endogenous endophthalmitis with pain and vision loss.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Emboli to the mesenteric arteries cause abdominal pain with bowel infarction.

answers.name: Austin Flint murmur
answers.pearl: A mid-diastolic rumble at the apex accompanying severe acute aortic regurgitation from aortic valve endocarditis.

answers.name: Positive ANCA
answers.pearl: PR3 and MPO ANCA positivity are described and can mimic ANCA vasculitis, leading to diagnostic error.

answers.name: Streptococcus gallolyticus bacteremia with colon cancer
answers.pearl: Bacteremia or endocarditis with S. gallolyticus (bovis) should prompt colonoscopy for neoplasia or polyps.

answers.name: Osler nodes
answers.pearl: Tender, transient nodules on the finger or toe pads, caused by immune complex deposition.

answers.name: Janeway lesions
answers.pearl: Non-tender macules on the palms and soles caused by septic microemboli, classically in S. aureus.

answers.name: Roth spots
answers.pearl: Retinal hemorrhages with pale centers are reported in a minority and are nonspecific.

prompts.prompt: Name sites or presentations of extrapulmonary tuberculosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Tuberculous aortitis, Thyroid tuberculosis and Pancreatic tuberculosis (case-series level), Erythema induratum (a tuberculid, hypersensitivity rather than infection), Poncet disease (reactive), Hypercalcemia, Tuberculous brain abscess; Pott disease, Miliary TB and TB Addison scored as board traps.

answers.name: Tuberculous lymphadenitis
answers.pearl: Lymph node TB (cervical scrofula, with or without draining sinus) is the most common extrapulmonary site, and diagnosis needs node aspirate or biopsy with AFB culture.

answers.name: Pleural tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Typically a lymphocyte-predominant exudative effusion with high adenosine deaminase, from a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to mycobacterial antigens.

answers.name: Tuberculous meningitis
answers.pearl: Subacute basilar meningitis with low CSF glucose, high protein and lymphocytes, and a high risk of death or disability if treatment is delayed.

answers.name: Genitourinary tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Hematogenous seeding of the kidney can persist silently for years before presenting with dysuria, hematuria, or flank pain.

answers.name: Constitutional symptoms
answers.pearl: Fever, night sweats, anorexia, and weight loss can be the only features of extrapulmonary TB, especially in disseminated disease.

answers.name: Skeletal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Bone and joint TB arises from hematogenous seeding and can involve any bone, often with indolent pain and little fever.

answers.name: Abdominal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Ileocecal involvement can mimic Crohn disease or cancer, and diagnosis often requires colonoscopy with biopsy.

answers.name: Tuberculous pericarditis
answers.pearl: Presents with effusion that may progress to tamponade or constriction, and it is a particularly common extrapulmonary TB form in HIV.

answers.name: Tuberculous peritonitis
answers.pearl: Presents with ascites that is a lymphocytic exudate with a low serum-ascites albumin gradient and high ADA.

answers.name: Tuberculous arthritis
answers.pearl: Typically an indolent monoarthritis of a weight-bearing joint such as the hip or knee, with synovial biopsy offering the best yield.

answers.name: Cutaneous tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Skin TB ranges from direct inoculation to contiguous spread to hematogenous seeding, with varied morphologies.

answers.name: Disseminated tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Hematogenous spread to multiple organs is more common with advanced HIV and may present with fever and cytopenias without chest findings.

answers.name: Fever of unknown origin
answers.pearl: TB, especially extrapulmonary or disseminated, remains a classic infectious cause of prolonged unexplained fever.

answers.name: Laryngeal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Causes hoarseness and odynophagia and is highly infectious because of heavy bacillary burden in the larynx.

answers.name: Intrathoracic lymph node tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Hilar or mediastinal nodal TB is classed as extrapulmonary, is typical of primary TB in children, and can compress bronchi.

answers.name: Sterile pyuria
answers.pearl: Pyuria with negative routine urine cultures is a classic clue to renal or urinary tract TB, so send three early-morning urine AFB cultures.

answers.name: Hydrocephalus
answers.pearl: A frequent complication of TB meningitis from basal exudates blocking CSF flow or absorption.

answers.name: Cranial nerve palsies
answers.pearl: Basal exudate and vasculitis in TB meningitis commonly cause palsies, especially of the sixth nerve.

answers.name: Male genital tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Epididymal involvement presents as a painless nodular swelling and may form a scrotal sinus.

answers.name: Tuberculous cold abscess
answers.pearl: A painless, non-inflamed abscess, often paraspinal, in the psoas, or in the chest wall, from spread of spinal or nodal TB.

answers.name: Tuberculoma
answers.pearl: A granulomatous mass lesion, most often in the brain, that can cause seizures or focal deficits and may enlarge paradoxically on treatment.

answers.name: Female genital tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Usually involves fallopian tubes and endometrium and is an important cause of infertility, particularly in endemic regions.

answers.name: Tuberculous empyema
answers.pearl: A chronic purulent pleural collection with a thick pleural rind, requiring drainage in addition to antituberculous drugs.

answers.name: Ocular tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Presents as granulomatous uveitis, choroiditis, or retinal vasculitis, and a positive interferon-gamma release assay supports the diagnosis.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis from tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Fibrosis and calcification of the pericardium after tuberculous pericarditis cause constriction with right-sided heart failure.

answers.name: Ureteral stricture with hydronephrosis
answers.pearl: Fibrotic stricturing of the ureter, typically at the vesicoureteral junction, can lead to silent loss of renal function.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Granulomatous tissue produces 1-alpha-hydroxylase and raises calcitriol, so hypercalcemia can occur with active TB.

answers.name: Hepatic tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous hepatitis and cholestatic liver tests, with fever and hepatomegaly, are common in miliary or disseminated TB.

answers.name: Scrofuloderma
answers.pearl: Cutaneous breakdown over an underlying tuberculous lymph node, bone, or joint produces ulcers and sinus tracts.

answers.name: Lupus vulgaris
answers.pearl: A slowly progressive, apple-jelly-colored plaque, usually on the face, seen in previously sensitized hosts.

answers.name: Putty kidney
answers.pearl: End-stage renal TB with caseation and calcification gives an autonephrectomy, also called putty kidney.

answers.name: Prostatic tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Part of genital TB in men; may produce prostatic nodules and is often found incidentally on biopsy or in resected tissue.

answers.name: Tuberculous mastitis
answers.pearl: A rare breast presentation that can mimic carcinoma or pyogenic abscess and is diagnosed by biopsy with AFB staining.

answers.name: Tuberculous arachnoiditis
answers.pearl: Spinal arachnoiditis from chronic basal or spinal meningitis can cause radiculomyelopathy with paraparesis.

answers.name: Splenic tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Seen mainly in miliary or immunocompromised patients; presents with splenomegaly or splenic abscesses.

answers.name: Tuberculous otitis media
answers.pearl: Painless otorrhea with multiple tympanic perforations and facial palsy, unresponsive to ordinary antibiotics.

answers.name: Tuberculous brain abscess
answers.pearl: A rare, pus-containing CNS lesion distinct from a tuberculoma, with a more acute course.

answers.name: Erythema induratum
answers.pearl: Nodular vasculitis of the lower legs (Bazin disease), a hypersensitivity tuberculid rather than true skin infection, which resolves on TB treatment.

answers.name: Thimble bladder
answers.pearl: Late genitourinary TB can cause a contracted, small-capacity bladder from scarring.

answers.name: Thyroid tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Very rare, usually presenting as a thyroid nodule or abscess and found on fine-needle aspiration.

answers.name: Spina ventosa
answers.pearl: Tuberculous dactylitis of short tubular bones of the hands and feet, mostly in children, with fusiform swelling.

answers.name: Pancreatic tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Mimics pancreatic cancer with a mass and obstructive jaundice, and EUS-guided aspiration with AFB analysis can avoid surgery.

answers.name: Esophageal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Rare; presents with dysphagia, usually from mediastinal nodes eroding into the esophagus.

answers.name: Poncet disease
answers.pearl: A reactive, aseptic polyarthritis in patients with active TB that resolves with antituberculous therapy.

answers.name: Tuberculous aortitis
answers.pearl: Direct extension from adjacent nodes or foci can cause aortitis or mycotic aneurysm, with a high rupture risk.

answers.name: Pott disease
answers.pearl: Spinal TB (tuberculous spondylitis) typically involves the thoracolumbar vertebrae and causes kyphosis and possible cord compression.

answers.name: Miliary tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Hematogenous spread appears as innumerable 1-3 mm nodules ('millet seeds') on chest imaging, often with choroidal tubercles.

answers.name: Tuberculous Addison disease
answers.pearl: Bilateral adrenal destruction by TB is a classic infectious cause of adrenal insufficiency, with early enlarged and later calcified glands.

prompts.prompt: Name ways giant cell arteritis can present (symptoms, signs, complications, or test findings).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Elevated interleukin-6 (research marker), Aortic regurgitation, Coronary arteritis, Hearing loss, Throat pain, Tongue necrosis (case-report level), Cough/Facial pain as loose presentations; Halo sign, Skip lesions and Chalky white disc edema scored as board traps.

answers.name: New headache
answers.pearl: A new-onset temporal or occipital headache in a patient older than 50 is the most common symptom and should prompt an ESR and CRP.

answers.name: Jaw claudication
answers.pearl: Pain with chewing relieved by rest is the most specific symptom and strongly predicts a positive biopsy.

answers.name: Scalp tenderness
answers.pearl: Pain when combing hair or lying on a pillow reflects inflamed superficial temporal and occipital arteries.

answers.name: Vision loss
answers.pearl: Sudden painless monocular visual loss is the most feared complication and can become bilateral within days if untreated.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever is common, and fever with high inflammatory markers can be the only presentation in some patients.

answers.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
answers.pearl: About half of GCA patients have PMR with shoulder and hip girdle stiffness, and about 15 percent of PMR patients develop GCA.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Malaise and fatigue are common systemic symptoms from IL-6-mediated inflammation.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Unintentional weight loss with anorexia reflects systemic inflammation and can mimic malignancy.

answers.name: Elevated ESR
answers.pearl: ESR is usually markedly raised, often above 50 mm/h, but it is normal in a minority of patients.

answers.name: Elevated CRP
answers.pearl: CRP is more sensitive than ESR and the combination of both gives the best negative predictive value.

answers.name: Abnormal temporal artery
answers.pearl: A tender, thickened, nodular, or pulseless superficial temporal artery on examination raises likelihood of GCA.

answers.name: Amaurosis fugax
answers.pearl: Transient monocular visual loss is a warning sign of impending permanent visual loss and warrants urgent steroids.

answers.name: Diplopia
answers.pearl: Double vision results from ischemia of extraocular muscles or ocular motor nerves.

answers.name: Normocytic anemia
answers.pearl: Anemia of chronic disease with a high inflammatory marker is a frequent laboratory finding.

answers.name: Night sweats
answers.pearl: Sweats are part of the constitutional picture and can lead to a workup for infection or lymphoma.

answers.name: Loss of appetite
answers.pearl: Anorexia is part of the systemic inflammatory syndrome.

answers.name: Thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Reactive thrombocytosis from IL-6 is a common finding and is associated with ocular ischemic complications.

answers.name: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Arteritic AION from posterior ciliary artery occlusion causes sudden vision loss with pale (chalky) optic disc edema.

answers.name: Granulomatous panarteritis on temporal artery biopsy
answers.pearl: Biopsy shows transmural inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and lymphocytes, though giant cells are not required for diagnosis.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Vertebrobasilar territory strokes or TIAs occur in a minority and carry a higher risk than in age-matched controls.

answers.name: Arm claudication
answers.pearl: Subclavian or axillary stenosis from large-vessel involvement causes arm fatigue and pain with use.

answers.name: Central retinal artery occlusion
answers.pearl: CRAO can occur directly from arteritis and appears as a cherry-red spot with a pale retina.

answers.name: Dry cough
answers.pearl: Persistent dry cough, sometimes with throat pain, occurs in about 10 percent and can delay diagnosis.

answers.name: Fever of unknown origin
answers.pearl: GCA is a recognized cause of FUO in older adults, sometimes with no headache or visual symptoms.

answers.name: Facial pain
answers.pearl: Facial, ear, or neck pain can be a presenting or accompanying symptom.

answers.name: Elevated alkaline phosphatase
answers.pearl: A cholestatic liver test pattern, especially elevated ALP, occurs in a notable minority.

answers.name: Diminished pulses or blood pressure asymmetry
answers.pearl: Large-vessel (extracranial) GCA can cause pulse deficits, bruits, and blood pressure differences between arms.

answers.name: Aortitis
answers.pearl: Large-vessel GCA can involve the aorta and its branches and may be seen on CT, MRI, or PET.

answers.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Aneurysm risk is increased many-fold years after diagnosis, so long-term imaging surveillance is recommended.

answers.name: Normal ESR
answers.pearl: A minority of biopsy-positive GCA patients present with a normal ESR, so a low suspicion test result should not override clinical judgment.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Dissection or rupture is a late complication of aortic wall inflammation and aneurysmal change.

answers.name: FDG-PET uptake in the aorta and branches
answers.pearl: FDG-PET shows increased vascular uptake in large-vessel GCA and can help identify aortic or extracranial arterial involvement.

answers.name: Tongue pain or claudication
answers.pearl: Lingual artery ischemia causes tongue pain, especially with chewing or talking.

answers.name: Ophthalmoplegia
answers.pearl: Ischemic cranial nerve palsy or extraocular muscle infarction may cause ptosis and impaired ocular movement.

answers.name: Hearing loss
answers.pearl: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus from labyrinthine artery involvement are reported.

answers.name: Throat pain
answers.pearl: Sore throat or pharyngeal pain from external carotid branch ischemia is an unusual presenting symptom.

answers.name: Vertigo
answers.pearl: Dizziness, vertigo, or imbalance may reflect vertebrobasilar involvement.

answers.name: Scalp necrosis
answers.pearl: Skin ulceration or gangrene of the scalp is an uncommon but classic ischemic complication.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Mononeuropathies, mononeuritis multiplex, and brachial plexopathy can occur from vasculitic nerve ischemia.

answers.name: Visual hallucinations
answers.pearl: Complex visual hallucinations (Charles Bonnet syndrome) may accompany visual loss from GCA.

answers.name: Coronary arteritis
answers.pearl: Coronary artery involvement is rare but can cause angina or myocardial infarction.

answers.name: Aortic regurgitation
answers.pearl: Aortic root dilation from aortitis can lead to valvular regurgitation.

answers.name: Elevated interleukin-6
answers.pearl: IL-6 is the key driver of the acute phase response in GCA, and its blockade (tocilizumab) is steroid-sparing.

answers.name: Tongue necrosis
answers.pearl: Infarction of the tongue from lingual artery occlusion is a rare, dramatic presentation of GCA.

answers.name: Halo sign on temporal artery ultrasound
answers.pearl: A hypoechoic halo around the temporal artery lumen reflects mural edema and is a sensitive and specific ultrasound finding.

answers.name: Skip lesions on biopsy
answers.pearl: Segmental involvement can make a single biopsy falsely negative, so a longer specimen or contralateral biopsy may be needed.

answers.name: Chalky white optic disc edema
answers.pearl: Pallid disc swelling in arteritic AION is a classic fundoscopic sign distinguishing it from non-arteritic AION.

prompts.prompt: Name ways acute (primary) HIV infection can present.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Optic neuritis, Acute psychosis, Acute myelopathy, Myositis, Brachial neuritis, Urticaria (case-report level); Esophageal ulcers, Atypical lymphocytes and Opportunistic infection as loose items; Negative HIV antibody, Positive p24 and Palmar-plantar rash scored as board traps.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever is the most common feature of acute retroviral syndrome, typically 2 to 4 weeks after exposure.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Marked fatigue and malaise accompany the viremic surge and may persist for weeks.

answers.name: Sore throat
answers.pearl: Pharyngitis, sometimes with exudate, is common and often mistaken for streptococcal or EBV pharyngitis.

answers.name: Lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Painful generalized lymphadenopathy, often cervical, axillary, or occipital, appears as immune response develops.

answers.name: Rash
answers.pearl: A maculopapular rash on the trunk and face is seen in about half of patients, and an HIV RNA test should be sent when it accompanies fever.

answers.name: Myalgias and arthralgias
answers.pearl: Diffuse muscle and joint aches are frequent in viral syndromes and are reported in more than half of patients.

answers.name: Headache
answers.pearl: Headache is common and may be severe, sometimes reflecting aseptic meningitis.

answers.name: Mononucleosis-like illness
answers.pearl: The syndrome resembles EBV or CMV mononucleosis, so HIV should be on the differential of heterophile-negative cases.

answers.name: Night sweats
answers.pearl: Night sweats are reported by a substantial minority and can be prominent.

answers.name: Asymptomatic infection
answers.pearl: A sizable proportion of patients have no symptoms or only mild illness that goes unrecognized.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Gastrointestinal upset, including diarrhea, is a frequent feature of acute infection.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss of 2 to 5 kg is described in the first weeks of illness.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Nausea and vomiting can dominate the presentation and prompt a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis.

answers.name: Oral ulcers
answers.pearl: Painful mucocutaneous ulcers in the mouth, which can be misdiagnosed as aphthous disease or herpes.

answers.name: Loss of appetite
answers.pearl: Anorexia accompanies the viremic illness.

answers.name: Cough
answers.pearl: A dry cough can occur and prompt a workup for respiratory infection.

answers.name: Oral candidiasis
answers.pearl: Thrush in a healthy young adult, owing to transient CD4 depletion, should always prompt HIV testing.

answers.name: Genital ulcers
answers.pearl: Genital or perianal ulcers can be a feature of acute HIV and a risk marker for coinfection with HSV or syphilis.

answers.name: Elevated liver enzymes
answers.pearl: Mild transaminase elevations occur in a notable proportion and mimic acute viral hepatitis.

answers.name: Retro-orbital pain
answers.pearl: Pain behind the eyes with or without photophobia is a recognized feature.

answers.name: Aseptic meningitis
answers.pearl: Meningeal signs with lymphocytic CSF and negative cultures occur in the first weeks and may be the main presentation.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Transient thrombocytopenia can occur from immune-mediated destruction and marrow suppression.

answers.name: Lymphopenia
answers.pearl: A transient drop in lymphocytes is common early, followed by lymphocytosis as the immune response develops.

answers.name: Esophageal candidiasis
answers.pearl: Transient CD4 depression can allow odynophagia from esophageal candida in acute infection.

answers.name: High plasma HIV viral load
answers.pearl: HIV RNA levels are extremely high at seroconversion (often over a million copies per mL) and detectable before antibodies.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Mild normocytic anemia from inflammation and marrow suppression may appear.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Mild enlargement of the spleen can accompany the mononucleosis-like illness.

answers.name: Meningoencephalitis
answers.pearl: Direct CNS invasion can cause encephalopathy, seizures, or cranial neuropathies in acute infection.

answers.name: Atypical lymphocytes
answers.pearl: A mononucleosis-like atypical lymphocytosis on smear mimics EBV infection.

answers.name: Transient low CD4 count
answers.pearl: A temporary CD4 depletion can be severe enough to permit opportunistic infection before partial recovery.

answers.name: Opportunistic infection
answers.pearl: Rarely, transient immunosuppression allows AIDS-defining illness such as Pneumocystis pneumonia even in acute infection.

answers.name: Photophobia
answers.pearl: Light sensitivity may accompany meningeal irritation or retro-orbital pain.

answers.name: Facial nerve palsy
answers.pearl: Bell palsy-like facial paralysis has been reported in acute HIV and should prompt testing in young adults.

answers.name: Guillain-Barre syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy can occur around seroconversion, sometimes before the diagnosis.

answers.name: Esophageal ulcers
answers.pearl: Idiopathic esophageal ulceration with odynophagia occurs in acute HIV, responding to steroids or antiretrovirals.

answers.name: Indeterminate Western blot
answers.pearl: During seroconversion, an incomplete band pattern (for example p24 alone) is indeterminate and should lead to RNA testing.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Sensory or motor neuropathies, including mononeuritis, have been reported at seroconversion.

answers.name: Urticaria
answers.pearl: A transient urticarial eruption has been described as an acute HIV manifestation.

answers.name: Brachial neuritis
answers.pearl: Brachial plexus neuritis (Parsonage-Turner syndrome) has been associated with acute HIV.

answers.name: Acute myelopathy
answers.pearl: Transverse myelitis around seroconversion is reported.

answers.name: Myositis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory myopathy with raised creatine kinase and rhabdomyolysis can occur.

answers.name: Acute psychosis
answers.pearl: Acute neuropsychiatric presentations including psychosis, mania, or confusion are described as presenting features.

answers.name: Optic neuritis
answers.pearl: Optic neuritis has been reported as a rare neuro-ophthalmic presentation of acute infection.

answers.name: Negative HIV antibody test
answers.pearl: Antibody assays can be negative during the window period, which is why a combined antigen-antibody test or RNA is needed when acute HIV is suspected.

answers.name: Positive p24 antigen
answers.pearl: p24 antigen appears about 2 weeks after exposure and before antibodies, forming the basis of fourth-generation assays.

answers.name: Rash on the palms and soles
answers.pearl: A palmar-plantar eruption can mimic secondary syphilis, which should be tested for given the shared risk.

prompts.prompt: Name ways celiac disease can present, including non-gastrointestinal presentations.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dilated cardiomyopathy, Epilepsy with occipital calcifications, Cavitating mesenteric lymph node syndrome, IgA nephropathy (association-level evidence); Dermatitis herpetiformis, EATL and IgA deficiency scored as board traps.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Chronic diarrhea is the classic presentation, though it is absent in many adults who present with extraintestinal features.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Weight loss from malabsorption is common in classic disease, though many adult celiac patients are of normal weight or overweight.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Nonspecific abdominal pain and cramping are frequent complaints.

answers.name: Bloating
answers.pearl: Gas, distension, and bloating are common and often lead to a diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome.

answers.name: Iron deficiency anemia
answers.pearl: Iron deficiency anemia refractory to oral iron is one of the most common presentations in adults, from duodenal malabsorption.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue results from anemia, malabsorption, and inflammation.

answers.name: Steatorrhea
answers.pearl: Fatty, foul-smelling, floating stools reflect fat malabsorption with villous atrophy.

answers.name: Malabsorption
answers.pearl: Villous atrophy in the proximal small bowel impairs absorption of iron, folate, calcium, and fat-soluble vitamins.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Bone loss occurs from calcium and vitamin D malabsorption and may be the only presentation in adults.

answers.name: Failure to thrive
answers.pearl: Growth failure is a classic pediatric presentation, along with short stature and poor weight gain.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Vomiting is more typical in children but is reported in adults.

answers.name: Irritable bowel syndrome-like symptoms
answers.pearl: Celiac disease is found in a small proportion of patients labeled with IBS-D, so guidelines recommend screening.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: A significant minority present with constipation rather than diarrhea.

answers.name: Positive anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA
answers.pearl: tTG-IgA is the best screening test, and its level correlates with the degree of villous atrophy.

answers.name: Elevated transaminases
answers.pearl: Unexplained mild transaminase elevations are present in a notable fraction and typically normalize on a gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Lactose intolerance
answers.pearl: Secondary lactase deficiency from damaged brush border is common and may improve after mucosal healing.

answers.name: Aphthous stomatitis
answers.pearl: Recurrent aphthous ulcers are more frequent in celiac disease and may improve with a gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Villous atrophy
answers.pearl: Total or subtotal villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia and intraepithelial lymphocytosis is the histologic hallmark (Marsh 3).

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption causes low vitamin D, contributing to osteoporosis and osteomalacia.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression and anxiety are more common in celiac disease and often improve with dietary treatment.

answers.name: Migraine
answers.pearl: Headache and migraine are more prevalent in celiac disease, and are reported to improve with gluten withdrawal.

answers.name: Folate deficiency
answers.pearl: Folate is absorbed in the proximal small bowel, so deficiency is common and causes macrocytosis.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: B12 deficiency is seen less often than iron deficiency but is present in a minority, since ileal absorption is usually spared.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy is the most common neurologic association and may be the sole presentation.

answers.name: Delayed puberty
answers.pearl: Delayed puberty and menarche can be the only manifestation in adolescents.

answers.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: About 5 percent of type 1 diabetics have celiac disease, which is why screening is recommended at diagnosis.

answers.name: Hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Calcium and vitamin D malabsorption can cause low calcium, with tetany, cramps, or paresthesias.

answers.name: Infertility
answers.pearl: Unexplained infertility has been associated with undiagnosed celiac disease in both sexes.

answers.name: Dental enamel defects
answers.pearl: Symmetric enamel hypoplasia of permanent teeth is a classic extraintestinal finding in children.

answers.name: Autoimmune thyroid disease
answers.pearl: Hashimoto thyroiditis and Graves disease cluster with celiac disease through shared HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility.

answers.name: Osteomalacia
answers.pearl: Severe vitamin D deficiency leads to defective bone mineralization, causing bone pain and proximal weakness.

answers.name: Gluten ataxia
answers.pearl: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with anti-gliadin antibodies can occur even without any gastrointestinal symptoms.

answers.name: Vitamin K deficiency
answers.pearl: Fat malabsorption can cause coagulopathy with prolonged PT and bleeding.

answers.name: Recurrent pregnancy loss
answers.pearl: Celiac disease is linked to miscarriage, low birth weight, and preterm delivery, which improve with treatment.

answers.name: Autoimmune liver disease
answers.pearl: Autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis are more prevalent in celiac disease.

answers.name: Refractory celiac disease
answers.pearl: Persistent villous atrophy and symptoms despite 6 to 12 months of strict gluten-free diet; type 2 carries a risk of lymphoma.

answers.name: Hyposplenism
answers.pearl: Functional hyposplenism occurs in a notable proportion and raises infection risk, so vaccination for encapsulated organisms is advised.

answers.name: Small bowel adenocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Celiac disease raises the risk of small intestinal adenocarcinoma, usually in the jejunum.

answers.name: IgA nephropathy
answers.pearl: Mesangial IgA deposition is linked to celiac disease and may improve on gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Celiac crisis
answers.pearl: A rare, life-threatening presentation with severe diarrhea, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, and hypoalbuminemia, treated with steroids.

answers.name: Ulcerative jejunoileitis
answers.pearl: Multifocal ulceration of the small bowel in refractory celiac disease, with fever, pain, and perforation risk.

answers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy has been associated with celiac disease and may improve on a gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Collagenous sprue
answers.pearl: Subepithelial collagen deposition in the mucosa, typically a refractory form with severe malabsorption.

answers.name: Epilepsy with occipital calcifications
answers.pearl: Celiac epilepsy cerebral calcification syndrome is a rare triad with a regional predominance.

answers.name: Cavitating mesenteric lymph node syndrome
answers.pearl: A rare complication with hyposplenism and cavitating mesenteric nodes, associated with poor prognosis.

answers.name: Dermatitis herpetiformis
answers.pearl: Intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on extensor surfaces with granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae; treat with dapsone and gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
aliases: T-cell lymphoma of the small bowel
answers.pearl: Aggressive intestinal T-cell lymphoma arising from refractory celiac disease, often presenting with perforation or obstruction.

answers.name: Selective IgA deficiency
aliases: IgA deficiency with false negative serology
answers.pearl: About 2 to 3 percent of celiac patients have IgA deficiency, which can cause false-negative tTG-IgA testing.

prompts.prompt: Name ways primary hyperparathyroidism can present (symptoms, signs, test findings, or complications).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome (genetic, rare), Conjunctival calcification, Vascular calcification, Left ventricular hypertrophy, Impaired glucose tolerance, Hypertension (association level), Loss of lamina dura; Osteitis fibrosa cystica, Salt-and-pepper skull and Subperiosteal resorption scored as board traps.

answers.name: Kidney stones
answers.pearl: Nephrolithiasis (calcium oxalate or phosphate) is the classic renal manifestation, with hypercalciuria driving stone formation.

answers.name: Asymptomatic hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Most patients are now diagnosed through incidental hypercalcemia on routine chemistry.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue and lethargy are common and nonspecific complaints.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: PTH preferentially causes cortical bone loss, so DXA of the distal one-third radius can be abnormal even when the spine is normal.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia reduces smooth muscle tone in the gut, causing constipation.

answers.name: Polyuria
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia reduces renal concentrating ability, causing polyuria and polydipsia.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Mood symptoms and anxiety are common neuropsychiatric manifestations and may improve after parathyroidectomy.

answers.name: Muscle weakness
answers.pearl: Proximal muscle weakness and fatigability are described as a hypercalcemic myopathy.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia can cause abdominal pain from constipation, ulcers, or pancreatitis ('abdominal groans').

answers.name: Nausea
answers.pearl: Nausea, vomiting, and anorexia are typical of moderate to severe hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Bone pain
answers.pearl: Bone and joint aches are common and may be diffuse.

answers.name: Fractures
answers.pearl: Skeletal fragility leads to vertebral and non-vertebral fractures, a standard indication for surgery.

answers.name: Cognitive impairment
answers.pearl: Memory loss, poor concentration, and confusion ('psychic moans') may occur and sometimes resolve after surgery.

answers.name: Elevated PTH
answers.pearl: PTH is high or inappropriately normal in the setting of hypercalcemia, which is the biochemical hallmark of PHPT.

answers.name: Hypophosphatemia
answers.pearl: PTH inhibits proximal tubular phosphate reabsorption, causing low serum phosphate.

answers.name: Loss of appetite
answers.pearl: Anorexia accompanies hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: Elevated urinary calcium excretion despite renal calcium reabsorption raises stone risk.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Hypertension is common in PHPT, though it often does not improve after surgery.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Polyuria and vomiting cause volume depletion, which further worsens hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Hypercalcemic crisis
answers.pearl: Severe hypercalcemia (often above 14 mg/dL) with altered mental status and AKI requires aggressive hydration.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: An association with PUD exists, and it should prompt considering MEN1 with gastrinoma.

answers.name: Nephrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Calcium deposits in the renal parenchyma reduce GFR and concentrating capacity.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia is a recognized cause of acute pancreatitis.

answers.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia impairs aquaporin-2 function and causes a concentrating defect with dilute urine.

answers.name: Pseudogout
answers.pearl: PHPT is associated with CPPD arthropathy and acute pseudogout flares, sometimes after parathyroidectomy.

answers.name: Reduced glomerular filtration rate
answers.pearl: Chronic hypercalcemia and nephrocalcinosis can lower GFR, which is a surgical criterion.

answers.name: Short QT interval
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia shortens the ST segment and QT interval on ECG.

answers.name: Gout
answers.pearl: Hyperuricemia and gout occur more often in PHPT.

answers.name: MEN syndrome features
answers.pearl: PHPT can be the first sign of MEN1 (pituitary, pancreatic islet) or MEN2A (medullary thyroid cancer, pheochromocytoma), especially in younger patients.

answers.name: Chondrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Calcification of articular cartilage on radiographs is more common in PHPT.

answers.name: Brown tumors
answers.pearl: Osteoclastic lesions from severe PTH excess; they are lytic and now rare because of earlier diagnosis.

answers.name: Impaired glucose tolerance
answers.pearl: PHPT is associated with insulin resistance and increased diabetes prevalence.

answers.name: Elevated chloride-to-phosphate ratio
answers.pearl: A ratio above about 33 suggests PTH-dependent hypercalcemia from the mild hyperchloremic acidosis.

answers.name: Normocalcemic primary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Elevated PTH with persistently normal calcium once secondary causes are excluded; may progress to hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Band keratopathy
answers.pearl: Calcium deposition in Bowman layer at the limbus produces a grayish band, visible on slit lamp.

answers.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
answers.pearl: PHPT is linked to LVH and increased cardiovascular risk, with some data showing improvement after surgery.

answers.name: Vascular calcification
answers.pearl: Calcium deposition in vessels and cardiac valves is reported in PHPT.

answers.name: Loss of lamina dura
answers.pearl: Resorption of the lamina dura around teeth on dental radiographs is a subtle sign of hyperparathyroid bone disease.

answers.name: Conjunctival calcification
answers.pearl: Calcium deposits at the conjunctiva can cause a chronic red eye.

answers.name: Parathyroid carcinoma
answers.pearl: Suspect it with a palpable neck mass, very high calcium (above 14), and very high PTH; surgery with en bloc resection is key.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
answers.pearl: A familial syndrome from CDC73 (HRPT2) mutation with ossifying jaw fibromas and increased parathyroid carcinoma risk.

answers.name: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
answers.pearl: The classic advanced bone disease of PHPT, with subperiosteal resorption, brown tumors, and cystic change, now uncommon.

answers.name: Salt-and-pepper skull
answers.pearl: A granular radiographic appearance of the calvarium from patchy resorption and sclerosis in severe PTH excess.

answers.name: Subperiosteal bone resorption of the phalanges
answers.pearl: Subperiosteal erosion on the radial side of the middle phalanges is the most specific radiographic sign.

prompts.prompt: Name ways vitamin B12 deficiency can present (symptoms, signs, test findings, or complications).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Fever, Venous thromboembolism, Infertility, Vitiligo (association level), Pseudothrombotic microangiopathy, Gastric neoplasia (complication of autoimmune gastritis, not B12 itself), Lhermitte sign, Neural tube defects in offspring; Subacute combined degeneration, Hypersegmented neutrophils and Megaloblastic madness scored as board traps.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue and weakness are the most common initial complaints, from anemia and impaired energy metabolism.

answers.name: Macrocytic anemia
answers.pearl: Impaired DNA synthesis produces large red cells and megaloblastic marrow, with an MCV that can exceed 110.

answers.name: Paresthesias
answers.pearl: Numbness and tingling in the hands and feet, from posterior column and peripheral nerve involvement, are common neurologic presentations.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Symmetric stocking-glove sensorimotor neuropathy can be irreversible if treatment is delayed.

answers.name: Glossitis
answers.pearl: A smooth, beefy-red, sore tongue from papillary atrophy.

answers.name: Weakness
answers.pearl: Generalized weakness is common and may be neuromuscular or anemia-related.

answers.name: Cognitive impairment
answers.pearl: Memory loss, slowed thinking, and dementia-like picture can occur, sometimes without anemia.

answers.name: Gait ataxia
answers.pearl: Dorsal column and cerebellar involvement cause unsteadiness and falls.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression, irritability, and personality change are among the neuropsychiatric effects and can be the only presentation.

answers.name: Low serum B12 level
answers.pearl: A level below about 200 pg/mL is diagnostic, while borderline values (200 to 300) should prompt methylmalonic acid testing.

answers.name: Pallor
answers.pearl: Pallor reflects anemia and may be accompanied by a lemon-yellow tint from mild hemolysis.

answers.name: Shortness of breath
answers.pearl: Exertional dyspnea occurs with moderate to severe anemia.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Anorexia and malabsorption can lead to weight loss.

answers.name: Tachycardia
answers.pearl: Compensatory tachycardia and palpitations accompany severe anemia.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Gastrointestinal mucosal turnover is affected, so diarrhea and other GI symptoms may occur.

answers.name: Mild jaundice
answers.pearl: Ineffective erythropoiesis causes intramedullary hemolysis and a mildly elevated indirect bilirubin.

answers.name: Loss of vibration and proprioception
answers.pearl: Posterior column dysfunction causes loss of vibration sense and position sense, often an early sign.

answers.name: Elevated methylmalonic acid
answers.pearl: MMA is elevated in tissue B12 deficiency and helps confirm borderline B12 levels; it also rises with renal insufficiency.

answers.name: Elevated homocysteine
answers.pearl: Homocysteine rises in both B12 and folate deficiency, so it is sensitive but less specific than MMA.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Low platelets can result from ineffective megakaryopoiesis.

answers.name: Leukopenia
answers.pearl: Ineffective granulopoiesis can lower the white count.

answers.name: Elevated LDH
answers.pearl: Ineffective erythropoiesis releases LDH from intramedullary hemolysis, sometimes to very high levels.

answers.name: Pancytopenia
aliases: low blood counts in all lines
answers.pearl: Severe deficiency suppresses all three cell lines and can mimic aplastic anemia or myelodysplasia.

answers.name: Angular cheilitis
answers.pearl: Cracking at the mouth corners accompanies other mucosal changes of B vitamin deficiency.

answers.name: Positive intrinsic factor antibodies
answers.pearl: Intrinsic factor antibodies are highly specific for pernicious anemia (autoimmune gastritis).

answers.name: Upper motor neuron signs
answers.pearl: Spastic weakness, hyperreflexia, and extensor plantar responses result from lateral corticospinal tract involvement.

answers.name: Neurologic disease without anemia
answers.pearl: Neuropsychiatric manifestations can occur with normal hemoglobin and MCV, so do not rely on the CBC to exclude B12 deficiency.

answers.name: Low reticulocyte count
answers.pearl: An inappropriately low reticulocyte response for the degree of anemia indicates a production defect.

answers.name: Megaloblastic bone marrow
answers.pearl: Hypercellular marrow with large precursors showing nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony and giant metamyelocytes.

answers.name: Oral ulcers
answers.pearl: Recurrent aphthous-type ulceration may be an overlooked manifestation.

answers.name: Urinary or fecal incontinence
answers.pearl: Sphincter disturbance can result from myelopathy or autonomic involvement.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Severe anemia can precipitate high-output heart failure, and hyperhomocysteinemia contributes to cardiovascular risk.

answers.name: Skin hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: Reversible hyperpigmentation of the knuckles, palms, soles, or nails occurs, mainly in darker-skinned patients.

answers.name: Neural tube defects in offspring
answers.pearl: Maternal B12 deficiency is an independent risk factor for neural tube defects, alongside folate.

answers.name: Developmental delay in infants
answers.pearl: Infants of B12-deficient mothers (often vegans) can present with hypotonia, failure to thrive, tremor, and developmental regression.

answers.name: Autonomic dysfunction
answers.pearl: Orthostatic hypotension, impotence, and bladder disturbance can arise from autonomic neuropathy.

answers.name: Optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Bilateral central visual loss from optic neuropathy is an uncommon, usually reversible manifestation.

answers.name: Vitiligo
answers.pearl: Vitiligo clusters with pernicious anemia through shared autoimmune susceptibility.

answers.name: Infertility
answers.pearl: B12 deficiency has been linked to infertility and recurrent miscarriage in both sexes.

answers.name: Venous thromboembolism
answers.pearl: Hyperhomocysteinemia is prothrombotic, and venous thrombosis has been reported with B12 deficiency.

answers.name: Lhermitte sign
aliases: electric shock sensation on neck flexion
answers.pearl: An electric shock sensation down the spine on neck flexion can occur with cervical cord dorsal column involvement.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever has been reported and resolves with treatment.

answers.name: Gastric neoplasia
answers.pearl: Pernicious anemia raises the risk of gastric adenocarcinoma and type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumors, so endoscopic surveillance is considered.

answers.name: Pseudothrombotic microangiopathy
answers.pearl: Severe deficiency can mimic TTP with schistocytes, high LDH, and thrombocytopenia, but resolves with B12 replacement.

answers.name: Subacute combined degeneration
aliases: subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord
answers.pearl: Demyelination of the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts causes sensory ataxia and spastic weakness.

answers.name: Hypersegmented neutrophils
answers.pearl: Five or more nuclear lobes in neutrophils is an early smear finding of megaloblastic anemia.

answers.name: Megaloblastic madness
answers.pearl: A term for psychosis, paranoia, or mania from B12 deficiency, which can precede hematologic changes.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypocalcemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Anti-CaSR antibodies (acquired hypocalcemia, case-series level); Wilson disease (parathyroid copper deposition, case reports); Toxic shock syndrome (documented but mechanism unclear); Fluoride toxicity; Gadolinium contrast interference (spurious, assay-dependent). Hypoalbuminemia lowers total but not ionized calcium (pseudohypocalcemia). Board Prep Traps: DiGeorge, pseudohypoparathyroidism, vitamin D-dependent rickets.

answers.name: Hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Inadequate PTH leaves calcium low and phosphate high, most often from neck surgery or autoimmune disease.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Low 25-OH vitamin D reduces intestinal calcium absorption, and secondary hyperparathyroidism often keeps calcium near normal until deficiency is severe.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Failure to make calcitriol plus phosphate retention drives hypocalcemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Acute pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Calcium saponifies in peripancreatic fat necrosis, and a low calcium signals more severe disease.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: Low magnesium impairs PTH secretion and causes PTH resistance, so calcium will not correct until magnesium is replaced.

answers.name: Neck surgery
answers.pearl: Thyroidectomy or parathyroidectomy can remove or devascularize the parathyroids, causing transient or permanent hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Low albumin lowers total calcium, but the ionized fraction is normal, so this is pseudohypocalcemia that needs correction or an ionized level.

answers.name: Malabsorption
answers.pearl: Fat malabsorption impairs absorption of vitamin D and calcium, and calcium binds to unabsorbed fatty acids in the gut.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics increase urinary calcium excretion by blocking the TAL transporter that drives paracellular calcium reabsorption.

answers.name: Bisphosphonates
answers.pearl: Potent osteoclast inhibition can reduce calcium, particularly when vitamin D is deficient, as with intravenous zoledronic acid.

answers.name: Denosumab
answers.pearl: RANKL blockade can cause profound hypocalcemia, especially in advanced kidney disease and vitamin D deficiency.

answers.name: Massive blood transfusion
answers.pearl: Citrate in stored blood chelates ionized calcium, especially with rapid transfusion or hepatic dysfunction.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Calcium deposits in injured muscle and phosphate release binds calcium, with rebound hypercalcemia later in recovery.

answers.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
answers.pearl: Massive cell lysis releases phosphate that complexes with calcium, producing hypocalcemia with hyperphosphatemia.

answers.name: Hyperphosphatemia
answers.pearl: Excess phosphate precipitates with calcium and suppresses calcitriol synthesis, lowering serum calcium.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Critical illness, cytokines and low PTH or calcitriol response contribute, and low ionized calcium predicts mortality.

answers.name: Chronic alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol causes hypomagnesemia, poor intake, pancreatitis and vitamin D deficiency, all lowering calcium.

answers.name: Nutritional rickets
answers.pearl: Dietary lack of vitamin D or calcium in children impairs bone mineralization, with hypocalcemia, high ALP and PTH.

answers.name: Alkalosis
answers.pearl: Alkalemia increases albumin binding of calcium, lowering the ionized fraction and causing tetany, as in hyperventilation.

answers.name: Anticonvulsants
answers.pearl: Phenytoin, phenobarbital and carbamazepine induce hepatic enzymes that accelerate vitamin D catabolism.

answers.name: Cinacalcet
answers.pearl: Calcimimetics suppress PTH by activating the calcium-sensing receptor, and can overshoot to hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Villous atrophy reduces absorption of calcium and vitamin D, producing osteomalacia and hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Bariatric surgery
answers.pearl: Roux-en-Y bypass bypasses the duodenum where calcium is absorbed and causes vitamin D malabsorption.

answers.name: Hungry bone syndrome
answers.pearl: After parathyroidectomy for severe hyperparathyroidism, bone avidly takes up calcium, causing profound hypocalcemia with low phosphate and magnesium.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents cause renal magnesium wasting and tubular injury, leading to hypomagnesemia and hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Urinary loss of vitamin D binding protein and albumin lowers total calcium and 25-OH vitamin D.

answers.name: Osteoblastic metastases
answers.pearl: Prostate and breast cancer osteoblastic lesions take up calcium into new bone, sometimes causing hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Long-term PPIs cause hypomagnesemia and may reduce calcium absorption, leading to secondary hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Foscarnet chelates ionized calcium and can cause symptomatic hypocalcemia with infusion.

answers.name: Ethylene glycol poisoning
answers.pearl: Oxalate formed from metabolism precipitates with calcium, and the ECG may show a prolonged QT.

answers.name: Radiation to the neck
answers.pearl: Prior radioiodine or external beam radiation can damage the parathyroids, causing delayed hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Hydrofluoric acid exposure
answers.pearl: Fluoride ions bind calcium and magnesium avidly, causing severe hypocalcemia and arrhythmias after even small burns.

answers.name: Iron overload
answers.pearl: Parathyroid iron deposition in hemochromatosis or transfusion-dependent thalassemia can cause hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1
answers.pearl: AIRE mutation causes chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism and Addison disease.

answers.name: Metastatic infiltration of parathyroid glands
answers.pearl: Rarely, tumor infiltration or amyloid deposition in the glands causes hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Activating mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor lower the PTH set point and cause hypercalciuria; calcium and vitamin D can worsen kidney calcification.

answers.name: Osteopetrosis
answers.pearl: Defective osteoclasts block bone resorption, so calcium cannot be mobilized, causing hypocalcemia in severe forms.

answers.name: Spurious hypocalcemia from gadolinium contrast
answers.pearl: Certain gadolinium agents interfere with colorimetric calcium assays, giving falsely low readings after MRI contrast.

answers.name: Mitochondrial disorders
answers.pearl: Kearns-Sayre and MELAS can include hypoparathyroidism with ophthalmoplegia and heart block.

answers.name: HDR syndrome
answers.pearl: GATA3 haploinsufficiency causes hypoparathyroidism, sensorineural deafness and renal dysplasia.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper deposition in the parathyroid glands has been reported to cause hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Anti-calcium-sensing receptor antibodies
answers.pearl: Acquired activating antibodies against the CaSR can cause autoimmune hypoparathyroid-like hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Toxic shock syndrome
answers.pearl: Hypocalcemia has been described with toxic shock, likely from cytokine effects and PTH resistance.

answers.name: DiGeorge syndrome
answers.pearl: 22q11.2 deletion causes thymic and parathyroid aplasia, cardiac defects and neonatal hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: End-organ resistance to PTH produces hypocalcemia with high PTH, and type 1a has Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.

answers.name: Vitamin D-dependent rickets
answers.pearl: Mutations in 1-alpha-hydroxylase (type 1) or the vitamin D receptor (type 2) cause hypocalcemic rickets despite normal vitamin D intake.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypomagnesemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Capreomycin (older TB drug, limited data); Hyperthyroidism not included; Catecholamine/MI shift (modest, mostly observational); Burns (documented, mechanism mixed); Mannitol and cardiopulmonary bypass (dilutional/renal losses); EAST/SeSAME and FXYD2 (rare monogenic). Gitelman scored as a Board Prep Trap.

answers.name: Alcohol use disorder
answers.pearl: Poor intake, GI losses, renal magnesium wasting and pancreatitis all contribute, and magnesium is frequently low in alcohol withdrawal.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Chronic PPI use impairs intestinal magnesium absorption, a recognized cause of severe hypomagnesemia refractory to oral supplements.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Inhibition of the thick ascending limb abolishes the lumen-positive potential that drives magnesium reabsorption.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause renal magnesium wasting and hypokalemia, with magnesium loss from DCT TRPM6 downregulation.

answers.name: Diarrhea
answers.pearl: Intestinal fluid is magnesium-rich and diarrhea from any cause depletes body magnesium.

answers.name: Malnutrition
answers.pearl: Reduced dietary intake lowers magnesium stores, particularly in hospitalized or elderly patients.

answers.name: Malabsorption
answers.pearl: Fat malabsorption and steatorrhea bind magnesium as soaps and cause fecal loss.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis and insulin resistance cause renal magnesium wasting, and hypomagnesemia worsens glycemic control.

answers.name: Refeeding syndrome
answers.pearl: Insulin-driven cellular uptake of magnesium, phosphate and potassium during nutritional repletion can drop levels abruptly.

answers.name: Vomiting
answers.pearl: Prolonged vomiting and nasogastric suction cause loss of upper GI magnesium and volume depletion.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agents damage the distal tubule and cause persistent urinary magnesium wasting even after therapy ends.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin causes distal tubular injury with wasting of magnesium and potassium.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides damage the tubule and may reduce magnesium reabsorption through calcium-sensing receptor stimulation.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus downregulate distal magnesium channels, causing renal wasting in transplant recipients.

answers.name: Acute pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Fat saponification binds magnesium, and alcohol use often coexists.

answers.name: EGFR inhibitors
answers.pearl: Cetuximab and panitumumab block EGF-mediated TRPM6 activation in the distal tubule, causing dose-related magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Bariatric surgery
answers.pearl: Malabsorptive procedures reduce intestinal magnesium uptake and cause diarrhea.

answers.name: Short bowel syndrome
answers.pearl: Loss of absorptive surface leads to magnesium malabsorption and chronic fecal loss.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Chronic diarrhea and ileal disease or resection reduce magnesium absorption.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Villous atrophy leads to malabsorption of magnesium along with other micronutrients.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: High calcium stimulates the calcium-sensing receptor in the thick ascending limb, reducing magnesium reabsorption.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use causes intestinal magnesium loss and volume depletion, often in eating disorders.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Critical illness commonly produces low magnesium through renal loss, redistribution and poor intake.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis depletes magnesium, and insulin therapy shifts remaining magnesium into cells.

answers.name: Insulin therapy
answers.pearl: Insulin moves magnesium into cells, lowering serum levels in already depleted patients.

answers.name: Primary aldosteronism
answers.pearl: Volume expansion and mineralocorticoid excess increase renal magnesium excretion.

answers.name: Postobstructive diuresis
answers.pearl: Large urine volume after relief of obstruction washes out magnesium and other electrolytes.

answers.name: Recovery phase of acute tubular necrosis
answers.pearl: Polyuria in the diuretic phase causes loss of magnesium before tubular reabsorption recovers.

answers.name: Hungry bone syndrome
answers.pearl: Avid skeletal uptake of mineral after parathyroidectomy lowers magnesium along with calcium and phosphate.

answers.name: Kidney transplantation
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors, post-transplant diuresis and PPIs combine to lower magnesium after transplant.

answers.name: Extreme sweating
answers.pearl: Prolonged exertion and heat exposure produce magnesium loss in sweat in addition to dilution.

answers.name: Acute myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surge and lipolysis shift magnesium intracellularly during acute coronary events.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Large burns cause exudative losses and increased urinary magnesium excretion.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Foscarnet is associated with renal magnesium wasting along with hypocalcemia and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Cardiopulmonary bypass
answers.pearl: Hemodilution, citrate and transfusion, and urinary loss after bypass lower serum magnesium.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis from mannitol increases urinary magnesium excretion.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine can cause renal magnesium and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide causes proximal tubular injury (Fanconi syndrome) with associated magnesium loss.

answers.name: Capreomycin
answers.pearl: Capreomycin, used in drug-resistant TB, causes tubular wasting of magnesium, potassium and calcium.

answers.name: Familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Mutations in claudin-16 or claudin-19 impair paracellular magnesium and calcium reabsorption in the thick ascending limb.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia with secondary hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Loss-of-function TRPM6 mutations impair intestinal and renal magnesium absorption and cause seizures in infancy.

answers.name: HNF1B mutation
answers.pearl: HNF1B defects cause renal cysts and diabetes with hypomagnesemia from reduced FXYD2 expression.

answers.name: FXYD2 mutation
answers.pearl: Defects in the gamma subunit of the Na-K-ATPase cause dominant renal magnesium wasting with hypocalciuria.

answers.name: EAST syndrome
answers.pearl: KCNJ10 mutations cause epilepsy, ataxia, sensorineural deafness and a salt-losing tubulopathy with hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Gitelman syndrome
answers.pearl: NCC loss-of-function causes hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia, resembling chronic thiazide use.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome
answers.pearl: Thick ascending limb transport defects cause hypokalemic alkalosis with hypercalciuria, and hypomagnesemia in some subtypes.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypophosphatemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Salicylate toxicity (reported, mechanism is respiratory alkalosis plus renal loss); Theophylline and heat stroke (modest data); Wilson disease and Lowe/Dent syndromes (renal Fanconi pattern, uncommon); Epidermal nevus syndrome and ADHR/ARHR (FGF23-mediated, rare); GM-CSF recovery (cell uptake); Glucocorticoids (weak). Board Prep Traps: X-linked hypophosphatemia, McCune-Albright syndrome, tumor-induced osteomalacia.

answers.name: Refeeding syndrome
answers.pearl: Insulin surge and anabolism drive phosphate into cells in malnourished patients restarting nutrition, causing dangerous drops within days.

answers.name: Alcohol use disorder
answers.pearl: Poor intake, vomiting, urinary loss and refeeding all lower phosphate, and nadir often follows admission glucose.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis depletes total body phosphate, and insulin therapy drives remaining phosphate into cells.

answers.name: Malnutrition
answers.pearl: Low dietary intake and low stores leave little buffer, especially in starvation or anorexia nervosa.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Lower calcium absorption raises PTH, which increases urinary phosphate loss.

answers.name: Phosphate binders and antacids
answers.pearl: Aluminum- or magnesium-containing antacids bind dietary phosphate in the gut.

answers.name: Malabsorption
answers.pearl: Fat malabsorption and diarrhea impair absorption of vitamin D and phosphate.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Excess PTH inhibits proximal tubular phosphate reabsorption via NaPi-IIa downregulation.

answers.name: Respiratory alkalosis
answers.pearl: Alkalemia stimulates glycolysis and intracellular phosphate trapping, and is a frequent contributor in sepsis and hyperventilation.

answers.name: Insulin and glucose infusion
answers.pearl: Glucose-insulin therapy and dextrose loads shift phosphate into cells.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Phosphate-poor TPN or sudden carbohydrate load causes intracellular uptake and low serum levels.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Cytokines, respiratory alkalosis and cellular shifts produce hypophosphatemia in critical illness.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition in the proximal tubule causes phosphaturia along with bicarbonaturia.

answers.name: Nutritional rickets
answers.pearl: Vitamin D deficiency in children causes secondary hyperparathyroidism and phosphaturia, with impaired mineralization.

answers.name: Continuous renal replacement therapy
answers.pearl: Prolonged CRRT removes phosphate efficiently, especially without phosphate in the replacement fluid.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction wastes phosphate, glucose, amino acids, bicarbonate and urate.

answers.name: Hungry bone syndrome
answers.pearl: After parathyroidectomy, bone remineralization consumes phosphate, calcium and magnesium.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Withdrawal causes hyperventilation, increased catecholamines and glucose use, which push phosphate into cells.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Major burns cause urinary losses, respiratory alkalosis and fluid shifts, with a typical nadir after the first few days.

answers.name: Kidney transplantation
answers.pearl: Early post-transplant phosphaturia from persistently high FGF23 and PTH lowers phosphate in many recipients.

answers.name: Intravenous iron
answers.pearl: Ferric carboxymaltose raises intact FGF23, causing phosphaturia and sometimes symptomatic osteomalacia.

answers.name: Acute leukemia
answers.pearl: Rapidly proliferating blasts consume phosphate, causing a low serum level before chemotherapy.

answers.name: Acute asthma treated with beta agonists
answers.pearl: Beta-agonists and alkalosis shift phosphate into cells.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate causes proximal tubular injury with phosphate wasting and Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Volume expansion
answers.pearl: Saline loading reduces proximal sodium and phosphate reabsorption.

answers.name: Glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: Steroids can increase renal phosphate excretion and reduce intestinal absorption.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Light chain deposition injures the proximal tubule and can cause acquired Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors can lower phosphate through effects on bone turnover and renal handling.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide causes proximal tubular toxicity, with phosphaturia and Fanconi syndrome in children and adults.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Hyperventilation, rhabdomyolysis recovery and cellular uptake can drive phosphate low.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Respiratory alkalosis and metabolic effects can lower phosphate in acute poisoning.

answers.name: Heavy metal toxicity
answers.pearl: Lead, cadmium and mercury injure the proximal tubule and cause Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Partial hepatectomy
answers.pearl: Liver regeneration is energy-intensive and consumes large amounts of phosphate postoperatively.

answers.name: Theophylline toxicity
answers.pearl: Methylxanthines stimulate catecholamines and lower serum phosphate through cellular shifts.

answers.name: Cystinosis
answers.pearl: Lysosomal cystine accumulation causes proximal tubulopathy with phosphate wasting and rickets in children.

answers.name: Dent disease
answers.pearl: CLCN5 mutations cause low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria and variable phosphate wasting.

answers.name: Lowe syndrome
answers.pearl: OCRL mutations cause congenital cataracts, intellectual disability and Fanconi syndrome in boys.

answers.name: GM-CSF therapy
answers.pearl: Marrow recovery with growth factors increases cellular phosphate utilization.

answers.name: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: SLC34A3 mutation causes phosphate wasting with elevated 1,25-vitamin D, hypercalciuria and rickets.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
answers.pearl: FGF23 mutations prevent its degradation, causing phosphate wasting with variable penetrance.

answers.name: Autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets
answers.pearl: DMP1 or ENPP1 loss-of-function increases FGF23 and causes rickets with phosphate wasting.

answers.name: Epidermal nevus syndrome
answers.pearl: Linear sebaceous nevi can produce FGF23 and cause hypophosphatemic rickets or osteomalacia.

answers.name: X-linked hypophosphatemia
answers.pearl: PHEX mutations raise FGF23, causing rickets, short stature and phosphate wasting, treated with burosumab.

answers.name: McCune-Albright syndrome
answers.pearl: GNAS mutation produces fibrous dysplasia with FGF23 excess and hypophosphatemia in some patients.

answers.name: Tumor-induced osteomalacia
answers.pearl: Small mesenchymal tumors secrete FGF23, causing phosphate wasting and osteomalacia that resolves with resection.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of respiratory alkalosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Opioid withdrawal and anemia (modest or inconsistent hyperventilation); Doxapram (stimulant, rarely used); Heat stroke (hyperventilation documented but variable); Cheyne-Stokes respiration (episodic, may have normal average PaCO2); Hepatopulmonary syndrome (hypoxic drive). Board Prep Traps: urea cycle disorders, Joubert syndrome, Rett syndrome.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Panic attacks and hyperventilation syndrome reduce PaCO2, with perioral paresthesias and carpopedal spasm from lower ionized calcium.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and pulmonary receptor stimulation increase ventilation, giving a low PaCO2 despite impaired gas exchange.

answers.name: Pain
answers.pearl: Pain stimulates respiratory drive and causes a reflex increase in ventilation.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and lung receptor stimulation increase ventilation, and an early respiratory alkalosis is typical before fatigue.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Progesterone raises respiratory drive, producing a compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO2 around 30 mmHg.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Early sepsis causes hyperventilation from cytokines and hypoxemia, and the alkalosis may precede lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Salicylates directly stimulate the medullary respiratory center, producing alkalosis early, then anion gap metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: High altitude
answers.pearl: Hypoxic stimulation of peripheral chemoreceptors increases ventilation, with renal bicarbonate excretion for compensation.

answers.name: Asthma exacerbation
answers.pearl: Early acute asthma causes hyperventilation, and normal or rising PaCO2 signals impending failure.

answers.name: Excessive mechanical ventilation
answers.pearl: Excess minute ventilation on a ventilator lowers PaCO2 and can cause cerebral vasoconstriction.

answers.name: Hypoxemia
answers.pearl: Any cause of low PaO2 stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors and increases ventilation.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever raises metabolic rate and stimulates respiration through hypothalamic effects.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Pulmonary congestion stimulates J receptors and causes hyperventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Liver failure increases respiratory drive through progesterone, ammonia and hypoxemia, producing chronic respiratory alkalosis.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Fibrosis stimulates ventilation through lung receptors and hypoxemia, with a low PaCO2 until late disease.

answers.name: Pneumothorax
answers.pearl: Pain and hypoxemia increase ventilation, giving respiratory alkalosis in the acute setting.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Autonomic hyperactivity and agitation drive hyperventilation in withdrawal and delirium tremens.

answers.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Brainstem and chemoreceptor effects can cause hyperventilation with a low PaCO2.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Lesions of the brainstem or cortex can produce central neurogenic hyperventilation.

answers.name: Meningitis
answers.pearl: CNS infection or inflammation can stimulate central chemoreceptors and respiratory centers.

answers.name: Traumatic brain injury
answers.pearl: Brainstem dysfunction and elevated ICP can cause central neurogenic hyperventilation.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and increased pulmonary vascular stretch receptors stimulate ventilation.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Increased metabolic rate and oxygen consumption raise ventilatory drive.

answers.name: Beta agonist therapy
answers.pearl: Albuterol and other beta agonists can stimulate respiration and induce anxiety or tremor.

answers.name: Theophylline toxicity
answers.pearl: Methylxanthines are respiratory stimulants and cause hyperventilation in overdose.

answers.name: Opioid withdrawal
