answers.name: Drug reaction
answers.pearl: A morbilliform drug eruption with fever generally appears 1 to 2 weeks after starting a new agent such as a beta-lactam, sulfonamide, or anticonvulsant.

answers.name: Varicella
answers.pearl: Primary chickenpox in adults presents with vesicles in crops at different stages and is more severe, with risk of pneumonia.

answers.name: Cellulitis
answers.pearl: Cellulitis causes a warm, spreading erythematous plaque with fever, most often from streptococci or S. aureus.

answers.name: Infectious mononucleosis
answers.pearl: EBV mononucleosis causes fever, pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy, and a rash is triggered in most patients given ampicillin or amoxicillin.

answers.name: Secondary syphilis
answers.pearl: A diffuse non-pruritic macular or papular rash involving the palms and soles, with fever, lymphadenopathy and condylomata lata.

answers.name: Acute HIV infection
answers.pearl: Acute retroviral syndrome produces fever, pharyngitis, mucocutaneous ulcers, and a truncal maculopapular rash 2 to 4 weeks after exposure.

answers.name: Meningococcemia
answers.pearl: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis produces fever with petechiae and purpura that can progress to purpura fulminans within hours.

answers.name: Scarlet fever
answers.pearl: Group A Streptococcus exotoxin causes a sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue and Pastia lines after pharyngitis.

answers.name: Measles
answers.pearl: Fever followed by cough, coryza and conjunctivitis, then a cephalocaudal maculopapular rash, with Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa.

answers.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
answers.pearl: Mucocutaneous blistering and epidermal detachment below 10 percent of body surface area, often triggered by drugs such as allopurinol, lamotrigine, or sulfonamides.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus flares may feature fever with a malar, photosensitive, or discoid rash together with arthritis and cytopenias.

answers.name: Toxic shock syndrome
answers.pearl: Superantigen-mediated illness with fever, hypotension, a diffuse erythroderma and later desquamation of the palms and soles.

answers.name: Lyme disease
answers.pearl: Erythema migrans appears days to weeks after an Ixodes tick bite as an expanding annular patch, often with fever and fatigue.

answers.name: Dengue fever
answers.pearl: Travelers from the tropics develop fever, retro-orbital pain and myalgias, with a flushing or maculopapular rash, thrombocytopenia and a positive tourniquet test.

answers.name: Parvovirus B19 infection
answers.pearl: In adults, slapped cheek is uncommon; instead, fever, a lacy reticular rash, and symmetrical polyarthritis predominate.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, splinter hemorrhages and petechiae accompany fever, and result from emboli and immune complexes.

answers.name: Disseminated gonococcal infection
answers.pearl: Fever, migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis and sparse pustular or hemorrhagic acral lesions in a sexually active adult.

answers.name: Rubella
answers.pearl: German measles in adults gives low-grade fever, a fine maculopapular rash, postauricular lymphadenopathy and arthralgias.

answers.name: Erythema multiforme
answers.pearl: Target lesions with fever, most often following herpes simplex or Mycoplasma infection.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Quotidian spiking fevers with a transient salmon-colored evanescent rash, arthritis, and very high ferritin.

answers.name: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura with fever following infection or drug exposure, confirmed by biopsy showing neutrophilic small-vessel inflammation.

answers.name: DRESS syndrome
aliases: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
answers.pearl: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms emerges 2 to 8 weeks after drug start, with facial edema, eosinophilia, hepatitis and HHV-6 reactivation.

answers.name: IgA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Adults with Henoch-Schonlein purpura have palpable purpura on the legs, abdominal pain, arthritis, and nephritis.

answers.name: Hand, foot and mouth disease
answers.pearl: Coxsackievirus A16 and enterovirus 71 cause oral ulcers and palm and sole vesicles, and can occur in adults.

answers.name: Mpox
answers.pearl: Monkeypox virus causes fever and lymphadenopathy followed by a vesiculopustular rash that is often genital or perianal in the recent outbreak.

answers.name: Necrotizing fasciitis
answers.pearl: Pain out of proportion with fever and skin changes progressing to bullae and dusky necrosis requires urgent surgical debridement.

answers.name: Serum sickness
answers.pearl: Fever, urticarial rash and arthralgias occur 1 to 2 weeks after a drug or antitoxin, with complement consumption.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum
answers.pearl: Tender pretibial nodules with fever suggest an underlying cause such as streptococcal infection, sarcoidosis, TB, IBD, or pregnancy.

answers.name: Chikungunya
answers.pearl: Abrupt high fever with severe polyarthralgia and a maculopapular rash after travel to endemic regions.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus infection
answers.pearl: CMV mononucleosis in adults gives prolonged fever, atypical lymphocytosis and occasionally a rash, again especially after ampicillin.

answers.name: Sweet syndrome
answers.pearl: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis with tender red plaques, neutrophilia, and associations with leukemia, infection and drugs such as G-CSF.

answers.name: Ehrlichiosis
answers.pearl: Human monocytic ehrlichiosis from Amblyomma tick bites causes fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and transaminitis, with a rash in a minority of adults.

answers.name: Zika virus infection
answers.pearl: Zika causes mild fever, conjunctivitis, arthralgia and a pruritic maculopapular rash after travel to endemic areas.

answers.name: Dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Heliotrope rash and Gottron papules may accompany fever and proximal muscle weakness, and raise the question of underlying malignancy.

answers.name: Reactive arthritis
answers.pearl: Fever, arthritis, urethritis and conjunctivitis after enteric or chlamydial infection with keratoderma blennorrhagicum.

answers.name: Polyarteritis nodosa
answers.pearl: Fever with livedo reticularis, painful subcutaneous nodules, mononeuritis multiplex and hypertension, sometimes triggered by hepatitis B.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Fever, conjunctival suffusion and myalgias after freshwater exposure, with a rash in some patients and hepatorenal involvement in Weil disease.

answers.name: Murine typhus
answers.pearl: Rickettsia typhi from fleas and rats causes fever, headache and a truncal macular rash, common in Texas, California and Hawaii.

answers.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Fever with palpable purpura, skin nodules, sinusitis, pulmonary nodules and glomerulonephritis in a PR3-ANCA positive adult.

answers.name: Cat scratch disease
answers.pearl: Bartonella henselae causes fever, regional lymphadenopathy and sometimes a papule or erythema nodosum after a kitten scratch.

answers.name: Cutaneous coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Early primary coccidioidal infection can cause a fever with erythema nodosum or erythema multiforme rash, and disseminated disease produces verrucous lesions.

answers.name: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
answers.pearl: Rapid onset of fever and diffuse sterile non-follicular pustules on erythema within days of a drug such as an aminopenicillin.

answers.name: Scrub typhus
answers.pearl: Orientia tsutsugamushi causes fever, an eschar and a rash after chigger exposure in Asia-Pacific.

answers.name: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
answers.pearl: Exfoliative toxin splits the superficial epidermis, causing fever, tender erythroderma and a positive Nikolsky sign, rarely in adults with kidney failure or immunosuppression.

answers.name: Ecthyma gangrenosum
answers.pearl: Painless necrotic ulcers with an eschar and surrounding erythema in neutropenic patients with Pseudomonas bacteremia.

answers.name: Disseminated histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Immunosuppressed patients may show fever, pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, oral ulcers, and papulonodular skin lesions.

answers.name: Mediterranean spotted fever
answers.pearl: Rickettsia conorii causes fever, a tache noire eschar and a maculopapular rash including the palms and soles after contact with dog ticks.

answers.name: Tularemia
answers.pearl: Francisella tularensis from rabbits or ticks gives fever with an ulceroglandular lesion and sometimes a generalized rash or erythema nodosum.

answers.name: Bacillary angiomatosis
answers.pearl: Bartonella infection in advanced HIV produces violaceous vascular papules resembling Kaposi sarcoma, with fever and visceral involvement.

answers.name: Vibrio vulnificus infection
answers.pearl: Hemorrhagic bullae and septic shock after raw oyster ingestion or seawater wound exposure, especially in cirrhosis or iron overload.

answers.name: Rickettsialpox
answers.pearl: Rickettsia akari from mite bites yields an eschar, fever and a vesicular rash resembling chickenpox in urban settings.

answers.name: Urticarial vasculitis
answers.pearl: Painful, burning urticaria lasting over 24 hours and leaving bruising, with hypocomplementemia and systemic symptoms including fever.

answers.name: Rat-bite fever
answers.pearl: Streptobacillus moniliformis causes abrupt fever, rash on the extremities including palms and soles, and migratory polyarthritis after rodent contact.

answers.name: African tick bite fever
answers.pearl: Rickettsia africae from sub-Saharan Africa leads to fever with multiple eschars and a vesicular rash in safari travelers.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura, arthralgia, fever and glomerulonephritis with low C4 and hepatitis C infection.

answers.name: Trichinellosis
answers.pearl: Eating undercooked pork or bear meat causes fever, periorbital edema, myalgias, eosinophilia and subungual splinter hemorrhages.

answers.name: Kikuchi disease
answers.pearl: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis causes fever, tender cervical nodes and sometimes a rash, mainly in young Asian women.

answers.name: Familial Mediterranean fever
answers.pearl: Recurrent episodes of fever with serositis and an erysipelas-like erythema on the lower leg, usually in people of Mediterranean ancestry.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum leprosum
answers.pearl: A type 2 lepra reaction in treated lepromatous leprosy brings fever, painful nodules, neuritis and uveitis.

answers.name: Anthrax
answers.pearl: Cutaneous anthrax presents with a painless black eschar with surrounding edema, and systemic anthrax follows spore exposure.

answers.name: Chronic meningococcemia
answers.pearl: Weeks of intermittent fever, rash, and arthralgias from low-grade Neisseria meningitidis bacteremia, often with complement deficiency.

answers.name: Viral hemorrhagic fever
answers.pearl: Ebola, Lassa, Marburg, and Crimean-Congo fevers cause fever with petechial or maculopapular rash and bleeding after endemic exposure.

answers.name: Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis
answers.pearl: Dog bite or lick in an asplenic or alcoholic patient leads to fulminant sepsis with purpura and DIC.

answers.name: Atypical measles
answers.pearl: Vaccinated adults with the old inactivated measles vaccine exposed to the wild virus develop high fever, pneumonia and a petechial rash that begins on the extremities.

answers.name: Disseminated strongyloidiasis
answers.pearl: In hyperinfection syndrome, filariform larvae in the dermis produce periumbilical purpura with fever and gram-negative sepsis in patients on corticosteroids.

answers.name: Intravascular lymphoma
answers.pearl: Fever of unknown origin with violaceous skin lesions or panniculitis-like plaques and elevated LDH, with diagnosis by random skin biopsy.

answers.name: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Fever, generalized lymphadenopathy, rash that is frequently drug-like, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia and Coombs-positive hemolysis.

answers.name: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome
answers.pearl: NLRP3-driven autoinflammation causing recurrent fever with cold-triggered urticarial rash, arthralgia and conjunctivitis.

answers.name: Schnitzler syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic nonpruritic urticarial rash with recurrent fever, bone pain, and a monoclonal IgM gammopathy that responds to IL-1 blockade.

answers.name: Smallpox
answers.pearl: Eradicated in 1980; it produces uniform deep-seated pustules in the same stage after a febrile prodrome, and is a bioterrorism concern.

answers.name: Rocky Mountain spotted fever
answers.pearl: Rickettsia rickettsii from Dermacentor ticks causes fever, headache, and a centripetal petechial rash starting on the wrists and ankles; doxycycline should not be delayed.

answers.name: Kawasaki disease
answers.pearl: Adult cases of fever of at least 5 days with conjunctivitis, oral changes, rash, extremity changes and lymphadenopathy are rare and carry a risk of coronary aneurysm.

answers.name: Typhoid fever
answers.pearl: Salmonella Typhi from endemic areas causes sustained fever, relative bradycardia, and faint salmon-colored rose spots on the trunk.

answers.name: Acute rheumatic fever
answers.pearl: After group A streptococcal pharyngitis, fever with migratory arthritis, carditis, and erythema marginatum is diagnosed by Jones criteria.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of a pericardial effusion.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Toxoplasma, Echinococcus (hydatid) and Q fever pericardial effusion (case-report level), Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (rare, ascites/pleural effusion with occasional pericardial effusion), Methysergide, phenytoin, cyclosporine and interferon-alpha (isolated reports), Anorexia nervosa (usually small, asymptomatic), Pregnancy (small physiologic), Lyme and Chagas pericarditis (uncommon), Cardiac transplant rejection, Primary cardiac angiosarcoma. Dressler syndrome, familial Mediterranean fever and acute rheumatic fever scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Idiopathic pericarditis
answers.pearl: Most acute pericarditis with effusion has no identified cause and is presumed viral, treated with NSAIDs and colchicine.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Metastatic involvement of the pericardium, most often from lung, breast, lymphoma or leukemia, is the leading cause of large effusions and tamponade in many series.

answers.name: Uremia
answers.pearl: Uremic pericarditis occurs with untreated advanced kidney failure and typically improves with dialysis.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Elevated systemic venous pressure and fluid overload produce transudative effusions that are usually small.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Myxedema causes slowly accumulating effusions rich in cholesterol that rarely lead to tamponade.

answers.name: Post-myocardial infarction pericarditis
answers.pearl: Early pericarditis within days of a transmural MI is caused by direct inflammation over the infarcted wall.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: TB is the leading cause of effusion in endemic regions and in HIV, with exudative bloody fluid and a high risk of constriction.

answers.name: Cardiac surgery
answers.pearl: Postoperative effusions are frequent after cardiac surgery and can cause late localized tamponade, particularly in patients on anticoagulants.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Serositis is a classic lupus criterion and pericardial effusions occur frequently during flares.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis can produce effusions with very low glucose and high rheumatoid factor in the fluid.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Type A dissection with retrograde rupture into the pericardial sac causes hemopericardium and sudden tamponade.

answers.name: Iatrogenic cardiac perforation
answers.pearl: Catheter ablation, pacemaker lead insertion, percutaneous coronary intervention and valve procedures can perforate the heart and cause acute hemopericardium.

answers.name: Trauma
answers.pearl: Blunt or penetrating chest trauma produces hemopericardium from myocardial or great vessel injury and is a cause of Beck triad.

answers.name: Bacterial pericarditis
answers.pearl: Purulent pericarditis from Staphylococcus, Streptococcus or gram-negative organisms is a surgical emergency needing drainage.

answers.name: Dialysis-related pericarditis
answers.pearl: Effusion that develops in patients already on adequate hemodialysis is thought to relate to inadequate dialysis, heparin use, or fluid overload.

answers.name: Radiation therapy
answers.pearl: Chest irradiation for lymphoma or breast and lung cancer can cause acute or delayed effusions years later, followed by constriction.

answers.name: Ventricular free wall rupture
answers.pearl: Rupture of the infarcted free wall a few days after MI causes hemopericardium and near-immediate tamponade or electromechanical dissociation.

answers.name: Anticoagulation
answers.pearl: Therapeutic anticoagulation, thrombolysis, and antiplatelet use make bleeding into the pericardium more likely after pericarditis or trauma.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Hypoalbuminemia and fluid retention in cirrhosis can cause small transudative effusions along with ascites and pleural effusions.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Severe hypoalbuminemia lowers oncotic pressure and results in polyserositis with pericardial and pleural effusions.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Right atrial hypertension and impaired lymphatic drainage cause effusions in pulmonary arterial hypertension, and their presence signals a poor prognosis.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Mediastinal or pericardial involvement in Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma produces malignant effusions, sometimes from obstructed lymphatic drainage.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Direct invasion or lymphatic spread from bronchogenic carcinoma accounts for the largest fraction of malignant pericardial effusions.

answers.name: Breast cancer
answers.pearl: Metastatic breast carcinoma can reach the pericardium years after primary treatment, and the effusion can recur after drainage.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Pericardial infiltration in acute leukemia can cause effusion, and chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity adds to risk.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: In HIV, effusions arise from TB, lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma, bacterial or fungal infection, or HIV itself, and indicate advanced disease.

answers.name: Systemic sclerosis
answers.pearl: Pericardial effusions are common in scleroderma, often asymptomatic, and are associated with pulmonary hypertension and worse prognosis.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Pericardial involvement is uncommon in sarcoidosis, but granulomatous pericarditis can produce effusion.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Serositis with pericarditis and effusion occurs in a considerable number of patients with Still disease flares.

answers.name: Drug-induced lupus
answers.pearl: Procainamide, hydralazine, and isoniazid can produce a lupus-like syndrome with pericarditis and effusion.

answers.name: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity
answers.pearl: Anthracyclines can cause myopericarditis with effusion in addition to dose-dependent cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitor therapy for lung cancer and melanoma can cause immune-related pericarditis with effusion and tamponade.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: In endemic areas, histoplasma pericarditis follows mediastinal lymph node involvement and is an immune-mediated inflammatory process.

answers.name: Mesothelioma
answers.pearl: Primary pericardial mesothelioma and pleural mesothelioma extending to the pericardium produce large bloody effusions with a poor prognosis.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Small asymptomatic pericardial effusions occur in a sizable fraction of normal third-trimester pregnancies.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Cardiac amyloid may cause small effusions together with low voltage on ECG and thickened walls on echocardiography.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: High-dose cyclophosphamide for transplant conditioning can cause hemorrhagic myopericarditis and effusion.

answers.name: Minoxidil
answers.pearl: Minoxidil causes sodium and water retention and pericardial effusion in up to a third of patients, occasionally with tamponade.

answers.name: Dasatinib
answers.pearl: Dasatinib causes pleural effusion in many patients, and pericardial effusion occurs as well, via fluid retention and immune mechanisms.

answers.name: Anorexia nervosa
answers.pearl: Severe malnutrition produces gelatinous, usually small, asymptomatic pericardial effusions that resolve with refeeding.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Sjogren-related serositis is uncommon, but pericardial effusion can occur, especially with overlapping lupus features.

answers.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis and pericardial effusion are among the less typical cardiac manifestations of ANCA vasculitis.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: IgG4-related pericarditis is a rare manifestation and the effusion responds to glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis and effusions are infrequent in inflammatory myopathies but may be seen in antisynthetase and overlap syndromes.

answers.name: Mixed connective tissue disease
answers.pearl: Pericarditis occurs in a substantial minority of patients with anti-U1 RNP antibodies and overlap features.

answers.name: Coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Coccidioides can spread to the pericardium with exudative effusions and later constrictive pericarditis in endemic areas.

answers.name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
answers.pearl: Pericarditis with effusion can complicate Mycoplasma infection as part of extrapulmonary immune-mediated disease.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Untreated Addison disease can cause pericardial effusion that resolves with glucocorticoid replacement.

answers.name: Chylopericardium
answers.pearl: Thoracic duct injury, mediastinal tumors, or lymphatic anomalies cause milky effusions rich in triglycerides.

answers.name: Pericardial angiosarcoma
answers.pearl: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma usually arises in the right atrium and presents with hemorrhagic effusion and tamponade.

answers.name: Candida pericarditis
answers.pearl: Fungal pericarditis occurs after cardiac surgery or in immunocompromised and critically ill patients.

answers.name: Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Pericarditis and effusion are described in Behcet disease, which also has cardiac thrombi and aneurysms.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Isolated reports link amiodarone to pericardial effusion, usually via hypothyroidism rather than a direct effect.

answers.name: Lyme carditis
answers.pearl: Borrelia burgdorferi usually causes AV block, but pericarditis with effusion has been described.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity pericarditis and effusion with lupus-like features has been reported.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon-alpha can cause pericarditis and effusion as part of autoimmune side effects.

answers.name: Methysergide
answers.pearl: This old migraine drug causes fibrotic serosal disease, including pericardial effusion and retroperitoneal fibrosis.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine has been linked to pericardial effusion in transplant recipients.

answers.name: Chagas disease
answers.pearl: Acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection can cause myopericarditis with effusion, and tamponade has been reported in immunocompromised hosts.

answers.name: Q fever
answers.pearl: Coxiella burnetii can cause myopericarditis with effusion, a recognized but unusual cardiac syndrome.

answers.name: Toxoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Toxoplasma pericarditis and myopericarditis have been described in immunocompromised hosts.

answers.name: Cardiac transplant rejection
answers.pearl: Acute rejection can produce a new pericardial effusion in heart transplant recipients.

answers.name: Hydatid cyst
answers.pearl: Echinococcus cyst rupture into the pericardium can cause tamponade or anaphylaxis.

answers.name: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
answers.pearl: Fertility drugs cause increased capillary permeability and third spacing, and in severe cases pericardial effusion.

answers.name: Dressler syndrome
answers.pearl: Delayed pericarditis weeks after MI, cardiac surgery or injury, probably autoimmune, with fever and pleuritic pain.

answers.name: Familial Mediterranean fever
answers.pearl: Recurrent short febrile attacks with serositis, including pericarditis, due to MEFV mutations and treated with colchicine.

answers.name: Acute rheumatic fever
answers.pearl: Pancarditis after group A streptococcal pharyngitis can include pericarditis with effusion, together with Jones major criteria.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs or conditions that increase digoxin levels or the risk of digoxin toxicity.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hawthorn, Siberian ginseng and licorice (herbal/assay-level evidence), Digoxin-like immunoreactive substances (assay artifact rather than true toxicity), Doxycycline, Alprazolam and Telmisartan (small or inconsistent changes in levels), Ritonavir, Posaconazole, Telaprevir and Rolapitant (P-gp inhibition, limited clinical data), Cardiac amyloidosis (binding by fibrils; reported clinical sensitivity), Oleander, foxglove, lily of the valley and toad venom (cardiac glycoside poisoning rather than a drug interaction). Quinidine, Spironolactone and Hypercalcemia scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Renal failure
answers.pearl: Digoxin is cleared renally, so reduced GFR or acute kidney injury is the most common reason for rising levels and toxicity.

answers.name: Hypokalemia
answers.pearl: Low potassium increases digoxin binding to the Na-K ATPase and amplifies toxicity at any given serum level.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal clearance, roughly doubling the digoxin level, so the dose is cut by about half.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Verapamil raises digoxin levels 50 to 75 percent and adds AV nodal block.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Furosemide and similar agents cause hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, and so predispose to toxicity.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: Low magnesium impairs the Na-K pump and potentiates digoxin-related arrhythmias, and often accompanies hypokalemia.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Hydrochlorothiazide and chlorthalidone cause hypokalemia and volume depletion.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion lowers GFR and digoxin clearance, particularly with gastroenteritis in the elderly.

answers.name: Clarithromycin
answers.pearl: Macrolide inhibition of P-glycoprotein and of gut flora that inactivate digoxin can double the digoxin concentration.

answers.name: Erythromycin
answers.pearl: Erythromycin inhibits P-gp and eradicates Eggerthella lenta in the gut, raising digoxin absorption.

answers.name: Elderly age
answers.pearl: Reduced lean mass, creatinine clearance and volume of distribution make older adults much more susceptible.

answers.name: Diltiazem
answers.pearl: Diltiazem raises digoxin levels modestly and adds additive AV nodal suppression.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Reduced renal clearance and a smaller volume of distribution raise levels, and thyroid replacement later reduces levels.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Dronedarone inhibits P-gp and is associated with a 2.5-fold rise in digoxin concentration.

answers.name: Propafenone
answers.pearl: Propafenone raises digoxin levels by 60 to 80 percent through P-gp inhibition and reduced clearance.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: Lisinopril, enalapril and captopril lower GFR in volume-depleted or renal artery stenosis patients and may modestly increase levels.

answers.name: Hypoxia
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and acidosis increase myocardial sensitivity to digoxin by altering electrolytes and the Na-K pump.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Nonsteroidal agents reduce renal blood flow and creatinine clearance, with ibuprofen and indomethacin raising digoxin levels.

answers.name: Myocardial ischemia
answers.pearl: Acute MI and ischemic myocardium are more irritable and respond to lower digoxin doses with arrhythmias.

answers.name: Itraconazole
answers.pearl: Itraconazole inhibits P-gp and raises digoxin concentration by up to 80 percent.

answers.name: Azithromycin
answers.pearl: Case reports show toxicity with azithromycin, although the effect is smaller than with clarithromycin.

answers.name: Flecainide
answers.pearl: Flecainide can raise digoxin levels by about 15 to 25 percent and both have negative conduction effects.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: High calcium raises myocardial excitability and synergizes with digoxin; IV calcium in a digitalized patient was historically feared.

answers.name: Laxative abuse
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use or diarrhea causes potassium and magnesium loss.

answers.name: Tetracycline
answers.pearl: Tetracycline, by altering gut flora, can increase digoxin absorption.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: High-dose glucocorticoids and amphotericin cause renal potassium wasting.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine reduces renal clearance and inhibits P-gp, increasing digoxin levels in transplant patients.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine reduces digoxin clearance and has an effect similar to quinidine but smaller.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Carvedilol raises digoxin levels through P-gp inhibition, and most beta blockers add AV nodal block.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin causes renal magnesium and potassium wasting and nephrotoxicity.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Omeprazole and others cause hypomagnesemia with long-term use and may slightly increase digoxin bioavailability.

answers.name: Atorvastatin
answers.pearl: Atorvastatin 80 mg was found to modestly increase digoxin exposure via P-gp inhibition.

answers.name: Trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim lowers renal tubular secretion of digoxin and raises levels in some studies.

answers.name: Beta-2 agonists
answers.pearl: Albuterol and similar agents shift potassium into cells, causing transient hypokalemia and increased risk of arrhythmia.

answers.name: Insulin
answers.pearl: Insulin given with dextrose for hyperkalemia moves potassium intracellularly and can unmask digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Ticagrelor
answers.pearl: Ticagrelor inhibits P-gp and increases digoxin concentration by about 30 percent.

answers.name: Doxycycline
answers.pearl: Case reports link doxycycline to digoxin toxicity; its effect on gut flora is thought to be the mechanism.

answers.name: Ranolazine
answers.pearl: Ranolazine inhibits P-gp and increases digoxin levels by roughly 1.5-fold.

answers.name: Mirabegron
answers.pearl: Mirabegron, a P-gp inhibitor, increases digoxin exposure by about 30 percent and requires starting at the lowest dose.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Gentamicin and others cause nephrotoxicity and magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Licorice
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhizin causes mineralocorticoid excess with hypokalemia, markedly increasing digoxin sensitivity.

answers.name: Tolvaptan
answers.pearl: Tolvaptan, a P-gp inhibitor, increases digoxin levels, and its aquaresis may cause volume depletion.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus can reduce renal function and cause hypomagnesemia and hyperkalemia, altering digoxin handling.

answers.name: Hawthorn
answers.pearl: Crataegus is a cardiac herbal remedy with additive inotropy and may interact with digoxin.

answers.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid fibrils bind digoxin strongly, and patients develop toxicity at lower serum levels, so it is typically avoided.

answers.name: Vemurafenib
answers.pearl: Vemurafenib is a P-gp inhibitor and increases digoxin AUC substantially.

answers.name: Posaconazole
answers.pearl: Posaconazole inhibits P-gp, with reports of digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Ritonavir
answers.pearl: Ritonavir inhibits P-gp and its use increases digoxin concentration, with required dose reduction.

answers.name: Alprazolam
answers.pearl: Alprazolam coadministration was reported to raise digoxin levels in older adults.

answers.name: Spironolactone
answers.pearl: Spironolactone lowers renal digoxin clearance, causes assay interference, and its hyperkalemia can mask toxicity.

answers.name: Telmisartan
answers.pearl: Telmisartan increased digoxin peak levels in healthy volunteers, though the clinical effect is small.

answers.name: Lapatinib
answers.pearl: Lapatinib inhibits P-gp and its use can increase digoxin exposure.

answers.name: Telaprevir
answers.pearl: Telaprevir is a P-gp inhibitor that increased digoxin AUC by about 85 percent.

answers.name: Rolapitant
answers.pearl: Rolapitant, an antiemetic, inhibits P-gp and increased digoxin exposure by about 80 percent.

answers.name: Digoxin-like immunoreactive substance
answers.pearl: Endogenous factors present in renal failure, liver disease, neonates and pregnancy, and spironolactone, falsely elevate digoxin immunoassays.

answers.name: Siberian ginseng
answers.pearl: Eleutherococcus extracts have produced falsely high digoxin immunoassay readings without causing true toxicity.

answers.name: Oleander
answers.pearl: Nerium and yellow oleander contain cardiac glycosides that cross-react with digoxin assays and cause a toxidrome identical to digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Foxglove
answers.pearl: Digitalis purpurea leaf or tea ingestion produces typical digoxin poisoning in gardeners and herbal users.

answers.name: Toad venom
answers.pearl: Bufadienolides in Chan Su and Bufo toads are Na-K ATPase inhibitors that cross-react with digoxin assays.

answers.name: Lily of the valley
answers.pearl: Convallaria contains cardenolides like convallatoxin that cause digoxin-like toxicity, sometimes after drinking vase water.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Quinidine reduces digoxin clearance and displaces tissue binding, doubling levels; this is a classic board interaction.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause acute pancreatitis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cannabis, Clonidine-class and methyldopa (case-report level), Lamotrigine, Topiramate, Lithium, Tacrolimus/mycophenolate, Bexarotene and ATRA (mainly via hypertriglyceridemia), Sorafenib/Sunitinib/Checkpoint inhibitors (small series), Ceftriaxone (biliary sludge mechanism), Angiotensin receptor blockers, Dapsone, Nitrofurantoin. GLP-1/DPP-4 association is debated in large trials. Valproic acid, Azathioprine, Didanosine and Sulfasalazine scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Ethanol is the leading drug-related cause of acute pancreatitis, through direct acinar toxicity and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Hydrochlorothiazide and related drugs cause pancreatitis through hypercalcemia and direct toxic effects, with onset typically months after starting.

answers.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
answers.pearl: Exenatide, liraglutide and semaglutide have been linked to pancreatitis in postmarketing reports, although large outcome trials show no clear excess.

answers.name: DPP-4 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sitagliptin and related gliptins carry a pancreatitis warning from postmarketing data.

answers.name: Furosemide
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics have been associated with pancreatitis with positive rechallenge in case reports.

answers.name: Estrogens
answers.pearl: Estrogen therapy and oral contraceptives can cause severe hypertriglyceridemia, particularly with underlying lipid disorders, leading to pancreatitis.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids have been reported to cause pancreatitis, although causality is hard to prove in patients with underlying inflammatory disease.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Simvastatin, atorvastatin and other statins are rarely associated with pancreatitis with a positive dechallenge.

answers.name: Acetaminophen overdose
answers.pearl: Massive acetaminophen overdose with hepatotoxicity can be complicated by acute pancreatitis.

answers.name: 6-Mercaptopurine
answers.pearl: A thiopurine that causes pancreatitis, usually within the first weeks of therapy, and is idiosyncratic rather than dose-related.

answers.name: Propofol
answers.pearl: Propofol infusion causes hypertriglyceridemia, and cases of pancreatitis follow prolonged use.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: 5-ASA compounds cause a drug-induced pancreatitis within weeks of starting, which can mimic IBD flare.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: Enalapril, captopril and lisinopril can cause pancreatitis, in some cases linked to angioedema.

answers.name: L-asparaginase
answers.pearl: Asparaginase and pegaspargase cause pancreatitis in up to 10 percent of patients with ALL, and rechallenge is usually avoided.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Reports describe pancreatitis within days of starting metronidazole, with recurrence on rechallenge.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: TMP-SMX has been reported to cause pancreatitis, particularly in HIV patients.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Morphine and other opioids cause sphincter of Oddi spasm that can precipitate pancreatitis.

answers.name: Erythromycin
answers.pearl: Macrolides, particularly erythromycin, have been reported to cause pancreatitis.

answers.name: Tetracyclines
answers.pearl: Tetracycline, especially in pregnancy and with intravenous use, has been implicated, along with doxycycline.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Tamoxifen can provoke marked hypertriglyceridemia and thereby pancreatitis, especially in women with lipid abnormalities.

answers.name: Protease inhibitors
answers.pearl: Ritonavir and other HIV protease inhibitors cause hypertriglyceridemia and have been tied to pancreatitis.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin-based regimens occasionally cause pancreatitis, possibly through ischemia and electrolyte effects.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid pancreatitis is rare but may recur on rechallenge and is not dose related.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine is directly toxic to pancreatic beta cells, causing pancreatitis and dysglycemia in HIV patients.

answers.name: Stavudine
answers.pearl: Nucleoside analogs such as stavudine and zalcitabine can cause pancreatitis, especially with lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Cytarabine
answers.pearl: High-dose cytarabine is linked to pancreatitis in leukemia regimens.

answers.name: Calcium infusion
answers.pearl: Parenteral calcium and other causes of hypercalcemia can precipitate pancreatitis through intrapancreatic trypsin activation.

answers.name: Tigecycline
answers.pearl: Tigecycline has an FDA label warning for acute pancreatitis, often in patients with other risk factors.

answers.name: Interferon alfa with ribavirin
answers.pearl: Pegylated interferon and ribavirin for hepatitis C have been tied to pancreatitis and hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Second-generation antipsychotics, particularly clozapine, are linked to pancreatitis, partly via metabolic effects.

answers.name: Sulindac
answers.pearl: Sulindac and other NSAIDs can cause pancreatitis, with sulindac the most frequently reported.

answers.name: Salicylates
answers.pearl: Aspirin in toxic doses has been associated with pancreatitis.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: High-dose or chronic methotrexate has been associated with pancreatitis, especially with intrathecal use.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: H2 receptor blockers such as cimetidine and ranitidine are rare causes of pancreatitis, with a positive rechallenge.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Omeprazole and other PPIs are rare causes of pancreatitis, with rechallenge-proven cases reported.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone has been associated with pancreatitis in case reports, usually after intravenous administration.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine hypersensitivity can include pancreatitis, with other anticonvulsants such as phenytoin reported.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibodies can cause immune-related pancreatitis that is often asymptomatic lipase elevation but sometimes severe.

answers.name: Infliximab
answers.pearl: Anti-TNF therapy such as infliximab and adalimumab has been reported to cause pancreatitis, mostly in Crohn disease where confounders exist.

answers.name: Sorafenib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors including sorafenib and sunitinib have been linked to pancreatitis in postmarketing data.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Ifosfamide has been reported to cause pancreatitis, mostly with high-dose regimens.

answers.name: Fenofibrate
answers.pearl: Fibrates are rarely linked to pancreatitis despite treating hypertriglyceridemia, and a paradoxical rise in triglycerides can occur.

answers.name: Niacin
answers.pearl: High-dose nicotinic acid has been associated with pancreatitis, possibly through glucose intolerance and hepatic injury.

answers.name: Octreotide
answers.pearl: Somatostatin analogs cause biliary sludge and gallstones, and pancreatitis follows mainly by gallstone migration.

answers.name: Ceftriaxone
answers.pearl: Ceftriaxone causes reversible biliary pseudolithiasis that can precipitate gallstone pancreatitis, especially in children and with high doses.

answers.name: Losartan
answers.pearl: Angiotensin receptor blockers have been reported rarely to cause pancreatitis.

answers.name: Bexarotene
answers.pearl: Retinoid X receptor agonist that causes severe hypertriglyceridemia and pancreatitis, requiring lipid monitoring.

answers.name: All-trans retinoic acid
answers.pearl: ATRA for acute promyelocytic leukemia has been reported to cause pancreatitis, with hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Cannabis
answers.pearl: Cannabis use is associated with recurrent pancreatitis in some young patients when other causes are excluded.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Case reports describe pancreatitis in children and adults taking lamotrigine, mostly with other anticonvulsants.

answers.name: Topiramate
answers.pearl: Case reports describe topiramate-associated pancreatitis, sometimes with metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Pancreatitis is a rare acute reaction to nitrofurantoin, usually with fever and rash.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome can include pancreatitis.

answers.name: Mycophenolate
answers.pearl: Mycophenolate mofetil used in transplant recipients has been associated with pancreatitis.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors have been implicated in post-transplant pancreatitis, though confounders are many.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Long-term lithium has been associated with pancreatitis, in part via hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: A rare idiosyncratic reaction to methyldopa, with positive rechallenge in reports.

answers.name: Clonidine
answers.pearl: Case reports link clonidine to pancreatitis, possibly via sphincter of Oddi effects.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Isolated case reports of pancreatitis with mirtazapine exist.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate-induced pancreatitis can occur at any time and is more common in children; it can be fatal and is a classic board association.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Idiosyncratic pancreatitis, often within the first month, which recurs quickly on rechallenge and is a classic IBD-patient complication.

answers.name: Didanosine
answers.pearl: The classic nucleoside analog culprit for pancreatitis, particularly with stavudine or hydroxyurea, and also causes lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfa component of sulfasalazine can cause pancreatitis, typically soon after starting for ulcerative colitis or RA.

prompts.prompt: Name organ manifestations or presentations of IgG4-related disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: IgG4-related GI tract involvement and IgG4-related mastopathy (debated or small series), paratesticular pseudotumor and coronary periarteritis (case series), circulating plasmablast expansion (biomarker rather than manifestation), elevated ESR with normal CRP (non-specific lab pattern), allergic features overlapping with eosinophilia and IgE, and splenic vein stenosis scored by clinical rarity.

answers.name: Autoimmune pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis is the pancreatic manifestation of IgG4-RD and presents with painless jaundice and a diffusely enlarged pancreas.

answers.name: Salivary gland enlargement
answers.pearl: Painless bilateral swelling of the submandibular, parotid or sublingual glands is a very common IgG4-RD sign.

answers.name: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
answers.pearl: Idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis is IgG4-related in roughly half of cases and can entrap ureters and the aorta.

answers.name: Lacrimal gland enlargement
answers.pearl: Bilateral painless lacrimal gland swelling (IgG4-related dacryoadenitis) is a classic orbital presentation.

answers.name: Elevated serum IgG4
answers.pearl: Serum IgG4 above 135 mg/dL supports the diagnosis but is neither sensitive nor specific, and is normal in up to 30 percent of cases.

answers.name: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: Biliary strictures mimicking primary sclerosing cholangitis or cholangiocarcinoma that respond to steroids and often accompany autoimmune pancreatitis.

answers.name: Lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Hilar, mediastinal and cervical lymph node enlargement is common and can be the only finding, creating a lymphoma mimic.

answers.name: Obstructive jaundice
answers.pearl: Jaundice from a pancreatic head mass or distal biliary stricture often leads to a presumed pancreatic cancer work-up.

answers.name: Pancreatic mass mimicking pancreatic cancer
answers.pearl: Focal mass-forming autoimmune pancreatitis is resected as presumed adenocarcinoma in a meaningful minority of patients.

answers.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: IgG4-related TIN is the most common renal lesion and presents with progressive CKD and bland urine.

answers.name: Orbital pseudotumor
answers.pearl: Orbital soft-tissue inflammation causing proptosis and diplopia that may be mistaken for thyroid eye disease or lymphoma.

answers.name: Peripheral eosinophilia
answers.pearl: Eosinophilia and atopic features occur in a large share of patients, which can lead to misdiagnosis as an allergic or eosinophilic disorder.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury or CKD of unclear cause
answers.pearl: Renal insufficiency with minimal proteinuria in a patient with other IgG4 findings should prompt a renal biopsy.

answers.name: Elevated total IgE
answers.pearl: Serum IgE is raised in many IgG4-RD patients, reflecting a Th2-skewed immune response.

answers.name: Aortitis or inflammatory aortic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Periaortitis and periarteritis can lead to aneurysm, dissection or rupture and may be found incidentally on CT.

answers.name: New-onset diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Pancreatic endocrine dysfunction can precede or accompany autoimmune pancreatitis and sometimes improves with steroids.

answers.name: Sausage-shaped pancreas on imaging
answers.pearl: Diffuse pancreatic enlargement with loss of lobulations and a hypodense peripheral halo is the classic imaging appearance of type 1 AIP.

answers.name: Hypocomplementemia
answers.pearl: Low C3 and C4 are common in IgG4-related kidney disease and reflect immune-complex activity.

answers.name: Sjogren-like sicca symptoms
answers.pearl: Dry eyes and dry mouth from gland involvement, but anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies are typically negative.

answers.name: IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltrate on biopsy
answers.pearl: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with IgG4-positive cells and an IgG4 to IgG ratio above 40 percent is the histologic anchor of the diagnosis.

answers.name: Ureteral obstruction with hydronephrosis
answers.pearl: Periureteral fibrosis from retroperitoneal disease causes obstructive uropathy that needs stenting before steroids work.

answers.name: Hypertrophic pachymeningitis
answers.pearl: Thickening and enhancement of the dura causes headaches and cranial neuropathies and can mimic GPA or sarcoidosis.

answers.name: Pulmonary nodules or masses
answers.pearl: Solid nodules and masses in the lung may mimic malignancy and appear alongside lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Chronic rhinosinusitis
answers.pearl: Sinonasal involvement, with or without nasal polyps, is frequent and overlaps with the atopic features of the disease.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: IgG4-related lung disease can appear as alveolar-interstitial infiltrates, ground-glass opacity or honeycombing.

answers.name: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
answers.pearl: Parenchymal loss causes steatorrhea and weight loss, which can persist even after the inflammation is controlled.

answers.name: Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia
answers.pearl: A raised total IgG and polyclonal gamma band on electrophoresis reflects B-cell activation.

answers.name: Storiform fibrosis
answers.pearl: Cartwheel-pattern fibrosis in the tissue is one of the three core histologic features of IgG4-RD.

answers.name: Membranous glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Membranous nephropathy accompanying tubulointerstitial disease is the commonest glomerular lesion in IgG4-RD.

answers.name: Hashimoto thyroiditis fibrosing variant
answers.pearl: IgG4-related thyroid disease includes a Hashimoto variant with dense fibrosis, higher IgG4 and more rapid hypothyroidism.

answers.name: IgG4-related prostatitis
answers.pearl: Prostate involvement can cause lower urinary tract obstruction and an elevated PSA that mimics prostate cancer.

answers.name: Hypophysitis
answers.pearl: Pituitary and infundibular inflammation can cause hypopituitarism and headaches.

answers.name: Orbital myositis
answers.pearl: Enlargement of the extraocular muscles with tendon sparing can mimic thyroid eye disease.

answers.name: Renal pseudotumor or hypodense renal cortical lesions
answers.pearl: Patchy low-attenuation cortical lesions or a solitary renal mass on contrast CT can mimic renal cell carcinoma or lymphoma.

answers.name: Pleural involvement
answers.pearl: Pleural thickening or effusion is a recognized but uncommon thoracic manifestation.

answers.name: Sclerosing mesenteritis
answers.pearl: Fibroinflammatory mesenteric disease may present as abdominal pain or an incidental mesenteric mass on CT.

answers.name: Obliterative phlebitis
answers.pearl: Lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with venous lumen obliteration is a core histologic finding that may be best seen on elastic stain.

answers.name: Renal pelvic or ureteral wall thickening
answers.pearl: Soft-tissue thickening of the collecting system can cause hydronephrosis and mimic urothelial malignancy.

answers.name: Elevated ESR with normal CRP
answers.pearl: Inflammatory markers are often discordant, with raised ESR from hypergammaglobulinemia but a normal or only mildly raised CRP.

answers.name: Bronchovascular bundle thickening
answers.pearl: Peribronchovascular and septal thickening on chest CT is one of four described radiologic patterns of IgG4-related lung disease.

answers.name: Cutaneous plaques or nodules
answers.pearl: Skin involvement, usually of the head and neck, appears as subcutaneous nodules, papules or plaques and can look like cutaneous pseudolymphoma.

answers.name: Capsule-like rim around the pancreas
answers.pearl: A delayed-enhancing capsule-like rim on CT or MRI is highly specific for autoimmune pancreatitis.

answers.name: Mediastinal fibrosis
answers.pearl: IgG4-related fibrosing mediastinitis may compress the SVC, airways and pulmonary vessels.

answers.name: Diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Posterior pituitary and stalk involvement from hypophysitis can cause central diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor
answers.pearl: Mass-like liver lesions with IgG4-positive plasma cells can mimic hepatocellular carcinoma or cholangiocarcinoma.

answers.name: Cranial nerve involvement
answers.pearl: Infraorbital and trigeminal nerve enlargement or perineural infiltration causes facial numbness or neuralgia.

answers.name: Castleman disease-like lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Some nodes show multicentric Castleman-like histology with prominent plasma cells and IgG4 positivity.

answers.name: Optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Optic nerve compression from orbital disease can cause visual loss, so urgent steroids may be needed.

answers.name: Left-sided portal hypertension from splenic vein stenosis
answers.pearl: Peripancreatic inflammation can compress or thrombose the splenic or portal veins and cause gastric varices.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial thickening or effusion is a reported cardiac manifestation of IgG4-RD.

answers.name: IgG4 hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Some patients have hepatitis-like portal inflammation with dense IgG4 plasma cells that can mimic autoimmune hepatitis.

answers.name: Circulating plasmablast expansion
answers.pearl: Elevated circulating plasmablasts correlate with disease activity and relapse risk and are a sensitive biomarker.

answers.name: IgG4-related cholecystitis
answers.pearl: Gallbladder wall thickening with IgG4-positive plasma cells can accompany sclerosing cholangitis.

answers.name: Intracranial inflammatory pseudotumor
answers.pearl: Dural-based or parenchymal masses can mimic meningioma or lymphoma.

answers.name: Coronary periarteritis
answers.pearl: Soft-tissue cuffing or aneurysm of the coronary arteries can lead to angina or MI and is seen on CT angiography or PET.

answers.name: Thoracic aortic dissection or rupture
answers.pearl: Inflammatory weakening of the aortic wall may produce dissection or rupture, sometimes as the first presentation.

answers.name: Paratesticular or epididymal pseudotumor
answers.pearl: Testicular and epididymal masses with IgG4-positive plasma cells have been reported and can be mistaken for tumor.

answers.name: Paravertebral band-like soft tissue
answers.pearl: Thoracic paravertebral band-like lesions are a recognized radiologic pattern of IgG4-related disease.

answers.name: IgG4-related mastopathy
answers.pearl: Sclerosing mastitis or breast pseudotumor with IgG4-positive plasma cells can mimic breast carcinoma.

answers.name: Spinal pachymeningitis causing myelopathy
answers.pearl: Epidural or spinal dural thickening can compress the cord and cause myelopathy or radiculopathy.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal tract involvement
answers.pearl: Esophageal, gastric, small bowel and colonic involvement with IgG4-positive infiltrates has been described but remains debated.

answers.name: Mikulicz disease
answers.pearl: Symmetric lacrimal, parotid and submandibular enlargement now considered part of IgG4-RD rather than a form of Sjogren syndrome.

answers.name: Riedel thyroiditis
answers.pearl: Stony-hard fibrosing thyroiditis extending beyond the capsule, now recognized as an IgG4-related lesion in many cases.

answers.name: Kuttner tumor
answers.pearl: Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis of the submandibular gland that mimics a neoplasm and is a localized IgG4-related lesion.

prompts.prompt: Name ways systemic amyloidosis can present (organ involvement, symptoms, signs, or test findings), and name amyloid types.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: ordering of apolipoprotein CII/CIII amyloid (very few kindreds), AA amyloid in FMF (a cause rather than a presentation), jaw claudication and amyloid myopathy (small case series), hypothyroidism/goiter and glaucoma aliases (rare), and the hyposplenism, spontaneous splenic rupture and hepatic rupture entries (case-report level). Hereditary variants are listed as types by allele.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Glomerular amyloid deposition causes heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema, often with normal-sized kidneys.

answers.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Biventricular wall thickening with diastolic dysfunction and heart failure with preserved EF is the main cardiac phenotype of AL and ATTR amyloid.

answers.name: AL amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Light-chain amyloid from a plasma cell clone is the most common systemic type and the most urgent to treat.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: A length-dependent painful sensorimotor and small-fiber neuropathy occurs in AL and hereditary ATTR.

answers.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
answers.pearl: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, often years before cardiac disease, is a red flag for ATTR amyloidosis.

answers.name: Hepatomegaly
answers.pearl: Hepatic infiltration enlarges the liver, with little hepatocellular dysfunction until late.

answers.name: Weight loss and fatigue
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms are the most common nonspecific presentation of AL amyloid and delay diagnosis.

answers.name: Orthostatic hypotension
answers.pearl: Autonomic neuropathy or adrenal and cardiac involvement can cause syncope and falls, and a prior hypertensive patient may become normotensive.

answers.name: AA amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Serum amyloid A deposition from chronic inflammation typically presents with renal disease.

answers.name: Easy bruising and purpura
answers.pearl: Vascular fragility and acquired clotting defects cause spontaneous or pinch purpura, particularly on the eyelids and neck.

answers.name: Transthyretin amyloidosis
answers.pearl: ATTR amyloid can be wild-type or hereditary and is now a common cause of heart failure in older adults.

answers.name: Chronic diarrhea
answers.pearl: Gastrointestinal infiltration and autonomic dysfunction cause diarrhea, constipation or malabsorption.

answers.name: Low-voltage ECG with increased wall thickness
answers.pearl: Reduced QRS voltage in the face of LV thickening on echo is a classic mismatch in AL amyloid.

answers.name: Elevated NT-proBNP and troponin
answers.pearl: Persistently elevated NT-proBNP and troponin are used to stage cardiac AL amyloid, even without chest pain.

answers.name: Monoclonal protein on SPEP or immunofixation
answers.pearl: A serum or urine monoclonal protein or abnormal free light chain ratio is found in nearly all AL patients and should prompt a search for amyloid.

answers.name: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Age-related ATTRwt, formerly senile systemic amyloidosis, causes heart failure in men over 60 and is underdiagnosed.

answers.name: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Pathogenic TTR variants cause familial amyloid polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Refractory pleural effusions, sometimes massive, can occur in AL amyloid and are often due to cardiac disease or pleural infiltration.

answers.name: Hepatic cholestasis with markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase
answers.pearl: Disproportionately raised alkaline phosphatase with hepatomegaly suggests infiltrative liver disease.

answers.name: Ascites and right heart failure
answers.pearl: Elevated right-sided pressures from restrictive physiology cause hepatic congestion and ascites.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Atrial arrhythmias are common and carry a high risk of intracardiac thrombus even with therapeutic anticoagulation.

answers.name: Dyspnea on exertion
answers.pearl: Exertional breathlessness is the dominant symptom of cardiac amyloid, often attributed to age or lung disease.

answers.name: Apical-sparing pattern on longitudinal strain
answers.pearl: Relative apical sparing on speckle-tracking strain, producing a cherry-on-top bullseye map, is a sensitive echo clue.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Syncope arises from autonomic failure, conduction disease or arrhythmia and may signal poor prognosis in AL cardiac amyloid.

answers.name: Conduction system disease
answers.pearl: AV block and bundle branch block can require pacemaker implantation, particularly in ATTR.

answers.name: Gastroparesis
answers.pearl: Autonomic involvement or smooth muscle infiltration delays gastric emptying with early satiety, nausea and vomiting.

answers.name: Pseudo-infarct pattern on ECG
answers.pearl: Q waves or poor R-wave progression in the absence of coronary disease reflect infiltration of the myocardium.

answers.name: Lumbar spinal stenosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposition in the ligamentum flavum causes lumbar stenosis years before ATTR cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Roughly 10-15 percent of older adults undergoing TAVR for aortic stenosis have wild-type ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

answers.name: Distal biceps tendon rupture
answers.pearl: Spontaneous biceps tendon rupture in older men is a recognized musculoskeletal precursor of ATTR cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Abdominal fat pad biopsy positive
answers.pearl: Fat pad aspirate is positive in most AL cases but misses many ATTR cases, so it cannot exclude amyloid on its own.

answers.name: Dialysis-related amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Beta-2 microglobulin amyloid in long-term dialysis patients causes carpal tunnel, destructive arthropathy and bone cysts.

answers.name: Cardiac MRI late gadolinium enhancement
answers.pearl: Diffuse subendocardial or transmural late enhancement and abnormal myocardial nulling are characteristic of cardiac amyloid.

answers.name: Technetium pyrophosphate scan uptake
answers.pearl: Grade 2-3 myocardial uptake of 99mTc-PYP or DPD with no monoclonal protein is diagnostic of ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

answers.name: Shoulder arthropathy
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration of synovium and periarticular tissue causes shoulder pain and stiffness, and the shoulder-pad sign if advanced.

answers.name: Acquired factor X deficiency
answers.pearl: Amyloid fibrils adsorb factor X, causing a prolonged PT/aPTT and a bleeding diathesis in AL amyloid.

answers.name: Intracardiac thrombus
answers.pearl: Atrial thrombus can form even in sinus rhythm because of atrial myopathy.

answers.name: Skin plaques and waxy papules
answers.pearl: Waxy, translucent papules and bullous lesions on the face and flexures are cutaneous AL amyloid.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Amyloid replacement of the adrenals can cause hypotension, hyponatremia and hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Val122Ile variant
answers.pearl: The V122I (Val142Ile) allele is carried by 3-4 percent of African Americans and causes late-onset hereditary ATTR cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Val30Met variant
answers.pearl: The Val30Met allele causes early-onset polyneuropathy in endemic foci in Portugal, Sweden and Japan.

answers.name: Hepatic rupture
answers.pearl: Spontaneous liver rupture is a rare, often fatal complication of hepatic amyloid.

answers.name: Hyposplenism
answers.pearl: Splenic infiltration causes functional asplenia with Howell-Jolly bodies and risk of encapsulated organism sepsis.

answers.name: Macroglossia
answers.pearl: Tongue enlargement with dental indentations is nearly pathognomonic for AL amyloid but is present in only a minority of patients.

answers.name: Periorbital purpura
answers.pearl: Raccoon-eye purpura after coughing or Valsalva is a hallmark of AL amyloid vascular fragility.

answers.name: Apple-green birefringence
aliases: apple green birefringence under polarized light
answers.pearl: Apple-green birefringence under polarized light after Congo red staining is the classic tissue diagnosis, though mass spectrometry typing is now required.

answers.name: Spontaneous splenic rupture
answers.pearl: Fragile infiltrated spleen can rupture spontaneously or with minor trauma.

answers.name: Secondary amyloid in familial Mediterranean fever
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation from FMF or other autoinflammatory disease drives AA amyloid and renal failure, which colchicine can prevent.

answers.name: Jaw claudication
answers.pearl: Vascular infiltration by amyloid may cause jaw claudication that mimics giant cell arteritis.

answers.name: Amyloid myopathy
answers.pearl: Muscle infiltration produces proximal weakness or pseudohypertrophy and may mimic inflammatory myopathy.

answers.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Tubular and medullary amyloid deposition can cause polyuria due to vasopressin resistance.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism or amyloid goiter
answers.pearl: Thyroid infiltration produces a firm goiter with hypothyroidism or euthyroid enlargement.

answers.name: Scalloped pupils
answers.pearl: Pupillary margin irregularity from iris amyloid deposition is a classic ocular sign in hereditary ATTR.

answers.name: Vitreous opacities
answers.pearl: Vitreous amyloid in hereditary ATTR causes floaters and visual blurring and often needs vitrectomy.

answers.name: Isolated atrial amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Atrial natriuretic peptide-derived amyloid (AANF) accumulates in atrial tissue with age, particularly in people with atrial fibrillation.

answers.name: Fibrinogen A alpha chain amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Hereditary AFib amyloidosis is a leading cause of hereditary renal amyloid, with hypertension and slowly progressive renal failure.

answers.name: Lysozyme amyloidosis
answers.pearl: ALys presents with sicca, GI involvement and renal disease and occasionally with spontaneous visceral hemorrhage.

answers.name: Apolipoprotein AI amyloidosis
answers.pearl: AApoAI variants cause hepatorenal, cardiac or laryngeal amyloid and sometimes testicular involvement.

answers.name: ALECT2 amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Leukocyte chemotactic factor 2 amyloid is an increasingly recognized renal amyloid, notably in Mexican-American, Punjabi and First Nations populations.

answers.name: Gelsolin amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Finnish-type AGel presents with corneal lattice dystrophy, cranial neuropathies and cutis laxa.

answers.name: Apolipoprotein AII amyloidosis
answers.pearl: AApoAII is a rare hereditary renal amyloid caused by stop-loss variants in APOA2.

answers.name: Apolipoprotein CII or CIII amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Extremely rare hereditary variants cause renal and vascular amyloid; AApoCII and AApoCIII were first described in the 2010s.

answers.name: Immunoglobulin heavy chain amyloidosis
answers.pearl: AH amyloid arises from clonal heavy chains and mimics AL with predominantly renal disease.

answers.name: TTR Thr60Ala variant
answers.pearl: Common in northwestern Ireland and Appalachia, producing mixed neuropathy and cardiac disease.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of Behcet disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: nail and hair changes, esophageal ulceration, glomerulonephritis and chylothorax (small series or case reports), trisomy 8 MDS association (intestinal Behcet, mostly East Asian cohorts), HLA-B51 and elevated acute phase reactants (markers, not manifestations), aortic or arterial pseudoaneurysm rupture, and the exact ranking of pulmonary infarction vs pulmonary vein thrombosis.

answers.name: Recurrent oral aphthous ulcers
answers.pearl: Painful oral ulcers at least three times in a year are the sine qua non of Behcet disease and are present in nearly all patients.

answers.name: Genital ulcers
answers.pearl: Deep, scarring ulcers of the scrotum or labia are highly specific and may heal with scars.

answers.name: Uveitis
answers.pearl: Recurrent anterior, posterior or panuveitis is the most feared ocular complication and is more severe in young men.

answers.name: Skin lesions
answers.pearl: Cutaneous lesions include papulopustular eruptions and erythema nodosum-like nodules in a large majority of patients.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum-like lesions
answers.pearl: Tender red nodules on the shins, histologically a septal or lobular panniculitis, can be the presenting cutaneous sign.

answers.name: Pathergy reaction
answers.pearl: A sterile pustule at a needle-prick site read at 24 to 48 hours is positive in fewer patients in Western countries than along the Silk Road.

answers.name: Papulopustular lesions
answers.pearl: Acneiform or pseudofolliculitis lesions are common and are not specific because they overlap with acne.

answers.name: Arthritis
answers.pearl: Nonerosive oligoarthritis of the knees, ankles, wrists and elbows is the commonest musculoskeletal feature.

answers.name: Deep vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Venous thrombosis is the commonest vascular lesion and is treated with immunosuppression rather than anticoagulation alone.

answers.name: Superficial thrombophlebitis
answers.pearl: Recurrent superficial vein thrombosis, sometimes migratory, occurs without the usual risk factors.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms and fever may accompany flares and make the picture overlap with infection.

answers.name: Retinal vasculitis
answers.pearl: Occlusive retinal vasculitis causes vision loss and is a major cause of blindness in Behcet disease.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal ulceration
answers.pearl: Ileocecal ulcers that can perforate or bleed resemble Crohn disease and are more common in Japan and Turkey.

answers.name: Neuro-Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Parenchymal brainstem lesions and cerebral venous thrombosis are the two main neurologic patterns.

answers.name: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
answers.pearl: Dural sinus thrombosis causes raised intracranial pressure and headache in young patients, mostly men.

answers.name: Brainstem lesions
answers.pearl: Parenchymal involvement favors the brainstem, diencephalon and basal ganglia, with a classic pontine lesion on MRI.

answers.name: Aseptic meningitis
answers.pearl: Neutrophil-predominant CSF pleocytosis with high protein may precede parenchymal disease.

answers.name: Epididymitis
answers.pearl: Recurrent epididymitis or epididymo-orchitis is a male-specific genital manifestation.

answers.name: Hypopyon
answers.pearl: Sterile layering of pus in the anterior chamber is a famous ocular sign, now seen less often with modern therapy.

answers.name: Pulmonary artery aneurysm
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery aneurysm with massive hemoptysis is a leading cause of death in young men and needs immunosuppression, not anticoagulation.

answers.name: Hemoptysis
answers.pearl: Hemoptysis in Behcet disease is a medical emergency until pulmonary artery aneurysm is excluded.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic vein thrombosis is the commonest cause of Budd-Chiari in some Mediterranean and Middle Eastern countries.

answers.name: Inferior vena cava thrombosis
answers.pearl: IVC thrombosis, often with hepatic vein extension, produces leg edema and collateral veins.

answers.name: Arterial aneurysm
answers.pearl: Aneurysms of the femoral, popliteal or other arteries can form and may rupture, particularly after puncture.

answers.name: Arterial occlusion
answers.pearl: Arterial thrombosis and stenosis are less common than venous disease but cause limb ischemia in young patients.

answers.name: Sacroiliitis
answers.pearl: Spondyloarthritis-like axial involvement occurs in a minority and is HLA-B27 negative.

answers.name: Hearing loss
answers.pearl: Sensorineural hearing loss, sometimes with vestibular symptoms, is reported in a minority.

answers.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum-like lesions
answers.pearl: Neutrophilic dermatosis with ulcerating lesions can occur and responds to the same immunosuppression.

answers.name: Myositis
answers.pearl: Focal or generalized myositis and myalgia occur occasionally, with fatigue overlapping with other features.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial involvement can occur with or without effusion and is usually mild.

answers.name: Intracardiac thrombus
answers.pearl: Right heart thrombus mimics a cardiac tumor and may be paired with pulmonary artery aneurysm or venous thrombosis.

answers.name: Optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Optic neuritis or ischemic optic neuropathy is rare and may occur from retinal vasculitis or intracranial hypertension.

answers.name: Elevated acute phase reactants
answers.pearl: ESR and CRP rise with flares but are not diagnostic.

answers.name: HLA-B51 positivity
answers.pearl: HLA-B51 is the strongest genetic association, mostly along the ancient Silk Road, but is neither necessary nor sufficient.

answers.name: Cataract
answers.pearl: Cataracts form from recurrent uveitis and steroid therapy.

answers.name: Secondary glaucoma
answers.pearl: Posterior synechiae and neovascularization from chronic uveitis can raise intraocular pressure.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Mesangial proliferative GN and IgA-like lesions have been described but renal involvement is uncommon.

answers.name: Cardiac valve regurgitation
answers.pearl: Aortic valve regurgitation from aortitis or valve ulceration may need surgery, with a high risk of paravalvular leak.

answers.name: Aortitis or aortic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Aortic aneurysm and pseudoaneurysm in Behcet disease are rare but life-threatening, particularly after surgery.

answers.name: Secondary AA amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation in Behcet disease can lead to AA amyloid, particularly in the Mediterranean region.

answers.name: Esophageal ulceration
answers.pearl: Esophageal aphthae or ulcers may cause dysphagia or odynophagia.

answers.name: Intracranial hypertension
answers.pearl: Raised ICP can come from venous sinus thrombosis and presents with papilledema and headache without a focal lesion.

answers.name: Neuropsychiatric and cognitive changes
answers.pearl: Chronic progressive neuro-Behcet may present with cognitive decline, personality changes and behavioral abnormalities.

answers.name: Cardiac involvement
answers.pearl: Myocarditis, endomyocardial fibrosis and coronary arteritis are rare cardiac manifestations of Behcet disease.

answers.name: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura with small-vessel inflammation can occur and may complicate drug therapy.

answers.name: Splenic or mesenteric infarction
answers.pearl: Thrombosis or arteritis of splenic and mesenteric vessels can cause abdominal pain and infarction.

answers.name: Vitritis
answers.pearl: Vitreous inflammation appears early in posterior segment disease and reflects active intraocular inflammation.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Peripheral nerve involvement is much less common than central involvement but is reported.

answers.name: Cranial neuropathies
answers.pearl: Isolated cranial nerve palsies can accompany brainstem lesions or sinus thrombosis.

answers.name: Spinal cord lesions
answers.pearl: Myelopathy from longitudinally extensive lesions is a rare but disabling pattern.

answers.name: Hughes-Stovin syndrome
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery aneurysms with peripheral venous thrombosis, considered by many a vascular variant of Behcet disease.

answers.name: Pseudoaneurysm at puncture sites
answers.pearl: Arterial puncture or surgical anastomoses can form pseudoaneurysms because of pathergy and vessel wall inflammation.

answers.name: Superior vena cava thrombosis
answers.pearl: Thrombosis of the SVC or brachiocephalic veins can cause facial swelling and chylothorax.

answers.name: Perianal ulcers
answers.pearl: Anorectal ulcers and perianal fistulas can resemble Crohn disease.

answers.name: Trisomy 8 in myelodysplastic syndrome
answers.pearl: Intestinal Behcet disease is associated with MDS that has trisomy 8, especially in East Asia, and may respond to MDS-directed therapy.

answers.name: Pulmonary infarction or pulmonary vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Pulmonary thrombosis in situ, as well as pulmonary infarcts, can occur along with arterial disease.

answers.name: Chylothorax
answers.pearl: Chylothorax can complicate SVC or mediastinal venous thrombosis in Behcet disease.

answers.name: Aortic or arterial pseudoaneurysm rupture
answers.pearl: Spontaneous arterial rupture is a recognized cause of sudden death in vascular Behcet disease.

answers.name: Nail and hair changes
answers.pearl: Rare reports of onycholysis, alopecia and nail fold lesions in Behcet disease.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyperammonemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: multiple myeloma and 5-FU associations (case reports/small series), zinc deficiency (mechanistic rather than established), HMG-CoA lyase deficiency and multiple carboxylase deficiency (hyperammonemia inconsistent), fatty acid oxidation disorders as a group, hereditary fructose intolerance, and the spurious-elevation entry (a lab artifact, not a true cause).

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Impaired hepatic urea synthesis and portosystemic shunting cause hyperammonemia and hepatic encephalopathy.

answers.name: Acute liver failure
answers.pearl: Fulminant hepatic failure causes severe hyperammonemia, and ammonia above 150-200 micromol/L predicts cerebral edema and herniation.

answers.name: Portosystemic shunt
answers.pearl: Ammonia from the gut bypasses the liver through spontaneous shunts, surgical shunts or TIPS.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate inhibits carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I and depletes carnitine, causing hyperammonemia even with normal liver tests.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
answers.pearl: Blood in the gut is a protein load for bacterial ammonia production and a classic precipitant of encephalopathy.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Slow transit increases the time for colonic bacteria to generate ammonia.

answers.name: Infection or sepsis
answers.pearl: Infection increases catabolism and ammonia production and impairs hepatic clearance, particularly in cirrhosis.

answers.name: Urea cycle disorders
answers.pearl: Inborn errors of the urea cycle cause hyperammonemia with respiratory alkalosis and low BUN.

answers.name: Diuretic-induced hypokalemia and alkalosis
answers.pearl: Hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis raise renal ammoniagenesis and shift NH4+ to NH3, which crosses the blood-brain barrier.

answers.name: High protein intake
answers.pearl: A large protein load increases nitrogen delivery to a liver with limited ability to detoxify it.

answers.name: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency
answers.pearl: X-linked OTC deficiency is the most common urea cycle disorder and can present in adults and heterozygous women under stress, with high orotic acid.

answers.name: Reye syndrome
answers.pearl: Aspirin use with a viral illness in a child causes hepatic mitochondrial injury, encephalopathy and hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Hyperornithinemia-hyperammonemia-homocitrullinuria syndrome
answers.pearl: HHH syndrome (ORNT1/SLC25A15) impairs mitochondrial ornithine import and causes protein-induced hyperammonemia and spastic paraparesis.

answers.name: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency
