answers.pearl: CPS1 deficiency presents with severe neonatal hyperammonemia and low citrulline and orotic acid.

answers.name: Citrullinemia type I
answers.pearl: Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency gives very high citrulline with hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Argininosuccinic aciduria
answers.pearl: Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency causes hyperammonemia, elevated argininosuccinate and trichorrhexis nodosa.

answers.name: Arginase deficiency
answers.pearl: Arginase 1 deficiency usually causes progressive spastic diplegia with milder hyperammonemia and high arginine.

answers.name: N-acetylglutamate synthase deficiency
answers.pearl: NAGS deficiency causes a CPS1-like picture that responds to the activator N-carbamylglutamate (carglumic acid).

answers.name: Medication: asparaginase
answers.pearl: Asparaginase hydrolyzes asparagine and glutamine and reduces urea cycle substrate, causing hyperammonemia and encephalopathy.

answers.name: 5-Fluorouracil
answers.pearl: High-dose or DPD-deficient 5-FU can cause hyperammonemic encephalopathy, possibly via impaired Krebs cycle and urea cycle flux.

answers.name: Organic acidemias
answers.pearl: Propionic, methylmalonic and isovaleric acidemia suppress NAGS and cause hyperammonemia with ketoacidosis and elevated anion gap.

answers.name: Urinary diversion with ureterosigmoidostomy
answers.pearl: Urine in contact with colonic mucosa allows reabsorption of ammonium and causes hyperchloremic acidosis and hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy with urease-producing bacteria
answers.pearl: Proteus, Klebsiella or Ureaplasma split urea to ammonia in an obstructed urinary system and the ammonia is absorbed systemically.

answers.name: Hyperammonemia after lung transplant
answers.pearl: Ureaplasma urealyticum or Mycoplasma hominis infection in immunosuppressed lung transplant recipients causes severe hyperammonemia with cerebral edema.

answers.name: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant
answers.pearl: Idiopathic hyperammonemia after stem cell transplant or high-dose chemotherapy is rare but often fatal.

answers.name: Hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome
answers.pearl: Activating GLUD1 mutations cause leucine-sensitive hypoglycemia with mild persistent hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Citrin deficiency
answers.pearl: SLC25A13 mutations cause adult-onset citrullinemia type II with neuropsychiatric episodes and a fondness for high-protein and fatty foods.

answers.name: Lysinuric protein intolerance
answers.pearl: SLC7A7 mutations impair dibasic amino acid transport, reducing ornithine and arginine and causing protein-induced hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Fatty acid oxidation disorders
answers.pearl: Disorders such as CPT1, CPT2 and long-chain defects can impair acetyl-CoA supply for NAG synthesis and cause secondary hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Transient hyperammonemia of the newborn
answers.pearl: A self-limited syndrome in premature infants with respiratory distress, probably from portosystemic shunting through a patent ductus venosus.

answers.name: Glycine irrigant absorption
answers.pearl: Glycine in TURP or hysteroscopy irrigants is metabolized to ammonia, causing hyperammonemic encephalopathy alongside hyponatremia.

answers.name: Post-bariatric surgery hyperammonemia
answers.pearl: Gastric bypass can cause hyperammonemia through protein malnutrition, bacterial overgrowth and unmasking of latent urea cycle defects.

answers.name: Topiramate
answers.pearl: Topiramate can cause hyperammonemia, particularly when combined with valproate, by inhibiting glutamine synthesis and carbonic anhydrase.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Hyperammonemia in myeloma is reported with high tumor burden and may reflect ammonia generation by plasma cells.

answers.name: Pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthetase deficiency
answers.pearl: P5CS deficiency (ALDH18A1) causes low ornithine, citrulline and proline with fasting hyperammonemia and cutis laxa.

answers.name: Carbonic anhydrase VA deficiency
answers.pearl: CA-VA is mitochondrial and supplies bicarbonate for CPS1, so its loss causes neonatal hyperammonemia with metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Reduced oxaloacetate and aspartate impair the urea cycle, with lactic acidosis and hyperammonemia, especially in the neonatal form.

answers.name: Multiple carboxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Biotinidase or holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency can cause organic aciduria, hyperammonemia and rash.

answers.name: HMG-CoA lyase deficiency
answers.pearl: A ketogenesis defect with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, acidosis and sometimes hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Hepatic ischemia or shock liver
answers.pearl: Ischemic hepatitis in cardiogenic or septic shock can acutely impair ureagenesis.

answers.name: Acetaminophen overdose
answers.pearl: Massive hepatocellular necrosis eliminates urea cycle capacity and can produce acute liver failure with hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction causes hepatic congestion, portal hypertension and portosystemic shunting.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Acute fulminant Wilson presents with liver failure, Coombs-negative hemolysis and low alkaline phosphatase.

answers.name: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Third-trimester microvesicular steatosis can cause liver failure with hypoglycemia and hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Extensive tumor replacement of the liver or portal vein invasion can precipitate encephalopathy and hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Amanita mushroom poisoning
answers.pearl: Amatoxin causes hepatocyte necrosis and fulminant liver failure after an initial GI phase.

answers.name: Galactosemia
answers.pearl: Neonates with classic galactosemia develop liver failure, E. coli sepsis and hyperammonemia after feeding.

answers.name: Hereditary tyrosinemia type I
answers.pearl: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency causes liver failure in infancy with succinylacetone elevation.

answers.name: Hereditary fructose intolerance
answers.pearl: Aldolase B deficiency causes liver failure and hypoglycemia after fructose exposure, and may be accompanied by hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Abernethy malformation
answers.pearl: Congenital extrahepatic portosystemic shunt causing hyperammonemia, hepatopulmonary syndrome and encephalopathy.

answers.name: Zinc deficiency
answers.pearl: Zinc is a cofactor for ornithine transcarbamylase and ureagenesis, and deficiency in cirrhosis or after bariatric surgery can worsen hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Seizures
answers.pearl: Generalized convulsions transiently raise ammonia through muscle ammonia production.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Vigorous exercise transiently raises plasma ammonia from muscle adenine nucleotide catabolism.

answers.name: Spurious elevation from sample handling
answers.pearl: Delayed processing, hemolysis, prolonged tourniquet use or failure to put the sample on ice can falsely raise ammonia.

answers.name: High-dose glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: Steroids increase protein catabolism and can unmask latent urea cycle disorders such as OTC deficiency.

answers.name: Parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Amino acid infusions lacking arginine, or excess nitrogen load, can precipitate hyperammonemia in infants and in patients with liver disease.

answers.name: Carnitine deficiency
answers.pearl: Carnitine depletion, as in valproate therapy, impairs mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-CoA supply for the urea cycle.

prompts.prompt: Name monogenic (Mendelian) disorders that cause electrolyte abnormalities, renal tubulopathies, or hypertension.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Bartter type V aliasing (CASR, listed under ADH), EGF and CNNM2 hypomagnesemia (few kindreds), KCNA1 episodic ataxia with hypomagnesemia (single family), EHHADH Fanconi (one family), KCNJ18 thyrotoxic periodic paralysis (susceptibility variants, not Mendelian), Williams syndrome (contiguous gene deletion), Andersen-Tawil potassium variability, and cystic fibrosis pseudo-Bartter. Familial dysautonomia scored for blood pressure lability. Scores of 100 reserved for the four ultra-rare entries (PDE3A hypertension-brachydactyly, EGF, MAGED2, EHHADH) and Jansen.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome
answers.pearl: Salt-wasting tubulopathy of the thick ascending limb with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypercalciuria and normal to low blood pressure.

answers.name: Gitelman syndrome
answers.pearl: SLC12A3 loss of function in the distal convoluted tubule causes hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalciuria and metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Liddle syndrome
answers.pearl: Gain-of-function mutations in ENaC subunits (SCNN1B or SCNN1G) cause early-onset hypertension with hypokalemia and low renin and aldosterone, responsive to amiloride or triamterene.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: PKD1 and PKD2 mutations cause cystic kidneys with hypertension that often precedes renal insufficiency.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
answers.pearl: A CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene places aldosterone synthase under ACTH control, causing early-onset hypertension and hemorrhagic stroke.

answers.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
answers.pearl: Loss of 11-beta-HSD2 allows cortisol to activate the mineralocorticoid receptor, giving hypertension, hypokalemia and low aldosterone and renin.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
answers.pearl: The salt-wasting form causes hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and hypotension from CYP21A2 loss of function.

answers.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: X-linked AVPR2 or recessive AQP2 mutations cause vasopressin resistance, hypernatremia and polyuria.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: CFTR mutations in sweat losses can produce pseudo-Bartter syndrome with hyponatremia, hypochloremia and metabolic alkalosis.

answers.name: Gordon syndrome
answers.pearl: Mutations in WNK1, WNK4, KLHL3 or CUL3 raise NCC activity, causing hypertension with hyperkalemia and non-anion-gap acidosis that respond to thiazides.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2
answers.pearl: RET mutations cause pheochromocytoma with episodic or sustained hypertension, and primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia in MEN2A.

answers.name: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Heterozygous inactivating CASR mutations cause lifelong benign hypercalcemia with low urine calcium excretion.

answers.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism in MEN1
answers.pearl: MEN1 mutations cause multiglandular parathyroid hyperplasia with hypercalcemia, often in the 20s and 30s.

answers.name: Hypokalemic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: CACNA1S or SCN4A mutations cause attacks of flaccid weakness with low potassium after carbohydrate loads or rest after exercise.

answers.name: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: SCN4A gain-of-function mutations cause episodes of weakness with high or normal potassium and myotonia.

answers.name: Distal renal tubular acidosis (SLC4A1)
answers.pearl: Dominant or recessive mutations in the Cl-/HCO3- exchanger AE1 cause hypokalemia, nephrocalcinosis and hyperchloremic acidosis.

answers.name: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) or ENaC loss of function causes neonatal salt wasting with hyperkalemia and high aldosterone.

answers.name: Dent disease
answers.pearl: X-linked CLCN5 or OCRL mutations cause a proximal tubulopathy with low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria and nephrolithiasis.

answers.name: Cystinosis
answers.pearl: Lysosomal cystine accumulation due to CTNS mutations leads to renal Fanconi syndrome, rickets and corneal crystals.

answers.name: Hypophosphatemic rickets
answers.pearl: X-linked PHEX mutations raise FGF23, causing phosphate wasting, rickets and osteomalacia.

answers.name: Nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis
answers.pearl: Activating AVPR2 mutations mimic SIADH with hyponatremia despite undetectable vasopressin.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome type I (SLC12A1)
answers.pearl: Loss of NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb causes severe antenatal polyhydramnios, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome type II (KCNJ1)
answers.pearl: ROMK loss of function gives transient neonatal hyperkalemia before hypokalemia and hyponatremia ensue.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome type III (CLCNKB)
answers.pearl: ClC-Kb loss of function causes the classic Bartter phenotype, which can overlap with Gitelman syndrome.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type III
answers.pearl: Gain-of-function KCNJ5 mutations cause severe early-onset aldosteronism with adrenal hyperplasia, not suppressed by dexamethasone.

answers.name: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
aliases: congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: CYP11B1 deficiency accumulates deoxycorticosterone, causing virilization with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: CYP17A1 deficiency causes hypertension with hypokalemia, low sex steroids and primary amenorrhea or ambiguous genitalia.

answers.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: GNAS inactivation causes PTH resistance with hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia, with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy in type 1a.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Activating CASR mutations reduce PTH and increase urinary calcium wasting, with a Bartter-like presentation in type 5 hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia with secondary hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Mutations in TRPM6 impair intestinal and renal magnesium handling, leading to infantile seizures and tetany from hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: CLDN16 or CLDN19 mutations impair paracellular Mg2+ and Ca2+ reabsorption, causing CKD; CLDN19 also causes severe ocular disease.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type II (CLCN2)
answers.pearl: Gain-of-function CLCN2 chloride channel mutations cause familial primary aldosteronism with early-onset hypertension.

answers.name: Geller syndrome
answers.pearl: The MR S810L mutation makes the receptor activated by progesterone, causing severe hypertension in pregnancy.

answers.name: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
answers.pearl: VHL mutations cause pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma with secondary hypertension, plus hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma.

answers.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
answers.pearl: NF1 mutations cause pheochromocytoma and renovascular hypertension from renal artery stenosis.

answers.name: Hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: SDHB, SDHD, SDHC, SDHAF2 and other mutations cause catecholamine-secreting paraganglioma and hypertension.

answers.name: Distal renal tubular acidosis with sensorineural deafness
answers.pearl: ATP6V1B1 or ATP6V0A4 mutations impair H+-ATPase in alpha-intercalated cells, causing acidosis and early or late hearing loss.

answers.name: Fanconi-Bickel syndrome
answers.pearl: GLUT2 (SLC2A2) deficiency causes hepatorenal glycogen accumulation, rickets and a proximal tubulopathy.

answers.name: Lowe syndrome
answers.pearl: OCRL mutations cause a proximal tubulopathy with cataracts, hypotonia and intellectual disability.

answers.name: Congenital chloride diarrhea
answers.pearl: SLC26A3 mutations cause lifelong watery diarrhea with high stool chloride, hypochloremic hypokalemic alkalosis and neonatal polyhydramnios.

answers.name: Andersen-Tawil syndrome
answers.pearl: KCNJ2 mutations cause periodic paralysis, ventricular arrhythmias with a long QU interval and dysmorphic features, with variable potassium levels.

answers.name: Proximal renal tubular acidosis (SLC4A4)
answers.pearl: Homozygous NBCe1 mutations cause proximal RTA with short stature, band keratopathy, glaucoma and cataracts.

answers.name: Central diabetes insipidus (AVP gene mutation)
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant AVP-NPII mutations cause gradual loss of vasopressin neurons and polyuria that begins after infancy.

answers.name: Williams syndrome
answers.pearl: Elastin gene deletion on 7q11.23 causes supravalvular aortic stenosis, renal artery stenosis with hypertension, and infantile hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Aldosterone synthase deficiency
answers.pearl: CYP11B2 loss of function causes neonatal salt wasting, hyperkalemia and failure to thrive with normal cortisol.

answers.name: Congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: StAR mutations block steroidogenesis in the adrenals and gonads, causing salt wasting, hyperkalemia and 46,XY female genitalia.

answers.name: X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita
answers.pearl: NR0B1 (DAX1) mutations cause salt-wasting adrenal insufficiency in infants and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid resistance (Chrousos syndrome)
answers.pearl: NR3C1 mutations increase ACTH and adrenal mineralocorticoid precursors, causing hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis and hyperandrogenism.

answers.name: Carbonic anhydrase II deficiency syndrome
answers.pearl: CA2 loss of function causes osteopetrosis, mixed proximal and distal RTA and cerebral calcification.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome type IV (BSND)
answers.pearl: Barttin mutations impair ClC-Ka and ClC-Kb, causing severe antenatal Bartter syndrome with sensorineural deafness.

answers.name: EAST syndrome
answers.pearl: KCNJ10 (Kir4.1) mutations cause epilepsy, ataxia, sensorineural deafness and a Gitelman-like tubulopathy with hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: HNF1B-related disease
answers.pearl: HNF1B mutations cause renal cysts, MODY5 diabetes, hypomagnesemia with hypocalciuria and uterine malformations.

answers.name: Hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: SLC34A3 (NaPi-IIc) mutations cause renal phosphate wasting with high 1,25-vitamin D, hypercalciuria and nephrolithiasis.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
answers.pearl: Stabilizing FGF23 mutations prevent cleavage and cause phosphate wasting that can present in adolescence or adulthood.

answers.name: Familial tumoral calcinosis
answers.pearl: GALNT3, FGF23 or KL mutations cause hyperphosphatemia with periarticular calcified masses.

answers.name: Isolated renal glucosuria
answers.pearl: SLC5A2 (SGLT2) mutations cause persistent glucosuria with normal glycemia, a model for SGLT2 inhibitors.

answers.name: Renal hypouricemia
answers.pearl: URAT1 (SLC22A12) or GLUT9 loss of function causes hypouricemia and exercise-induced AKI.

answers.name: Familial dysautonomia
aliases: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type III
answers.pearl: Riley-Day syndrome (ELP1) causes extreme blood pressure lability with hypertensive crises and orthostatic hypotension.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type IV (CACNA1H)
answers.pearl: CACNA1H gain-of-function variants cause early-onset primary aldosteronism and hypertension in childhood.

answers.name: PASNA syndrome (CACNA1D)
aliases: primary aldosteronism seizures and neurologic abnormalities
answers.pearl: De novo CACNA1D variants cause primary aldosteronism with seizures and neurologic abnormalities.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
answers.pearl: CDC73 (HRPT2) mutations cause parathyroid tumors or carcinoma with hypercalcemia and ossifying jaw fibromas.

answers.name: Neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Biallelic CASR inactivation causes life-threatening neonatal hypercalcemia and bone demineralization.

answers.name: Idiopathic infantile hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Biallelic CYP24A1 or SLC34A1 mutations cause 1,25-vitamin D excess with hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.

answers.name: Carney complex
answers.pearl: PRKAR1A mutations cause primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease with Cushing syndrome, hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: ARMC5 primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Germline ARMC5 mutations cause cortisol excess with hypertension, often presenting in the fifth decade.

answers.name: Isolated dominant hypomagnesemia (FXYD2)
aliases: Na K ATPase gamma subunit mutation
answers.pearl: FXYD2 mutations (gamma subunit of Na/K ATPase) cause renal magnesium wasting with hypocalciuria.

answers.name: Congenital sodium diarrhea
answers.pearl: SPINT2 or SLC9A3 mutations cause severe neonatal diarrhea with high stool sodium, hyponatremia and metabolic acidosis.

answers.name: Episodic ataxia type 1 with hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: KCNA1 mutations cause episodic ataxia, myokymia and, in one family, renal magnesium wasting.

answers.name: CNNM2-related hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: CNNM2 mutations cause renal hypomagnesemia with seizures, intellectual disability and obesity.

answers.name: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis susceptibility (KCNJ18)
answers.pearl: Loss-of-function KCNJ18 variants predispose to hypokalemic paralysis with hyperthyroidism, mostly in Asian men.

answers.name: Brachydactyly with hypertension
answers.pearl: Gain-of-function PDE3A mutations cause severe salt-independent hypertension with brachydactyly type E and short stature.

answers.name: Isolated recessive renal hypomagnesemia (EGF)
answers.pearl: Recessive EGF mutations impair EGFR signaling to TRPM6, causing hypomagnesemia, seizures and intellectual disability.

answers.name: Transient antenatal Bartter syndrome (MAGED2)
answers.pearl: X-linked MAGED2 mutations cause severe polyhydramnios and prematurity with spontaneous resolution of the tubulopathy.

answers.name: EHHADH-related Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Dominant EHHADH mutations cause renal Fanconi syndrome through mitochondrial dysfunction in proximal tubule cells.

answers.name: Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
answers.pearl: Activating PTH1R mutations cause hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia and low PTH with severe short-limbed dwarfism.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of acute dyspnea.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pulmonary AVM rupture (HHT, case-level), Pulmonary tumor embolism, Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (geographic), Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, Air embolism; Goodpasture, Legionella and Takotsubo scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Heart failure exacerbation
answers.pearl: Acute decompensated HF causes pulmonary congestion with orthopnea, edema, and elevated BNP.

answers.name: COPD exacerbation
answers.pearl: Increased sputum, purulence, and wheeze in a patient with chronic obstructive disease.

answers.name: Asthma exacerbation
answers.pearl: Reversible bronchospasm with wheeze and a prolonged expiratory phase.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Consolidation with fever, productive cough, and focal crackles.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Sudden dyspnea with tachycardia and hypoxia, often with clear lungs on exam.

answers.name: Pneumothorax
answers.pearl: Sudden pleuritic pain and dyspnea with unilateral absent breath sounds.

answers.name: Acute coronary syndrome
answers.pearl: Ischemia can present as exertional or rest dyspnea, especially in women and diabetics.

answers.name: Anxiety or panic attack
answers.pearl: Hyperventilation with paresthesias, but a diagnosis of exclusion after organic causes are ruled out.

answers.name: Anaphylaxis
answers.pearl: Bronchospasm and upper airway edema following allergen exposure with urticaria and hypotension.

answers.name: Cardiac tamponade
answers.pearl: Pericardial fluid compresses the heart, producing Beck triad and pulsus paradoxus.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Kussmaul respirations compensate for metabolic acidosis and are perceived as breathlessness.

answers.name: Aspiration pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Chemical injury from gastric contents after witnessed aspiration or altered consciousness.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Large effusions compress lung and cause dyspnea, with dullness and decreased breath sounds.

answers.name: ARDS
answers.pearl: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with bilateral infiltrates not fully explained by cardiac failure.

answers.name: Acute valvular regurgitation
answers.pearl: Sudden aortic or mitral regurgitation from endocarditis or papillary muscle rupture causes pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
answers.pearl: Loss of atrial kick with rapid rate reduces filling and causes dyspnea.

answers.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
answers.pearl: Headache, dyspnea, and normal pulse oximetry despite tissue hypoxia, diagnosed with co-oximetry.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pleuritic positional chest pain with diffuse ST elevation and PR depression; dyspnea is common.

answers.name: Metabolic acidosis
answers.pearl: Any severe acidosis such as lactic acidosis or uremia stimulates deep, rapid breathing.

answers.name: Upper airway obstruction
answers.pearl: Stridor suggests a fixed or dynamic obstruction at or above the larynx.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease acute exacerbation
aliases: acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Acute worsening of IPF with new ground-glass opacities carries very high mortality.

answers.name: Obesity hypoventilation
answers.pearl: Chronic hypercapnia with obesity may decompensate and present with acute breathlessness.

answers.name: Neuromuscular respiratory failure
answers.pearl: Weak respiratory muscles from Guillain-Barre or myasthenia cause dyspnea with falling vital capacity.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Primary respiratory alkalosis with anion gap acidosis and tinnitus; tachypnea may be profound.

answers.name: Transfusion-related acute lung injury
answers.pearl: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours of transfusion due to donor antibodies.

answers.name: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia
answers.pearl: Acute febrile hypoxemic illness with eosinophilia on BAL, often after new smoking or inhaled exposure.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Dyspnea with falling hemoglobin and bilateral infiltrates, from vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, or lupus.

answers.name: Fat embolism syndrome
answers.pearl: Dyspnea, petechiae, and confusion 1 to 3 days after long bone fracture or orthopedic surgery.

answers.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
answers.pearl: Peripartum cardiovascular collapse with hypoxia and DIC due to fetal material entering maternal circulation.

answers.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: New heart failure in the last month of pregnancy or within 5 months postpartum.

answers.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Stress-induced apical ballooning mimics acute MI and can cause acute heart failure.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Dissection with acute aortic regurgitation or tamponade can present with dyspnea.

answers.name: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis
answers.pearl: Malignant infiltration of lymphatics gives progressive dyspnea with septal thickening on CT.

answers.name: Negative pressure pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Pulmonary edema after relieving upper airway obstruction such as laryngospasm following extubation.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Viral or immune myocarditis causes acute heart failure, often after a prodromal illness.

answers.name: Acute chest syndrome
answers.pearl: Sickle cell complication of new infiltrate, fever, and hypoxia from infection, infarction, or fat embolism.

answers.name: Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity
answers.pearl: Drug-induced pneumonitis and fibrosis, made worse by high inspired oxygen.

answers.name: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
answers.pearl: Intrapulmonary shunting in cirrhosis causes platypnea and orthodeoxia.

answers.name: Methemoglobinemia
answers.pearl: Chocolate-brown blood with pulse oximetry stuck near 85 percent, triggered by dapsone, benzocaine, or nitrates.

answers.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
answers.pearl: Surfactant accumulation with crazy-paving pattern on CT; often autoimmune GM-CSF antibodies.

answers.name: Cyanide poisoning
answers.pearl: Severe lactic acidosis with normal PaO2 after smoke inhalation or nitroprusside infusion.

answers.name: Air embolism
answers.pearl: Gas entering the venous circulation after central line removal or procedures causes acute dyspnea and hypoxia.

answers.name: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
answers.pearl: Rare pulmonary hypertension with Kerley B lines and normal wedge pressure and a poor vasodilator response.

answers.name: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and shock after rodent exposure in the Americas.

answers.name: Pulmonary tumor embolism
answers.pearl: Tumor cells occluding pulmonary microvasculature, causing subacute dyspnea with pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Goodpasture syndrome
answers.pearl: Anti-GBM disease causes alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis, a classic board pairing.

answers.name: Legionella pneumonia
answers.pearl: Atypical pneumonia with hyponatremia, diarrhea, and high fever, memorized as a board classic.

answers.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
answers.pearl: Genetic emphysema in a young nonsmoker with basilar predominance, a board favorite.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause diarrhea.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: SSRIs and statins-level mild effects, Ezetimibe, Ticagrelor, Potassium chloride, Herbal supplements (varied constituents), Neomycin (malabsorption mechanism); Olmesartan, Irinotecan and Orlistat scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Antibiotics
answers.pearl: Broad-spectrum agents disrupt gut flora, causing antibiotic-associated diarrhea and C. difficile risk.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Causes dose-related GI intolerance with diarrhea, mitigated by extended-release formulation.

answers.name: Laxatives
answers.pearl: Osmotic and stimulant laxatives, including surreptitious use, cause secretory or osmotic diarrhea.

answers.name: Magnesium-containing antacids
answers.pearl: Magnesium hydroxide acts as an osmotic laxative.

answers.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
answers.pearl: Clavulanate stimulates GI motility and commonly causes diarrhea.

answers.name: Clindamycin
answers.pearl: Classically linked with C. difficile colitis.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Increase risk of C. difficile and microscopic colitis.

answers.name: Colchicine
answers.pearl: Diarrhea is the dose-limiting toxicity and an early sign of colchicine toxicity.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Can cause enteropathy and microscopic colitis.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Fluorouracil, irinotecan, and many agents injure the gut mucosa.

answers.name: Irinotecan
answers.pearl: Causes early cholinergic diarrhea and late severe diarrhea related to SN-38 glucuronidation.

answers.name: Orlistat
answers.pearl: Lipase inhibition causes steatorrhea and oily stools.

answers.name: Acarbose
answers.pearl: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor leaves carbohydrate in the colon for bacterial fermentation.

answers.name: Lactulose
answers.pearl: Nonabsorbable disaccharide causing osmotic diarrhea, dosed to produce soft stools.

answers.name: Sorbitol containing medications
answers.pearl: Sugar alcohols in liquid medications and gum cause osmotic diarrhea.

answers.name: Mycophenolate
answers.pearl: GI toxicity including diarrhea is among its most common adverse effects.

answers.name: Olmesartan
answers.pearl: Sprue-like enteropathy with villous atrophy and chronic diarrhea.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: Serotonergic effect increases gut motility; sertraline in particular.

answers.name: Cholinesterase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Increased cholinergic tone causes diarrhea.

answers.name: Pyridostigmine
answers.pearl: Cholinergic stimulation of the gut.

answers.name: Misoprostol
answers.pearl: Prostaglandin E1 analogue with dose-related diarrhea.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: GI symptoms including diarrhea can signal digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Bile acid binders
answers.pearl: Cholestyramine and colesevelam can cause GI effects, though they are used to treat bile acid diarrhea.

answers.name: Levothyroxine overdose
answers.pearl: Excess thyroid hormone speeds gut transit.

answers.name: Oral sodium phosphate
answers.pearl: Phosphate bowel preps cause osmotic diarrhea and can cause acute phosphate nephropathy.

answers.name: Ezetimibe
answers.pearl: Diarrhea occurs more often when combined with a statin.

answers.name: Ipilimumab
answers.pearl: CTLA-4 blockade causes immune-mediated colitis.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: PD-1 and PD-L1 blockade can cause immune-related colitis and diarrhea.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Lapatinib, neratinib, and EGFR inhibitors commonly cause diarrhea.

answers.name: Idelalisib
answers.pearl: PI3K delta inhibitor with early and late-onset severe colitis.

answers.name: Somatostatin analogs
answers.pearl: Octreotide causes malabsorption and steatorrhea.

answers.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
answers.pearl: Diarrhea and nausea are common, dose-related adverse effects.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Antimetabolite toxicity to rapidly dividing enterocytes.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Diarrhea is among its most frequent adverse effects.

answers.name: Entacapone
answers.pearl: COMT inhibitor with delayed diarrhea occurring weeks to months after start.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Frequently causes diarrhea, which is a common reason for discontinuation.

answers.name: Ticagrelor
answers.pearl: Diarrhea is a recognized side effect.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Rarely paradoxical worsening of diarrhea can occur with 5-ASA agents.

answers.name: Neomycin
answers.pearl: Aminoglycoside given orally causes malabsorption by damaging enterocytes.

answers.name: Alosetron
answers.pearl: Used to treat IBS with diarrhea but can cause ischemic colitis.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Contribute to C. difficile and cause GI upset.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Third-generation agents are a leading antibiotic class associated with C. difficile.

answers.name: Neratinib
answers.pearl: HER2 inhibitor with near-universal diarrhea, often needing loperamide prophylaxis.

answers.name: Everolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitors commonly cause diarrhea and mucositis.

answers.name: Vitamin C excess
answers.pearl: High-dose ascorbic acid acts as an osmotic agent.

answers.name: Herbal supplements
answers.pearl: Senna, aloe, cascara, and ginseng-containing products contain stimulant laxatives.

answers.name: Fructose-containing medications
answers.pearl: Fructose and polyol excipients in medications are poorly absorbed and cause osmotic diarrhea.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: GI effects including diarrhea occur early or with toxicity.

prompts.prompt: Name ways a stroke or transient ischemic attack can present, including atypical presentations.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hiccups and Hoarseness (lateral medullary, limited reports), Alien hand syndrome, Bow-type rare syndromes, Gerstmann syndrome (localization debated), Urinary incontinence; Wallenberg, Locked-in and Gerstmann scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Unilateral weakness
answers.pearl: Hemiparesis from motor cortex or internal capsule ischemia is the classic stroke deficit.

answers.name: Speech difficulty
answers.pearl: Slurred speech or expressive aphasia from dominant hemisphere or brainstem involvement.

answers.name: Facial droop
answers.pearl: Central facial palsy spares the forehead because of bilateral upper facial motor input.

answers.name: Unilateral numbness
answers.pearl: Sensory loss from thalamic or parietal cortex ischemia.

answers.name: Vision loss
answers.pearl: Monocular loss suggests retinal or ophthalmic artery ischemia, while homonymous loss suggests posterior circulation.

answers.name: Headache
answers.pearl: Present in a minority of ischemic strokes and more common with hemorrhage or dissection.

answers.name: Dizziness
answers.pearl: Isolated vertigo can be the only sign of cerebellar or brainstem infarction.

answers.name: Confusion
answers.pearl: Acute confusion may result from thalamic, frontal, or right parietal infarction.

answers.name: Gait instability
answers.pearl: Truncal ataxia from cerebellar stroke can mimic intoxication.

answers.name: Diplopia
answers.pearl: Brainstem lesions disrupt cranial nerve nuclei or the medial longitudinal fasciculus.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Lateral medullary and bilateral hemispheric strokes impair swallowing.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Rarely vertebrobasilar ischemia causes transient loss of consciousness.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Posterior circulation strokes can present with nausea and vomiting mimicking gastroenteritis.

answers.name: Seizure
answers.pearl: Seizure at onset occurs in a small percentage and may confuse the picture.

answers.name: Coma
answers.pearl: Large basilar artery occlusion or hemispheric hemorrhage can cause unresponsiveness.

answers.name: Neglect
answers.pearl: Right parietal lesions cause failure to attend to left space, sometimes without awareness of deficit.

answers.name: Hiccups
answers.pearl: Lateral medullary infarction (Wallenberg) can cause persistent hiccups.

answers.name: Hoarseness
answers.pearl: Nucleus ambiguus involvement produces vocal cord paralysis.

answers.name: Drop attacks
answers.pearl: Sudden loss of postural tone without loss of consciousness from vertebrobasilar ischemia.

answers.name: Acute isolated amnesia
answers.pearl: Posterior cerebral artery or thalamic infarction can cause isolated memory loss.

answers.name: Horner syndrome
answers.pearl: Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis from lateral medullary or carotid dissection.

answers.name: Alien hand syndrome
answers.pearl: Anterior cerebral artery or callosal infarction with involuntary limb movements.

answers.name: Isolated monoparesis
answers.pearl: Cortical branch infarction can produce hand or leg weakness alone, mimicking a peripheral neuropathy.

answers.name: Pure motor hemiparesis
answers.pearl: Lacunar infarct in the internal capsule or pons with no sensory or cortical signs.

answers.name: Pure sensory stroke
answers.pearl: Thalamic lacune causes hemisensory loss without weakness.

answers.name: Ataxic hemiparesis
answers.pearl: A lacunar syndrome of ipsilateral weakness and cerebellar-type incoordination.

answers.name: Dysarthria clumsy hand syndrome
answers.pearl: Lacunar infarct in the basis pontis causing slurred speech and a clumsy hand.

answers.name: Wallenberg syndrome
answers.pearl: Lateral medullary infarct with crossed pain and temperature loss, Horner syndrome, and dysphagia.

answers.name: Neck pain
answers.pearl: Pain from cervical artery dissection can precede stroke by days.

answers.name: Acute psychosis or behavior change
answers.pearl: Frontal or right hemispheric infarcts can produce abulia, disinhibition, or agitation.

answers.name: Aphasia without weakness
answers.pearl: Isolated Wernicke or Broca aphasia from cortical branch occlusion.

answers.name: Urinary incontinence
answers.pearl: Frontal infarcts may cause incontinence; it can accompany any severe stroke.

answers.name: Fall
answers.pearl: Elderly patients with stroke often present after a fall or with new immobility.

answers.name: Hemiballismus
answers.pearl: Subthalamic nucleus infarct causes violent contralateral flinging movements.

answers.name: Locked-in syndrome
answers.pearl: Ventral pontine infarct with preserved vertical eye movement and consciousness but quadriplegia.

answers.name: Gerstmann syndrome
answers.pearl: Dominant angular gyrus lesion: agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, and left-right confusion.

answers.name: Transient monocular blindness
answers.pearl: Embolus to the retinal artery causes a curtain-like unilateral visual loss.

answers.name: Anton syndrome
answers.pearl: Cortical blindness with denial of visual loss following bilateral occipital infarcts.

answers.name: Balint syndrome
answers.pearl: Bilateral parieto-occipital lesions with simultanagnosia, optic ataxia, and ocular apraxia.

answers.name: Alexia without agraphia
answers.pearl: Left posterior cerebral artery infarction involving the splenium disconnects visual input from language areas.

answers.name: Top of the basilar syndrome
answers.pearl: Midbrain and thalamic infarcts causing somnolence, vertical gaze palsy, and visual deficits.

answers.name: Capsular warning syndrome
answers.pearl: Stuttering recurrent lacunar TIAs over hours or days preceding a capsular infarct.

answers.name: Limb-shaking TIA
answers.pearl: Hemodynamic TIA from carotid stenosis causing brief contralateral shaking, mimicking focal seizure.

answers.name: Opercular syndrome
answers.pearl: Bilateral anterior opercular lesions cause facial, pharyngeal, and masticatory paralysis with preserved reflexive movements.

answers.name: Artery of Percheron infarct
answers.pearl: Bilateral paramedian thalamic infarct causing hypersomnolence, vertical gaze palsy, and amnesia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of shock.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypermagnesemia-type rare causes were dropped; Cytokine release syndrome and HLH (overlap with sepsis physiology), Carcinoid crisis, Beriberi, Capnocytophaga sepsis (case-report level), Sickle cell splenic sequestration (pediatric); Toxic shock syndrome, Takotsubo and Waterhouse-Friderichsen scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Septic shock
answers.pearl: Vasodilatory shock from infection with hypotension persisting after fluid resuscitation.

answers.name: Hypovolemic shock
answers.pearl: Volume loss from hemorrhage, GI losses, or burns reduces preload.

answers.name: Hemorrhagic shock
answers.pearl: Acute blood loss with tachycardia, narrow pulse pressure, and cool extremities.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Pump failure with elevated filling pressures and low cardiac output, often after MI.

answers.name: Anaphylactic shock
answers.pearl: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation with vasodilation, bronchospasm, and angioedema.

answers.name: Obstructive shock
answers.pearl: Impaired filling or outflow from mechanical obstruction.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Massive PE obstructs the right ventricular outflow and causes obstructive shock.

answers.name: Tension pneumothorax
answers.pearl: Air trapped under pressure compresses the mediastinum and impairs venous return.

answers.name: Cardiac tamponade
answers.pearl: Pericardial fluid impairs diastolic filling, with Beck triad and pulsus paradoxus.

answers.name: Neurogenic shock
answers.pearl: Loss of sympathetic tone after cervical or high thoracic spinal cord injury causes hypotension with bradycardia.

answers.name: Adrenal crisis
answers.pearl: Acute cortisol deficiency from adrenal failure or abrupt steroid cessation produces refractory hypotension.

answers.name: Distributive shock
answers.pearl: Vasodilation with low systemic vascular resistance, including sepsis, anaphylaxis, and neurogenic causes.

answers.name: Massive myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Large infarction with pump failure is the most common cause of cardiogenic shock.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation, and rapid or slow arrhythmias, can reduce output.

answers.name: Acute valvular regurgitation
answers.pearl: Sudden mitral or aortic regurgitation overwhelms a non-compliant ventricle.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Rupture or tamponade from dissection causes shock with possible blood pressure differential.

answers.name: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Triad of hypotension, pulsatile abdominal mass, and back or abdominal pain.

answers.name: Toxic shock syndrome
answers.pearl: Superantigen-mediated shock from Staphylococcus aureus or group A Streptococcus with rash and multiorgan failure.

answers.name: Drug overdose
answers.pearl: Calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers, and sedatives can cause profound hypotension.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Third-spacing and systemic inflammation cause hypovolemic and distributive shock in severe disease.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Large burns cause massive fluid shifts and loss of intravascular volume.

answers.name: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy
answers.pearl: Intraperitoneal hemorrhage in a woman of reproductive age with a positive pregnancy test.

answers.name: Acute mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Bowel necrosis with sepsis and third spacing leads to shock; lactate rises late.

answers.name: Perforated viscus
answers.pearl: Peritonitis from perforation causes septic and hypovolemic shock.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Fulminant myocarditis produces acute pump failure in young patients.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Profound osmotic diuresis causes hypovolemic shock in severe DKA.

answers.name: Thyroid storm
answers.pearl: Severe hyperthyroidism with high output failure, fever, and arrhythmia.

answers.name: Myxedema coma
answers.pearl: Severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, and hypotension.

answers.name: Severe anemia
answers.pearl: Critical reduction in oxygen delivery, even without bleeding, as in hemolysis.

answers.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Stress cardiomyopathy with apical ballooning can cause cardiogenic shock.

answers.name: Right ventricular infarction
answers.pearl: Preload-dependent shock with clear lungs and elevated JVP after inferior MI.

answers.name: Acute liver failure
answers.pearl: Vasodilation and sepsis physiology in fulminant hepatic failure.

answers.name: Capillary leak syndrome
answers.pearl: Cytokine-mediated leak causes hypotension, edema, and hemoconcentration.

answers.name: Cytokine release syndrome
answers.pearl: Immune activation after CAR-T or bispecific antibody therapy causes fever and vasodilatory shock.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Hyperinflammatory state with fever, cytopenias, and shock.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma crisis
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surge can cause cardiogenic shock or vasodilatory collapse after tumor manipulation.

answers.name: Carcinoid crisis
answers.pearl: Massive serotonin and vasoactive release causes shock with bronchospasm.

answers.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: New systolic failure near delivery can cause cardiogenic shock.

answers.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
answers.pearl: Sudden cardiopulmonary collapse and DIC during labor or immediately postpartum.

answers.name: Cyanide poisoning
answers.pearl: Cytochrome oxidase blockade causes lactic acidosis and shock after fires or nitroprusside.

answers.name: Beriberi (wet)
answers.pearl: Thiamine deficiency causes high-output failure with vasodilation, known as Shoshin beriberi in fulminant cases.

answers.name: Capnocytophaga sepsis
answers.pearl: Fulminant sepsis with purpura after dog or cat bites, especially in asplenic patients.

answers.name: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome
answers.pearl: Meningococcemia with adrenal hemorrhage, a boards classic.

answers.name: Sickle cell splenic sequestration
answers.pearl: Acute splenic pooling of red cells causes hypovolemic shock, mostly in children with sickle cell disease.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of chest pain.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mondor-type and Cervical radiculopathy referral, Precordial catch and Slipping rib (benign, clinical diagnosis), Radiation heart disease latency, Pleurodynia (Coxsackie B); Coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal), Boerhaave and Takotsubo scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Acute coronary syndrome
answers.pearl: Ischemic pressure-like pain with exertion or rest, radiating to the arm or jaw.

answers.name: Stable angina
answers.pearl: Exertional chest pressure relieved by rest or nitroglycerin.

answers.name: Musculoskeletal chest pain
answers.pearl: Reproducible with palpation or movement.

answers.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
answers.pearl: Burning retrosternal pain related to meals and lying down.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Pleuritic pain with dyspnea and tachycardia.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Pleuritic chest pain with fever and cough from pleural involvement.

answers.name: Pneumothorax
answers.pearl: Sudden unilateral pleuritic pain with decreased breath sounds.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Sharp positional pain relieved by leaning forward with diffuse ST elevation.

answers.name: Aortic dissection
answers.pearl: Abrupt tearing pain radiating to the back with blood pressure differential.

answers.name: Anxiety or panic attack
answers.pearl: Chest tightness with palpitations and hyperventilation, after exclusion of organic causes.

answers.name: Esophageal spasm
answers.pearl: Squeezing pain, sometimes relieved by nitroglycerin and mimicking angina.

answers.name: Pleuritis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of the pleura causes sharp inspiratory pain.

answers.name: Herpes zoster
answers.pearl: Dermatomal pain may precede the vesicular rash by days.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: Epigastric pain can radiate to the chest.

answers.name: Cholecystitis
answers.pearl: Right upper quadrant pain can be referred to the chest or mimic ischemia.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Chest pain after viral illness with troponin elevation and normal coronaries.

answers.name: Esophageal rupture
answers.pearl: Severe pain after forceful vomiting with subcutaneous emphysema and mediastinitis.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Exertional chest pain from right ventricular ischemia.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Angina from increased myocardial oxygen demand with reduced supply.

answers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Exertional chest pain with dynamic outflow obstruction and a murmur that increases with Valsalva.

answers.name: Coronary vasospasm
answers.pearl: Rest pain with transient ST elevation, often at night, responsive to nitrates and calcium channel blockers.

answers.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Stress-related apical ballooning mimicking acute MI.

answers.name: Cocaine-associated chest pain
answers.pearl: Vasospasm and thrombosis cause ischemia, and benzodiazepines are first-line.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Large effusion or underlying pleural inflammation can cause chest pain.

answers.name: Pulmonary malignancy
answers.pearl: Chest wall or pleural invasion causes persistent pain.

answers.name: Rib fracture
answers.pearl: Traumatic or pathologic fracture with focal tenderness and pain with breathing.

answers.name: Mitral valve prolapse
answers.pearl: Atypical chest pain with a midsystolic click.

answers.name: Esophagitis
answers.pearl: Infectious or pill esophagitis causes odynophagia and retrosternal pain.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Epigastric pain radiating to the back, sometimes with chest involvement.

answers.name: Sickle cell acute chest syndrome
answers.pearl: Chest pain, fever, and new infiltrate in sickle cell disease.

answers.name: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
answers.pearl: Acute MI in young women, postpartum or with fibromuscular dysplasia.

answers.name: Mediastinitis
answers.pearl: Deep neck infection or esophageal perforation causes severe pain with fever.

answers.name: Precordial catch syndrome
answers.pearl: Brief sharp localized pain in young people, benign and often with inspiration.

answers.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
answers.pearl: Rapid rhythm with demand ischemia causes chest discomfort.

answers.name: Thoracic outlet syndrome
answers.pearl: Neurovascular compression produces chest and arm pain.

answers.name: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum
answers.pearl: Alveolar rupture with air tracking centrally after cough or Valsalva, with Hamman crunch.

answers.name: Cardiac sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous disease causing arrhythmia and chest pain.

answers.name: Coronary artery anomaly
answers.pearl: Anomalous origin of a coronary artery causes exertional ischemia in young people.

answers.name: Kawasaki disease coronary aneurysm
answers.pearl: Coronary artery aneurysms from childhood vasculitis can thrombose in adulthood.

answers.name: Coronary arteritis
answers.pearl: Vasculitis such as Takayasu or polyarteritis nodosa can involve the coronaries.

answers.name: Pleurodynia
answers.pearl: Coxsackie B infection causes sharp chest wall pain with fever, called Bornholm disease.

answers.name: Radiation-induced coronary disease
answers.pearl: Accelerated atherosclerosis and pericarditis years after mediastinal radiation.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause thrombocytopenia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Digoxin-class rare immune reports, Thiazides, Amiodarone, Phenytoin, Oxaliplatin (immune mechanism), Beyond-label rare reports such as Rituximab late-onset and Tocilizumab; Quinine, Linezolid and Ticlopidine (TTP) scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia from anti-PF4 antibodies typically appears 5 to 10 days after exposure and causes thrombosis.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Myelosuppression from cytotoxic drugs is the most common cause of drug-related thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Reversible marrow suppression, usually after more than 10 to 14 days of therapy.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent antibodies can cause severe immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides are a classic cause of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Beta-lactam antibiotics
answers.pearl: Penicillins and cephalosporins can trigger drug-dependent platelet antibodies.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Dose-related thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Can suppress marrow or cause immune platelet destruction.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: The prototype for drug-dependent antibody thrombocytopenia, also found in tonic water.

answers.name: Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors
answers.pearl: Abciximab, eptifibatide, and tirofiban cause acute thrombocytopenia within hours, sometimes due to pre-existing antibodies.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Direct marrow toxicity and folate deficiency reduce platelet production.

answers.name: Clopidogrel
answers.pearl: Associated with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, rarely.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Intermittent dosing can cause immune-mediated thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Antimetabolite marrow suppression.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Rare drug-dependent platelet antibody formation.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Immune thrombocytopenia has been reported with several agents.

answers.name: Mycophenolate
answers.pearl: Antiproliferative agent that can cause cytopenias.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Dose-related marrow suppression, worse with TPMT deficiency or allopurinol.

answers.name: Ganciclovir
answers.pearl: Bone marrow suppression including thrombocytopenia and neutropenia.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Marrow suppression and immune-mediated platelet destruction.

answers.name: Ribavirin
answers.pearl: Mainly hemolysis but contributes to cytopenias with interferon.

answers.name: Zidovudine
answers.pearl: Marrow suppression, mainly anemia and neutropenia, sometimes thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Hematologic toxicities including cytopenias.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Rare immune thrombocytopenia as part of a hypersensitivity reaction.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Rare cause of immune-mediated thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Lenalidomide
answers.pearl: Myelosuppressive immunomodulator with frequent thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Proteasome inhibitor with transient cyclic thrombocytopenia due to inhibition of megakaryocyte function.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Dasatinib, imatinib, and others cause thrombocytopenia through marrow suppression.

answers.name: PARP inhibitors
answers.pearl: Olaparib and niraparib cause cytopenias, and niraparib particularly thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Thrombotic microangiopathy and myelosuppression.

answers.name: Mitomycin C
answers.pearl: Thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis and thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine can cause thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Ticlopidine
answers.pearl: Can cause TTP and neutropenia.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Auranothiomalate and related compounds cause immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: Immune thrombocytopenia and marrow suppression in rheumatoid arthritis patients.

answers.name: Sirolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitors cause dose-dependent thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Inotuzumab ozogamicin
answers.pearl: Hepatotoxicity and cytopenias, including thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Alemtuzumab
answers.pearl: Immune thrombocytopenia occurs in a minority of patients treated for multiple sclerosis.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Delayed-onset cytopenias including immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Cocaine adulterated with levamisole
answers.pearl: Levamisole causes agranulocytosis, vasculitis, and rarely thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Oxaliplatin
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent immune thrombocytopenia unlike direct marrow suppression of other platinums.

answers.name: Platinum agents
answers.pearl: Carboplatin causes dose-limiting marrow suppression with notable thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Ipilimumab
answers.pearl: Checkpoint inhibitors cause immune thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Vaccine-induced thrombotic thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Adenoviral vector COVID-19 vaccines caused anti-PF4 thrombosis with thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Tocilizumab
answers.pearl: IL-6 blockade is associated with thrombocytopenia and neutropenia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes or triggers of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hepatitis A/B/C and Varicella (case series), Mycoplasma, Q fever, Babesiosis, Anaplasmosis, Sarcoidosis, Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, Drug-induced HLH (overlap with DRESS); Familial HLH, Chediak-Higashi and XLP scored as Board Prep Traps (primary HLH, not strictly secondary).

answers.name: Epstein-Barr virus
answers.pearl: The most common infectious trigger of HLH, including in adults with primary EBV infection.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: The most common malignancy-associated trigger, especially T cell and NK cell lymphomas.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Bacterial sepsis can trigger secondary HLH, and HLH can mimic sepsis.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: HLH occurs as macrophage activation syndrome in active lupus.

answers.name: Macrophage activation syndrome
answers.pearl: The rheumatologic form of secondary HLH, most often in Still disease and systemic JIA.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: A classic autoinflammatory trigger of macrophage activation syndrome.

answers.name: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis
answers.pearl: The childhood analogue of Still disease and a leading cause of MAS.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus
answers.pearl: CMV infection triggers HLH in transplant recipients and immunocompromised hosts.

answers.name: HIV
answers.pearl: HIV, often with opportunistic infections or lymphoma, can precipitate HLH.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated or miliary TB is among the most common bacterial triggers worldwide.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Acute leukemias can cause HLH at presentation or during chemotherapy.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated histoplasmosis is a well-described fungal trigger in immunosuppressed patients.

answers.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
answers.pearl: Kala-azar commonly produces an HLH-like picture with pancytopenia and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma
aliases: hepatosplenic gamma delta T cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Aggressive lymphoma strongly associated with HLH and immunosuppressant exposure.

answers.name: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: A T-cell lymphoma with a known tendency to cause HLH.

answers.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: The most common B cell lymphoma associated with HLH, including intravascular variants.

answers.name: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: Notorious for fever, cytopenias, and hemophagocytosis, with diagnosis often by random skin or marrow biopsy.

answers.name: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: T cell lymphomas frequently cause HLH through cytokine overproduction.

answers.name: NK/T-cell lymphoma
answers.pearl: EBV-associated extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma is a recognized HLH trigger, especially in Asia.

answers.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
answers.pearl: Less common but documented, often with EBV positivity.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Rarely associated with HLH, especially in the context of treatment or infection.

answers.name: Solid tumors
answers.pearl: Rare carcinomas have been linked to HLH, including germ cell tumors.

answers.name: Immunosuppression after transplant
answers.pearl: Solid organ and stem cell transplantation can trigger HLH via infection or alloreactivity.

answers.name: Chemotherapy-related HLH
answers.pearl: Chemotherapy and immune effector therapy may cause or unmask HLH.

answers.name: CAR T-cell therapy
aliases: chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy
answers.pearl: Cytokine release can evolve into HLH-like toxicity known as IEC-HS.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune-related adverse event that can present as secondary HLH.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Rarely MAS occurs in adult RA and is easily misattributed to a flare.

answers.name: Dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Reported MAS in dermatomyositis and other inflammatory myopathies.

answers.name: Vasculitis
answers.pearl: MAS can complicate systemic vasculitides including Kawasaki disease.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Rarely HLH has been reported in sarcoid.

answers.name: Influenza
answers.pearl: Severe influenza, including H1N1 and H5N1, has been reported to trigger HLH.

answers.name: SARS-CoV-2
answers.pearl: Severe COVID-19 shows a hyperinflammatory state and some cases meet HLH criteria.

answers.name: Dengue
answers.pearl: Dengue virus is a recognized viral trigger, especially in endemic regions.

answers.name: Parvovirus B19
answers.pearl: Can trigger HLH, particularly in patients with hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Herpes simplex virus
answers.pearl: Disseminated HSV in immunocompromised and neonates can cause HLH.

answers.name: Varicella zoster virus
answers.pearl: VZV reactivation or disseminated disease has been reported as a trigger.

answers.name: Adenovirus
answers.pearl: Disseminated adenoviral infection in immunocompromised hosts can trigger HLH.

answers.name: Human herpesvirus 8
answers.pearl: KSHV-associated multicentric Castleman disease and HIV-associated HLH.

answers.name: Hepatitis A
answers.pearl: Reported viral trigger of HLH, especially with acute liver injury.

answers.name: Hepatitis B
answers.pearl: Reported as a trigger, with hepatitis B reactivation during immunosuppression.

answers.name: Hepatitis C
answers.pearl: Rare hepatitis-associated HLH.

answers.name: Rickettsial infection
answers.pearl: Scrub typhus, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and other rickettsioses cause HLH.

answers.name: Brucellosis
answers.pearl: Reported in endemic areas with marrow involvement.

answers.name: Salmonella typhi infection
answers.pearl: Typhoid fever is a well-recognized bacterial trigger with marrow hemophagocytosis.

answers.name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
answers.pearl: Atypical pneumonia occasionally triggers HLH.

answers.name: Q fever
answers.pearl: Coxiella burnetii infection can cause hemophagocytosis with granulomatous hepatitis.

answers.name: Bartonella
answers.pearl: Disseminated Bartonella in immunocompromised patients and cat scratch disease.

answers.name: Candida
answers.pearl: Invasive fungal infections, including candidemia, can trigger HLH.

answers.name: Cryptococcus
answers.pearl: Disseminated cryptococcosis is reported in advanced immune compromise.

answers.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
answers.pearl: Pneumocystis in immunosuppressed patients has been reported as an HLH trigger.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Severe malaria, especially P. falciparum, may precipitate HLH.

answers.name: Toxoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated toxoplasmosis in transplant or HIV patients.

answers.name: Babesiosis
answers.pearl: Tick-borne infection reported to trigger HLH, particularly in asplenic patients.

answers.name: Familial HLH
answers.pearl: Primary HLH from PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, or STXBP2 mutations can first appear in adulthood.

answers.name: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease
answers.pearl: SH2D1A or XIAP mutations cause HLH, usually triggered by EBV in boys.

answers.name: Griscelli syndrome type 2
answers.pearl: RAB27A mutation with partial albinism, silvery hair, and HLH.

answers.name: Chediak-Higashi syndrome
answers.pearl: LYST mutation with oculocutaneous albinism, giant lysosomal granules, and an accelerated HLH phase.

answers.name: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 2
answers.pearl: AP3B1 mutation causing albinism, platelet dysfunction, and HLH.

answers.name: Drug-induced HLH
answers.pearl: Drugs including allopurinol, lamotrigine, and phenytoin can cause a hypersensitivity picture overlapping with HLH.

answers.name: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
answers.pearl: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis that can be complicated by HLH.

answers.name: Castleman disease
answers.pearl: Multicentric Castleman disease with cytokine storm may mimic or trigger HLH.

answers.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
answers.pearl: Can present with or be complicated by hemophagocytosis, mostly in infants.

answers.name: SFTS virus
answers.pearl: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus commonly triggers HLH in East Asia.

answers.name: Hantavirus hemorrhagic fever
answers.pearl: Hantavirus renal syndrome has been reported with HLH.

answers.name: Primary immunodeficiency
answers.pearl: Several immunodeficiencies carry HLH risk, such as CVID.

answers.name: Anaplasmosis
answers.pearl: Rickettsia-like tick-borne illness with HLH reported.

answers.name: Chronic active EBV infection
answers.pearl: Persistent EBV with organomegaly and hemophagocytosis.

prompts.prompt: Name ways atrial fibrillation can present or cause complications.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dysphagia megalatriensis and coronary embolism causing MI (case-report level), Polyuria from ANP release (variable), Silent cerebral infarcts and cognitive decline (association, not always causal), Regularized ventricular rhythm as a sign of digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: Palpitations
answers.pearl: The most typical symptom, described as an irregular, racing or fluttering heartbeat.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Left atrial stasis leads to cardioembolic stroke, the most feared complication of AF.

answers.name: Dyspnea
answers.pearl: Loss of atrial kick and rapid rates raise filling pressures and cause exertional breathlessness.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Reduced cardiac output and rate irregularity commonly cause tiredness.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: AF can precipitate or worsen heart failure, especially with diastolic dysfunction.

answers.name: Dizziness
answers.pearl: Beat-to-beat variation in output causes lightheadedness.

answers.name: Chest pain
answers.pearl: Rapid rates cause demand ischemia and angina, even with normal coronaries.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Rapid rates, hypotension, or post-conversion pauses (tachy-brady) can cause fainting.

answers.name: Asymptomatic
answers.pearl: Many patients have no symptoms and AF is found on a pulse check or ECG.

answers.name: Exercise intolerance
answers.pearl: Impaired rate control and chronotropic response limit exertional capacity.

answers.name: Transient ischemic attack
answers.pearl: Embolic TIA may be the first manifestation of previously unrecognized AF.

answers.name: Rapid ventricular response
answers.pearl: Uncontrolled AV conduction produces ventricular rates above 100 to 150.

answers.name: Hypotension
answers.pearl: Loss of atrial contribution plus rapid rates can drop blood pressure.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Awareness of an irregular rapid heartbeat is often experienced as panic or anxiety.

answers.name: Bleeding from anticoagulation
answers.pearl: The main complication of treatment; HAS-BLED helps assess the risk.

answers.name: Acute limb ischemia
answers.pearl: Peripheral arterial emboli from the left atrium cause the six Ps of acute ischemia.

answers.name: Pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Acute loss of atrial kick with high rates can cause flash pulmonary edema, notably in mitral stenosis or stiff ventricles.

answers.name: Left atrial appendage thrombus
answers.pearl: Over 90 percent of thrombi in non-valvular AF form in the appendage, found by TEE.

answers.name: Postoperative atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Occurs in a large fraction of patients after cardiac surgery, from adrenergic surge and inflammation.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Severe cases with rapid rates on a poor ventricle can cause shock requiring cardioversion.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Embolization to the superior mesenteric artery causes sudden abdominal pain out of proportion to exam.

answers.name: Type 2 myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Rapid rates cause supply-demand mismatch and troponin elevation without plaque rupture.

answers.name: Polyuria
answers.pearl: Atrial stretch releases ANP, producing increased urination during episodes.

answers.name: First presentation of hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: AF can be the initial clue to thyrotoxicosis, so TSH is part of the new-onset workup.

answers.name: Retinal artery occlusion
answers.pearl: Cardioembolic occlusion causes sudden monocular vision loss or amaurosis fugax.

answers.name: Dementia or cognitive decline
answers.pearl: AF is associated with cognitive impairment, likely via silent infarcts and hypoperfusion.

answers.name: Renal infarction
answers.pearl: Embolic occlusion of a renal artery causes flank pain, hematuria and raised LDH.

answers.name: Splenic infarction
answers.pearl: Splenic emboli cause left upper quadrant pain and may mimic other abdominal pathology.

answers.name: Bradycardia or tachy-brady syndrome
answers.pearl: AF often coexists with sinus node disease, and conversion may be followed by long pauses.

answers.name: Loss of atrial kick decompensation
answers.pearl: Patients with stiff ventricles, aortic stenosis or HCM depend on atrial contraction and decompensate when it is lost.

answers.name: Stroke after cardioversion
answers.pearl: Restoration of atrial contraction can dislodge thrombus, so anticoagulation is needed around cardioversion.

answers.name: Silent cerebral infarcts
answers.pearl: MRI frequently shows clinically silent embolic infarcts in AF patients.

answers.name: Regularized rhythm with digoxin toxicity
answers.pearl: A regular slow ventricular rhythm in AF suggests complete heart block with a junctional escape, often from digoxin.

answers.name: Embolic myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Coronary embolism from the left atrium is an uncommon cause of MI with normal coronary anatomy.

answers.name: Ashman phenomenon
answers.pearl: A long-short cycle sequence produces aberrant wide-complex beats that mimic ventricular tachycardia.

answers.name: Dysphagia megalatriensis
answers.pearl: Marked left atrial enlargement can compress the esophagus and cause dysphagia.

answers.name: Holiday heart syndrome
answers.pearl: Binge alcohol use triggers new-onset AF in otherwise healthy people.

answers.name: Pre-excited atrial fibrillation in WPW
answers.pearl: AF conducted over an accessory pathway gives a rapid irregular wide-complex rhythm that can degenerate to VF, so AV nodal blockers are avoided.

answers.name: Tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Sustained rapid ventricular rates can cause reversible LV systolic dysfunction.

answers.name: Irregularly irregular pulse
answers.pearl: The classic bedside sign, with absent P waves on ECG.

answers.name: Pulse deficit
answers.pearl: The apical rate exceeds the radial rate because short-diastole beats fail to generate a palpable pulse.

answers.name: Cryptogenic stroke with occult atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Prolonged monitoring in embolic stroke of undetermined source detects paroxysmal AF in a meaningful minority.

answers.name: Left atrial enlargement
answers.pearl: Both a cause and a consequence of AF, remodeling the atrium and predisposing to stasis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of chronic kidney disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mesoamerican nephropathy (etiology debated), Hyperoxaluria and cystinosis (genetic, rarely named), ADTKD naming varies, Radiation nephropathy, Sjogren and sarcoid interstitial disease (less common causes).

answers.name: Diabetic kidney disease
answers.pearl: The leading cause of CKD and ESRD in many countries, with albuminuria preceding GFR decline.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Long-standing hypertension causes nephrosclerosis with arteriolar hyalinosis and global glomerulosclerosis.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Chronic glomerular inflammation progresses to scarring and ESRD if untreated.

answers.name: Polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: ADPKD from PKD1 or PKD2 mutations causes progressive cyst growth and CKD.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic obstruction from BPH, stones, strictures or tumors causes hydronephrosis and parenchymal loss.

answers.name: IgA nephropathy
answers.pearl: The most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, often with episodic hematuria after infections.

answers.name: Chronic NSAID use
answers.pearl: NSAIDs cause hemodynamic AKI and chronic interstitial nephritis, with papillary necrosis in analgesic nephropathy.

answers.name: Lupus nephritis
answers.pearl: Immune complex GN in SLE, with class IV the most aggressive.

answers.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
answers.pearl: A common cause of nephrotic syndrome, with primary, genetic (APOL1) and adaptive forms.

answers.name: Reflux nephropathy
answers.pearl: Vesicoureteral reflux with infection in childhood causes cortical scarring and later CKD.

answers.name: Kidney stones
answers.pearl: Recurrent stones, obstruction and infection cause progressive parenchymal damage.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Atherosclerotic renovascular disease causes ischemic nephropathy and can be accompanied by flash pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Prior acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Even recovered AKI raises the risk of later CKD through maladaptive repair and fibrosis.

answers.name: Membranous nephropathy
answers.pearl: Often caused by anti-PLA2R antibodies, with secondary forms from cancer, hepatitis B, lupus and drugs.

answers.name: Cardiorenal syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic heart failure causes renal congestion and hypoperfusion leading to CKD.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Light chain cast nephropathy is the most common renal lesion in myeloma.

answers.name: Obesity-related glomerulopathy
answers.pearl: Hyperfiltration and secondary FSGS develop with severe obesity.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: AL or AA amyloid deposits cause nephrotic range proteinuria and progressive renal failure.

answers.name: ANCA-associated vasculitis
answers.pearl: Pauci-immune crescentic GN from GPA or MPA causes rapidly progressive disease and chronic scarring.

answers.name: HIV-associated nephropathy
answers.pearl: Collapsing FSGS in patients of African ancestry with uncontrolled HIV, linked to APOL1 risk alleles.

answers.name: Hepatitis B or C related renal disease
answers.pearl: HBV causes membranous disease and HCV causes MPGN with cryoglobulinemia.

answers.name: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Immune complex or complement-mediated disease with a tram-track pattern on biopsy.

answers.name: Anti-GBM disease
answers.pearl: Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies cause rapidly progressive GN, often with lung hemorrhage.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity
answers.pearl: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus cause afferent vasoconstriction and chronic striped interstitial fibrosis.

answers.name: Lithium nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic lithium causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

answers.name: Congenital anomalies of kidney and urinary tract
answers.pearl: Dysplasia, hypoplasia and posterior urethral valves are leading causes of pediatric CKD.

answers.name: Sickle cell nephropathy
answers.pearl: Medullary hypoxia from sickling causes papillary necrosis, hyposthenuria and FSGS.

answers.name: Thrombotic microangiopathy
answers.pearl: HUS, TTP and scleroderma crisis damage endothelium and cause irreversible renal injury.

answers.name: Chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Drugs such as PPIs, autoimmune disease and infection cause chronic interstitial fibrosis.

answers.name: Hyperuricemia or gouty nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic urate deposition and uric acid stones contribute to CKD.

answers.name: Scleroderma renal crisis
answers.pearl: Accelerated hypertension with AKI in systemic sclerosis, treated with ACE inhibitors.

answers.name: Hypercalcemic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic hypercalcemia causes nephrocalcinosis and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Tenofovir nephrotoxicity
answers.pearl: Proximal tubular injury causes Fanconi syndrome and progressive CKD with long-term use.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous interstitial nephritis and hypercalcemia can lead to CKD.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Lymphocytic tubulointerstitial nephritis causes distal RTA and CKD.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease of unknown etiology
answers.pearl: Agricultural workers in Central America and South Asia develop tubulointerstitial disease, possibly from heat stress and dehydration.

answers.name: Radiation nephropathy
answers.pearl: Renal radiation exposure causes delayed vascular and tubulointerstitial injury.

answers.name: Lead nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic lead exposure causes tubulointerstitial disease, hyperuricemia and hypertension.

answers.name: Light chain deposition disease
answers.pearl: Monoclonal kappa light chains deposit along basement membranes, causing nodular glomerulosclerosis.

answers.name: Nephronophthisis
answers.pearl: Autosomal recessive ciliopathy with polyuria, tubulointerstitial fibrosis and corticomedullary cysts.

answers.name: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease
