answers.pearl: Mutations in UMOD, MUC1 or REN cause bland urine and slowly progressive CKD with gout.

answers.name: Primary hyperoxaluria
answers.pearl: AGXT mutation causes oxalate stones and nephrocalcinosis, with systemic oxalosis in advanced disease.

answers.name: Cystinosis
answers.pearl: Lysosomal cystine accumulation causes renal Fanconi syndrome and progressive CKD in children.

answers.name: Alport syndrome
answers.pearl: COL4A3-5 mutations cause hematuria, sensorineural deafness and lenticonus.

answers.name: Fabry disease
answers.pearl: GLA mutation causes globotriaosylceramide accumulation, with angiokeratomas, acroparesthesias and proteinuric CKD.

answers.name: Balkan endemic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic interstitial nephritis from aristolochic acid with urothelial carcinoma risk.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of right upper quadrant pain.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hepatic infarction, Right adrenal hemorrhage, Slipping rib, ACNES (case-series level), Hemobilia and hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm, Sickle cell hepatic crisis, Biloma.

answers.name: Biliary colic
answers.pearl: Episodic postprandial RUQ pain from a gallstone transiently obstructing the cystic duct.

answers.name: Acute cholecystitis
answers.pearl: Persistent RUQ pain, fever and a positive Murphy sign from cystic duct obstruction.

answers.name: Choledocholithiasis
answers.pearl: A common bile duct stone causes pain with cholestatic liver enzymes.

answers.name: Ascending cholangitis
answers.pearl: Biliary obstruction with infection gives fever, jaundice and RUQ pain (Charcot triad).

answers.name: Hepatitis
answers.pearl: Liver inflammation of viral, alcoholic, autoimmune or drug-induced origin stretches Glisson capsule.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Epigastric pain radiating to the back can also be located in the RUQ, especially with gallstone disease.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: Duodenal or gastric ulcers can present with RUQ or epigastric pain.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Right lower lobe pneumonia can cause referred pleuritic pain to the RUQ.

answers.name: Pyelonephritis
answers.pearl: Flank or RUQ pain with fever and pyuria from an ascending infection.

answers.name: Nephrolithiasis
answers.pearl: Right renal or ureteral stone causes colicky flank pain that may radiate anteriorly.

answers.name: Appendicitis
answers.pearl: A high-lying retrocecal appendix or the gravid uterus can shift pain to the RUQ.

answers.name: GERD
answers.pearl: Reflux can cause epigastric and RUQ burning.

answers.name: Hepatic congestion
answers.pearl: Right heart failure or tricuspid regurgitation stretches the liver capsule.

answers.name: Alcoholic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Tender hepatomegaly with jaundice and fever after heavy drinking.

answers.name: Musculoskeletal pain
answers.pearl: Costochondral, muscular or rib pain can mimic visceral RUQ pain and is reproducible on palpation.

answers.name: Herpes zoster
answers.pearl: Pre-eruptive dermatomal pain at T7 to T10 can be mistaken for biliary disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Peripheral emboli with infarction cause pleuritic pain referred to the RUQ.

answers.name: Pleurisy or pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Right-sided pleural irritation causes pain on inspiration localized to the upper abdomen.

answers.name: Liver abscess
answers.pearl: Fever, RUQ pain and elevated alkaline phosphatase; pyogenic, usually from biliary or portal seeding.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis and chronic HBV or HCV predispose, and tumors can present with pain or rupture.

answers.name: Liver metastases
answers.pearl: Capsular stretch from metastatic disease, often from colorectal cancer.

answers.name: Inferior myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Inferior MI can present with epigastric or RUQ pain, nausea and vomiting.

answers.name: Acalculous cholecystitis
answers.pearl: Gallbladder inflammation without stones in critically ill patients from stasis and ischemia.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction causes RUQ pain, ascites and hepatomegaly.

answers.name: Colonic pathology
answers.pearl: Hepatic flexure diverticulitis, colitis, or constipation can localize to the RUQ.

answers.name: Biliary dyskinesia
answers.pearl: Functional gallbladder dysfunction with a low ejection fraction on HIDA.

answers.name: Portal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Acute thrombosis can cause abdominal pain, and chronic thrombosis causes portal hypertension.

answers.name: Gallbladder cancer
answers.pearl: Often found at advanced stage, associated with gallstones and porcelain gallbladder.

answers.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Biliary tract cancer with obstructive jaundice, linked to PSC and liver flukes.

answers.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: Multifocal bile duct strictures, often with IBD, causing cholestasis and episodic pain.

answers.name: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction
answers.pearl: Dysmotility of the sphincter causes biliary pain or recurrent pancreatitis, often after cholecystectomy.

answers.name: Spontaneous hepatic hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Adenoma or HCC rupture causes sudden RUQ pain and hemodynamic instability.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune destruction of small bile ducts, usually in middle-aged women with antimitochondrial antibodies.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets in late pregnancy causing RUQ or epigastric pain.

answers.name: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Third-trimester microvesicular steatosis with liver failure and hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Amebic liver abscess
answers.pearl: Entamoeba histolytica abscess in travelers or endemic areas with anchovy-paste aspirate.

answers.name: Subphrenic abscess
answers.pearl: Postoperative or perforation-related collection that irritates the diaphragm.

answers.name: Hydatid cyst
answers.pearl: Echinococcus granulosus cysts can rupture or become infected, causing RUQ pain and anaphylaxis.

answers.name: Hepatic infarction
answers.pearl: Ischemic necrosis from hepatic artery compromise, HELLP, or shock gives pain and a wedge-shaped defect.

answers.name: Sickle cell hepatic crisis
answers.pearl: Sinusoidal sickling causes RUQ pain, fever and hyperbilirubinemia.

answers.name: Right adrenal hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Anticoagulation, sepsis or antiphospholipid syndrome cause adrenal bleeding with flank or RUQ pain.

answers.name: Hemobilia
answers.pearl: Bleeding into the biliary tree causes biliary colic, GI bleeding and jaundice, typically after trauma or biopsy.

answers.name: Slipping rib syndrome
answers.pearl: Hypermobile lower ribs impinge on intercostal nerves, giving positive hooking maneuver.

answers.name: Anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome
answers.pearl: Entrapment in the abdominal wall causes focal pain with positive Carnett sign.

answers.name: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome
answers.pearl: Perihepatitis from pelvic chlamydia or gonorrhea gives RUQ pain with violin-string adhesions.

answers.name: Mirizzi syndrome
answers.pearl: A stone in the cystic duct or gallbladder neck compresses the common hepatic duct.

answers.name: Acute intermittent porphyria
answers.pearl: Severe abdominal pain with neuropathy and psychiatric symptoms triggered by drugs and fasting.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause neutropenia or agranulocytosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Amodiaquine and aminopyrine (largely historical), Mirtazapine, Olanzapine, Felbamate, Lamotrigine and Clopidogrel (rare, case-series), Colchicine overdose, Metamizole (not available in US), Rituximab late-onset neutropenia.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Cytotoxic agents suppress myeloid precursors, with nadir at 7 to 14 days.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Agranulocytosis occurs in about 1 percent, requiring REMS ANC monitoring.

answers.name: Methimazole
answers.pearl: Dose-related agranulocytosis typically in the first three months; counsel patients to report fever and sore throat.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil
answers.pearl: Idiosyncratic agranulocytosis, also with hepatotoxicity and ANCA vasculitis.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides can cause immune-mediated neutropenia, and folate antagonism adds marrow suppression.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: A folate antagonist that causes dose-related myelosuppression, worsened by renal impairment.

answers.name: Beta-lactam antibiotics
answers.pearl: Prolonged high-dose therapy such as nafcillin, piperacillin or ceftriaxone can cause neutropenia after two or more weeks.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Usually transient mild leukopenia, with rare aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Myelosuppression is dose-related and increased by TPMT deficiency or allopurinol.

answers.name: Zidovudine
answers.pearl: Bone marrow toxicity causing macrocytic anemia and neutropenia.

answers.name: Ganciclovir
answers.pearl: Dose-limiting neutropenia, more so than with foscarnet.

answers.name: Mycophenolate
answers.pearl: Leukopenia is common, particularly with higher doses.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Agranulocytosis typically in the first three months, commonly checked with CBC monitoring.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Rare hematologic effects include neutropenia and megaloblastic anemia.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Phenothiazines and other agents can rarely cause agranulocytosis, mostly in the first weeks.

answers.name: Hydroxyurea
answers.pearl: Reversible myelosuppression that is dose-limiting.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Myelosuppression occurs with prolonged courses beyond 2 weeks, usually thrombocytopenia but neutropenia can occur.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Usually thrombocytopenia but leukopenia and neutropenia are reported.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Reversible neutropenia can develop after prolonged therapy.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Interferon-alfa and peginterferon cause dose-dependent neutropenia.

answers.name: CDK4/6 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Palbociclib and ribociclib cause neutropenia by reversible cell-cycle arrest of progenitors.

answers.name: Procainamide
answers.pearl: Agranulocytosis occurs in a small fraction, often in the first 12 weeks, and drug-induced lupus is separate.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Late-onset neutropenia can appear weeks to months after treatment.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Agranulocytosis is rare but reported, in addition to hemolysis and methemoglobinemia.

answers.name: Anti-thymocyte globulin
answers.pearl: Depleting antibody therapy causes leukopenia and neutropenia.

answers.name: Tocilizumab
answers.pearl: IL-6 receptor blockade lowers neutrophil counts in a dose-related manner.

answers.name: Chloramphenicol
answers.pearl: Dose-related reversible suppression and idiosyncratic aplastic anemia.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Rare idiosyncratic agranulocytosis with agents such as diclofenac and indomethacin.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity can include marrow suppression and neutropenia.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Aurothiomalate causes immune-mediated neutropenia and aplastic anemia, rarely used now.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated marrow suppression including agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Captopril
answers.pearl: Neutropenia occurs particularly with high doses and renal impairment or collagen vascular disease.

answers.name: Alemtuzumab
answers.pearl: Profound lymphopenia and neutropenia, with prolonged infection risk.

answers.name: Mirtazapine
answers.pearl: Agranulocytosis reported rarely, with a labeled warning.

answers.name: Olanzapine
answers.pearl: Neutropenia occasionally occurs, and cross-sensitivity with clozapine is a concern.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Cytopenias including neutropenia can occur, especially in combination with methotrexate.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Rare blood dyscrasias including neutropenia are reported with 5-ASA agents.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated neutropenia or thrombocytopenia from drug-dependent antibodies.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Rare hematologic reactions including neutropenia, often within DRESS.

answers.name: Felbamate
answers.pearl: Aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis limit its use.

answers.name: Clopidogrel
answers.pearl: Neutropenia and TTP have been reported, mainly in the first months.

answers.name: Metamizole
answers.pearl: Dipyrone causes agranulocytosis, with the risk varying by region and drug availability.

answers.name: Colchicine
answers.pearl: Overdose causes bone marrow aplasia and pancytopenia; usual dosing has rare marrow effects.

answers.name: Amodiaquine
answers.pearl: Antimalarial associated with agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Aminopyrine
answers.pearl: Historical analgesic that caused the original description of drug-induced agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Levamisole-adulterated cocaine
answers.pearl: Levamisole causes neutropenia and ANCA-positive vasculitis with retiform purpura.

answers.name: Deferiprone
answers.pearl: Oral iron chelator with a boxed warning for agranulocytosis requiring weekly ANC checks.

answers.name: Ticlopidine
answers.pearl: Thienopyridine antiplatelet associated with neutropenia and TTP, limiting its use.

prompts.prompt: Name presentations or complications of diabetes mellitus.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Diabetic mastopathy and diabetic muscle infarction (case-series level), Diabetic papillopathy, Mauriac syndrome, Emphysematous cholecystitis and pyelonephritis (associations), Scleredema diabeticorum, Eruptive xanthomas (via hypertriglyceridemia), Euglycemic DKA from SGLT2 inhibitors (treatment complication).

answers.name: Polyuria
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis from glucosuria when glucose exceeds the renal threshold.

answers.name: Polydipsia
answers.pearl: Thirst driven by hyperosmolality and volume loss.

answers.name: Diabetic retinopathy
answers.pearl: Microvascular retinal disease leading to proliferative changes and macular edema.

answers.name: Diabetic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Albuminuria progressing to CKD with Kimmelstiel-Wilson lesions in advanced disease.

answers.name: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Distal symmetric sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Insulin deficiency causes ketogenesis with high anion gap acidosis, most often in type 1 diabetes.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: The most common acute treatment complication, especially with insulin and sulfonylureas.

answers.name: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
answers.pearl: Severe hyperglycemia and dehydration with altered mental status and minimal ketosis, typical in type 2 diabetes.

answers.name: Coronary artery disease
answers.pearl: Diabetes is a coronary disease equivalent, with frequent silent ischemia.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Diabetes roughly doubles the risk of ischemic stroke.

answers.name: Peripheral arterial disease
answers.pearl: Accelerated atherosclerosis of the lower limb with claudication and nonhealing ulcers.

answers.name: Diabetic foot ulcer
answers.pearl: Neuropathy and pressure with ischemia and infection lead to ulcers and amputation.

answers.name: Infections
answers.pearl: Hyperglycemia impairs neutrophil function, increasing risk of skin, urinary and fungal infections.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Hyperglycemia and volume depletion commonly cause generalized tiredness.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Catabolic state from insulin deficiency despite increased appetite.

answers.name: Cataracts
answers.pearl: Earlier and more frequent cataract formation, partly via sorbitol accumulation.

answers.name: Candidiasis
answers.pearl: Glycosuria and impaired immunity promote vulvovaginitis, balanitis and oral thrush.

answers.name: Erectile dysfunction
answers.pearl: Neuropathic and vasculogenic mechanisms impair erection.

answers.name: Gastroparesis
answers.pearl: Autonomic neuropathy delays emptying, with early satiety, nausea and erratic glycemia.

answers.name: Autonomic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Orthostatic hypotension, resting tachycardia and silent ischemia are manifestations.

answers.name: Hyperlipidemia
answers.pearl: Insulin resistance causes high triglycerides and low HDL, intensifying cardiovascular risk.

answers.name: Charcot foot
answers.pearl: Neuropathic arthropathy with destruction of midfoot architecture, resembling cellulitis or gout.

answers.name: Acanthosis nigricans
answers.pearl: Velvety hyperpigmented plaques in the neck and axilla marking insulin resistance.

answers.name: Lactic acidosis with metformin
answers.pearl: Metformin accumulation in renal failure or hypoxia can cause MALA.

answers.name: Fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: MASLD and NASH are common in type 2 diabetes and can progress to cirrhosis.

answers.name: Diabetic dermopathy
answers.pearl: Atrophic hyperpigmented shin spots from microangiopathy.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia unawareness
answers.pearl: Recurrent hypoglycemia blunts the counter-regulatory and autonomic warning response.

answers.name: Diabetic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Myocardial dysfunction independent of coronary disease and hypertension.

answers.name: Neurogenic bladder
answers.pearl: Autonomic bladder dysfunction causes retention, overflow incontinence and recurrent UTI.

answers.name: Adhesive capsulitis
answers.pearl: Frozen shoulder is notably more common in diabetes.

answers.name: Osteomyelitis
answers.pearl: Contiguous spread from foot ulcers, often with a probe-to-bone positive test.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes
answers.pearl: New-onset diabetes in older adults with weight loss can be an early sign of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

answers.name: Necrobiosis lipoidica
answers.pearl: Shiny yellow-brown atrophic plaques with telangiectasia on the shins.

answers.name: Diabetic amyotrophy
answers.pearl: Subacute asymmetric proximal leg pain and quadriceps weakness from lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy.

answers.name: Cranial nerve palsy
answers.pearl: Ischemic third nerve palsy with pupillary sparing, or sixth nerve palsy, from microvascular infarction.

answers.name: Limited joint mobility
answers.pearl: Cheiroarthropathy with a prayer sign and tight waxy skin from glycation of collagen.

answers.name: Mucormycosis
answers.pearl: Rhinocerebral infection in ketoacidosis with black eschar and facial pain.

answers.name: Malignant otitis externa
answers.pearl: Pseudomonas invasion of skull base in older diabetic patients with severe ear pain.

answers.name: Emphysematous pyelonephritis
answers.pearl: Gas-forming renal infection with E. coli or Klebsiella in poorly controlled diabetes.

answers.name: Bullosis diabeticorum
answers.pearl: Spontaneous tense painless bullae on the feet and legs without trauma.

answers.name: Fournier gangrene
answers.pearl: Necrotizing perineal infection with increased risk in diabetes, including with SGLT2 inhibitors.

answers.name: Diabetic papillopathy
answers.pearl: Self-limited optic disc swelling in young diabetics with mild visual loss.

answers.name: Diabetic muscle infarction
answers.pearl: Spontaneous painful thigh swelling from muscle ischemia, usually in long-standing poorly controlled diabetes.

answers.name: Diabetic mastopathy
answers.pearl: Fibrous breast mass in long-standing type 1 diabetes that mimics cancer.

answers.name: Euglycemic DKA with SGLT2 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose from SGLT2 inhibitors, particularly with illness or surgery.

answers.name: Wolfram syndrome
answers.pearl: DIDMOAD: diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy and deafness from WFS1.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis-related diabetes
answers.pearl: Iron deposition in the pancreas causes bronze diabetes with skin pigmentation and cirrhosis.

answers.name: Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules
answers.pearl: Nodular glomerulosclerosis, the pathognomonic lesion of diabetic nephropathy.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of thrombocytosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Familial thrombocytosis genes, MDS/MPN-RS-T naming, Pseudothrombocytosis (not true thrombocytosis), Vincristine rebound (mechanism-level), Castleman disease, Ovarian and renal cancer (association strength), Alcohol-withdrawal rebound, ALK-positive IMT.

answers.name: Infection
answers.pearl: Cytokines such as IL-6 drive thrombopoietin and platelet production in reactive thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Iron deficiency
answers.pearl: A frequent cause of mild to moderate reactive thrombocytosis that resolves with iron repletion.

answers.name: Inflammation
answers.pearl: Acute-phase reaction raises platelets, with IL-6 stimulating hepatic thrombopoietin.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Solid tumors can cause reactive thrombocytosis, which is a poor prognostic sign.

answers.name: Asplenia or splenectomy
answers.pearl: The spleen sequesters about a third of platelets, so loss raises the count, often transiently.

answers.name: Essential thrombocythemia
answers.pearl: Myeloproliferative neoplasm with JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations and thrombotic and bleeding risk.

answers.name: Acute blood loss
answers.pearl: Hemorrhage stimulates thrombopoiesis with a rebound rise days later.

answers.name: Surgery or trauma
answers.pearl: Tissue injury produces transient acute-phase thrombocytosis, usually peaking in one to two weeks.

answers.name: Polycythemia vera
answers.pearl: JAK2-positive MPN where thrombocytosis often accompanies elevated red cell mass.

answers.name: Chronic myeloid leukemia
answers.pearl: BCR-ABL positive MPN, with thrombocytosis occasionally the presenting finding.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation drives reactive thrombocytosis that tracks disease activity.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis cause thrombocytosis through inflammation and iron deficiency.

answers.name: Primary myelofibrosis
answers.pearl: Prefibrotic phase can present with thrombocytosis, mimicking essential thrombocythemia.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Hemolysis causes marrow stimulation, often with iron-deficient states.

answers.name: Rebound after thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Platelets overshoot during recovery from ITP, chemotherapy or alcohol-related suppression.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Chronic granulomatous infection causes marked reactive thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory states including pancreatitis raise platelets.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Functional asplenia from autoinfarction causes persistent thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Exercise
answers.pearl: Epinephrine-driven release of splenic and marrow platelets causes transient increase.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Paraneoplastic IL-6-mediated thrombocytosis is frequent in lung cancer.

answers.name: Colorectal cancer
answers.pearl: Thrombocytosis is a recognized sign, partly through chronic blood loss and inflammation.

answers.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation drives reactive thrombocytosis and is part of the adverse prognostic score.

answers.name: Vasculitis
answers.pearl: Large and medium vessel vasculitis cause marked acute-phase thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Hyposplenism from celiac disease and iron deficiency contribute.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 treatment
answers.pearl: Platelets overshoot when megaloblastic anemia is corrected after starting B12 or folate.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous inflammation can raise platelets.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Urinary losses and hepatic synthesis drive thrombopoietic stimulation and hypercoagulability.

answers.name: Renal cell carcinoma
answers.pearl: Paraneoplastic cytokines and thrombopoietin raise platelets.

answers.name: Ovarian cancer
answers.pearl: IL-6 and thrombopoietin production cause a poor-prognosis thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Tumor production of thrombopoietin can cause thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: Steroids and epinephrine can increase counts in some patients.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal rebound
answers.pearl: Platelets rise above baseline after cessation of chronic alcohol-induced suppression.

answers.name: Acute rheumatic fever
answers.pearl: Acute-phase response in the inflammatory phase of rheumatic fever.

answers.name: Pseudothrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Cell fragments such as schistocytes, microspherocytes, cryoglobulin or bacteria are counted as platelets by analyzers.

answers.name: Vincristine rebound
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloids can cause platelet rise after treatment, possibly by promoting megakaryocyte release.

answers.name: Castleman disease
answers.pearl: IL-6 overproduction by lymph nodes produces thrombocytosis, anemia and fever, notably in iATL and TAFRO variants.

answers.name: ATRA therapy
answers.pearl: All-trans retinoic acid for APL or other conditions can raise platelets and cause leukocytosis.

answers.name: MDS with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis
aliases: refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: A MDS/MPN overlap with SF3B1 mutation, anemia, thrombocytosis and frequent JAK2 V617F.

answers.name: Hereditary thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Germline THPO, MPL or JAK2 mutations cause familial persistent thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
answers.pearl: Tumors with ALK rearrangements produce IL-6 and thrombocytosis.

answers.name: Kawasaki disease
answers.pearl: Platelets rise in the second to third week, often exceeding 450000 and sometimes a million.

answers.name: 5q- syndrome
answers.pearl: MDS with isolated del(5q), macrocytic anemia, normal or high platelets and lenalidomide sensitivity.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of pulmonary-renal syndrome.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Penicillamine, Silica, Paraquat, Fibrillary GN, Lymphomatoid granulomatosis, Erdheim-Chester, Birt-Hogg-Dube, Relapsing polychondritis, IgG4-RD, Hydrocarbon exposure (association-level); uremic pulmonary edema and volume overload are pulmonary-renal mimics rather than true capillaritis syndromes.

answers.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: ANCA vasculitis with upper airway, lung and pauci-immune GN, often PR3-ANCA.

answers.name: Microscopic polyangiitis
answers.pearl: MPO-ANCA small vessel vasculitis with capillaritis and necrotizing GN, without granulomas.

answers.name: Anti-GBM disease
answers.pearl: Anti-GBM antibodies against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen cause DAH and rapidly progressive GN.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus nephritis with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is rare but carries high mortality.

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Asthma, eosinophilia and vasculitis with glomerulonephritis in a minority, often ANCA-negative.

answers.name: Volume overload with acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Cardiogenic or renal pulmonary edema mimics true pulmonary-renal syndrome and must be excluded.

answers.name: Sepsis with ARDS and AKI
answers.pearl: Septic multi-organ failure produces lung injury with acute tubular necrosis.

answers.name: Pneumonia with acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Severe pneumonia with sepsis-related AKI, or Legionella, can look like a pulmonary-renal process.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
answers.pearl: Immune complex vasculitis, usually from hepatitis C, with MPGN and occasionally alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: IgA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Henoch-Schonlein purpura with GN and, rarely in adults, alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Immune complex GN and septic pulmonary emboli in right-sided disease.

answers.name: Uremic lung
answers.pearl: Uremia causes increased capillary permeability with pulmonary edema and pleural effusion.

answers.name: Systemic sclerosis
answers.pearl: Scleroderma renal crisis with ILD, and rarely alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis vasculitis
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid vasculitis, ILD and rheumatoid nodules with immune complex GN are rare.

answers.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome
answers.pearl: Catastrophic APS causes pulmonary hemorrhage or ARDS with renal thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil-induced ANCA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Antithyroid drug can induce MPO-ANCA vasculitis with DAH and GN.

answers.name: Hydralazine-induced ANCA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Hydralazine causes MPO-ANCA vasculitis, often with lupus-like features.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome with pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Renal vein thrombosis and hypercoagulability cause PE and flank pain with renal dysfunction.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous interstitial nephritis with parenchymal lung involvement.

answers.name: Mixed connective tissue disease
answers.pearl: Overlap syndrome with anti-U1 RNP, ILD, and occasional membranous nephropathy.

answers.name: Levamisole-adulterated cocaine vasculitis
answers.pearl: Levamisole induces ANCA-positive (often both PR3 and MPO) vasculitis, retiform purpura and occasional DAH.

answers.name: Double-positive ANCA and anti-GBM disease
answers.pearl: About 10 to 40 percent of anti-GBM patients also have ANCA, with mixed features and relapses.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Interstitial nephritis and lymphocytic lung disease or rare capillaritis.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Falciparum malaria can cause ARDS with AKI, a pulmonary-renal presentation in travelers.

answers.name: Drug-induced interstitial nephritis with pulmonary eosinophilia
answers.pearl: Nitrofurantoin, sulfonamides and others can cause hypersensitivity lung and kidney disease together.

answers.name: Minocycline-induced ANCA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Rare drug-induced p-ANCA vasculitis with lung and kidney involvement.

answers.name: Primary amyloidosis
answers.pearl: AL amyloid involves kidney and lung parenchyma, and alveolar-septal deposits can cause alveolar hemorrhage rarely.

answers.name: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
answers.pearl: Thrombotic microangiopathy with AKI, and ARDS or pulmonary hemorrhage in severe cases.

answers.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex with LAM
answers.pearl: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis cysts and angiomyolipomas affect lungs and kidneys; AML hemorrhage can cause shock.

answers.name: D-penicillamine-induced Goodpasture-like syndrome
answers.pearl: Penicillamine can produce an anti-GBM-like pulmonary-renal syndrome and membranous nephropathy.

answers.name: Fibrillary glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Congo red negative fibrils with DNAJB9 positivity; rare reports of pulmonary hemorrhage.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: Tubulointerstitial nephritis and lung or mediastinal fibro-inflammatory lesions.

answers.name: Relapsing polychondritis
answers.pearl: Airway cartilage inflammation with ANCA-associated GN in some patients.

answers.name: Silica exposure
answers.pearl: Silica associates with ANCA vasculitis, silicosis and glomerulonephritis.

answers.name: Hydrocarbon solvent exposure
answers.pearl: Solvent inhalation is linked to anti-GBM disease onset and relapse.

answers.name: Paraquat poisoning
answers.pearl: Herbicide ingestion causes rapidly progressive pulmonary fibrosis with AKI.

answers.name: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
answers.pearl: EBV-driven lymphoproliferative disorder with pulmonary nodules and rare renal involvement.

answers.name: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome
answers.pearl: FLCN mutation causes pulmonary cysts with spontaneous pneumothorax and renal tumors.

answers.name: Erdheim-Chester disease
answers.pearl: Non-Langerhans histiocytosis with perirenal fibrosis ("hairy kidney") and pulmonary fibrosis.

answers.name: Hantavirus infection
answers.pearl: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome form two ends of the same infection.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Weil disease with jaundice, AKI and pulmonary hemorrhage, treated with penicillin or doxycycline.

answers.name: Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Variable vessel vasculitis with pulmonary artery aneurysms that can rupture and with renal amyloidosis or GN.

answers.name: Legionella pneumonia
answers.pearl: Legionnaires disease causes pneumonia with AKI from rhabdomyolysis or interstitial nephritis.

answers.name: ANCA-associated interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: MPO-ANCA vasculitis frequently presents with pulmonary fibrosis (UIP) and GN.

answers.name: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis
answers.pearl: Anti-C1q syndrome with urticaria, COPD-like lung disease and GN.

answers.name: Sickle cell acute chest syndrome with AKI
aliases: sickle cell crisis with multiorgan failure
answers.pearl: Multiorgan sickle crisis can mimic a pulmonary-renal process.

answers.name: Rickettsial infection
answers.pearl: Scrub typhus and spotted fevers cause ARDS with AKI and vasculitis.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: Severe disease causes ARDS with AKI and occasionally alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Volume overload with pulmonary edema can accompany acute nephritic syndrome.

answers.name: Methotrexate toxicity
answers.pearl: Methotrexate can cause pneumonitis and crystal or tubular AKI.

answers.name: TNF inhibitor-induced vasculitis
answers.pearl: Anti-TNF agents can induce ANCA-positive or lupus-like vasculitis with lung and kidney disease.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Schistosoma causes immune complex glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Infection-related glomerulonephritis with pneumonia
answers.pearl: Staphylococcal and other infection-associated GN can coexist with lung infection and look like a vasculitis.

answers.name: Lung cancer with paraneoplastic glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Membranous nephropathy and other GN are associated with lung carcinoma.

answers.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic infiltration can involve lung and kidney.

answers.name: Pickering syndrome
aliases: flash pulmonary edema with renal artery stenosis
bilateral renal artery stenosis with flash pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Bilateral renal artery stenosis causing recurrent flash pulmonary edema and renal dysfunction.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hemoptysis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pulmonary vein stenosis after AF ablation, Amyloidosis (tracheobronchial), Leptospirosis, Pulmonary endometriosis, Dieulafoy bronchial lesion (case-report level); Takayasu arteritis and Behcet/Hughes-Stovin (uncommon). Goodpasture, HHT and Rasmussen aneurysm scored as board traps.

answers.name: Acute bronchitis
answers.pearl: Self-limited airway inflammation, usually viral, that causes streaky blood-tinged sputum.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Alveolar infection with inflammation can produce rust-colored or blood-streaked sputum.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Bronchogenic carcinoma is the key cause to exclude in a smoker with recurrent hemoptysis.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Chronically dilated, inflamed bronchi with hypertrophied bronchial arteries cause recurrent, sometimes massive bleeding.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Cavitary TB causes hemoptysis from active disease or from sequelae such as bronchiectasis and aspergilloma.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Pulmonary infarction from a peripheral embolus can cause hemoptysis with pleuritic pain.

answers.name: COPD exacerbation
answers.pearl: Airway inflammation and bronchitis in COPD frequently cause blood-streaked sputum, but new hemoptysis in a smoker still warrants imaging.

answers.name: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy
answers.pearl: Bleeding drugs unmask an underlying lesion and also raise the risk of alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Bronchiectasis with chronic infection in CF can cause life-threatening hemoptysis from hypertrophied bronchial arteries.

answers.name: Mitral stenosis
answers.pearl: Raised left atrial pressure ruptures engorged bronchial veins, causing hemoptysis.

answers.name: Pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Frothy pink sputum from left heart failure reflects blood-tinged alveolar fluid.

answers.name: Lung abscess
answers.pearl: Necrotic cavitary infection, often from aspiration, erodes vessels and causes bleeding.

answers.name: Aspergilloma
answers.pearl: A fungus ball in an old cavity (often post-TB) causes recurrent, sometimes massive hemoptysis from adjacent bronchial arteries.

answers.name: Foreign body aspiration
answers.pearl: A retained airway foreign body causes local mucosal injury and bleeding.

answers.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: ANCA vasculitis causing cavitary nodules or capillaritis with alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Chest trauma
answers.pearl: Pulmonary contusion or airway injury causes hemoptysis after blunt or penetrating trauma.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Bleeding from alveolar capillaries, from vasculitis, lupus, or drugs, presents with hemoptysis, anemia, and infiltrates.

answers.name: Metastatic cancer to the lung
answers.pearl: Endobronchial metastases (for example from renal cell carcinoma, melanoma, or colon) can bleed.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus can cause diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with high mortality, often in the setting of nephritis.

answers.name: Microscopic polyangiitis
answers.pearl: ANCA (MPO) vasculitis with pulmonary-renal syndrome and capillaritis.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Rupture of dilated bronchial or pulmonary arteries, as in Eisenmenger syndrome, can cause fatal hemoptysis.

answers.name: Crack cocaine inhalation
answers.pearl: Alveolar injury and hemorrhage after smoking crack cocaine.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Endemic fungal disease with cavitary or fibrosing mediastinitis changes that can cause bleeding.

answers.name: Bronchial carcinoid
answers.pearl: A vascular endobronchial neuroendocrine tumor can cause recurrent hemoptysis and postobstructive pneumonia.

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: ANCA vasculitis with asthma and eosinophilia; alveolar hemorrhage is uncommon but described.

answers.name: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
answers.pearl: Cavitary or bronchiectatic MAC disease, typically in older women, can cause hemoptysis.

answers.name: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
answers.pearl: Abnormal pulmonary AV connections can rupture into airway or pleura.

answers.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
answers.pearl: HHT causes pulmonary AVMs that bleed, and recurrent epistaxis is the classic clue.

answers.name: Goodpasture syndrome
answers.pearl: Anti-GBM disease causes pulmonary hemorrhage with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, mostly in smokers.

answers.name: Rasmussen aneurysm
answers.pearl: A pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm in a tuberculous cavity that can rupture and cause massive hemoptysis.

answers.name: Vaping-associated lung injury
answers.pearl: EVALI can present with cough, infiltrates, and occasionally hemoptysis or alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Fungal pneumonia (coccidioidomycosis or blastomycosis)
answers.pearl: Endemic fungi cause cavitary or nodular lung disease that may bleed.

answers.name: Pulmonary infarction from septic emboli
answers.pearl: Septic emboli from right-sided endocarditis or Lemierre syndrome cause cavitating nodules with hemoptysis.

answers.name: Anti-VEGF therapy
answers.pearl: Bevacizumab (especially with squamous tumors near large vessels) is associated with pulmonary hemorrhage.

answers.name: Kaposi sarcoma
answers.pearl: Endobronchial or parenchymal Kaposi lesions in advanced HIV can bleed.

answers.name: Pulmonary artery catheter injury
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery rupture from balloon inflation or a distally wedged catheter causes sudden hemoptysis.

answers.name: Aortobronchial fistula
answers.pearl: A thoracic aneurysm or graft eroding into the airway causes a herald bleed followed by massive hemorrhage.

answers.name: Broncholithiasis
answers.pearl: Calcified peribronchial nodes (from TB or histoplasmosis) erode into the airway and cause hemoptysis and lithoptysis.

answers.name: Pulmonary vein stenosis
answers.pearl: Stenosis after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation causes venous hypertension with hemoptysis.

answers.name: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
answers.pearl: Recurrent alveolar hemorrhage without a systemic cause, mostly in children, with iron-laden macrophages.

answers.name: Paragonimiasis
answers.pearl: Lung fluke infection from raw freshwater crab or crayfish causes chronic rusty-brown hemoptysis that mimics TB.

answers.name: Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery aneurysms (Hughes-Stovin) in Behcet can rupture and cause fatal hemoptysis.

answers.name: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
answers.pearl: Cystic lung disease in women of reproductive age that can cause hemoptysis along with pneumothorax and chylous effusion.

answers.name: Hydatid cyst rupture
answers.pearl: Echinococcal lung cysts that rupture into a bronchus cause hemoptysis with cystic fluid expectoration.

answers.name: Tracheobronchial amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposits in the airway are friable and bleed.

answers.name: Pulmonary endometriosis
answers.pearl: Catamenial hemoptysis recurring with menses from ectopic endometrial tissue in the lung or airway.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Severe icteric leptospirosis can cause hemorrhagic pneumonitis with hemoptysis (Weil disease).

answers.name: Takayasu arteritis
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery involvement in Takayasu can cause hemoptysis from vascular lesions.

answers.name: Dieulafoy lesion of the bronchus
answers.pearl: An abnormal submucosal bronchial artery protrudes through the mucosa and bleeds; rare, diagnosed at bronchoscopy.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can raise blood pressure.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mirabegron (small average increase, label warning), Dexmedetomidine bolus (transient), Abiraterone (via mineralocorticoid excess), Carbenoxolone (withdrawn in many countries), Phenylpropanolamine (withdrawn), Oxymetazoline (systemic absorption). Licorice (a substance, not a drug), MAOI with tyramine and clonidine withdrawal scored as board traps.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Prostaglandin inhibition causes sodium retention and blunts the effect of most antihypertensives.

answers.name: Pseudoephedrine
answers.pearl: An oral alpha-agonist decongestant that raises blood pressure and heart rate.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids cause sodium and water retention and mineralocorticoid effects.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen increases hepatic angiotensinogen, causing small and occasionally significant pressure rises.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Chronic heavy intake raises blood pressure, and withdrawal produces sympathetic surges.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Sympathomimetic with intense vasoconstriction, causing hypertensive emergencies and aortic dissection.

answers.name: Amphetamines
answers.pearl: Release of catecholamines raises blood pressure and heart rate.

answers.name: Caffeine
answers.pearl: Acute adenosine antagonism briefly raises blood pressure, especially in nonhabitual users.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitor causing renal vasoconstriction and sodium retention.

answers.name: Epinephrine
answers.pearl: Direct alpha and beta agonist that raises blood pressure.

answers.name: Phenylephrine
answers.pearl: Pure alpha-1 agonist, present in oral and topical decongestants and given as a vasopressor.

answers.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
answers.pearl: Epoetin and darbepoetin raise blood pressure, particularly in CKD, through increased viscosity and vasoconstriction.

answers.name: Venlafaxine
answers.pearl: An SNRI that raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent manner.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitor with a somewhat lower hypertension rate than cyclosporine.

answers.name: Anabolic steroids
answers.pearl: Androgens cause fluid retention, erythrocytosis, and dyslipidemia that elevate blood pressure.

answers.name: Fludrocortisone
answers.pearl: A mineralocorticoid causing sodium retention and supine hypertension.

answers.name: Midodrine
answers.pearl: An alpha-1 agonist used for orthostatic hypotension that causes supine hypertension.

answers.name: VEGF pathway inhibitors
answers.pearl: Bevacizumab and similar agents cause hypertension through reduced nitric oxide and capillary rarefaction.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sunitinib, sorafenib, pazopanib, lenvatinib and axitinib cause frequent dose-related hypertension.

answers.name: Bupropion
answers.pearl: Noradrenergic and dopaminergic effects can raise blood pressure, especially in combination with nicotine patches.

answers.name: Atomoxetine
answers.pearl: A norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used for ADHD that increases blood pressure and heart rate.

answers.name: Levothyroxine overdose
answers.pearl: Excess thyroid hormone raises systolic pressure and cardiac output.

answers.name: Ephedra
answers.pearl: Ephedrine alkaloids in supplements cause hypertension and were banned by the FDA for this reason.

answers.name: Triptans
answers.pearl: Vasoconstrictors that cause transient rises in blood pressure.

answers.name: Ibrutinib
answers.pearl: BTK inhibitor with a high rate of new or worsened hypertension and atrial fibrillation.

answers.name: Ergot alkaloids
answers.pearl: Ergotamine and dihydroergotamine cause vasoconstriction and hypertension.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Weak MAO inhibition with sympathomimetics or tyramine can cause hypertensive reactions.

answers.name: Ketamine
answers.pearl: Sympathomimetic effects raise blood pressure and heart rate.

answers.name: Abiraterone
answers.pearl: CYP17 inhibition causes ACTH-driven mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Ponatinib
answers.pearl: BCR-ABL TKI with a notable rate of hypertension and arterial thrombosis.

answers.name: Dexmedetomidine
answers.pearl: Rapid loading doses can cause transient hypertension through peripheral alpha-2B vasoconstriction.

answers.name: Mirabegron
answers.pearl: A beta-3 agonist for overactive bladder with a modest blood pressure increase.

answers.name: Synthetic cathinones
answers.pearl: Bath salts cause amphetamine-like sympathomimetic hypertension.

answers.name: Oxymetazoline
answers.pearl: Topical decongestant that can raise blood pressure through systemic absorption.

answers.name: Carbenoxolone
answers.pearl: An 11-beta-HSD inhibitor given for ulcers that causes mineralocorticoid-like hypertension.

answers.name: Phenylpropanolamine
answers.pearl: Withdrawn decongestant and appetite suppressant linked to hypertensive crisis and hemorrhagic stroke.

answers.name: Licorice
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhizic acid blocks 11-beta-HSD2, causing pseudohyperaldosteronism with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Tyramine with a MAO inhibitor
answers.pearl: Aged cheese with a nonselective MAOI causes catecholamine release and hypertensive crisis.

answers.name: Clonidine withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation causes rebound sympathetic surge and hypertensive crisis.

answers.name: Norepinephrine
answers.pearl: A vasopressor that causes vasoconstriction through alpha-1 receptors.

answers.name: Modafinil
answers.pearl: A wakefulness-promoting drug with a modest blood pressure elevation.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Hypertension is a known adverse effect of this DMARD.

answers.name: Yohimbine
answers.pearl: An alpha-2 antagonist that increases sympathetic outflow and blood pressure.

answers.name: Droxidopa
answers.pearl: A norepinephrine prodrug that causes supine hypertension.

answers.name: Sibutramine
answers.pearl: Withdrawn weight-loss drug that raised blood pressure and heart rate and increased cardiovascular events.

prompts.prompt: Name complications or manifestations of chronic kidney disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hyperhomocysteinemia (common but not clearly causal), Uremic lung (radiographic descriptor), Hypermagnesemia (mainly advanced CKD), Hiccups (uremic), Taste disturbance, Acquired cystic kidney disease with RCC (mainly in long-term dialysis). Calciphylaxis, nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and dialysis-related amyloidosis scored as board traps.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Reduced erythropoietin production causes normocytic anemia that appears as GFR falls below about 60.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Sodium retention and RAAS activation make hypertension both a cause and a consequence of CKD.

answers.name: Hyperkalemia
answers.pearl: Reduced potassium excretion, worsened by ACE inhibitors, acidosis and diet.

answers.name: Metabolic acidosis
answers.pearl: Impaired ammonia and acid excretion causes a low bicarbonate and accelerates bone loss and muscle wasting.

answers.name: Hyperphosphatemia
answers.pearl: Reduced phosphate excretion drives FGF23 and PTH elevation.

answers.name: Secondary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Low calcitriol, hypocalcemia and phosphate retention stimulate the parathyroid glands.

answers.name: Volume overload
answers.pearl: Sodium and water retention cause edema, pulmonary congestion and resistant hypertension.

answers.name: Hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Reduced calcitriol production and phosphate retention lower serum calcium.

answers.name: Uremia
answers.pearl: Retained nitrogenous waste causes nausea, anorexia, malaise and encephalopathy.

answers.name: Cardiovascular disease
answers.pearl: CKD is a major cardiovascular risk equivalent, and patients are more likely to die of cardiovascular disease than reach dialysis.

answers.name: Proteinuria
answers.pearl: Albuminuria both marks kidney damage and drives progression.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Anemia, uremia and sleep disturbance contribute to a very high symptom burden.

answers.name: Renal osteodystrophy
answers.pearl: Bone disease from CKD-mineral bone disorder, including high- and low-turnover forms.

answers.name: Uremic pruritus
answers.pearl: Itch related to uremic toxins, inflammation and opioid receptor imbalance, treated with difelikefalin.

answers.name: Dyslipidemia
answers.pearl: Hypertriglyceridemia and low HDL are typical, and statins are used to reduce events.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Uremic toxin accumulation causes anorexia and nausea.

answers.name: Uremic pericarditis
answers.pearl: An indication for urgent dialysis, presenting with a friction rub and pericardial effusion.

answers.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
answers.pearl: Pressure and volume overload, anemia and hyperphosphatemia remodel the left ventricle.

answers.name: Uremic platelet dysfunction
answers.pearl: Impaired platelet adhesion causes bleeding that responds to desmopressin or dialysis.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Loss of renal 1-alpha hydroxylase reduces calcitriol.

answers.name: Protein-energy wasting
answers.pearl: Inflammation, acidosis, anorexia and dietary restriction cause muscle and fat loss.

answers.name: Restless legs syndrome
answers.pearl: More frequent in CKD, linked to iron deficiency, uremia and neuropathy.

answers.name: Insomnia
answers.pearl: Sleep apnea, restless legs and pruritus all disrupt sleep.

answers.name: Uremic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Distal symmetric sensorimotor neuropathy from retained toxins in advanced CKD.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression is common and linked to worse outcomes in CKD.

answers.name: Infection risk
answers.pearl: Uremia impairs neutrophil and lymphocyte function and lowers vaccine response.

answers.name: Sexual dysfunction
answers.pearl: Erectile dysfunction and decreased libido from hormonal and vascular changes.

answers.name: Gout
answers.pearl: Reduced urate excretion causes hyperuricemia, though gout is less common than expected.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: From volume overload, uremic pleuritis, or heart failure.

answers.name: Uremic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Confusion, asterixis, myoclonus and seizures from uremic toxins.

answers.name: Vascular calcification
answers.pearl: Phosphate and calcium overload drive vascular smooth muscle osteogenic change and arterial stiffness.

answers.name: Cognitive impairment
answers.pearl: Vascular disease, uremia and anemia contribute to cognitive decline.

answers.name: Bone fractures
answers.pearl: Altered bone turnover and mineralization raise fracture risk.

answers.name: Muscle cramps
answers.pearl: Common, especially during dialysis, related to shifts in volume and electrolytes.

answers.name: Menstrual disorders
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis disruption causes amenorrhea and infertility.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Impaired free-water excretion leads to dilutional hyponatremia in advanced CKD.

answers.name: Insulin clearance reduction
answers.pearl: Reduced renal insulin degradation increases hypoglycemia risk in diabetic patients.

answers.name: Dysgeusia
answers.pearl: Metallic or altered taste from uremic toxins and urea breakdown in saliva.

answers.name: Hypermagnesemia
answers.pearl: Reduced magnesium excretion in advanced CKD, worsened by antacids and laxatives.

answers.name: Adynamic bone disease
answers.pearl: Low-turnover bone disease from oversuppressed PTH or aluminum.

answers.name: Hiccups
answers.pearl: Intractable hiccups can be a manifestation of uremia.

answers.name: Acquired cystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Cystic transformation of kidneys in long-standing CKD or dialysis, with an increased risk of renal cell carcinoma.

answers.name: Hyperhomocysteinemia
answers.pearl: Reduced renal clearance raises homocysteine, a marker associated with vascular risk.

answers.name: Uremic frost
answers.pearl: Crystalline urea deposits on the skin from extreme azotemia, now rarely seen.

answers.name: Calciphylaxis
answers.pearl: Painful skin necrosis from calcification of small vessels, mostly in dialysis patients.

answers.name: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Gadolinium exposure in advanced CKD causes skin and organ fibrosis.

answers.name: Dialysis-related amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Beta-2 microglobulin deposition causing carpal tunnel and destructive arthropathy after years of dialysis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hermansky-Pudlak (case series), SFTPC/SFTPA surfactant mutations, Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis, Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis, Gaucher/Niemann-Pick (rare infiltrative), Ankylosing spondylitis (apical fibrosis, uncommon), GERD/microaspiration (association rather than proven cause), Hard metal lung. Berylliosis, Hamman-Rich/AIP and pulmonary alveolar proteinosis scored as board traps.

answers.name: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
answers.pearl: Progressive fibrosing ILD with a UIP pattern of basal, subpleural honeycombing in older adults.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Noncaseating granulomas cause upper-lobe fibrosis in some stage IV patients.

answers.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Immune reaction to inhaled organic antigens (bird, mold, hot tub) with upper and mid lung predominance.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: RA-ILD is often UIP pattern and may precede joint disease.

answers.name: Systemic sclerosis
answers.pearl: Scleroderma ILD is typically NSIP and is the leading cause of death in the disease.

answers.name: Asbestosis
answers.pearl: Inhaled asbestos fibers cause lower-lobe fibrosis with pleural plaques after a latency of decades.

answers.name: Amiodarone toxicity
answers.pearl: Dose-related pneumonitis with high-attenuation lung changes from the iodinated drug.

answers.name: Silicosis
answers.pearl: Inhaled crystalline silica causes upper-lobe nodules and eggshell hilar node calcification.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis-like reaction that can occur at any time and at low doses.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Chronic use causes subacute fibrosing pneumonitis, mainly in older women.

answers.name: Radiation pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Subacute inflammation within the radiation field, followed by fibrosis.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: Chemotherapy-induced pneumonitis that is dose-related and worsened by high oxygen.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus pneumonitis or chronic ILD is less common than pleuritis.

answers.name: Coal workers pneumoconiosis
answers.pearl: Coal dust causes macules and nodules with progressive massive fibrosis in upper zones.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Lymphocytic or NSIP-type ILD can complicate Sjogren, sometimes with lymphoma.

answers.name: Dermatomyositis or polymyositis
answers.pearl: Myositis-associated ILD, especially with antisynthetase antibodies, may precede muscle weakness.

answers.name: Antisynthetase syndrome
answers.pearl: Anti-Jo-1 and related antibodies with ILD, myositis, mechanic's hands, and Raynaud phenomenon.

answers.name: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
answers.pearl: Uniform ground-glass and reticulation with better prognosis than UIP, often tied to connective tissue disease.

answers.name: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
answers.pearl: Patchy, migratory consolidations that respond to steroids, also called BOOP.

answers.name: Smoking-related ILD
answers.pearl: Respiratory bronchiolitis-ILD and desquamative interstitial pneumonia occur in smokers.

answers.name: Mixed connective tissue disease
answers.pearl: Overlap syndrome with anti-U1 RNP antibodies that can cause ILD.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis
answers.pearl: PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors cause steroid-responsive pneumonitis.

answers.name: Post-COVID-19 fibrosis
answers.pearl: Persistent fibrotic changes can follow severe COVID-19 pneumonia and ARDS.

answers.name: Eosinophilic pneumonia
answers.pearl: Acute or chronic eosinophilic infiltrates; drugs, parasites and fungi are triggers.

answers.name: Chronic aspiration
answers.pearl: Recurrent microaspiration causes bronchiolitis and fibrosis.

answers.name: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
answers.pearl: Smoking-related cystic and nodular upper-lobe disease sparing the costophrenic angles.

answers.name: Microscopic polyangiitis
answers.pearl: ANCA-associated vasculitis can cause pulmonary fibrosis, often UIP-like, before or with renal disease.

answers.name: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
answers.pearl: Tumor in pulmonary lymphatics produces thickened septa and a mimic of ILD.

answers.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
answers.pearl: Surfactant accumulates in alveoli, with crazy-paving on CT and milky lavage fluid; often anti-GM-CSF antibodies.

answers.name: Berylliosis
answers.pearl: Chronic beryllium disease mimics sarcoidosis, with a positive beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test.

answers.name: Acute interstitial pneumonia
answers.pearl: Fulminant idiopathic diffuse alveolar damage resembling ARDS, historically the Hamman-Rich syndrome.

answers.name: Lymphoid interstitial pneumonia
answers.pearl: Polyclonal lymphoid infiltrate associated with Sjogren, HIV, and common variable immunodeficiency.

answers.name: Ankylosing spondylitis
answers.pearl: Apical fibrosis can mimic tuberculosis.

answers.name: Busulfan lung
answers.pearl: An alkylating agent causing delayed pneumonitis and fibrosis.

answers.name: Familial pulmonary fibrosis
answers.pearl: Telomerase (TERT, TERC) and related gene mutations underlie familial and short-telomere disease.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Ulcerative colitis and Crohn can be associated with ILD, bronchiectasis and drug-induced pneumonitis.

answers.name: Hard metal lung disease
answers.pearl: Cobalt exposure in tungsten carbide workers causes giant-cell interstitial pneumonia.

answers.name: IV talc granulomatosis
answers.pearl: Injection of crushed oral tablets causes talc granulomas and fibrosis.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: Lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates with fibrosis can involve lung, pleura and mediastinum.

answers.name: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis
answers.pearl: Upper-lobe pleural and subpleural fibroelastosis, often after transplant or chemotherapy.

answers.name: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome
answers.pearl: Oculocutaneous albinism with platelet dysfunction and a fibrosing interstitial pneumonia, typically HPS-1.

answers.name: Surfactant protein gene mutations
answers.pearl: SFTPC and related gene variants cause familial ILD in children and adults.

answers.name: Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis
answers.pearl: Autosomal recessive SLC34A2 mutation causes diffuse sandlike calcifications.

answers.name: Gaucher disease
answers.pearl: Lysosomal storage disease with pulmonary infiltration and pulmonary hypertension in rare cases.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of dysphagia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy, Lambert-Eaton, Esophageal lichen planus and pemphigus, Rabies, Esophageal tuberculosis, Dysphagia aortica, Paraneoplastic achalasia, Hypothyroid myopathy, Left atrial enlargement (rare, well-described). Plummer-Vinson, Chagas disease and Zenker diverticulum scored as board traps.

answers.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
answers.pearl: Chronic reflux causes esophagitis and peptic strictures that lead to progressive solid-food dysphagia.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Brainstem or hemispheric strokes cause oropharyngeal dysphagia with aspiration risk.

answers.name: Esophageal cancer
answers.pearl: Progressive solid-food dysphagia with weight loss suggests adenocarcinoma or squamous carcinoma.

answers.name: Achalasia
answers.pearl: Failure of LES relaxation and loss of peristalsis cause solid and liquid dysphagia, with a bird's-beak on barium.

answers.name: Eosinophilic esophagitis
answers.pearl: Allergic esophagitis in young atopic men presenting with food impaction and rings on endoscopy.

answers.name: Esophageal stricture
answers.pearl: Fibrotic narrowing from reflux, caustics, radiation or prolonged tube use.

answers.name: Candida esophagitis
answers.pearl: Odynophagia with white plaques in immunocompromised patients or those using inhaled steroids.

answers.name: Parkinson disease
answers.pearl: Bradykinesia of oropharyngeal muscles causes aspiration and delayed swallowing.

answers.name: Dementia
answers.pearl: Loss of swallowing initiation and coordination in advanced neurodegenerative disease.

answers.name: Head and neck cancer
answers.pearl: Oropharyngeal, laryngeal and hypopharyngeal tumors obstruct or impair swallowing.

answers.name: Food bolus impaction
answers.pearl: Often due to eosinophilic esophagitis, rings, strictures or poor dentition.

answers.name: Schatzki ring
answers.pearl: A lower esophageal mucosal ring producing intermittent solid-food dysphagia.

answers.name: Pill esophagitis
answers.pearl: Doxycycline, bisphosphonates, potassium chloride, NSAIDs and iron cause ulcers when taken without enough water.

answers.name: Scleroderma
answers.pearl: Smooth muscle atrophy causes aperistalsis with a patulous LES and severe reflux.

answers.name: Myasthenia gravis
answers.pearl: Fatigable bulbar weakness causing dysphagia that worsens with repeated swallowing.

answers.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
answers.pearl: Bulbar-onset ALS causes progressive dysphagia and dysarthria.

answers.name: Radiation esophagitis
answers.pearl: Radiation to the chest or neck causes acute mucositis and late strictures.

answers.name: Diffuse esophageal spasm
answers.pearl: Intermittent chest pain and dysphagia with a corkscrew esophagus on barium.

answers.name: Thyroid goiter
answers.pearl: A large goiter extrinsically compresses the esophagus.

answers.name: Peritonsillar or retropharyngeal abscess
answers.pearl: Deep neck infections cause odynophagia, trismus and a muffled voice.

answers.name: Mediastinal mass
answers.pearl: Lymphadenopathy or tumor extrinsically compress the esophagus.

answers.name: Caustic ingestion
answers.pearl: Lye or acid ingestion causes strictures weeks later.

answers.name: Viral esophagitis
answers.pearl: HSV or CMV cause well-circumscribed ulcers with odynophagia in immunocompromised patients.

answers.name: Multiple sclerosis
answers.pearl: Brainstem and cranial nerve involvement impair the oropharyngeal phase.

answers.name: Xerostomia
answers.pearl: Dry mouth from Sjogren syndrome, anticholinergics or radiation impairs bolus formation.

answers.name: Jackhammer esophagus
answers.pearl: Hypercontractile peristalsis causing chest pain and dysphagia.

answers.name: Polymyositis or dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory myopathy involving striated pharyngeal muscle, with poor prognosis for aspiration.

answers.name: Esophageal diverticulum
answers.pearl: Epiphrenic or midesophageal diverticula can trap food and cause dysphagia.

answers.name: Botulism
answers.pearl: Descending paralysis from toxin with bulbar signs, including dysphagia and diplopia.

answers.name: Cricopharyngeal dysfunction
answers.pearl: Failure of upper esophageal sphincter relaxation causes cervical dysphagia and a cricopharyngeal bar.

answers.name: Cervical osteophytes
answers.pearl: Anterior cervical spine osteophytes or DISH can compress the pharynx.

answers.name: Guillain-Barre syndrome
answers.pearl: Cranial nerve variants cause bulbar weakness and aspiration.

answers.name: Left atrial enlargement
answers.pearl: Marked enlargement from mitral stenosis can compress the esophagus (cardiovocal and dysphagia).

answers.name: Vocal cord paralysis
answers.pearl: Impaired laryngeal closure leads to aspiration and cough on swallowing.

answers.name: Pseudoachalasia
answers.pearl: Gastric or other malignancy at the cardia mimics idiopathic achalasia, usually with rapid onset and weight loss.

answers.name: Inclusion body myositis
answers.pearl: Pharyngeal weakness is common and a major cause of dysphagia in older patients.

answers.name: Dysphagia aortica
answers.pearl: An ectatic or aneurysmal thoracic aorta compresses the esophagus.

answers.name: Lambert-Eaton syndrome
answers.pearl: Presynaptic calcium channel autoimmunity with proximal weakness and, uncommonly, bulbar and autonomic symptoms.

answers.name: Esophageal lichen planus
answers.pearl: Erosive lichen planus causes strictures, mostly in women with oral disease.

answers.name: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy
answers.pearl: PABPN1 repeat disorder with ptosis and progressive dysphagia in midlife.

answers.name: Paraneoplastic achalasia
answers.pearl: Anti-neuronal antibodies (anti-Hu, ANNA-1) with small cell lung cancer destroy myenteric neurons.

answers.name: Rabies
answers.pearl: Hydrophobia results from painful pharyngeal spasm triggered by drinking.

answers.name: Esophageal pemphigus
answers.pearl: Pemphigus vulgaris can involve the esophageal mucosa and cause desquamation.

answers.name: Plummer-Vinson syndrome
answers.pearl: Iron-deficiency anemia, esophageal web, and dysphagia in middle-aged women, with squamous cancer risk.

answers.name: Chagas disease
answers.pearl: Trypanosoma cruzi destroys myenteric neurons, producing secondary achalasia and megaesophagus.

answers.name: Zenker diverticulum
answers.pearl: A pharyngoesophageal pulsion diverticulum causes regurgitation of undigested food and halitosis.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause peripheral neuropathy.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Misonidazole (investigational radiosensitizer), Perhexiline (limited availability), Podophyllin, Suramin, Colchicine (neuromyopathy, mainly with renal impairment), Allopurinol (rare), Statins (weak association), Ixabepilone, Eribulin. Dapsone, Disulfiram and Pyridoxine excess scored as board traps.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Causes pyridoxine-deficiency sensory neuropathy by interfering with B6 metabolism, especially in slow acetylators; give pyridoxine prophylaxis.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Prolonged courses (typically above 42 g total) cause sensory axonal neuropathy.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloid causing dose-limiting sensorimotor and autonomic neuropathy, including constipation and jaw pain.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum drug causing a dorsal root ganglionopathy with large-fiber sensory loss and ototoxicity.

answers.name: Paclitaxel
answers.pearl: Taxane causing painful, length-dependent sensory neuropathy through microtubule stabilization.

answers.name: Oxaliplatin
answers.pearl: Causes acute cold-triggered paresthesias and a cumulative sensory neuropathy.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Neuropathy risk is highest with renal impairment and longer courses.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Chronic therapy causes demyelinating or axonal neuropathy and tremor.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: FDA warns of persistent peripheral neuropathy with ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin and related drugs.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Long-term use causes a mild sensory axonal polyneuropathy.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial toxicity with prolonged therapy causes peripheral and optic neuropathy.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Proteasome inhibitor causing painful small-fiber neuropathy, less with subcutaneous dosing.

answers.name: Thalidomide
answers.pearl: Cumulative sensory neuropathy limits long-term use in myeloma.

answers.name: Antiretroviral nucleoside analogs
answers.pearl: Stavudine, didanosine and zalcitabine cause painful mitochondrial neuropathy.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Long-term metformin reduces B12 absorption and can cause neuropathy by deficiency.

answers.name: Nitrous oxide
answers.pearl: Inactivates cobalamin, causing myeloneuropathy with recreational or repeated use.

answers.name: Hydralazine
answers.pearl: Pyridoxine antagonism produces sensory neuropathy, particularly in slow acetylators.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Rare small-fiber or axonal neuropathy has been reported, with a weak association.

answers.name: Colchicine
answers.pearl: Neuromyopathy occurs mainly with renal impairment or interacting drugs.

answers.name: Ethambutol
answers.pearl: Optic neuropathy is classic, but peripheral neuropathy can also occur.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Peripheral neuropathy is a labeled adverse effect and reported in a minority of users.

answers.name: Brentuximab vedotin
answers.pearl: Antibody-drug conjugate causing cumulative sensory and motor neuropathy.

answers.name: TNF inhibitors
answers.pearl: Anti-TNF drugs are associated with demyelinating neuropathy and GBS-like syndromes.

answers.name: Checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune neuropathies including Guillain-Barre-like syndromes can occur.

answers.name: Chloramphenicol
answers.pearl: Prolonged therapy can cause optic and peripheral neuropathy.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Peripheral neuropathy is reported with prolonged therapy.

answers.name: Cytarabine
answers.pearl: High-dose therapy causes cerebellar toxicity and, occasionally, neuropathy.

answers.name: Fludarabine
answers.pearl: Neurotoxicity includes neuropathy at high doses.

answers.name: Arsenic trioxide
answers.pearl: Arsenic neuropathy is a length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy.

answers.name: Chloroquine
answers.pearl: Neuromyopathy and rare neuropathy with chronic use.

answers.name: Ethionamide
answers.pearl: Neuropathy in treatment of MDR-TB, mitigated by pyridoxine.

answers.name: Eribulin
answers.pearl: Microtubule inhibitor with frequent peripheral neuropathy.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Chrysotherapy rarely causes polyneuropathy or myokymia.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Peripheral neuropathy is reported alongside tremor and PRES.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Neuromuscular blockade and rare neuropathy with high doses.

answers.name: Procarbazine
answers.pearl: Alkylating agent with sensory neuropathy.

answers.name: Ixabepilone
answers.pearl: An epothilone with dose-dependent sensory neuropathy.

answers.name: Perhexiline
answers.pearl: Antianginal that causes peripheral neuropathy, hepatotoxicity and requires drug-level monitoring.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Rare cases of axonal neuropathy have been reported.

answers.name: Suramin
answers.pearl: Antiparasitic and investigational anticancer agent causing a Guillain-Barre-like neuropathy.

answers.name: Podophyllin
answers.pearl: Absorption of topical podophyllin causes neuropathy after large-area application.

answers.name: Misonidazole
answers.pearl: A hypoxic radiosensitizer limited by dose-dependent sensory neuropathy.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Causes motor-predominant axonal neuropathy, in addition to hemolysis and methemoglobinemia.

answers.name: Disulfiram
answers.pearl: Chronic therapy causes sensory-motor axonal neuropathy, as in aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition toxicity.

answers.name: Pyridoxine excess
answers.pearl: High doses of vitamin B6 (above roughly 200 mg daily) cause a pure sensory ganglionopathy.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of multiple pulmonary nodules.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Meningothelial-like nodules, Benign metastasizing leiomyoma, Pulmonary hyalinizing granuloma, Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, Pulmonary blastoma, Dirofilariasis, Silicone embolism, Rhodococcus, Methotrexate nodulosis, Pulmonary endometriosis (all case-report or rare-series level). Lymphomatoid granulomatosis and DIPNECH are rare but literature-supported. Caplan syndrome, paragonimiasis and lymphomatoid granulomatosis scored as board traps.

answers.name: Metastatic disease
answers.pearl: Hematogenous spread from any extrathoracic cancer produces multiple, well-defined, basilar-predominant nodules.

answers.name: Septic emboli
answers.pearl: Right-sided endocarditis, IV drug use or infected lines produce peripheral cavitating nodules, often with feeding vessel sign.

answers.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Multiple cavitary nodules with sinus and renal disease; c-ANCA positive.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Perilymphatic micronodules with hilar adenopathy; the nodular form can have larger nodules.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Miliary or nodular TB produces multiple nodules with calcification.

answers.name: Fungal infection
answers.pearl: Histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis and cryptococcosis produce multiple granulomas or nodules.

answers.name: Rheumatoid nodules
answers.pearl: Necrobiotic nodules in seropositive RA, often subpleural or cavitary.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma can present with multiple nodules or masses.

answers.name: Multifocal adenocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Multiple synchronous primary lung adenocarcinomas or lepidic-type lesions appear as ground-glass or solid nodules.

answers.name: Invasive aspergillosis
answers.pearl: Angioinvasive mold gives multiple nodules with the halo sign in neutropenic patients.

answers.name: Nocardiosis
answers.pearl: Multiple nodules or abscesses in immunosuppressed patients, with possible brain abscesses.

answers.name: Silicosis
answers.pearl: Upper-zone small nodules with eggshell hilar node calcification.

answers.name: Coal workers pneumoconiosis
answers.pearl: Dust macules and nodules with possible progressive massive fibrosis.

answers.name: Organizing pneumonia
answers.pearl: Multifocal consolidative nodules that can be migratory.

answers.name: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
answers.pearl: Nodular bronchiectatic MAC disease causes tree-in-bud nodules and small nodules.

answers.name: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations
answers.pearl: Multiple PAVMs are classic for HHT and enhance with contrast.

answers.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Poorly defined centrilobular nodules with air trapping.

answers.name: Pulmonary infarcts
answers.pearl: Multiple peripheral wedge-shaped nodules from emboli.

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Transient nodules and migratory infiltrates in asthma with eosinophilia.

answers.name: Germ cell tumor metastases
answers.pearl: Cannonball metastases from testicular cancer and choriocarcinoma.

answers.name: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
answers.pearl: Early nodules cavitate and become cysts in smokers.

answers.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
answers.pearl: Atypical nodular and cavitary forms occur, especially with pentamidine prophylaxis.

answers.name: Actinomycosis
answers.pearl: Multifocal nodular or mass-like consolidation with sulfur granules and extension through the chest wall.

answers.name: Hamartomas
answers.pearl: Multiple pulmonary hamartomas are uncommon but described, sometimes with Carney triad.

answers.name: Intravenous drug-use related disease
answers.pearl: Talc granulomatosis, septic emboli and foreign body granulomas appear as small nodules.

answers.name: Kaposi sarcoma
answers.pearl: Peribronchovascular nodules with flame-shaped appearance in HIV.

answers.name: Melanoma metastases
answers.pearl: Metastatic melanoma commonly spreads hematogenously to lung.

answers.name: Sarcoma metastases
answers.pearl: Osteosarcoma and soft tissue sarcomas metastasize mainly to lung and may calcify.

answers.name: Berylliosis
answers.pearl: Chronic beryllium disease causes granulomas mimicking sarcoidosis.

answers.name: Hydatid disease
answers.pearl: Multiple echinococcal cysts present as round nodules or masses.

answers.name: Respiratory bronchiolitis
answers.pearl: Smoking-related centrilobular nodules with ground glass.

answers.name: Melioidosis
answers.pearl: Burkholderia pseudomallei produces multiple nodules or abscesses in endemic Southeast Asia and northern Australia.

answers.name: Intrapulmonary lymph nodes
answers.pearl: Benign subpleural nodules, usually small and sharply marginated.

answers.name: Eosinophilic pneumonia
answers.pearl: Peripheral and migratory opacities that can appear nodular.

answers.name: DIPNECH
answers.pearl: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia causes carcinoid tumorlets presenting as multiple nodules.

answers.name: Lipoid pneumonia
answers.pearl: Aspiration or injection of oils forms fat-density nodules or consolidation.

answers.name: Pulmonary amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Nodular amyloid deposits can be multiple, and may calcify.

answers.name: IgG4-related disease
answers.pearl: Solid nodules and masses can occur with lymphoplasmacytic infiltration.

answers.name: Rhodococcus equi infection
