answers.pearl: Cavitating nodules in HIV and transplant patients exposed to livestock.

answers.name: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
answers.pearl: HPV 6 and 11 cause laryngeal papillomas that seed lung with cavitating nodules.

answers.name: Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Pulmonary artery aneurysms or thrombi appear as multiple nodular opacities.

answers.name: Angiosarcoma
answers.pearl: Multifocal hemorrhagic nodules from primary or metastatic angiosarcoma.

answers.name: Methotrexate nodulosis
answers.pearl: Accelerated nodulosis in methotrexate-treated RA patients.

answers.name: Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis
answers.pearl: Diffuse sandlike calcifications forming micronodules in the lower zones.

answers.name: Pulmonary hyalinizing granuloma
answers.pearl: Multiple, slow-growing nodules, with sclerosing hyaline fibrosis; associated with autoimmune disease and sometimes IgG4.

answers.name: Dirofilariasis
answers.pearl: Dirofilaria immitis causes pulmonary coin lesions, usually single but multiple in some cases.

answers.name: Silicone embolism
answers.pearl: Silicone injection embolizes to lung causing multiple opacities.

answers.name: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
answers.pearl: Multiple small bilateral nodules in young women, often asymptomatic, a low-grade vascular tumor.

answers.name: Benign metastasizing leiomyoma
answers.pearl: Well-differentiated uterine leiomyoma cells deposit in lung of women with prior myomectomy or hysterectomy.

answers.name: Minute pulmonary meningothelial-like nodules
answers.pearl: Incidental tiny nodules with meningothelial histology found on CT or autopsy; larger forms are called meningotheliomatosis.

answers.name: Pulmonary blastoma
answers.pearl: Rare biphasic lung tumor that can metastasize to the lungs and appear as multiple nodules.

answers.name: Caplan syndrome
answers.pearl: Rheumatoid arthritis with pneumoconiosis produces multiple well-defined peripheral nodules.

answers.name: Paragonimiasis
answers.pearl: Lung fluke infection produces nodules and cysts, often mistaken for TB.

answers.name: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
answers.pearl: EBV-driven angiocentric B-cell lymphoproliferation producing multiple nodules, mostly in the lower lungs.

answers.name: Renal cell carcinoma metastases
answers.pearl: Renal cell carcinoma classically produces large cannonball nodules, sometimes years after nephrectomy.

answers.name: Multifocal bacterial pneumonia or abscesses
answers.pearl: Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA) and other pathogens cause multiple cavitating or necrotic nodules, often hematogenous.

answers.name: Thyroid cancer metastases
answers.pearl: Papillary and follicular thyroid cancer spread as micronodules or nodules to lung.

answers.name: Mucormycosis
answers.pearl: Angioinvasive mold causing multiple nodules or cavities with reverse halo sign in diabetes or neutropenia.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Egg granulomas can appear as multiple nodules, usually with pulmonary hypertension.

prompts.prompt: Name complications or manifestations of cirrhosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Distal renal tubular acidosis, Hepatic myelopathy, Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration (rare, literature-supported), Parotid enlargement, Clubbing (weak association), Dupuytren contracture and Terry nails scored as board traps.

answers.name: Ascites
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension with splanchnic vasodilation and hypoalbuminemia drives sodium retention and fluid accumulation in the peritoneum.

answers.name: Esophageal varices
answers.pearl: Portosystemic collaterals in the distal esophagus can rupture and cause life-threatening upper GI bleeding.

answers.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Gut-derived ammonia and other toxins bypass the failing liver and cause confusion, asterixis, and coma.

answers.name: Jaundice
answers.pearl: Impaired bilirubin conjugation and excretion cause scleral and skin icterus, usually as synthetic function worsens.

answers.name: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
answers.pearl: Infection of ascitic fluid without a surgical source, diagnosed with an ascitic PMN count of 250 or more per mm3.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension causes congestive enlargement of the spleen.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Splenic sequestration and reduced hepatic thrombopoietin production lower the platelet count.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis of any cause is the main risk factor, so patients need ultrasound surveillance every 6 months.

answers.name: Coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Decreased synthesis of clotting factors raises the INR, though cirrhosis is a rebalanced rather than purely bleeding state.

answers.name: Hepatorenal syndrome
answers.pearl: Functional renal failure from intense renal vasoconstriction in advanced portal hypertension, treated with albumin plus vasoconstrictors.

answers.name: Spider angiomata
answers.pearl: Central arteriole with radiating vessels on the upper trunk, attributed to hyperestrogenism.

answers.name: Palmar erythema
answers.pearl: Redness of the thenar and hypothenar eminences from altered sex hormone metabolism.

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Reduced hepatic albumin synthesis lowers oncotic pressure and contributes to ascites and edema.

answers.name: Peripheral edema
answers.pearl: Low oncotic pressure and sodium retention cause leg swelling, often with ascites.

answers.name: Asterixis
answers.pearl: Flapping tremor of dorsiflexed hands that signals grade 2 or higher hepatic encephalopathy.

answers.name: Gynecomastia
answers.pearl: Altered androgen to estrogen ratio, and spironolactone use, cause male breast enlargement.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Occult GI blood loss, hypersplenism, folate deficiency, and marrow suppression from alcohol all contribute.

answers.name: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
answers.pearl: Congested, mosaic-pattern gastric mucosa that causes chronic or acute upper GI bleeding.

answers.name: Gastric varices
answers.pearl: Fundal varices bleed less often than esophageal varices but more severely, and are often due to splenic vein thrombosis or portal hypertension.

answers.name: Caput medusae
answers.pearl: Dilated periumbilical veins from recanalized paraumbilical collaterals; a classic exam sign that is actually uncommon.

answers.name: Malnutrition
answers.pearl: Anorexia, malabsorption, and catabolism cause protein-calorie malnutrition that worsens outcomes.

answers.name: Sarcopenia
answers.pearl: Muscle wasting from hyperammonemia and catabolism is an independent predictor of mortality.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Nonosmotic ADH release and impaired free water excretion cause dilutional hyponatremia.

answers.name: Hepatic hydrothorax
answers.pearl: Ascitic fluid crosses diaphragmatic defects into the pleural space, usually on the right side.

answers.name: Pruritus
answers.pearl: Retained bile salts and other pruritogens cause itching, more typical of cholestatic disease.

answers.name: Umbilical hernia
answers.pearl: Raised intra-abdominal pressure from ascites predisposes to umbilical and other abdominal wall hernias.

answers.name: Hypersplenism
answers.pearl: An overactive enlarged spleen sequesters and destroys blood cells, causing cytopenias.

answers.name: Portal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Sluggish portal flow predisposes to thrombosis, which may worsen portal hypertension.

answers.name: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
answers.pearl: Intrapulmonary vasodilation causes hypoxemia and platypnea-orthodeoxia, shown by a positive bubble echo.

answers.name: Fetor hepaticus
answers.pearl: A sweet musty breath odor from volatile mercaptans in advanced liver disease.

answers.name: Loss of body hair
answers.pearl: Hyperestrogenism and hypoandrogenism reduce axillary and pubic hair.

answers.name: Testicular atrophy
answers.pearl: Hypogonadism from direct toxic effects and altered hormone metabolism shrinks the testes.

answers.name: Hepatic osteodystrophy
answers.pearl: Osteoporosis and osteomalacia arise from vitamin D deficiency, hypogonadism, and chronic liver disease.

answers.name: Infections
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction predisposes to bacterial infections such as pneumonia and urinary tract infection.

answers.name: Portopulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Pulmonary arterial hypertension in portal hypertension, which can be a contraindication to liver transplantation if severe.

answers.name: Hemorrhoids
answers.pearl: Rectal varices and hemorrhoids can both bleed in portal hypertension.

answers.name: Dupuytren contracture
answers.pearl: Palmar fascia thickening associated with alcohol-related cirrhosis, though the link is weak.

answers.name: Terry nails
answers.pearl: Proximal two thirds of the nail appear white with a distal reddish band, linked to cirrhosis, heart failure, and diabetes.

answers.name: Glucose dysregulation
answers.pearl: Hepatogenic diabetes from insulin resistance is common, and fasting hypoglycemia can occur in advanced disease.

answers.name: Acute-on-chronic liver failure
answers.pearl: Acute decompensation with organ failure on top of cirrhosis, triggered by infection, alcohol, or bleeding.

answers.name: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Blunted contractile response, diastolic dysfunction, and prolonged QT in cirrhosis occur without other cardiac disease.

answers.name: Hepatic myelopathy
answers.pearl: Progressive spastic paraparesis in cirrhosis with large portosystemic shunts, from spinal cord demyelination.

answers.name: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration
answers.pearl: Chronic parkinsonism, ataxia, and cognitive decline from manganese deposition in the basal ganglia.

answers.name: Cruveilhier-Baumgarten syndrome
answers.pearl: A venous hum over a patent umbilical vein with periumbilical collateral veins in portal hypertension.

answers.name: Splenic artery aneurysm
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension and hyperdynamic circulation are associated with splenic artery aneurysms, which can rupture.

answers.name: Platypnea-orthodeoxia
answers.pearl: Dyspnea and hypoxemia in the upright position, a marker of hepatopulmonary syndrome from basal intrapulmonary shunts.

answers.name: Clubbing
answers.pearl: Digital clubbing and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy occur in cirrhosis, especially with hepatopulmonary syndrome.

answers.name: Distal renal tubular acidosis
answers.pearl: Acquired tubular dysfunction, especially distal RTA, is described in cirrhosis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of pulmonary edema (cardiogenic and non-cardiogenic).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hydrochlorothiazide-induced pulmonary edema and Cor triatriatum (rare/case-series level), Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, Post-cardiopulmonary bypass lung injury, Tocolytic therapy; TRALI, neurogenic edema and HAPE scored as board traps.

answers.name: Acute decompensated heart failure
answers.pearl: Elevated left atrial pressure from LV systolic dysfunction drives transudation of fluid into alveoli.

answers.name: Myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Acute ischemia produces LV systolic and diastolic dysfunction and abruptly raises left atrial pressure.

answers.name: ARDS
answers.pearl: Diffuse alveolar damage increases capillary permeability, giving noncardiogenic edema with a normal wedge pressure.

answers.name: Volume overload
answers.pearl: Excess IV fluids or sodium retention raise hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary capillaries.

answers.name: Hypertensive emergency
answers.pearl: Sudden afterload surge causes flash pulmonary edema, even with preserved ejection fraction.

answers.name: Renal failure
answers.pearl: Salt and water retention in AKI or ESRD cause volume overload, and uremia increases permeability.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation causes widespread endothelial injury and leaky pulmonary capillaries.

answers.name: Acute mitral regurgitation
answers.pearl: Papillary muscle rupture or chordal rupture causes abrupt left atrial pressure rise and flash edema.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Severe pneumonia injures the alveolar-capillary barrier and can progress to ARDS.

answers.name: Mitral stenosis
answers.pearl: Obstruction of left atrial emptying raises pulmonary venous pressure, often unmasked by tachycardia, AF, or pregnancy.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
answers.pearl: Loss of atrial kick and shortened diastolic filling raise left atrial pressure.

answers.name: Aspiration
answers.pearl: Gastric acid injures the alveolar-capillary membrane, causing chemical pneumonitis and noncardiogenic edema.

answers.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
answers.pearl: Stiff LV with high filling pressures leads to pulmonary congestion despite normal EF.

answers.name: Acute aortic regurgitation
answers.pearl: Sudden volume load on an unprepared left ventricle, such as in aortic dissection or endocarditis, causes pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Fixed outflow obstruction raises LV end-diastolic pressure and causes dyspnea and edema, especially with tachyarrhythmia.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Bradycardia or tachycardia can reduce cardiac output and precipitate pulmonary congestion.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Acute inflammatory loss of LV function leads to pulmonary congestion.

answers.name: Opioid overdose
answers.pearl: Heroin and other opioids cause noncardiogenic edema through hypoxia, hypoventilation, and direct capillary injury.

answers.name: Drowning
answers.pearl: Aspiration of fresh or salt water damages the surfactant and alveolar membranes.

answers.name: Smoke inhalation
answers.pearl: Heat and toxic gases cause direct airway and alveolar injury.

answers.name: Acute pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Circulating pancreatic enzymes and cytokines trigger ARDS-type capillary leak.

answers.name: TRALI
answers.pearl: Transfusion-related acute lung injury occurs within 6 hours of transfusion from donor anti-HLA or anti-neutrophil antibodies.

answers.name: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload
answers.pearl: TACO is hydrostatic edema from rapid or large transfusion, with hypertension and raised BNP.

answers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Diastolic dysfunction and dynamic outflow obstruction with mitral regurgitation raise left atrial pressure.

answers.name: Stress cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Transient apical ballooning with acute LV dysfunction can cause pulmonary edema in some patients.

answers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Chronic LV systolic dysfunction raises filling pressures and predisposes to pulmonary congestion.

answers.name: Neurogenic pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Massive catecholamine surge after subarachnoid hemorrhage, seizure, or head injury raises pulmonary pressures and capillary permeability.

answers.name: High-altitude pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Uneven hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction causes stress failure of capillaries in unacclimatized people above about 2500 m.

answers.name: Negative pressure pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Forceful inspiration against an obstructed airway, such as laryngospasm after extubation, creates large negative intrathoracic pressure.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Salicylate poisoning increases capillary permeability, more often in chronic toxicity in older adults.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine causes ischemia, severe hypertension, and direct pulmonary vascular injury, and crack lung can cause edema.

answers.name: Reexpansion pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Rapid reexpansion of a collapsed lung after large thoracentesis or chest tube drainage causes unilateral edema.

answers.name: Naloxone administration
answers.pearl: Rapid opioid reversal, especially postoperatively, can trigger catecholamine-driven pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Fat embolism syndrome
answers.pearl: Marrow fat embolism after long-bone fracture causes lung injury, petechiae, and neurologic changes.

answers.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
answers.pearl: Peripartum anaphylactoid reaction causing acute cardiopulmonary collapse and DIC.

answers.name: Tocolytic therapy
answers.pearl: Beta-agonists and magnesium sulfate with IV fluids in pregnancy cause pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Anaphylaxis
answers.pearl: Massive mediator release and capillary leak can produce noncardiogenic edema alongside hypotension.

answers.name: Left atrial myxoma
answers.pearl: A prolapsing atrial tumor mimics mitral stenosis by obstructing LV inflow.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
aliases: flash pulmonary edema with renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Bilateral renal artery stenosis causes recurrent flash pulmonary edema through sodium retention and renin-driven hypertension (Pickering syndrome).

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma crisis
answers.pearl: Catecholamine excess causes severe hypertension and cardiomyopathy, and sometimes pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Hydrochlorothiazide-induced pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Idiosyncratic noncardiogenic edema within hours of a dose, with rapid resolution after drug withdrawal.

answers.name: Chemotherapy-induced pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Gemcitabine, cytarabine, and other agents can cause capillary leak and noncardiogenic edema.

answers.name: Capillary leak syndrome
answers.pearl: Episodic leak of plasma into tissues with hypotension, hemoconcentration, and hypoalbuminemia, and often a monoclonal gammopathy.

answers.name: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
answers.pearl: Viral infection of pulmonary endothelium causes severe capillary leak with rapid cardiopulmonary failure.

answers.name: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
answers.pearl: Occlusion of small pulmonary veins causes edema, which worsens after pulmonary vasodilator therapy.

answers.name: Cor triatriatum
answers.pearl: A membrane in the left atrium obstructs pulmonary venous return, resembling mitral stenosis.

answers.name: Lung transplant reperfusion injury
answers.pearl: Primary graft dysfunction is noncardiogenic edema early after lung transplant.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hemosuccus pancreaticus, Gastric volvulus-type rarities dropped, Pseudoxanthoma elasticum and blue rubber bleb nevus (case-series level), Metastatic disease to stomach, Uremic gastropathy; Dieulafoy lesion, GAVE and Zollinger-Ellison scored as board traps.

answers.name: Duodenal ulcer
answers.pearl: Most often H. pylori or NSAID related, and the posterior wall can erode the gastroduodenal artery.

answers.name: Gastric ulcer
answers.pearl: Bleeding gastric ulcers need biopsy and follow-up endoscopy because some are malignant.

answers.name: Esophageal varices
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension produces submucosal esophageal varices that bleed massively and are treated with banding and octreotide.

answers.name: Gastritis
answers.pearl: Erosive gastritis from NSAIDs, alcohol, or stress causes diffuse mucosal bleeding.

answers.name: Erosive esophagitis
answers.pearl: Severe reflux esophagitis can cause hematemesis or occult blood loss.

answers.name: Mallory-Weiss tear
answers.pearl: Mucosal laceration at the gastroesophageal junction after forceful retching, usually self-limited.

answers.name: Stress ulcer
answers.pearl: Critically ill patients with respiratory failure or coagulopathy develop stress-related mucosal bleeding.

answers.name: Gastric cancer
answers.pearl: Ulcerated gastric adenocarcinoma can present with melena or hematemesis.

answers.name: Duodenitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of the duodenal mucosa from NSAIDs, alcohol, or H. pylori may bleed.

answers.name: Angiodysplasia
answers.pearl: Gastric and duodenal vascular ectasias cause chronic or acute bleeding, especially in older adults and with renal disease.

answers.name: Esophageal cancer
answers.pearl: Esophageal carcinoma bleeds from friable tumor tissue.

answers.name: Gastric varices
answers.pearl: Isolated gastric varices from splenic vein thrombosis or portal hypertension bleed severely.

answers.name: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
answers.pearl: Mosaic-pattern gastric mucosa from portal hypertension causes chronic oozing.

answers.name: Infectious esophagitis
answers.pearl: CMV, HSV, and Candida esophagitis cause ulcers that can bleed in immunocompromised patients.

answers.name: Pill esophagitis
answers.pearl: Doxycycline, bisphosphonates, potassium, and NSAIDs cause local ulceration when pills lodge in the esophagus.

answers.name: Hiatal hernia
answers.pearl: Cameron lesions in a large hiatal hernia cause chronic iron-deficiency anemia and occasional overt bleeding.

answers.name: Dieulafoy lesion
answers.pearl: A large submucosal artery protrudes through a tiny mucosal defect, usually in the proximal stomach, and causes sudden severe bleeding.

answers.name: Gastric antral vascular ectasia
answers.pearl: Watermelon stomach causes striped antral vessels and chronic iron-deficiency anemia, often in cirrhosis and scleroderma.

answers.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
answers.pearl: Gastrinoma causes severe, refractory, and often multiple ulcers beyond the duodenal bulb.

answers.name: Aortoenteric fistula
answers.pearl: Prior aortic graft or aneurysm erodes into the third part of the duodenum, with a herald bleed before massive hemorrhage.

answers.name: Marginal ulcer
answers.pearl: Anastomotic ulcers occur after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, worsened by smoking and NSAIDs.

answers.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
answers.pearl: Osler-Weber-Rendu causes mucocutaneous telangiectasias with GI bleeding from gastric and duodenal lesions.

answers.name: Heyde syndrome
answers.pearl: Aortic stenosis associated with acquired von Willebrand syndrome and GI angiodysplasia bleeding.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
answers.pearl: GIST ulcerates through the mucosa and presents with bleeding.

answers.name: Gastric lymphoma
answers.pearl: MALT lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma can ulcerate and bleed.

answers.name: Caustic ingestion
answers.pearl: Acid or alkali ingestion causes necrosis of the esophagus and stomach with hemorrhage.

answers.name: Post-endoscopic intervention bleeding
answers.pearl: Delayed bleeding after polypectomy, sphincterotomy, dilation, or banding ulcer.

answers.name: Hemobilia
answers.pearl: Bleeding from the biliary tree enters the duodenum via the ampulla, causing the triad of biliary colic, jaundice, and GI bleeding.

answers.name: Hemosuccus pancreaticus
answers.pearl: Bleeding from the pancreatic duct, from a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm or chronic pancreatitis, appears through the ampulla.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer invading the duodenum
answers.pearl: Direct tumor invasion of the duodenum causes ulceration and bleeding.

answers.name: Pseudoaneurysm rupture into the gastrointestinal tract
answers.pearl: Gastroduodenal or splenic artery pseudoaneurysm from pancreatitis erodes into the stomach or duodenum.

answers.name: Duodenal varices
answers.pearl: Ectopic varices at the duodenum, with high rebleeding risk, arise in portal hypertension.

answers.name: Radiation gastritis
answers.pearl: Prior upper abdominal radiotherapy causes telangiectatic, friable gastric or duodenal mucosa.

answers.name: Metastatic disease to the stomach
aliases: melanoma metastasis to the GI tract
answers.pearl: Breast cancer, melanoma, and lung cancer metastases can ulcerate in the stomach and bleed.

answers.name: Kaposi sarcoma
answers.pearl: Gastric Kaposi sarcoma lesions in advanced HIV can bleed.

answers.name: Crohn disease of the upper gastrointestinal tract
answers.pearl: Gastroduodenal Crohn disease can cause ulcers and bleeding.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration of vessels and mucosa causes fragility and GI bleeding.

answers.name: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum
answers.pearl: Calcified elastic fibers in GI submucosal arteries cause gastric hemorrhage.

answers.name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome vascular type
answers.pearl: Collagen III defects cause fragile vessels and spontaneous GI bleeding or perforation.

answers.name: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
answers.pearl: Multiple cavernous venous malformations of skin and bowel cause GI bleeding and iron-deficiency anemia.

answers.name: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
answers.pearl: Hamartomatous polyps in the stomach and small intestine can ulcerate and bleed.

answers.name: Gastric polyps
answers.pearl: Hyperplastic or adenomatous polyps can ulcerate and bleed.

answers.name: Uremic gastropathy
answers.pearl: Platelet dysfunction and mucosal vulnerability in uremia increase GI bleeding from erosions or angiodysplasia.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus gastritis
answers.pearl: CMV infection in transplant and HIV patients causes gastric or duodenal ulcers.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause tinnitus or hearing loss.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Vincristine, Teicoplanin, Oxaliplatin, Eflornithine (reports/studies of limited size), Tricyclic antidepressants and Benzodiazepine withdrawal (tinnitus only), Opioids (case-series level), Bismuth subsalicylate; Streptomycin, Ethacrynic acid and Erythromycin scored as board traps.

answers.name: Aspirin
answers.pearl: High-dose salicylates cause reversible tinnitus and hearing loss through cochlear effects, a sign of toxicity.

answers.name: Gentamicin
answers.pearl: Aminoglycoside hair cell toxicity causes irreversible high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss.

answers.name: Furosemide
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics affect the stria vascularis, usually reversible, and risk rises with rapid IV bolus and renal failure.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum accumulation in the cochlea causes bilateral, permanent high-frequency hearing loss and tinnitus, dose dependent.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Ibuprofen, naproxen, and others can cause reversible tinnitus and hearing loss, especially at high doses.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Cinchonism produces tinnitus, hearing loss, headache, and visual disturbance.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Hearing loss was described mainly with older impure formulations and high serum levels, and it often occurs with aminoglycosides.

answers.name: Tobramycin
answers.pearl: Aminoglycoside with cochlear and vestibular toxicity, risk grows with prolonged exposure and renal failure.

answers.name: Amikacin
answers.pearl: Amikacin is predominantly cochleotoxic, damaging high-frequency hearing first.

answers.name: Streptomycin
answers.pearl: Streptomycin is predominantly vestibulotoxic and a classic ototoxic anti-TB drug.

answers.name: Ethacrynic acid
answers.pearl: Loop diuretic with the highest ototoxic potential, used in sulfa-allergic patients.

answers.name: Erythromycin
answers.pearl: Dose-related reversible sensorineural hearing loss, especially with IV high doses, renal or hepatic disease.

answers.name: Azithromycin
answers.pearl: Hearing loss and tinnitus, usually reversible, were reported with long-term or high-dose macrolide use.

answers.name: Clarithromycin
answers.pearl: Reversible sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus reported with macrolides.

answers.name: Neomycin
answers.pearl: Oral or topical neomycin can cause deafness after absorption, especially with impaired renal function.

answers.name: Kanamycin
answers.pearl: Mainly cochleotoxic aminoglycoside used in resistant TB regimens.

answers.name: Bumetanide
answers.pearl: Loop diuretic with lower ototoxicity than furosemide but still reported.

answers.name: Torsemide
answers.pearl: Loop diuretic with rare reports of tinnitus and hearing loss.

answers.name: Carboplatin
answers.pearl: Less ototoxic than cisplatin, but high-dose carboplatin and combinations cause hearing loss.

answers.name: Chloroquine
answers.pearl: Tinnitus and sensorineural hearing loss are described, with a higher risk in chronic use.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: Rare reports of tinnitus and sensorineural hearing loss.

answers.name: Mefloquine
answers.pearl: Neuropsychiatric and vestibulocochlear effects include tinnitus and vertigo.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Cinchona-derived antiarrhythmic that can cause cinchonism with tinnitus and deafness.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition causes tinnitus and paresthesias in many patients.

answers.name: Bismuth subsalicylate
answers.pearl: Large amounts of Pepto-Bismol deliver significant salicylate and can cause tinnitus.

answers.name: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sildenafil, tadalafil, and vardenafil are linked to sudden sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon, with or without ribavirin, is associated with sudden hearing loss and tinnitus.

answers.name: Ototoxic ear drops
answers.pearl: Neomycin or gentamicin drops can reach the inner ear through a perforated tympanic membrane.

answers.name: Polymyxin B
answers.pearl: Polymyxins can cause neurotoxicity with reports of hearing loss, especially in renal impairment.

answers.name: Capreomycin
answers.pearl: Second-line anti-TB injectable with cochlear and vestibular toxicity.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Tinnitus and sensorineural hearing loss are reported with ciprofloxacin and related drugs.

answers.name: Deferoxamine
answers.pearl: High-frequency sensorineural hearing loss from chelation therapy at high doses, particularly in young patients.

answers.name: Eflornithine
answers.pearl: Dose-related, usually high-frequency hearing loss in studies of difluoromethylornithine.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Amitriptyline and related agents can cause or worsen tinnitus.

answers.name: Benzodiazepine withdrawal
answers.pearl: Tinnitus can appear or worsen on withdrawal of benzodiazepines.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Case series link heavy hydrocodone, methadone, and heroin use to sudden sensorineural hearing loss.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Vinca alkaloids can cause sensorineural hearing loss in addition to neuropathy.

answers.name: Teicoplanin
answers.pearl: Glycopeptide with reported ototoxicity, mostly with high doses.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Tinnitus is a listed adverse effect and has been reported to improve after discontinuation.

answers.name: Oxaliplatin
answers.pearl: Platinum agent with far less ototoxicity than cisplatin, but hearing loss and tinnitus are reported.

prompts.prompt: Name complications or extrapulmonary manifestations of COPD.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis, Pneumomediastinum, Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (overlap rather than complication), Hypogonadism, Metabolic alkalosis; Secondary polycythemia, Multifocal atrial tachycardia and Hoover sign scored as board traps.

answers.name: Acute exacerbation
answers.pearl: Infectious or noninfectious triggers worsen dyspnea, cough, and sputum and drive hospitalizations and mortality.

answers.name: Respiratory failure
answers.pearl: Hypoxemic and hypercapnic failure can develop acutely or chronically, with NIV reducing intubation and mortality.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: COPD and inhaled steroids both increase pneumonia risk, which is a major cause of exacerbation.

answers.name: Cor pulmonale
answers.pearl: Chronic hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction causes right heart failure with edema and elevated JVP.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Chronic hypoxia and vascular remodeling cause group 3 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Hypercapnia
answers.pearl: CO2 retention reflects ventilation-perfusion mismatch and respiratory muscle fatigue.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Smoking is shared risk, and emphysema itself independently increases the risk of lung cancer.

answers.name: Pneumothorax
answers.pearl: Ruptured bullae or blebs cause secondary spontaneous pneumothorax, with high morbidity because of poor reserve.

answers.name: Cardiovascular disease
answers.pearl: COPD is an independent risk factor for coronary artery disease, partly through systemic inflammation and shared smoking exposure.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Smoking, inactivity, vitamin D deficiency, systemic inflammation, and steroids reduce bone density.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression is common and linked to worse exacerbation rates and quality of life.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation, increased work of breathing, and dyspnea during eating cause pulmonary cachexia, a poor prognostic sign.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Anxiety disorders and panic are common and worsen dyspnea perception.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: COPD and left heart failure are often confused and frequently coexist.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia, beta-agonists, and atrial remodeling predispose to atrial arrhythmias.

answers.name: Secondary polycythemia
answers.pearl: Chronic hypoxemia stimulates erythropoietin, raising hematocrit and increasing viscosity.

answers.name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
answers.pearl: Irregular rhythm with three or more P-wave morphologies, strongly associated with severe COPD and theophylline use.

answers.name: Skeletal muscle dysfunction
answers.pearl: Deconditioning, hypoxia, steroids, and inflammation cause peripheral muscle weakness and wasting independent of lung function.

answers.name: Giant bullae
answers.pearl: Large emphysematous bullae compress adjacent lung and can become infected or rupture.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea overlap
answers.pearl: OSA coexisting with COPD (overlap syndrome) causes severe nocturnal hypoxemia and hypercapnia.

answers.name: GERD
answers.pearl: GERD is a recognized exacerbation risk factor in COPD, partly through microaspiration.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Metabolic syndrome and diabetes are more frequent in COPD, aggravated by steroid courses.

answers.name: Oral candidiasis
answers.pearl: Inhaled corticosteroids cause thrush, prevented by spacers and rinsing the mouth.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: PE is an under-recognized cause of exacerbation-like symptoms.

answers.name: Corticosteroid adverse effects
answers.pearl: Repeated systemic steroid bursts cause hyperglycemia, myopathy, adrenal suppression, and cataracts.

answers.name: Barrel chest
answers.pearl: Chronic hyperinflation increases the anteroposterior chest diameter.

answers.name: Hoover sign
answers.pearl: Paradoxical inward movement of the lower rib cage on inspiration from a flattened diaphragm.

answers.name: Frailty
answers.pearl: Frailty and physical inactivity are common and predict hospitalization and mortality.

answers.name: Sleep disturbance
answers.pearl: Insomnia and poor sleep quality are frequent and related to nocturnal symptoms and therapy.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation, renal disease, and low erythropoietin response can cause anemia in some patients, which worsens dyspnea.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Coexisting bronchiectasis worsens exacerbations and increases risk of Pseudomonas colonization.

answers.name: Respiratory muscle fatigue
answers.pearl: Hyperinflation flattens the diaphragm and increases the work of breathing until the muscles fatigue.

answers.name: Cognitive impairment
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and vascular disease are associated with memory problems and dementia.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Low sun exposure and reduced activation are common and contribute to bone loss and muscle weakness.

answers.name: Hyponatremia
answers.pearl: Hypoxia, chronic hypercapnia, and SIADH-like physiology can lead to low sodium, sometimes with concurrent lung cancer.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: Prevalence is increased in COPD, as in other smokers.

answers.name: Hypogonadism
answers.pearl: Low testosterone is common in men with severe COPD and contributes to muscle weakness and bone loss.

answers.name: Metabolic alkalosis
answers.pearl: Chronic hypercapnia renal compensation plus diuretics and steroids raise bicarbonate and can blunt ventilatory drive.

answers.name: Erectile dysfunction
answers.pearl: Common in COPD from hypoxemia, vascular disease, hypogonadism, and depression.

answers.name: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
answers.pearl: Structural lung disease and inhaled steroids increase the risk of MAC and other NTM infections.

answers.name: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
answers.pearl: Aspergilloma and chronic cavitary aspergillosis occur in damaged emphysematous lung with cavities.

answers.name: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema
answers.pearl: Upper lobe emphysema coexists with lower lobe fibrosis, giving preserved volumes, severely reduced DLCO, and high pulmonary hypertension risk.

answers.name: Pneumomediastinum
answers.pearl: Alveolar rupture in emphysema or severe exacerbations can dissect air into the mediastinum.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Smoking and COPD increase the risk of active pulmonary TB.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of dilated cardiomyopathy.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Desmin mutation, Phospholamban mutation, Arsenic toxicity, Anabolic steroid abuse (case-level DCM), Hypocalcemia, Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy; Peripartum cardiomyopathy, Chagas disease and Selenium deficiency scored as board traps.

answers.name: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: A large share of cases have no identified cause, and many are probably undiagnosed familial or postmyocarditis.

answers.name: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Multivessel coronary disease with prior infarction causes LV dilation that mimics DCM.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Chronic heavy alcohol use causes a dilated cardiomyopathy that can improve with abstinence.

answers.name: Viral myocarditis
answers.pearl: Prior viral infection with persistent inflammation can progress to dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Long-standing pressure overload eventually leads to LV dilation and systolic failure.

answers.name: Anthracyclines
answers.pearl: Doxorubicin causes dose-related irreversible cardiomyopathy, with a cumulative dose threshold of about 450 to 550 mg/m2.

answers.name: Valvular heart disease
answers.pearl: Chronic mitral or aortic regurgitation causes volume overload and progressive LV dilation.

answers.name: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Sustained rapid rates such as atrial fibrillation or frequent PVCs cause reversible LV dysfunction.

answers.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: LV systolic dysfunction late in pregnancy or within 5 months postpartum, with prolactin fragments implicated and bromocriptine investigated.

answers.name: Familial dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: About one third of cases are familial, mostly autosomal dominant.

answers.name: Methamphetamine and cocaine
answers.pearl: Chronic stimulant use causes catecholamine toxicity and myocardial damage.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Reduced contractility and increased afterload can cause reversible dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Chronic thyrotoxicosis causes tachycardia-mediated and high-output LV dysfunction.

answers.name: Chagas disease
answers.pearl: Trypanosoma cruzi causes dilated cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm, conduction disease, and arrhythmias in endemic regions.

answers.name: Trastuzumab
answers.pearl: HER2 inhibition causes reversible cardiomyopathy, especially with prior anthracyclines.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Diabetic cardiomyopathy causes LV dysfunction independent of coronary disease.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Cardiac sarcoid can cause dilated cardiomyopathy with conduction abnormalities and ventricular arrhythmias.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Iron overload can cause a dilated phenotype, and early phlebotomy can reverse it.

answers.name: Thalassemia major
answers.pearl: Transfusional iron overload causes dilated cardiomyopathy, a leading cause of death, tracked by cardiac T2* MRI.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV can cause dilated cardiomyopathy directly and through opportunistic infection or antiretroviral toxicity.

answers.name: Titin truncating variants
answers.pearl: TTN truncating variants account for about 20 to 25 percent of familial DCM.

answers.name: Lamin A/C mutation
answers.pearl: LMNA mutations cause DCM with early conduction disease and malignant ventricular arrhythmias, so earlier ICD placement is considered.

answers.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
answers.pearl: Dystrophin deficiency causes a progressive dilated cardiomyopathy, and carriers can also be affected.

answers.name: Thiamine deficiency
answers.pearl: Wet beriberi causes high-output failure and may progress to dilated cardiomyopathy, reversible with thiamine.

answers.name: Selenium deficiency
answers.pearl: Keshan disease is a selenium-deficiency cardiomyopathy first described in endemic regions of China.

answers.name: Cobalt toxicity
answers.pearl: The beer-drinker cardiomyopathy outbreak was linked to cobalt added as a foam stabilizer, and metal hip prostheses have caused similar toxicity.

answers.name: Giant cell myocarditis
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive myocarditis with ventricular arrhythmias and heart block that needs combined immunosuppression.

answers.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a leading cause of death in EGPA.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus myocarditis can lead to dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Systemic sclerosis
answers.pearl: Primary myocardial fibrosis and microvascular disease cause LV dysfunction.

answers.name: Left ventricular noncompaction
answers.pearl: Trabeculated LV with deep recesses leads to heart failure, arrhythmia, and thromboembolism, and often a dilated phenotype.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine excess can cause dilated cardiomyopathy that regresses after tumor resection.

answers.name: Acromegaly
answers.pearl: Chronic growth hormone excess causes biventricular hypertrophy followed by dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis
answers.pearl: PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 inhibitors cause fulminant myocarditis that can leave a dilated ventricle.

answers.name: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Chronic high-burden RV pacing causes dyssynchrony and LV dilation, reversible with resynchronization.

answers.name: Uremia
answers.pearl: Anemia, volume overload, and uremic toxins contribute to LV dilation and systolic dysfunction in chronic kidney disease.

answers.name: Mitochondrial disease
answers.pearl: MELAS, Kearns-Sayre, and other mitochondrial disorders cause hypertrophic then dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Myotonic dystrophy
answers.pearl: Conduction disease and LV dysfunction occur in type 1 myotonic dystrophy.

answers.name: Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy
answers.pearl: Emery-Dreifuss, from emerin or LMNA mutations, causes early contractures, conduction disease, and dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Carnitine deficiency
answers.pearl: Primary systemic carnitine deficiency impairs fatty acid oxidation and causes dilated cardiomyopathy that responds to carnitine.

answers.name: Barth syndrome
answers.pearl: X-linked tafazzin deficiency causes DCM, neutropenia, and 3-methylglutaconic aciduria in boys.

answers.name: Hypocalcemia
answers.pearl: Severe prolonged hypocalcemia can reversibly depress contractility and cause dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Phospholamban mutation
answers.pearl: The PLN R14del variant causes DCM or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with ventricular arrhythmia.

answers.name: Arsenic toxicity
answers.pearl: Chronic arsenic exposure and arsenic trioxide therapy are cardiotoxic, causing QT prolongation and cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Anabolic steroid abuse
answers.pearl: Supraphysiologic androgen use is linked to LV hypertrophy and dilated cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Desmin mutation
answers.pearl: Desminopathy causes skeletal myopathy, conduction disease, and DCM or restrictive cardiomyopathy.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure (case-report level): Atorvastatin, Bupropion, Olanzapine, Sitagliptin, Fluconazole, Rufinamide, Clobazam, Cenobamate, Imatinib, Metronidazole, Iodinated contrast; Vancomycin, Dapsone and Nevirapine scored as board traps (dapsone and nevirapine reactions are DRESS-like hypersensitivity syndromes).

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: The leading cause of DRESS in many series, strongly linked to HLA-B*58:01 and renal impairment, with high mortality.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Aromatic antiepileptic with the classic DRESS latency of 2 to 8 weeks, and cross-reactivity with phenytoin and phenobarbital.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Classic culprit with the aromatic anticonvulsant hypersensitivity syndrome, and fosphenytoin shares the risk.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Rash risk rises with rapid titration and valproate co-administration, and it can present as DRESS.

answers.name: Phenobarbital
answers.pearl: Aromatic anticonvulsant with cross-reactivity to carbamazepine and phenytoin.

answers.name: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide antibiotics are common causes, especially in HIV-positive patients.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Vancomycin DRESS is a recognized entity with delayed onset, often after prolonged courses, and flagged in hospitalized patients on boards.

answers.name: Minocycline
answers.pearl: Tetracycline with a recognized DRESS association, often with long courses for acne and with lupus-like or hepatic involvement.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome is a DRESS-like reaction with fever, rash, and hepatitis, with HLA-B*13:01 risk in Asian patients.

answers.name: Nevirapine
answers.pearl: NNRTI causing early severe rash with hepatitis and DRESS-like reactions, and the risk is highest in women with higher CD4 counts.

answers.name: Amoxicillin
answers.pearl: Beta-lactams are common antibiotic causes, especially with concurrent viral infections such as EBV.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Cefazolin, ceftriaxone, and cefepime are reported culprits of DRESS.

answers.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
answers.pearl: Delayed hypersensitivity with eosinophilia and organ involvement after prolonged courses.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Non-aromatic anticonvulsant with fewer cases, but DRESS has been reported.

answers.name: Oxcarbazepine
answers.pearl: Cross-reacts with carbamazepine in a notable portion of patients.

answers.name: Zonisamide
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide anticonvulsant with reported DRESS.

answers.name: Lacosamide
answers.pearl: Newer anticonvulsant with a few DRESS case reports.

answers.name: Levetiracetam
answers.pearl: Rare DRESS reports despite its generally benign profile.

answers.name: Ethosuximide
answers.pearl: Reported in a handful of cases.

answers.name: Cenobamate
answers.pearl: DRESS was seen during rapid titration in early trials, leading to slower titration schedules.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfapyridine moiety causes hypersensitivity, typically in the first months of therapy.

answers.name: Celecoxib
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide-containing NSAID with DRESS reports.

answers.name: Ibuprofen
answers.pearl: NSAIDs are uncommon causes but have been reported.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: First-line TB drug that can cause DRESS, complicating TB treatment.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity to anti-TB drugs may cause DRESS with hepatitis and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Pyrazinamide
answers.pearl: Reported with multidrug TB regimens, which are hard to attribute.

answers.name: Ethambutol
answers.pearl: Documented in TB treatment as part of DRESS from multiple drugs.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Oxazolidinone with rare DRESS reports.

answers.name: Daptomycin
answers.pearl: Daptomycin DRESS is rare but described, sometimes together with eosinophilic pneumonia.

answers.name: Teicoplanin
answers.pearl: Glycopeptide cross-reactive with vancomycin in some cases.

answers.name: Ciprofloxacin
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones have been reported to cause DRESS.

answers.name: Clindamycin
answers.pearl: Delayed reactions with fever, rash, and eosinophilia have been reported.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: A few cases of DRESS are described.

answers.name: Doxycycline
answers.pearl: Tetracycline class reported to cause DRESS, but less often than minocycline.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Immunosuppressant with delayed hypersensitivity reactions that sometimes meet DRESS criteria.

answers.name: Mexiletine
answers.pearl: Class IB antiarrhythmic with early DRESS reports and a typical latency of 2 to 6 weeks.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Rare DRESS reports in addition to its better known toxicities.

answers.name: Diltiazem
answers.pearl: Calcium channel blockers reported to cause DRESS, usually with prominent skin and liver involvement.

answers.name: Captopril
answers.pearl: ACE inhibitor with scattered reports of DRESS.

answers.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
answers.pearl: Thiazides have occasional reports, likely sulfonamide-related.

answers.name: Strontium ranelate
answers.pearl: Withdrawn osteoporosis drug that had a well-documented DRESS signal.

answers.name: Febuxostat
answers.pearl: Alternative to allopurinol with few case reports of DRESS, including in patients who tolerated allopurinol.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: Rare reports of DRESS and AGEP, with latency up to several weeks.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: 5-ASA agents have rare reports of DRESS or hypersensitivity myocarditis.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Omeprazole and others have case reports of DRESS.

answers.name: Iodinated contrast
answers.pearl: Delayed hypersensitivity to contrast media can mimic or cause DRESS.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: NNRTI with reports of DRESS, usually early after starting therapy.

answers.name: Raltegravir
answers.pearl: Integrase inhibitor with rare DRESS cases.

answers.name: Telaprevir
answers.pearl: Hepatitis C protease inhibitor with severe cutaneous reactions including DRESS, and now largely withdrawn from use.

answers.name: Methimazole
answers.pearl: Antithyroid drugs have rare DRESS reports.

answers.name: Vemurafenib
answers.pearl: BRAF inhibitor with rash and DRESS-like reactions.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: PD-1 inhibitors can cause DRESS-like drug reactions with eosinophilia and organ involvement.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a few DRESS reports.

answers.name: Sitagliptin
answers.pearl: DPP-4 inhibitors are rarely reported to cause DRESS.

answers.name: Rufinamide
answers.pearl: Triazole anticonvulsant with rare DRESS reports.

answers.name: Clobazam
answers.pearl: Benzodiazepine antiepileptic with case reports.

answers.name: Fluconazole
answers.pearl: Azole antifungals are rare causes of DRESS.

answers.name: Atorvastatin
answers.pearl: Statins are a very rare reported cause of DRESS.

answers.name: Bupropion
answers.pearl: Case reports describe DRESS following bupropion use.

answers.name: Olanzapine
answers.pearl: Atypical antipsychotic with isolated DRESS case reports.

answers.name: Antimalarials
answers.pearl: Case reports link antimalarials to DRESS, including artesunate.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: stercoral ulcer, Heyde syndrome (association via acquired von Willebrand syndrome), cap polyposis, Klippel-Trenaunay rectal hemangiomas, colonic amyloidosis, GI GVHD, intestinal endometriosis (cyclic bleeding is uncommon), colonic schistosomiasis.

answers.name: Diverticular bleeding
answers.pearl: Painless large-volume hematochezia from a vasa recta rupture at the diverticular dome, usually stopping spontaneously.

answers.name: Hemorrhoids
answers.pearl: Bright red blood on the paper or in the bowl, painless, from internal hemorrhoidal cushions.

answers.name: Colorectal cancer
answers.pearl: Right-sided lesions bleed occultly and cause iron deficiency, while left-sided and rectal lesions cause visible blood.

answers.name: Anal fissure
answers.pearl: Pain with defecation and a small amount of bright red blood on the paper, typically at the posterior midline.

answers.name: Angiodysplasia
answers.pearl: Degenerative submucosal vein ectasias, mostly in the right colon of older adults, causing painless recurrent bleeding.

answers.name: Ischemic colitis
answers.pearl: Abrupt cramping pain then hematochezia, at watershed areas such as the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid.

answers.name: Ulcerative colitis
answers.pearl: Continuous mucosal inflammation from the rectum causing bloody diarrhea with tenesmus.

answers.name: Colonic polyps
answers.pearl: Large or ulcerated polyps can bleed intermittently.

answers.name: Infectious colitis
answers.pearl: Invasive organisms such as Shigella, Campylobacter and Salmonella cause bloody diarrhea with fever.

answers.name: Crohn disease
answers.pearl: Colonic or ileal ulceration can cause hematochezia, less often than in ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Brisk upper GI bleed
aliases: upper gastrointestinal bleeding presenting as hematochezia
answers.pearl: Roughly 10 percent of hematochezia with instability is an upper source, so consider a high BUN ratio and EGD.

answers.name: Post-polypectomy bleeding
answers.pearl: Delayed bleeding can occur up to about 2 weeks after polypectomy, higher with large sessile polyps and anticoagulants.

answers.name: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet-related bleeding
answers.pearl: Anticoagulation rarely creates a lesion but unmasks bleeding from diverticula, angioectasia or polyps.

answers.name: Radiation proctitis
answers.pearl: Telangiectatic friable rectal mucosa after pelvic radiation, with bleeding months to years later, treated with argon plasma coagulation.

answers.name: Clostridioides difficile colitis
answers.pearl: Usually non-bloody diarrhea, but fulminant disease can have hematochezia.

answers.name: NSAID-induced colopathy
answers.pearl: NSAIDs cause colonic ulcers and diaphragm-like strictures that can bleed.

answers.name: Meckel diverticulum
answers.pearl: Ectopic gastric mucosa ulcerates adjacent ileum causing painless maroon bleeding, classically in young children, and a technetium pertechnetate scan detects it.

answers.name: Rectal varices
answers.pearl: Portosystemic collaterals at the rectum bleed in portal hypertension and are distinct from hemorrhoids.

answers.name: Cytomegalovirus colitis
answers.pearl: Seen in immunosuppressed patients and IBD flares, with ulcers and bloody diarrhea, and viral inclusions on biopsy.

answers.name: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic straining and internal prolapse produce anterior rectal ulceration with bleeding and mucus.

answers.name: Stercoral ulcer
answers.pearl: Pressure necrosis from hard stool, typically in the rectosigmoid of constipated or bedbound patients, can bleed or perforate.

answers.name: Small bowel angioectasia
answers.pearl: A cause of obscure bleeding found by capsule endoscopy that can present as melena or hematochezia.

answers.name: Dieulafoy lesion
answers.pearl: A large submucosal artery eroding through normal mucosa causes massive bleeding, including in the rectum.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
answers.pearl: Submucosal tumors that ulcerate overlying mucosa and cause occult or overt bleeding.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor colitis
answers.pearl: Diarrhea with or without blood from CTLA-4 or PD-1 therapy, treated with steroids and infliximab or vedolizumab.

answers.name: Neutropenic enterocolitis
answers.pearl: Cecal inflammation in neutropenic chemotherapy patients, with right lower quadrant pain, fever and occasional bleeding.

answers.name: Heyde syndrome
answers.pearl: Aortic stenosis with acquired von Willebrand syndrome (loss of large multimers) fuels angiodysplasia bleeding.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Pain out of proportion to exam, with later bloody stools from transmural infarction.

answers.name: Aortoenteric fistula
answers.pearl: A herald bleed in a patient with an aortic graft should prompt CT angiography.

answers.name: Intussusception in adults
answers.pearl: Usually has a lead point such as a tumor in adults and can cause bleeding with obstruction.

answers.name: Amebic colitis
answers.pearl: Flask-shaped ulcers cause bloody diarrhea after travel, treated with metronidazole then a luminal agent.

answers.name: IgA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura with abdominal pain and GI bleeding, including in adults, from small vessel IgA deposition.

answers.name: Intestinal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Ileocecal ulcers and strictures can mimic Crohn disease and bleed.

answers.name: Intestinal lymphoma
answers.pearl: Ulcerated lymphomatous masses can bleed, as in MALT or enteropathy-associated T cell lymphoma.

answers.name: Behcet disease
answers.pearl: Deep ileocecal ulcers can bleed severely in patients with recurrent oral and genital ulcers.

answers.name: Colonic varices
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension produces colonic varices that bleed massively and are easily missed at colonoscopy.

answers.name: Gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease
answers.pearl: After allogeneic transplant, mucosal sloughing causes watery diarrhea and bleeding, aggravated by thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Kaposi sarcoma
answers.pearl: Violaceous mucosal lesions in AIDS can bleed even when skin disease is absent.

answers.name: Intestinal endometriosis
answers.pearl: Cyclic hematochezia with menses suggests mucosal involvement, which is uncommon.

answers.name: Juvenile polyposis syndrome
answers.pearl: Hamartomatous colonic polyps cause painless rectal bleeding, and SMAD4 carriers may also have hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Egg deposition in the colonic wall causes polyps, ulcers and bloody stool in endemic areas.

answers.name: Colonic amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration makes mucosal vessels fragile and causes bleeding or ulceration.

answers.name: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
answers.pearl: Venous malformations of the rectosigmoid in this limb overgrowth syndrome cause recurrent rectal bleeding.

answers.name: Cap polyposis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory cap-covered polyps in the rectosigmoid cause bloody diarrhea with mucus.

answers.name: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
answers.pearl: Cavernous venous malformations of skin and bowel cause chronic GI bleeding and anemia, with TEK mutations.

answers.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant mucocutaneous telangiectasias cause epistaxis and GI bleeding, mainly in stomach and small bowel.

answers.name: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
answers.pearl: STK11 hamartomatous polyps with mucocutaneous pigmentation cause bleeding and intussusception.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause cough.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: inhaled treprostinil, aztreonam lysine, colistin, mannitol, loxapine and zanamivir (airway irritation or bronchospasm rather than classic ADR cough), dasatinib (via effusion), daptomycin, minocycline, mesalamine, ergot dopamine agonists, gold, penicillamine.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: Bradykinin and substance P accumulate, causing a dry cough in roughly 10 to 20 percent of patients that resolves weeks after stopping.

answers.name: Inhaled medications
answers.pearl: Powder and propellant irritation trigger cough, mitigated by a spacer and mouth rinsing.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Block bronchodilatory beta-2 receptors, producing cough and wheeze in reactive airway disease.

answers.name: Aspirin and NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Cyclooxygenase inhibition shifts arachidonate to leukotrienes, causing cough and bronchospasm in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis presents with subacute cough, fever and dyspnea and can occur at low doses.

answers.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers
answers.pearl: Cough is less frequent than with ACE inhibitors but can still occur, particularly in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough.

answers.name: Tiotropium and inhaled anticholinergics
answers.pearl: Inhaled antimuscarinic powders commonly cause cough and throat irritation.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune-related pneumonitis presents as cough, dyspnea and ground glass opacities and is treated with steroids.

answers.name: Fentanyl
answers.pearl: A rapid IV bolus causes a brief reflex cough, reduced by slower injection.

answers.name: Inhaled insulin
answers.pearl: Cough is the leading adverse effect, and it can cause bronchospasm in asthma or COPD.

answers.name: Busulfan
answers.pearl: Late-onset alkylator pulmonary fibrosis occurs after prolonged therapy.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: Early pneumonitis or late fibrosis with cough and dyspnea.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Dry cough and dyspnea can occur, and interferon rarely triggers pneumonitis or sarcoid-like disease.

answers.name: Gefitinib and erlotinib
answers.pearl: EGFR-TKI interstitial lung disease is uncommon but potentially fatal, with cough and dyspnea.

answers.name: mTOR inhibitors
answers.pearl: Noninfectious pneumonitis with cough and dyspnea that often improves with dose reduction.

answers.name: Inhaled pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pneumocystis prophylaxis by aerosol causes cough and bronchospasm, so pretreat with a bronchodilator.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Infusion reaction cough and, rarely, delayed interstitial pneumonitis.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Pulmonary toxicity includes pneumonitis and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema.

answers.name: Inhaled tobramycin
answers.pearl: Cough and bronchospasm are the dominant adverse effects in cystic fibrosis patients.

answers.name: Inhaled treprostinil
answers.pearl: Cough is the most common adverse reaction of this inhaled prostacyclin for pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Interstitial lung disease, particularly with preexisting lung disease in rheumatoid arthritis.

answers.name: Mitomycin
answers.pearl: Pneumonitis and fibrosis with cough and dyspnea.

answers.name: Carmustine
answers.pearl: Delayed pulmonary fibrosis related to cumulative dose, sometimes years after therapy.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic pneumonia with cough and fever.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Rare eosinophilic pneumonitis presenting as cough and dyspnea after starting therapy.

answers.name: Inhaled aztreonam lysine
answers.pearl: Cough is a frequent adverse effect in cystic fibrosis, so a bronchodilator is given first.

answers.name: Inhaled mannitol
answers.pearl: Used for bronchial challenge and CF therapy, causing cough and bronchospasm.

answers.name: Inhaled colistin
answers.pearl: Cough and bronchospasm limit nebulized colistin.

answers.name: Daptomycin
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic pneumonia with fever, cough and hypoxia after about 2 to 4 weeks of therapy.

answers.name: Minocycline
answers.pearl: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia with fever, cough and peripheral eosinophilia.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Rare pulmonary complications include pneumonitis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.

answers.name: Bromocriptine and cabergoline
answers.pearl: Ergot derivatives can cause pleuropulmonary fibrosis with chronic cough and effusions.

answers.name: Dasatinib
answers.pearl: Pleural effusion is common and can cause cough and dyspnea.

answers.name: Gold salts
answers.pearl: Gold pneumonitis and bronchiolitis obliterans occur in rheumatoid patients.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: Can cause bronchiolitis obliterans and rarely a Goodpasture-like illness.

answers.name: Inhaled zanamivir
answers.pearl: Bronchospasm and cough can occur in asthma or COPD, so avoid it in these patients.

answers.name: Inhaled loxapine
answers.pearl: Boxed warning for bronchospasm, with cough and wheeze in patients with airway disease.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Interstitial pneumonitis and fibrosis cause dry cough and dyspnea with reduced DLCO.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Acute hypersensitivity (fever, cough, eosinophilia) within days, or chronic fibrosis after months of use.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: Dose-related pulmonary fibrosis worsened by oxygen and prior radiation.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations or consequences of obstructive sleep apnea.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: floppy eyelid, keratoconus, central serous chorioretinopathy, NAION, normal-tension glaucoma, IIH (associations rather than proven causal), cancer risk, gout, bruxism, adult enuresis, primary aldosteronism association, dementia risk.

answers.name: Excessive daytime sleepiness
answers.pearl: The main symptom, quantified by the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, from fragmented sleep.

answers.name: Snoring
answers.pearl: Loud habitual snoring with witnessed apneas is a core clue, but snoring alone is nonspecific.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Repeated arousals drive sympathetic surges and raise blood pressure.

answers.name: Atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Intrathoracic pressure swings and hypoxemia promote atrial remodeling.

answers.name: Resistant hypertension
answers.pearl: OSA is among the commonest causes of resistant hypertension, often with a non-dipping pattern.

answers.name: Type 2 diabetes
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation worsen insulin resistance independent of obesity.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: OSA raises stroke risk and is also common after stroke.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: OSA is both a contributor to and a comorbidity of heart failure, and central apnea predominates in HFrEF.

answers.name: Coronary artery disease
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia and sympathetic activation raise cardiovascular events.

answers.name: Motor vehicle accidents
answers.pearl: Sleepiness is associated with a several-fold higher crash risk.

answers.name: Morning headache
answers.pearl: Nocturnal hypercapnia and hypoxia cause vasodilation and morning headache.

answers.name: Nocturia
answers.pearl: Atrial natriuretic peptide release from negative intrathoracic pressure causes nocturnal diuresis.

answers.name: Gastroesophageal reflux
answers.pearl: Negative inspiratory pressure and arousals promote reflux, and CPAP often improves it.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Common comorbidity, with symptoms often improving with treatment.

answers.name: Impaired concentration and memory
answers.pearl: Executive dysfunction and attention deficits come from sleep fragmentation and hypoxia.

answers.name: Witnessed apneas
answers.pearl: The bed partner reports pauses in breathing followed by a snort or gasp.

answers.name: Metabolic syndrome
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia and visceral adiposity cluster with OSA.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Chronic nocturnal hypoxic vasoconstriction produces mild pulmonary hypertension, usually in overlap with lung disease or obesity hypoventilation.

answers.name: Erectile dysfunction
answers.pearl: Associated with nocturnal hypoxia and may improve with CPAP.

answers.name: Insomnia
answers.pearl: Frequent arousals can present as insomnia.

answers.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia independently worsens steatohepatitis and fibrosis.

answers.name: Nondipping blood pressure
aliases: lack of nocturnal blood pressure dip
answers.pearl: Failure of BP to fall at night on ambulatory monitoring suggests OSA.

answers.name: Polycythemia
answers.pearl: Hypoxia-driven erythropoietin can raise hemoglobin, usually mildly.

answers.name: Postoperative complications
answers.pearl: OSA raises the risk of postoperative hypoxemia, respiratory failure and unplanned ICU transfer, particularly with opioids.

answers.name: Nocturnal bradyarrhythmias
answers.pearl: Apnea-associated vagal surges cause bradycardia and pauses that resolve with CPAP.

answers.name: Nocturnal sudden cardiac death
answers.pearl: OSA shifts sudden cardiac death into sleeping hours rather than the usual morning peak.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease progression
answers.pearl: Hypoxia and sympathetic activity are linked with faster decline in eGFR.

answers.name: Adult nocturnal enuresis
answers.pearl: Seen with ANP-driven nocturnal diuresis and reduced arousal.

answers.name: Gout
answers.pearl: Nocturnal hypoxia increases uric acid production through purine degradation.

answers.name: Dementia risk
answers.pearl: Untreated OSA is associated with earlier cognitive decline.

answers.name: Bruxism
answers.pearl: Grinding occurs with respiratory arousals during sleep.

answers.name: AF recurrence after cardioversion or ablation
answers.pearl: Untreated OSA raises AF recurrence after rhythm control.

answers.name: Cerebral small vessel disease
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia and blood pressure surges associate with white matter damage.

answers.name: Primary aldosteronism association
answers.pearl: Frequently found in resistant hypertension with OSA, and CPAP may lower aldosterone.

answers.name: Normal-tension glaucoma
answers.pearl: Associated with OSA in observational studies, possibly via optic nerve perfusion.

answers.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
answers.pearl: Frequently coexists, and treating OSA can improve papilledema.

answers.name: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: OSA is a recognized risk factor, with nocturnal hypotension and optic disc crowding.

answers.name: Central serous chorioretinopathy
answers.pearl: Observational association, possibly through sympathetic activation.

answers.name: Cancer risk
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia is linked with more aggressive tumors in epidemiologic data.

answers.name: Keratoconus
answers.pearl: Reported association, perhaps from eye rubbing and floppy lids.

answers.name: Pickwickian syndrome
answers.pearl: Obesity with daytime hypercapnia, which overlaps with OSA in many patients.

answers.name: Cor pulmonale
answers.pearl: Chronic hypoxia and pulmonary hypertension strain the right ventricle.

answers.name: Floppy eyelid syndrome
answers.pearl: Easily everted lax upper lids with papillary conjunctivitis, strongly associated with OSA.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of secondary hypertension.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Geller syndrome, baroreflex failure, familial dysautonomia, lead exposure, hypercalcemia, autonomic dysreflexia, GRA, DOC-secreting tumors, Page kidney, porphyria, reninoma, CAH variants, Guillain-Barre dysautonomia.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: The most common secondary cause, via sodium retention and RAAS activation.

answers.name: Primary aldosteronism
answers.pearl: Hypertension with low renin, often with hypokalemia, diagnosed by the aldosterone-to-renin ratio.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: A common cause of resistant hypertension via sympathetic surges.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Abrupt rise, flash pulmonary edema or a creatinine jump after an ACE inhibitor suggests it.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Cortisol overwhelms 11-beta-HSD2 and activates the mineralocorticoid receptor.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Renal prostaglandin inhibition causes sodium retention and blunts antihypertensives.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen raises angiotensinogen and blood pressure.

answers.name: Coarctation of the aorta
answers.pearl: Upper extremity hypertension with weak femoral pulses and radiofemoral delay.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Systolic hypertension with a wide pulse pressure.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Diastolic hypertension from increased vascular resistance.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Chronic intake raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent manner.

answers.name: Decongestants
answers.pearl: Alpha-agonist effect raises blood pressure.

answers.name: Polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Cyst expansion activates RAAS, and hypertension often precedes GFR loss.

answers.name: Cocaine and amphetamines
answers.pearl: Sympathomimetic surges produce severe hypertension.

answers.name: Fibromuscular dysplasia
answers.pearl: String-of-beads renal artery disease in young women, causing hypertension.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid effect and sodium retention.

answers.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia raises vascular resistance and is associated with hypertension.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Afferent vasoconstriction and sodium retention cause transplant hypertension.

answers.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
answers.pearl: Raised blood viscosity and vascular tone with rapid hemoglobin rise.

answers.name: VEGF pathway inhibitors
answers.pearl: Reduced nitric oxide production causes hypertension in many treated patients.

answers.name: Preeclampsia
answers.pearl: Hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks of gestation.

answers.name: Acromegaly
answers.pearl: Growth hormone excess causes sodium retention and hypertension.

answers.name: Black licorice
answers.pearl: Inhibits 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, mimicking mineralocorticoid excess.

answers.name: Antidepressants
answers.pearl: Noradrenergic effects raise blood pressure, particularly with venlafaxine at higher doses.

answers.name: Paraganglioma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine-secreting tumors often with SDHx mutations.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy
answers.pearl: Obstruction activates RAAS and causes volume-related hypertension.

answers.name: Takayasu arteritis
answers.pearl: Renal or aortic stenosis causes hypertension in young women.

answers.name: MAO inhibitor-tyramine reaction
answers.pearl: Dietary tyramine with irreversible MAOIs precipitates hypertensive crisis.

answers.name: Increased intracranial pressure
answers.pearl: Hypertension with bradycardia from brainstem compression.

answers.name: Spinal cord injury autonomic dysreflexia
answers.pearl: Injuries above T6 cause paroxysmal hypertension triggered by bladder or bowel distension.

answers.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
answers.pearl: Renal artery stenosis and pheochromocytoma cause hypertension.

answers.name: Acute intermittent porphyria
answers.pearl: Autonomic neuropathy during attacks causes hypertension and tachycardia.

answers.name: Lead exposure
answers.pearl: Chronic low-level exposure is associated with hypertension and CKD.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Deoxycorticosterone excess causes hypertension with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
answers.pearl: A chimeric CYP11B1/CYP11B2 gene lets ACTH drive aldosterone, suppressed by dexamethasone.

answers.name: Renin-secreting tumor
answers.pearl: Young patients with hypertension, hypokalemia and high renin without renal artery stenosis.

answers.name: Page kidney
answers.pearl: External compression of the kidney by a subcapsular collection activates renin.

answers.name: Guillain-Barre autonomic dysfunction
answers.pearl: Fluctuating hypertension and arrhythmia from autonomic involvement.

answers.name: DOC-secreting tumor
answers.pearl: Rare adrenal tumors making deoxycorticosterone cause hypertension with hypokalemia and low renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Gordon syndrome
answers.pearl: WNK1/WNK4 mutations activate the thiazide-sensitive NCC, causing hyperkalemia and hypertension that responds to thiazides.

answers.name: Baroreflex failure
answers.pearl: After neck irradiation or surgery, paroxysmal hypertension and tachycardia occur because baroreflexes are lost.

answers.name: Familial dysautonomia
answers.pearl: Autonomic crises with hypertension occur in Ashkenazi children.

answers.name: Geller syndrome
answers.pearl: A mineralocorticoid receptor gain-of-function mutation makes progesterone an agonist, with severe hypertension in pregnancy.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Paroxysmal headache, sweats and palpitations, screened with plasma free metanephrines.

answers.name: Liddle syndrome
answers.pearl: ENaC gain-of-function causes hypertension with low renin and aldosterone, treated with amiloride.

answers.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
answers.pearl: Cortisol activates the mineralocorticoid receptor because 11-beta-HSD2 is deficient.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of jaundice.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mirizzi, hepatic sarcoidosis, sickle hepatopathy, PFIC, liver flukes, hydatid biliary rupture, EPP hepatopathy, AIDS cholangiopathy, vanishing bile duct syndrome, hepatic amyloidosis.

answers.name: Choledocholithiasis
answers.pearl: Biliary colic with obstructive jaundice and a cholestatic panel.

answers.name: Alcoholic hepatitis
answers.pearl: AST:ALT above 2 with bilirubin elevation after heavy drinking.

answers.name: Viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Hepatocellular injury with marked transaminase elevation.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Reduced conjugation and excretion capacity when decompensated.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer
aliases: carcinoma of the head of the pancreas
answers.pearl: Painless jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier sign).

answers.name: Hemolysis
answers.pearl: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with high LDH and low haptoglobin.

answers.name: Drug-induced liver injury
answers.pearl: Hepatocellular, cholestatic or mixed patterns, often from antibiotics and herbal products.

answers.name: Acute cholangitis
answers.pearl: Charcot triad of fever, jaundice and RUQ pain.

answers.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Hilar tumors cause progressive painless jaundice.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Arises in cirrhosis, with jaundice from biliary invasion or liver failure.

answers.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
answers.pearl: Dose-dependent centrilobular necrosis treated with N-acetylcysteine.

answers.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: Beaded biliary strictures, often with ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Antimitochondrial antibodies and raised alkaline phosphatase in middle-aged women.

answers.name: Sepsis-associated cholestasis
answers.pearl: Cytokines downregulate bile salt transporters, causing cholestasis in critical illness.

answers.name: Congestive hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Right-sided heart failure raises central venous pressure and causes cholestatic liver injury.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: ANA, anti-smooth muscle antibodies and high IgG with hepatocellular injury.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition cholestasis
