answers.pearl: Prolonged TPN, especially with lipid emulsions, causes cholestasis.

answers.name: Ischemic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Very high transaminases after hypotension that fall quickly.

answers.name: Postoperative biliary stricture
answers.pearl: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the commonest cause of bile duct injury.

answers.name: Hepatic metastases
answers.pearl: Diffuse infiltration or hilar nodes cause jaundice.

answers.name: Ampullary carcinoma
answers.pearl: Intermittent jaundice from tumor necrosis, with a better prognosis than pancreatic cancer.

answers.name: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Pruritus without rash in the third trimester with elevated bile acids.

answers.name: Chronic pancreatitis stricture
answers.pearl: Fibrosis of the pancreatic head narrows the intrapancreatic bile duct.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Abdominal pain, ascites and hepatomegaly from hepatic vein outflow obstruction.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets in pregnancy.

answers.name: Choledochal cyst
answers.pearl: Congenital bile duct dilation causing jaundice, cholangitis and cancer risk.

answers.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
answers.pearl: Z-allele protein accumulates in hepatocytes causing neonatal cholestasis or adult cirrhosis.

answers.name: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Late pregnancy jaundice, hypoglycemia and coagulopathy with liver failure.

answers.name: Resorption of a large hematoma
answers.pearl: Heme from a large hematoma overloads bilirubin conjugation.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Portal nodes compress the bile duct.

answers.name: Amanita mushroom poisoning
answers.pearl: Amatoxin causes delayed severe hepatocellular necrosis after initial gastroenteritis.

answers.name: Veno-occlusive disease
answers.pearl: After stem cell transplant or oxaliplatin, painful hepatomegaly, weight gain and jaundice.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Jaundice, kidney injury and hemorrhage after freshwater exposure.

answers.name: Graft-versus-host disease of the liver
answers.pearl: Cholestatic jaundice after allogeneic transplant, with skin or gut involvement.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis liver disease
answers.pearl: Thick bile causes focal biliary cirrhosis.

answers.name: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: Biliary strictures that mimic cholangiocarcinoma and respond to steroids.

answers.name: Hepatic amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Infiltration produces hepatomegaly with a cholestatic pattern and occasionally jaundice.

answers.name: Sickle cell intrahepatic cholestasis
answers.pearl: Sinusoidal sickling can cause severe cholestasis with extremely high bilirubin.

answers.name: Hepatic sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomas cause cholestasis and portal hypertension.

answers.name: Vanishing bile duct syndrome
answers.pearl: Loss of interlobular ducts from drugs, GVHD, rejection or Hodgkin disease.

answers.name: AIDS cholangiopathy
answers.pearl: Papillary stenosis and sclerosing cholangitis from Cryptosporidium or CMV in advanced HIV.

answers.name: Alagille syndrome
answers.pearl: JAG1 bile duct paucity with cardiac, facial and vertebral anomalies.

answers.name: Liver flukes
answers.pearl: Biliary flukes cause obstruction and cholangiocarcinoma risk in endemic regions.

answers.name: Hydatid cyst biliary rupture
answers.pearl: Rupture into the bile duct causes obstructive jaundice and cholangitis.

answers.name: Benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis
answers.pearl: ATP8B1 or ABCB11 variants cause episodic cholestasis with normal intervals.

answers.name: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis
answers.pearl: Bile salt transporter defects cause cholestasis, usually in children, with low GGT in types 1 and 2.

answers.name: Erythropoietic protoporphyria liver disease
answers.pearl: Protoporphyrin deposition in bile can cause cholestatic liver failure.

answers.name: Dubin-Johnson syndrome
answers.pearl: Benign conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with a black liver due to an MRP2 defect.

answers.name: Crigler-Najjar syndrome
answers.pearl: UGT1A1 deficiency causes severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, with kernicterus risk in type I.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper overload with low ceruloplasmin and Kayser-Fleischer rings, can cause hemolysis and liver failure.

answers.name: Gilbert syndrome
answers.pearl: Mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia increased by fasting, from reduced UGT1A1 activity.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hypercalcemia.
prompts.review_notes: Fewer than 40 valid answers exist, doubtful ones (theophylline, GH) dropped. Least sure: palopegteriparatide, abaloparatide, checkpoint inhibitors, paraffin/silicone injections, toremifene, dihydrotachysterol, TPN, compounded vitamin D errors, dialysate calcium, isotretinoin, androgens.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Reduce urinary calcium excretion and can unmask primary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Calcium supplements
answers.pearl: Excess intake, particularly with vitamin D or renal impairment.

answers.name: Vitamin D
answers.pearl: Excess intake raises 25-OH vitamin D and intestinal calcium absorption, and the effect can last weeks.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Shifts the calcium set point at the parathyroid cell, causing hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Vitamin A
answers.pearl: Excess promotes osteoclastic bone resorption.

answers.name: Teriparatide
answers.pearl: Daily PTH analog can cause mild transient hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Calcitriol
answers.pearl: Active vitamin D causes hypercalcemia, particularly with calcium supplements in renal disease.

answers.name: Alfacalcidol
answers.pearl: A prohormone vitamin D analog used in CKD that can cause hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Calcium-based phosphate binders
answers.pearl: Calcium load in CKD patients contributes to hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Intravenous calcium
answers.pearl: Excess or rapid infusion during hypocalcemia treatment.

answers.name: Thyroid hormone
answers.pearl: Increases bone resorption and can raise calcium in iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Starting therapy in breast cancer with bone metastases can cause a flare of hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Calcipotriene
answers.pearl: Topical psoriasis therapy used in excess can be absorbed systemically and cause hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Estrogen therapy in metastatic breast cancer
answers.pearl: Hormonal manipulation can cause a hypercalcemic flare with bone metastases.

answers.name: Abaloparatide
answers.pearl: PTHrP analog, with hypercalcemia reported less often than with teriparatide.

answers.name: Isotretinoin
answers.pearl: Retinoids increase bone resorption and hypercalcemia has been reported.

answers.name: All-trans retinoic acid
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia can occur in treated acute promyelocytic leukemia.

answers.name: Denosumab discontinuation
answers.pearl: Stopping denosumab can cause rebound bone turnover with hypercalcemia, particularly in children and high-turnover states.

answers.name: Recombinant PTH 1-84
answers.pearl: Replacement for hypoparathyroidism with a risk of overshoot hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Excess calcium and vitamin D in the solution can cause hypercalcemia.

answers.name: High-calcium dialysate
answers.pearl: Excess calcium delivered during dialysis, particularly with adynamic bone disease.

answers.name: Dihydrotachysterol
answers.pearl: Vitamin D analog used for hypoparathyroidism with a risk of prolonged hypercalcemia.

answers.name: Multivitamin megadosing
answers.pearl: Cumulative calcium and vitamin D with high intake.

answers.name: Compounded or mislabeled vitamin D
answers.pearl: Manufacturing and labeling errors have caused severe toxicity.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Reported via PTHrP, sarcoid-like reaction with 1,25 vitamin D, or primary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Palopegteriparatide
answers.pearl: Prodrug PTH replacement with hypercalcemia as a recognized risk.

answers.name: Toremifene
answers.pearl: Antiestrogen with a flare like tamoxifen in breast cancer metastatic to bone.

answers.name: Androgens
answers.pearl: Androgen therapy in breast cancer can cause hypercalcemia from bone stimulation.

answers.name: Paraffin and silicone injections
answers.pearl: Granulomas make 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, a literature-described cause after cosmetic augmentation.

answers.name: Milk-alkali syndrome
answers.pearl: Calcium carbonate with absorbable alkali causes hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis and AKI.

answers.name: Cholecalciferol
answers.pearl: Over-the-counter vitamin D3 megadoses are a common cause of toxicity, with levels staying high for weeks.

answers.name: Ergocalciferol
answers.pearl: High-dose prescription vitamin D2 can cause hypercalcemia, usually with very high 25-OH vitamin D levels.

answers.name: Chlorthalidone
answers.pearl: Thiazide-like diuretic with reduced urinary calcium excretion.

answers.name: Indapamide
answers.pearl: Thiazide-like diuretic that lowers urinary calcium excretion.

answers.name: Paricalcitol
answers.pearl: Selective vitamin D receptor activator for secondary hyperparathyroidism, with less hypercalcemia but still possible.

answers.name: Doxercalciferol
answers.pearl: Vitamin D2 prohormone used in dialysis patients with a hypercalcemia risk.

answers.name: Calcifediol
answers.pearl: Extended-release vitamin D prohormone for secondary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia risk.

answers.name: Vitamin D-fortified milk errors
answers.pearl: Documented outbreaks of hypervitaminosis D came from dairies adding excess vitamin D.

answers.name: Eldecalcitol
answers.pearl: Vitamin D analog used for osteoporosis in Japan, with hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria as recognized effects.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause thrombotic microangiopathy.
prompts.review_notes: Count is below the 55-70 target because doubtful items were dropped. Least sure (case-report level): ibrutinib, dasatinib, lenvatinib, sorafenib, checkpoint inhibitors, valacyclovir, trabectedin, pentostatin, prasugrel, ticagrelor, cocaine, ruxolitinib, OKT3, oral contraceptives, quinidine.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Dose-related endothelial toxicity causing TMA, often renal predominant, typically after months of therapy.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitor endothelial injury with TMA in transplant patients, dose related.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Endothelial injury with TMA in transplants, often responding to dose reduction.

answers.name: Clopidogrel
answers.pearl: Thienopyridine TTP-like illness, typically within the first 2 weeks of therapy and often with preserved ADAMTS13.

answers.name: Bevacizumab
answers.pearl: VEGF blockade leads to glomerular endothelial injury and a renal-limited TMA.

answers.name: Sirolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitor causing TMA, especially combined with calcineurin inhibitors.

answers.name: Everolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitor with TMA, particularly combined with cyclosporine.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Endothelial injury and TMA in hepatitis C or malignancy therapy.

answers.name: Sunitinib
answers.pearl: VEGF receptor TKI with hypertension, proteinuria and TMA.

answers.name: Carfilzomib
answers.pearl: Proteasome inhibitor with TMA, apparently more frequent than with bortezomib.

answers.name: Interferon beta
answers.pearl: Reported TMA after months to years of therapy in multiple sclerosis.

answers.name: Oxaliplatin
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent antibodies can cause hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and TMA.

answers.name: Aflibercept
answers.pearl: VEGF trap with hypertension and renal TMA.

answers.name: Bortezomib
answers.pearl: Rare proteasome inhibitor associated TMA.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Endothelial injury, most often with bleomycin in germ cell regimens.

answers.name: Pazopanib
answers.pearl: VEGFR TKI with TMA reports.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent antibodies like those of quinine can cause TMA.

answers.name: Ramucirumab
answers.pearl: VEGFR2 antibody, with rare TMA and proteinuria.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: TMA reported with cisplatin-based regimens, from endothelial injury.

answers.name: Estrogen-progestin oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Reported as a trigger for TMA in susceptible patients.

answers.name: OKT3
answers.pearl: Cytokine release causes endothelial injury and TMA in transplant recipients.

answers.name: Oxymorphone injection
answers.pearl: An outbreak linked injected extended-release oxymorphone to TMA, thought to be due to the excipient.

answers.name: Pentostatin
answers.pearl: Case reports of TMA with purine analog therapy.

answers.name: Ponatinib
answers.pearl: BCR-ABL TKI with vascular occlusion and reported TMA.

answers.name: Temsirolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitor in renal cell carcinoma, with TMA reported.

answers.name: Sorafenib
answers.pearl: Case reports of TMA with VEGF TKIs.

answers.name: Ticagrelor
answers.pearl: Case reports of TTP after starting therapy.

answers.name: Valacyclovir
answers.pearl: Case reports of TTP and TMA in patients treated for herpes viruses.

answers.name: Prasugrel
answers.pearl: Case-level TTP in patients on thienopyridines.

answers.name: Dasatinib
answers.pearl: Case reports of TMA in CML patients.

answers.name: Trabectedin
answers.pearl: Case reports of TMA in sarcoma patients.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Case reports describe TMA in patients on PD-1 therapy.

answers.name: Lenvatinib
answers.pearl: Hypertension and proteinuria with case-level TMA reports.

answers.name: Ibrutinib
answers.pearl: Rare case reports of TMA in B cell malignancies.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Case reports link cocaine use to renal TMA and hypertension.

answers.name: Ruxolitinib
answers.pearl: Rare case reports of TMA in patients treated for myelofibrosis.

answers.name: Ticlopidine
answers.pearl: Classically associated with TTP through anti-ADAMTS13 antibodies, which led to its decline.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Drug-dependent antibodies cause TMA with acute kidney injury, even from tonic water.

answers.name: Mitomycin C
answers.pearl: Cumulative-dose endothelial toxicity, with TMA after exposure of roughly 40 mg/m2 or more.

prompts.prompt: Name ways Cushing syndrome can present.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cyclic Cushing syndrome and Epidural/Mediastinal lipomatosis (rare, imaging-based clues); Food-dependent Cushing syndrome and ARMC5 hyperplasia (uncommon causes rather than presentations); Hypokalemia and Venous thromboembolism magnitude varies by etiology; Pituitary and adrenal incidentalomas are findings not symptoms. PPNAD and McCune-Albright scored as board traps.

answers.name: Weight gain
answers.pearl: Central obesity with weight gain is the most frequent feature, but it is nonspecific and often the reason the diagnosis is delayed.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Cortisol activates mineralocorticoid receptors and raises vascular tone, so resistant or early-onset hypertension is a key clue.

answers.name: Easy bruising
answers.pearl: Skin thinning and capillary fragility from glucocorticoid excess cause ecchymoses after minimal trauma.

answers.name: Violaceous striae
answers.pearl: Wide (over 1 cm) purple abdominal striae reflect dermal collagen loss and are more specific than thin pink striae.

answers.name: Moon facies
answers.pearl: Rounded plethoric face from facial fat deposition.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Cortisol drives hepatic gluconeogenesis and insulin resistance, producing new or worsening hyperglycemia.

answers.name: Proximal muscle weakness
answers.pearl: Steroid myopathy produces difficulty rising from a chair or climbing stairs.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Neuropsychiatric symptoms including depression are common and often improve after cortisol normalizes.

answers.name: Menstrual irregularity
answers.pearl: Hypercortisolism suppresses the gonadal axis, causing oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea in women.

answers.name: Dorsocervical fat pad
answers.pearl: A posterior neck fat accumulation (buffalo hump) is seen in Cushing syndrome though also in obesity and HIV lipodystrophy.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids suppress osteoblasts and increase bone resorption, so low bone density can be the presenting problem.

answers.name: Iatrogenic glucocorticoid exposure
answers.pearl: Oral, inhaled, topical, intra-articular or epidural steroids are the most common cause of cushingoid features.

answers.name: Hirsutism
answers.pearl: Adrenal androgen excess, especially with ACTH-driven disease or adrenal carcinoma, causes excess terminal hair in women.

answers.name: Acne
answers.pearl: Androgen excess and steroid effects on pilosebaceous glands cause acne.

answers.name: Fragility fracture
answers.pearl: Vertebral compression fractures in a young person should prompt screening for hypercortisolism.

answers.name: Hypokalemia
answers.pearl: Very high cortisol overwhelms 11-beta-HSD2, causing mineralocorticoid-like potassium wasting, most prominent in ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Poor wound healing
answers.pearl: Cortisol impairs fibroblast function and collagen synthesis, delaying healing.

answers.name: Opportunistic infection
answers.pearl: Cortisol impairs cell-mediated immunity, and Pneumocystis, fungal or other opportunistic infection can be the first presentation.

answers.name: Hyperlipidemia
answers.pearl: Hypercortisolism raises triglycerides and LDL and promotes visceral adiposity.

answers.name: Insomnia
answers.pearl: Sleep disruption and loss of the normal circadian cortisol nadir are common.

answers.name: Peripheral edema
answers.pearl: Sodium retention from mineralocorticoid effects causes leg swelling.

answers.name: Anxiety and irritability
answers.pearl: Emotional lability, irritability and anxiety are frequent neuropsychiatric manifestations.

answers.name: Venous thromboembolism
answers.pearl: Hypercortisolism raises factor VIII, von Willebrand factor and fibrinogen, causing a prothrombotic state.

answers.name: Cognitive impairment
answers.pearl: Memory and concentration deficits are linked to hippocampal effects of chronic cortisol excess.

answers.name: Nephrolithiasis
answers.pearl: Hypercortisolism causes hypercalciuria, leading to kidney stones.

answers.name: Hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: High ACTH, especially in ectopic ACTH or severe pituitary disease, stimulates melanocytes through MC1R.

answers.name: Glaucoma
answers.pearl: Chronic glucocorticoid excess raises intraocular pressure.

answers.name: Cataracts
answers.pearl: Posterior subcapsular cataracts develop with chronic glucocorticoid exposure.

answers.name: Psychosis
answers.pearl: Severe hypercortisolism can cause mania or psychosis that resolves after cure.

answers.name: Pituitary incidentaloma
answers.pearl: An incidentally found pituitary microadenoma on imaging may lead to work-up that reveals ACTH-secreting disease.

answers.name: Adrenal incidentaloma
answers.pearl: A sizeable minority of adrenal incidentalomas show autonomous cortisol secretion, often mild.

answers.name: Childhood growth failure
aliases: pediatric weight gain with short stature
answers.pearl: Children with Cushing syndrome have weight gain with growth deceleration, a clue that separates it from simple obesity.

answers.name: Hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids reduce intestinal calcium absorption and increase renal calcium excretion.

answers.name: Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis
answers.pearl: Severe ectopic ACTH syndrome presents with profound potassium wasting and alkalosis.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: Central fat deposition and upper airway fat contribute to OSA.

answers.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: Visceral adiposity and insulin resistance cause hepatic steatosis, sometimes the first clue.

answers.name: Ectopic ACTH syndrome
answers.pearl: Aggressive tumors such as small cell lung cancer or bronchial carcinoid cause rapid onset with myopathy, hypokalemia and hyperpigmentation rather than classic habitus.

answers.name: Adrenocortical carcinoma
answers.pearl: Adrenal carcinoma often presents with rapid virilization and cortisol excess together.

answers.name: Cyclic Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Episodic cortisol secretion with intermittently normal tests can cause fluctuating symptoms and falsely negative screening.

answers.name: Epidural lipomatosis
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoid excess causes fat deposition in the spinal epidural space, producing back pain or radiculopathy.

answers.name: Mediastinal lipomatosis
answers.pearl: Abnormal mediastinal fat on imaging is a rare radiologic clue to chronic hypercortisolism.

answers.name: Food-dependent Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Aberrant GIP receptor expression in adrenal tissue causes cortisol surges after meals.

answers.name: ARMC5 macronodular hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia due to ARMC5 variants is a familial cause of slowly progressive hypercortisolism.

answers.name: Primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease
answers.pearl: PPNAD, usually in Carney complex, causes ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome with a paradoxical cortisol rise after dexamethasone.

answers.name: McCune-Albright syndrome
answers.pearl: Somatic GNAS mutations can cause bilateral adrenal hyperplasia and neonatal Cushing syndrome.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypothermia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Multiple sclerosis and Neurosarcoidosis (case-report level hypothalamic involvement); Spontaneous periodic hypothermia (Shapiro syndrome, rare); Wernicke encephalopathy; Hypothalamic tumor; Clonidine and Beta-blockers (weak/modest effect); Pancreatitis dropped. Myxedema coma and Sepsis in neonates scored as board traps.

answers.name: Cold environmental exposure
answers.pearl: Prolonged exposure to cold air or water overwhelms heat production and is the commonest cause of accidental hypothermia.

answers.name: Cold water immersion
answers.pearl: Water conducts heat away about 25 times faster than air, so immersion causes rapid core cooling.

answers.name: Alcohol intoxication
answers.pearl: Alcohol causes vasodilation, impaired shivering and poor judgment, predisposing to hypothermia even at modest cold.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Septic patients, especially the elderly and neonates, may be hypothermic rather than febrile, which carries a worse prognosis.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Reduced metabolic rate and heat production lower core temperature, and myxedema coma classically presents with hypothermia.

answers.name: Advanced age
answers.pearl: Elderly patients have blunted thermoregulation, reduced shivering and less subcutaneous insulation.

answers.name: Homelessness
answers.pearl: Social vulnerability and inadequate shelter lead to exposure hypothermia even in mild weather.

answers.name: Malnutrition
answers.pearl: Low fat stores and limited calories reduce insulation and thermogenesis.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Glucose is required for shivering, and hypoglycemia impairs hypothalamic thermoregulation.

answers.name: Opioid overdose
answers.pearl: Sedation and reduced activity, plus central effects on thermoregulation, can lower body temperature.

answers.name: Sedative-hypnotic overdose
answers.pearl: Benzodiazepines and barbiturates depress hypothalamic function and mobility.

answers.name: Phenothiazines
answers.pearl: Antipsychotics impair central thermoregulation and shivering and predispose to temperature dysregulation.

answers.name: Neonatal prematurity
answers.pearl: Neonates have a high surface area to mass ratio, limited fat and immature thermogenesis.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency leads to impaired thermogenesis and hypoglycemia, which can present as hypothermia in adrenal crisis.

answers.name: Hypopituitarism
answers.pearl: Combined TSH and ACTH deficiency reduces heat generation.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic or brainstem lesions and immobility can impair temperature control.

answers.name: Traumatic brain injury
answers.pearl: Central injury and immobility, plus resuscitation fluids, contribute to heat loss.

answers.name: Major trauma with hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Hemorrhage, cold resuscitation fluids and exposure drive the lethal triad of hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Loss of skin barrier increases evaporative and conductive heat loss.

answers.name: Spinal cord injury
answers.pearl: Loss of sympathetic vasomotor control below the lesion causes poikilothermia.

answers.name: Dermatologic disease
answers.pearl: Erythroderma and extensive skin disorders cause large vasodilatory heat losses.

answers.name: Cold intravenous fluid infusion
answers.pearl: Rapid infusion of unwarmed fluids or blood products lowers core temperature.

answers.name: Surgical anesthesia
answers.pearl: General anesthesia redistributes heat and abolishes thermoregulatory vasoconstriction, often with open body cavities.

answers.name: Hypothalamic dysfunction
answers.pearl: Tumors, infiltrative disease or injury to the preoptic hypothalamus disrupt setpoint control.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Peripheral vasodilation, acidosis and infection can produce low temperature despite severe illness.

answers.name: Uremia
answers.pearl: Advanced kidney failure lowers metabolic rate and baseline body temperature.

answers.name: Liver failure
answers.pearl: Impaired gluconeogenesis and reduced heat production contribute to hypothermia in cirrhosis and fulminant hepatic failure.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Low cardiac output and vasoconstriction lower core temperature and impair rewarming.

answers.name: Hypotension and vasodilatory shock
answers.pearl: Distributive shock states impair thermoregulatory control and promote heat loss.

answers.name: Immobility
answers.pearl: Reduced activity and inability to shiver or seek warmth lower heat production, especially in the nursing home setting.

answers.name: Dementia
answers.pearl: Impaired judgment and wandering expose patients to cold without protective behavior.

answers.name: Beta-blockers
answers.pearl: Reduced sympathetic response may lessen shivering and cold-induced vasoconstriction in vulnerable patients.

answers.name: Clonidine
answers.pearl: Alpha-2 agonists reduce the shivering threshold and central thermoregulatory response.

answers.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Thiamine deficiency affects the hypothalamus and posterior hypothalamic lesions cause hypothermia.

answers.name: Hypothalamic glioma
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic tumors can produce episodic hypothermia from loss of thermoregulatory control.

answers.name: Cerebral palsy
answers.pearl: Chronic neurologic impairment and hypothalamic dysfunction can cause intermittent or chronic hypothermia.

answers.name: Spontaneous periodic hypothermia
answers.pearl: Rare syndrome of episodic hypothermia due to hypothalamic dysfunction, sometimes with agenesis of the corpus callosum.

answers.name: Anorexia nervosa with low body temperature
answers.pearl: Extreme low fat mass and low metabolic rate predispose to low body temperature and bradycardia.

answers.name: Sepsis in neonates
answers.pearl: Neonatal group B Streptococcus and other infections often cause temperature instability and hypothermia rather than fever.

answers.name: Myxedema coma
answers.pearl: Classic board scenario of severe hypothyroid decompensation presenting with hypothermia, bradycardia and hyponatremia.

answers.name: Therapeutic hypothermia
answers.pearl: Targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest, or deliberate cooling during surgery, intentionally lowers core temperature.

answers.name: Neurosarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Sarcoid infiltration of the hypothalamus can disturb thermoregulation and cause hypothermia.

answers.name: Multiple sclerosis
answers.pearl: Plaques involving the hypothalamus or diencephalon have been reported to cause episodic hypothermia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of microcytic anemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Linezolid (sideroblastic changes, case series); Copper deficiency (more often normocytic or macrocytic); Pyridoxine deficiency; Chronic alcohol use; Anemia of chronic disease (usually normocytic); Aluminum toxicity (historical); Chronic intravascular hemolysis (via iron loss). HHT, Plummer-Vinson and Cameron lesions scored as board traps.

answers.name: Iron deficiency anemia
answers.pearl: The most common cause of microcytosis worldwide, with low ferritin, high TIBC and elevated RDW.

answers.name: Thalassemia trait
answers.pearl: Microcytosis out of proportion to mild anemia with a high red cell count and a Mentzer index below 13.

answers.name: Chronic blood loss
answers.pearl: Gastrointestinal or menstrual blood loss depletes iron stores and is the usual route to iron deficiency in adults.

answers.name: Anemia of chronic disease
answers.pearl: Inflammation raises hepcidin, trapping iron in macrophages, and is usually normocytic but can become microcytic with chronicity.

answers.name: Beta thalassemia major
answers.pearl: Severe transfusion-dependent anemia from absent beta globin production with ineffective erythropoiesis.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Increased iron requirements from expanded red cell mass and fetal needs cause iron deficiency.

answers.name: Sideroblastic anemia
answers.pearl: Defective heme synthesis causes ring sideroblasts on marrow iron stain, with a microcytic hypochromic or dimorphic picture.

answers.name: Colon cancer
answers.pearl: Right-sided colon cancer commonly presents with occult bleeding and iron deficiency in older adults.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Duodenal villous atrophy impairs iron absorption, and unexplained iron deficiency may be the only manifestation.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: Chronic occult ulcer bleeding and reduced acid with iron malabsorption lead to iron deficiency.

answers.name: Poor dietary iron intake
answers.pearl: Vegetarian diets, infants on cow milk and malnutrition lead to inadequate iron intake.

answers.name: Lead poisoning
answers.pearl: Lead inhibits ferrochelatase and ALA dehydratase, causing basophilic stippling and microcytic anemia.

answers.name: Alpha thalassemia
answers.pearl: Deletion of alpha globin genes produces microcytosis, with hemoglobin H disease at three deleted genes.

answers.name: Hemoglobin E
answers.pearl: A common beta globin variant in Southeast Asians causing mild microcytosis, and E-beta thalassemia can be severe.

answers.name: Hemoglobin C disease
answers.pearl: Homozygous Hb C produces mild hemolysis with microcytosis and target cells.

answers.name: Atrophic gastritis
answers.pearl: Loss of gastric acid decreases conversion of ferric iron to the absorbable ferrous form.

answers.name: Gastric bypass
answers.pearl: Bypassing the duodenum and proximal jejunum, major sites of iron absorption, causes iron deficiency.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitor use
answers.pearl: Long-term acid suppression reduces absorption of nonheme iron and can contribute to deficiency.

answers.name: Hookworm infection
answers.pearl: Ancylostoma and Necator attach to small bowel mucosa and cause chronic blood loss, a leading global cause of iron deficiency.

answers.name: Frequent blood donation
answers.pearl: Each donation removes roughly 200 to 250 mg of iron and can exhaust stores in regular donors.

answers.name: Angiodysplasia
answers.pearl: Small bowel and colonic vascular malformations cause chronic occult bleeding, notably in older adults and aortic stenosis.

answers.name: Hemorrhoids
answers.pearl: Chronic bleeding from hemorrhoids may lead to iron deficiency.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Chronic bleeding, inflammation and malabsorption produce mixed iron deficiency and chronic disease anemia.

answers.name: NSAID use
answers.pearl: NSAID gastropathy causes chronic occult blood loss.

answers.name: Helicobacter pylori infection
answers.pearl: H pylori causes iron deficiency through occult bleeding, reduced acid and sequestration of iron, sometimes as the only manifestation.

answers.name: Hemoglobin Lepore
answers.pearl: Delta-beta fusion hemoglobin produces a thalassemia intermedia-like picture.

answers.name: Hemoglobin Constant Spring
answers.pearl: An elongated alpha globin variant that causes nondeletional alpha thalassemia, especially in Southeast Asia.

answers.name: Copper deficiency
answers.pearl: Reduced ceruloplasmin and hephaestin function impair iron transport and can cause microcytosis or sideroblastic changes, though anemia is more often normocytic or macrocytic.

answers.name: Pyridoxine deficiency
answers.pearl: B6 is required for ALA synthase and deficiency can cause a sideroblastic microcytic anemia, seen with isoniazid.

answers.name: Chronic alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol impairs heme synthesis and contributes to sideroblastic changes, along with associated poor intake and bleeding.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Prolonged linezolid can cause myelosuppression and reversible sideroblastic changes in marrow.

answers.name: Iron refractory iron deficiency anemia
answers.pearl: IRIDA is caused by TMPRSS6 mutations that raise hepcidin, producing microcytic anemia unresponsive to oral iron.

answers.name: X-linked sideroblastic anemia
answers.pearl: ALAS2 mutations cause X-linked microcytic anemia that may respond to pyridoxine.

answers.name: Atransferrinemia
answers.pearl: Absent transferrin causes severe microcytic anemia with iron overload in tissues despite deficient erythroid iron delivery.

answers.name: DMT1 deficiency
answers.pearl: SLC11A2 mutations impair iron uptake and cause microcytic anemia with hepatic iron overload.

answers.name: Pulmonary hemosiderosis
answers.pearl: Chronic alveolar hemorrhage traps iron in macrophages and can produce iron deficiency anemia.

answers.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
answers.pearl: Recurrent epistaxis and GI telangiectasia cause chronic iron deficiency.

answers.name: Plummer-Vinson syndrome
answers.pearl: Iron deficiency with dysphagia from esophageal webs and glossitis, memorized for boards.

answers.name: Cameron lesions
answers.pearl: Linear erosions in a large hiatal hernia cause chronic occult bleeding and iron deficiency.

answers.name: Epistaxis
answers.pearl: Recurrent nosebleeds are a surprisingly common source of chronic blood loss and iron deficiency.

answers.name: Hemodialysis blood loss
answers.pearl: Residual blood in dialysis circuits and frequent phlebotomy cause iron depletion in dialysis patients.

answers.name: Whipworm infection
answers.pearl: Trichuris trichiura causes chronic colitis with blood loss and iron deficiency, especially in children.

answers.name: Long-distance running
answers.pearl: Foot strike hemolysis, gastrointestinal bleeding and sweat losses plus hepcidin changes cause athletic iron deficiency.

answers.name: Cow milk protein enteropathy
answers.pearl: Whole cow milk in infants causes occult intestinal blood loss and low iron intake.

answers.name: Gastric antral vascular ectasia
answers.pearl: Watermelon stomach causes chronic occult bleeding and refractory iron deficiency.

answers.name: Aluminum toxicity
answers.pearl: Aluminum interferes with heme synthesis and iron utilization, producing microcytic anemia in dialysis patients historically.

answers.name: Chronic intravascular hemolysis
answers.pearl: Persistent hemoglobinuria from PNH or mechanical valves causes urinary iron loss and iron deficiency.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hypomagnesemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Digoxin (association, mechanism debated); Metformin (observational); Theophylline, Epinephrine, Dextrose (mostly intracellular shift, modest); Sirolimus; Colistin; Cidofovir and Streptozocin (Fanconi-type tubulopathy); EGFR TKIs; Edetate disodium. Cetuximab, Panitumumab, Foscarnet and Capreomycin scored as board traps.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Chronic PPI use impairs intestinal active magnesium absorption (TRPM6/7) and can cause severe hypomagnesemia after months to years.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Furosemide and related drugs block the thick ascending limb, reducing paracellular magnesium reabsorption.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Chronic thiazide use causes renal magnesium wasting, partly through reduced distal TRPM6 expression.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin causes renal magnesium wasting from tubular injury that may persist for months after therapy.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Gentamicin and related drugs cause tubular magnesium wasting with hypokalemia and hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Distal tubular injury produces magnesium and potassium wasting.

answers.name: Laxatives
answers.pearl: Chronic laxative use and diarrhea cause gastrointestinal magnesium loss.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Alcohol causes renal wasting, poor intake and gastrointestinal loss of magnesium.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibition reduces TRPM6 expression and causes renal magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Causes renal magnesium wasting, which can promote cyclosporine neurotoxicity and seizures.

answers.name: Carboplatin
answers.pearl: Less nephrotoxic than cisplatin but still associated with magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Insulin
answers.pearl: Insulin drives magnesium into cells, lowering serum levels, especially during treatment of DKA.

answers.name: Beta-agonists
answers.pearl: Intracellular shifts after beta agonist exposure lower serum magnesium transiently.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Causes renal magnesium wasting and nephrotoxicity, including with aerosolized use.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids can increase urinary magnesium loss modestly.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Osmotic diuresis increases urinary magnesium excretion.

answers.name: Zoledronic acid
answers.pearl: Intravenous bisphosphonates can lower serum calcium and magnesium.

answers.name: Pamidronate
answers.pearl: Bisphosphonate associated with hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia in some patients.

answers.name: Sirolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibition has been associated with renal magnesium wasting, though less than calcineurin inhibitors.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Parenteral nutrition without adequate magnesium, and refeeding with intracellular shift, causes hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Proximal tubular toxicity causes Fanconi syndrome with magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Observational data link long-term metformin use to lower serum magnesium.

answers.name: Theophylline
answers.pearl: Xanthines increase urinary magnesium loss and beta-adrenergic effects may shift magnesium into cells.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir disoproxil proximal tubulopathy can cause Fanconi syndrome with magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Colistin
answers.pearl: Polymyxins can cause tubular injury and electrolyte wasting.

answers.name: Streptozocin
answers.pearl: Nitrosourea with proximal tubular toxicity and Fanconi syndrome that includes magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Cidofovir
answers.pearl: Proximal tubular injury can cause Fanconi syndrome and electrolyte wasting.

answers.name: Necitumumab
answers.pearl: EGFR antibody with hypomagnesemia as a labeled adverse effect.

answers.name: Citrate anticoagulation
answers.pearl: Citrate in CRRT or apheresis chelates ionized magnesium and calcium and increases losses.

answers.name: Patiromer
answers.pearl: The potassium binder also binds magnesium in the gut, and hypomagnesemia is a labeled effect.

answers.name: Edetate disodium
answers.pearl: EDTA chelates divalent cations and can lower serum calcium and magnesium.

answers.name: Cetuximab
answers.pearl: EGFR antibodies block EGF-dependent TRPM6 magnesium channels in the distal tubule, a classic oncology board association.

answers.name: Panitumumab
answers.pearl: Another EGFR antibody that causes renal magnesium wasting in a large proportion of patients.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Causes hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia and hypokalemia through chelation and tubular effects.

answers.name: Capreomycin
answers.pearl: Tuberculosis injectable that causes tubular damage with magnesium, potassium and calcium wasting.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: Digoxin inhibits Na/K ATPase and is associated with renal magnesium loss, and low magnesium worsens digoxin toxicity.

answers.name: EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Agents such as erlotinib and afatinib have been associated with hypomagnesemia, though less than EGFR antibodies.

answers.name: Dextrose infusion
answers.pearl: Glucose infusion stimulates insulin and shifts magnesium intracellularly, especially in malnourished patients.

answers.name: Epinephrine
answers.pearl: Catecholamine beta-adrenergic stimulation shifts magnesium into cells.

prompts.prompt: Name ways pheochromocytoma can present.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Polycythemia (erythropoietin secretion, case-level); Ectopic ACTH secretion and VIP-secreting tumors (rare, case series); Dopamine-secreting silent tumor; VHL, MEN2 and NF1 scored as board traps (syndromic presentations).

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Sustained or paroxysmal hypertension from catecholamine excess is the most common presentation, and may be resistant to treatment.

answers.name: Headache
answers.pearl: Episodic severe headache is part of the classic triad and is linked to blood pressure surges.

answers.name: Palpitations
answers.pearl: Catecholamine-driven tachycardia and ectopy cause awareness of the heartbeat.

answers.name: Episodic sweating
answers.pearl: Profuse diaphoresis during spells is the third element of the classic triad.

answers.name: Paroxysmal hypertension
answers.pearl: Intermittent surges in blood pressure with normal readings between attacks suggest episodic catecholamine release.

answers.name: Anxiety or panic attacks
answers.pearl: Spells with fear, tremor and tachycardia mimic panic disorder.

answers.name: Tremor
answers.pearl: Adrenergic excess causes tremulousness during attacks.

answers.name: Pallor
answers.pearl: Alpha-mediated vasoconstriction produces pallor during episodes, as opposed to flushing in carcinoid.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Hypermetabolic state and catecholamine-driven lipolysis cause weight loss despite normal appetite.

answers.name: Adrenal incidentaloma
answers.pearl: Many pheochromocytomas are found incidentally on imaging, with attenuation above 10 Hounsfield units on noncontrast CT.

answers.name: Orthostatic hypotension
answers.pearl: Volume contraction and receptor downregulation cause postural hypotension despite hypertension, a useful clue.

answers.name: Hyperglycemia
answers.pearl: Catecholamines inhibit insulin and stimulate glycogenolysis, causing new diabetes or impaired glucose control.

answers.name: Chest pain
answers.pearl: Coronary vasospasm and demand ischemia can cause angina with normal coronaries.

answers.name: Nausea and vomiting
answers.pearl: Abdominal symptoms during spells reflect catecholamine effects on the gut.

answers.name: Hypertensive crisis
answers.pearl: Severe, sometimes life-threatening hypertensive emergency may be the first presentation.

answers.name: Anesthesia or surgery-induced hypertensive crisis
answers.pearl: Intubation, induction or manipulation of an undiagnosed tumor can provoke catastrophic catecholamine release.

answers.name: Medication-triggered crisis
answers.pearl: Drugs such as beta-blockers without alpha blockade, glucocorticoids, metoclopramide, opioids and tricyclic antidepressants can precipitate paroxysmal crises.

answers.name: Flushing
answers.pearl: Although pallor is more typical, flushing occurs in some patients, particularly with epinephrine-predominant tumors.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Catecholamines reduce gut motility and can cause severe constipation or pseudo-obstruction.

answers.name: Blurred vision
answers.pearl: Hypertensive retinopathy and spells can cause visual changes.

answers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Chronic catecholamine excess causes myocardial injury and heart failure.

answers.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surge can cause stress cardiomyopathy as the first presentation of pheochromocytoma.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Catecholamines cause ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias, including sudden cardiac death.

answers.name: Acute coronary syndrome
answers.pearl: Myocardial infarction with normal coronaries or from vasospasm can be the first sign.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Severe hypertension or catecholamine-induced vasospasm may cause ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke.

answers.name: Pregnancy-associated hypertension
answers.pearl: Pheochromocytoma can masquerade as preeclampsia and carries high maternal mortality if unrecognized.

answers.name: Shock with multisystem failure
answers.pearl: Pheochromocytoma crisis can present with fever, encephalopathy, shock and multiorgan failure that mimic sepsis.

answers.name: Lactic acidosis
answers.pearl: Severe catecholamine excess can cause lactic acidosis through impaired perfusion and increased glycolysis.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia suggests concurrent hyperparathyroidism in MEN2A or tumor production of PTHrP.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Fever without infection may accompany pheochromocytoma crisis through catecholamine and cytokine release.

answers.name: Pulmonary edema
answers.pearl: Catecholamine-induced pulmonary edema can be cardiogenic or noncardiogenic.

answers.name: Polycythemia
answers.pearl: Erythropoietin production by tumor (or volume contraction) can raise hematocrit.

answers.name: Cyclic Cushing-like features from ACTH secretion
answers.pearl: Some pheochromocytomas secrete ACTH and cause ectopic Cushing syndrome.

answers.name: Watery diarrhea
answers.pearl: VIP secreted by some tumors causes watery diarrhea with hypokalemia (WDHA).

answers.name: Mass effect or flank pain
answers.pearl: Large tumors cause abdominal or flank pain, or rare hemorrhage into the tumor.

answers.name: Bladder paraganglioma micturition attacks
answers.pearl: Bladder paragangliomas cause hypertensive spells provoked by urination or defecation.

answers.name: Head and neck paraganglioma
answers.pearl: Parasympathetic paragangliomas present as neck mass, hearing loss or pulsatile tinnitus rather than catecholamine symptoms.

answers.name: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
answers.pearl: VHL is a hereditary syndrome with pheochromocytoma, hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma, classic for boards.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2
answers.pearl: MEN2A and 2B carry RET variants with medullary thyroid cancer and bilateral pheochromocytoma.

answers.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
answers.pearl: NF1 is associated with pheochromocytoma in a small percentage of patients.

answers.name: Familial paraganglioma syndromes
answers.pearl: SDHx variants cause hereditary paraganglioma and pheochromocytoma, often presenting as extra-adrenal or multifocal disease.

answers.name: Dopamine-secreting tumor with normal blood pressure
answers.pearl: Dopamine-predominant paragangliomas may be silent or cause hypotension, nausea and flushing rather than hypertension.

answers.name: Hypertension in children
answers.pearl: Children with sustained hypertension warrant evaluation for pheochromocytoma, often due to a germline variant.

answers.name: Metastatic disease
answers.pearl: Malignant pheochromocytoma presents with bone, liver or lung metastases, most often with SDHB variants.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of lactic acidosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Multiple carboxylase deficiency, Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency and Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency (infant-onset, rare); Toxic alcohol ingestion (lactate may be spurious on some analyzers); Cocaine, Heat stroke and Cardiopulmonary bypass (mostly hypoperfusion); Mitochondrial disorders. MELAS, GSD type I and Metformin overdose scored as board traps.

answers.name: Septic shock
answers.pearl: Sepsis causes lactate elevation from hypoperfusion plus catecholamine-driven aerobic glycolysis, and persistent elevation predicts mortality.

answers.name: Hypovolemic shock
answers.pearl: Hemorrhage or severe volume loss reduces oxygen delivery and causes anaerobic metabolism.

answers.name: Cardiogenic shock
answers.pearl: Pump failure reduces tissue perfusion and causes type A lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Cardiac arrest
answers.pearl: Complete circulatory arrest causes global tissue hypoxia and profound lactate elevation.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Elevated lactate in acute bowel ischemia is a late and ominous sign of infarcted bowel.

answers.name: Metformin
answers.pearl: Biguanides inhibit mitochondrial complex I and gluconeogenesis, causing lactic acidosis especially with renal failure or overdose.

answers.name: Severe hypoxemia
answers.pearl: Respiratory failure or severe hypoxia shifts cells to anaerobic glycolysis.

answers.name: Seizure
answers.pearl: Generalized convulsions produce a transient lactate rise that clears within an hour or two.

answers.name: Liver failure
answers.pearl: The liver clears most circulating lactate, so cirrhosis or acute failure raises levels.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Intense muscular activity transiently outstrips oxidative metabolism.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Concurrent lactic acidosis occurs from volume depletion or from the precipitating illness.

answers.name: Severe anemia
answers.pearl: Marked reduction in oxygen-carrying capacity may cause tissue hypoxia.

answers.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
answers.pearl: CO binds hemoglobin and cytochrome oxidase, impairing oxygen delivery and use.

answers.name: Cyanide poisoning
answers.pearl: Cyanide blocks cytochrome c oxidase, halting oxidative phosphorylation and causing lactate elevation.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Lymphoma, leukemia and bulky tumors produce lactate through the Warburg effect and tumor burden or liver infiltration.

answers.name: Alcohol intoxication
answers.pearl: Altered NADH/NAD ratio and thiamine deficiency impair lactate clearance in alcohol use.

answers.name: Acute limb ischemia
answers.pearl: Reperfusion of ischemic tissue releases lactate.

answers.name: Thiamine deficiency
answers.pearl: Thiamine is a cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, so deficiency causes pyruvate to be converted to lactate.

answers.name: Epinephrine
answers.pearl: Beta-2 stimulation increases glycolysis and lactate production, as with infusions or pheochromocytoma.

answers.name: Albuterol
answers.pearl: Beta-2 agonists promote glycolysis and lactate release, especially at high doses in asthma.

answers.name: Propofol infusion syndrome
answers.pearl: Prolonged high-dose propofol impairs mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, causing lactic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis and arrhythmia.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis can cause lactic acidosis with prolonged therapy.

answers.name: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Stavudine, didanosine and zidovudine inhibit mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, causing lactic acidosis with hepatic steatosis.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Aspirin overdose uncouples oxidative phosphorylation and causes lactate accumulation with a mixed acid-base disorder.

answers.name: Toxic alcohol ingestion
answers.pearl: Methanol and ethylene glycol increase NADH and can raise lactate, and glycolate may falsely raise lactate readings on some analyzers.

answers.name: Lorazepam infusion with propylene glycol
answers.pearl: Propylene glycol is metabolized to D- and L-lactate, causing anion gap acidosis in high-dose benzodiazepine infusions.

answers.name: Severe asthma
answers.pearl: Respiratory muscle work and beta-agonist therapy both increase lactate.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Massive PE with shock and hypoxemia causes type A lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Hyperthermia increases metabolic demand and produces hypoperfusion with lactate rise.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Muscle injury and compartment ischemia release lactate.

answers.name: Nitroprusside
answers.pearl: Metabolism of nitroprusside releases cyanide, particularly with prolonged infusion or renal failure.

answers.name: Isoniazid overdose
answers.pearl: Overdose causes refractory seizures and high anion gap lactic acidosis by pyridoxine depletion.

answers.name: Acetaminophen overdose
answers.pearl: Severe poisoning and hepatic failure produce lactate elevation, and mitochondrial injury contributes.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: Severe falciparum infection causes lactic acidosis through microvascular sequestration and anemia, and predicts high mortality.

answers.name: Short bowel syndrome
answers.pearl: Colonic bacteria ferment carbohydrates to D-lactate, which is not detected by standard L-lactate assays.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine excess drives glycolysis, vasoconstriction and hypoperfusion.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Vasoconstriction, seizures and a hyperadrenergic state increase lactate.

answers.name: Cardiopulmonary bypass
answers.pearl: Hypoperfusion, hemodilution and hypothermia during bypass raise lactate, and elevated lactate predicts poor outcome.

answers.name: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired pyruvate oxidation shunts pyruvate to lactate, often with neurologic disease.

answers.name: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired gluconeogenesis causes fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in infants.

answers.name: Mitochondrial respiratory chain disorders
answers.pearl: Defects in oxidative phosphorylation, including complex I deficiency, cause chronic lactic acidosis.

answers.name: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired gluconeogenesis and anaplerosis cause lactic acidosis with hyperammonemia and ketosis.

answers.name: Leigh syndrome
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial disease with elevated lactate and basal ganglia lesions.

answers.name: Multiple carboxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Biotinidase or holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency causes organic acidemia with lactic acidosis, treatable with biotin.

answers.name: MELAS
aliases: mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with stroke like episodes
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes, from mtDNA mutations such as m.3243A>G.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease type I
answers.pearl: Von Gierke disease causes fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia and hyperlipidemia from glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause pulmonary hypertension or valvular heart disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Phentermine alone, Diethylpropion, Leflunomide, Interferon beta, Anagrelide (case reports or weak association); L-tryptophan (contaminant-related); St. John wort (case-control only); Gemcitabine and Conditioning chemotherapy (PVOD reports); Dopamine agonist bromocriptine (weaker valvular evidence); Protamine (acute reaction). Fen-phen, Aminorex, Dasatinib and Pergolide scored as board traps. Only about 47 answers because the valid list is limited; weak items were dropped rather than padded.

answers.name: Methamphetamine
answers.pearl: Stimulant use is a recognized cause of PAH resembling idiopathic disease, with worse outcomes than idiopathic PAH.

answers.name: Amphetamines
answers.pearl: Amphetamine-type stimulants are classed as definite risk factors for PAH.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine has been associated with pulmonary hypertension through vasoconstriction and chronic injury to the pulmonary vasculature.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Pulmonary fibrosis from amiodarone may lead to group 3 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: Pulmonary fibrosis and rarely pulmonary veno-occlusive disease with chemotherapy may cause pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Cabergoline
answers.pearl: Dopamine agonist with 5-HT2B agonism causing fibrotic valvular disease, particularly at high Parkinson doses.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Chronic pneumonitis and fibrosis can produce group 3 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Busulfan
answers.pearl: Alkylating agent causing pulmonary fibrosis and rarely PH.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Chronic therapy causes interstitial fibrosis that can lead to group 3 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferon therapy has been linked to PAH, with possible improvement after stopping.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: Alkylating agent associated with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease.

answers.name: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors
answers.pearl: Use in late pregnancy increases the risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and some data suggest PAH risk in adults.

answers.name: NSAIDs in late pregnancy
answers.pearl: Prostaglandin inhibition causes premature ductus arteriosus closure and persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn.

answers.name: Intravenous injection of crushed oral tablets
answers.pearl: Talc and insoluble fillers cause pulmonary arteriolar granulomas and PH, seen with injected methylphenidate, methadone or opioid tablets.

answers.name: Dexfenfluramine
answers.pearl: Anorexigen linked to both pulmonary arterial hypertension and valvular regurgitation.

answers.name: MDMA
answers.pearl: Ecstasy has 5-HT2B agonist activity and has been linked to valvular heart disease.

answers.name: Mitomycin C
answers.pearl: Chemotherapy associated with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease.

answers.name: Bromocriptine
answers.pearl: Ergot-derived dopamine agonist with less 5-HT2B activity, but associated with valvular regurgitation in some studies.

answers.name: Methysergide
answers.pearl: Ergot derivative that causes retroperitoneal, pleural and cardiac valve fibrosis through 5-HT2B stimulation.

answers.name: Anthracyclines
answers.pearl: Cardiomyopathy from doxorubicin or similar drugs can lead to group 2 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Ergotamine
answers.pearl: Chronic ergot use is linked to cardiac valve fibrosis through 5-HT2B receptors.

answers.name: Dihydroergotamine
answers.pearl: Ergot derivative with 5-HT2B activity and reported valvulopathy with chronic use.

answers.name: Carmustine
answers.pearl: Nitrosourea causing pulmonary fibrosis and pulmonary veno-occlusive disease.

answers.name: Epoprostenol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt interruption of prostacyclin infusion causes rebound pulmonary hypertensive crisis.

answers.name: Ponatinib
answers.pearl: Multikinase inhibitor with cardiovascular toxicity including pulmonary hypertension and vascular occlusion.

answers.name: Bosutinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor with reports of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

answers.name: Phenylpropanolamine
answers.pearl: Appetite suppressant and decongestant linked to PAH in case-control data.

answers.name: Carfilzomib
answers.pearl: Proteasome inhibitor with a labeled warning for pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Protamine
answers.pearl: Reversal of heparin with protamine can cause acute pulmonary vasoconstriction and catastrophic pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Benfluorex
answers.pearl: Fenfluramine-like drug marketed in Europe, causing valvular disease and PAH and withdrawn in 2009.

answers.name: Conditioning chemotherapy before stem cell transplant
answers.pearl: Alkylating regimens before HSCT have been associated with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease.

answers.name: St. John's wort
answers.pearl: Case-control and in vitro data suggest serotonergic herbal use may increase PAH risk.

answers.name: Gemcitabine
answers.pearl: Reported in association with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and pulmonary toxicity.

answers.name: L-tryptophan
answers.pearl: Contaminated L-tryptophan caused eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome, with some cases developing pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Fenfluramine for seizure disorders
answers.pearl: Low-dose fenfluramine for Dravet syndrome carries a boxed warning for valvular heart disease and pulmonary arterial hypertension, requiring echocardiographic monitoring.

answers.name: Inhaled nitric oxide withdrawal
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation of nitric oxide can trigger rebound pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Phentermine
answers.pearl: Phentermine alone has an uncertain association with PAH, mainly from case reports and the fen-phen experience.

answers.name: Diazoxide
answers.pearl: FDA warned of pulmonary hypertension in infants treated with diazoxide for hyperinsulinism.

answers.name: Trastuzumab
answers.pearl: Cardiomyopathy from HER2 therapy may lead to group 2 pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Anagrelide
answers.pearl: Platelet-lowering agent with pulmonary hypertension in its prescribing information and case series.

answers.name: Interferon beta
answers.pearl: Case reports link interferon beta used in multiple sclerosis to PAH.

answers.name: Diethylpropion
answers.pearl: Anorexigen with a possible association with PAH in epidemiologic studies.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Case reports of pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease in patients on leflunomide.

answers.name: Fenfluramine-phentermine
answers.pearl: Fen-phen caused valvular regurgitation and PAH through 5-HT2B stimulation and was withdrawn in 1997.

answers.name: Aminorex
answers.pearl: 1960s European anorexigen that caused an epidemic of PAH.

answers.name: Dasatinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor with an established risk of precapillary PAH that may reverse after stopping.

answers.name: Pergolide
answers.pearl: Ergot dopamine agonist withdrawn in 2007 for causing cardiac valve fibrosis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of neutropenia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Levamisole-adulterated cocaine (well documented but a street-drug history), Rituximab late-onset neutropenia (timing variable), Hemodialysis-related transient neutropenia (historical, cellulose membranes), Reticular dysgenesis (AK2; neonatal), Thymoma-associated pure white cell aplasia (rare, case-series level), Anorexia nervosa (usually mild). Felty syndrome, cyclic neutropenia and Chediak-Higashi scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Cytotoxic agents suppress marrow precursors, with neutrophil nadir typically 7 to 14 days after dosing.

answers.name: Viral infection
answers.pearl: Many viruses cause transient neutropenia through marrow suppression and margination, usually self-limited.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Overwhelming infection consumes neutrophils faster than the marrow can replace them, and neutropenia in sepsis carries a worse prognosis.

answers.name: Acute leukemia
answers.pearl: Marrow replacement by blasts crowds out normal granulopoiesis, so neutropenia coexists with high or low blast counts.

answers.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome
answers.pearl: Ineffective, dysplastic hematopoiesis produces cytopenias, often with hypogranular neutrophils and pseudo-Pelger-Huet cells.

answers.name: Aplastic anemia
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated marrow failure causes pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Clozapine causes agranulocytosis in roughly 1 percent, so absolute neutrophil count monitoring is mandated through a REMS program.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide and related antibiotics cause idiosyncratic or dose-related neutropenia, especially with prolonged courses.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired DNA synthesis causes megaloblastic marrow with ineffective granulopoiesis, hypersegmented neutrophils and cytopenias.

answers.name: Folate deficiency
answers.pearl: Like B12 deficiency, folate lack produces megaloblastic hematopoiesis and cytopenias including neutropenia.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus causes leukopenia through autoantibodies against neutrophils and marrow suppression.

answers.name: Radiation therapy
answers.pearl: Ionizing radiation to marrow-bearing bone, or total body exposure, ablates hematopoietic precursors.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV causes neutropenia through marrow involvement, opportunistic infection and antiretroviral or prophylactic drugs.

answers.name: Benign ethnic neutropenia
answers.pearl: Duffy-null associated neutrophil count is a normal variant in people of African, Middle Eastern or West Indian ancestry, with no infection risk.

answers.name: Methimazole
answers.pearl: Thionamide antithyroid drugs cause agranulocytosis in a small percentage, usually within the first 3 months, so fever or sore throat requires an urgent CBC.

answers.name: Hypersplenism
answers.pearl: Splenic sequestration lowers circulating neutrophils along with other cell lines, typically seen with portal hypertension.

answers.name: Epstein-Barr virus
answers.pearl: Infectious mononucleosis may cause neutropenia early, usually transient, before lymphocytosis dominates.

answers.name: Beta-lactam antibiotics
answers.pearl: Prolonged high-dose penicillins and cephalosporins can cause immune-mediated or marrow-suppressive neutropenia, typically after 2 or more weeks.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol suppresses marrow production and impairs release of neutrophils, particularly during acute infection.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Neutropenia in RA can reflect drug effect, immune destruction, or the large granular lymphocyte variant of Felty syndrome.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Thiopurine toxicity causes dose-related myelosuppression, much more severe in TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine can cause leukopenia, and rarely aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Marrow infiltration
answers.pearl: Lymphoma, metastatic carcinoma, granulomas or fibrosis can displace hematopoietic tissue, producing cytopenias.

answers.name: Autoimmune neutropenia
answers.pearl: Antineutrophil antibodies cause isolated neutropenia, primary in children and secondary to lupus or other autoimmune disease in adults.

answers.name: Large granular lymphocytic leukemia
answers.pearl: Clonal T-cell LGL expansion causes severe neutropenia, often with rheumatoid arthritis and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Chronic idiopathic neutropenia
answers.pearl: A diagnosis of exclusion in adults with persistent mild to moderate neutropenia and no secondary cause.

answers.name: Mycophenolate mofetil
answers.pearl: Mycophenolate causes dose-dependent leukopenia and neutropenia in transplant and lupus patients.

answers.name: Valganciclovir
answers.pearl: Ganciclovir and valganciclovir commonly cause dose-limiting neutropenia and often need G-CSF or dose reduction.

answers.name: Typhoid fever
answers.pearl: Salmonella typhi infection characteristically causes leukopenia and relative bradycardia.

answers.name: Copper deficiency
answers.pearl: Copper lack, from zinc excess, bariatric surgery or malabsorption, causes anemia and neutropenia mimicking MDS, with myeloneuropathy.

answers.name: Anaplasmosis
answers.pearl: Anaplasma and Ehrlichia infections typically produce leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and elevated transaminases after a tick bite.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Linezolid causes reversible myelosuppression, usually thrombocytopenia first, with neutropenia in prolonged courses.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Late-onset neutropenia can arise weeks to months after rituximab, typically self-limited.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Cytokine-driven marrow suppression and hemophagocytosis cause cytopenias along with fever, ferritin elevation and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
answers.pearl: CVID can be accompanied by autoimmune cytopenias, including autoimmune neutropenia.

answers.name: X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome
answers.pearl: CD40 ligand deficiency causes recurrent infections and neutropenia in a large share of patients.

answers.name: Dyskeratosis congenita
answers.pearl: Telomere biology disorder with nail dystrophy, reticulate pigmentation and leukoplakia, leading to marrow failure.

answers.name: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome
answers.pearl: SBDS mutation causes exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, neutropenia and skeletal changes.

answers.name: GATA2 deficiency
answers.pearl: GATA2 haploinsufficiency causes monocytopenia, neutropenia, MDS and mycobacterial or HPV infection.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease type Ib
answers.pearl: G6PT deficiency adds neutropenia and neutrophil dysfunction to hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly, causing inflammatory bowel disease-like colitis.

answers.name: Barth syndrome
answers.pearl: X-linked tafazzin (TAZ) mutation causes cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy and cyclic or chronic neutropenia.

answers.name: WHIM syndrome
answers.pearl: CXCR4 gain-of-function causes warts, hypogammaglobulinemia, infections and myelokathexis, a neutropenia from marrow retention.

answers.name: Thymoma-associated pure white cell aplasia
answers.pearl: Rare autoimmune selective aplasia of granulocytic precursors can accompany thymoma, similar to pure red cell aplasia.

answers.name: Levamisole-adulterated cocaine
answers.pearl: Levamisole cut into cocaine causes agranulocytosis, ANCA positivity and retiform purpura on the ears.

answers.name: Reticular dysgenesis
answers.pearl: AK2 mutation causes a severe combined immunodeficiency with absent neutrophils and lymphocytes and sensorineural deafness.

answers.name: Felty syndrome
answers.pearl: Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with splenomegaly and neutropenia, classic on boards.

answers.name: Cyclic neutropenia
answers.pearl: ELANE mutations cause neutrophil counts to oscillate roughly every 21 days, with fever and oral ulcers at the nadirs.

answers.name: Chediak-Higashi syndrome
answers.pearl: LYST mutation gives giant lysosomal granules, partial albinism, and neutropenia with recurrent infections.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause gynecomastia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Omeprazole and PPIs (inconsistent association), Tea tree/lavender oil (prepubertal case-series), Abiraterone excluded, Tamoxifen (paradoxical, rare), Penicillamine and Busulfan (older reports), Minoxidil (case-level), Growth hormone (mostly with prolonged high doses). Digoxin, Isoniazid and Metronidazole scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Spironolactone
answers.pearl: It blocks androgen receptors and inhibits testosterone synthesis, so gynecomastia is dose-dependent; eplerenone is largely spared.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: It acts as a weak androgen receptor antagonist and raises estradiol, unlike other H2 blockers.

answers.name: Ketoconazole
answers.pearl: It inhibits steroidogenic enzymes, lowering testosterone synthesis, which shifts the estrogen to androgen ratio.

answers.name: Finasteride
answers.pearl: A 5-alpha reductase inhibitor that raises the estrogen to androgen ratio, with breast tenderness and enlargement.

answers.name: GnRH agonists
answers.pearl: Androgen deprivation therapy lowers testosterone, and unopposed estrogen produces gynecomastia, which is why breast irradiation or tamoxifen is used preventively.

answers.name: Bicalutamide
answers.pearl: Nonsteroidal antiandrogens block androgen receptors with a rise in estradiol, producing gynecomastia in a large share of patients.

answers.name: Anabolic steroids
answers.pearl: Exogenous androgens are aromatized to estradiol and suppress the endogenous gonadotropins.

answers.name: Estrogens
answers.pearl: Direct estrogen exposure from therapy, including in transgender care, stimulates breast tissue.

answers.name: Risperidone
answers.pearl: Prolactin-raising antipsychotic that causes hyperprolactinemia, hypogonadism and gynecomastia.

answers.name: Metoclopramide
answers.pearl: Dopamine antagonism raises prolactin, which suppresses gonadotropins and produces gynecomastia.

answers.name: Haloperidol
answers.pearl: Typical antipsychotics block D2 receptors, raising prolactin and sometimes causing gynecomastia.

answers.name: Flutamide
answers.pearl: A nonsteroidal antiandrogen with high rates of gynecomastia, with a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Marijuana
answers.pearl: Cannabis use has been associated with gynecomastia, thought to be through reduced testosterone, though evidence is weak.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Chronic use causes hypogonadism and liver disease with impaired estrogen clearance.

answers.name: Testosterone
answers.pearl: Exogenous testosterone is aromatized to estradiol, and gynecomastia can also follow hCG or testosterone replacement.

answers.name: Dutasteride
answers.pearl: A dual 5-alpha reductase inhibitor that can produce gynecomastia, with a rate similar to finasteride.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Calcium channel blockers have been associated with gynecomastia, with verapamil most frequently reported.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Reported to cause gynecomastia through thyroid and endocrine effects, though the association is modest.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: TCAs have been linked to gynecomastia through prolactin or hormonal changes.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opiates suppress gonadotropin release, causing hypogonadism and gynecomastia, including with heroin and methadone.

answers.name: Chlorpromazine
answers.pearl: Phenothiazines raise prolactin and are an old classic cause of drug-induced gynecomastia.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors
answers.pearl: Captopril and enalapril have been reported to cause gynecomastia, which resolves with withdrawal.

answers.name: Nifedipine
answers.pearl: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are less commonly reported than verapamil, but documented.

answers.name: Domperidone
answers.pearl: A dopamine antagonist that raises prolactin, causing gynecomastia and galactorrhea.

answers.name: Ranitidine
answers.pearl: Other H2 blockers are far less implicated than cimetidine, but isolated cases are reported.

answers.name: Human chorionic gonadotropin
answers.pearl: hCG stimulates Leydig cell aromatase and estradiol production, leading to gynecomastia.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: Antiretroviral therapy, particularly efavirenz, has been associated with gynecomastia in men with HIV.

answers.name: Cyproterone acetate
answers.pearl: A steroidal antiandrogen with progestogenic activity widely used outside the US, causing gynecomastia.

answers.name: Alkylating agents
answers.pearl: Cytotoxic therapy damages Leydig cells and alters the hormonal milieu, causing gynecomastia during or after chemotherapy.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: A centrally acting antihypertensive linked to hyperprolactinemia and gynecomastia.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Anticonvulsants can alter sex hormone-binding globulin and lower free testosterone, with reported gynecomastia.

answers.name: Diazepam
answers.pearl: Benzodiazepines have been reported to cause gynecomastia, though the association is uncommon.

answers.name: Diethylstilbestrol
answers.pearl: A synthetic estrogen formerly used for prostate cancer, with a frequent breast effect.

answers.name: Reserpine
answers.pearl: A rauwolfia alkaloid raises prolactin through catecholamine depletion, an old cause of gynecomastia.

answers.name: Omeprazole
answers.pearl: Proton pump inhibitors have been reported in case series and observational data, though the association is inconsistent.

answers.name: Sulpiride
answers.pearl: A substituted benzamide antipsychotic that strongly raises prolactin.

answers.name: Busulfan
answers.pearl: An alkylating agent with older reports of gynecomastia, thought to reflect gonadal damage.

answers.name: Penicillamine
answers.pearl: Reported in case series, including with Wilson disease treatment.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Paradoxically reported to cause gynecomastia in rare cases despite being used to treat it.

answers.name: Minoxidil
answers.pearl: Oral minoxidil has been reported to cause gynecomastia in case reports.

answers.name: Growth hormone
answers.pearl: Recombinant GH therapy has been linked to gynecomastia in children and adults.

answers.name: Lavender oil
answers.pearl: Topical lavender and tea tree oils are weakly estrogenic and anti-androgenic, with prepubertal gynecomastia in case series.

answers.name: Digoxin
answers.pearl: Digitalis has a steroid-like structure that binds estrogen receptors, a boards classic cause.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid is a classic board-listed cause, with a vague hormonal mechanism.

answers.name: Metronidazole
answers.pearl: Reported to cause gynecomastia, featuring in standard mnemonic tables.

prompts.prompt: Name ways multiple myeloma can present.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Spurious pseudohyponatremia (historical with older assays), Type 1 renal tubular acidosis (reported), CNS myeloma and pleural myeloma (rare extramedullary), Orthostatic hypotension via amyloid (AL amyloidosis rather than myeloma per se), Acquired von Willebrand syndrome, Cutaneous plasmacytoma. Rouleaux, Bence Jones proteinuria and raccoon eyes scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Bone pain
answers.pearl: Osteolytic lesions cause pain, most often in the back or ribs, and worse with movement.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Often multifactorial, reflecting anemia, hypercalcemia, and renal impairment.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Normocytic normochromic anemia results from marrow replacement and renal dysfunction.

answers.name: Pathologic fracture
answers.pearl: Lytic bone destruction weakens bone, so fractures occur with minimal trauma.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Osteoclast activation by cytokines releases calcium, causing confusion, constipation, polyuria and AKI.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Cast nephropathy from free light chains and hypercalcemia are leading mechanisms of renal failure.

answers.name: Recurrent infections
answers.pearl: Hypogammaglobulinemia of normal immunoglobulins impairs host defense, often with pneumococcus and gram-negative bacilli.

answers.name: Vertebral compression fracture
answers.pearl: Often the presenting event, with acute back pain and loss of height.

answers.name: Lytic bone lesions
answers.pearl: Punched-out lesions on skeletal survey or CT are characteristic and lack a sclerotic rim.
