answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms accompany advanced disease.

answers.name: Spinal cord compression
answers.pearl: Vertebral collapse or paraspinal plasmacytoma may compress the cord, causing weakness, sensory loss and bladder dysfunction.

answers.name: Elevated total protein
answers.pearl: A widened protein gap, with total protein exceeding albumin by more than 4 g/dL, is a clue to a monoclonal protein.

answers.name: Elevated ESR
answers.pearl: Paraprotein increases rouleaux and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate, sometimes above 100.

answers.name: Proteinuria
answers.pearl: Light chains pass through the glomerulus, and dipstick detects mostly albumin, so urine protein electrophoresis is needed.

answers.name: Confusion
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia, uremia or hyperviscosity can cause altered mental status.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Diffuse osteopenia on imaging in a patient with an unexplained cause should prompt SPEP.

answers.name: Solitary plasmacytoma
answers.pearl: A single plasma cell tumor of bone or soft tissue without marrow involvement may later progress to myeloma.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Caused by amyloid deposition, POEMS or treatments such as bortezomib and thalidomide.

answers.name: Pneumococcal sepsis
answers.pearl: Encapsulated organism infections occur from defective antibody production.

answers.name: Hyperviscosity syndrome
answers.pearl: Very high paraprotein levels cause mucosal bleeding, visual changes and neurologic symptoms, more often with IgA or IgG3.

answers.name: Radiculopathy
answers.pearl: Nerve root compression from vertebral collapse or plasmacytoma causes radicular pain.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia slows gastrointestinal motility.

answers.name: Herpes zoster
answers.pearl: Cellular immune dysfunction and treatment increase risk of shingles.

answers.name: Cast nephropathy
answers.pearl: Light chains form casts with Tamm-Horsfall protein in the distal tubule, giving myeloma kidney.

answers.name: Pancytopenia
answers.pearl: Extensive marrow replacement can result in leukopenia and thrombocytopenia as well as anemia.

answers.name: AKI after IV contrast
answers.pearl: Dehydration, NSAIDs, contrast and hypercalcemia commonly precipitate acute kidney injury in a patient with undiagnosed myeloma.

answers.name: Blurred vision
answers.pearl: Hyperviscosity can cause retinal vein engorgement and visual disturbance.

answers.name: Polyuria
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus produces polyuria and dehydration.

answers.name: AL amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Light chain amyloid deposits cause nephrotic syndrome, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy and macroglossia.

answers.name: Bleeding
answers.pearl: Hyperviscosity, thrombocytopenia, and amyloid-related factor X deficiency can cause mucosal or easy bleeding.

answers.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposition in the flexor retinaculum may be the first sign.

answers.name: Palpable bone mass
answers.pearl: Expansile lesions of the skull, ribs or sternum may be felt as soft tissue masses.

answers.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
aliases: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
answers.pearl: Cardiac amyloid presents with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, low voltage on ECG and thickened walls.

answers.name: Low anion gap
answers.pearl: Cationic IgG paraprotein can lower the calculated anion gap.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Monoclonal cryoglobulins can cause purpura, Raynaud phenomenon and glomerulonephritis in plasma cell disorders.

answers.name: Macroglossia
answers.pearl: Amyloid deposition enlarges the tongue.

answers.name: Light chain Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Light chains accumulate in proximal tubular cells, leading to glycosuria, phosphaturia and proximal tubular acidosis.

answers.name: Autonomic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration of autonomic nerves produces orthostatic hypotension, gastroparesis and bladder dysfunction.

answers.name: Plasma cell leukemia
answers.pearl: More than 2 x 10^9/L circulating plasma cells signals aggressive disease with a poor prognosis.

answers.name: Extramedullary plasmacytoma
answers.pearl: Soft tissue tumors can occur in the upper airway, liver, skin or other sites, usually with advanced disease.

answers.name: Type 1 renal tubular acidosis
answers.pearl: Light chain damage to the distal nephron can cause a nongap acidosis with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome
answers.pearl: Paraprotein can bind von Willebrand factor, causing mucocutaneous bleeding with low VWF activity.

answers.name: Malignant pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Myelomatous pleural effusion occurs in less than 1 percent, usually with advanced disease.

answers.name: Cutaneous plasmacytoma
answers.pearl: Skin involvement presents as violaceous nodules in advanced disease.

answers.name: CNS myeloma
answers.pearl: Meningeal or parenchymal myeloma is rare and carries a poor prognosis.

answers.name: Rouleaux formation
answers.pearl: Stacked red cells on smear due to increased globulins, a standard boards finding.

answers.name: Bence Jones proteinuria
answers.pearl: Free light chains in urine are not detected by dipstick, detected by urine protein electrophoresis.

answers.name: Raccoon eyes
answers.pearl: Periorbital purpura classically from amyloid involvement of small vessels, a board-famous sign.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyperuricemia or gout.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Down syndrome (reported association), Obstructive sleep apnea (hypoxia-driven purine catabolism; modest evidence), Ketogenic diet (transient), Teriparatide (mild), Sarcoidosis (inconsistent), Hereditary fructose intolerance (older literature), Tacrolimus. Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, Glycogen storage disease type I and Lead nephropathy scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced glomerular filtration lowers renal urate excretion, the main route of elimination.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Volume contraction and competition at organic anion transporters reduce urate secretion.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Furosemide and similar agents increase proximal urate reabsorption through volume depletion.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Alcohol raises purine breakdown and lactate, and beer also contains guanosine, increasing urate.

answers.name: Obesity
answers.pearl: Insulin resistance reduces renal urate excretion and adiposity increases production.

answers.name: Purine-rich diet
answers.pearl: Red meat, organ meats and shellfish increase the urate pool, though the effect on serum levels is modest.

answers.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
answers.pearl: Massive cell death releases nucleic acids that are converted to uric acid, risking urate nephropathy.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion increases proximal urate reabsorption.

answers.name: Low-dose aspirin
answers.pearl: Salicylates at low dose inhibit tubular urate secretion, while high doses are uricosuric.

answers.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm
answers.pearl: High cell turnover increases purine breakdown and urate production.

answers.name: Hematologic malignancy
answers.pearl: Leukemia and lymphoma raise nucleic acid turnover, even before cytotoxic therapy.

answers.name: Fructose intake
answers.pearl: Fructose metabolism consumes ATP and generates AMP, driving purine degradation to urate.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors reduce renal urate clearance, causing hyperuricemia and gout in transplant recipients.

answers.name: Pyrazinamide
answers.pearl: Its metabolite pyrazinoic acid blocks tubular urate secretion, raising serum urate during TB therapy.

answers.name: Psoriasis
answers.pearl: Rapid keratinocyte turnover increases urate production.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Associated with reduced renal urate clearance and often treated with urate-raising diuretics.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Decreased renal blood flow and GFR lower urate excretion.

answers.name: Niacin
answers.pearl: Nicotinic acid competes with urate for renal secretion and raises serum urate.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Reduced renal perfusion and diuretics both raise urate, and xanthine oxidase activity is higher.

answers.name: Lactic acidosis
answers.pearl: Organic acids compete with urate for tubular secretion.

answers.name: Starvation
answers.pearl: Ketones compete with urate for renal tubular secretion, and fasting raises serum urate.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Increased turnover of red cell nucleotides releases purines.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Muscle ATP breakdown and lactate production transiently raise urate.

answers.name: Preeclampsia
answers.pearl: Reduced renal clearance raises urate, which correlates with disease severity.

answers.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia and tubular effects raise urate, with gout seen in a minority.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Muscle breakdown releases purine nucleotides and impairs renal clearance.

answers.name: Ethambutol
answers.pearl: Reduces renal urate excretion, causing hyperuricemia in a minority.

answers.name: Menopause
answers.pearl: Loss of estrogen's uricosuric effect increases serum urate after menopause.

answers.name: Tacrolimus
answers.pearl: Reduces renal urate clearance, though less than cyclosporine.

answers.name: Genetic variants of urate transporters
answers.pearl: Polymorphisms in SLC2A9, ABCG2 and URAT1 alter renal and gut urate handling, explaining familial hyperuricemia.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Associated with hyperuricemia in some series, probably from impaired renal clearance.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: Intermittent hypoxia increases ATP breakdown and purine catabolism.

answers.name: Ketogenic diet
answers.pearl: Ketones compete with urate for excretion, causing transient hyperuricemia.

answers.name: Teriparatide
answers.pearl: Can cause mild, usually asymptomatic hyperuricemia.

answers.name: Down syndrome
answers.pearl: Increased urate production is described in trisomy 21, with a higher prevalence of hyperuricemia.

answers.name: Kelley-Seegmiller syndrome
answers.pearl: Partial HGPRT deficiency causes purine overproduction with gout and nephrolithiasis, without severe neurologic disease.

answers.name: Familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant UMOD or REN mutations cause reduced fractional excretion of urate, gout and progressive CKD.

answers.name: Hereditary fructose intolerance
answers.pearl: Fructose-1-phosphate accumulation depletes ATP and sequesters phosphate, generating urate.

answers.name: PRPP synthetase superactivity
answers.pearl: X-linked gain of function increases PRPP and de novo purine synthesis, causing gout and sensorineural deafness.

answers.name: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome
answers.pearl: Complete HGPRT deficiency causes hyperuricemia, self-mutilation, dystonia and intellectual disability.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease type I
answers.pearl: G6Pase deficiency causes hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis and overproduction plus reduced excretion of urate.

answers.name: Lead nephropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic lead exposure impairs tubular urate excretion, leading to saturnine gout.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of elevated aminotransferases (AST or ALT).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Macro-AST (benign but needs electrophoresis to confirm), Anorexia nervosa (usually mild, hepatocyte autophagy), Adult-onset Still disease, Brucellosis, Q fever, Syphilis (secondary), Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency, Pompe disease (muscle-derived), Cocaine/MDMA. Wilson disease, Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and Amanita phalloides scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
answers.pearl: The most common cause of mild chronic transaminase elevation, with ALT usually exceeding AST.

answers.name: Alcohol-associated liver disease
answers.pearl: Classically AST greater than ALT, with a ratio above 2 and values usually below 300.

answers.name: Hepatitis C
answers.pearl: Chronic infection typically causes fluctuating mild ALT elevation.

answers.name: Hepatitis B
answers.pearl: Both acute infection and chronic flares cause hepatocellular injury, with marked ALT increases in flares.

answers.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
answers.pearl: Overdose causes centrilobular necrosis with transaminases in the thousands, treated with N-acetylcysteine.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Mild transaminase elevations are common and usually do not require stopping the drug.

answers.name: Hepatitis A
answers.pearl: Acute infection causes a marked ALT rise, often over 1000, that resolves without chronic disease.

answers.name: Ischemic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Hypoperfusion causes a rapid, massive aminotransferase surge that falls quickly after resuscitation.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Young to middle-aged women with high IgG, ANA or anti-smooth muscle antibodies, responding to steroids.

answers.name: Choledocholithiasis
answers.pearl: Acute bile duct obstruction can cause a transient aminotransferase spike before cholestatic enzymes rise.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Iron overload causes hepatocellular injury, with elevated ferritin and transferrin saturation.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: AST rises from skeletal muscle injury along with a very elevated CK.

answers.name: Congestive hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Right heart failure causes passive hepatic congestion with mild aminotransferase and ALP elevation.

answers.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
answers.pearl: The most common cause of idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury, often cholestatic or mixed and delayed after therapy.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Dose-independent hepatotoxicity occurs in a small share of users, more with age, alcohol and slow acetylators.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Unexplained mild transaminase elevations can be the only manifestation, resolving with a gluten-free diet.

answers.name: Epstein-Barr virus
answers.pearl: Infectious mononucleosis commonly causes mild hepatitis in the first weeks.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Skeletal muscle release raises AST and ALT, usually normalizing within days.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Chronic therapy can cause fibrosis and aminotransferase elevations, particularly with alcohol, obesity or diabetes.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Common asymptomatic transaminase rise, and rarely fulminant hepatotoxicity or hyperammonemia.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Cytokine-mediated cholestasis and hypoperfusion can raise transaminases.

answers.name: Herbal supplements
answers.pearl: Green tea extract, kava, comfrey and turmeric are recognized causes of hepatotoxicity.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Causes mild elevations commonly and occasionally steatohepatitis or phospholipidosis.

answers.name: Anabolic steroids
answers.pearl: Androgens cause cholestatic injury, peliosis hepatis and aminotransferase rise, partly from muscle.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Tumor can produce mild aminotransferase elevations along with those of underlying cirrhosis.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Predominantly cholestatic, but ALT and AST are often mildly raised.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Thyrotoxicosis can raise AST, ALT and ALP via increased hepatic metabolism and hypoxia.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic vein outflow obstruction causes hepatomegaly, ascites and elevated aminotransferases.

answers.name: Hepatitis E
answers.pearl: Acute hepatitis acquired by fecal-oral spread, with high mortality in pregnancy.

answers.name: Herpes simplex hepatitis
answers.pearl: Fulminant hepatitis with very high transaminases, fever and minimal jaundice, seen in pregnancy and immunosuppression.

answers.name: Polymyositis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory myopathy raises AST and ALT from muscle, so a high CK identifies the source.

answers.name: Hemolysis
answers.pearl: Red cell destruction releases AST, usually in association with high LDH and low haptoglobin.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets complicate preeclampsia, often in the third trimester.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Hyperthermia causes direct hepatocellular injury and ischemia with dramatic aminotransferase rise.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Cocaine and MDMA cause hepatic necrosis through hyperthermia and ischemia.

answers.name: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
answers.pearl: Third-trimester microvesicular steatosis with hypoglycemia, coagulopathy and elevated transaminases.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Reported cause of reversible mild aminotransferase elevation.

answers.name: Anorexia nervosa
answers.pearl: Starvation causes mild to marked transaminase rise from hepatocyte autophagy, resolving with refeeding.

answers.name: Q fever
answers.pearl: Coxiella burnetii often causes granulomatous hepatitis with fever and elevated enzymes.

answers.name: Dengue
answers.pearl: Acute dengue causes AST-predominant elevation, often with thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Weil disease causes jaundice with only modestly raised transaminases and renal failure.

answers.name: Adult-onset Still disease
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation with fever, rash and arthritis commonly raises aminotransferases.

answers.name: Pompe disease
answers.pearl: Acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency raises AST, ALT and CK from muscle damage.

answers.name: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency
answers.pearl: Wolman disease and cholesteryl ester storage disease cause hepatomegaly, steatosis, dyslipidemia and elevated transaminases.

answers.name: Macro-AST
answers.pearl: Complexing of AST with immunoglobulin gives persistently elevated AST with normal ALT and no liver disease.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper accumulation causes hepatitis with a low ALP-to-bilirubin ratio and Coombs-negative hemolysis.

answers.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
answers.pearl: Misfolded Z protein accumulates in hepatocytes, causing liver disease with emphysema.

answers.name: Amanita phalloides poisoning
answers.pearl: Alpha-amanitin causes delayed severe hepatocyte necrosis after a latent GI phase.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Modafinil, Tramadol, Zonisamide, Levetiracetam, Voriconazole, Vancomycin (reports only), Strontium ranelate, Chlormezanone (withdrawn). Valdecoxib, Nevirapine and Thiacetazone scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: A leading cause of SJS/TEN worldwide, with risk strongly tied to HLA-B*58:01 and renal impairment.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Risk rises with rapid titration and co-administration of valproate, typically within the first 8 weeks.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Strongly linked to HLA-B*15:02 in people of Southeast Asian ancestry, with screening recommended.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide antibiotics are among the most common antimicrobial causes, particularly in HIV.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Aromatic anticonvulsant with risk early in therapy and increased by cranial radiation; HLA-B*15:02 is associated in Asian patients.

answers.name: Phenobarbital
answers.pearl: An aromatic anticonvulsant with cross-reactivity to phenytoin and carbamazepine.

answers.name: Aminopenicillins
answers.pearl: Penicillins, particularly amoxicillin and ampicillin, are frequent causes of SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide-containing DMARD with SJS/TEN risk early in therapy.

answers.name: Oxicam NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Piroxicam and meloxicam have the highest risk among NSAIDs.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Ceftriaxone and other agents have been associated with SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Ciprofloxacin and others have been linked to SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Ibuprofen
answers.pearl: Propionic acid NSAIDs less frequently cause SJS/TEN than oxicams but are commonly implicated, partly from their ubiquity.

answers.name: Acetaminophen
answers.pearl: Case-control data show an association, as an often overlooked over-the-counter trigger.

answers.name: Macrolides
answers.pearl: Azithromycin and erythromycin have reported cases, mostly in children.

answers.name: Doxycycline
answers.pearl: Tetracyclines, including minocycline, are rare but recognized triggers.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Anti-PD-1 and CTLA-4 agents cause severe cutaneous reactions, including SJS/TEN, typically within weeks to months.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: An important cause in leprosy and dermatologic use, with HLA-B*13:01 risk.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Occasional SJS/TEN, particularly with lamotrigine co-administration.

answers.name: Celecoxib
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide-containing COX-2 inhibitor with reported SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: NNRTIs other than nevirapine have lower but real SJS/TEN risk.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, including methazolamide, are reported triggers, especially in Asian patients with HLA-B*59:01.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Anti-tuberculous drugs including isoniazid, ethambutol and rifampin have been reported.

answers.name: Terbinafine
answers.pearl: Oral antifungals have SJS/TEN reports.

answers.name: Fluconazole
answers.pearl: Triazole antifungals have been linked with SJS/TEN, mainly in case series.

answers.name: Levetiracetam
answers.pearl: Rare but increasingly documented SJS/TEN, usually within the first weeks.

answers.name: Zonisamide
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide-based antiepileptic with SJS/TEN risk early in therapy.

answers.name: Tramadol
answers.pearl: Several case reports and pharmacovigilance signals link tramadol to SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Modafinil
answers.pearl: Rare SJS/TEN reports led to FDA warnings of serious rash.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Reported in case series, often with linear IgA bullous dermatosis as a differential.

answers.name: Voriconazole
answers.pearl: Rare, often with photosensitivity, with reported SJS/TEN.

answers.name: BRAF inhibitors
answers.pearl: Vemurafenib and other targeted agents have been reported to cause SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
answers.pearl: Fansidar used for malaria prophylaxis was withdrawn in large part for SJS/TEN.

answers.name: Strontium ranelate
answers.pearl: Associated with DRESS and rare SJS/TEN, leading to restrictions in the EU.

answers.name: Chlormezanone
answers.pearl: A withdrawn muscle relaxant noted for SJS/TEN in the EuroSCAR and international case-control studies.

answers.name: Valdecoxib
answers.pearl: The COX-2 inhibitor withdrawn in 2005, which carried a boxed warning for serious skin reactions.

answers.name: Nevirapine
answers.pearl: An NNRTI with SJS/TEN risk in the first 18 weeks, with a boxed warning for rash.

answers.name: Thiacetazone
answers.pearl: Antituberculous drug discontinued for high SJS risk in HIV-positive patients.

answers.name: Leflunomide
answers.pearl: Labeled for rare SJS/TEN, with risk higher in patients switched from methotrexate.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor with reported SJS/TEN in case series.

answers.name: Ethosuximide
answers.pearl: An antiepileptic used for absence seizures, with SJS reported in labeling.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of antiphospholipid syndrome.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Sensorineural hearing loss, Psychosis, Anetoderma, Osteonecrosis, Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, Nodular regenerative hyperplasia, Neonatal thrombosis, Lupus anticoagulant-hypoprothrombinemia syndrome (bleeding paradox), Dilated cardiomyopathy, Splenic infarction, Coronary graft occlusion. Libman-Sacks endocarditis, Sneddon syndrome, false-positive VDRL/RPR and catastrophic APS scored as Board Prep Traps.

answers.name: Deep vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Venous thrombosis, most often in the lower limb, is the most common clinical manifestation.

answers.name: Recurrent pregnancy loss
answers.pearl: Three or more consecutive losses before 10 weeks is a classic obstetric criterion.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Arterial thrombosis causes ischemic stroke, often in young patients without traditional risk factors.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Venous clots embolize to the lungs and may recur despite short-term treatment.

answers.name: Transient ischemic attack
answers.pearl: Recurrent TIAs in a young patient should prompt antiphospholipid testing.

answers.name: Livedo reticularis
answers.pearl: A fixed, net-like violaceous skin pattern reflecting dermal small vessel occlusion.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Mild to moderate thrombocytopenia is a common finding and not protective against thrombosis.

answers.name: Prolonged aPTT
answers.pearl: A lupus anticoagulant prolongs phospholipid-dependent clotting tests in vitro without correcting on mixing.

answers.name: Myocardial infarction
answers.pearl: Arterial thrombosis can cause MI in young patients without atherosclerosis.

answers.name: Fetal death
answers.pearl: One or more unexplained deaths of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond 10 weeks is a clinical criterion.

answers.name: Preeclampsia
answers.pearl: Severe preeclampsia or eclampsia before 34 weeks counts toward obstetric criteria.

answers.name: Migraine
answers.pearl: A frequent neurologic complaint, with an unclear mechanism.

answers.name: Placental insufficiency
answers.pearl: Placental infarction and vasculopathy cause growth restriction, fetal distress and premature birth.

answers.name: Superficial thrombophlebitis
answers.pearl: Recurrent or migratory superficial vein thrombosis may occur.

answers.name: Hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia with positive Coombs test can occur, sometimes with Evans syndrome.

answers.name: Cognitive dysfunction
answers.pearl: Impaired memory, attention and executive function can arise from chronic microvascular ischemia.

answers.name: Seizures
answers.pearl: Cerebral ischemic lesions or venous infarcts can be epileptogenic.

answers.name: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
answers.pearl: Dural sinus thrombosis presents with headache, papilledema or seizures.

answers.name: Retinal vascular occlusion
answers.pearl: Retinal artery or vein occlusion and amaurosis fugax can be the first events.

answers.name: Skin ulcers
answers.pearl: Painful leg ulcers or necrosis reflect cutaneous small vessel thrombosis.

answers.name: Valvular heart disease
answers.pearl: Valve thickening, regurgitation and vegetations occur frequently on echocardiography.

answers.name: Dementia
answers.pearl: Multi-infarct dementia can occur from recurrent small vessel thrombosis.

answers.name: HELLP syndrome
answers.pearl: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets complicating pregnancy, often in the presence of antibodies.

answers.name: Digital gangrene
answers.pearl: Thrombosis of digital arteries can cause ischemia, with necrosis of fingers or toes.

answers.name: Chorea
answers.pearl: Rare movement disorder from basal ganglia involvement, particularly in young women or in pregnancy.

answers.name: Portal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Splanchnic thrombosis can occur in unusual sites, so cause evaluation should include antiphospholipid antibodies.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic vein thrombosis occurs in a minority of APS patients, so testing is part of work-up.

answers.name: Renal artery thrombosis
answers.pearl: Renal artery or vein thrombosis causes hypertension, infarction or kidney injury.

answers.name: APS nephropathy
answers.pearl: Thrombotic microangiopathy, fibrous intimal hyperplasia and focal cortical atrophy produce hypertension and proteinuria.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Chronic thromboembolic disease or in situ thrombosis produces pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Adrenal hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Adrenal vein thrombosis causes hemorrhagic infarction and acute adrenal insufficiency, a notable APS complication.

answers.name: Intracardiac thrombus
answers.pearl: Left ventricular or atrial thrombi may occur, sometimes mimicking myxoma.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Arterial or venous thrombosis of the mesenteric vessels causes abdominal pain and bowel infarction.

answers.name: Inferior vena cava thrombosis
answers.pearl: Thrombosis of large veins at unusual sites can occur.

answers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
answers.pearl: Vasospasm and small vessel occlusion cause color changes in the digits.

answers.name: Axillary vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Upper extremity venous thrombosis, including subclavian, is an unusual site.

answers.name: Splinter hemorrhages
answers.pearl: Small vessel occlusion in the nail bed gives linear subungual hemorrhages, which can mimic endocarditis.

answers.name: Culture-negative endocarditis mimic
answers.pearl: Valve vegetations from APS may be mistaken for infective endocarditis when cultures are negative.

answers.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
answers.pearl: Widespread pulmonary microthrombosis can produce ARDS, particularly in catastrophic disease.

answers.name: Livedoid vasculopathy
answers.pearl: Segmental hyalinizing vasculitis causes painful lower-leg ulcers and atrophie blanche.

answers.name: Optic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Ischemic optic neuropathy and other visual syndromes are reported.

answers.name: Aortic thrombosis
answers.pearl: Arterial thrombosis of the aorta or branches has been described.

answers.name: Splenic infarction
answers.pearl: Splenic artery or vein thrombosis can cause infarction.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Pulmonary capillaritis or microvascular thrombosis can cause hemoptysis and alveolar bleeding.

answers.name: Transverse myelitis
answers.pearl: Spinal cord ischemia or demyelination presents as acute myelopathy, often in APS with lupus.

answers.name: Coronary graft occlusion
answers.pearl: Early graft thrombosis after CABG or PCI stent thrombosis can be an unrecognized presentation.

answers.name: Osteonecrosis
answers.pearl: Avascular necrosis of bone, especially the femoral head, has been associated with antiphospholipid antibodies.

answers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Coronary microvascular thrombosis can cause global ventricular dysfunction.

answers.name: Sensorineural hearing loss
answers.pearl: Cochlear vascular thrombosis can cause sudden hearing loss.

answers.name: Psychosis
answers.pearl: Neuropsychiatric manifestations including psychosis and mood disorders have been reported.

answers.name: Anetoderma
answers.pearl: Focal loss of dermal elastic tissue gives a skin atrophy that is associated with antiphospholipid antibodies.

answers.name: Nodular regenerative hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Hepatic small vessel occlusion leads to nodular transformation and noncirrhotic portal hypertension.

answers.name: Neonatal thrombosis
answers.pearl: Transplacental passage of antibodies is a reported cause of thrombosis in newborns.

answers.name: Lupus anticoagulant-hypoprothrombinemia syndrome
answers.pearl: Antibodies binding prothrombin speed its clearance, causing paradoxical bleeding with a prolonged PT.

answers.name: Libman-Sacks endocarditis
answers.pearl: Sterile verrucous vegetations on both surfaces of the mitral or aortic valve are classically tied to SLE and APS.

answers.name: Sneddon syndrome
answers.pearl: Livedo racemosa with cerebrovascular events and antiphospholipid antibodies.

answers.name: False-positive syphilis test
answers.pearl: Cardiolipin is the antigen in nontreponemal tests, so VDRL or RPR may be falsely positive.

answers.name: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid multiorgan microvascular thrombosis within a week, often after a trigger such as infection or surgery.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of syphilis (all stages).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Gastric syphilis, Syphilitic arthritis, Splenomegaly and Syphilitic proctitis (case-series level); Acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis and Lues maligna (rare variants); Hutchinson triad is congenital, included as a Board Prep Trap.

answers.name: Chancre
answers.pearl: A painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer at the inoculation site marks primary syphilis and appears about 3 weeks after exposure.

answers.name: Maculopapular rash
answers.pearl: Secondary syphilis classically causes a diffuse, non-pruritic copper-colored macular or papular rash.

answers.name: Palmar and plantar rash
answers.pearl: Involvement of the palms and soles is a hallmark of secondary syphilis and prompts RPR testing.

answers.name: Generalized lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Rubbery, nontender nodes, including epitrochlear nodes, are common in secondary syphilis.

answers.name: Regional lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Painless, firm nodes draining the chancre accompany the primary lesion.

answers.name: Condyloma lata
answers.pearl: Broad, moist, flat-topped, highly infectious plaques in intertriginous skin appear in secondary syphilis.

answers.name: Mucous patches
answers.pearl: Painless grayish erosions on the oral or genital mucosa teem with spirochetes in secondary syphilis.

answers.name: Fever and malaise
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever, malaise and myalgias commonly accompany the secondary stage.

answers.name: Asymptomatic latent infection
answers.pearl: Latent syphilis has positive treponemal serology without symptoms and is staged by whether infection occurred within the past year.

answers.name: Sore throat
answers.pearl: Pharyngitis can be part of the secondary syphilis prodrome and may be mistaken for viral illness.

answers.name: Patchy alopecia
answers.pearl: Patchy, moth-eaten scalp hair loss reflects secondary syphilis involving hair follicles.

answers.name: Aortitis
answers.pearl: Obliterative endarteritis of the vasa vasorum causes tertiary aortitis 10 to 30 years after infection.

answers.name: Ascending aortic aneurysm
answers.pearl: Syphilitic aortitis characteristically involves the ascending aorta and may produce a saccular aneurysm with tree-bark calcification.

answers.name: Aortic regurgitation
answers.pearl: Dilation of the aortic root from syphilitic aortitis causes secondary aortic valve regurgitation.

answers.name: Gumma
answers.pearl: A granulomatous, necrotizing lesion of tertiary syphilis that can involve skin, bone, liver and other organs.

answers.name: General paresis
answers.pearl: Parenchymal neurosyphilis that causes progressive dementia, personality change and psychosis years after infection.

answers.name: Tabes dorsalis
answers.pearl: Degeneration of the dorsal columns and roots causes sensory ataxia, lightning pains and loss of reflexes.

answers.name: Lightning pains
answers.pearl: Brief, stabbing limb or trunk pains are an early feature of tabes dorsalis.

answers.name: Sensory ataxia
answers.pearl: Loss of proprioception from dorsal column damage produces a wide-based, stomping gait and a positive Romberg sign.

answers.name: Meningovascular syphilis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of meningeal vessels causes stroke in younger patients, often 5 to 12 years after infection.

answers.name: Syphilitic meningitis
answers.pearl: Meningitis with headache, stiff neck and cranial neuropathies can occur in the first year or two of infection.

answers.name: Asymptomatic neurosyphilis
answers.pearl: CSF pleocytosis or a reactive CSF VDRL can be present without neurologic symptoms.

answers.name: Cranial neuropathy
answers.pearl: Cranial nerves II, III, VI, VII and VIII are most often involved in early neurosyphilis.

answers.name: Ocular syphilis
answers.pearl: Syphilis can involve any part of the eye and can occur at any stage, and requires neurosyphilis evaluation.

answers.name: Uveitis
answers.pearl: Syphilis is a great mimicker of intraocular inflammation and should be tested for in unexplained uveitis.

answers.name: Optic neuritis
answers.pearl: Optic nerve inflammation or perineuritis from syphilis can lead to vision loss if not treated.

answers.name: Retinitis
answers.pearl: Retinal and choroidal inflammation can be seen in secondary and later syphilis.

answers.name: Acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis
answers.pearl: A distinctive macular placoid yellow lesion pattern strongly suggests ocular syphilis.

answers.name: Otosyphilis
answers.pearl: Cochleovestibular involvement causes tinnitus, vertigo and sudden or progressive sensorineural hearing loss.

answers.name: Syphilitic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Secondary syphilis can cause hepatitis with a disproportionately elevated alkaline phosphatase.

answers.name: Syphilitic glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Immune-complex disease in secondary syphilis can cause membranous nephropathy and nephrotic-range proteinuria.

answers.name: Madarosis
answers.pearl: Thinning of the lateral eyebrows is a classic secondary syphilis sign.

answers.name: Periostitis
answers.pearl: Secondary syphilis can cause painful periosteal inflammation, often of long bones and the skull.

answers.name: Syphilitic arthritis
answers.pearl: Joint inflammation and arthralgias have been described in secondary and tertiary syphilis.

answers.name: Lues maligna
answers.pearl: A severe necrotic, ulcerating form of secondary syphilis, classically seen with HIV infection.

answers.name: Annular syphilid
answers.pearl: Ring-shaped papules, especially on the face of patients with darker skin, are a secondary syphilis variant.

answers.name: Pustular syphilid
answers.pearl: Pustular lesions mimicking acne or pox occur in a minority of secondary syphilis cases.

answers.name: Syphilitic proctitis
answers.pearl: Anorectal infection in men who have sex with men can present as proctitis, tenesmus and rectal mass.

answers.name: Gastric syphilis
answers.pearl: Gastric involvement can mimic lymphoma or carcinoma on imaging and endoscopy and responds to penicillin.

answers.name: Gummatous hepatitis
answers.pearl: Tertiary hepatic gummas heal with scarring and can produce a lobulated liver.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Mild splenomegaly may accompany secondary syphilis along with hepatic involvement.

answers.name: Coronary ostial stenosis
answers.pearl: Syphilitic aortitis can narrow the coronary ostia and cause angina.

answers.name: Argyll Robertson pupil
answers.pearl: Small irregular pupils that accommodate but do not react to light are the classic neurosyphilis sign.

answers.name: Charcot joint
answers.pearl: Loss of proprioception and pain in tabes dorsalis leads to a destroyed, painless neuropathic joint.

answers.name: Hutchinson triad
answers.pearl: Notched peg-shaped incisors, interstitial keratitis and eighth nerve deafness characterize late congenital syphilis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of polyuria.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cerebral salt wasting (polyuria with volume depletion, debated entity); Foscarnet and Tenofovir (case-report level); Renal glucosuria (mild); Caffeine (modest effect); Sjogren and amyloidosis (uncommon).

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Glucose above the renal threshold causes an osmotic diuresis with polyuria.

answers.name: Primary polydipsia
answers.pearl: Excess water intake suppresses ADH and yields dilute urine.

answers.name: Loop and thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Diuretics inhibit tubular sodium and water reabsorption and increase urine output.

answers.name: Central diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Deficient ADH release causes large volumes of dilute urine that respond to desmopressin.

answers.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: The kidney fails to respond to ADH, so urine remains dilute and desmopressin does not correct it.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: Marked hyperglycemia and ketonuria drive an osmotic diuresis.

answers.name: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
answers.pearl: Severe hyperglycemia produces profound osmotic diuresis and volume depletion.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Calcium impairs aquaporin-2 action and concentrating ability, causing nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium enters collecting duct cells and impairs ADH signaling to cause nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Post-obstructive diuresis
answers.pearl: Relief of a high-grade obstruction can cause solute and water diuresis from retained urea and tubular dysfunction.

answers.name: Recovery phase of acute tubular necrosis
answers.pearl: Recovering tubules initially cannot concentrate urine, producing large urine volumes.

answers.name: Hypokalemia
answers.pearl: Potassium depletion downregulates aquaporin-2 and causes nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Nephron loss and tubular dysfunction lead to isosthenuria and nocturia.

answers.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
answers.pearl: SGLT2 inhibition causes glucosuria and osmotic diuresis.

answers.name: Mannitol
answers.pearl: Non-reabsorbed solute in the tubule holds water and increases urine volume.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Ethanol suppresses ADH release and causes a water diuresis.

answers.name: Caffeine
answers.pearl: Caffeine has a mild diuretic effect.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Medullary ischemia impairs concentrating ability, causing isosthenuria even in sickle cell trait.

answers.name: Craniopharyngioma
answers.pearl: Suprasellar masses damage the hypothalamic-pituitary axis and can cause central DI.

answers.name: Head trauma
answers.pearl: Trauma to the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk can cause transient or permanent central DI.

answers.name: Pituitary surgery
answers.pearl: Manipulation of the stalk and posterior pituitary often causes transient central DI after surgery.

answers.name: Congestive heart failure nocturia
answers.pearl: Overnight mobilization of dependent edema and natriuretic peptides increase nocturnal urine output.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: Atrial stretch from negative intrathoracic pressure releases ANP and causes nocturnal polyuria.

answers.name: Polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Cysts impair concentrating ability, and polyuria and nocturia are early findings.

answers.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Damage to medullary tubules impairs urinary concentration.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Distal tubular injury causes nephrogenic DI and potassium and magnesium wasting.

answers.name: Demeclocycline
answers.pearl: This tetracycline antagonizes ADH in the collecting duct and is used therapeutically to induce nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Tolvaptan
answers.pearl: V2 receptor blockade causes aquaresis and increased urine volume.

answers.name: Urea diuresis
answers.pearl: A large urea load from catabolism or high-protein feeds causes an osmotic diuresis.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Global proximal tubular dysfunction can produce polyuria with glucosuria, phosphaturia and aminoaciduria.

answers.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Hypokalemia from aldosterone excess blunts concentrating ability and causes polyuria and nocturia.

answers.name: Nephronophthisis
answers.pearl: Tubular concentrating defects cause polyuria and polydipsia before ESRD.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: Tubulointerstitial nephritis can cause distal RTA and nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Renal amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid infiltration of the medulla can impair concentrating ability.

answers.name: Foscarnet
answers.pearl: Foscarnet is a recognized cause of drug-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Proximal tubular injury can lead to Fanconi syndrome and polyuria.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Tubular toxicity can cause Fanconi syndrome and nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Neurosarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration of the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk can cause central DI.

answers.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
answers.pearl: Infiltration of the pituitary stalk causes central DI, often the first sign.

answers.name: Brain death
answers.pearl: Loss of hypothalamic function causes abrupt central DI in organ donors.

answers.name: Cerebral salt wasting
answers.pearl: Natriuresis and polyuria after intracranial disease can mimic SIADH but with volume depletion.

answers.name: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of the posterior pituitary or stalk can cause central DI.

answers.name: X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Loss-of-function mutations in the V2 receptor gene cause hereditary nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Aquaporin-2 mutation
answers.pearl: Recessive or dominant defects in the water channel cause hereditary nephrogenic DI.

answers.name: Familial neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Mutations in the AVP gene cause progressive loss of ADH-secreting neurons.

answers.name: Renal glucosuria
answers.pearl: Inherited tubular glucose wasting causes a mild osmotic diuresis.

answers.name: Wolfram syndrome
aliases: diabetes insipidus diabetes mellitus optic atrophy deafness
answers.pearl: A WFS1 disorder with DI, diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy and deafness.

answers.name: Gestational diabetes insipidus
answers.pearl: Placental vasopressinase degrades ADH and causes transient DI late in pregnancy.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome
answers.pearl: A salt-wasting tubulopathy from loop-of-Henle transporter defects causes polyuria, hypokalemia and alkalosis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of proteinuria.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mercury and Immune checkpoint inhibitors (case-report level); Pamidronate and Interferon (collapsing FSGS reports); Nail-patella and Pierson syndrome (rare genetic); Solitary kidney (secondary FSGS).

answers.name: Diabetic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Hyperfiltration and mesangial expansion from long-standing diabetes make this the leading cause of proteinuria in adults.

answers.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
answers.pearl: Chronic hypertension causes arteriolar sclerosis and mild to moderate proteinuria.

answers.name: Preeclampsia
answers.pearl: New hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks result from glomerular endotheliosis.

answers.name: Minimal change disease
answers.pearl: The leading cause of nephrotic syndrome in children, with foot process effacement on electron microscopy only.

answers.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
answers.pearl: A common cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults, especially in Black patients with APOL1 variants.

answers.name: Membranous nephropathy
answers.pearl: Subepithelial immune deposits, often anti-PLA2R antibody mediated, cause nephrotic syndrome in adults.

answers.name: Lupus nephritis
answers.pearl: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis in SLE causes proteinuria and hematuria across several histologic classes.

answers.name: IgA nephropathy
answers.pearl: The most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, with hematuria and variable proteinuria.

answers.name: Exercise-induced proteinuria
answers.pearl: Transient proteinuria after heavy exertion resolves within about a day.

answers.name: Urinary tract infection
answers.pearl: Infection can add transient proteinuria through inflammation and leukocytes.

answers.name: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Immune-complex disease after streptococcal infection causes nephritic syndrome with low C3.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Acute illness with fever causes a transient increase in protein excretion.

answers.name: Orthostatic proteinuria
answers.pearl: Protein excretion occurs when upright but not in the first morning urine, and is typically benign in adolescents.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Filtered light chains overwhelm tubular reabsorption but do not react on dipstick, so urine protein electrophoresis is needed.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Venous congestion and neurohormonal activation can raise glomerular protein leakage.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Glomerular amyloid deposits cause nephrotic-range proteinuria with a Congo red apple-green birefringence.

answers.name: Obesity-related glomerulopathy
answers.pearl: Hyperfiltration from obesity causes secondary FSGS with variable proteinuria.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs can cause minimal change disease with interstitial nephritis and nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: ANCA-associated vasculitis
answers.pearl: Pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis causes hematuria and proteinuria.

answers.name: HIV-associated nephropathy
answers.pearl: Collapsing FSGS in patients with HIV, particularly Black patients, causes heavy proteinuria.

answers.name: Sickle cell nephropathy
answers.pearl: Hyperfiltration and glomerular injury cause proteinuria early in sickle cell disease.

answers.name: Solitary kidney
answers.pearl: Reduced nephron number causes compensatory hyperfiltration and secondary FSGS.

answers.name: Hepatitis B and C
answers.pearl: Viral hepatitis can cause membranous nephropathy or membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis.

answers.name: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Capillary wall thickening with tram-track basement membranes is seen on light microscopy.

answers.name: Reflux nephropathy
answers.pearl: Renal scarring causes secondary FSGS with proteinuria.

answers.name: Polycystic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Mild proteinuria can accompany cystic disease and signals faster progression.

answers.name: Anti-GBM disease
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with linear IgG deposition along the basement membrane.

answers.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Tubular injury causes low-grade proteinuria, usually under 2 g per day.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Hodgkin lymphoma can cause minimal change disease through cytokine effects on podocytes.

answers.name: Solid tumor-associated membranous nephropathy
answers.pearl: Membranous nephropathy in older patients can be paraneoplastic, especially with lung, colon or breast cancer.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium can cause minimal change disease or FSGS with nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: Gold and penicillamine
answers.pearl: These agents are classic causes of drug-induced membranous nephropathy.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Immune complexes with cryoglobulins cause membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis with hepatitis C association.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis complicates subacute bacterial endocarditis.

answers.name: Renal vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Thrombosis can both cause and result from nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: Fibrillary glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Congo red-negative randomly arranged fibrils with DNAJB9 positivity on biopsy.

answers.name: Light chain deposition disease
answers.pearl: Monoclonal light chain deposition mimics diabetic nodular glomerulosclerosis.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Low molecular weight proteins escape reabsorption, giving tubular proteinuria that dipstick underestimates.

answers.name: Pamidronate
answers.pearl: High-dose pamidronate can cause collapsing FSGS.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Interferon therapy has been linked to collapsing glomerulopathy and minimal change disease.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause interstitial nephritis and, rarely, glomerular disease with proteinuria.

answers.name: Mercury
answers.pearl: Mercury exposure, for example from skin-lightening creams, can cause membranous nephropathy or minimal change disease.

answers.name: Dent disease
answers.pearl: An X-linked proximal tubulopathy with low molecular weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria and stones.

answers.name: Nail-patella syndrome
answers.pearl: Skeletal and nail abnormalities with nephropathy from LMX1B mutations.

answers.name: Cadmium
answers.pearl: Chronic exposure causes proximal tubular injury with low molecular weight proteinuria.

answers.name: Pierson syndrome
answers.pearl: LAMB2 mutations cause congenital nephrotic syndrome with ocular abnormalities including microcoria.

answers.name: Denys-Drash syndrome
answers.pearl: WT1 mutations cause early nephrotic syndrome with Wilms tumor and genital anomalies.

answers.name: Fabry disease
answers.pearl: X-linked GLA deficiency causes globotriaosylceramide accumulation, with proteinuria and kidney disease.

answers.name: Alport syndrome
answers.pearl: Collagen IV defects cause hematuria, sensorineural hearing loss and proteinuria.

answers.name: Congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type
answers.pearl: NPHS1 (nephrin) mutations cause massive proteinuria beginning in utero or at birth.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause drug fever.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mycophenolate, Hydroxyurea, Linezolid, Nifedipine and Iodinated contrast (listed in reviews but sparse evidence); Anticholinergics (hyperthermia rather than classic drug fever); Cimetidine and Furosemide (rare reports).

answers.name: Penicillins
answers.pearl: Beta-lactams are among the most frequent causes of hypersensitivity-type drug fever, often with eosinophilia.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamides are common causes of drug fever, often with rash.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Cephalosporins frequently cause drug fever after about a week of exposure.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Aromatic anticonvulsants cause fever with rash, lymphadenopathy and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Fever may be part of DRESS with carbamazepine.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity can present with fever, rash and organ involvement.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: Vancomycin can cause fever after days of therapy or during infusion.

answers.name: Isoniazid
answers.pearl: Isoniazid can cause fever, often alongside hepatitis.

answers.name: Procainamide
answers.pearl: Procainamide is a classic cause of drug-induced lupus with fever.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Can cause fever with pulmonary hypersensitivity and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Hydralazine
answers.pearl: Causes fever and drug-induced lupus, especially in slow acetylators.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Rifampin can cause a flu-like syndrome with fever, especially with intermittent dosing.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: A classic old antihypertensive causing fever with hepatitis and hemolytic anemia.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Interferons cause fever as a pharmacologic effect and flu-like syndrome.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs occasionally cause hypersensitivity fever.

answers.name: Quinidine
answers.pearl: Cinchona alkaloids are recognized causes of fever, sometimes with thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Bleomycin
answers.pearl: Fever occurs in many patients within hours of bleomycin as a pharmacologic effect.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Infusion reactions with fever and chills are a classic effect.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: A sulfonamide-containing drug that causes hypersensitivity fever and rash.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Quinolone fever is uncommon but recognized.

answers.name: Barbiturates
answers.pearl: Barbiturates can cause fever with rash and lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Clindamycin
answers.pearl: Clindamycin has been linked to drug fever and rash.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Fever can accompany lamotrigine hypersensitivity syndrome.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin has been reported to cause drug fever, as has enoxaparin.

answers.name: Tetracyclines
answers.pearl: Minocycline can cause DRESS-like fever with eosinophilia.

answers.name: Cytarabine
answers.pearl: Cytarabine causes a syndrome of fever, myalgia and rash.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Azathioprine hypersensitivity can present with fever, rash and hypotension.

answers.name: Antihistamines
answers.pearl: Antihistamines are described causes of drug fever.

answers.name: Thionamides
answers.pearl: Antithyroid drugs can cause fever with rash and agranulocytosis.

answers.name: Anticholinergics
answers.pearl: Impaired sweating raises body temperature in anticholinergic toxicity.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Dapsone hypersensitivity causes fever, rash and hepatitis.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune-related adverse events can present with isolated fever.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Infusion-related fever is common.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: H2 blockers are infrequently reported to cause drug fever.

answers.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
answers.pearl: Thiazides are reported causes of hypersensitivity fever.

answers.name: Furosemide
answers.pearl: Reported cause of drug fever with rash.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Fever can accompany amiodarone pulmonary toxicity or hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Mesalamine can cause fever mimicking inflammatory bowel disease flare.

answers.name: Anti-thymocyte globulin
answers.pearl: Cytokine release causes fever and chills.

answers.name: Interleukin-2
answers.pearl: Pharmacologic fever occurs with cytokine therapy.

answers.name: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
answers.pearl: Fever and bone pain accompany growth factor use.

answers.name: Captopril
answers.pearl: Reported cause of fever, often with rash.

answers.name: Daptomycin
answers.pearl: Fever can accompany daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonia.

answers.name: Nifedipine
answers.pearl: Described in lists of drugs that cause fever.

answers.name: Linezolid
answers.pearl: Rare cause of drug fever.

answers.name: Levamisole
answers.pearl: Cocaine adulterated with levamisole causes fever with agranulocytosis and vasculitic rash.

answers.name: Iodinated contrast
answers.pearl: Iodides are described causes of fever.

answers.name: Hydroxyurea
answers.pearl: Hydroxyurea fever is documented but unusual.

answers.name: Mycophenolate
answers.pearl: A rare cause of drug fever.

answers.name: Asparaginase
answers.pearl: Fever occurs with hypersensitivity and as a pharmacologic effect.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of Lyme disease (all stages).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cerebral vasculitis, Cerebellar ataxia, Orchitis, Dilated cardiomyopathy (case-report or debated); Keratitis and Optic neuritis (rare); Syncope (secondary to heart block). ACA, lymphocytoma and Bannwarth syndrome are mainly European.

answers.name: Erythema migrans
answers.pearl: An expanding erythematous rash at the bite site is the hallmark of early localized Lyme disease and is diagnosed clinically.

answers.name: Facial nerve palsy
answers.pearl: Unilateral or bilateral facial palsy is the most common cranial neuropathy of early disseminated Lyme.

answers.name: Lyme arthritis
answers.pearl: Intermittent or persistent large-joint, usually knee, arthritis occurs months after infection.

answers.name: Lyme carditis
answers.pearl: Fluctuating AV nodal block, sometimes high-grade, occurs in early disseminated Lyme.

answers.name: Flu-like illness
answers.pearl: Fever, chills and fatigue commonly accompany erythema migrans.

answers.name: Migratory arthralgia
answers.pearl: Brief migratory joint and muscle pains occur early in infection.

answers.name: Aseptic meningitis
answers.pearl: Lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis with headache occurs in early neuroborreliosis.

answers.name: Multiple erythema migrans
answers.pearl: Hematogenous spread causes multiple secondary skin lesions away from the bite.

answers.name: Myalgia
answers.pearl: Muscle pain is a common nonspecific early symptom.

answers.name: Lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Regional lymph nodes near the bite site can enlarge early.

answers.name: Radiculoneuritis
answers.pearl: Painful meningoradiculitis with cranial neuritis, mostly reported in Europe with Borrelia garinii.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Chronic axonal sensory polyneuropathy can occur in late Lyme.

answers.name: Conjunctivitis
answers.pearl: Conjunctivitis occurs in a small proportion of early disseminated cases.

answers.name: Encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Cognitive impairment with abnormal CSF or neuropsychological testing can occur in late disease.

answers.name: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans
answers.pearl: A late European cutaneous finding with bluish-red infiltrated skin evolving to atrophy, usually from Borrelia afzelii.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Mild myocarditis can accompany the conduction disease of Lyme carditis.

answers.name: Cranial neuropathy
answers.pearl: Besides the facial nerve, cranial nerves V, VI, III and VIII can be involved.

answers.name: Bilateral facial palsy
answers.pearl: Bilateral facial palsy in an endemic area should raise suspicion for Lyme disease.

answers.name: Hepatitis
answers.pearl: Mild liver enzyme elevations are seen in early disseminated Lyme.

answers.name: Borrelial lymphocytoma
answers.pearl: A solitary bluish-red nodule on the earlobe, nipple or scrotum, mostly in Europe.

answers.name: Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome
answers.pearl: Persistent fatigue, pain or cognitive complaints for at least 6 months after treated infection.

answers.name: Antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis
answers.pearl: Synovitis persisting after adequate antibiotics is attributed to immune dysregulation.

answers.name: Uveitis
answers.pearl: Intermediate or anterior uveitis has been described in Lyme disease.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial involvement is uncommon but reported.

answers.name: Keratitis
answers.pearl: Keratitis is a rare ocular manifestation.

answers.name: Optic neuritis
answers.pearl: Optic neuritis is rare in Lyme disease.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Mild splenomegaly occurs in early disseminated disease.

answers.name: Plexopathy
answers.pearl: Plexus involvement, mostly in Europe, can mimic radiculopathy.

answers.name: Papilledema
answers.pearl: Elevated intracranial pressure with papilledema is reported, especially in children.

answers.name: Myositis
answers.pearl: Focal or diffuse inflammatory myositis is rare.

answers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Chronic cardiomyopathy has been reported in European Lyme disease but remains debated.

answers.name: Encephalomyelitis
answers.pearl: Parenchymal CNS inflammation is rare and more often seen in Europe.

answers.name: Orchitis
answers.pearl: Rare reports of orchitis in early disseminated disease.

answers.name: Cerebral vasculitis
answers.pearl: Borrelia-associated CNS vasculitis causing stroke is rare.

answers.name: Cerebellar ataxia
answers.pearl: Acute cerebellar ataxia is a rare neuroborreliosis presentation.

answers.name: Headache
answers.pearl: Headache is common in early disseminated disease even without meningitis.

answers.name: Syncope
answers.pearl: Complete heart block can cause presyncope or syncope.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypoalbuminemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Fontan circulation and Constrictive pericarditis (via protein-losing enteropathy); Hookworm infection (documented); Cystic fibrosis; Hepatic congestion; SLE (protein-losing enteropathy is rare); Aging (modest effect).

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Reduced hepatic synthesis plus dilution from volume expansion lowers albumin.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Heavy glomerular losses exceed hepatic synthesis capacity.

answers.name: Malnutrition
answers.pearl: Reduced intake of protein and calories lowers synthesis, though albumin is a poor nutritional marker.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Cytokines suppress synthesis and increase capillary leak, so albumin falls as a negative acute-phase reactant.

answers.name: Protein-losing enteropathy
answers.pearl: Gut mucosal injury or lymphatic obstruction leaks albumin into the lumen, detected by alpha-1 antitrypsin clearance.

answers.name: Acute liver failure
answers.pearl: Severe hepatocellular injury reduces albumin synthesis.

answers.name: Chronic inflammation
answers.pearl: IL-6 and TNF reduce hepatic albumin synthesis during chronic inflammation.

answers.name: Hemodilution
answers.pearl: Expanded plasma volume lowers concentration without changing total body albumin.

answers.name: Malabsorption
answers.pearl: Impaired absorption of amino acids and gut protein loss lower albumin.

answers.name: Burns
answers.pearl: Extensive burns cause capillary leak and exudative losses.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Hepatic congestion, gut edema and dilution lower albumin in advanced heart failure.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Inflammation and poor intake lower albumin in advanced cancer.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Plasma volume expansion physiologically lowers albumin.

answers.name: Capillary leak syndrome
answers.pearl: Increased vascular permeability shifts albumin into the interstitium.

answers.name: Crohn disease
answers.pearl: Inflammation, gut leakage and malabsorption lower albumin.

answers.name: Ulcerative colitis
answers.pearl: Colonic protein loss and inflammation lower albumin.

answers.name: Kwashiorkor
answers.pearl: Protein-deficient diets cause edema and low albumin in children.

answers.name: Aging
answers.pearl: Albumin falls modestly with age and comorbid illness.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation, capillary leak and third spacing lower albumin.

answers.name: Eating disorders
answers.pearl: Chronic restriction decreases protein synthesis.

answers.name: Peritoneal dialysis
answers.pearl: Albumin is lost across the peritoneal membrane into dialysate.

answers.name: Exfoliative dermatitis
answers.pearl: Skin losses and inflammation lower albumin.

answers.name: Paracentesis
answers.pearl: Ascitic protein loss and redistribution lower serum albumin.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis
answers.pearl: Elevated venous pressure causes protein-losing enteropathy and hepatic congestion.

answers.name: Acute blood loss
answers.pearl: Loss of albumin-containing plasma plus dilution from fluid replacement lowers levels.

answers.name: Intestinal lymphangiectasia
answers.pearl: Lymphatic obstruction leaks protein-rich lymph into the gut lumen.

answers.name: Hookworm infection
answers.pearl: Chronic gut blood and protein loss can cause hypoalbuminemia.

answers.name: Whipple disease
answers.pearl: Malabsorption and lymphatic involvement cause protein loss.

answers.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
answers.pearl: Large denuded skin areas lose protein-rich fluid.

answers.name: Menetrier disease
answers.pearl: Foveolar hyperplasia causes gastric protein loss and hypoalbuminemia.

answers.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
answers.pearl: Extensive skin loss causes protein and fluid losses.

answers.name: Fontan circulation
answers.pearl: Elevated systemic venous pressure causes protein-losing enteropathy in a subset of patients.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Lupus can cause albumin loss via nephritis, enteropathy and inflammation.

answers.name: Large-volume plasmapheresis
answers.pearl: Plasma exchange with non-albumin replacement lowers albumin.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Pancreatic insufficiency and malnutrition can lower albumin.

answers.name: Analbuminemia
answers.pearl: A rare autosomal recessive absence of albumin that surprisingly causes only mild edema.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Nephrotic losses and gut involvement both lower albumin.

answers.name: Hepatic congestion
answers.pearl: Chronic congestion reduces hepatic synthetic function.

answers.name: Diabetic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Heavy proteinuria in advanced diabetic kidney disease lowers albumin.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of Wilson disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cardiomyopathy, Arrhythmia, Chondrocalcinosis, Hypoparathyroidism, Nephrocalcinosis, Hyperpigmentation of the shins and Peripheral neuropathy (case-report level); Hypoparathyroidism is listed but weakly supported; Azure lunulae and Sunflower cataract are rare signs.

answers.name: Kayser-Fleischer rings
answers.pearl: Copper deposition in Descemet membrane is seen on slit-lamp examination in nearly all patients with neurologic Wilson disease.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Chronic copper accumulation causes progressive fibrosis and cirrhosis, often silently in adolescents.

answers.name: Chronic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Wilson disease can mimic autoimmune or viral hepatitis in young patients.

answers.name: Acute liver failure
answers.pearl: Acute liver failure with Coombs-negative hemolysis is a dramatic presentation requiring transplant evaluation.

answers.name: Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia
answers.pearl: Release of copper from necrotic hepatocytes causes acute intravascular hemolysis.

answers.name: Tremor
answers.pearl: A coarse proximal "wing-beating" tremor on arm abduction is characteristic.

answers.name: Dysarthria
answers.pearl: Speech abnormalities are among the earliest neurologic features.

answers.name: Dystonia
answers.pearl: Basal ganglia copper deposition causes dystonic postures, often bulbar or limb.

answers.name: Parkinsonism
answers.pearl: Rigidity and slowness occur in young patients with atypical parkinsonism.

answers.name: Ataxia
answers.pearl: Cerebellar involvement causes ataxia and dysmetria.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Psychiatric symptoms may precede neurologic ones by years.

answers.name: Personality change
answers.pearl: Disinhibition, irritability or aggression can be the presenting complaint.

answers.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Decompensated liver disease causes confusion unrelated to copper neurotoxicity.

answers.name: Jaundice
answers.pearl: Hemolysis and liver failure both elevate bilirubin.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension from cirrhosis enlarges the spleen and causes cytopenias.

answers.name: Ascites
answers.pearl: Decompensated cirrhosis leads to ascites and edema.

answers.name: Portal hypertension
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis causes varices and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Hepatomegaly
answers.pearl: Copper accumulation can enlarge the liver early.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Bulbar involvement impairs swallowing and increases aspiration risk.

answers.name: Drooling
answers.pearl: Oromandibular dystonia and impaired swallowing cause drooling.

answers.name: Cognitive decline
answers.pearl: Subcortical cognitive slowing and executive dysfunction can occur.

answers.name: Psychosis
answers.pearl: Psychosis can be the presenting feature and delays diagnosis.

answers.name: Chorea
answers.pearl: Hyperkinetic movements occur less commonly than dystonia and tremor.

answers.name: Basal ganglia T2 hyperintensity
answers.pearl: MRI shows T2 changes in putamen, thalamus and brainstem in neurologic disease.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Anxiety and emotional instability are common psychiatric manifestations.

answers.name: Seizures
answers.pearl: Seizures occur in a minority of patients.

answers.name: Declining school performance
answers.pearl: Adolescents may first show academic deterioration and behavioral changes.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Bone demineralization can be an early finding in young patients.

answers.name: Sunflower cataract
answers.pearl: Copper in the lens produces a petal-like anterior capsular pattern that does not impair vision.

answers.name: Pseudosclerosis
answers.pearl: An old name for the tremor and ataxia predominant presentation resembling multiple sclerosis.

answers.name: Risus sardonicus
answers.pearl: Dystonia of facial muscles produces a fixed smile.

answers.name: Amenorrhea
answers.pearl: Gynecologic features include menstrual irregularities.

answers.name: Renal tubular acidosis
answers.pearl: Copper deposition in tubules causes distal or proximal tubular dysfunction.

answers.name: Thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: Splenic sequestration lowers platelets.

answers.name: Migraine headache
answers.pearl: Headaches are reported more often than in the general population.

answers.name: Recurrent miscarriage
answers.pearl: Recurrent abortions in women can reveal undiagnosed Wilson disease.

answers.name: Handwriting deterioration
answers.pearl: Deterioration of fine motor control, such as handwriting, is a common early complaint.

answers.name: Azure lunulae
answers.pearl: Bluish discoloration of the nail half-moons is a rare cutaneous sign.

answers.name: Mania
answers.pearl: Manic features are described among psychiatric presentations.

answers.name: Fanconi syndrome
answers.pearl: Proximal tubular copper injury causes Fanconi-type changes.

answers.name: Early osteoarthritis
answers.pearl: Joint degeneration of the knees and wrists can occur in young patients.

answers.name: Infertility
answers.pearl: Fertility can be reduced in untreated disease.

answers.name: Nephrolithiasis
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria and tubular dysfunction can lead to stones.

answers.name: Oculomotor abnormalities
answers.pearl: Impaired vertical gaze and saccadic abnormalities may be seen.

answers.name: Spontaneous fractures
answers.pearl: Bone demineralization predisposes to fractures.

answers.name: Aminoaciduria
answers.pearl: Tubular dysfunction produces aminoaciduria.

answers.name: Sleep disorders
answers.pearl: Sleep disturbances occur and may relate to basal ganglia involvement.

answers.name: Hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: Tubular copper injury can cause calcium wasting.

answers.name: Rickets
answers.pearl: Tubular disease with phosphate wasting can cause rickets in children.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Cardiac involvement is rare but described in cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Rhythm abnormalities are reported in Wilson disease.

answers.name: Hyperpigmentation of the shins
answers.pearl: Hyperpigmentation over the lower legs has been described.

answers.name: Nephrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Calcium deposition can be seen with renal tubular disease.

answers.name: Chondrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Articular calcification has been reported in Wilson disease.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Neuropathy is uncommon but reported, often as a treatment effect.

answers.name: Hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Parathyroid dysfunction has been reported in case series.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: HCC is rare in Wilson disease but can complicate cirrhosis.

answers.name: Low alkaline phosphatase to bilirubin ratio
answers.pearl: A ratio below 4 together with AST:ALT above 2.2 suggests Wilson-related acute liver failure.

answers.name: AST to ALT ratio above 2.2
answers.pearl: A high AST:ALT ratio with a low ALP:bilirubin ratio suggests Wilson-related acute liver failure.

answers.name: Steatosis
answers.pearl: Hepatic steatosis can be a presenting finding and is commonly mistaken for NAFLD.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis-like presentation
answers.pearl: Wilson disease can mimic autoimmune hepatitis with elevated IgG and autoantibodies.

answers.name: Asymptomatic transaminase elevation
answers.pearl: Some patients are identified when persistent elevation in aminotransferases is evaluated.

answers.name: Face of the giant panda sign
answers.pearl: A midbrain MRI pattern in Wilson disease from tegmental hyperintensity with sparing of the red nucleus.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of peripheral edema.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pretibial myxedema and Hypothyroidism (nonpitting, so only loosely 'edema'); Lymphedema (nonpitting later); Eosinophilic fasciitis (woody induration more than fluid edema); RS3PE and POEMS syndrome (rare, literature-supported); Paget disease of bone (high-output state, uncommon); Gabapentinoids (mechanism unclear). Filariasis, nephritic syndrome and angioedema scored as board traps.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Elevated venous pressure and renal sodium retention produce bilateral dependent pitting edema.

answers.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
answers.pearl: Incompetent venous valves cause ambulatory venous hypertension with edema, hyperpigmentation, and stasis changes.

answers.name: Deep vein thrombosis
answers.pearl: Acute unilateral leg swelling with calf tenderness should prompt duplex ultrasonography.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Hypoalbuminemia, portal hypertension, and secondary hyperaldosteronism combine to cause leg edema and ascites.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and primary renal sodium retention causes anasarca and periorbital edema.

answers.name: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Amlodipine and nifedipine dilate arterioles more than venules, raising capillary hydrostatic pressure and causing dose-related ankle edema.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced sodium excretion causes volume expansion and edema, especially with advanced CKD.

answers.name: Obesity
answers.pearl: Increased venous pressure, sleep apnea, and reduced mobility contribute to chronic dependent leg edema.

answers.name: Lymphedema
answers.pearl: Impaired lymphatic drainage causes protein-rich swelling that is initially pitting and later firm, including the toes (Stemmer sign).

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Low oncotic pressure from malnutrition or protein-losing states shifts fluid into the interstitium.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Prostaglandin inhibition causes renal sodium and water retention and can worsen edema and heart failure.

answers.name: Cellulitis
answers.pearl: Infection causes local inflammatory edema, usually unilateral with erythema, warmth, and tenderness.

answers.name: Prolonged standing or sitting
answers.pearl: Gravity-dependent venous pooling without calf muscle pump activity causes benign bilateral ankle swelling.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Venous compression by the gravid uterus plus sodium retention causes physiologic leg edema.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Myxedema produces nonpitting, mucin-related swelling, often with periorbital puffiness and delayed reflexes.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid effect and sodium retention cause edema, particularly with fludrocortisone and prednisone.

answers.name: Thiazolidinediones
answers.pearl: Pioglitazone causes PPAR-gamma mediated renal sodium retention and edema, and is contraindicated in advanced heart failure.

answers.name: Pelvic mass compression
answers.pearl: Pelvic tumors or adenopathy can compress iliac veins or lymphatics, causing leg swelling.
