answers.name: Post-thrombotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Chronic valve damage after DVT causes persistent swelling, pain, and skin changes in the affected limb.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Right ventricular failure from elevated pulmonary pressures leads to systemic venous congestion and edema.

answers.name: Idiopathic cyclic edema
answers.pearl: Women develop fluctuating fluid retention with orthostatic weight gain without identifiable heart, liver, or kidney disease.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis
answers.pearl: Fixed ventricular filling raises systemic venous pressure and can present with edema and ascites despite normal EF.

answers.name: Inferior vena cava obstruction
answers.pearl: IVC thrombosis or tumor invasion causes bilateral leg swelling, often with collateral abdominal veins.

answers.name: Protein-losing enteropathy
answers.pearl: Gut protein loss from intestinal lymphangiectasia, Menetrier disease, or inflammatory bowel disease causes hypoalbuminemic edema.

answers.name: Minoxidil
answers.pearl: This potent vasodilator causes reflex sodium and water retention, often requiring a loop diuretic.

answers.name: Gabapentinoids
answers.pearl: Gabapentin and pregabalin commonly cause peripheral edema through an incompletely understood vascular mechanism.

answers.name: Complex regional pain syndrome
answers.pearl: Limb swelling, allodynia, and autonomic changes can follow injury and mimic other causes of unilateral edema.

answers.name: Compartment syndrome
answers.pearl: Swelling within a closed fascial space causes pain out of proportion, tense edema, and neurovascular compromise.

answers.name: Arteriovenous fistula
answers.pearl: A large AV shunt raises venous pressure and can cause limb edema and high-output heart failure.

answers.name: Pretibial myxedema
answers.pearl: Thyroid dermopathy of Graves disease causes nonpitting, violaceous plaques over the shins from glycosaminoglycan deposition.

answers.name: May-Thurner syndrome
answers.pearl: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the right common iliac artery predisposes to left leg swelling and DVT.

answers.name: Interleukin-2 therapy
answers.pearl: High-dose IL-2 causes capillary leak syndrome with generalized edema, hypotension, and hypoalbuminemia.

answers.name: Wet beriberi
answers.pearl: Thiamine deficiency causes high-output heart failure with peripheral edema.

answers.name: Systemic capillary leak syndrome
answers.pearl: Episodic endothelial leak causes edema, hypotension, hypoalbuminemia, and hemoconcentration, with a monoclonal gammopathy in many patients.

answers.name: Paget disease of bone
answers.pearl: Extensive disease acts as a high-output arteriovenous shunt and may contribute to cardiac failure and limb swelling.

answers.name: Eosinophilic fasciitis
answers.pearl: Shulman syndrome presents with edematous, woody induration of the limbs with a groove sign and peripheral eosinophilia.

answers.name: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
answers.pearl: Capillary malformation, venous anomalies, and limb overgrowth cause chronic unilateral limb swelling.

answers.name: Milroy disease
answers.pearl: Hereditary lymphedema from VEGFR3 mutations presents in infancy with leg swelling.

answers.name: RS3PE syndrome
aliases: remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema
answers.pearl: Remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema causes sudden bilateral hand and foot edema in older adults and can accompany occult malignancy.

answers.name: POEMS syndrome
answers.pearl: VEGF-driven disease with polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, M-protein and skin changes that frequently includes edema, effusions, and ascites.

answers.name: Filariasis
answers.pearl: Wuchereria bancrofti infection obstructs lymphatics and causes elephantiasis, a classic boards answer.

answers.name: Acute glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Nephritic syndrome causes sodium retention with periorbital edema, hypertension, and hematuria.

answers.name: Angioedema
answers.pearl: Bradykinin or histamine-mediated swelling, classically from ACE inhibitors or C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency, is nonpitting and not dependent.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause photosensitivity.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Sulfonylureas (older, minor reports); Statins (case reports, class effect uncertain); Ranitidine/H2 blockers (rare reports); Benzodiazepines (rare); Tricyclic antidepressants (uncommon); Efavirenz and Imatinib (case-level or pseudoporphyria); Olanzapine (case reports); Artificial sweeteners (historical); Cephalosporins (case reports). Psoralens, Demeclocycline and Amiodarone scored as board traps.

answers.name: Doxycycline
answers.pearl: Tetracyclines cause a dose-dependent phototoxic reaction resembling severe sunburn.

answers.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
answers.pearl: Thiazides cause photosensitivity and are associated with increased risk of squamous cell and basal cell carcinoma.

answers.name: Fluoroquinolones
answers.pearl: Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and especially lomefloxacin cause phototoxic reactions.

answers.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide antibiotics can cause both phototoxic and photoallergic reactions.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Propionic acid derivatives, especially ketoprofen and naproxen, cause photoallergic and phototoxic reactions, and naproxen can cause pseudoporphyria.

answers.name: Furosemide
answers.pearl: Loop diuretics are sulfonamide derivatives that can produce phototoxicity and pseudoporphyria.

answers.name: Isotretinoin
answers.pearl: Retinoids thin the stratum corneum and increase UV sensitivity.

answers.name: Voriconazole
answers.pearl: Phototoxicity with long-term use is associated with accelerated cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

answers.name: Chlorpromazine
answers.pearl: Phenothiazines cause phototoxicity and blue-gray photodistributed pigmentation with chronic use.

answers.name: Methotrexate
answers.pearl: Methotrexate can produce photosensitivity and recall of sunburn in previously UV-exposed skin.

answers.name: Hydroxychloroquine
answers.pearl: Antimalarials can cause photosensitivity, though they are also used to treat photosensitive lupus.

answers.name: Statins
answers.pearl: Simvastatin, atorvastatin, and others have been linked to photosensitive eruptions.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Aromatic anticonvulsants can cause photosensitive eruptions and photoallergic reactions.

answers.name: Vemurafenib
answers.pearl: BRAF inhibitors commonly cause severe UVA-mediated phototoxicity.

answers.name: Griseofulvin
answers.pearl: This antifungal can cause photosensitivity and exacerbate or unmask lupus.

answers.name: Nifedipine
answers.pearl: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers can cause photodistributed telangiectasias and photosensitivity.

answers.name: Fluorouracil
answers.pearl: Systemic and topical fluorouracil can cause photosensitivity and enhanced reactions to sunlight.

answers.name: Benzodiazepines
answers.pearl: Alprazolam and chlordiazepoxide rarely cause photosensitive eruptions.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Amitriptyline, imipramine, and desipramine can produce photosensitivity.

answers.name: Ranitidine
answers.pearl: H2 blockers have occasional case reports of photosensitivity.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Quinine and quinidine can cause photoallergic reactions and lichenoid photodermatitis.

answers.name: Sulfonylureas
answers.pearl: Glipizide and glyburide are sulfonamide derivatives with occasional photosensitivity.

answers.name: Pirfenidone
answers.pearl: Photosensitivity is a labeled adverse effect in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, so sunscreen is advised.

answers.name: Fenofibrate
answers.pearl: Fibrates, particularly fenofibrate and gemfibrozil, can cause photoallergic reactions.

answers.name: Vandetanib
answers.pearl: This thyroid cancer kinase inhibitor carries a labeled phototoxicity warning.

answers.name: Sorafenib
answers.pearl: Multikinase inhibitors can cause phototoxic skin eruptions and hand-foot skin reaction.

answers.name: St. John's wort
answers.pearl: Hypericin is a photosensitizer causing phototoxic reactions, especially at high doses.

answers.name: Lomefloxacin
answers.pearl: This fluoroquinolone has among the highest phototoxic rates and was withdrawn in the United States.

answers.name: Dapsone
answers.pearl: Sulfone derivatives can rarely cause photosensitivity and photoallergic reactions.

answers.name: Triamterene
answers.pearl: Triamterene alone or combined with hydrochlorothiazide can cause photosensitivity.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: Antiretrovirals such as efavirenz have been associated with photosensitive eruptions.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Imatinib has been linked to pseudoporphyria and photosensitivity.

answers.name: Flutamide
answers.pearl: This antiandrogen is a well-documented cause of photosensitive dermatitis.

answers.name: Cyclamates
answers.pearl: Artificial sweeteners such as cyclamate and saccharin are sulfonamide-like and have caused photosensitive eruptions.

answers.name: Telaprevir
answers.pearl: This hepatitis C protease inhibitor carried a labeled photosensitivity warning.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Ceftazidime and certain other cephalosporins have case reports of photosensitivity.

answers.name: Sparfloxacin
answers.pearl: Another highly phototoxic fluoroquinolone, now largely withdrawn.

answers.name: Olanzapine
answers.pearl: Atypical antipsychotics have rare case reports of photosensitivity.

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Photosensitivity occurs in many patients and chronic use causes blue-gray photodistributed pigmentation; a classic boards answer.

answers.name: Psoralens
answers.pearl: Methoxsalen is the intentional photosensitizer for PUVA therapy and is a classic boards phototoxic drug.

answers.name: Demeclocycline
answers.pearl: Among tetracyclines it carries the highest phototoxic potential and is a classic boards answer.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of hereditary hemochromatosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Porphyria cutanea tarda association (HFE is a risk factor, not a manifestation per se); Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism features such as gynecomastia and testicular atrophy (scored as features of pituitary involvement); Increased infection risk (Vibrio vulnificus, Yersinia, Listeria; mechanistic, case-supported); Hypothyroidism and Adrenal insufficiency (uncommon, iron deposition); Pseudogout (chondrocalcinosis overlap); Hepatic encephalopathy as an end-stage feature. Pseudogout and 2nd-3rd MCP arthropathy scored as board traps.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Nonspecific fatigue is the most common early symptom and often precedes any organ damage.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Joint pain, especially of the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints, is a common presenting complaint.

answers.name: Elevated liver enzymes
answers.pearl: Mild elevations in transaminases often prompt the first iron studies.

answers.name: Hepatomegaly
answers.pearl: Iron-laden hepatocytes enlarge the liver, often found on examination before symptoms develop.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Progressive hepatic iron overload leads to fibrosis and cirrhosis, particularly with alcohol or ferritin above 1000.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Pancreatic beta-cell iron deposition and insulin resistance produce diabetes.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis in hemochromatosis carries a high risk of HCC, estimated at over 20-fold in cirrhotic patients.

answers.name: Skin hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: Increased melanin and hemosiderin cause bronze or gray skin discoloration, especially in sun-exposed areas.

answers.name: Erectile dysfunction
answers.pearl: Pituitary iron deposition causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, leading to impotence and low libido.

answers.name: Decreased libido
answers.pearl: Loss of libido results from gonadotroph damage in the anterior pituitary.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Right upper quadrant discomfort from hepatomegaly is a recognized early symptom.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Iron deposition in the myocardium produces a dilated and sometimes restrictive cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Elevated ferritin
answers.pearl: Ferritin reflects iron stores but is also an acute-phase reactant, so it is an unreliable marker alone.

answers.name: Arrhythmias
answers.pearl: Cardiac siderosis causes conduction defects and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias.

answers.name: Hypogonadism
answers.pearl: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism from pituitary iron deposition is a common endocrine feature.

answers.name: Amenorrhea
answers.pearl: Women may develop secondary amenorrhea from pituitary involvement, with menopause delaying iron accumulation until later.

answers.name: Testicular atrophy
answers.pearl: Hypogonadism leads to small, soft testes.

answers.name: Ascites
answers.pearl: Decompensated cirrhosis causes ascites.

answers.name: Chondrocalcinosis
answers.pearl: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition in articular cartilage is common with iron arthropathy, and iron inhibits pyrophosphatase.

answers.name: Hook-like osteophytes
answers.pearl: Characteristic hook-shaped osteophytes at the metacarpal heads of the second and third digits suggest hemochromatosis arthropathy.

answers.name: Gynecomastia
answers.pearl: Altered sex hormone balance from liver disease and hypogonadism can cause breast enlargement in men.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Hypogonadism and direct iron toxicity to osteoblasts reduce bone density.

answers.name: Loss of body hair
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis and hypogonadism cause loss of axillary and pubic hair.

answers.name: Spider angiomata
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis causes hyperestrogenism-related vascular spiders.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension from cirrhosis causes splenic enlargement.

answers.name: Liver failure
answers.pearl: End-stage hepatic disease causes coagulopathy, encephalopathy and jaundice.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Iron deposition in the thyroid can cause primary hypothyroidism, though this is less common than other endocrinopathies.

answers.name: Increased infection risk
answers.pearl: Excess iron promotes siderophilic organisms, particularly Vibrio vulnificus, Yersinia enterocolitica, and Listeria.

answers.name: Elevated transferrin saturation
answers.pearl: Transferrin saturation above 45 percent is the earliest biochemical abnormality and the best screening test.

answers.name: Variceal bleeding
answers.pearl: Portal hypertension in cirrhosis causes esophageal varices that can bleed.

answers.name: Hypopituitarism
answers.pearl: Pituitary iron deposition can impair multiple anterior pituitary axes beyond gonadotropins.

answers.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Cirrhosis with impaired ammonia clearance causes neurocognitive dysfunction.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Iron deposition in the adrenal glands can occasionally cause cortisol deficiency.

answers.name: Cognitive changes
answers.pearl: Neuropsychiatric symptoms including depression and memory problems have been reported with iron overload.

answers.name: Hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Parathyroid iron deposition has been reported, mostly in secondary iron overload states.

answers.name: Porphyria cutanea tarda
answers.pearl: HFE mutations are a risk factor for PCT, and iron removal can induce remission.

answers.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
answers.pearl: Restrictive filling from myocardial iron deposition can present with diastolic dysfunction.

answers.name: Hypogonadism from juvenile hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: HJV or hepcidin mutations produce early-onset hypogonadism and cardiomyopathy before age 30.

answers.name: Hepatic hemosiderosis on MRI
answers.pearl: T2-weighted MRI shows low signal in the liver from iron deposition, allowing noninvasive quantification.

answers.name: Cirrhosis-related coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Decreased synthesis of clotting factors can cause bleeding in decompensated disease.

answers.name: Hepatic iron index elevated
answers.pearl: A hepatic iron index above 1.9 on biopsy suggests homozygous hemochromatosis rather than secondary siderosis.

answers.name: Diabetic complications
answers.pearl: Hemochromatosis-related diabetes can lead to usual microvascular complications.

answers.name: Bronze diabetes
aliases: triad of cirrhosis diabetes and bronzing
answers.pearl: The classic triad of cirrhosis, bronze skin, and diabetes is a boards staple.

answers.name: Pseudogout
answers.pearl: CPPD arthritis with chondrocalcinosis of knees, wrists, and symphysis pubis is a classic association.

answers.name: Second and third MCP arthropathy
answers.pearl: Involvement of the second and third MCP joints is the signature joint pattern of hemochromatosis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypertriglyceridemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Lipodystrophy subtypes (rarity of each); Glycogen storage disease type I (secondary HTG via lactic acidosis/insulin deficiency); Systemic lupus and Multiple myeloma/MGUS (autoantibody or paraprotein inhibition of lipoprotein lipase, case-supported); Acute intermittent porphyria (weak); Sepsis; Lymphoma; Anti-lipoprotein lipase antibodies. Familial chylomicronemia syndrome, Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia and Familial combined hyperlipidemia scored as board traps.

answers.name: Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Insulin deficiency or resistance reduces lipoprotein lipase activity and increases hepatic VLDL production.

answers.name: Obesity
answers.pearl: Visceral fat and insulin resistance increase free fatty acid flux to the liver and VLDL secretion.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Alcohol increases hepatic fatty acid synthesis and reduces VLDL clearance, and can precipitate severe hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: High-carbohydrate or high-fat diet
answers.pearl: Excess simple carbohydrate and fat intake raises triglyceride production, particularly with fructose.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Reduced lipoprotein lipase and LDL receptor activity raise triglycerides and LDL.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced lipoprotein lipase and hepatic lipase activity impair triglyceride clearance, especially in uremia.

answers.name: Nephrotic syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic overproduction of lipoproteins and loss of lipoprotein lipase cofactors raise triglycerides and cholesterol.

answers.name: Familial hypertriglyceridemia
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant overproduction of VLDL causes isolated elevated triglycerides in adulthood.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Estrogen-driven VLDL production and reduced lipoprotein lipase raise triglycerides, which can precipitate pancreatitis in the third trimester.

answers.name: Estrogen therapy
answers.pearl: Oral estrogens increase hepatic VLDL synthesis, raising triglycerides.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides can modestly elevate triglycerides through reduced insulin sensitivity.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Nonselective beta blockers can raise triglycerides and lower HDL through unopposed alpha activity and reduced lipoprotein lipase.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Glucocorticoids increase VLDL production and induce insulin resistance.

answers.name: Atypical antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Olanzapine and clozapine cause weight gain, insulin resistance, and elevated triglycerides.

answers.name: Protease inhibitors
answers.pearl: HIV protease inhibitors, particularly ritonavir, impair lipid metabolism and markedly raise triglycerides.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Estrogenic activity can raise triglycerides, occasionally precipitating pancreatitis.

answers.name: Retinoids
answers.pearl: Isotretinoin and acitretin raise triglycerides through increased hepatic VLDL production.

answers.name: Cholestasis
answers.pearl: Lipoprotein X and altered lipid metabolism in cholestatic disease can raise triglycerides.

answers.name: Sirolimus
answers.pearl: mTOR inhibitors commonly raise triglycerides and cholesterol by impairing lipoprotein clearance.

answers.name: Cyclosporine
answers.pearl: Calcineurin inhibitors cause dyslipidemia, including elevated triglycerides.

answers.name: Bile acid sequestrants
answers.pearl: Colesevelam and cholestyramine increase hepatic VLDL production and can worsen existing hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Lipodystrophy
answers.pearl: Loss of adipose tissue causes ectopic fat deposition, severe insulin resistance, and marked hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Hereditary lipoprotein lipase deficiency
answers.pearl: Loss of LPL activity causes severe chylomicronemia with eruptive xanthomas and recurrent pancreatitis.

answers.name: Intravenous lipid emulsions
answers.pearl: Parenteral nutrition with lipid emulsions or propofol delivers triglycerides directly, exceeding clearance capacity.

answers.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
answers.pearl: Insulin resistance and hyperandrogenism are associated with atherogenic dyslipidemia, including high triglycerides.

answers.name: Propofol
answers.pearl: The lipid emulsion vehicle provides triglycerides, and prolonged infusion can cause marked hypertriglyceridemia and pancreatitis.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Cortisol excess causes visceral obesity and insulin resistance with elevated triglycerides.

answers.name: Acromegaly
answers.pearl: Growth hormone excess causes insulin resistance and impaired lipoprotein lipase activity.

answers.name: Acute stress or sepsis
answers.pearl: Cytokines such as TNF and IL-1 reduce lipoprotein lipase activity and raise triglycerides.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: Inflammation, nephrotic syndrome, and anti-lipoprotein lipase antibodies can raise triglycerides.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Paraproteins can bind and inhibit lipoprotein lipase or apolipoproteins, causing secondary hypertriglyceridemia.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Rare cases of hypertriglyceridemia are attributed to antibodies against lipoprotein lipase or cytokine effects.

answers.name: Glycogen storage disease type I
answers.pearl: Von Gierke disease causes hypertriglyceridemia from impaired glucose-6-phosphatase function with hepatic lipogenesis.

answers.name: Apolipoprotein C-II deficiency
answers.pearl: Absent apoC-II, the cofactor for lipoprotein lipase, produces severe chylomicronemia in adults and children.

answers.name: GPIHBP1 deficiency
answers.pearl: Loss of the endothelial protein that transports lipoprotein lipase to the capillary lumen causes severe chylomicronemia.

answers.name: APOA5 mutation
answers.pearl: Loss-of-function variants in apolipoprotein A-V reduce lipoprotein lipase activation, raising triglycerides.

answers.name: Anti-lipoprotein lipase antibodies
answers.pearl: Autoantibodies against LPL or GPIHBP1 have caused acquired chylomicronemia in autoimmune disease.

answers.name: LMF1 mutation
answers.pearl: Lipase maturation factor 1 defects prevent proper LPL folding and secretion, causing chylomicronemia.

answers.name: Familial chylomicronemia syndrome
answers.pearl: Homozygous or compound heterozygous defects in the LPL pathway cause severe triglyceride elevation, eruptive xanthomas, and pancreatitis.

answers.name: Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia
answers.pearl: ApoE2 homozygosity with a second metabolic hit causes mixed hyperlipidemia with palmar xanthomas and remnant lipoproteins.

answers.name: Familial combined hyperlipidemia
answers.pearl: Overproduction of apoB with variable elevations of cholesterol and triglycerides is the most common genetic dyslipidemia.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of unintentional weight loss in an older adult.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypercalcemia (scored as a cause via anorexia, less direct); Polymyalgia rheumatica / Giant cell arteritis (weight loss is a recognized feature); Constrictive pericarditis and Cardiac cachexia from heart failure (indirect); Subclinical hyperthyroidism (weak); Apathetic hyperthyroidism is the board version. Lead/mercury and Chronic mesenteric ischemia (food fear) are less common but literature-supported; Hypoadrenalism subtle.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Occult cancer, notably lung, gastrointestinal, pancreatic, and hematologic, is the leading organic cause in older adults after nonmalignant GI disease.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Depression is among the most common causes of weight loss in older adults through reduced appetite and interest in eating.

answers.name: Dementia
answers.pearl: Cognitive decline causes forgetting to eat, apraxia of feeding, and dysphagia.

answers.name: Medication adverse effects
answers.pearl: Polypharmacy including digoxin, metformin, SSRIs, and cholinesterase inhibitors can cause anorexia or nausea.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Increased metabolic rate causes weight loss, and older adults may present with apathy rather than adrenergic symptoms.

answers.name: Social isolation or poverty
answers.pearl: Food insecurity, loneliness, and inability to shop or cook contribute to inadequate intake.

answers.name: Poor dentition
answers.pearl: Ill-fitting dentures, dental pain, or edentulism limit food choices and intake.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Esophageal or oropharyngeal swallowing disorders reduce intake and may be unrecognized in older adults.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Uncontrolled hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis and catabolic weight loss from insulin deficiency.

answers.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
answers.pearl: Increased work of breathing, inflammation, and early satiety cause cachexia in advanced COPD.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Cardiac cachexia results from inflammation, gut edema, anorexia, and increased metabolic demand.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Uremia causes nausea, dysgeusia, and anorexia, and protein-energy wasting is common in advanced disease.

answers.name: Peptic ulcer disease
answers.pearl: Postprandial pain and early satiety cause reduced intake.

answers.name: Alcohol use disorder
answers.pearl: Alcohol displaces nutrient intake and causes malabsorption and liver disease.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms with weight loss, night sweats, and cough may represent reactivation in older adults.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Late-onset celiac disease can present with weight loss and malabsorption even without classic diarrhea.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Chronic intestinal inflammation causes malabsorption, diarrhea, and anorexia.

answers.name: Chronic pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Exocrine insufficiency causes steatorrhea, maldigestion, and fear of eating from postprandial pain.

answers.name: Parkinson disease
answers.pearl: Dysphagia, tremor, depression, and hyposmia reduce intake, and dyskinesias raise energy expenditure.

answers.name: Stroke
answers.pearl: Dysphagia, depression, and functional impairment reduce oral intake after stroke.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: Wasting syndrome, opportunistic infection, and malabsorption cause weight loss in untreated HIV.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Subacute infection causes constitutional symptoms including anorexia and weight loss.

answers.name: Giant cell arteritis
answers.pearl: Large-vessel vasculitis causes constitutional symptoms with weight loss, fever, and jaw claudication in older adults.

answers.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation with shoulder and hip girdle stiffness can include weight loss and malaise.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia, renal failure, and anemia in myeloma cause anorexia and weight loss.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: B symptoms of fever, night sweats, and weight loss accompany many lymphomas.

answers.name: Hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Anorexia, nausea, constipation, and volume depletion from high calcium contribute to weight loss.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency causes anorexia, nausea, weight loss, and fatigue.

answers.name: Chronic mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Postprandial abdominal pain causes food fear and weight loss in patients with atherosclerotic mesenteric disease.

answers.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
answers.pearl: Bacterial overgrowth causes bile acid deconjugation, malabsorption, bloating, and weight loss.

answers.name: Chronic infections including osteomyelitis
answers.pearl: Persistent occult infection produces cytokine-mediated cachexia.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Hypercalcemia-related anorexia and constipation may contribute to weight loss.

answers.name: Sarcopenia and frailty
answers.pearl: Age-related loss of muscle and anabolic resistance accompanies reduced appetite, known as the anorexia of aging.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamine excess raises metabolic rate and causes weight loss alongside hypertension and sweating.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Systemic amyloid deposition in the gut and autonomic nerves causes malabsorption and weight loss.

answers.name: Cocaine or stimulant use
answers.pearl: Stimulants suppress appetite and raise energy expenditure, an uncommon but real contributor even in older adults.

answers.name: Whipple disease
answers.pearl: Tropheryma whipplei infection causes malabsorption, arthralgia, and weight loss, usually in middle-aged and older men.

answers.name: Hypopituitarism
answers.pearl: Pituitary hormone deficiency, including secondary adrenal and thyroid failure, may cause anorexia and weight loss.

answers.name: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
answers.pearl: Eosinophilic infiltration of the gut wall causes pain, malabsorption, and weight loss.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism from amiodarone
answers.pearl: Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis presents with weight loss in older adults taking the drug for arrhythmias.

answers.name: Heavy metal poisoning
answers.pearl: Chronic lead, mercury, or arsenic exposure can cause anorexia, abdominal pain, and weight loss.

answers.name: Mast cell disease
answers.pearl: Systemic mastocytosis can cause malabsorption, diarrhea, and weight loss.

answers.name: Chronic mesenteric venous thrombosis
answers.pearl: Chronic venous outflow obstruction of the intestine can cause malabsorption and weight loss.

answers.name: Pancreatic cancer
answers.pearl: Weight loss with painless jaundice or new diabetes in older adults is a boards staple.

answers.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
answers.pearl: Gastrinoma causes peptic ulcers and diarrhea with steatorrhea and weight loss.

answers.name: Carcinoid syndrome
answers.pearl: Serotonin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor causes diarrhea, flushing, and weight loss.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause or worsen heart failure or cardiomyopathy.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pregabalin (fluid retention, label warning only); Cilostazol (contraindicated in HF, mainly class labeling); Itraconazole (negative inotropy, labeled); Triptans/ergots and Methylphenidate (indirect, vasoconstriction); Lithium (rare cardiomyopathy reports); Chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine (rare cardiomyopathy); Clozapine (myocarditis/cardiomyopathy, rare); Anagrelide; Hydroxyurea. Cobalt, Emetine and Fenfluramine-phentermine scored as board traps.

answers.name: Doxorubicin
answers.pearl: Anthracyclines cause dose-dependent irreversible cardiomyopathy via oxidative stress and topoisomerase II-beta, typically above 450-550 mg/m2.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Initiation or uptitration of a beta blocker in decompensated patients can worsen acute heart failure.

answers.name: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
answers.pearl: NSAIDs cause sodium and water retention and blunt diuretic effect, precipitating decompensation.

answers.name: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Verapamil and diltiazem are negatively inotropic and harmful in HFrEF.

answers.name: Thiazolidinediones
answers.pearl: Pioglitazone and rosiglitazone cause renal sodium retention and edema, and are contraindicated in NYHA class III-IV heart failure.

answers.name: Trastuzumab
answers.pearl: HER2 inhibition impairs cardiomyocyte survival and causes reversible cardiotoxicity, especially after anthracyclines.

answers.name: Class I antiarrhythmics
answers.pearl: Flecainide and propafenone are negatively inotropic and increase mortality in structural heart disease.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Chronic heavy alcohol use causes dilated cardiomyopathy that may improve with abstinence.

answers.name: Cocaine
answers.pearl: Catecholamine excess, ischemia, and direct toxicity can cause cardiomyopathy and acute heart failure.

answers.name: Methamphetamine
answers.pearl: Chronic use causes a dilated cardiomyopathy with pulmonary hypertension from catecholamine toxicity.

answers.name: Cyclophosphamide
answers.pearl: High-dose cyclophosphamide can cause acute hemorrhagic myocarditis and heart failure.

answers.name: Dronedarone
answers.pearl: Contraindicated in decompensated or NYHA class IV heart failure after excess mortality in ANDROMEDA.

answers.name: Itraconazole
answers.pearl: Negative inotropic effects led to a boxed warning against use in patients with ventricular dysfunction.

answers.name: Minoxidil
answers.pearl: Reflex tachycardia and sodium retention can precipitate decompensation, and it can cause pericardial effusion.

answers.name: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors
answers.pearl: Infliximab at high doses worsened heart failure in a randomized trial, so it is avoided in NYHA class III-IV.

answers.name: Imatinib
answers.pearl: Tyrosine kinase inhibition can cause left ventricular dysfunction and fluid retention in some patients.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Mineralocorticoid effects cause sodium and water retention that can precipitate decompensation.

answers.name: Cilostazol
answers.pearl: Phosphodiesterase 3 inhibitors increased mortality in HFrEF, so cilostazol is contraindicated in heart failure of any severity.

answers.name: Bevacizumab
answers.pearl: VEGF inhibition causes hypertension and LV dysfunction through endothelial dysfunction.

answers.name: Pregabalin
answers.pearl: Peripheral edema and cases of precipitated heart failure carry labeled warnings in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Fluorouracil
answers.pearl: Coronary vasospasm can lead to ischemia and a stress-type cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: Immune-mediated myocarditis can cause fulminant heart failure and arrhythmias.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Rare cardiotoxicity including bradyarrhythmia and heart failure exacerbation has been reported.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Overdose or high doses cause negative inotropy and conduction slowing.

answers.name: Sodium-containing intravenous fluids
answers.pearl: Sodium and volume loading precipitates congestion in patients with limited cardiac reserve.

answers.name: Saxagliptin
answers.pearl: The SAVOR-TIMI 53 trial showed increased hospitalization for heart failure, and alogliptin showed a signal as well.

answers.name: Interferon alfa
answers.pearl: Interferons have been associated with cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias in rare cases.

answers.name: Interleukin-2
answers.pearl: Capillary leak and direct myocardial effects cause hypotension and LV dysfunction.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Clozapine can cause myocarditis, usually within the first weeks, and cardiomyopathy with longer exposure.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Cardiotoxicity is uncommon, but lithium can cause cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias especially in toxicity.

answers.name: Antimalarials
answers.pearl: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can cause restrictive or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with long-term use.

answers.name: Sympathomimetic decongestants
answers.pearl: Pseudoephedrine and similar agents raise blood pressure and heart rate and can worsen congestive symptoms.

answers.name: Ergot-derived dopamine agonists
answers.pearl: Cabergoline and pergolide cause valvular fibrosis with regurgitation that can lead to heart failure.

answers.name: Methysergide
answers.pearl: Ergot derivative that caused retroperitoneal and cardiac valvular fibrosis.

answers.name: Arsenic trioxide
answers.pearl: QT prolongation is the best-known toxicity, but heart failure and effusions also occur.

answers.name: Anagrelide
answers.pearl: Phosphodiesterase 3 inhibition causes tachycardia and has been associated with cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

answers.name: Hydroxyurea
answers.pearl: Rare case-level reports of cardiomyopathy have been published.

answers.name: Proteasome inhibitors
answers.pearl: Carfilzomib and bortezomib have been associated with new or worsened heart failure.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Agents such as dasatinib, nilotinib, ponatinib, and lapatinib are linked to heart failure and vascular events.

answers.name: Mitoxantrone
answers.pearl: An anthracenedione used in multiple sclerosis that produces cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Cardiotoxic herbal ephedra
answers.pearl: Ephedra (ma huang) caused arrhythmias, hypertension, and cardiomyopathy.

answers.name: Rituximab
answers.pearl: Rare arrhythmias and cardiomyopathy cases have been reported during infusion.

answers.name: Paclitaxel
answers.pearl: Taxanes cause fluid retention with docetaxel and occasional LV dysfunction, particularly with anthracyclines.

answers.name: Fenfluramine-phentermine
answers.pearl: Anorectic agents caused serotonin-mediated valvulopathy and pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Cobalt
answers.pearl: Chronic cobalt exposure from metal-on-metal hip prostheses has caused cardiomyopathy, and historically beer additives did.

answers.name: Emetine
answers.pearl: Ipecac alkaloid abuse by patients with eating disorders causes myopathy and cardiomyopathy.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of adult-onset Still disease.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pericarditis tamponade and Myocarditis (reported, uncommon); Pulmonary hypertension (case-series level); Acute respiratory distress syndrome and Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (severe MAS-associated or case-level); Thrombotic microangiopathy / TTP-like (case reports); Aseptic meningitis (rare); Amyloidosis AA (long-standing disease); Sensorineural hearing loss and Optic neuritis-type items are case-report level; Sore throat as most common early symptom is well documented. Macrophage activation syndrome, IL-18 and glycosylated ferritin scored as board traps.

answers.name: Quotidian fever
answers.pearl: Spiking fevers above 39 C, usually once daily in the afternoon or evening, are the defining feature and return to normal between spikes.

answers.name: Evanescent salmon-colored rash
answers.pearl: A transient, nonpruritic salmon-pink macular or maculopapular rash on the trunk and proximal limbs appears with fever spikes.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Joint pain is nearly universal and often present at disease onset.

answers.name: Arthritis
answers.pearl: A symmetric polyarthritis of knees, wrists, and ankles may become erosive, especially at the wrists.

answers.name: Sore throat
answers.pearl: A sore throat without exudate often precedes other features and can lead to a misdiagnosis of pharyngitis.

answers.name: Leukocytosis with neutrophilia
answers.pearl: White cell counts often exceed 15,000 with more than 80 percent neutrophils, helping separate this disease from infection only by exclusion.

answers.name: Hyperferritinemia
answers.pearl: Markedly elevated ferritin is typical, with a low glycosylated ferritin fraction below 20 percent supporting the diagnosis.

answers.name: Lymphadenopathy
answers.pearl: Generalized or cervical lymph node enlargement is common and can mimic lymphoma.

answers.name: Myalgia
answers.pearl: Muscle aches accompany fever spikes in many patients.

answers.name: Splenomegaly
answers.pearl: Enlargement of the spleen occurs in around half of patients.

answers.name: Elevated ESR and CRP
answers.pearl: Acute-phase reactants are markedly elevated during flares.

answers.name: Hepatomegaly
answers.pearl: Liver enlargement occurs in a minority of patients and accompanies abnormal liver tests.

answers.name: Elevated transaminases
answers.pearl: Mild to moderate elevations of AST and ALT are common and can be severe in fulminant disease.

answers.name: Anemia of chronic disease
answers.pearl: Normocytic anemia from chronic inflammation is frequently present.

answers.name: Thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Reactive thrombocytosis accompanies active inflammation.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Prolonged systemic inflammation leads to weight loss and fatigue.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms including fatigue and malaise are common.

answers.name: Pleuritis
answers.pearl: Serositis can cause pleural effusions and pleuritic chest pain.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial inflammation with pain or effusion occurs in a fraction of patients.

answers.name: Abdominal pain
answers.pearl: Abdominal pain may reflect serositis, lymphadenopathy, or hepatosplenomegaly.

answers.name: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase
answers.pearl: LDH is often elevated and extremely high levels suggest macrophage activation syndrome or lymphoma.

answers.name: Negative rheumatoid factor and ANA
answers.pearl: Seronegativity for RF and ANA is typical and supports the diagnosis by exclusion of other rheumatic disease.

answers.name: Persistent pruritic papules and plaques
answers.pearl: A persistent, linear, pruritic eruption with a dermographic or Koebner-like pattern is a distinct atypical skin finding.

answers.name: Hypoalbuminemia
answers.pearl: Low albumin reflects chronic inflammation and hepatic synthetic changes.

answers.name: Flagellate erythema
answers.pearl: Linear streaky pigmented lesions resembling bleomycin-induced erythema occur in Still disease.

answers.name: Dermographism
answers.pearl: Skin rash can be induced by scratching (Koebner), a clue to the evanescent eruption.

answers.name: Polyserositis
answers.pearl: Simultaneous inflammation of several serous membranes can occur.

answers.name: Leukopenia
answers.pearl: Atypical presentations or MAS-associated disease can have cytopenias instead of leukocytosis.

answers.name: Hypertriglyceridemia
answers.pearl: High triglycerides with falling fibrinogen and ESR signal MAS developing on a background of Still disease.

answers.name: Cervical spine involvement
answers.pearl: Cervical and carpal ankylosis can develop, and atlantoaxial subluxation has been reported.

answers.name: Reactive lymph node hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Node biopsy shows paracortical hyperplasia with immunoblasts, which can be mistaken for lymphoma.

answers.name: Carpal ankylosis
answers.pearl: Fusion of the carpal bones is a characteristic late radiographic finding.

answers.name: Temporomandibular joint involvement
answers.pearl: Jaw pain and limited opening reflect temporomandibular arthritis.

answers.name: Ascites
answers.pearl: Peritoneal serositis can occasionally cause ascites.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Rare cases of interstitial pneumonitis and ARDS have been described.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Cardiac inflammation is rare but reported, and can cause heart failure.

answers.name: Neutrophilic dermal infiltrate on skin biopsy
answers.pearl: Biopsy of the rash shows perivascular neutrophils, and persistent plaques show dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the upper epidermis.

answers.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
answers.pearl: Fulminant disease or MAS can cause ARDS with high mortality.

answers.name: Cardiac tamponade
answers.pearl: Large pericardial effusions can cause tamponade, particularly in flares.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Chronic uncontrolled inflammation can cause AA amyloidosis, with proteinuria or renal failure.

answers.name: Bone marrow hemophagocytosis
answers.pearl: Marrow may show hemophagocytic histiocytes, which suggests macrophage activation syndrome.

answers.name: Tarsal ankylosis
answers.pearl: Fusion of the tarsal bones can occur with long-standing disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
answers.pearl: Case series link Still disease with pulmonary arterial hypertension, including cases responding to IL-1 blockade.

answers.name: Elevated soluble IL-2 receptor
answers.pearl: Soluble CD25 rises with macrophage and T-cell activation and is markedly elevated in MAS.

answers.name: Hepatic failure
answers.pearl: Fulminant hepatitis with liver failure is a rare, life-threatening complication.

answers.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
answers.pearl: Severe flares and MAS can produce a consumptive coagulopathy.

answers.name: Thrombotic microangiopathy
answers.pearl: Rare cases mimic TTP with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Aseptic meningitis
answers.pearl: Neurologic involvement is rare, with meningitis, seizures, or encephalopathy described in case reports.

answers.name: Elevated S100A8/A9
answers.pearl: Serum S100 proteins (calprotectin) are markedly raised and correlate with disease activity.

answers.name: Orbital or ocular inflammation
answers.pearl: Uveitis, scleritis, and orbital pseudotumor are rare reported ocular manifestations.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Rare renal involvement apart from amyloidosis includes mesangial proliferation and IgA-type disease.

answers.name: Sensorineural hearing loss
answers.pearl: Rare case reports describe hearing loss that responds to immunosuppression.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Rare case reports of pulmonary hemorrhage appear in severe disease.

answers.name: Macrophage activation syndrome
answers.pearl: Life-threatening hemophagocytic complication with pancytopenia, falling ESR, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and extreme ferritin.

answers.name: Increased glycosylated ferritin deficit
answers.pearl: A glycosylated ferritin fraction below 20 percent has high specificity for AOSD.

answers.name: Elevated IL-18
answers.pearl: Very high serum IL-18 is a hallmark of the disease, frequently cited as a marker distinguishing it from infection and malignancy.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of Sjogren syndrome.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Dry skin and Dysphagia (frequent but nonspecific); Optic neuritis, Transverse myelitis and Hyperviscosity syndrome (usually via AQP4/NMO overlap or cryoglobulins, uncommon); Myositis (overlap-level).

answers.name: Dry eyes
answers.pearl: Lacrimal gland lymphocytic infiltration reduces tear production, causing gritty, burning eyes.

answers.name: Dry mouth
answers.pearl: Salivary gland infiltration causes xerostomia, difficulty swallowing dry food, and altered taste.

answers.name: Dental caries
answers.pearl: Loss of saliva's protective effects causes rapid cervical and root caries.

answers.name: Parotid gland enlargement
answers.pearl: Recurrent or chronic painless parotid swelling occurs in a sizable minority of patients.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Nonerosive polyarthralgia or arthritis in a rheumatoid-like distribution is common.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Disabling fatigue is among the most frequent and least specific systemic complaints.

answers.name: Oral candidiasis
answers.pearl: Reduced saliva predisposes to oropharyngeal candidiasis and angular cheilitis.

answers.name: Dry skin
answers.pearl: Cutaneous xerosis reflects exocrine gland dysfunction.

answers.name: Vaginal dryness
answers.pearl: Mucosal gland involvement causes vaginal dryness and painful intercourse.

answers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
answers.pearl: Seen in roughly a third of patients and may precede sicca symptoms.

answers.name: Dry cough
answers.pearl: Dryness of airway mucosa causes chronic nonproductive cough.

answers.name: Anti-Ro antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-Ro/SSA is the most common autoantibody and is associated with extraglandular disease.

answers.name: Anti-La antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-La/SSB usually accompanies anti-Ro and is more specific.

answers.name: Rheumatoid factor positivity
answers.pearl: RF is positive in most patients even without rheumatoid arthritis.

answers.name: Antinuclear antibody positivity
answers.pearl: ANA is positive in the majority, typically speckled pattern.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Sensorimotor and small fiber neuropathies are the most common neurologic manifestations.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia is most common; lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia is more characteristic.

answers.name: Purpura
answers.pearl: Palpable purpura of the legs reflects cryoglobulinemic or immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis.

answers.name: Hypergammaglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Polyclonal B-cell activation raises IgG and often the ESR.

answers.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
answers.pearl: Lymphocytic interstitial infiltration is the most common renal lesion.

answers.name: Hypokalemic paralysis
answers.pearl: Distal RTA with potassium wasting can present as acute flaccid weakness.

answers.name: Nephrolithiasis
answers.pearl: Distal RTA causes alkaline urine, hypocitraturia, and calcium phosphate stones.

answers.name: Autoimmune thyroiditis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune thyroid disease is the most frequent associated endocrine disorder.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Liver involvement can mimic autoimmune hepatitis with elevated transaminases.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: PBC overlaps with Sjogren, with antimitochondrial antibodies and sicca symptoms.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Mixed cryoglobulins with low C4 predict lymphoma and worse outcome.

answers.name: Low C4 complement
answers.pearl: Low C4 is an adverse prognostic marker for lymphoma development.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Glomerular disease is uncommon and usually linked to cryoglobulinemia.

answers.name: Cranial neuropathy
answers.pearl: Trigeminal sensory neuropathy is the classic cranial nerve manifestation.

answers.name: Cytopenias
answers.pearl: Mild leukopenia, lymphopenia, and anemia occur with active disease.

answers.name: Corneal ulceration
answers.pearl: Severe aqueous deficiency can lead to filamentary keratitis, ulcers, and scarring.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Dry mucosa and esophageal dysmotility cause trouble swallowing solid food.

answers.name: Chronic atrophic gastritis
answers.pearl: Gastric mucosal atrophy and autoimmune gastritis are described.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Lymphocytic infiltration of the pancreas can cause exocrine dysfunction.

answers.name: Autonomic neuropathy
answers.pearl: Autonomic dysfunction presents as orthostasis, abnormal pupils, and sweating abnormalities.

answers.name: Sensory ataxic neuronopathy
answers.pearl: Dorsal root ganglion inflammation causes sensory ataxia with pseudoathetosis.

answers.name: Central nervous system involvement
answers.pearl: Focal or diffuse CNS disease is rare and can mimic multiple sclerosis.

answers.name: Myositis
answers.pearl: An inflammatory myopathy can overlap with Sjogren syndrome.

answers.name: Optic neuritis
answers.pearl: Optic neuritis and NMO spectrum disease can occur with anti-AQP4 antibodies.

answers.name: Transverse myelitis
answers.pearl: Myelitis can be a presenting manifestation, often with AQP4 antibodies.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Nodular pulmonary amyloid and salivary gland amyloid are reported.

answers.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
answers.pearl: PAH is a rare but described severe complication.

answers.name: Lung cysts
answers.pearl: Thin-walled cysts from LIP or airway amyloid appear on CT.

answers.name: Hyperviscosity syndrome
answers.pearl: Marked hypergammaglobulinemia or cryoglobulinemia can rarely cause hyperviscosity.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Lifetime risk of B-cell lymphoma, especially parotid MALT marginal zone type, is elevated several-fold.

answers.name: Congenital heart block
answers.pearl: Maternal anti-Ro/La crosses the placenta and can injure the fetal conduction system.

answers.name: Renal tubular acidosis
answers.pearl: Distal (type 1) RTA from interstitial nephritis is the classic renal complication.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of secondary osteoporosis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hemophilia and Sickle cell disease (mechanistic, modest data); Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome (case-report level); Medroxyprogesterone acetate (partly reversible); Thyroid TSH suppression; Hypercalciuria (as a driver versus a consequence).

answers.name: Glucocorticoid use
answers.pearl: The most common cause of secondary osteoporosis; bone loss is rapid in the first months and affects trabecular bone.

answers.name: Menopause
answers.pearl: Estrogen loss increases osteoclast activity and bone resorption.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Excess thyroid hormone accelerates bone turnover.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Excess PTH preferentially resorbs cortical bone, such as the distal radius.

answers.name: Vitamin D deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes secondary hyperparathyroidism and impaired mineralization.

answers.name: Hypogonadism
answers.pearl: A major and often missed cause of osteoporosis in men.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Mineral and bone disorder from phosphate retention, low calcitriol, and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Alcohol directly suppresses osteoblasts and is linked to poor nutrition and falls.

answers.name: Smoking
answers.pearl: Reduces bone density and is an independent fracture risk factor.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Malabsorption of calcium and vitamin D; screen in unexplained osteoporosis.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory cytokines and steroids both drive periarticular and generalized bone loss.

answers.name: Immobilization
answers.pearl: Disuse increases resorption and decreases formation, especially below the level of injury.

answers.name: Anorexia nervosa
answers.pearl: Low weight, hypoestrogenism, and cortisol excess lower bone density.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Inflammation, steroids, and malabsorption combine to cause bone loss.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Long-term use is associated with a modestly increased fracture risk.

answers.name: Anticonvulsants
answers.pearl: CYP-inducing drugs accelerate vitamin D catabolism.

answers.name: Aromatase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Profound estrogen suppression in postmenopausal breast cancer causes bone loss.

answers.name: Androgen deprivation therapy
answers.pearl: Hypogonadism from ADT causes rapid bone loss and fractures.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Prolonged heparin exposure, particularly in pregnancy, is associated with osteoporosis.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Osteoclast-activating factors cause diffuse osteopenia and lytic lesions.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Endogenous cortisol excess causes vertebral fractures, sometimes as the presenting feature.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Type 1 lowers density; type 2 raises fracture risk despite normal or higher BMD.

answers.name: Thiazolidinediones
answers.pearl: PPAR gamma activation shifts marrow cells away from osteoblasts, raising fracture risk.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Cholestatic and cirrhotic disease cause bone loss through low vitamin D and IGF-1.

answers.name: Bariatric surgery
answers.pearl: Malabsorption and weight loss lower density, especially after Roux-en-Y bypass.

answers.name: Hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: Chronic urinary calcium loss can lower bone density.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Mast cell mediators, such as heparin and histamine, drive bone loss; a cause in young men and premenopausal women.

answers.name: Hyperprolactinemia
answers.pearl: Suppresses gonadotropins, causing hypogonadism and bone loss.

answers.name: Thyroid hormone excess from TSH suppression
answers.pearl: Iatrogenic subclinical hyperthyroidism in thyroid cancer patients lowers bone density.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Malabsorption, inflammation, hypogonadism, and steroids drive bone disease.

answers.name: Hypophosphatasia
answers.pearl: Low alkaline phosphatase with elevated pyridoxal phosphate; can mimic osteoporosis in adults.

answers.name: Osteogenesis imperfecta
answers.pearl: COL1A1/COL1A2 mutations; mild adult forms are labeled as early osteoporosis.

answers.name: Homocystinuria
answers.pearl: Causes premature osteoporosis, lens dislocation, and thromboembolism.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Hypogonadism and direct iron toxicity lower bone density.

answers.name: Thalassemia
answers.pearl: Marrow expansion, hypogonadism, and iron overload cause severe bone loss.

answers.name: Gaucher disease
answers.pearl: Infiltration of bone marrow by Gaucher cells causes osteopenia and bone crises.

answers.name: Hemophilia
answers.pearl: Joint bleeding, reduced activity, and low vitamin D contribute to reduced bone density.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Marrow expansion, vitamin D deficiency, and hypogonadism reduce bone mass.

answers.name: Idiopathic juvenile osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Rare self-limited childhood osteoporosis with vertebral fractures.

answers.name: Medroxyprogesterone acetate
answers.pearl: Hypoestrogenism from DMPA decreases BMD, partly reversible after cessation.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
answers.pearl: Heritable parathyroid carcinoma-prone syndrome; osteoporosis from PTH excess is described.

answers.name: Cancer chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Gonadotoxic chemotherapy causes premature ovarian failure and rapid bone loss.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of vertigo or dizziness.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Cervicogenic dizziness (controversial entity); Phenytoin toxicity vs nystagmus-ataxia; Susac syndrome and Subclavian steal (rare); Carbon monoxide; Lyme and syphilis (case-series level for vertigo); Vitamin B12 deficiency as dizziness.

answers.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
answers.pearl: Brief positional spells triggered by head turns; Dix-Hallpike confirms and the Epley maneuver treats.

answers.name: Vestibular neuritis
answers.pearl: Acute continuous vertigo without hearing loss; HINTS exam shows a peripheral pattern.

answers.name: Labyrinthitis
answers.pearl: Vertigo with hearing loss from labyrinth inflammation.

answers.name: Meniere disease
answers.pearl: Episodic vertigo with fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness.

answers.name: Vertebrobasilar stroke
answers.pearl: Acute vestibular syndrome with a central HINTS pattern should be treated as stroke until proven otherwise.

answers.name: Orthostatic hypotension
answers.pearl: Lightheadedness on standing from impaired blood pressure compensation.

answers.name: Medication side effect
answers.pearl: Antihypertensives, sedatives, and many other drugs commonly cause dizziness.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Reduced oxygen delivery can cause presyncopal lightheadedness.

answers.name: Hypoglycemia
answers.pearl: Neuroglycopenia causes lightheadedness, tremor, and confusion.

answers.name: Cardiac arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Transient hypoperfusion from rhythm disturbance causes presyncope.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume loss causes orthostatic dizziness.

answers.name: Anxiety
answers.pearl: Hyperventilation and panic produce non-vertiginous dizziness.

answers.name: Migraine
answers.pearl: The most common cause of spontaneous episodic vertigo; history of headache or photophobia helps.

answers.name: Multiple sclerosis
answers.pearl: Brainstem demyelination can cause acute vertigo and internuclear ophthalmoplegia.

answers.name: Acoustic neuroma
answers.pearl: Progressive unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus and imbalance; MRI with gadolinium.

answers.name: Aortic stenosis
answers.pearl: Fixed outflow obstruction limits cardiac output on exertion, causing presyncope.

answers.name: Vasovagal syncope
answers.pearl: Triggered presyncope with prodrome of warmth, nausea, and visual dimming.

answers.name: Cerebellar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Sudden vertigo with vomiting, headache, and gait ataxia; neurosurgical emergency.

answers.name: Ototoxic medications
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides and cisplatin damage the vestibular and cochlear hair cells.

answers.name: Head trauma
answers.pearl: Post-traumatic BPPV, labyrinthine concussion, and perilymph fistula all cause vertigo.

answers.name: Persistent postural-perceptual dizziness
answers.pearl: Chronic non-spinning dizziness worse with upright posture and visual motion.

answers.name: Alcohol intoxication
answers.pearl: Alcohol alters endolymph density in the cupula causing positional vertigo.

answers.name: Cervicogenic dizziness
answers.pearl: Controversial; disequilibrium attributed to abnormal cervical proprioception.

answers.name: Otitis media
answers.pearl: Middle ear disease and cholesteatoma can erode the labyrinth.

answers.name: Bilateral vestibular hypofunction
answers.pearl: Imbalance and oscillopsia, worse in darkness, from loss of both vestibular nerves.

answers.name: Superior semicircular canal dehiscence
answers.pearl: Sound or pressure-induced vertigo with autophony; CT shows thinning of the bony roof.

answers.name: Perilymph fistula
answers.pearl: Vertigo after barotrauma, straining, or trauma from perilymph leak.

answers.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
answers.pearl: Triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and confusion; nystagmus is common.

answers.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes sensory ataxia and gait imbalance.

answers.name: Chiari malformation
answers.pearl: Downbeat nystagmus and positional dizziness from craniocervical junction crowding.

answers.name: Phenytoin toxicity
answers.pearl: Dose-related nystagmus, ataxia, and vertigo.

answers.name: Autoimmune inner ear disease
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular symptoms; steroid-responsive.

answers.name: Susac syndrome
answers.pearl: Encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions, and sensorineural hearing loss.

answers.name: Episodic ataxia type 2
answers.pearl: Hours-long vertigo and ataxia with interictal nystagmus; acetazolamide responsive.

answers.name: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration
answers.pearl: Subacute pancerebellar syndrome with anti-Yo or anti-Hu antibodies.

answers.name: Cogan syndrome
answers.pearl: Interstitial keratitis with vestibuloauditory dysfunction and possible aortitis.

answers.name: Syphilis
answers.pearl: Otosyphilis causes fluctuating hearing loss and vertigo mimicking Meniere.

answers.name: Lyme disease
answers.pearl: Cranial neuropathy including cranial nerve VIII dysfunction is described.

answers.name: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
answers.pearl: Ear vesicles, facial palsy, hearing loss, and vertigo from VZV.

answers.name: Vertebral artery dissection
answers.pearl: Neck pain with vertigo after minor trauma or manipulation.

answers.name: Subclavian steal syndrome
answers.pearl: Arm exercise causes reversed vertebral flow and posterior circulation symptoms.

answers.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
answers.pearl: Headache with dizziness in multiple occupants in winter; check carboxyhemoglobin.

answers.name: Lateral medullary syndrome
answers.pearl: Vertigo, dysphagia, ipsilateral Horner syndrome, and crossed sensory loss.

answers.name: Mal de debarquement
answers.pearl: Persistent rocking sensation after sea travel; named in many vertigo lists.

answers.name: Motion sickness
answers.pearl: Sensory conflict between visual and vestibular input causes nausea and dizziness.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause acute interstitial nephritis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Metamizole, Levetiracetam, Abacavir, Clozapine, Diltiazem, BRAF inhibitors, Interferon (case-report level); Fenoprofen (older literature); Triamterene and Phenobarbital (sparse reports); Aristolochic acid (chronic interstitial rather than classic acute AIN).

answers.name: Penicillin
answers.pearl: Beta-lactams are the classic cause of drug-induced AIN, typically 7-14 days after exposure.

answers.name: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
answers.pearl: NSAID AIN often occurs after months of use, with proteinuria and little rash or eosinophilia.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: A leading cause of AIN, with a long and often silent latency; may progress to CKD.

answers.name: Cephalosporins
answers.pearl: Beta-lactam hypersensitivity can cause AIN.

answers.name: Ciprofloxacin
answers.pearl: Fluoroquinolones are among the more frequent non-beta-lactam antibiotic causes.

answers.name: Sulfonamides
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide antibiotics cause AIN and also raise creatinine by blocking secretion.

answers.name: Furosemide
answers.pearl: Sulfonamide-structure loop diuretics are classic but uncommon causes.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Thiazides are well described causes of AIN.

answers.name: Allopurinol
answers.pearl: Can cause AIN as part of DRESS-like hypersensitivity, mainly with renal impairment.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Intermittent dosing is associated with AIN, hemolysis, and thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Vancomycin
answers.pearl: AIN is reported, especially with piperacillin-tazobactam combination.

answers.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
answers.pearl: Beta-lactam with AIN risk, additive nephrotoxicity with vancomycin.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: The most common renal immune-related adverse event; may arise after PPI exposure.

answers.name: Acyclovir
answers.pearl: Crystal nephropathy is more common, but AIN also occurs.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Anticonvulsant hypersensitivity with AIN and DRESS.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Antiepileptic AIN with rash and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Ranitidine
answers.pearl: H2 blockers, especially cimetidine, are rare causes of AIN.

answers.name: Mesalamine
answers.pearl: Chronic interstitial nephritis can occur years after aminosalicylate therapy; monitor creatinine.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Chronic tubulointerstitial disease with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Erythromycin
answers.pearl: Macrolides can cause AIN.

answers.name: Tetracyclines
answers.pearl: Minocycline and doxycycline have been associated with AIN.

answers.name: Indinavir
answers.pearl: Crystalline nephropathy and interstitial nephritis; atazanavir is also implicated.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: More often proximal tubulopathy, but interstitial nephritis is reported.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: One of the earliest reported H2 blockers causing AIN; also lowers tubular creatinine secretion.

answers.name: Aristolochic acid
answers.pearl: Herbal toxin causing aggressive interstitial fibrosis and urothelial cancer.

answers.name: Sulfasalazine
answers.pearl: Sulfa and salicylate moieties can both cause AIN.

answers.name: Celecoxib
answers.pearl: COX-2 selective NSAIDs can also cause AIN.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Rare reports of AIN and Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Azathioprine
answers.pearl: Rare cases of AIN complicating azathioprine hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Interferon
answers.pearl: Reports of interstitial nephritis, usually with other renal injury.

answers.name: Methicillin
answers.pearl: The historical prototype of drug-induced AIN, from a classic board topic.

answers.name: Meropenem
answers.pearl: Carbapenems are beta-lactams and can cause AIN.

answers.name: Nitrofurantoin
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity reactions including AIN occur with nitrofurantoin.

answers.name: Phenobarbital
answers.pearl: Anticonvulsant AIN reported with systemic hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Triamterene
answers.pearl: Potassium-sparing diuretic associated with AIN.

answers.name: Lamotrigine
answers.pearl: Reported with DRESS-type hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Quinine
answers.pearl: Causes AIN and also drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy.

answers.name: Fenoprofen
answers.pearl: NSAID classically linked to AIN with nephrotic-range proteinuria (minimal change pattern).

answers.name: Diltiazem
answers.pearl: Rare reports of AIN with diltiazem.

answers.name: Abacavir
answers.pearl: Isolated case reports of AIN in abacavir hypersensitivity.

answers.name: Clozapine
answers.pearl: Case series report AIN, often with eosinophilia.

answers.name: Levetiracetam
answers.pearl: Rare case reports of AIN.

answers.name: Metamizole
answers.pearl: Pyrazolone analgesic used outside the US; AIN reported.

answers.name: BRAF inhibitors
answers.pearl: Interstitial nephritis described with BRAF inhibitors.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of systemic sclerosis (scleroderma).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pruritus, Hypo/hyperpigmentation, Anemia (indirect manifestations); Pneumatosis intestinalis; Anti-Th/To and Anti-U3 RNP associations; Trigeminal neuropathy; Hypothyroidism (autoimmune overlap).

answers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
answers.pearl: Present in nearly all patients and often the first manifestation, preceding other features by years.

answers.name: Skin thickening
answers.pearl: Cutaneous fibrosis defines the disease and extent separates limited from diffuse subsets.

answers.name: Gastroesophageal reflux
answers.pearl: Esophageal smooth muscle atrophy lowers sphincter tone, causing reflux in most patients.

answers.name: Esophageal dysmotility
answers.pearl: Loss of distal esophageal peristalsis causes dysphagia and aspiration risk.

answers.name: Digital ulcers
answers.pearl: Ischemic ulcers at fingertips and over joints are painful and slow to heal.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: The leading cause of death; usually nonspecific interstitial pneumonia, detected by HRCT and PFTs.

answers.name: Telangiectasias
answers.pearl: Facial and hand matted telangiectasias are typical, especially in limited disease.

answers.name: Calcinosis cutis
answers.pearl: Calcium deposits at pressure points are characteristic of limited disease (CREST).

answers.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
answers.pearl: A leading cause of death in limited disease; screen with echo and DLCO trends.

answers.name: Joint contractures
answers.pearl: Skin and tendon fibrosis cause flexion contractures of fingers.

answers.name: Scleroderma renal crisis
answers.pearl: Abrupt hypertension and AKI treated with ACE inhibitors; risk factors include steroids and anti-RNA polymerase III.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: A common nonspecific symptom.

answers.name: Puffy hands
answers.pearl: Early edematous phase of diffuse disease precedes skin thickening.

answers.name: Anti-centromere antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with limited disease, calcinosis, and pulmonary hypertension.

answers.name: Anti-Scl-70 antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with diffuse disease and interstitial lung disease.

answers.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
answers.pearl: Dysmotility of the small bowel causes bloating, diarrhea, and malabsorption.

answers.name: Gastric antral vascular ectasia
answers.pearl: Striped antral vascular lesions cause chronic occult GI bleeding and iron deficiency.

answers.name: Gastroparesis
answers.pearl: Neuropathy and smooth muscle fibrosis delay gastric emptying.

answers.name: Constipation
answers.pearl: Colonic hypomotility causes constipation and pseudo-obstruction.

answers.name: Fecal incontinence
answers.pearl: Internal anal sphincter fibrosis causes incontinence.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Gut involvement and dysphagia lead to malnutrition.

answers.name: Microstomia
answers.pearl: Perioral skin tightening limits mouth opening and dental care.

answers.name: Pericardial effusion
answers.pearl: Pericardial involvement is common but rarely tamponade; large effusions can foreshadow renal crisis.

answers.name: Myocardial fibrosis
answers.pearl: Patchy fibrosis from microvascular ischemia causes diastolic dysfunction and arrhythmias.

answers.name: Arrhythmia
answers.pearl: Conduction disease and ventricular ectopy occur with myocardial fibrosis.

answers.name: Inflammatory myopathy
answers.pearl: Overlap myositis occurs with anti-PM/Scl, anti-Ku, and anti-U3 RNP antibodies.

answers.name: Sicca symptoms
answers.pearl: Overlap with Sjogren occurs in a subset.

answers.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
answers.pearl: Fibrosis and edema compress the median nerve.

answers.name: Trigeminal neuropathy
answers.pearl: Trigeminal sensory neuropathy is an under-recognized early manifestation.

answers.name: Tendon friction rubs
answers.pearl: Palpable rubs over tendons predict diffuse disease and worse outcome.

answers.name: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies
answers.pearl: Predicts rapidly progressive skin disease, renal crisis, and association with malignancy.

answers.name: Cancer
answers.pearl: Increased cancer risk, especially near onset in anti-RNA polymerase III and anti-Scl-70.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Overlaps with limited cutaneous disease.

answers.name: Pneumatosis intestinalis
answers.pearl: Gas within the bowel wall from dysmotility and bacterial overgrowth; often benign.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Autoimmune thyroid disease is overrepresented.

answers.name: Anti-U3 RNP antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with PAH, myositis, and gastrointestinal disease, more in Black patients.

answers.name: Anti-Th/To antibodies
answers.pearl: Limited disease with ILD and PAH.

answers.name: Osteolysis of distal phalanges
answers.pearl: Bone resorption of the fingertip tufts follows chronic digital ischemia.

answers.name: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
answers.pearl: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease is an uncommon cause of PAH in scleroderma, with pulmonary edema if vasodilators are given.

answers.name: Erectile dysfunction
answers.pearl: Vasculopathy and fibrosis cause erectile dysfunction in most men with the disease.

answers.name: Anemia
answers.pearl: Occult GI blood loss from GAVE, inflammation, and B12 malabsorption from bacterial overgrowth.

answers.name: Periodontal disease
answers.pearl: Reduced mouth opening, xerostomia, and gum disease lead to tooth loss.

answers.name: Barrett esophagus
answers.pearl: Chronic reflux leads to strictures, Barrett metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma risk.

answers.name: Digital gangrene
answers.pearl: Severe ischemia can progress to necrosis requiring amputation.

answers.name: Hypo- and hyperpigmentation
answers.pearl: Salt-and-pepper pigmentation is a characteristic skin change.

answers.name: Pruritus
answers.pearl: Itch is common in the early edematous phase.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyperprolactinemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Adrenal insufficiency (small series), Genetic hyperprolactinemia (AIP), Intracranial aneurysm (stalk compression, case-report level), Hypothalamic germinoma, Pituitary metastases, Hypophysitis, Chest wall injury subtypes, Verapamil and Methyldopa (weak data).

answers.name: Prolactinoma
answers.pearl: The most common pathologic cause; prolactin generally tracks tumor size and exceeds 200 ng/mL in macroadenomas.

answers.name: Pregnancy
answers.pearl: Estrogen stimulates lactotroph hyperplasia, with levels rising progressively through gestation.

answers.name: Lactation
answers.pearl: Nipple stimulation triggers a neural reflex raising prolactin.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: D2 blockade removes dopamine inhibition; risperidone and paliperidone are most potent.

answers.name: Hypothyroidism
answers.pearl: Raised TRH stimulates prolactin release; resolves with levothyroxine.

answers.name: Metoclopramide
answers.pearl: Central dopamine antagonist that can raise prolactin well above normal.

answers.name: Stress
answers.pearl: Mild transient elevations; recheck a fasting, resting sample.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Reduced clearance and increased production raise prolactin.

answers.name: Antidepressants
answers.pearl: Mild elevations with tricyclics, SSRIs, and MAOIs.

answers.name: Stalk effect
answers.pearl: Any sellar mass compressing the stalk blocks dopamine delivery, usually giving prolactin under 100 ng/mL.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Reduced hepatic clearance and altered dopamine tone.

answers.name: Nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma
answers.pearl: A nonsecreting sellar mass raises prolactin by stalk compression; compare with prolactinoma level.

answers.name: Idiopathic hyperprolactinemia
answers.pearl: No cause identified after excluding lesions and drugs.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen stimulates lactotroph proliferation, with mild elevations.

answers.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
answers.pearl: Mildly elevated prolactin in a minority; the association is debated.

answers.name: Macroprolactinemia
answers.pearl: Prolactin-immunoglobulin complexes are biologically inactive and cause asymptomatic high immunoreactive prolactin.

answers.name: Hook effect
answers.pearl: With massive prolactin, assay saturation gives falsely low results; dilute the sample.

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids reduce hypothalamic dopamine and raise prolactin.

answers.name: Chest wall injury
answers.pearl: Afferent neural stimulation mimics suckling.

answers.name: Cimetidine
answers.pearl: Especially intravenous H2 blockers acutely raise prolactin.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Verapamil can raise prolactin in a small fraction of patients.

answers.name: Methyldopa
answers.pearl: Depletes central dopamine, causing elevated prolactin.

answers.name: Ectopic prolactin secretion
answers.pearl: Rare tumors such as renal cell carcinoma and bronchogenic cancer can secrete prolactin.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic or stalk granulomas disrupt dopamine delivery.

answers.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic involvement often with diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Hypophysitis
answers.pearl: Inflammatory sellar disease can raise prolactin by stalk effect.

answers.name: Empty sella syndrome
answers.pearl: Pituitary flattening with mildly raised prolactin from stalk traction.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Reported with raised prolactin in untreated disease, reversible with glucocorticoids.

answers.name: Acromegaly
answers.pearl: Co-secretion of GH and prolactin occurs in a substantial fraction of GH adenomas.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1
answers.pearl: Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary tumor in MEN1.

answers.name: Craniopharyngioma
