answers.pearl: Classic suprasellar mass causing stalk effect.

answers.name: Head trauma
answers.pearl: Stalk transection from head injury raises prolactin and causes hypopituitarism.

answers.name: Radiation
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic damage from irradiation can raise prolactin.

answers.name: Chronic nipple stimulation
answers.pearl: Sexual or manual nipple stimulation raises prolactin transiently.

answers.name: Granulomatous disease
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration of the hypothalamic region causes stalk effect.

answers.name: Genetic hyperprolactinemia
answers.pearl: AIP mutations cause aggressive familial pituitary adenomas, including prolactinomas.

answers.name: Intracranial aneurysm
answers.pearl: Sellar or parasellar aneurysm can compress the stalk.

answers.name: Hypothalamic germinoma
answers.pearl: Suprasellar germ cell tumors cause stalk disruption and diabetes insipidus.

answers.name: Pituitary metastases
answers.pearl: Breast and lung metastases can compress the stalk.

answers.name: Hypothalamic disease
answers.pearl: Hypothalamic lesions reduce dopamine and raise prolactin.

answers.name: Sleep
answers.pearl: Prolactin rises during sleep, so morning samples can be mildly high.

answers.name: Prochlorperazine
answers.pearl: Dopamine-blocking antiemetics raise prolactin.

answers.name: Protein-rich meal
answers.pearl: Eating, especially protein, causes a transient prolactin rise.

answers.name: Pituitary carcinoma
answers.pearl: Rare prolactin-secreting carcinomas with metastases are poorly responsive to dopamine agonists.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypokalemia with hypertension.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pheochromocytoma (hypokalemia via beta-2 shift, not universal); Nafcillin (hypertension mostly from sodium load); Ectopic renin, Ask-Upmark kidney, Aldosterone-secreting ovarian tumor, Ectopic CRH, PASNA, McCune-Albright (case-report level); Azole antifungals and Takayasu arteritis.

answers.name: Thiazide diuretics
answers.pearl: Kaliuresis from distal sodium delivery is the commonest cause in treated hypertensives.

answers.name: Primary aldosteronism
answers.pearl: The classic endocrine cause: low renin, high aldosterone, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis; screen with aldosterone-renin ratio.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Increased distal sodium delivery drives potassium loss.

answers.name: Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: The most common subtype of primary aldosteronism; treated with mineralocorticoid antagonists rather than surgery.

answers.name: Renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Renal hypoperfusion raises renin and aldosterone, causing secondary hyperaldosteronism.

answers.name: Cushing syndrome
answers.pearl: Excess cortisol overwhelms 11-beta-HSD2 and activates the mineralocorticoid receptor.

answers.name: Licorice ingestion
answers.pearl: Glycyrrhetinic acid inhibits 11-beta-HSD2, producing a syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess.

answers.name: Malignant hypertension
answers.pearl: Pressure natriuresis and renal ischemia activate renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Fibromuscular dysplasia
answers.pearl: Young women with renal artery string-of-beads lesions can develop renovascular hypertension.

answers.name: Ectopic ACTH syndrome
answers.pearl: Very high cortisol with severe hypokalemia and alkalosis is typical of ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: 11-beta-hydroxylase and 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency both give hypertension with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Exogenous glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: Supraphysiologic steroid exposure has mineralocorticoid effect and promotes potassium wasting.

answers.name: Fludrocortisone
answers.pearl: A direct mineralocorticoid; overreplacement causes hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Cushing disease
answers.pearl: Pituitary ACTH excess; hypokalemia is less common than with ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Cortisol-producing adrenal adenoma
answers.pearl: Adrenal source of hypercortisolism with suppressed ACTH.

answers.name: Chewing tobacco
answers.pearl: Some products contain licorice flavoring and glycyrrhizin.

answers.name: Carbenoxolone
answers.pearl: Licorice-derived ulcer drug that inhibits 11-beta-HSD2.

answers.name: Page kidney
answers.pearl: External compression causes ischemia and high renin hypertension.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma
answers.pearl: Catecholamines shift potassium intracellularly via beta-2 receptors, sometimes with hypokalemia.

answers.name: Adrenocortical carcinoma
answers.pearl: Can secrete cortisol, aldosterone, or deoxycorticosterone.

answers.name: Polyarteritis nodosa
answers.pearl: Renal artery involvement causes hyperreninemic hypertension.

answers.name: Renin-secreting tumor
answers.pearl: A rare tumor with very high renin, secondary hyperaldosteronism, and refractory hypertension.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I
answers.pearl: A CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene places aldosterone synthase under ACTH control; suppress with dexamethasone.

answers.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
aliases: ectopic ACTH from medullary thyroid cancer
answers.pearl: A neuroendocrine tumor that can produce ectopic ACTH.

answers.name: Bronchial carcinoid
answers.pearl: Bronchial carcinoids are a recognized source of ectopic ACTH, often occult.

answers.name: Macronodular adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: ACTH-independent cortisol excess; aberrant receptors drive steroid secretion.

answers.name: Abiraterone
answers.pearl: CYP17 blockade raises ACTH and deoxycorticosterone, causing hypertension and hypokalemia unless prednisone is co-administered.

answers.name: Azole antifungals
answers.pearl: Posaconazole and itraconazole inhibit 11-beta-HSD2 (and steroidogenic enzymes), causing pseudohyperaldosteronism.

answers.name: Deoxycorticosterone-secreting tumor
answers.pearl: A rare adrenal tumor secreting a potent mineralocorticoid with suppressed renin and aldosterone.

answers.name: Metyrapone
answers.pearl: 11-beta-hydroxylase inhibition increases deoxycorticosterone with hypertension and hypokalemia.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type II
answers.pearl: Familial primary aldosteronism not suppressed by dexamethasone, linked to CLCN2 mutations in some families.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type III
answers.pearl: Germline KCNJ5 mutation causes severe early hypertension and massive bilateral hyperplasia.

answers.name: Glucocorticoid resistance syndrome
answers.pearl: Compensatory ACTH rise increases mineralocorticoid precursors, causing hypertension and hypokalemia without Cushingoid features.

answers.name: Ectopic renin secretion
answers.pearl: Rare reports with ovarian, lung, and Wilms tumors.

answers.name: Ask-Upmark kidney
answers.pearl: Segmental hypoplasia with a hyperreninemic hypertension picture.

answers.name: Carney complex
answers.pearl: Cortisol excess from pigmented nodular adrenal disease with PRKAR1A mutation.

answers.name: Familial hyperaldosteronism type IV
answers.pearl: CACNA1H gain-of-function mutation causes early-onset hypertension and aldosteronism.

answers.name: Cortisol co-secretion with primary aldosteronism
answers.pearl: Aldosterone-producing adenomas can co-secrete cortisol, raising surgical complication risk.

answers.name: Aldosterone-secreting ovarian tumor
answers.pearl: Extremely rare ectopic aldosterone source; case-report level.

answers.name: Ectopic CRH secretion
answers.pearl: Rare tumors secrete CRH, driving ACTH and cortisol excess.

answers.name: PASNA syndrome
aliases: primary aldosteronism with seizures and neurologic abnormalities
answers.pearl: CACNA1D de novo mutations cause aldosteronism with neurologic features; case-series level.

answers.name: Unilateral adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: A surgically curable form of primary aldosteronism resembling an adenoma.

answers.name: McCune-Albright syndrome
answers.pearl: Activating GNAS mutations can cause neonatal Cushing syndrome, a rare cause.

answers.name: Liddle syndrome
answers.pearl: ENaC activating mutation: low renin, low aldosterone, responds to amiloride or triamterene, not spironolactone.

answers.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
answers.pearl: HSD11B2 loss lets cortisol act on the mineralocorticoid receptor; high cortisol-to-cortisone ratio.

answers.name: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: Hypertension, hypokalemia, and absent puberty from excess deoxycorticosterone.

answers.name: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
answers.pearl: The commonest CAH cause of hypertension; virilization accompanies DOC excess.

answers.name: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
answers.pearl: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors can cause ectopic ACTH syndrome.

answers.name: Thymic neuroendocrine tumor
answers.pearl: Thymic carcinoids are a recognized, often occult, ectopic ACTH source.

answers.name: Oral contraceptives
answers.pearl: Estrogen increases hepatic angiotensinogen, causing hypertension with secondary aldosteronism.

answers.name: Takayasu arteritis
answers.pearl: Renal artery stenosis from large-vessel arteritis causes hyperreninemic hypertension.

answers.name: Renin-responsive aldosterone-producing adenoma
answers.pearl: A rare adenoma subtype whose aldosterone rises with upright posture, mimicking idiopathic hyperplasia.

answers.name: Aldosterone-producing cell clusters
answers.pearl: Histologic micronodules can drive bilateral or unilateral aldosteronism without a visible adenoma.

answers.name: Aldosterone-secreting adrenal carcinoma
answers.pearl: Rare malignant cause of primary aldosteronism, usually with large tumors.

answers.name: Transplant renal artery stenosis
answers.pearl: Post-transplant renal artery stenosis causes renin-driven hypertension.

answers.name: Nafcillin
answers.pearl: Large doses of sodium-containing penicillins deliver nonabsorbable anions that promote renal potassium loss.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hepatomegaly.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: acromegaly and mastocytosis (organomegaly reported, not a usual presenting cause), glycogenic hepatopathy; case-report level: peliosis hepatis, hepatic angiosarcoma. Wilson disease omitted (liver often small). Traps: Gaucher, hemochromatosis, amyloidosis.

answers.name: Alcoholic fatty liver
answers.pearl: Chronic alcohol use causes macrovesicular steatosis, the commonest cause of a smooth enlarged liver.

answers.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
answers.pearl: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the leading cause of hepatomegaly in obesity and diabetes.

answers.name: Congestive heart failure
answers.pearl: Raised right atrial pressure congests the sinusoids and gives a tender liver with hepatojugular reflux.

answers.name: Viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Acute viral hepatitis causes tender hepatomegaly, while chronic infection often leaves liver size normal until cirrhosis.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: HCC arises mostly in cirrhosis and can present as a hard, nodular, enlarging liver with a bruit.

answers.name: Metastatic liver disease
answers.pearl: Colorectal, breast, lung and pancreatic cancers commonly cause a hard, irregular, nodular liver.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Early or compensated cirrhosis often enlarges the liver, while end-stage disease shrinks it.

answers.name: Lymphoma
answers.pearl: Lymphoma infiltrates the liver diffusely, often with splenomegaly and raised alkaline phosphatase.

answers.name: Pyogenic liver abscess
answers.pearl: Fever and tender hepatomegaly with a cavitary lesion suggests biliary or portal-seeded infection such as Klebsiella.

answers.name: Alcoholic hepatitis
answers.pearl: Alcoholic hepatitis presents with fever, jaundice, tender hepatomegaly and an AST to ALT ratio above 2.

answers.name: Leukemia
answers.pearl: Leukemic infiltration of sinusoids causes hepatomegaly, usually with splenomegaly.

answers.name: Biliary obstruction
answers.pearl: Prolonged bile duct obstruction produces a bile-stained, enlarged liver with cholestatic enzyme elevation.

answers.name: Drug-induced liver injury
answers.pearl: Many drugs cause hepatic steatosis or hepatitis with tender enlargement of the liver.

answers.name: Polycystic liver disease
answers.pearl: Polycystic kidney disease or isolated polycystic liver disease can massively enlarge the liver.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune hepatitis in young women may present with hepatomegaly, high IgG and positive ANA or anti-smooth muscle antibody.

answers.name: Hepatic hemangioma
answers.pearl: Giant cavernous hemangiomas can enlarge the liver, and biopsy is avoided because of bleeding risk.

answers.name: Tricuspid regurgitation
answers.pearl: Severe TR transmits systolic pressure waves to the liver, giving a pulsatile enlarged liver.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: PBC causes hepatomegaly with pruritus, high alkaline phosphatase and antimitochondrial antibodies.

answers.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
answers.pearl: PSC with beaded bile ducts and ulcerative colitis can cause hepatomegaly with cholestasis.

answers.name: Constrictive pericarditis
answers.pearl: Constriction raises central venous pressure so hepatic congestion and ascites exceed peripheral edema.

answers.name: Infectious mononucleosis
answers.pearl: EBV commonly causes mild hepatitis with mild hepatomegaly and splenomegaly.

answers.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
answers.pearl: Retained Z-protein in hepatocytes causes liver disease with PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules.

answers.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
answers.pearl: Hepatic vein outflow block causes painful hepatomegaly, ascites and caudate hypertrophy, often from a myeloproliferative neoplasm.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Intrahepatic sickling and transfusional iron overload cause hepatomegaly with cholestasis.

answers.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
answers.pearl: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma can present as a large mass, and PSC and liver flukes are risk factors.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Noncaseating granulomas occur in the liver in many sarcoid patients and may cause hepatomegaly and cholestasis.

answers.name: Amebic liver abscess
answers.pearl: Travel to endemic regions with tender hepatomegaly and an anchovy paste aspirate suggests amebic abscess.

answers.name: Hepatic adenoma
answers.pearl: Adenomas linked to oral contraceptives or anabolic steroids can enlarge and hemorrhage.

answers.name: Miliary tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated TB seeds the liver with granulomas, causing hepatomegaly and raised alkaline phosphatase.

answers.name: Myelofibrosis
answers.pearl: Extramedullary hematopoiesis in the liver and spleen causes organomegaly in myelofibrosis.

answers.name: Hydatid disease
answers.pearl: Hydatid cysts of the liver cause hepatomegaly, and aspiration risks anaphylaxis.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Egg granulomas cause presinusoidal portal hypertension with hepatosplenomegaly and periportal fibrosis.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis liver disease
answers.pearl: Focal biliary cirrhosis and steatosis are well-described hepatic complications of cystic fibrosis.

answers.name: Thalassemia major
answers.pearl: Extramedullary hematopoiesis and transfusional iron overload enlarge the liver.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: HLH presents with fever, cytopenias, hepatosplenomegaly and very high ferritin.

answers.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
answers.pearl: Kala-azar causes massive splenomegaly with hepatomegaly, fever and pancytopenia.

answers.name: Kwashiorkor
answers.pearl: Severe protein deficiency with preserved calories leads to fatty liver and enlargement.

answers.name: Amiodarone hepatotoxicity
answers.pearl: Amiodarone can cause phospholipidosis and steatohepatitis resembling alcoholic liver disease.

answers.name: Total parenteral nutrition
answers.pearl: Prolonged TPN causes steatosis and cholestasis with hepatomegaly.

answers.name: Disseminated histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Disseminated histoplasmosis causes hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia and high ferritin in endemic areas.

answers.name: Hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome
answers.pearl: Tender hepatomegaly, jaundice and weight gain follow myeloablative conditioning for stem cell transplant.

answers.name: Glycogenic hepatopathy
answers.pearl: Large glucose swings with insulin treatment cause glycogen accumulation, enlarged liver and raised transaminases.

answers.name: Acromegaly
answers.pearl: Growth hormone causes visceromegaly, including liver enlargement.

answers.name: Systemic mastocytosis
answers.pearl: Mast cell infiltration of liver and spleen causes organomegaly and portal hypertension in advanced disease.

answers.name: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency
answers.pearl: Lipid accumulation in hepatocytes gives hepatomegaly with high LDL and low HDL.

answers.name: Peliosis hepatis
answers.pearl: Blood-filled cavities in the liver are associated with Bartonella in HIV, anabolic steroids and azathioprine.

answers.name: Hepatic angiosarcoma
answers.pearl: Linked to vinyl chloride, arsenic and Thorotrast exposure, this tumour enlarges the liver and may bleed.

answers.name: Gaucher disease
answers.pearl: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias and bone disease with Gaucher cells.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Iron deposition causes hepatomegaly, bronze skin, diabetes and arthropathy.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Hepatic amyloid deposition produces a firm, enlarged, often non-tender liver with high alkaline phosphatase.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that induce cytochrome P450 enzymes.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: metamizole (recent PK data, not US-marketed), sotorasib, pitolisant, ivosidenib, cenobamate (labelled inducers, little clinical experience), topiramate (dose dependent), aprepitant (moderate 2C9 induction only). Traps: griseofulvin, nafcillin, modafinil. Sulfonylureas omitted because mnemonic inclusion is not supported.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: Rifampin is the prototypical potent CYP3A4 inducer and lowers levels of warfarin, OCPs, tacrolimus and antiretrovirals.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, 1A2 and 2C9, and also induces its own metabolism (autoinduction).

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Phenytoin induces CYP3A4 and 2C enzymes, lowering levels of OCPs, many antiretrovirals and others.

answers.name: Phenobarbital
answers.pearl: Barbiturates cause broad enzyme induction including CYP2C9, 2C19 and 3A4.

answers.name: St John's wort
answers.pearl: Hyperforin activates PXR to induce CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, lowering cyclosporine, OCPs and antiretrovirals.

answers.name: Chronic alcohol use
answers.pearl: Chronic ethanol induces CYP2E1, increasing conversion of acetaminophen to NAPQI.

answers.name: Efavirenz
answers.pearl: Efavirenz induces CYP3A4 and 2B6, and lowers levels of methadone, voriconazole and others.

answers.name: Primidone
answers.pearl: Primidone is metabolized to phenobarbital and shares its inducing effect.

answers.name: Rifabutin
answers.pearl: Rifabutin is a weaker inducer than rifampin but still lowers protease inhibitor levels.

answers.name: Nevirapine
answers.pearl: Nevirapine induces CYP3A4 and 2B6 and lowers methadone and hormonal contraceptive exposure.

answers.name: Oxcarbazepine
answers.pearl: Oxcarbazepine is a weaker 3A4 inducer but still reduces OCP efficacy.

answers.name: Dexamethasone
answers.pearl: Dexamethasone induces CYP3A4 through PXR, which matters with agents such as voriconazole and some chemotherapies.

answers.name: Modafinil
answers.pearl: Modafinil is a weak CYP3A4 inducer that can reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

answers.name: Armodafinil
answers.pearl: The R-enantiomer of modafinil induces CYP3A4 and can lower contraceptive levels.

answers.name: Topiramate
answers.pearl: Topiramate at doses above 200 mg per day lowers ethinyl estradiol exposure through weak CYP3A4 induction.

answers.name: Rifapentine
answers.pearl: Rifapentine induces CYP3A4 and lowers levels of many drugs, including some HIV antiretrovirals.

answers.name: Cigarette smoke
answers.pearl: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons induce CYP1A2, lowering clozapine, olanzapine and theophylline levels.

answers.name: Omeprazole
answers.pearl: Omeprazole and lansoprazole induce CYP1A2 via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor.

answers.name: Nafcillin
answers.pearl: Nafcillin induces CYP2C9 and 3A4, causing warfarin resistance and subtherapeutic voriconazole.

answers.name: Griseofulvin
answers.pearl: Griseofulvin induces CYP enzymes and can lower warfarin effect and OCP efficacy.

answers.name: Bosentan
answers.pearl: Bosentan induces CYP3A4 and 2C9, lowering levels of hormonal contraceptives and sildenafil.

answers.name: Eslicarbazepine
answers.pearl: Eslicarbazepine is a weak CYP3A4 inducer.

answers.name: Felbamate
answers.pearl: Felbamate induces CYP3A4 and inhibits CYP2C19.

answers.name: Rufinamide
answers.pearl: Rufinamide is a weak CYP3A4 inducer that can reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

answers.name: Etravirine
answers.pearl: Etravirine induces CYP3A4 and lowers levels of some protease inhibitors and other drugs.

answers.name: Enzalutamide
answers.pearl: Enzalutamide is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and a moderate 2C9 and 2C19 inducer.

answers.name: Apalutamide
answers.pearl: Apalutamide induces CYP3A4, 2C19 and 2C9, so concomitant medicines need review.

answers.name: Mitotane
answers.pearl: Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer that blunts steroid replacement and many other drugs.

answers.name: Lumacaftor
answers.pearl: Lumacaftor with ivacaftor is a strong CYP3A4 inducer in cystic fibrosis therapy.

answers.name: Lorlatinib
answers.pearl: Lorlatinib is a moderate CYP3A4 inducer used in ALK-positive lung cancer.

answers.name: Dabrafenib
answers.pearl: Dabrafenib induces CYP3A4 and 2C9 and can lower hormonal contraceptive levels.

answers.name: Ivosidenib
answers.pearl: Ivosidenib induces CYP3A4 and can reduce exposure of co-administered substrates.

answers.name: Artemisinin
answers.pearl: Artemisinin derivatives induce CYP2B6 and 3A4, including autoinduction of their own clearance.

answers.name: Aprepitant
answers.pearl: Aprepitant moderately induces CYP2C9 and can lower warfarin and OCP effects.

answers.name: Cenobamate
answers.pearl: Cenobamate induces CYP3A4 and 2B6 and inhibits 2C19.

answers.name: Pitolisant
answers.pearl: Pitolisant is a weak CYP3A4 inducer that can reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

answers.name: Letermovir
answers.pearl: Letermovir induces CYP2C9 and 2C19 and can lower voriconazole levels.

answers.name: Sotorasib
answers.pearl: Sotorasib is a CYP3A4 inducer that can lower levels of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates.

answers.name: Clobazam
answers.pearl: Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce hormonal contraceptive exposure.

answers.name: Phenylbutazone
answers.pearl: Phenylbutazone is an older enzyme inducer that lowers warfarin and other drug levels.

answers.name: Lesinurad
answers.pearl: Lesinurad, a withdrawn urate transporter inhibitor, was a weak CYP3A4 inducer.

answers.name: Metamizole
answers.pearl: Metamizole induces CYP2B6 and 3A4 and can lower levels of substrates such as bupropion.

prompts.prompt: Name extra-articular manifestations of spondyloarthritis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: prostatitis and hidradenitis suppurativa (association evidence only), cervicitis, diastolic dysfunction, mitral regurgitation, IgA nephropathy as the 'most common' glomerulopathy. Enthesitis and dactylitis counted as extra-articular by convention. Traps: keratoderma blennorrhagicum, circinate balanitis, cauda equina syndrome, apical pulmonary fibrosis.

answers.name: Anterior uveitis
answers.pearl: Acute, unilateral, recurrent anterior uveitis is the commonest extra-articular feature, especially in HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis.

answers.name: Psoriasis
answers.pearl: Skin psoriasis defines psoriatic arthritis and is associated with HLA-B27 axial disease.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis are linked to enteropathic spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Enthesitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation at tendon and ligament insertions is a hallmark of spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Dactylitis
answers.pearl: Diffuse swelling of a whole digit is characteristic of psoriatic and reactive arthritis.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Fatigue is a very common and disabling feature of active axial spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Aortic regurgitation
answers.pearl: Aortitis with aortic root dilatation causes aortic regurgitation in long-standing ankylosing spondylitis.

answers.name: Osteoporosis
answers.pearl: Inflammation causes bone loss even early, despite syndesmophyte formation.

answers.name: Conjunctivitis
answers.pearl: Conjunctivitis occurs in the classic reactive arthritis triad of urethritis, conjunctivitis and arthritis.

answers.name: Urethritis
answers.pearl: Sterile urethritis follows genitourinary or enteric infection in reactive arthritis.

answers.name: Vertebral fracture
answers.pearl: A rigid ankylosed spine is prone to unstable fractures after minor trauma.

answers.name: Conduction abnormalities
answers.pearl: Inflammation of the AV node and aortic root causes conduction disturbances, sometimes needing a pacemaker.

answers.name: Aortitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of the aortic root can precede valve disease and dilation.

answers.name: Oral ulcers
answers.pearl: Painless oral ulcers occur in reactive arthritis and with IBD.

answers.name: Nail changes
answers.pearl: Pitting, onycholysis and ridging suggest psoriatic arthritis, especially with distal interphalangeal disease.

answers.name: Restrictive lung disease
answers.pearl: Costovertebral ankylosis reduces chest expansion and vital capacity.

answers.name: Cardiovascular disease
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation increases the risk of coronary disease and stroke in spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Anemia of chronic disease
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation causes a normocytic anemia with raised CRP.

answers.name: Erythema nodosum
answers.pearl: Erythema nodosum occurs with enteropathic spondyloarthritis and reactive arthritis.

answers.name: Costochondritis
answers.pearl: Enthesitis at costosternal junctions gives pleuritic or anterior chest wall pain mimicking cardiac pain.

answers.name: Apical pulmonary fibrosis
answers.pearl: Upper lobe fibrosis occurs late in ankylosing spondylitis and can be colonised by Aspergillus.

answers.name: Secondary amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Chronic inflammation can cause AA amyloidosis with proteinuria and renal failure.

answers.name: IgA nephropathy
answers.pearl: IgA nephropathy is the most common glomerulopathy described in ankylosing spondylitis.

answers.name: Scleritis
answers.pearl: Scleritis and episcleritis occur less often than anterior uveitis, with inflammatory bowel disease associations.

answers.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
answers.pearl: Pyoderma gangrenosum is associated with IBD-related spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Subclinical gut inflammation
answers.pearl: A large share of patients with spondyloarthritis show microscopic gut inflammation on ileocolonoscopy.

answers.name: Cervical myelopathy
answers.pearl: Cord compression can follow vertebral fracture or atlantoaxial subluxation in long-standing disease.

answers.name: Palmoplantar pustulosis
answers.pearl: Palmoplantar pustulosis with acne, hyperostosis and osteitis defines the SAPHO syndrome.

answers.name: Cauda equina syndrome
answers.pearl: Late ankylosing spondylitis can cause arachnoiditis and dural ectasia with sacral and lumbar root symptoms.

answers.name: Keratoderma blennorrhagicum
aliases: pustular skin lesions of palms and soles
answers.pearl: Hyperkeratotic papules on the soles and palms are classic in reactive arthritis.

answers.name: Circinate balanitis
answers.pearl: Painless shallow ulcers on the glans occur in reactive arthritis.

answers.name: Mitral regurgitation
answers.pearl: A fibrous subaortic bump can involve the anterior mitral leaflet and cause regurgitation.

answers.name: Venous thromboembolism
answers.pearl: Inflammation raises the risk of venous thrombosis in spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Cervicitis
answers.pearl: Female reactive arthritis may present with cervicitis, often overlooked.

answers.name: Diastolic dysfunction
answers.pearl: Echocardiographic diastolic dysfunction is more common in ankylosing spondylitis than controls.

answers.name: Fibrocavitary lung disease
answers.pearl: Apical cavitation may be colonized by Aspergillus, causing hemoptysis.

answers.name: Prostatitis
answers.pearl: Prostatic inflammation is reported at higher frequency in ankylosing spondylitis, with weaker supporting evidence.

answers.name: Low-grade fever
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation can cause low-grade fever and weight loss in active disease.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericarditis is a rare cardiac manifestation of spondyloarthritis.

answers.name: Depression
answers.pearl: Chronic pain and inflammation are associated with higher rates of depression.

answers.name: Hidradenitis suppurativa
answers.pearl: Hidradenitis is epidemiologically linked with spondyloarthritis, particularly with HLA-B27 axial disease.

prompts.prompt: Name triggers or causes of atrial fibrillation.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: epicardial adipose tissue and anabolic steroids (association level), corticosteroids and chemotherapy agents (observational), peripartum cardiomyopathy, hypothermia. Traps: WPW, left atrial myxoma, hemochromatosis.

answers.name: Hypertension
answers.pearl: Chronic hypertension drives left atrial enlargement and fibrosis and is the most common modifiable AF risk factor.

answers.name: Heart failure
answers.pearl: Heart failure and AF each promote the other through atrial stretch and neurohormonal activation.

answers.name: Valvular heart disease
answers.pearl: Mitral valve disease raises left atrial pressure and causes atrial dilatation.

answers.name: Advanced age
answers.pearl: Age-related atrial fibrosis makes AF prevalence rise steeply after 65.

answers.name: Coronary artery disease
answers.pearl: Atrial ischemia and acute MI can trigger AF, which worsens outcomes.

answers.name: Hyperthyroidism
answers.pearl: Excess thyroid hormone is a classic reversible cause and should be checked with a TSH in every new AF.

answers.name: Alcohol
answers.pearl: Binge drinking triggers new AF and chronic use raises its risk dose-dependently.

answers.name: Obesity
answers.pearl: Obesity increases atrial size and epicardial fat, raising AF risk.

answers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
answers.pearl: Intrathoracic pressure swings, hypoxia and autonomic surges promote AF and recurrence after ablation.

answers.name: Postoperative state
answers.pearl: Postoperative AF affects up to a third of patients after cardiac surgery, peaking days 2 to 3.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation and catecholamines trigger new-onset AF in critically ill patients.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Acute right heart strain from PE can precipitate AF.

answers.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
answers.pearl: Hypoxemia, hypercapnia and beta agonists promote atrial arrhythmias in COPD.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Diabetes increases AF risk through atrial remodeling and autonomic dysfunction.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: CKD is associated with AF through volume overload, inflammation and electrolyte shifts.

answers.name: Electrolyte abnormalities
answers.pearl: Low potassium and magnesium predispose to atrial ectopy and AF.

answers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: HCM causes AF through atrial enlargement and diastolic dysfunction, and AF is poorly tolerated.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Atrial epicardial inflammation can trigger AF.

answers.name: Congenital heart disease
answers.pearl: Atrial septal defects cause right atrial dilation and AF in adulthood.

answers.name: Myocarditis
answers.pearl: Atrial inflammation causes arrhythmias including AF.

answers.name: Stimulants
answers.pearl: Sympathomimetic stimulants trigger AF through adrenergic surge.

answers.name: Beta-agonists
answers.pearl: Beta-agonists increase atrial excitability and AF in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Theophylline
answers.pearl: Theophylline raises AF risk through adenosine antagonism and catecholamine release.

answers.name: Rheumatic heart disease
answers.pearl: Rheumatic mitral stenosis is a classic cause of AF with high embolic risk.

answers.name: Pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Right atrial enlargement from raised pulmonary pressure promotes AF.

answers.name: Exogenous thyroid hormone excess
answers.pearl: Overtreatment with levothyroxine lowers TSH and increases AF risk.

answers.name: Sick sinus syndrome
answers.pearl: Atrial fibrosis in sick sinus syndrome produces both bradycardia and AF.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: Hypoxia, inflammation and critical illness drive new AF in COVID-19.

answers.name: Ibrutinib
answers.pearl: BTK inhibitors, especially ibrutinib, raise AF risk in a dose-related way.

answers.name: Endurance athletics
answers.pearl: Long-term high-volume endurance training increases AF risk through atrial remodeling and vagal tone.

answers.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Neurogenic autonomic surge produces atrial arrhythmias after intracranial injury.

answers.name: Hyperaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Primary aldosteronism confers higher AF risk than essential hypertension.

answers.name: Chemotherapy
answers.pearl: Several cytotoxics are linked to AF, especially in perioperative and peri-treatment settings.

answers.name: Familial atrial fibrillation
answers.pearl: Gain-of-function KCNQ1 and other channel variants cause early-onset familial AF.

answers.name: Cardiac sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Granulomatous infiltration of atria causes AF alongside ventricular arrhythmias and heart block.

answers.name: Corticosteroids
answers.pearl: Observational data link high-dose steroids with AF.

answers.name: Epicardial adipose tissue
answers.pearl: Epicardial fat releases inflammatory mediators that promote atrial fibrosis.

answers.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
answers.pearl: Accessory pathways predispose to AF, which can conduct rapidly and cause ventricular fibrillation.

answers.name: Left atrial myxoma
answers.pearl: A left atrial tumor can obstruct the mitral valve and cause AF and emboli.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Iron-overload cardiomyopathy causes atrial arrhythmias along with restrictive and dilated physiology.

answers.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Atrial amyloid infiltration commonly causes AF, which responds poorly to rhythm control.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of a prolonged PT or aPTT.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: acquired factor V inhibitor, LAHPS, acquired factor X deficiency/amyloid, paraproteinemia interference, celiac disease (indirect), sepsis (partly overlaps DIC), polycythemia pre-analytic effect. Traps: von Willebrand disease, lupus anticoagulant, factor XII deficiency.

answers.name: Warfarin
answers.pearl: Warfarin reduces factors II, VII, IX and X, prolonging PT first and later aPTT.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Unfractionated heparin prolongs aPTT by potentiating antithrombin, and high doses also lengthen PT.

answers.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
answers.pearl: Consumption of factors and fibrinogen prolongs PT and aPTT with low platelets and raised D-dimer.

answers.name: Liver disease
answers.pearl: Reduced synthesis of factors other than VIII causes prolonged PT first, with Factor VII having the shortest half-life.

answers.name: Vitamin K deficiency
answers.pearl: Lack of vitamin K impairs gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX and X.

answers.name: Hemophilia A
answers.pearl: Isolated prolonged aPTT with normal PT that corrects on mixing.

answers.name: Direct oral anticoagulants
answers.pearl: Anti-Xa agents may modestly prolong PT, and dabigatran prolongs aPTT, but the tests are insensitive.

answers.name: Hemophilia B
answers.pearl: Isolated aPTT prolongation corrects with mixing, with lower factor IX activity.

answers.name: Von Willebrand disease
answers.pearl: Low vWF shortens factor VIII half-life, so aPTT may be prolonged but is often normal.

answers.name: Lupus anticoagulant
answers.pearl: Antiphospholipid antibodies prolong phospholipid-dependent tests in vitro but cause thrombosis, not bleeding.

answers.name: Heparin contamination of sample
answers.pearl: Drawing from a heparinized line prolongs aPTT spuriously and corrects with repeat peripheral draw.

answers.name: Antibiotic-related vitamin K depletion
answers.pearl: Gut flora suppression in poorly eating patients lowers vitamin K and prolongs PT.

answers.name: Dilutional coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Large-volume crystalloid or red cell resuscitation without plasma dilutes clotting factors.

answers.name: Direct thrombin inhibitors
answers.pearl: Argatroban and bivalirudin prolong aPTT and can raise INR, confounding warfarin monitoring.

answers.name: Low molecular weight heparin
answers.pearl: LMWH and fondaparinux have little effect on aPTT and are monitored with anti-Xa levels.

answers.name: Underfilled citrate tube
answers.pearl: Underfilled tubes have excess citrate relative to plasma and prolong results spuriously.

answers.name: Acquired hemophilia A
answers.pearl: Autoantibody against factor VIII causes severe bleeding with isolated aPTT prolongation not correcting on mixing.

answers.name: Factor XI deficiency
answers.pearl: Common in Ashkenazi Jews, with prolonged aPTT and bleeding that correlates poorly with factor level.

answers.name: Trauma-induced coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Hypoperfusion and tissue injury cause early coagulopathy with prolonged PT.

answers.name: Superwarfarin poisoning
answers.pearl: Rodenticides inhibit vitamin K epoxide reductase for weeks to months.

answers.name: Fibrinogen disorder
answers.pearl: Very low or abnormal fibrinogen prolongs PT, aPTT and thrombin time.

answers.name: Thrombolytic therapy
answers.pearl: Systemic fibrinolysis consumes fibrinogen and prolongs clotting times.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Sepsis activates coagulation and depletes factors, often without overt DIC.

answers.name: Snake envenomation
answers.pearl: Pit viper venom causes consumption and defibrination with unclottable blood.

answers.name: Obstetric coagulopathy
answers.pearl: Tissue factor release causes acute consumptive coagulopathy in obstetric emergencies.

answers.name: Cardiopulmonary bypass
answers.pearl: High-dose intraoperative heparin causes marked aPTT prolongation.

answers.name: Factor VII deficiency
answers.pearl: The only deficiency with isolated PT prolongation and normal aPTT.

answers.name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
answers.pearl: Procoagulant promyelocytes cause DIC with hyperfibrinolysis.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Fat malabsorption leads to vitamin K deficiency.

answers.name: Factor XII deficiency
answers.pearl: Markedly prolonged aPTT without bleeding, because contact factor deficiencies do not impair hemostasis.

answers.name: Factor X deficiency
answers.pearl: Prolongs PT and aPTT, and can be acquired in AL amyloidosis.

answers.name: L-asparaginase
answers.pearl: Asparaginase depletes fibrinogen and other synthesized factors.

answers.name: Cefotetan
answers.pearl: The N-methylthiotetrazole side chain inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase.

answers.name: Factor V deficiency
answers.pearl: Prolongs both PT and aPTT and is accompanied by mild to moderate bleeding.

answers.name: Prothrombin deficiency
answers.pearl: Congenital hypoprothrombinemia prolongs PT and aPTT.

answers.name: Polycythemia
answers.pearl: A hematocrit above 55 percent leaves relative excess citrate in standard tubes and spuriously prolongs tests.

answers.name: Acquired factor X deficiency in amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid fibrils adsorb factor X and cause bleeding with prolonged PT and aPTT.

answers.name: Paraproteinemia
answers.pearl: Paraproteins can interfere with fibrin polymerization and prolong tests.

answers.name: Prekallikrein deficiency
answers.pearl: Isolated aPTT prolongation that shortens with prolonged incubation, without bleeding.

answers.name: Acquired factor V inhibitor
answers.pearl: Exposure to topical bovine thrombin can induce antibodies that cross-react with factor V.

answers.name: High molecular weight kininogen deficiency
answers.pearl: Isolated aPTT prolongation without bleeding.

answers.name: Lupus anticoagulant-hypoprothrombinemia syndrome
answers.pearl: Antibodies against prothrombin cause rapid clearance and bleeding in a few lupus patients.

answers.name: Combined factor V and VIII deficiency
answers.pearl: ER cargo receptor mutations impair secretion of factors V and VIII.

answers.name: Combined vitamin K-dependent factor deficiency
aliases: hereditary vitamin K clotting factor deficiency
answers.pearl: Mutations in vitamin K cycle proteins cause deficiency of factors II, VII, IX and X.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause urinary retention.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: loperamide (misuse level), mexiletine, dantrolene, clonidine, SSRIs, verapamil and androgen therapy (weak evidence), beta agonists. Traps: vincristine, disopyramide, scopolamine. Lomotil listed under antispasmodic aliases (anticholinergic component).

answers.name: Opioids
answers.pearl: Opioids reduce detrusor contractility and raise sphincter tone, causing retention especially postoperatively.

answers.name: Anticholinergic bladder medications
answers.pearl: Antimuscarinics block detrusor contraction and can cause retention in men with prostate enlargement.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
answers.pearl: Strong anticholinergic activity reduces bladder contractility.

answers.name: First-generation antihistamines
answers.pearl: Sedating antihistamines have antimuscarinic effects and are a common over-the-counter culprit.

answers.name: Decongestants
answers.pearl: Alpha-agonists contract the bladder neck and prostatic smooth muscle, precipitating retention in men with BPH.

answers.name: Benzodiazepines
answers.pearl: Sedation and pelvic floor relaxation can impair voiding, mostly in older adults.

answers.name: Spinal or epidural anesthesia
answers.pearl: Neuraxial blockade removes bladder sensation and detrusor tone, a classic postoperative retention cause.

answers.name: Antipsychotics
answers.pearl: Anticholinergic and antiadrenergic effects of antipsychotics can produce retention.

answers.name: Antiparkinson anticholinergics
answers.pearl: Central anticholinergics reduce detrusor contraction and cause retention in older adults.

answers.name: Muscle relaxants
answers.pearl: Some muscle relaxants have anticholinergic action or relax the external sphincter and detrusor.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Prostaglandin inhibition reduces detrusor contraction, especially in older men.

answers.name: Hyoscyamine
answers.pearl: Antispasmodics used for IBS and cramps are potent antimuscarinics.

answers.name: Volatile general anesthetics
answers.pearl: General anesthesia contributes to postoperative urinary retention, along with fluid load.

answers.name: Calcium channel blockers
answers.pearl: Calcium channel blockers impair detrusor smooth muscle contraction.

answers.name: Promethazine
answers.pearl: Phenothiazine antiemetic with marked antihistaminic and anticholinergic effects.

answers.name: Ipratropium
answers.pearl: Inhaled antimuscarinics can cause retention in older men with prostatic obstruction.

answers.name: Cyclobenzaprine
answers.pearl: Structurally tricyclic with anticholinergic effects.

answers.name: Baclofen
answers.pearl: Baclofen can impair voiding by reducing external sphincter and detrusor tone.

answers.name: Dicyclomine
answers.pearl: Anticholinergic antispasmodic used for IBS and a frequent cause in older adults.

answers.name: Hydroxyzine
answers.pearl: First-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic effects.

answers.name: Tiotropium
answers.pearl: Inhaled long-acting antimuscarinic with reported urinary retention.

answers.name: Amphetamines
answers.pearl: Sympathomimetic stimulants increase bladder outlet tone.

answers.name: Duloxetine
answers.pearl: Norepinephrine reuptake inhibition raises urethral tone and can cause hesitancy or retention.

answers.name: Amantadine
answers.pearl: Amantadine has anticholinergic effects and can cause retention in the elderly.

answers.name: Dimenhydrinate
answers.pearl: Vestibular antihistamines are anticholinergic and common in older adults with vertigo.

answers.name: Mirabegron
answers.pearl: Beta-3 agonists relax the detrusor and can precipitate retention in bladder outlet obstruction.

answers.name: Atomoxetine
answers.pearl: Noradrenergic effects on urethral tone cause hesitancy and retention.

answers.name: SSRIs
answers.pearl: Paroxetine is more anticholinergic, but other SSRIs rarely cause retention.

answers.name: Glycopyrrolate
answers.pearl: Antimuscarinics used during anesthesia reversal or secretion control cause retention.

answers.name: Ephedrine
answers.pearl: Mixed alpha agonist contracts the bladder neck.

answers.name: Midodrine
answers.pearl: Alpha-1 agonist raises bladder outlet resistance and can cause retention.

answers.name: Verapamil
answers.pearl: Has been associated with retention through detrusor effects.

answers.name: Beta-adrenergic agonists
answers.pearl: Detrusor relaxation through beta-receptors, reported more in men with outlet obstruction.

answers.name: Androgen therapy
answers.pearl: Testosterone can enlarge the prostate, worsening obstruction in susceptible men.

answers.name: Mexiletine
answers.pearl: Reported cause of retention in prescribing information.

answers.name: Clonidine
answers.pearl: Central alpha-2 agonist, retention reported but uncommon.

answers.name: Dantrolene
answers.pearl: Urinary retention listed as a side effect.

answers.name: Botulinum toxin
answers.pearl: Detrusor injection or systemic spread can cause retention.

answers.name: Loperamide
answers.pearl: High-dose loperamide misuse or opioid-like effects can cause retention.

answers.name: Vincristine
answers.pearl: Autonomic neuropathy from vincristine causes constipation, ileus and bladder atony.

answers.name: Disopyramide
answers.pearl: A class Ia antiarrhythmic with strong anticholinergic effects, classically causing retention.

answers.name: Scopolamine
answers.pearl: Anticholinergic patch for motion sickness that can cause retention and delirium.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of renal tubular acidosis (types 1, 2 and 4).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: autoimmune hepatitis, cryoglobulinemia and valproate (case/series level), beta-blockers and aliskiren (contribute to hyperkalemia rather than a defined RTA), deferasirox, carbonic anhydrase II deficiency (mixed type 3), topiramate grouped with acetazolamide. Traps: medullary sponge kidney, cystinosis, expired tetracycline, hereditary fructose intolerance.

answers.name: Sjogren syndrome
answers.pearl: The commonest autoimmune cause of distal RTA, from interstitial nephritis involving the collecting duct, and may also affect proximal tubule.

answers.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
answers.pearl: SLE causes distal RTA and, with lupus nephritis, hyperkalemic type 4.

answers.name: Amphotericin B
answers.pearl: Amphotericin makes the collecting duct membrane leaky to protons, causing distal RTA.

answers.name: Diabetes mellitus
answers.pearl: Diabetic nephropathy is the commonest cause of type 4 RTA through hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism.

answers.name: ACE inhibitors and ARBs
answers.pearl: Reduced angiotensin II and aldosterone cause hyperkalemic type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
answers.pearl: Block aldosterone action or ENaC, impairing potassium and proton secretion in the collecting duct.

answers.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune tubulointerstitial disease causes distal RTA in some patients.

answers.name: NSAIDs
answers.pearl: Reduced renal prostaglandins lower renin and aldosterone, causing hyperkalemic type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Multiple myeloma
answers.pearl: Light chains injure the proximal tubule and cause Fanconi syndrome and proximal RTA.

answers.name: Trimethoprim
answers.pearl: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC like amiloride, causing hyperkalemia and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Heparin
answers.pearl: Heparin suppresses aldosterone synthesis by inhibiting the zona glomerulosa.

answers.name: Calcineurin inhibitors
answers.pearl: These reduce ENaC and aldosterone sensitivity, causing type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Medullary sponge kidney
answers.pearl: Cystic dilation of collecting ducts causes stones, nephrocalcinosis and distal RTA.

answers.name: Acetazolamide
answers.pearl: Inhibition of proximal tubular carbonic anhydrase impairs bicarbonate reabsorption and causes proximal RTA.

answers.name: Obstructive uropathy
answers.pearl: Obstruction damages distal tubule function, causing hyperkalemic distal RTA.

answers.name: Adrenal insufficiency
answers.pearl: Low aldosterone causes hyperkalemic type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism
answers.pearl: Interstitial disease reduces renin release, lowering aldosterone and impairing potassium excretion.

answers.name: Tenofovir
answers.pearl: Tenofovir causes proximal tubular mitochondrial injury and Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Ifosfamide
answers.pearl: Chloroacetaldehyde damages proximal tubule, causing Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Lithium impairs distal acidification and causes incomplete distal RTA.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Autoimmune cholangitis is associated with distal RTA, often subclinical.

answers.name: Idiopathic hypercalciuria
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria causes stones and nephrocalcinosis and is linked to distal RTA.

answers.name: Sickle cell disease
answers.pearl: Medullary ischemia damages distal nephron, causing distal or type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Kidney transplant
answers.pearl: Rejection and immunosuppression cause distal and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin injures proximal tubules, producing Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Chronic kidney disease
answers.pearl: Tubulointerstitial damage reduces ammonium and potassium handling.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: HIV causes type 4 RTA via adrenal dysfunction, drugs and tubular injury.

answers.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis can cause distal RTA, while PTH causes bicarbonate wasting.

answers.name: Heavy metal toxicity
answers.pearl: Heavy metals injure proximal tubular transport and cause Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Cystinosis
answers.pearl: Lysosomal cystine storage causes the classic childhood Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Amyloidosis
answers.pearl: Amyloid causes proximal RTA or type 4 RTA through tubulointerstitial damage.

answers.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
answers.pearl: Reported cause of distal RTA with hypergammaglobulinemia.

answers.name: Toluene
answers.pearl: Toluene causes distal RTA with hypokalemia and a wide acid-base picture.

answers.name: Expired tetracycline
answers.pearl: Degradation products (anhydro-4-epitetracycline) cause proximal tubulopathy.

answers.name: Analgesic nephropathy
answers.pearl: Papillary damage leads to distal RTA and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Vitamin D intoxication
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria causes nephrocalcinosis and distal RTA.

answers.name: Hereditary distal RTA
answers.pearl: Autosomal dominant or recessive defects of collecting-duct acidification, some with deafness.

answers.name: Valproic acid
answers.pearl: Valproate can cause reversible Fanconi syndrome, especially in children.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides accumulate in proximal tubule cells and cause Fanconi-type tubular injury.

answers.name: Sarcoidosis
answers.pearl: Hypercalciuria and granulomatous interstitial nephritis can cause distal RTA.

answers.name: Hereditary fructose intolerance
answers.pearl: Fructose-1-phosphate accumulation damages proximal tubule and causes Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Cryoglobulinemia
answers.pearl: Reported cause of distal RTA from tubulointerstitial involvement.

answers.name: Pentamidine
answers.pearl: Pentamidine blocks ENaC and causes hyperkalemia and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Beta-blockers
answers.pearl: Beta blockade lowers renin and aldosterone and can aggravate hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper deposition causes proximal and distal tubular dysfunction.

answers.name: Southeast Asian ovalocytosis
answers.pearl: Band 3 variants cause distal RTA in this red cell disorder.

answers.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
answers.pearl: Salt-wasting forms cause mineralocorticoid deficiency and hyperkalemic acidosis.

answers.name: Aliskiren
answers.pearl: Blocks renin and lowers aldosterone, causing hyperkalemic acidosis.

answers.name: Deferasirox
answers.pearl: Deferasirox causes proximal tubulopathy and Fanconi syndrome.

answers.name: Hereditary aldosterone synthase deficiency
answers.pearl: Impaired aldosterone synthesis causes salt wasting and hyperkalemic acidosis.

answers.name: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1
answers.pearl: Receptor or ENaC defects cause aldosterone resistance with high aldosterone and type 4 RTA.

answers.name: Gordon syndrome
answers.pearl: WNK kinase mutations cause hypertension, hyperkalemia and hyperchloremic acidosis.

answers.name: Fanconi-Bickel syndrome
answers.pearl: GLUT2 deficiency causes proximal tubulopathy with hepatomegaly.

answers.name: Dent disease
answers.pearl: CLCN5 mutations cause low molecular weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria and sometimes proximal RTA.

answers.name: Carbonic anhydrase II deficiency
answers.pearl: Causes mixed proximal and distal acidosis with osteopetrosis and cerebral calcification.

answers.name: Lowe syndrome
answers.pearl: OCRL mutation causes cataracts, hypotonia and proximal RTA.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Breast mass, Pancreatitis, Orchitis (rare reported GPA involvement); Pituitary involvement; Pyoderma gangrenosum-like ulcers; Pericarditis; Interstitial lung disease with MPO-ANCA (association, not classic vasculitis). Asthma and eosinophilia are EGPA-specific.

answers.name: Glomerulonephritis
answers.pearl: Pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis is the classic renal lesion in GPA and MPA.

answers.name: Hematuria
answers.pearl: Dysmorphic red cells and red cell casts reflect active glomerular inflammation.

answers.name: Acute kidney injury
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive renal failure over days to weeks can be the presenting event.

answers.name: Proteinuria
answers.pearl: Usually sub-nephrotic, though nephrotic-range protein can occur.

answers.name: Sinusitis
answers.pearl: Chronic refractory sinusitis is a frequent early upper airway sign of GPA.

answers.name: Epistaxis
answers.pearl: Nasal mucosal inflammation and crusting cause bleeding.

answers.name: Hemoptysis
answers.pearl: Alveolar hemorrhage or cavitary nodules produce coughing of blood.

answers.name: Dyspnea
answers.pearl: Shortness of breath may reflect alveolar hemorrhage, nodules, or airway disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary nodules
answers.pearl: Multiple nodules, often cavitating, are typical of GPA.

answers.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Capillaritis causes life-threatening bilateral infiltrates and falling hemoglobin, seen in MPA and GPA.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms are common at presentation.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation produces anorexia and weight loss.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Malaise and fatigue accompany active vasculitis.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Migratory polyarthralgia or arthritis is common in all ANCA vasculitides.

answers.name: Myalgia
answers.pearl: Muscle pain accompanies systemic inflammation.

answers.name: Palpable purpura
answers.pearl: Small-vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis on the lower legs is the commonest skin lesion.

answers.name: Nasal crusting
answers.pearl: Crusting and bloody rhinorrhea reflect granulomatous mucosal inflammation.

answers.name: Mononeuritis multiplex
answers.pearl: Vasculitis of vasa nervorum causes asymmetric motor and sensory deficits such as foot drop, especially in MPA and EGPA.

answers.name: Peripheral neuropathy
answers.pearl: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy occurs in a significant minority.

answers.name: Scleritis
answers.pearl: Painful red eye with deep violaceous injection that may threaten vision.

answers.name: Episcleritis
answers.pearl: Milder, self-limited eye inflammation that blanches with phenylephrine.

answers.name: Otitis media
answers.pearl: Serous otitis media and Eustachian tube dysfunction are common in GPA.

answers.name: Hearing loss
answers.pearl: Conductive or sensorineural loss from middle-ear or inner-ear involvement.

answers.name: Nasal septal perforation
answers.pearl: Septal granulomatous inflammation destroys cartilage and can collapse the bridge into a saddle nose.

answers.name: Pleural effusion
answers.pearl: Effusions or pleuritis may accompany pulmonary involvement.

answers.name: Oral ulcers
answers.pearl: Oral ulcers and strawberry gingivitis can occur in GPA.

answers.name: Asthma
answers.pearl: Late-onset asthma is the hallmark prodrome of EGPA.

answers.name: Eosinophilia
answers.pearl: Peripheral eosinophilia above 1,000 per microliter characterizes EGPA.

answers.name: Venous thromboembolism
answers.pearl: GPA carries an increased risk of DVT and PE during active disease.

answers.name: Orbital mass
answers.pearl: Retro-orbital granuloma pushes the globe forward and threatens the optic nerve.

answers.name: Subglottic stenosis
answers.pearl: Circumferential subglottic narrowing causes stridor and is more typical of GPA.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Cardiac involvement, especially in EGPA, includes eosinophilic myocarditis and heart failure.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia
answers.pearl: Visceral vasculitis may cause abdominal pain, bleeding, or bowel infarction.

answers.name: Pericarditis
answers.pearl: Pericardial inflammation is described in GPA and EGPA.

answers.name: Digital ischemia
answers.pearl: Small-vessel occlusion can produce digital infarcts, gangrene, or splinter hemorrhages.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Pulmonary fibrosis, often a UIP pattern, is associated with MPO-ANCA and can precede overt vasculitis.

answers.name: Drug-induced ANCA vasculitis
answers.pearl: Propylthiouracil, hydralazine, minocycline and levamisole-adulterated cocaine can induce ANCA vasculitis, often with MPO or dual positivity.

answers.name: Hypertrophic pachymeningitis
answers.pearl: Dural thickening and enhancement cause headache and cranial neuropathies, mostly in GPA.

answers.name: Central nervous system vasculitis
answers.pearl: Stroke, seizures, or encephalopathy are uncommon neurologic complications.

answers.name: Pituitary involvement
answers.pearl: Granulomatous hypophysitis can cause diabetes insipidus or hypopituitarism in GPA.

answers.name: Tracheobronchial stenosis
answers.pearl: Endobronchial granulomatous disease can narrow the bronchi and cause lobar collapse.

answers.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum-like ulcers
answers.pearl: Necrotic, ulcerating skin lesions can mimic pyoderma gangrenosum in GPA.

answers.name: Orchitis
answers.pearl: Genitourinary involvement with testicular or epididymal inflammation is a rare GPA manifestation.

answers.name: Breast mass
answers.pearl: Breast involvement by granulomatous inflammation has been reported in GPA.

answers.name: Pancreatitis
answers.pearl: Pancreatic involvement is a rare reported vasculitic complication.

answers.name: Positive c-ANCA PR3
answers.pearl: PR3-ANCA with cytoplasmic pattern is the classic serologic marker for granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

answers.name: Positive p-ANCA MPO
answers.pearl: MPO-ANCA with perinuclear pattern is typical of microscopic polyangiitis and EGPA.

answers.name: Pulmonary-renal syndrome
answers.pearl: Simultaneous alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis is a classic presentation of ANCA vasculitis and anti-GBM disease.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hyperthermia or hyperpyrexia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Pheochromocytoma crisis (hyperpyrexia reported), Lithium toxicity (fever uncommon), Dopamine agonist withdrawal, Baclofen withdrawal, Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Familial dysautonomia, Fatal familial insomnia, Intravascular lymphoma (fever of unknown origin more than hyperpyrexia). Infection counted as hyperpyrexia though technically fever.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Failure of thermoregulation with core temperature above 40 C and CNS dysfunction, either classic or exertional.

answers.name: Sepsis
answers.pearl: Overwhelming infection can produce hyperpyrexia above 41.5 C through pyrogenic cytokine release.

answers.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
answers.pearl: Dopamine antagonism or withdrawal causes lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia and autonomic instability over days.

answers.name: Serotonin syndrome
answers.pearl: Excess serotonergic activity causes hyperthermia, clonus, hyperreflexia and diarrhea, usually within hours.

answers.name: Sympathomimetic toxicity
answers.pearl: Cocaine, amphetamines and MDMA raise heat production and impair heat loss.

answers.name: Salicylate toxicity
answers.pearl: Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation generates heat along with tachypnea and anion gap acidosis.

answers.name: Anticholinergic toxicity
answers.pearl: Impaired sweating produces hot, dry skin, mydriasis and delirium.

answers.name: Thyroid storm
answers.pearl: Severe thyrotoxicosis with fever, tachycardia and altered mental status.

answers.name: Meningitis
answers.pearl: CNS infection frequently presents with high fever and altered mentation.

answers.name: Seizures
answers.pearl: Prolonged convulsive activity generates large amounts of heat.

answers.name: Alcohol withdrawal
answers.pearl: Delirium tremens produces autonomic hyperactivity with fever.

answers.name: Drug fever
answers.pearl: Hypersensitivity to a medication can cause persistent fever, sometimes with rash and eosinophilia.

answers.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
answers.pearl: Central fever follows hypothalamic injury or blood in the ventricles.

answers.name: Hot environment exposure
answers.pearl: Hot ambient temperature or poor ventilation overwhelms heat dissipation.

answers.name: Heat exhaustion
answers.pearl: Milder heat illness without CNS dysfunction, with temperature generally under 40 C.

answers.name: Dehydration
answers.pearl: Volume depletion reduces sweating and impairs heat loss.

answers.name: Neoplastic fever
answers.pearl: Lymphoma, renal cell carcinoma and others produce tumor-related fever through cytokines.

answers.name: Pulmonary embolism
answers.pearl: Low-grade temperature elevation can occur with infarction.

answers.name: Autoimmune disease flare
answers.pearl: Active SLE, adult-onset Still disease, or vasculitis can produce high spiking fevers.

answers.name: Transfusion reaction
answers.pearl: Febrile non-hemolytic and acute hemolytic reactions cause fever during or after transfusion.

answers.name: Adrenal crisis
answers.pearl: Cortisol deficiency can present with fever, hypotension and hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Tricyclic antidepressant toxicity
answers.pearl: Anticholinergic effects cause hyperthermia with QRS widening and seizures.

answers.name: Cerebrovascular accident
answers.pearl: Large strokes, particularly brainstem and hypothalamic, can produce fever.

answers.name: Lithium toxicity
answers.pearl: Lithium toxicity can cause fever with tremor, neuromuscular excitability and confusion.

answers.name: Hypothalamic dysfunction
answers.pearl: Damage to the preoptic anterior hypothalamus or its pathways abolishes thermoregulation.

answers.name: Withdrawal of baclofen
answers.pearl: Abrupt cessation of intrathecal baclofen causes spasticity, fever and rhabdomyolysis, mimicking NMS.

answers.name: Dopamine agonist withdrawal
answers.pearl: Sudden cessation of levodopa or dopamine agonists in Parkinson disease can cause a parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia syndrome.

answers.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
answers.pearl: Fever is part of the classic pentad of TTP.

answers.name: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
answers.pearl: Uncontrolled cytokine release causes persistent high fever, cytopenias and marked ferritin elevation.

answers.name: Lethal catatonia
answers.pearl: Malignant catatonia produces fever, autonomic instability and rigidity that resembles NMS.

answers.name: Monoamine oxidase inhibitor toxicity
answers.pearl: MAOI interactions with meperidine, SSRIs or tyramine produce severe hyperthermic crises.

answers.name: Exertional hyperthermia
answers.pearl: Strenuous exercise in heat raises core temperature before heat stroke, with or without CNS dysfunction.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Severe pulmonary infection can cause hyperpyrexia through cytokine release.

answers.name: Tetanus
answers.pearl: Muscle spasm and autonomic instability can raise body temperature in severe tetanus.

answers.name: Extensive skin disease
answers.pearl: Burns, erythroderma and widespread dermatologic disease impair sweating and heat loss.

answers.name: Neonatal overbundling
answers.pearl: Neonates dressed or wrapped in too many layers cannot dissipate heat, causing hyperthermia.

answers.name: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
answers.pearl: Absent sweat glands prevent heat dissipation, so infants can develop unexplained hyperthermia.

answers.name: Synthetic cathinone toxicity
answers.pearl: Bath salts and synthetic cannabinoids cause agitation, rhabdomyolysis and hyperthermia.

answers.name: Dinitrophenol toxicity
answers.pearl: The uncoupling agent 2,4-dinitrophenol, abused as a weight-loss supplement, causes fatal hyperthermia.

answers.name: Intravascular lymphoma
answers.pearl: Intravascular large B cell lymphoma can present as fever of unknown origin with hypoxia and neurologic signs.

answers.name: Fatal familial insomnia
answers.pearl: Prion thalamic degeneration causes dysautonomia, insomnia and hyperthermia.

answers.name: Familial dysautonomia
aliases: congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis
answers.pearl: Impaired autonomic regulation produces episodic fever and temperature instability.

answers.name: Malignant hyperthermia
answers.pearl: Volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine trigger uncontrolled calcium release from RYR1 mutations; treat with dantrolene.

answers.name: Pheochromocytoma crisis
answers.pearl: Catecholamine surge produces hyperthermia, hypertension and multi-organ failure.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of fever in a returning traveler.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Kyasanur Forest disease, Hantavirus (geographically limited), Tick-borne relapsing fever, Trench fever, African trypanosomiasis (rare in travelers), Katayama fever timing, Lassa fever (imported cases rare), Rat-bite fever and Tularemia are not classic travel illnesses. Dengue, malaria, typhoid kept as common answers; viral hemorrhagic fevers and Ebola scored as board traps.

answers.name: Malaria
answers.pearl: The first diagnosis to exclude in any febrile traveler from an endemic area; thick and thin smears or rapid test, repeated if negative.

answers.name: Dengue fever
answers.pearl: Mosquito-borne flavivirus causing fever, severe myalgia, retro-orbital pain and thrombocytopenia.

answers.name: Typhoid fever
answers.pearl: Salmonella Typhi causes stepwise fever, relative bradycardia and abdominal pain; enteric fever is a leading cause of fever in South Asian travelers.

answers.name: Influenza
answers.pearl: Respiratory viruses are a frequent cause of fever in travelers and cluster in crowded transport.

answers.name: Gastroenteritis
answers.pearl: Bacterial or viral traveler's diarrhea can present with fever.

answers.name: Urinary tract infection
answers.pearl: Pyelonephritis and UTI remain common in febrile travelers.

answers.name: Pneumonia
answers.pearl: Community-acquired pneumonia, including Legionella, occurs in travelers and cruise passengers.

answers.name: Chikungunya
answers.pearl: Alphavirus causing abrupt fever and severe symmetric polyarthralgia that may persist for months.

answers.name: Hepatitis A
answers.pearl: Fecal-oral infection with fever, jaundice and hepatitis in unvaccinated travelers.

answers.name: COVID-19
answers.pearl: SARS-CoV-2 remains a common cause of fever in travelers.

answers.name: Rickettsial infection
answers.pearl: African tick bite fever and spotted fever group rickettsiae cause fever, eschar and rash after safari or hiking.

answers.name: Zika virus
answers.pearl: Flavivirus causing mild fever, rash and conjunctivitis; congenital infection is the major concern.

answers.name: Amebic liver abscess
answers.pearl: Entamoeba histolytica causes fever and right upper quadrant pain after travel to endemic regions.

answers.name: HIV acute retroviral syndrome
answers.pearl: Mononucleosis-like illness 2 to 4 weeks after sexual exposure during travel.

answers.name: Leptospirosis
answers.pearl: Spirochetal infection from freshwater exposure causing fever, conjunctival suffusion, myalgia and kidney injury.

answers.name: Infectious mononucleosis
answers.pearl: EBV can present in travelers as pharyngitis, fever and lymphadenopathy.

answers.name: Tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Reactivation or new exposure causes prolonged fever and night sweats.

answers.name: Strep pharyngitis
answers.pearl: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis is a common benign cause of fever.

answers.name: Sexually transmitted infections
answers.pearl: Syphilis, gonorrhea and chlamydia can present with fever after unprotected sex during travel.

answers.name: Schistosomiasis
answers.pearl: Acute infection (Katayama fever) causes fever, urticaria and eosinophilia 2 to 8 weeks after freshwater exposure.

answers.name: Brucellosis
answers.pearl: Zoonosis from unpasteurized dairy causing undulant fever, sweats and osteoarticular disease.

answers.name: Q fever
answers.pearl: Coxiella burnetii infection from livestock exposure causes pneumonia, hepatitis and culture-negative endocarditis.

answers.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
answers.pearl: Kala-azar produces prolonged fever, splenomegaly and pancytopenia after sandfly exposure.

answers.name: Scrub typhus
answers.pearl: Orientia tsutsugamushi causes fever, eschar and rash after rural exposure in Asia.

answers.name: Murine typhus
answers.pearl: Flea-borne Rickettsia typhi causes fever and rash in travelers to warm coastal areas.

answers.name: Legionnaires disease
answers.pearl: Legionella pneumonia after hotel or cruise ship stays; urinary antigen testing is useful.

answers.name: Meningococcal disease
answers.pearl: Neisseria meningitidis outbreaks occur in Hajj pilgrims and meningitis-belt travelers.

answers.name: Histoplasmosis
answers.pearl: Cave exploration exposes travelers to Histoplasma, causing fever and pulmonary infiltrates.

answers.name: Coccidioidomycosis
answers.pearl: Desert travel to the American Southwest or Latin America can cause fever and pneumonia.

answers.name: Rabies prodrome
answers.pearl: Fever, paresthesia at the bite site and anxiety precede encephalitis after animal exposure.

answers.name: Melioidosis
answers.pearl: Burkholderia pseudomallei from soil or water in Southeast Asia causes pneumonia, abscesses and sepsis.

answers.name: Japanese encephalitis
answers.pearl: Mosquito-borne flavivirus in rural Asia causing fever and encephalitis; preventable with vaccine.

answers.name: Tick-borne encephalitis
answers.pearl: Flavivirus in forested Central/Eastern Europe and Russia causing biphasic fever and meningoencephalitis.

answers.name: Typhus (louse-borne)
answers.pearl: Rickettsia prowazekii causes epidemic typhus in crowded, louse-infested conditions.

answers.name: Relapsing fever
answers.pearl: Borrelia spirochetes cause recurrent febrile episodes after tick or louse exposure.

answers.name: West Nile virus
answers.pearl: Mosquito-borne flavivirus with fever, headache and sometimes neuroinvasive disease.

answers.name: Yellow fever
answers.pearl: Flavivirus causing biphasic fever, jaundice and hemorrhage in unvaccinated travelers to Africa and South America.

answers.name: Rift Valley fever
answers.pearl: Bunyavirus from livestock contact in Africa causing fever, hepatitis, retinitis and hemorrhage.

answers.name: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever
answers.pearl: Tick-borne nairovirus that causes hemorrhagic fever and has nosocomial spread.

answers.name: Kyasanur Forest disease
answers.pearl: Flavivirus transmitted by ticks in southwestern India causing fever and hemorrhage.

answers.name: African trypanosomiasis
answers.pearl: Tsetse-fly Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense causes acute fever, chancre and CNS disease in safari travelers.

answers.name: Lassa fever
answers.pearl: Arenavirus from rodent excreta causing fever, mucosal bleeding and hearing loss in West Africa.

answers.name: Ebola virus disease
answers.pearl: Filovirus with high fatality after contact with body fluids; any febrile traveler from an outbreak area should be isolated.

answers.name: Viral hemorrhagic fever
answers.pearl: Umbrella syndrome (Ebola, Lassa, Marburg, CCHF) of fever with bleeding and shock requiring isolation.

prompts.prompt: Name drugs that can cause hypothyroidism or thyroid dysfunction.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Perchlorate, Aminoglutethimide, Ethionamide, Interferon-gamma, Tyrosine kinase inhibitor drugs such as sorafenib/imatinib rank, Thalidomide and lenalidomide thyroid effects (more commonly mild), Rifampin (via increased levothyroxine metabolism), Phenytoin and carbamazepine (lower T4 without clear hypothyroidism), Bexarotene and Alemtuzumab mechanisms (central and autoimmune respectively).

answers.name: Amiodarone
answers.pearl: Its iodine load and direct thyroid toxicity cause either hypothyroidism or thyrotoxicosis.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.pearl: Inhibits thyroid hormone release and can cause goiter and hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Radioactive iodine
answers.pearl: Ablative treatment for Graves disease often causes permanent hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Methimazole
answers.pearl: Antithyroid thionamide that blocks organification and can overshoot into hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Propylthiouracil
answers.pearl: A thionamide that also blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion and can cause hypothyroidism if over-treated.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
answers.pearl: PD-1, PD-L1 and CTLA-4 agents cause thyroiditis followed by hypothyroidism in a substantial proportion of patients.

answers.name: Interferon alpha
answers.pearl: Triggers autoimmune thyroiditis, with hypothyroidism or thyrotoxicosis, particularly in patients treated for hepatitis C.

answers.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
answers.pearl: Sunitinib and other TKIs commonly cause hypothyroidism through thyroid destruction and altered metabolism.

answers.name: Iodinated contrast
answers.pearl: An iodine load can cause the Wolff-Chaikoff effect with transient or sustained hypothyroidism in susceptible patients.

answers.name: Phenytoin
answers.pearl: Increases hepatic metabolism of thyroid hormones and lowers total and free T4.

answers.name: Carbamazepine
answers.pearl: Induces hepatic enzymes that accelerate levothyroxine clearance.

answers.name: Rifampin
answers.pearl: A potent inducer of hepatic metabolism that increases levothyroxine requirements.

answers.name: Iodine supplements
answers.pearl: Kelp, potassium iodide and other iodine-containing supplements can induce thyroid dysfunction.

answers.name: Levothyroxine overreplacement
answers.pearl: Excess exogenous hormone causes thyrotoxicosis and suppresses endogenous production.

answers.name: Calcium carbonate
answers.pearl: Binds levothyroxine in the gut, reducing absorption and causing apparent hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Iron supplements
answers.pearl: Ferrous sulfate chelates levothyroxine and impairs its absorption.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Raised gastric pH reduces levothyroxine tablet dissolution and absorption.

answers.name: Cholestyramine
answers.pearl: Bile acid sequestrants bind levothyroxine in the intestine.

answers.name: Sucralfate
answers.pearl: Aluminum-containing agents bind levothyroxine and reduce its absorption.

answers.name: Glucocorticoids
answers.pearl: High-dose steroids suppress TSH secretion and reduce T4 to T3 conversion.

answers.name: Dopamine
answers.pearl: Suppresses TSH secretion, particularly in critically ill patients.

answers.name: Sevelamer
answers.pearl: Phosphate binders can bind levothyroxine and reduce absorption.

answers.name: Thalidomide
answers.pearl: Immunomodulators such as thalidomide and lenalidomide have been associated with hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Bexarotene
answers.pearl: A retinoid X receptor agonist that suppresses TSH and induces central hypothyroidism in most patients.

answers.name: Alemtuzumab
answers.pearl: Lymphocyte depletion and reconstitution drives autoimmune thyroid disease, mostly Graves disease and also hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Interleukin-2
answers.pearl: High-dose IL-2 can induce autoimmune thyroiditis and hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Perchlorate
answers.pearl: Competitively inhibits the sodium-iodide symporter, blocking thyroid iodide uptake.

answers.name: Aminoglutethimide
answers.pearl: Inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis and has been associated with goiter and hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Ethionamide
answers.pearl: Antituberculous agent with antithyroid activity and a documented rate of hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Phenobarbital
answers.pearl: Induces hepatic metabolism of thyroid hormone, lowering T4.

answers.name: Mitotane
answers.pearl: Increases hepatic cortisol and thyroxine-binding globulin changes and may lower free T4.

answers.name: Tamoxifen
answers.pearl: Mildly increases TBG and total T4, which can alter thyroid test interpretation.

answers.name: Orlistat
answers.pearl: Reduces levothyroxine absorption, with reports of increased TSH in patients on replacement.

answers.name: Cabozantinib
answers.pearl: A multikinase inhibitor with high rates of hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Povidone-iodine
answers.pearl: Topical iodine from antiseptics can be absorbed, particularly in neonates and burn patients, causing hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Valproate
answers.pearl: Valproic acid has been associated with subclinical hypothyroidism and elevated TSH.

answers.name: Sodium nitroprusside
answers.pearl: Thiocyanate generated from nitroprusside inhibits iodide uptake, with prolonged infusion producing hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Stavudine
answers.pearl: Stavudine-based antiretroviral therapy has been linked to subclinical hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Resorcinol
answers.pearl: Chronic topical resorcinol use on ulcers has been reported to cause goiter and hypothyroidism.
