answers.name: Danazol
answers.pearl: Androgenic steroid that lowers TBG and total T4, a classic cause of low total thyroxine without true hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Estrogen
answers.pearl: Estrogens raise TBG and total T4, so oral contraceptives raise levothyroxine needs and distort total hormone assays.

prompts.prompt: Name manifestations of inflammatory myopathy (dermatomyositis and polymyositis).
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Mechanic's hands (antisynthetase), Calcinosis (more in juvenile), Hypoxemic respiratory failure in MDA5 disease, Esophageal/cricopharyngeal dysfunction, Cardiac conduction disease, Pneumomediastinum (MDA5 amyopathic DM), Sjogren overlap, Lipodystrophy and Hypothyroidism (association only), Fever. Cancer association is strongest in dermatomyositis with TIF1-gamma and NXP2 antibodies.

answers.name: Proximal muscle weakness
answers.pearl: Symmetric weakness of shoulder and hip girdle muscles is the defining feature, causing difficulty with stairs and overhead tasks.

answers.name: Elevated creatine kinase
answers.pearl: Muscle enzymes (CK, aldolase, AST, ALT, LDH) rise with myofiber necrosis.

answers.name: Heliotrope rash
answers.pearl: Violaceous periorbital rash, sometimes with edema, is pathognomonic for dermatomyositis.

answers.name: Gottron papules
answers.pearl: Violaceous papules over the knuckles and other joints are pathognomonic for dermatomyositis.

answers.name: Myalgia
answers.pearl: Muscle pain or tenderness occurs in a minority and is not required for diagnosis.

answers.name: Dysphagia
answers.pearl: Involvement of striated pharyngeal and upper esophageal muscles causes swallowing difficulty and aspiration risk.

answers.name: Fatigue
answers.pearl: Systemic inflammation and weakness cause marked tiredness.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Occurs especially with antisynthetase and anti-MDA5 antibodies and strongly affects prognosis.

answers.name: Shawl sign
answers.pearl: Erythema over the upper back, shoulders and posterior neck.

answers.name: V sign
answers.pearl: Erythema over the anterior neck and upper chest in a V distribution.

answers.name: Malignancy
answers.pearl: Dermatomyositis, and to a lesser degree polymyositis, is associated with an increased risk of cancer, especially ovarian, lung and gastric.

answers.name: Arthralgia
answers.pearl: Nonerosive inflammatory arthritis or arthralgia is frequent, especially with antisynthetase antibodies.

answers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
answers.pearl: Digital vasospasm occurs in overlap states and antisynthetase syndrome.

answers.name: Weight loss
answers.pearl: Constitutional symptoms and dysphagia can lead to weight loss.

answers.name: Dyspnea
answers.pearl: Shortness of breath may reflect ILD, respiratory muscle weakness or cardiac involvement.

answers.name: Photosensitive rash
answers.pearl: Facial and exposed-area erythema worsens with sun exposure.

answers.name: Periungual erythema
answers.pearl: Nailfold erythema, dilated capillary loops and cuticular overgrowth reflect microangiopathy.

answers.name: Pruritus
answers.pearl: Itch is common in dermatomyositis, often prominent on the scalp.

answers.name: Scalp involvement
answers.pearl: Scaly, violaceous scalp erythema with diffuse hair loss.

answers.name: Fever
answers.pearl: Low-grade fever occurs with active disease, especially antisynthetase syndrome.

answers.name: Calcinosis cutis
answers.pearl: Calcium deposits in skin and muscle are more common in juvenile dermatomyositis and chronic disease.

answers.name: Mechanic's hands
answers.pearl: Roughened, cracked skin along the radial fingers is characteristic of antisynthetase syndrome.

answers.name: Poikiloderma
answers.pearl: Atrophy, telangiectasia and pigment change in a chronic photo-exposed distribution.

answers.name: Cardiomyopathy
answers.pearl: Myocardial involvement can cause conduction disturbance, arrhythmia or heart failure.

answers.name: Esophageal dysmotility
answers.pearl: Smooth muscle involvement of the upper esophagus causes reflux and dysphagia.

answers.name: Neck flexor weakness
answers.pearl: Head drop and inability to lift the head off the bed are signs of axial muscle weakness.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Severe necrosis can cause myoglobinuria and acute kidney injury.

answers.name: Dry cough
answers.pearl: Cough is often the first sign of ILD.

answers.name: Hypoventilation
answers.pearl: Respiratory muscle weakness causes hypercapnic respiratory failure.

answers.name: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
answers.pearl: Classic skin lesions with little or no muscle weakness; often has anti-MDA5 antibodies.

answers.name: Anti-Jo-1 antibodies
answers.pearl: The most common antisynthetase antibody, tied to ILD, arthritis, mechanic's hands and Raynaud.

answers.name: Anti-Mi-2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Associated with classic dermatomyositis, shawl sign and a good response to therapy.

answers.name: Anti-SRP antibodies
answers.pearl: Signal recognition particle antibodies mark severe necrotizing myopathy with prominent weakness and little inflammation.

answers.name: Anti-MDA5 antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-MDA5 is linked to amyopathic disease, skin ulcers and rapidly progressive ILD with high mortality.

answers.name: Anti-TIF1-gamma antibodies
answers.pearl: Antibodies against transcription intermediary factor 1 gamma carry the strongest association with adult cancer-associated dermatomyositis.

answers.name: Anti-NXP2 antibodies
answers.pearl: Anti-nuclear matrix protein 2 is associated with calcinosis in juveniles and cancer in adults.

answers.name: Anti-HMGCR antibodies
answers.pearl: Linked to statin-associated or statin-exposed necrotizing autoimmune myopathy that persists after the statin is stopped.

answers.name: Cutaneous ulceration
answers.pearl: Painful digital or skin ulceration reflects vasculopathy and is typical of anti-MDA5 disease.

answers.name: Pneumomediastinum
answers.pearl: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum can complicate anti-MDA5 rapidly progressive ILD.

answers.name: Lipodystrophy
answers.pearl: Acquired lipoatrophy and metabolic abnormalities are reported in juvenile dermatomyositis.

answers.name: Cricopharyngeal dysfunction
answers.pearl: Failure of upper esophageal sphincter relaxation is a recognized cause of treatment-refractory dysphagia.

answers.name: Colonic pseudo-obstruction
answers.pearl: Smooth muscle involvement, particularly in juvenile disease, can slow GI transit and cause bowel perforation or ischemia.

answers.name: Sjogren-like sicca symptoms
answers.pearl: Overlap with Sjogren syndrome produces dry eyes and mouth.

answers.name: Panniculitis
answers.pearl: Inflammation of subcutaneous fat is a rare cutaneous finding in dermatomyositis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of digital clubbing.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy paraneoplastic items such as POEMS, Thyroid acropachy (distinct from true clubbing), Hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula (unilateral), Subclavian aneurysm and brachial arteriovenous malformation (unilateral), Chronic pulmonary tuberculosis, Helicobacter-related causes, Cirrhosis-mechanism, Pachydermoperiostosis and Whipple disease. POEMS and Mesothelioma left out as doubtful.

answers.name: Lung cancer
answers.pearl: Non-small cell lung cancer, especially adenocarcinoma and squamous types, is the commonest cause of acquired clubbing.

answers.name: Bronchiectasis
answers.pearl: Chronic suppurative airway disease commonly produces clubbing.

answers.name: Cystic fibrosis
answers.pearl: Clubbing is nearly universal in patients with advanced cystic fibrosis lung disease.

answers.name: Cyanotic congenital heart disease
answers.pearl: Chronic right-to-left shunting leads to clubbing in congenital heart defects such as tetralogy of Fallot.

answers.name: Interstitial lung disease
answers.pearl: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis commonly causes clubbing.

answers.name: Infective endocarditis
answers.pearl: Subacute endocarditis can cause clubbing within weeks.

answers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
answers.pearl: Crohn disease is more commonly associated with clubbing than ulcerative colitis.

answers.name: Cirrhosis
answers.pearl: Clubbing occurs in advanced liver disease, particularly with hepatopulmonary syndrome.

answers.name: Lung abscess
answers.pearl: Chronic suppurative lung infection causes clubbing.

answers.name: Idiopathic or hereditary clubbing
answers.pearl: Familial clubbing is benign, appears at puberty and is not associated with disease.

answers.name: Pulmonary tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Chronic tuberculosis with cavitation or bronchiectasis can cause clubbing.

answers.name: Celiac disease
answers.pearl: Malabsorption disease, occasionally with clubbing in long-standing cases.

answers.name: Mesothelioma
answers.pearl: Pleural mesothelioma can cause clubbing and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

answers.name: Asbestosis
answers.pearl: Asbestos-related fibrosis can cause clubbing, though the sign may reflect underlying cancer.

answers.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
answers.pearl: Chronic cholestatic liver disease, including PBC and biliary atresia in children, is associated with clubbing.

answers.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
answers.pearl: Uncomplicated COPD does not cause clubbing, and its presence should prompt a search for lung cancer or bronchiectasis.

answers.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
answers.pearl: Reported with hypertrophic osteoarthropathy and clubbing in lymphoma.

answers.name: Pleural fibrous tumor
answers.pearl: Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura is a classic cause of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

answers.name: Thyroid acropachy
answers.pearl: Graves disease can produce clubbing with periosteal new bone, in addition to ophthalmopathy and dermopathy.

answers.name: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
answers.pearl: Right-to-left shunting through HHT-associated pulmonary AVMs causes hypoxemia and clubbing.

answers.name: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
answers.pearl: Intrapulmonary shunting in cirrhosis causes platypnea, hypoxemia and clubbing.

answers.name: Esophageal cancer
answers.pearl: Clubbing can be a paraneoplastic sign of esophageal and other GI malignancies.

answers.name: Primary pulmonary hypertension
answers.pearl: Idiopathic and congenital pulmonary hypertension have been associated with clubbing.

answers.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
answers.pearl: Liver cancer can cause paraneoplastic clubbing in addition to its link with cirrhosis.

answers.name: Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
answers.pearl: Pachydermoperiostosis is an inherited cause of clubbing with skin thickening and periostosis.

answers.name: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
answers.pearl: Reported as a cause of paraneoplastic clubbing and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

answers.name: Unilateral clubbing from vascular lesion
answers.pearl: Subclavian or axillary artery aneurysm, brachial AV malformation, and Pancoast tumors can cause clubbing on the involved side.

answers.name: Dialysis arteriovenous fistula
answers.pearl: Clubbing of the ipsilateral hand has been described distal to a dialysis fistula.

answers.name: Whipple disease
answers.pearl: Rare multisystem infection with Tropheryma whipplei that can cause arthropathy and clubbing.

answers.name: Bronchial carcinoid
answers.pearl: Neuroendocrine lung tumors can cause clubbing and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

answers.name: Chronic dysentery
answers.pearl: Chronic amebic or bacillary dysentery is a traditional cause of clubbing.

answers.name: Intestinal tuberculosis
answers.pearl: Abdominal tuberculosis is a classic textbook cause of clubbing with malabsorption.

answers.name: HIV-associated lymphoid interstitial pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Lymphoid interstitial pneumonitis in HIV-infected children is associated with clubbing.

answers.name: Atrial myxoma
answers.pearl: Left atrial myxoma has been reported to cause clubbing alongside constitutional features.

answers.name: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
answers.pearl: Periostitis of long bones with clubbing and synovitis, classically paraneoplastic in lung cancer; the traditional boards link to Marie-Bamberger syndrome.

answers.name: Empyema
answers.pearl: Chronic pleural infection with pus has been associated with clubbing and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

answers.name: Ulcerative colitis
answers.pearl: Clubbing is less frequent than in Crohn disease but occurs in a minority of patients.

answers.name: Chronic viral hepatitis
answers.pearl: Chronic active hepatitis can produce clubbing even before cirrhosis.

answers.name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia
answers.pearl: Impaired mucociliary clearance leads to bronchiectasis, sinusitis and clubbing; Kartagener syndrome adds situs inversus.

answers.name: Chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis
answers.pearl: Fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis can cause clubbing, which signals worse prognosis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of hypoparathyroidism.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypomagnesemia and hypermagnesemia (functional PTH failure rather than gland destruction), Wilson disease and thalassemia (iron/copper deposition, case series), HIV-related parathyroid infiltration (autopsy and case reports), Checkpoint inhibitors (case reports), CHARGE syndrome, Pearson syndrome, Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency, Bartter type 5, Maternal diabetes and prematurity (neonatal transient). Total of 48 answers; the true-gland-failure list is shorter than the 55-70 target and doubtful items were dropped.

answers.name: Total thyroidectomy
answers.pearl: The commonest cause by far; parathyroids are removed or devascularized, and hypocalcemia usually appears within 24 to 72 hours.

answers.name: Parathyroidectomy
answers.pearl: Removal of an adenoma or hyperplastic glands can leave suppressed or devascularized remnants, causing transient or permanent hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: Isolated autoimmune destruction of parathyroid tissue, often with antibodies against the calcium-sensing receptor.

answers.name: Radical neck dissection
answers.pearl: Central compartment dissection for head and neck or thyroid cancer, or laryngectomy, can injure the parathyroid blood supply.

answers.name: Idiopathic hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: A diagnosis of exclusion when no surgical, autoimmune, or genetic cause is found.

answers.name: Hypomagnesemia
answers.pearl: Severe magnesium depletion impairs PTH secretion and causes PTH resistance, so calcium will not correct until magnesium is replaced.

answers.name: Neck irradiation
answers.pearl: Radiation to the neck or radioiodine therapy can damage parathyroid tissue, sometimes years later.

answers.name: Reoperative neck surgery
answers.pearl: Repeat neck surgery greatly raises the risk because remaining glands are scarred or devascularized.

answers.name: Hemochromatosis
answers.pearl: Iron deposition destroys parathyroid tissue in iron overload states.

answers.name: Alcohol use
answers.pearl: Chronic alcohol use depletes magnesium, impairing PTH secretion.

answers.name: Proton pump inhibitors
answers.pearl: Long-term use can cause severe hypomagnesemia with functional hypoparathyroidism and hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Loop diuretics
answers.pearl: Furosemide-induced renal magnesium wasting can produce functional PTH deficiency.

answers.name: Cisplatin
answers.pearl: Cisplatin causes renal magnesium wasting, producing hypomagnesemia and low PTH.

answers.name: Aminoglycosides
answers.pearl: Aminoglycosides and amphotericin B cause renal magnesium wasting and functional hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: EGFR inhibitors
answers.pearl: Cetuximab and panitumumab block EGF-mediated magnesium reabsorption, causing hypomagnesemia and hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Metastatic cancer infiltration
answers.pearl: Breast, lung and other metastases can replace parathyroid tissue, though this is uncommonly symptomatic.

answers.name: Thalassemia major
answers.pearl: Transfusional iron overload deposits iron in parathyroid glands.

answers.name: Neonatal hypoparathyroidism from maternal hypercalcemia
answers.pearl: Maternal hyperparathyroidism exposes the fetus to high calcium, suppressing fetal parathyroid glands and causing transient neonatal hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Infiltrative disease
answers.pearl: Amyloid, granulomas and sarcoid replace parathyroid tissue in rare cases.

answers.name: Wilson disease
answers.pearl: Copper deposition in parathyroid tissue is described in a few patients.

answers.name: Activating calcium-sensing receptor mutation
answers.pearl: Activating CASR mutations make glands interpret normal calcium as high and suppress PTH, causing hypocalcemia with relative hypercalciuria.

answers.name: Calcium-sensing receptor autoantibodies
answers.pearl: Acquired activating antibodies against the CaSR produce autoimmune hypocalcemia, sometimes with APS-1 or isolated.

answers.name: GCM2 mutation
answers.pearl: Inactivating or dominant-negative mutations of the parathyroid-specific transcription factor GCM2 cause familial isolated hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: PTH gene mutation
answers.pearl: Mutations in the PTH signal peptide cause dominant or recessive isolated hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: X-linked recessive hypoparathyroidism
answers.pearl: A rearrangement near SOX3 causes parathyroid agenesis in affected males.

answers.name: Gain-of-function GNA11 mutation
answers.pearl: Activating mutations in Galpha-11, the CaSR signalling protein, cause autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 2.

answers.name: Bartter syndrome type 5
answers.pearl: Activating CASR mutations can also inhibit the renal ROMK channel and NKCC2, causing a Bartter-like phenotype with hypocalcemia.

answers.name: Kenny-Caffey syndrome
answers.pearl: TBCE (type 1) or FAM111A (type 2) mutations cause short stature, thick cortical bone and hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Sanjad-Sakati syndrome
answers.pearl: Autosomal recessive TBCE mutation causes hypoparathyroidism, retardation, and dysmorphism, mostly in Arab populations.

answers.name: Kearns-Sayre syndrome
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial DNA deletions cause hypoparathyroidism together with ophthalmoplegia, retinopathy and heart block.

answers.name: MELAS syndrome
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial tRNA mutations can include hypoparathyroidism among multisystem features.

answers.name: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency
answers.pearl: Long-chain fatty acid oxidation defects (LCHAD and trifunctional protein deficiency) are associated with hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: Pearson syndrome
answers.pearl: Mitochondrial deletion syndrome with sideroblastic anemia and pancreatic dysfunction that rarely includes hypoparathyroidism.

answers.name: CHARGE syndrome
aliases: coloboma heart defects choanal atresia syndrome
answers.pearl: CHD7-related disorder in which hypoparathyroidism, parathyroid aplasia and thymic hypoplasia occur in a 22q11-like pattern.

answers.name: Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy
answers.pearl: Case reports describe autoimmune hypoparathyroidism with PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade.

answers.name: HIV infection
answers.pearl: Infiltration by cytomegalovirus, Mycobacterium avium complex, or Kaposi sarcoma has been reported at autopsy.

answers.name: Severe hypermagnesemia
answers.pearl: Very high magnesium can transiently suppress PTH release.

answers.name: Parathyroid agenesis
answers.pearl: Congenital absence of parathyroid glands occurs in DiGeorge and other developmental syndromes.

answers.name: Maternal diabetes
answers.pearl: Infants of diabetic mothers can have transient neonatal hypoparathyroidism related to hypomagnesemia and delayed parathyroid maturation.

answers.name: Prematurity
answers.pearl: Immature parathyroid function contributes to early neonatal hypocalcemia.

answers.name: HDR syndrome
answers.pearl: GATA3 haploinsufficiency causes hypoparathyroidism, sensorineural deafness, and renal dysplasia.

answers.name: DiGeorge syndrome
answers.pearl: 22q11.2 deletion causes parathyroid hypoplasia with cardiac defects, thymic hypoplasia and facial anomalies; hypocalcemia may present in the neonate.

answers.name: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1
answers.pearl: AIRE gene mutations cause hypoparathyroidism, adrenal insufficiency and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.

prompts.prompt: Name causes of pseudohyperkalemia or transcellular-shift hyperkalemia.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Hypertonic mannitol, Hypertonic saline and Hyperosmolar radiocontrast (small transient shifts), Aminocaproic acid (mainly with renal failure), Bufadienolide toad toxin and Fluoride poisoning (toxicology case-report level), Hereditary stomatocytosis (rare), Post-dialysis potassium rebound, Absorption of blood from a GI bleed (K+ load rather than a shift), Mesenteric ischemia. Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis, Familial pseudohyperkalemia and Arginine infusion are scored as board traps. Several entries are true cell release rather than pure shift (rhabdomyolysis, TLS, hemolysis).

answers.name: Hemolyzed sample
answers.pearl: In vitro hemolysis releases intracellular potassium and is the commonest cause of spurious hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Insulin deficiency
answers.pearl: Insulin drives K+ into cells via Na-K-ATPase; its absence shifts K+ out even when total body K+ is low.

answers.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
answers.pearl: DKA combines insulin deficiency, hyperosmolality and acidosis, so serum K+ is often high despite a large total body deficit.

answers.name: Metabolic acidosis
answers.pearl: H+ buffered into cells displaces K+ out, most strongly with non-organic (hyperchloremic) acidosis.

answers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
answers.pearl: Injured muscle releases large intracellular K+ stores, compounded by AKI.

answers.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
answers.pearl: Rapid lysis of malignant cells releases K+, phosphate and urate, typically in high-burden leukemia or lymphoma.

answers.name: Beta blockers
answers.pearl: Nonselective beta blockers block beta-2 mediated cellular K+ uptake and blunt disposal of a K+ load.

answers.name: Fist clenching during phlebotomy
answers.pearl: Repeated forearm muscle contraction releases K+ locally and can raise sampled K+ by 1-2 mEq/L.

answers.name: Prolonged tourniquet time
answers.pearl: Ischemia, venous stasis and muscle activity increase K+ in the drawn sample.

answers.name: Hyperglycemia
answers.pearl: Hyperosmolality draws water and K+ out of cells (solvent drag) when insulin is lacking.

answers.name: Severe burns
answers.pearl: Tissue destruction and hemolysis release K+, and the later susceptibility to succinylcholine rises.

answers.name: Succinylcholine
answers.pearl: Depolarization of upregulated extrajunctional receptors causes K+ efflux in burns, denervation, spinal cord injury and prolonged immobility.

answers.name: Digoxin toxicity
answers.pearl: Inhibition of Na-K-ATPase blocks cellular K+ uptake; in acute overdose the level of hyperkalemia predicts mortality.

answers.name: Thrombocytosis
answers.pearl: Platelets release K+ during clotting, so serum K+ exceeds plasma K+ at very high platelet counts.

answers.name: Marked leukocytosis
answers.pearl: Fragile leukocytes in very high WBC counts leak K+ in vitro, classically in CLL.

answers.name: Tissue ischemia or reperfusion
answers.pearl: Ischemic cells lose K+; revascularization or clamp release flushes it into the circulation.

answers.name: Delayed sample processing
answers.pearl: Unspun blood sitting for hours loses K+ from cells as metabolism and the Na-K pump fail.

answers.name: Crush injury or compartment syndrome
answers.pearl: Necrotic muscle releases K+ and myoglobin, and reperfusion after release causes abrupt hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Refrigerated sample
answers.pearl: Cold inhibits Na-K-ATPase so cells cannot retain K+; whole blood should not be iced for K+.

answers.name: Massive transfusion of stored blood
answers.pearl: Stored red cells leak K+ into the supernatant, and irradiated units leak more.

answers.name: Hypertonic mannitol
answers.pearl: Hyperosmolality pulls water and K+ out of cells, raising serum K+ transiently.

answers.name: Pneumatic tube transport
answers.pearl: Mechanical stress during tube transport can hemolyze fragile cells and raise measured K+.

answers.name: Difficult or traumatic venipuncture
answers.pearl: Small-gauge needles, forceful aspiration and repeated attempts hemolyze red cells.

answers.name: EDTA contamination
answers.pearl: K2EDTA carried over from a lavender tube raises K+ and lowers calcium, magnesium and ALP.

answers.name: Vigorous tube mixing or underfilled tube
answers.pearl: Shaking or excess vacuum shear on a poorly filled tube lyses red cells.

answers.name: Strenuous exercise
answers.pearl: Working muscle releases K+, and the rise is larger in people taking beta blockers.

answers.name: Hypertonic saline
answers.pearl: Raising plasma tonicity draws water and K+ out of cells as with other hyperosmolar solutes.

answers.name: Intravascular hemolysis
answers.pearl: Hemolytic anemia, hemolytic transfusion reactions or prosthetic valve hemolysis release red cell K+ in vivo.

answers.name: Malignant hyperthermia
answers.pearl: Uncontrolled skeletal muscle calcium release causes rhabdomyolysis, acidosis and hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Mesenteric ischemia or bowel infarction
answers.pearl: Dying bowel releases K+ together with acidosis, and hyperkalemia is a poor prognostic sign.

answers.name: Heat stroke
answers.pearl: Exertional heat stroke causes rhabdomyolysis and acidosis with hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Status epilepticus
answers.pearl: Prolonged convulsions cause muscle breakdown and lactic acidosis, shifting K+ outward.

answers.name: Alpha-adrenergic agonists
answers.pearl: Alpha stimulation impairs cellular K+ uptake, an effect described with phenylephrine and high-dose catecholamines.

answers.name: Post-dialysis potassium rebound
answers.pearl: After hemodialysis, K+ moves from the intracellular space back into plasma, so levels climb in the hours after treatment.

answers.name: Serum-plasma potassium gap
answers.pearl: Serum K+ exceeds plasma K+ by more than 0.4 mEq/L when clotting releases K+; a lithium heparin plasma sample resolves it.

answers.name: Capillary sampling with forceful milking
answers.pearl: Fingerstick or heel samples squeezed hard are hemolyzed, a frequent artifact in neonates.

answers.name: Reperfusion of a transplanted liver or kidney
answers.pearl: Preservation fluid and ischemic graft cells flood the circulation with K+ at reperfusion.

answers.name: IV fluid contamination of the sample
aliases: drawing from arm with IV infusion
answers.pearl: Blood drawn above an infusion containing KCl or parenteral nutrition gives a falsely high K+.

answers.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm
answers.pearl: Polycythemia vera or essential thrombocythemia can give spurious K+ from thrombocytosis and leukocytosis.

answers.name: Absorption of blood from a GI bleed or large hematoma
answers.pearl: Lysed red cells in the gut or tissue deliver a K+ load, particularly when renal function is poor.

answers.name: Acute leukemia with hyperleukocytosis
answers.pearl: Blast counts in the hundreds of thousands leak K+ in vitro; run a whole blood or plasma sample.

answers.name: Hyperosmolar radiocontrast
answers.pearl: Hypertonic contrast raises osmolality and pulls K+ from cells, a small effect that matters in renal failure.

answers.name: Infused hydrochloric acid or ammonium chloride
answers.pearl: Mineral acid loads cause acidosis with a larger outward K+ shift than organic acids do.

answers.name: Tourniquet release during limb surgery
answers.pearl: Deflating a limb tourniquet reperfuses ischemic muscle and releases K+ and acid into the circulation.

answers.name: Hereditary stomatocytosis
answers.pearl: Cation-leaky red cells (xerocytosis) can show pseudohyperkalemia, especially on delayed or cold samples.

answers.name: Propofol infusion syndrome
answers.pearl: High-dose prolonged propofol causes mitochondrial failure, rhabdomyolysis, metabolic acidosis and hyperkalemia.

answers.name: Aminocaproic acid
answers.pearl: Epsilon-aminocaproic acid, a lysine analog, shifts K+ extracellularly, mainly in renal impairment.

answers.name: Cardiopulmonary bypass with cardioplegia
answers.pearl: High-K+ cardioplegia and circuit hemolysis raise K+ transiently.

answers.name: ECMO or mechanical circuit hemolysis
answers.pearl: Shear stress or pump thrombosis cause hemolysis and a K+ load.

answers.name: Cardiac glycoside plant poisoning
answers.pearl: Oleander, foxglove or lily-of-the-valley contain glycosides that block Na-K-ATPase like digoxin.

answers.name: Fluoride poisoning
answers.pearl: Fluoride inhibits Na-K-ATPase, causing hyperkalemia with hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia.

answers.name: Bufadienolide toad toxin
answers.pearl: Chan Su and Bufo toad toxins are digoxin-like Na-K-ATPase inhibitors.

answers.name: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
answers.pearl: SCN4A sodium channel mutation with attacks of weakness after rest following exercise or K+ intake.

answers.name: Familial pseudohyperkalemia
answers.pearl: Inherited red cell membrane K+ leak at cold temperatures gives high measured K+ in a well patient.

answers.name: Arginine infusion
answers.pearl: Arginine hydrochloride shifts K+ out of cells; seen in ICU use and growth hormone stimulation testing.

prompts.prompt: Name hereditary cancer predisposition or tumor syndromes seen in adult medicine.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: Tylosis with esophageal cancer, Familial EGFR T790M lung cancer susceptibility, Gastric adenocarcinoma and proximal polyposis of the stomach, Epidermolysis bullosa with squamous cell carcinoma, Epidermodysplasia verruciformis, TMEM127/MAX pheochromocytoma, Hereditary mixed polyposis syndrome and ANKRD26/CEBPA/DDX41 familial myeloid syndromes (case-report or small-series level, scored 90+). Serrated polyposis syndrome (germline basis unclear), Hereditary pancreatitis (cancer predisposition rather than a classic tumor syndrome) and Retinoblastoma survivors (adult second cancers) are borderline. Peutz-Jeghers, Carney complex, Gorlin and Turcot are scored as board traps.

answers.name: Lynch syndrome
answers.pearl: Germline MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 or EPCAM defect causing colorectal, endometrial and other cancers.

answers.name: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
answers.pearl: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations raise risk of breast, ovarian, pancreatic and prostate cancer.

answers.name: Familial adenomatous polyposis
answers.pearl: Germline APC mutation causing hundreds to thousands of colonic adenomas with near-certain colorectal cancer.

answers.name: Li-Fraumeni syndrome
answers.pearl: Germline TP53 mutation with sarcoma, breast cancer, brain tumors, adrenocortical carcinoma and leukemia.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1
answers.pearl: MEN1 mutation causing parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.

answers.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2
answers.pearl: Activating RET mutation causing medullary thyroid cancer, pheochromocytoma and (in 2A) hyperparathyroidism.

answers.name: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
answers.pearl: VHL inactivation causing hemangioblastomas, clear cell renal carcinoma and pheochromocytoma.

answers.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
answers.pearl: NF1 mutation with neurofibromas, cafe-au-lait macules, optic glioma and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.

answers.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex
answers.pearl: TSC1 or TSC2 mutations cause renal angiomyolipomas, SEGAs, cardiac rhabdomyomas and LAM.

answers.name: Cowden syndrome
answers.pearl: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome with breast, thyroid and endometrial cancer, macrocephaly and trichilemmomas.

answers.name: Neurofibromatosis type 2
answers.pearl: NF2 mutation causing bilateral vestibular schwannomas, meningiomas and ependymomas.

answers.name: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer
answers.pearl: CDH1 mutation with signet-ring gastric cancer and lobular breast cancer; prophylactic gastrectomy is considered.

answers.name: Familial atypical multiple mole melanoma syndrome
answers.pearl: CDKN2A mutations cause melanoma and pancreatic cancer.

answers.name: MUTYH-associated polyposis
answers.pearl: Biallelic MUTYH mutation causes an autosomal recessive attenuated polyposis with colorectal cancer.

answers.name: Juvenile polyposis syndrome
answers.pearl: SMAD4 or BMPR1A mutation with hamartomatous GI polyps and colorectal and gastric cancer; SMAD4 carriers may have HHT.

answers.name: Hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndrome
answers.pearl: SDHx mutations produce head and neck paragangliomas, pheochromocytoma, GIST and renal cancer.

answers.name: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome
answers.pearl: FLCN mutation with fibrofolliculomas, lung cysts and pneumothorax, and chromophobe or hybrid renal tumors.

answers.name: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
answers.pearl: FH mutation causing cutaneous and uterine leiomyomas and aggressive type 2 papillary renal cancer.

answers.name: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
answers.pearl: STK11 mutation with mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyps, plus risk of GI, breast, pancreatic and sex cord tumors.

answers.name: Carney complex
answers.pearl: PRKAR1A mutation with cardiac myxomas, spotty skin pigmentation, PPNAD and endocrine tumors.

answers.name: Gorlin syndrome
answers.pearl: PTCH1 mutation with multiple basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic keratocysts, medulloblastoma and palmar pits.

answers.name: PALB2-associated cancer predisposition
answers.pearl: PALB2 mutation confers a breast cancer risk approaching that of BRCA2, plus pancreatic cancer risk.

answers.name: CHEK2-associated cancer predisposition
answers.pearl: CHEK2 variants such as 1100delC raise breast and colorectal cancer risk moderately.

answers.name: ATM-associated cancer predisposition
answers.pearl: Heterozygous ATM mutation confers moderate breast and pancreatic cancer risk; biallelic loss causes ataxia-telangiectasia.

answers.name: Hereditary pancreatic cancer
answers.pearl: Familial pancreatic cancer kindreds with two or more affected first-degree relatives merit germline testing and pancreas surveillance.

answers.name: Hereditary pancreatitis
answers.pearl: PRSS1 gain-of-function mutation causes recurrent pancreatitis and a markedly raised lifetime pancreatic cancer risk.

answers.name: Hereditary prostate cancer
answers.pearl: HOXB13 G84E and BRCA2 variants are associated with early-onset familial prostate cancer.

answers.name: Retinoblastoma survivors with germline RB1 mutation
answers.pearl: Survivors of heritable retinoblastoma carry high lifetime risk of sarcomas (osteosarcoma), melanoma and lung cancer.

answers.name: Xeroderma pigmentosum
answers.pearl: Defective nucleotide excision repair leads to extreme UV sensitivity with early basal cell, squamous cell cancer and melanoma.

answers.name: Muir-Torre syndrome
answers.pearl: Lynch syndrome variant with sebaceous adenomas, carcinomas and keratoacanthomas.

answers.name: Turcot syndrome
answers.pearl: Colorectal polyposis or cancer with brain tumors, caused by APC (medulloblastoma) or mismatch repair (glioblastoma) defects.

answers.name: Hereditary papillary renal carcinoma
aliases: hereditary type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma
answers.pearl: Activating MET mutations cause multifocal type 1 papillary renal carcinoma.

answers.name: Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
answers.pearl: A RET-related variant of MEN2 with medullary thyroid cancer alone.

answers.name: BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome
answers.pearl: BAP1 mutation causes uveal and cutaneous melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cell carcinoma and atypical melanocytic tumors.

answers.name: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
answers.pearl: CDC73 (HRPT2) mutation causing parathyroid adenomas and carcinoma, ossifying jaw fibromas and renal lesions.

answers.name: DICER1 syndrome
answers.pearl: DICER1 mutation with pleuropulmonary blastoma, thyroid disease, cystic nephroma and Sertoli-Leydig tumors; adults can present with multinodular goiter or thyroid cancer.

answers.name: Hereditary multiple osteochondromas
answers.pearl: EXT1 or EXT2 mutation with exostoses and risk of secondary chondrosarcoma.

answers.name: Schwannomatosis
answers.pearl: SMARCB1 or LZTR1 mutations cause multiple painful schwannomas without bilateral vestibular tumors.

answers.name: Fanconi anemia
answers.pearl: DNA crosslink repair defect with marrow failure, AML and head and neck or anogenital squamous cell carcinoma; some are diagnosed in adulthood.

answers.name: Telomere biology disorders
answers.pearl: Dyskeratosis congenita and related TERT, TERC or RTEL1 disease cause marrow failure, pulmonary fibrosis, liver disease and squamous cell cancers.

answers.name: Werner syndrome
answers.pearl: WRN helicase mutation causing premature aging with sarcomas, thyroid cancer, melanoma and other tumors.

answers.name: Bloom syndrome
answers.pearl: BLM helicase defect with growth deficiency, sun-sensitive rash and many cancer types at young ages.

answers.name: Rothmund-Thomson syndrome
answers.pearl: RECQL4 mutation with poikiloderma and a high rate of osteosarcoma and skin cancer.

answers.name: GATA2 deficiency syndrome
answers.pearl: GATA2 mutation with MonoMAC, Emberger syndrome, MDS and AML and susceptibility to mycobacterial infection.

answers.name: Familial platelet disorder with predisposition to AML
answers.pearl: RUNX1 germline mutation causing thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction and later MDS or AML.

answers.name: DDX41-associated familial myeloid neoplasm
answers.pearl: Germline DDX41 mutation with late-onset MDS and AML in adults, often with preceding macrocytosis and cytopenias.

answers.name: CEBPA-associated familial AML
answers.pearl: Germline CEBPA mutation causes AML with high penetrance and long latency, often with later somatic second hits.

answers.name: ANKRD26-related thrombocytopenia
answers.pearl: 5'UTR ANKRD26 mutation (thrombocytopenia 2) with mild thrombocytopenia and predisposition to AML and MDS.

answers.name: Cylindromatosis syndrome
answers.pearl: CYLD mutation causing cylindromas, trichoepitheliomas and spiradenomas (Brooke-Spiegler, Fordyce-Spiegler).

answers.name: Hereditary GIST syndrome
answers.pearl: Germline KIT or PDGFRA mutations lead to multiple gastrointestinal stromal tumors, mastocytosis and hyperpigmentation.

answers.name: Carney-Stratakis syndrome
answers.pearl: Germline SDHx mutations cause the dyad of gastric GIST and paraganglioma.

answers.name: MEN4
answers.pearl: CDKN1B mutations cause a MEN1-like syndrome of parathyroid and pituitary tumors.

answers.name: Familial isolated pituitary adenoma
answers.pearl: AIP mutation causes aggressive GH-secreting adenomas, often in young patients.

answers.name: Polymerase proofreading-associated polyposis
answers.pearl: Germline POLE or POLD1 exonuclease mutations cause ultramutated colorectal adenomas and cancers, plus endometrial and brain tumors.

answers.name: NTHL1-associated polyposis
answers.pearl: Biallelic NTHL1 mutations cause autosomal recessive base excision repair deficiency with colorectal, breast and other cancers.

answers.name: Hereditary mixed polyposis syndrome
answers.pearl: A GREM1 upstream duplication in Ashkenazi families causes mixed adenomatous, serrated and juvenile-type polyps.

answers.name: Serrated polyposis syndrome
answers.pearl: Multiple or large serrated colorectal polyps with raised colorectal cancer risk; a germline cause (RNF43) is found only rarely.

answers.name: Gastric adenocarcinoma and proximal polyposis of the stomach
answers.pearl: A rare APC promoter 1B variant gives fundic gland polyps with gastric cancer, without colonic polyposis.

answers.name: Attenuated familial adenomatous polyposis
answers.pearl: Fewer than 100 adenomas at later onset due to APC mutations at the 5' or 3' ends.

answers.name: Hereditary ovarian cancer genes RAD51C, RAD51D and BRIP1
answers.pearl: Mutations in these homologous recombination genes raise ovarian cancer risk without a large breast cancer risk.

answers.name: Familial non-medullary thyroid cancer
answers.pearl: Non-syndromic clustering of papillary thyroid cancer in families; also seen with PTEN, APC and DICER1 syndromes.

answers.name: Epidermolysis bullosa with squamous cell carcinoma
answers.pearl: Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa causes aggressive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, often from chronic wounds.

answers.name: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis
answers.pearl: Inherited susceptibility to beta-HPV (TMC6/TMC8 mutations) causes widespread warts and skin squamous cell carcinoma in sun-exposed areas.

answers.name: Tylosis with esophageal cancer
aliases: focal non-epidermolytic palmoplantar keratoderma esophageal cancer
answers.pearl: RHBDF2 mutation causing palmoplantar keratoderma with high risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

answers.name: Familial EGFR T790M lung cancer susceptibility
answers.pearl: Germline EGFR T790M predisposes carriers, including never-smokers, to multiple lung adenocarcinomas.

answers.name: Hereditary pheochromocytoma from TMEM127 or MAX mutations
answers.pearl: These less common susceptibility genes cause pheochromocytoma, often bilateral, with MAX also linked to paraganglioma.

prompts.prompt: Name disease-specific autoantibodies (outside paraneoplastic syndromes) and the conditions they mark.
prompts.review_notes: Least sure: anti-nephrin (recent series, not yet standard), anti-IgLON5, anti-tryptophan hydroxylase and anti-ASGPR (limited-evidence markers at 100), anti-calcium-sensing receptor, anti-interferon-gamma and anti-factor H (case-series level). Anti-NMDAR, anti-AQP4 and anti-GAD65 overlap the paraneoplastic prompt but are included here as non-paraneoplastic disease markers.

answers.name: Anti-dsDNA antibodies (SLE)
answers.pearl: Highly specific for SLE; titers track disease activity and lupus nephritis.

answers.name: Anti-CCP antibodies (rheumatoid arthritis)
answers.pearl: Highly specific for rheumatoid arthritis and predicts erosive disease, often preceding symptoms.

answers.name: Rheumatoid factor
answers.pearl: IgM against the Fc of IgG; sensitive for RA but also raised in Sjogren, cryoglobulinemia and chronic infection.

answers.name: Anti-TPO antibodies (Hashimoto thyroiditis)
answers.pearl: Most sensitive marker of autoimmune thyroiditis and predicts progression to hypothyroidism.

answers.name: Anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (celiac disease)
answers.pearl: First-line celiac screen, interpreted with total IgA because IgA deficiency gives false negatives.

answers.name: Anti-PR3 antibodies (granulomatosis with polyangiitis)
answers.pearl: Cytoplasmic ANCA to proteinase 3 marks GPA with sinus, lung and renal disease.

answers.name: Anti-MPO antibodies (microscopic polyangiitis)
answers.pearl: Perinuclear ANCA to myeloperoxidase marks MPA, EGPA and renal-limited pauci-immune GN.

answers.name: Anti-centromere antibodies (limited systemic sclerosis)
answers.pearl: Marks limited cutaneous scleroderma (CREST) with pulmonary hypertension risk.

answers.name: Anti-Scl-70 antibodies (diffuse systemic sclerosis)
answers.pearl: Anti-topoisomerase I marks diffuse scleroderma with interstitial lung disease.

answers.name: Anti-Smith antibodies (SLE)
answers.pearl: Anti-Sm is highly specific for SLE but does not track activity.

answers.name: Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies (Sjogren syndrome)
answers.pearl: Cross the placenta and cause neonatal lupus with congenital heart block; also mark subacute cutaneous lupus.

answers.name: Anti-SSB/La antibodies (Sjogren syndrome)
answers.pearl: Usually accompany anti-Ro in Sjogren and confer added congenital heart block risk.

answers.name: Antimitochondrial antibodies (primary biliary cholangitis)
answers.pearl: Directed at the E2 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex; present in over 90 percent of PBC.

answers.name: Anti-smooth muscle antibodies (autoimmune hepatitis type 1)
answers.pearl: Type 1 autoimmune hepatitis hallmark, usually with ANA and hypergammaglobulinemia.

answers.name: Anti-TSH receptor antibodies (Graves disease)
answers.pearl: Stimulating IgG drives hyperthyroidism, Graves orbitopathy and pretibial myxedema.

answers.name: Anti-histone antibodies (drug-induced lupus)
answers.pearl: Seen in procainamide and hydralazine lupus, with negative anti-dsDNA.

answers.name: Anti-U1 RNP antibodies (mixed connective tissue disease)
answers.pearl: High-titer anti-U1 RNP defines MCTD with Raynaud, puffy hands and myositis.

answers.name: Anti-Jo-1 antibodies (antisynthetase syndrome)
answers.pearl: Most common antisynthetase antibody: myositis, ILD, mechanic hands, Raynaud and arthritis.

answers.name: Anti-GBM antibodies (Goodpasture disease)
answers.pearl: IgG to the alpha-3 chain NC1 domain of type IV collagen causes pulmonary-renal syndrome.

answers.name: Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies (myasthenia gravis)
answers.pearl: Present in about 85 percent of generalized MG and associated with thymoma and thymic hyperplasia.

answers.name: Anti-endomysial antibodies (celiac disease)
answers.pearl: Very specific immunofluorescence test whose target antigen is tissue transglutaminase.

answers.name: Anti-intrinsic factor antibodies (pernicious anemia)
answers.pearl: Very specific for pernicious anemia and block B12 binding to intrinsic factor.

answers.name: Anti-parietal cell antibodies (autoimmune gastritis)
answers.pearl: Target the gastric proton pump; sensitive but less specific marker of autoimmune atrophic gastritis.

answers.name: Anti-GAD65 antibodies (type 1 diabetes)
answers.pearl: Most useful antibody for adult LADA and persists longer than islet-cell antibodies.

answers.name: Anti-desmoglein 3 antibodies (pemphigus vulgaris)
answers.pearl: Cause suprabasal acantholysis with mucosal erosions.

answers.name: Anti-BP180 antibodies (bullous pemphigoid)
answers.pearl: Hemidesmosomal collagen XVII antibodies cause subepidermal blisters in older patients.

answers.name: Anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies (autoimmune Addison disease)
answers.pearl: Best marker of autoimmune adrenalitis, the most common cause of Addison disease in high-income countries.

answers.name: Anti-thyroglobulin antibodies
answers.pearl: Raised in Hashimoto and interfere with thyroglobulin tumor-marker assays in thyroid cancer follow-up.

answers.name: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (Crohn disease)
answers.pearl: Associated with Crohn disease, usually with a negative pANCA.

answers.name: Anti-PLA2R antibodies (primary membranous nephropathy)
answers.pearl: Positive in roughly 70 percent of primary membranous; titer guides treatment and can obviate biopsy.

answers.name: Anti-platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antibodies (immune thrombocytopenia)
answers.pearl: Opsonize platelets for splenic clearance; testing is insensitive so ITP remains a clinical diagnosis.

answers.name: Anti-PF4/heparin antibodies (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia)
answers.pearl: Platelet-activating IgG causes thrombocytopenia with thrombosis 5-10 days after heparin.

answers.name: Anti-ADAMTS13 antibodies (immune TTP)
answers.pearl: Inhibit the VWF-cleaving protease, with activity below 10 percent in acquired TTP.

answers.name: Anti-ribosomal P antibodies (neuropsychiatric lupus)
answers.pearl: Linked to lupus psychosis and depression and to lupus hepatitis.

answers.name: Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I antibodies (antiphospholipid syndrome)
answers.pearl: Criteria antibody, with lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin, for thrombotic and obstetric APS.

answers.name: Anti-factor VIII antibodies (acquired hemophilia A)
answers.pearl: Isolated prolonged aPTT that does not correct on mixing; bleeding in older adults or postpartum.

answers.name: Anti-Mi-2 antibodies (dermatomyositis)
answers.pearl: Classic dermatomyositis with shawl sign and cuticular overgrowth; good steroid response.

answers.name: Anti-SRP antibodies (immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy)
answers.pearl: Severe proximal weakness with very high CK and little inflammation on biopsy.

answers.name: Anti-HMGCR antibodies (statin-associated necrotizing myopathy)
answers.pearl: Weakness persists after stopping the statin and needs immunotherapy.

answers.name: Anti-MDA5 antibodies (clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis)
answers.pearl: Skin ulcers and rapidly progressive ILD with high ferritin and poor prognosis.

answers.name: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies (scleroderma renal crisis)
answers.pearl: Rapidly progressive diffuse skin disease, renal crisis and a modest cancer association.

answers.name: Anti-MuSK antibodies (myasthenia gravis)
answers.pearl: AChR-negative MG with bulbar and neck weakness, muscle atrophy and poor response to pyridostigmine.

answers.name: Anti-LKM-1 antibodies (autoimmune hepatitis type 2)
answers.pearl: Type 2 AIH targets CYP2D6, mostly in children and young women.

answers.name: Anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies (neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder)
answers.pearl: Astrocytic channelopathy with longitudinally extensive myelitis, optic neuritis and area postrema syndrome.

answers.name: Anti-MOG antibodies (MOG antibody-associated disease)
answers.pearl: Distinct from MS and NMOSD, with optic neuritis, ADEM and myelitis.

answers.name: Anti-NMDA receptor antibodies (autoimmune encephalitis)
answers.pearl: Young women with psychosis, seizures and dyskinesia; teratoma in a minority, many cases have no tumor.

answers.name: Anti-ganglioside GQ1b antibodies (Miller Fisher syndrome)
answers.pearl: Ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia after an infection such as Campylobacter.

answers.name: Anti-GM1 antibodies (multifocal motor neuropathy)
answers.pearl: Conduction-block motor neuropathy without sensory loss that responds to IVIG.

answers.name: Anti-MAG antibodies (IgM paraproteinemic neuropathy)
answers.pearl: Slowly progressive distal sensory ataxic neuropathy with IgM monoclonal gammopathy.

answers.name: Anti-transglutaminase 3 antibodies (dermatitis herpetiformis)
answers.pearl: Granular IgA at dermal papillae and gluten sensitivity with pruritic vesicles.

answers.name: Anti-collagen VII antibodies (epidermolysis bullosa acquisita)
answers.pearl: Anchoring-fibril antibodies cause mechanobullous skin fragility and scarring.

answers.name: Anti-desmoglein 1 antibodies (pemphigus foliaceus)
answers.pearl: Superficial acantholysis with crusted scaly lesions and no mucosal involvement.

answers.name: Anti-gp210 antibodies (primary biliary cholangitis)
answers.pearl: Nuclear rim pattern marking AMA-negative or more progressive PBC.

answers.name: Anti-PM/Scl antibodies (scleroderma-myositis overlap)
answers.pearl: Overlap of scleroderma and polymyositis with ILD and calcinosis, good prognosis.

answers.name: Anti-C3 nephritic factor (C3 glomerulopathy)
answers.pearl: Autoantibody stabilizing alternative-pathway C3 convertase and causing low C3 in MPGN and acquired partial lipodystrophy.

answers.name: Anti-cN-1A antibodies (inclusion body myositis)
answers.pearl: Present in a fraction of IBM; helps distinguish it from polymyositis, with modest sensitivity.

answers.name: Anti-GM-CSF antibodies (autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis)
answers.pearl: Neutralize GM-CSF, impair alveolar macrophage surfactant clearance and cause crazy-paving on CT.

answers.name: Anti-SLA/LP antibodies (autoimmune hepatitis)
answers.pearl: Most specific AIH antibody; marks severe disease and relapse.

answers.name: Anti-contactin-1 antibodies (autoimmune nodopathy)
answers.pearl: CIDP-like neuropathy with aggressive onset, tremor and sometimes membranous nephropathy.

answers.name: Anti-neurofascin-155 antibodies (autoimmune nodopathy)
answers.pearl: CIDP variant with tremor, ataxia and poor IVIG response, responding to rituximab.

answers.name: Anti-laminin 332 antibodies (mucous membrane pemphigoid)
answers.pearl: Scarring pemphigoid with ocular involvement and an association with solid cancers.

answers.name: Anti-ganglionic acetylcholine receptor antibodies (autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy)
answers.pearl: Subacute panautonomic failure with orthostasis, anhidrosis and tonic pupils.

answers.name: Anti-NALP5 antibodies (APS-1 hypoparathyroidism)
answers.pearl: Autoantibody linked to hypoparathyroidism in autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1.

answers.name: Anti-erythropoietin antibodies (pure red cell aplasia)
answers.pearl: Neutralizing antibodies emerged with subcutaneous epoetin alfa, causing transfusion-dependent anemia.

answers.name: Anti-calcium-sensing receptor antibodies (acquired hypocalciuric hypercalcemia)
answers.pearl: Mimic familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and occur with other autoimmune disease.

answers.name: Anti-interferon-gamma antibodies (adult-onset immunodeficiency)
answers.pearl: Cause disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial and other opportunistic infections, mainly in Southeast Asian adults.

answers.name: Anti-insulin receptor antibodies (type B insulin resistance)
answers.pearl: Severe insulin resistance with acanthosis nigricans, hyperandrogenism and sometimes hypoglycemia.

answers.name: Anti-factor H antibodies (autoimmune atypical HUS)
answers.pearl: Mostly children; associated with CFHR1/3 deletion and treated with plasma exchange and immunosuppression.

answers.name: Anti-17-alpha-hydroxylase and anti-side-chain cleavage antibodies (autoimmune ovarian failure)
answers.pearl: Steroid-cell antibodies mark autoimmune primary ovarian insufficiency, often with Addison disease.

answers.name: Anti-tryptophan hydroxylase antibodies (APS-1 intestinal disease)
answers.pearl: APS-1 antibody associated with intestinal dysfunction and enterochromaffin cell loss.

answers.name: Anti-IgLON5 antibodies (IgLON5 disease)
answers.pearl: Sleep disorder with REM and NREM parasomnia, bulbar dysfunction and tau deposition, HLA-DRB1*10:01.

answers.name: Anti-nephrin antibodies (minimal change disease)
answers.pearl: Recent series show nephrin antibodies in active minimal change disease and idiopathic nephrotic syndrome.

answers.name: Anti-ASGPR antibodies (autoimmune hepatitis)
answers.pearl: Hepatocyte surface antibody correlating with histologic activity in AIH.
